Dec 2013:This has to be a long term review. I've only had the printer about a week and I can't possibly comment on total cost of ownership or reliability until I've used it for a few months. So I will update this review as things happen. If I haven't updated the review, nothing has happened yet...OK on to the review:If you don't have a printer, and this is going to be your only printer, then stop, leave this page, and go get a black and white LASER printer. One for which you can buy 3rd party toner. For example I have an HP 1320 printer (it's old I know but it works). HP wanted about two hundred bucks for a toner but I found one that works well for a lot lessCompatible Toner Cartridge to Replace HP Q5949X LJ1320 Series (Black)(less than twenty bucks). This is the only way you don't get ripped off.Now if you already have a laser printer for most of your printouts, then maybe inkjet isn't so bad. I don't know yet because I haven't had this printer for very long.What I have noticed so far (little bit random order):-It's an amazing piece of tech. EPSON has to be losing money. Very sophisticated printer.-Printouts are amazing.-Ink is very water-resistant even on glossy paper.-Duplex printing and scanning is very nice.-Installed on 2 Macs with Mavericks. CD told me to go to website. I wasn't sure it was Mavericks compatible but it's working flawlessly.-After a reboot and 2 software updates, I can see detailed controls for the scanner.-Has airprint so iOS devices can print to it.I have some negative things to say:-It will not let me chose all special characters for wifi password. The screnn turns into to phone-keypad interface to put wifi in (why?). I have to push 1 to get to the special characters. But "{" was not one of them. I have a very long and complicated wifi password and I'm not going to change all my devices to accommodate lazy programming. I have long Ethernet cables so I used that and it works fine.-I don't know if I'm supposed to turn it off or let it go to sleep. If I turn it off it'll ask if I want it to retract the output tray and then I can manually close the display. Or I can set the sleep timer and it stays open. If off, then I have to turn it on before I can print. If sleeping, then it'll wake up when computer prints to it. I don't know what best practice is.So far, I think a dedicated scanner will be more useful if you scan a lot. But this is convenient if you need to photocopy once in a while (or scan many pages quickly if you don't care about resolution/color settings etc).I will update how long the cartridges last and how expensive they are.

The Vtech CS6219-2DECT6.0 Expandable 2-Handset Cordless Phone System with Caller ID and Handset Speakerphone comes as a good product at a good price, delivering just the technology I wanted, and nothing I didn't want.  It gives me Caller ID/call waiting and a handset speakerphone in each phone to make hands-free conversations easy.  In addition, most important to me, it requires only one phone jack: the additional phone can be placed where I need it, so long as an electrical outlet is nearby, and does not require its own phone jack.  It will expand up to five phones, using CS6309 accessory handsets, stores 50 calls, with a 100 name and number phone book directory.  It's also got a voicemail waiting indicator, (though you must subscribe to voicemail from your local provider), backlit keypad and display. And, wonder of wonders, it's compatible with hearing aids, a concern if your hearing is going as the years pile on. The DECT6.0 digital technology utilizes a newly available frequency band, to give lower-interference technology,better range and sound quality, and superior protection against eavesdropping.What doesn't it have?  Its own voicemail system, which would be a waste, as I subscribe to that service through my provider.  Bloated, irresponsible packaging: the packaging is 100% recyclable, and uses a non-toxic aqueous ink coating.  Furthermore, it complies with a RoHS Directive (2002/95/EC) that limits the use of hazardous substances such as lead, mercury, and cadmium, while it earns an Energy Star. In sum, the phone is convenient, flexible,well-designed for easy, intuitive use, and is good-looking enough to be at home in most rooms in the house.  And let's not forget the surprisingly good price.

I'm a big Canon product buyer and this is my first all-in-one from them. Its a nice compact well designed printer although its a bit on the heavy side but that's not an issue. I've always used Epson for my all in one but have been finding them to be trouble some with ink and then printheads not lasting more than a year. Upon setting the Canon up which took all of 30 minutes from box to printing first page, I found that the button layout to be clear, easy to figure out and not cluttered (like some epsons). There is one simple button for start/copy, in both color and B/W which makes things simple. There's a full set of number keys for various needs like fax and changing # of print copies etc. They are also letters too so when setting up your wifi, take your time to make sure you've set the right password to join your network.One of the not so great features is the small 2 line LCD screen. If it could have been slightly larger it would have helped as its a bit small and hard to read. The next model up has a color LCD that is  2.5" and depending on what you are doing (copy,fax) the entire lcd pad lights up with its available options. Is it worth another $50 dollars? not sure, guess depends on what your needs are. For me, i'd rather save the money and put it towards future ink replacements because the included inks are just starters and won't last that long. Canon usually makes printers with the individual CMYK inks (4) but this printer has just 2 one for black and the other for color. Replacements for it if you buy the dual pack of 1 each black/color is $50, half the price of the printer and the extra cost of the next model with the larger lcd.Its been my experience with my older photo printer (Canon iP4500) that the inks last a decently long time. I'm hoping that this printer does the same. I like that the ink tanks are installed thru the front where you open the door for the paper tray. This feature makes it real easy if you have the printer on a higher shelf on your desk as I do and you don't have to take it down to see what your doing. I've had my ip4500 for many years and Canon printers seem to last until the printhead wears out which is years!I love the wifi, which was so easy to setup. I have a mac and a few laptops that connected to it with ease. I'll be using this mostly for making copies and printing coupons, photos and the occasional fax. It has the ability to print from your smartphone and iPad but I have not tried this yet. Overall printing is quiet and fast and that is something Canon has been able to achieve for a long time while not sacrificing speed. This model does not have one of those memory card slots so if you print directly from your cameras memory card your out of luck on this model. You have to plug it in via usb to to this. Regular paper printouts were colorful and sharp and when I made a few 4x6 prints on gloss photo paper WOW they looked real good. I usually use the ip4500 and found better results from this MX432.The scanner was real easy to use also, my copies were super quick and pretty sharp. I also scanned a few photos and liked the speed and simplicity of the scanning software. The auto sheet feeder on the top is great, very much like the Epson's which I really love.Conclusion:Great all-in-one printer on a budget. May not have some of the bells and whistles as its older siblings but still does a great job. Its a great size printer and won't hog up too much space although its a bit heavy its great. I think the print quality is great considering its only 2 ink tanks and the speeds of print/scanning is pretty fast and quiet. This is definitely a printer to consider if you are in the market not only for a new printer but an all-in-one too.

I was going to do an "unboxing" video, but it would have been really boring to see us trying to peel off/cut through the sticky tape that held the box closed.  Further, it's a recommended two person lift and we had to spend some time locating a sturdy table to set it on.  So I'm just going to give the details about set up and use.I have had wireless printers before, one that even purported to have the same functions as this one--Lexmark X9350 Wireless Office All-in-One.  If you check the link out believe every bad review.  It's now sitting in a little used office where it occasionally is used for printing directly from one computer.  The Wi-Fi never did work.Anyway, back to our set up.  Five PCs running 32 bit XP (yeah, I know, but it works for us) on a partly wifi partly ethernet network, connected to the internet through DSL.  We scan a lot of documents and download a lot of documents from a government web site.  We also prepare a certain number of color exhibits.  four of the computers do not have CD drives.First thing I did after retrieving the instructions and locating a table sturdy enough to hold the printer was take a thumb drive and downloaded the setup fire from the Epson web site to make sure I had the most recent software.  This can be found on the Epson.com website under Drivers and Support.  Get the Combo Package which has everything.If you are using XP home follow the instructions on the quick start guide to the letter. DO NOT CONNECT THE PRINTER TO YOUR COMPUTER WITH USB UNTIL INSTRUCTED TO DO SO.Because I didn't have a computer close enough to where I wanted to locate the sturdy table that the printer was sitting on, I used my laptop with a USB cable (NOT SUPPLIED BTW) and the thumb drive for initial wifi set up. Not a hitch.  Know your wifi details such as the SSDI name and password type and password and it shouldn't be a problem at all.Next I set up the other computers using the thumb drive.  Just select the option that adds the computer to the printer, so it doesn't take long.One of the features that I was most interested in was being able to fax from individual computers through the printer.  At first I had a port problem.  I went into control panel/Printers and faxes/epson 7520 series network fax/ properties/Ports.  I unslected the checked box and then selected the Epson Net FAX Port which fixed the problem.  You will have to select the port for the fax on each computer you want to send a fax from.Because we do not have a dedicated fax line-- seems a total waste of money given how much our evil carrier wants to charge for another line-- I plugged the phone line we use for faxing into the fax machine then used the supplied phone cable to attach to the phone base.  When the phone is answered an a fax noise sounds we just lay the receiver down and let the fax go on through.  Seems to work very well.  Our previous fax machine was aBrother IntelliFAX 775 Plain Paper Fax/Phone/Copierwith a carbon film cartridge.  Not only are the faxed copies clearer, using the Epson, the machine is faster at sending and receiving.There's lots of other features (such as printing from a memory card) that I tried and had no trouble with.  I also was able to print directly from Google docs using the free iPhone app.  Epson offers something called Epson connect that allows you to send your photos and documents directly to the printer by email.  No problem with either of these.I will update if there is any change in my opinion or rating.Don't know if this was just something I missed or Epson improved the software.  I found that I can fax directly to one of the computers.  GREAT SAVINGS of ink and paper. There's a little fax icon that pops up on the toolbar and a balloon appears telling me I have a FAX. Click on it and the folder opens containing my FAXES. I can view, print, copy (and delete those annoying junk faxes).  Avoids problems due to ink running out or paper jams.  And if you want to go back to printing FAXES a simple click and a brief wait will do it.

Background information: I am not a terribly tech-savvy person, but I can usually hook up a printer and do small trouble shooting.I have been using a sad 10 year old printer for far too long and needed an update, but it is so hard to choose printers these days.This one had everything all in one machine and seemed like a good choice.Setup: This is ridiculously simple to set up. Our household has 2 iPad 3s, one iPhone and 2 MacBooks- one significantly older than the other. The newer technology (phone, Pad, and new laptop) all synced up with the printer with minimal effort via the wireless connection. The older laptop was a little trickier. It wouldn't acknowledge the specific printer model and when I tried to use a different model, the printing was screwed up and took forever. So I decided to install the printer with the disc provided (which was unnecessary for the new technology) and it took about 2 minutes and worked perfectly with that laptop from then on.Wireless Aspect: My husband and I run a dorm so we put this printer outside the apartment in the common room and the wireless connection acknowledges the printer from inside the apartment. We have the printer set on the Eco mode which turns it off when unused for a few minutes but kicks it on as soon as you print (no need for manual powering up). This has to be my favorite feature of this machine.Scanning: I installed the Epson app onto my iPad which makes scanning and saving images incredibly easy. Even without it, though, the scanning is terribly easy. The image is not the clearest as i have seen with other scanners, but it isn't bad.Photo printing: the printing of a photo was incredibly clear and sharp and didn't take as long as I would have thought!I don't have a landline, so i didn't not test the the fax option.Overall, this looks like an intimidating machine, but I think it is so easy to use that it would be a great option for anyone who is nervous about having a "complicated" machine. It does everything in one machine and wasn't a hassle to figure out. One weird glitch was how the printer registered low ink levels after the power went out in the recent storm on the east coast. I had to pluck out the cartridges and reinsert them to get the proper levels to register. It was an easy fix, but odd that the machine did that. Still, this is an excellent machine and I am pretty confident I will be sticking with Epson from here on out!

This sharpener works but leaves much to be desired.  It is a plug-in 120V 1.0A max desktop sharpener with a 5 foot cord and a 2-prong polarized plug (one side is wider).  It is made in China and has a 5-year warranty.The first thing I noticed is my pencil wobbles during sharpening.  It feels like the blades aren't quite centered inside.  After sharpening the pencil is nice and sharp but the tip isn't centered.  If I push downward firmly during sharpening it comes out better though.  The sound is higher pitched than other electric sharpeners which I found a bit annoying.  This one doesn't stop sharpening automatically, although you can tell the tip has hit something when it's sharp and pull it out.  The pencil doesn't have to go in very far - it can sharpen a pencil as short as 2.5".Although in the pictures it looks like it might tip over when you use it like an Imperial AT-PT walker being attacked by Ewoks, it doesn't, though the rubber feet don't hold well enough to allow single-handed sharpening.  The shavings tray is smallish and is the sort of hard plastic that seems like it might crack after a bit of use.Compared to my other Westcott iPoint sharpener, theWestcott Axis iPoint Evolution, this one is sorely lacking.  To be fair, it isn't as expensive either, but at this price I still expect better.  The iPoint Axis has a dial to accept different width pencils, sharpens evenly, has a quieter lower pitched sound, doesn't slip so you can sharpen with one hand, and stops sharpening when the pencil is ready.  It also has a larger and better quality plastic shavings tray.  It also has a 10-year warranty.  If you want a good quality sharpener, I recommend that one over the iPoint Curve Axis.A couple others I own are theX-Acto Electric Pencil Sharpener (1818), which is cheaper but after a year of light use started making a loud grinding noise, and also only handles standard-size pencils, and the manualX-Acto Model KS Table- or Wall-Mount Pencil Sharpener (1031), which works but isn't as solid as the original Boston model of old.PROS:Strong motor sharpens quicklyPencils come out sharpCan sharpen a shorter pencil5-year warrantyCONS:Doesn't sharpen on centerHigh-pitched whiny soundPencil wobbles during sharpeningDoesn't turn off automaticallyNeed 2 hands to sharpenOnly fits standard size pencilsShavings tray seems brittle and flimsy

When these pencils first arrived to my home office, I couldn't believe how the point was brought to such a strong sharpened point. Great, clean eraser ... as expected in a good quality No. 2 pencil.
Beautiful cards with gorgeous pictures and verses!  You won't be disappointed with these cards and they will bring a smile to whomever you send them to.

I was looking for a place to put important family messages and information, and this board does a great job. I love that I not only can leave notes, but the magnets allow me to post papers that we want to refer to. I used to work for a guy who required us to wrap every square inch of a shipped package in tape. "Pack for a water landing", he would say.  He would have loved this stuff!  From the first moment you peel a length of this tape off the roll, you can feel the difference between it and ordinary packing tape.  Regular tape will tangle, fold back over, stick to itself and cause untold grief and frustration.  This tape has a thickness and stiffness to it that will eliminate all that.  I think you could dispense a pretty long piece and position it where you need it without having to fight with it at all.  Eliminating waste would likely offset any cost difference for this premium product.  It has comparable strength to strapping tape without the annoying filaments that make strapping tape impossible to cut off the roll with your teeth.  I consider this a huge plus! These are, essentially, sheets of post-it notes on pads you can feed into a printer.They work like post its, with a strip of adhesive on the top of each label.Believe it or not, but I am impressed with such a simple sounding product. I like this Epson Labelworks Label Printer over my existing Brother p-Touch for the following reasons :- the unit is more compact than the P-touch and is easier to hold- much less wasted label due to the smaller margins- features rich functions (14 fonts, 8 styles, symbols, accent marks, mirrored text, vertical text, frames, index tab, and barcode printing)- huge variety of labels available. The Epson Workforce 320 All-in-One inkjet is a solid performer at a very nice price.  This is the first all-in-one I have used and, although there are compromises, it performs very well.The printer is noisy and slower than dedicated color inkjets (my cannon pixma ip4500 is much faster, quieter and also uses seperate ink tanks). However, print quality is very good for text and good for photos.  The scanner works well with the included software, the software can scan and convert a document into an editable Word document - very cool.  It scans in color making photo scanning a cinch, can auto feed up to 30 sheets and is quick at lower (but good) resolutions.  It is very fast for B&W; text scanning.  The copier works well, is fast with B&W; text with up to 30 page auto feed.  I didn't test the fax because I don't use a fax much, if at all.  I usually email documents instead of faxing.Installation was easy, just follow the quick guide included with the printer.  The cost to print is probably in line with other major printers (according to consumer reports, most color inkjet printers cost .35 cents to .50 cents to print a color photo (depending no size) and .03 cents to .06 cents to print a page of text.The biggest plus to this printer is the low price.  It is not designed for a high volume office environment but is a very good consideration for home and small office use.  The box does not include a usb printer cable but not many printers do.  Manufacturers keep the cost lower by not including it and assuming most people already have a cable.There are better all-in-one printers but they are at least twice as expensive.  If you don't need a fast all-in-one for a high volume office environment then this Epson will fit the bill.Note: The scanner is fixed focus which is not an issue if all scanning is for documents and photos.  Epson offers some 3 in 1 printers with variable focus scanning.

I am writing this review using anApple Thunderbolt Displayon sitting on this Fellowes Monitor Lift. This is 27" display that measures 26x20" and weighs 24 lbs on my digital scale. I like the additional height provided by the lift, and especially like that it has created a place for my tablet and wireless keyboard underneath the display. The small display base fits easily on top of the lift, with room on either side for pens and post-its, etc.However, as I sit here and type these words, the monitor is wobbling slightly. Evidently, my keystrokes are shaking the oak dining table that I use for a desk, and these vibrations are in turn passed through the lift to the monitor. When I remove the monitor from the lift and place it directly on the table, the monitor does not wobble, so the effect is amplified by the construction of the lift. Prior to this machine I had three Canon All-in-Ones: a Pixma MP610, a Pixma MP560 (the only one with a footprint small enough to fit on the corner of my desk), and a Pixma MP640R.  Although the latter machine is still scarcely a year old, I've never gotten more than a couple of years' use out of any printer regardless of brand.  In fact, I was hoping that the move to the more pedestrian, "office-like" MX series would not only assure me of typical Canon quality (unsurpassed, in my experience) but give me a printer I could rely upon for longer than the usual two years.Somewhat to my surprise, the MX512 comes with more bells and whistles than the MP640R that it's now ready to replace. There have been times when I've missed the FAX machine of my old HP Multi-Function, and the MX512 has one.  It also comes with extras such as high definition printing of images from digital movies and the ability to print wirelessly from an Apple mobile device through "Air Play."What I hadn't factored into my decision to move to the MX series is the difference between a 5-cartridge MP machine and a 2-cartridge MX one.  The sharpness of the print and the resolution of the colors of the MX512 approach my MP640R only when I print in "fine" rather than "fast print" mode.  By doing so, the machine slows down considerably, especially compared to the MP640, which is definitely more speedy.  Also, while some users will undoubtedly welcome a two-cartridge system, I've got it down to a system where the 5-cartridge set-up is both economical and efficient, while delivering blacker blacks and more vibrant reds, blues and yellows than could any two-cartridge machine.  On a positive note, the MX512 operates more quietly and smoothly than the MP640, which tends to swing its supporting table wildly from one side to the other.The wireless feature can be a bit misleading.  Since my wife's MP610 is connected to our "access point," which is an Airport router connected to the cable from Time-Warner, hers is the machine that shows up on the MX512's printer menu.  It does appear to have greater sensitivity than my MP640R for wireless use, but rather than string an ethernet cable across the hallway or invest in another "access point" ("Look, mom! I'm printing wirelessly!"), I've decided it makes more sense to use an old fashioned, ultra-dependable "wired" connection via a USB cable, whether I'm using the MP640 or MX512.For the present the MX512 has not impressed me enough to swap out my still fresh and ready MP640 in favor of the more stable, full-featured,  professional-looking newcomer. In fact, the MX512 is currently standing in the wings,  temporarily demoted to the role of an understudy while I devote more than my usual amount of attention to the health of my Canon MP640R with its Apple-red sexy body.[Re: complaints about the instructions.  It's true the included hard-copy documentation is scarce and potentially confusing. But the on-screen instructions are thorough and clear. Moreover, the machine itself offers step-by-step instructions in its illuminated window.]My summary of Canon Pixma MX12:Pros:1. Duplex printing2. Versatility--at least 2 wireless printing methods plus scanner, OCR, FAX, auto-fix for photos3. Convenience--only 2 cartridges to replace4. Quiet and stable (little shake during operation; suppressed noise)5. Top-side auto document feederCons:1. Resolution--half that of Canon's MP series' 5-cartridge machines2. Speed--slow, unless "fast print" is selected with a loss in sharpness and resolution3. Economy--the 2-cartridge system is definitely less economical than Canon's 5-cartridge machines4. Size--slightly larger than MP series (enough to require a separate table in place of a desktop corner)5. Machine has "identity crisis": too pedestrian for hobbyists; too lightweight for the workplace.MX512 vs. MX522: I've read several reviews by "professionals" comparing the 2 machines.  Conclusion: They look and function identically, with comparable ink expense.  The newer machine is 3" less deep but 2" wider.  The newer machine has provisions for printing from Google Cloud but has eliminated all of the 512's reader-card ports. Unless you have a space that works only with a machine of shallower dimensions, I'd let price alone determine which of the two machines to buy.

This is a good printer - it produces quality pages, fast, and it was easy to set up with my network.  I never thought an inkjet could replace my laser printer, but this one just did.  (Granted, my old printer was an 11-year old Samsung ML-1430 which was totally incompatible with printing by WIFi; besides, said printer's ink cartridge was about to run dry and I was reluctant to shell out $80 for a new one.)That being said, I have three gripes with this product, of increasing severity.1) The nitpicky:  the instructions say that when you install the ink cartridge, you have to push down until it clicks.  Well, it really has to click - in my first attempt at setting the printer up, I thought it had clicked but I didn't push hard enough, and the printer went on priming forever without telling me that there was just no cartridge installed properly.  Just remember to push firmer than you might think you need to.2)  The obnoxious:  the starter ink cartridge is apparently just that, with only enough ink for 200 pages of normal use.  Of course Epson sells a2400 page "XL" cartridge, but that'll set you back $50.  Come on, Epson, don't be so cheap.  Just price the printer a little higher and include the XL cartridge.  This by itself would have made me rate this with four stars, but then there's . . .3)  The seriously bad:  this is the second Epson printer I've installed on OSX where I couldn't get it to work without going to their support website first, the other being theXP-400whose installation CD lacked a Mountain Lion compatible driver.  And this one was a real honest to God pain in the tush because the installation kept failing until, as per the not-so-easy-to-find instructions on Epson's site, I reset my printer preferences and printer list altogether.  In other words, I frankly don't know how anyone without at least moderate tech savvy could have succeeded in installing this on OSX without either calling Epson support or throwing their hands up in angry despair.  GET YOUR ACT TOGETHER, EPSON - THIS IS A SERIOUSLY BAD TREND.  There is no excuse in this day and age for allowing home printer installations to be anything but brainless.  None.  And this is why I'm only giving this product three stars.  For what it's worth, this printer doesn't do AirPlay either.There you have it.  I like this thing now that I've installed it, but I wish I hadn't gone through the aggravation.  It's a shame too, because Epson really should not be driving willing consumers away from an otherwise great product.I hope this is informative - and please, if you're an OSX user having trouble with your install, feel free to send me a message and I'll try to help.

I know almost nothing about electronics, just enough to press the button to Copy, Scan, and Print (I haven't used the Fax yet). I'm very pleased with the HP Officejet 6500A Plus.  It's my first all-in-one and it's a great to be able to make a copy of something without running to the store.That said, it does make an awful lot of clunk-bang-thwap noise everytime it's turned on and when it does a job.  I don't know if this is common to all such printers, but it seems like a real design flaw, so I deducted one star for that.The machine isn't intimidating for a beginner; it's easy to use and a snap to put in new ink cartridges.  Overall, I'm glad I bought it.

I used the Scotch Pouches in my Scotch brand laminator and it made a perfect cover. The 3 mil plastic is thick enough to be firm but flexible. I am very pleased with the results. I like that the top of the pouch is sealed already and all I have to do is position the sides evenly and then feed it into the laminator.
A great organizational product from a great company!  My desk if full of Avery products, which makes my life a lot more organized!

This are not your normal sticky notes. The colors are bright and vivid, making it easy to see the label. The nifty perforated tab makes it easy to apply, and then remove so that the label remains stuck where you stick it. They're a bit thicker than regular sticky notes and the all-over sticky makes them less likely to catch on something and be torn off. They all peel all and re-stick easily, which is great if you need to upsize or downsize a container where those items are stored. This is a nice, versatile product.

The foam wrist rest is great on my wrist.  However, I was not prepared for the smell.  It has a really strong chemical scent that was not pleasant.  If you can get past the smell...you will enjoy the foam comfort.

I have these Avery sticky notes in several spots around the house and I use them all the time.I used to carry these around in my briefcase and duffel bag as well,but it was kind of a drag offering the info I needed to pass along to someone with the sticky section as well,but No Longer!I now carry the Avery perforated Sticky Notes,which I can use with the sticky area when I need them and tear-off from the adhesive section if I just want the note pad to pass my info along.I've used a lot of these over the years and I've noticed that the Avery ones are by far the best.

I had no difficulties running these through our Canon inket printer, and the labels look really nice when you print them.  I picked the gold color to use with our holiday cards for this year, and they look classy and elegant.That being said, it was a pain to deal with the template!  My version of MS Word didn't have the label number built into it as a template, so I had to go to Avery's website to download it.  From there, I tried copying and pasting the addresses I had typed into an old label template into this new one, and it got really wonky on me.  I've done the same thing many times before with other template numbers, so I'm not sure why this one was so screwy. I ended up up just re-typing all my addresses in, and then it was fine, but I wish it had been easier.Overall, this stick well and look nice!

Overall, this is a simple and basic folder with alphabetic (or whatever method you want) organization. The folder is nicely compact and should easily hold 100 to 200 sheets of paper. Anything above that - it will hold, but the material that it is made of is relatively light weight. This does make it easier to carry and doesn't add bulk to your pack or briefcase. But it does seem a little less robust. All of this depends on the amount of use and how long you normally have these types of goods anyway. No matter how often I use these organizers, I always seem to need a new one every coupe of years. No matter how bullet proof they are ...So in that case, it is good and should easily last ....Bottom line: nice compact design, light weight, good holding with fastener, should hold an adequate number of pages, don't expect bullet proof construction.

My son has Asperger's syndrome, and he can't stand writing with pencils. He says the sound a pencil makes on paper, plus the scratchy way it feels on his hand, is "horrible".  Problem is, in school they want kids to write in pencil, esp. in Algebra, as they can erase their work rather than scratch it through with a pen.  Enter this pen!  Problem solved!  He can focus on the problem at hand rather than the sensory issues, and the teacher gets a neat paper.The pen writes so smoothly, it feels "silky" according to my son.  And the eraser is a bit of plastic, not rubber that will wear away.  Rub gently on your writing, and it disappears!!  No sensory issues for the erasing, either.Now if the geniuses at Pilot could just find a way to make these as affordable as pencils.....

This perfect organizer is just the right size to hold many different items. I was pleased to find that I could store business size envelopes in the front right pocket, cell phone/pens/calculator in the left and Ipad safely tucked away in the back storage spot with bills, notepads, etc. It is very sturdily made and did not tip over despite the numerous items I filled it with. The pockets are deep enough and wide enough to accept just about anything you'd want to store.I love the professional "look" of leather and neutral colors certainly go with everything - making this pleather organizer a plus in my book. Further, it's open design allows for a quick reach of everything I need for my workspace. Definitely a smart purchase.

This marker set has fun, bright colors (although the yellow one is of limited use on a white board).  They have magnets in the cap, which makes them handy for white boards without a pen tray.  They have little erasers on the cap, which is convenient for making a small correction.  For erasing the whole board, you're still going to want a separate, full-size eraser.These don't seem quite as high quality as the office standards like Expo, but the little handy touches make them nice for home calendars, kids rooms, dorm rooms, etc.

This is a really cute and well-made pencil cup. Very strong magnets. It's intended for a school locker, and it would work great that way, but my favorite is on a dry-erase board.  You can leave it folded and it looks very nice on a desk or shelf . Unfold it and stick on a fridge, filing cabinet or anything that will hold a magnet. Very nice fabric cover.

The gimmickof this product is not the amount of sheets, that for sure, but the quality of each one of the 5 and their extra width. So, fon of wide issues, chapters or subjects, this proves perfect.Also, they are hard plastic thus providing excellent separation of subjects. Use with wide binders ideal.

Amazon is the place to get ink cartridges. It's inexpensive, easy, and the whole thing's a snap. The cartridge itself is very easy to install. If changing oil in your car was this easy, life would be almost perfect.

I did not notice that the size of this is 8.5" X 5.5".  This is for an organizer not a notebook.  And with organizers, they tend to have different perforations.  So I would check this out at Staples before buying to make sure that you can use it.Now that the warning has been stated, Avery makes fantastic products that are easy to use.  I have used a number of different products by Avery and their tab sheets for laser printers are user friendly (once you set it up in Word.)  These are no different.What also is great, if you make a mistake and apply the tab title, you can easily remove it.  That is if you discover it fairly quickly.  Because the other great thing about this system is after a few hours the lables really adhere to the page and are not easily removed.  With an organizer, this can be crucial with everyday use.

I love to print my recipes, but after a few uses they are stained.  I am a little messy when I cook... OK, but its fun.  I started printing my recipes on card stock so they will stand up as I cook.... NOW I am able to laminate them...  SO much better, afterwards I can just wipe down my recipes and store them away for the next time.  I am so happy!!!  I would recommend these. Jesus' Blessings and Peace
This support is great.  It keeps me from having discomfort with prolongedlaptop  use.  It is a replacement for the previous as it finally gave up aftermany  years and daily use.
It's just fine.  Shipped quickly, and works well.I really do love my Epson 'small-in-one' printer.  But I would always recommend the larger volume toner.

I've checked over some of the reviews that came before mine and there seems to be a lot of Love It or Hate It going on.  I'm somewhere in the middle, I guess.First up, I will be the first to admit that this *not* the Trapper Keeper from my youth. That was fabric glued to cardboard with the world's most annoying Velcro closure mechanism.  I don't know who all these folks are saying that Trapper Keepers were so much better back in the day, but man... I kind of hated mine.  It was damn near indestructible, and that's another reason I hated it: I couldn't break it to warrant getting a new one!  Ugly thing lasted for years...This one is clearly fabric over plastic and lacks the dozens of pouches, pockets, and compartments of the ye olde, dare I say, "proper" Trapper Keepers.  HOWEVER, since this is clearly labelled as a "binder" and *not* a "system" (like the old ones were) I have to disagree with the haters, and say that it lives up to its name.  It's just a binder, no pouches, no zippered pen & pencil pouches... simply: binder.That said, it does its job. It does come with dividers and will lie flat when opened.  I'm using mine to store sheet music.  The dividers are great for divvying up the music into my own personal categories.  At 1.5 inches for the ring size, it tucks easily in to a backpack/bookbag/messenger bag.  And because of the black fabric covering, it doesn't mess with the sundry cables and connectors I pack away, like a shiny plastic cover would. (Although, it does include a clear plastic sleeve on the outside so you can personalize it.)My only ding against this Trapper Keeper binder is the closure.  It mostly works, but it takes some fiddling to snap it shut sometimes. ...I don't need the annoyance.

This box contains 20 folders in 5 colors - Red, Green, Blue, Orange and Yellow. There are 4 of each color. These are Pendaflex folders and, believe it or not, they are made in the good old USA. I have not found a better folder than Pendaflex and these are the best I have seen. I have hundreds of folders that I use for my genealogy research. A few years ago I started replacing all other brands with Pendaflex. This box is a welcome addition and the colors are helpful in separating lineages.If you need hanging folders it pays to go for the best with Pendaflex.
I love how little this is. I only laminate about once a month and it works great gears up fast. But the vest is how little it is for storage.
We wanted to print to finish like what you would get from a school picture photographer and this was it.  Definitely not glossy, but one step above white paper matt finish.

This is a high quality and very comfortable task chair.The chair is easy to assemble and the directions were not needed. The upper chair assembly was in one piece. One simply has to pop the 5 wheels into the star shaped base, drop the pneumatic device in the center of the base and set the upper chair assembly down on the pneumatic device and you are done.The chair is very heavy, which speaks to its quality. The seat is very comfortable.  The arms are adjustable both in height and width. They do not, however, adjust in a roational manner. In other words the arms face straight forward and that is it.  The seat back is easily adjustable up and down and the lumbar support is extremely comforable. It immediately took pressure off my low back. The seat is adjustable up and down and can either rock or be locked flat.  The seat cannot be locked in any reclined position.  The tension for the resistance to rocking is easily set with the very large knob under the seat.I have now spent several 10-12 hour days in this chair and I find it very comfortable.  I am a larger person and find the seat width fine and have been easily able to adjust the chair to fit my ergonomics for long days at the computer.This chair is definitely worth the price and I am looking to purchase another for home use.

I'm constantly writing articles. These Avery NoteTabs are great for marking pages in books.  Nice and stiff, so they don't wimp out. Brightly colored, so you can spot them.  Also great that you can write a note on them and erase for reuse. So, for example, I might write something like Monks1 to indicate this marks the first of several quotes of Robert Monks. Very helpful, if you have a lot of references and can use a simple manual system, rather than scanning into a database.

I was excited to test out this docking station and had high hopes it would reduce the cord clutter from all my various rechargeable devices.  I have chargers for my phone, Zomm wireless leash, camera batteries, MP3 player and charger for standard AA/AAA batteries that are all currently jumbled in a basket.  I dumped out the basket and began to organize them into the cubbies of the Steelmaster docking station.  First problem-there were not enough cubbies for each device to have its own spot.  Second problem-the phone charger cord connection WOULD NOT FIT through any of the holes to feed it into a cubbie.  (As long as your connection is no wider than a USB port you will be OK but I'm out of luck.)  Third and here is the deal breaker- all this thing really accomplishes is keeping your devices somewhat separated and moving the clutter behind.  You still have a big tangled mess at the back since all the plugs and adapters basically have nowhere to go.  I've been told it is not good to leave any kind of charger plugged in when it is not charging something, so between uses they're all just laying back there.  If the bottom of it was open you could shove them all in there to be out of sight but the back of the drawer area is solid so as to provide a "secure locking charging spot".  This in itself is a joke because if someone wanted to steal anything, they could just walk off with the entire station and all its contents under their arm.Not only is the design flawed, but I would describe the workmanship of the station to be strong yet sloppy.  Mine has numerous blemishes at the seams. It doesn't sit level despite the little silicone feet that were included. The drawer slides awkwardly and has so much play from side to side you could easily pinch any cord fed through the back since the holes don't stay lined up if the drawer goes off to one side.  Look at the pictures I posted to see what I'm talking about.I suppose you could use this just to store your chargers and abandon the docking station aspect but then it becomes a bulky and really expensive desk organizer. If you wanted to design a docking station it should include a power strip in the bottom where each cord could stay plugged in from the inside, have a toggle switch on the outside to turn each outlet on or off as needed and have only one cord in view ever-where the power strip plugged into the wall. Oh and it should be made out of wood or plastic.  This thing sounds like a marching band drum line anytime I move the contents.I'm afraid all my chargers are going back in the basket. I'll have to use this as a cumbersome holder for pencils and Post-its instead.  Back to the drawing board, Steelmaster!

I've used a variety of label makers for decades, and this app-enabled product is the most convenient yet. I can keep it loaded with my default labels, and wherever I am around the house, I can pull out my iphone 5s, open the app, and print a label. Templates are good. Setup was simple and fast. Like with most printers, the long term cost may become evident when purchasing replacement labels.

This model is incredibly easy to use- I took it out of the box, plugged it in, turned it on and waited about 10 minutes for it to get hot, and then ran through my first paper (in a plastic pouch) to be laminated.  It was easy and I got perfect results (and a wonderfully laminated number for our school's pick-up lane).  The only downside to this machine that I saw was that it was easy to forget it was on, and the unit does get pretty hot.  There's no automatic shut-off after inactivity.  I love that this was so easy to use- I'm looking forward to using it for kids' projects and to save important papers.

I've been using these for awhile now, writing notes on my refrigerator whiteboard.  The colors are bright and they write smoothly and don't dry-up easily.  Some cheaper markers, the tip will tend to dry a bit as you're writing.  That hasn't happened with this set at all.  I also like the caps as they are flared out a bit so they are easily removed from the pen.  I've thought of gluing a small piece of felt on each one to act as an eraser.

Let's face it, there's not a lot that you can do to improve a file folder. What makes these folders different is the extra space in the tab area. You can add larger labels, enter more information, write in larger print, whatever.Otherwise, these are your basic folders. The box comes in four different colors. The folders are sturdy yet thin.Enough said.

I have used many printers in the past and I used to be a pro-Canon person. I was asked by a friend of mine to fine a nice affordable printer for him so I did research to find this printer to be the best option based on the feedback and functions. After I received the package, I went off to set it up for him, and found so easy to do! The wireless set up is flawless, unlike my Canon MP series printer, which I can't even connect to wifi. I connected to the wifi in a minute, and set up was done! It's a very compact size to have this many functions. I haven't used this yet it has not been a year yet,but a friend of mine has used his and I have printed things while over at his place and it works great

I might have preferred the colors to be more jewel toned, but these are files so probably won't be on display as much.  A bit pricey. I have been using a hand rest because my fingers and hand is getting numb from some much typing.  I like this one better than what I was using because the older one was just too high.  This is a vinyl type material and it has a kind of "bounce" to it so that thee is more flexibility at the wrist, and yet it cuts out the numbness by at least 80 percent.It is hooked into something that looks like a mouse pad which bugged me at first because i no longer use a mouse pad but i am now used to it. This is hands down the easiest printer I have ever set up. It was about 10 minutes from start to finish. No cd's or downloads from the internet. (That i could tell) I can print from my iphone too. Thats useful if theres a document id rather print than read on my phone. I'm not sure how useful that feature will be but maybe some people cary valuable docs with em on their iphone or iPad, but at any rate its an added feature that i had never been able to use before. It also crams a pretty good scanner in there too. All of this and like I said 10 minutes of setup. (I'm pretty sure the scanning feature downloaded drivers in the background.) My gf was able to print in a bout 2 minutes with her Mac Book too.It has a copy feature on there as well. Which brings me to the biggest downside. Ink prices. We burned through an ink cartridge pretty quick test printing photos. They came out gorgeous on photo paper, but on highest resolution we got maybe 50 full size images done before the ink started to go. And they run anywhere from $20-50Canon Office Products PG-240XL/CL-241XL/PP-201 - Combo Pack InkSo i dont think it would be very effective to use as a copy machine. Also double check the dimensions.All in all Its one of the easiest, best looking printers ive used both in terms in looks and results, with the same downside as just about any inkjet printer. I know many people who keep track of their budgeting and expenses using computer software designed for that purpose.  I'm kind of primitive, so keeping some budgeting program on a computer makes me uneasy.  I want to be able to put my hands on my information.  That's why I really like this little binder.  I can put all my receipts in a monthly folder, write down my expenses and budget, and keep it all physically in one place where I can lay my hands on it.  This organizer is perfect for the job. All in all, I'm very happy with this expense binder.

This is a very nice office printer at a good price and with the useful capability of making larger sized output. 8.5x11 prints really do not stand out these days, so being able to go to 11x17 is a big plus. I wasn't able to get the magic "Push WPS butttons on the printer and your router" method to work, but once I plugged my laptop in via USB it went through and set everything up correctly for network access after that. With my Epson C60 (and still working perfectly) I was seeking any printer that does what my Epson C60 does.  That is print a single business size envelope without having to take the paper out of feed tray.  This printer does exactly that.  First I contacted Epson USA and asked if Epson sells any printer that does what my Epson C60 does.  That is print a single business envelope without having to take the paper out place envelope into feeder and slide tabs to edge of single envelope.  Epson USA stated to me that no printer that they have currently does this.  None.  Then I contacted HP USA and spoke with a customer service person and that person put me on hold then came back and stated that no HP printer does what I am asking. I repeated multiple times what I was seeking in a printer.  No HP printer does this I was told.  It just so happens that I mentioned these conversations with neighbors and one neighbor stated that his HP J4680 does exactly what I was seeking.  So, after speaking with HP customer service, and HP telling me they do not sell any printer that does what I am seeking I went to neighbors house and viewed his printer - to see if what I was stating was in fact true.  And low and  behold he printed a single business envelope on the HP J4680 and he did not have to take the paper out, place envelope in tray and then slide tabs to edges of envelope.  Apparently HP Customer Service knows squat about what any of the HP printers can and cannot do.  And that may or many not be true for Epson USA.  Anyway I now have a new printer that does exactly what I want. I can print a business size envelope without having to move any tabs or take the paper out of the tray. With this HP printer just place the envelope to the right and make sure you have correct side up and it feeds perfectly with paper still in tray.I have read all of these reviews.  I have Windows 7.  In the HP J4680 box is a CD software disk for Windows 7.  I installed software using the supplied disk with zero issues.  The printer operates flawlessly.  I do not use any wireless so I don't know any issues with that.  This printer has a small LCD screen that for some may be hard to read.  I had to use a flashlight and a magnifying glass to read the LCD screen.  A bigger color screen would be much better.  Some of you younger folks may have no issues reading the LCD screen.  I hooked up the fax and you MUST use the supplied phone cable/wire for the fax to operate.HP does supply a lot of software for this printer.  Some of it I like.  Others call this bloatware.  But you can turn off this extra software or bloatware.  Or as one above/below states just go to HP web site and download drivers if that is all you want.This printer is slower than my Epson C60 but not by much.  This printer is a small form factor printer and fits exactly on the footprint of my Epson C60.  I did not want a huge printer.  This is a small printer and exactly what fits my needs.  There is also a scanner with this prnter.  This is a two ink printer and the inks are not that expensive.  Some state that 3 inks is better and some printers come with 6 ink cartridges.  I have a larger Epson Workforce 500 with my other computer and that takes 6 inks.  I don't care how many ink cartridges you have but my colors all seem to need replacement near the same time.  So whether I have 5 colors or 1 color - they all seem to need replacement at the same time.  My Epson C60 fed paper from rear and printed paper came out front.  This printer feeds paper from front and printed paper also comes out front.  This may or may not bother some.I am not an office.  This printer is for personal use.  If you are a business then maybe other printers will meet your needs better.  For me this printer is an excellent choice for what I do.I would have preferred an Epson as I have had 8 years with the C60 with no issues.  Epson was good in that they provided drivers for Windows Vista and Windows 7 with the Epson C60.  I am a loyal Epson consumer but here I am now with my first HP printer.

****I rate this at five stars for the following reasons.  The Westcott TrimAir Guillotine Wood Trimmer with Microban Protection does what it says, it whacks through 31 sheets of 20-pound copy paper when operated pretty enthusiastically, it makes a clean, straight cut under a more normal load, and the ruler along the top is accurate if not as helpful if you prefer metric measurements to Imperial, which we all in this otherwise great country of the United States of America should join you in doing.Also, although I do not subtract any starts for this, the product under review is lighter in mass than paper trimmers I've used in the past, which means sometimes you have to use your non-guillotine hand to stop the whole thing from sliding around on the table a little more than I expected.  One obvious option to solve this problem permanently is to drive some long deck screws through the top of the product and into the top of the table or desk where you want it (remembering to countersink, of course).  Another option is to place under the product a sheet of something that's the opposite of Teflon, something that increases the coefficient of friction between the table top and the sheet and between the sheet and the product's feet.  I can't remember any names for this stuff, sorry.  It's sold as shelf liner, if that helps, and if you know what I'm talking about and know the generic name for it, you can let the rest of the world know by leaving a comment, and then I'll edit this review, and give you credit if you want, and thanks.****But I do subtract a star for the inanity of the Microban Protection feature, which I can only assume is a marketing gimmick some customers might be attracted to, that might sway some towards this product and away from a competing one.  Presumably this feature added to production costs, and presumably it added to the price.The Amazon description page says, "Handle infused with Microban protection to inhibit the growth of bacterial odors."  Since when, no matter what "Microban" means, do we need the handle of a paper trimmer to be rendered less bacterially noisome?  Not fewer bacteria, mind you, just less odor therefrom.Are there all sorts of bacterial stenches on handles out there I keep missing?  Are lots of other people going around all the time sniffing various handles and I just never noticed?  Should I start?  Should Microban be infused into many more handles in the world?My answer -- and no doubt yours -- to all of the above is No.  The Microban feature is just silly, and the manufacturer should be punished for that by a whole entire star.****What the manufacturer and its marketing department should not be punished or rewarded for is the performance of the Westcott TrimAir Guillotine Wood Trimmer with Microban Protection in off-label applications.  Here are a few I tried so you won't have to.-- It slices Genoa salami and dry pepperoni better than you might think.  It works well enough on saffron and your smaller white truffles and those stubborn hamster thighs.  I don't know whether the product is dishwasher safe even on the top rack, but once I do find out I'll update this review to let you know.-- It will not slice at all through many objects, including the International Space Station (too far away), the Grand Canyon (only air, if you think about it), the USS Nimitz aircraft carrier (more than 12 inches in every direction), and Superman's toenails (too strong).****

I think this product is a great idea. No waste because you can tear off just the right length each time. And you can reuse the strips a couple of times. The adhesive is strong. The only thing I don't like about the way it's dispensed is that you can't write on it until after you tear off the strip. That's fine if you are using it on a horizontal surface or an object you can pick up or manipulate. But if it a vertical surface that you can't reach easily to write on after you stick the label, it's harder to use. Love the bright green color and there is a lot of length on this roll too. This is definitely a product I will buy.

The basic concept of this envelope is that you fold up a little flap to reveal the glue before closing the envelope rather than peeling off a little strip of paper.  The little strip is easier.  This type is a bit awkward since you need to hold up the bottom flap with one hand as you fold down the top flap with the other.  It gets the job done, but I'm not sure of the point.  The little flap surely has has much paper as the strip you throw away so I don't think there's an environmental argument.  One advantage that I have found is that these seem to bunch up less frequently in my printer than the strip type envelopes so if you're printing return addresses that could be a feature.  The security print also works well.  This isn't see-through.

Received this chair really fast because I had the Amazon Prime.  Set-up was a breeze.  Took me no longer than 10 minutes to put together.  I didn't need to look at instructions because this is not my first time putting together a chair.  Pretty straightforward setup.First impressions were not very favorable.  One thing I will give the chair is that the fit and finish is phenomenal.  I mean, Audi-like.  Everything fit perfectly and it's spot-on level and balanced.  In other words, all angles are 90 degree with no visible crookedness.  It really is a gorgeous looking chair.  It looks even better in person than in the pictures.  Now, the bad stuff.  This is NOT leather.  You can spot the fakeness a mile away.  The chair smelled horrible and sitting on it for 5 minutes, I got a really bad headache from the fumes.  It's definitely toxic and bad for your health.  Also, the chair was rock hard!  I read all the reviews and there was only one person who commented on how hard the chair is.  Therefore, I was not prepared for it the first time I sat on it.  I have a very big butt.  The staff that work for me call me "Rob Kardashian."  Ten minutes sitting in this chair and my butt was numb.  I admit, the first few days, I HATED this chair.  I even went so far as to get a return authorization from Amazon.  Amazon, btw, has the best customer service I have ever encountered anywhere.It's been about a week now with this chair.  The fumes are finally starting to dissipate.  There is still a smell, but it's faint, and I'm waiting for it to completely disappear.  The chair is softening up a bit. The Epson WorkForce 545 Color Inkjet Wireless All-In-One Printer and Copier with Fax is a great printer in a very affordable package. It has all the bells and whistles you could possibly want in a printer where it prints, copies, faxes and scans in one convenient configuration. Plus it is wireless so you can configure it in your home or office network. The WorkForce series in the Epson line of printers are primarily geared for business but works great for home use too, as in my case. Note that the WorkForce 545 is much bigger and bulkier than conventional home printers. Since this was meant for business, the configuration was made to accomodate the demanding needs of the workplace.Out of the box, the printer is attractive and easy to handle. It can be held by its side to be placed on your desired location. Although big, it is not so much heavy. The WorkForce 545 comes with everything (but not the USB cable) to get you started: 4 different colored high capacity ink cartridges, the instruction manual, CD-ROM drivers/software, phone cord (for faxing) and the power cable. This printer is also ENERGY STAR qualified, meaning it is an electrical equipment that meets energy efficiency standards set by the federal government.Setting it up poses no problem. I already have a wireless network at home so this is my default connection. Initial set up though requires you to connect the printer to your pc via USB to "configure" the printer so that your network will recognize the printer. It is smooth sailing from then on.The quality and speed of prints you get from the WorkForce 545 is simply amazing. At the indicated speeds of 15 ppm for black and 7 ppm for colored, this is one fast printer that will certainly meet your demanding business needs. I tried printing several pages of a PDF file and it was done in less than 3 minutes. It has a 2.5-inch colored LCD screen telling you the status of printing. It also serves as a monitor when you are trying to print pictures from your memory card. It handles a variety of flash media that are widely used today by different electronic brands and equipment. You are pretty much covered whether it is SDHC, xD, compact flash or memory stick. With adapters, can even handle a micro-SD.This is a great overall printer that is more than capable of meeting your expectations without spending a hefty sum. Very highly recommeded!

Well, the other guys are all complaining about Amazon's shipping charge.  Amazon's "free shipping for over $25" offer comes and goes, so if you see it in effect -- it is as of today (10/12/2005) -- grab whatever you need.  As for buying the ink tanks, just buy all three colors in the set at the same time to qualify.Anyway, let me talk about the ink tanks themselves.  The three "BCI-6" ink tanks work in the Canon Pixma iP3000 printer.  (Maybe in other models as well, but I have the iP3000.)  These are official Canon ink tanks so you'll know they'll work well.  The number of prints you get heavily depends on your printing habit, e.g., what you print, how much you print, and at what quality you print.Using my usage as an example.  I print at Normal Quality most of the time, and I print about 50% photos (at 200 or 300 dpi, depending on needs) and 50% web pages (e.g., flight confirmations, Hotmail messages, etc.).  I don't print Word text documents much.  I've run through 2 sets of ink tanks, and my very rough estimate is each set has lasted about 250-300 8.5"x11" sheets.  Maybe more, but I don't wish to raise your expectations too much.  Suffice it to say that of all the inkjet printers I've owned -- photo or not -- the iP3000 has a terrific ink capacity record.  Of course, if you use one color more than the others, that particular ink tank (or ink tank combinations) will go out faster.(For your reference, a few months ago I read in a magazine review the the average per letter-size print cost of the iP3000 came out to around 12 cents per page on plain paper, one of the lowest average costs for inkjets.  Not sure what settings they used in their tests or how much they paid for ink tanks, though.)In case you are interested... the new Canon iP4200 model employs a new formula of ink which supposedly will not fade for at least 30 years.  My own take is, no matter how you print your photos -- even at professional photo labs -- a photo print will eventually fade if exposed to light.  It's just a simple law of chemistry.  So be sure to archive your digital photos on CDs or DVDs so 30 or 40 years from now, you can still print fresh copies and relive your treasured memories in their full colors.

3M's Post-It line is famous for their sticky notes.  In recent years they have been extending out a bit more -- they now have Post-It computer software so you can make quick notes on your desktop, and now printable labels.For the most part, when I think of printable labels, I immediately think of the Avery brand.  They have been the dominant brand in this market for years.  Avery has all their templates in Microsoft Word which usually makes it the most convenient choice. Just like the product name indicates, the labels are sticky and removable.  Traditional labels can lose its adhesiveness after moving it around a few times, or paper rips... The adhesiveness on these labels seemed to remain intact, and like Post-It notes, does not cause rips on the paper that its stuck to.Setting the labels up for printing was simple.  Within the package, theres a set of instructions on setting it up for Microsoft Word.  There are two options:OPTION A: Visit Post-It's website at [...] where you can find and download templates that match the labels.OPTION B: Use existing templates in Microsoft Word.  Search for the template ID that is located on the label itself.I tried Option B first.  On Word 2003, I could not locate any 3M or Post-It templates.  However, on the packaging, it indicated that these 2100-H labels would be compatible with Avery 5366 templates, which I found easily.  Locating the correct template on 3M's website was as simple as inputting 2100-H into the search box.I printed these labels using my laser printer -- the output turned out perfectly.Pros:- Removable!  I used to use permanent labels on my file folders... Problem is that if I want to reuse it, the label rips the folder.  Though I could easily place this label over the existing label, or on the ripped folder, I can get OCD at times.  If these labels remain removable after a lengthy period of time, I would be completely sold on these labels!- Compatible with inkjet and laser- Easy to locate templatesCons:- Not free- Once you start labeling, you may not want to stop.One remaining question is whether it will remain adhesive/removable over time.  I haven't found any information on that so I suppose only time will tell!

இ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:ѾѾѾѾѾ Highly recommended with warm fuzzies!This is my first home-laminating experience, and I am thoroughly pleased with how easy and trouble-free this process is and how nice the results are.  This H320 model has settings for using pouches of 3 mil, 4 mil, and 5 mil thickness, with either cold lamination or hot lamination.  For the past few months, all of my experiences with this laminator have been with hot lamination using both GBC HeatSeal Laminating Pouches and also 4 packages ofScotch(TM) Thermal Laminating Pouches, 9 Inches x 11.4 Inches, 50 Pouches (TP3854-50).  Both the GBC and Scotch pouches give equally good results, so you can use them interchangeably.  This laminator lives up to its "QuickStart" name.  From the moment that I plug it in and push the [Power] and [3 Mil] buttons, it is ready for hot lamination within 50 seconds.Even though this laminator's 'Instruction Manual' says "Use the unit only for its intended purpose of laminating documents", I have successfully used this to laminate not only documents, cooking recipes, photos, and other keepsakes, but during the past two months, I have laminated more than 150 sheets of pressed-and-dried autumn leaves that have been collected over the past few years.  The autumn leaves of maples, oaks, aspen, sumacs, and smoke trees are now preserved and protected with this lamination.With another autumn season coming up, here is how you can use this laminator to preserve beautiful autumn foliage:1) First, as soon as you collect the leaves, press and dry them.  I sandwich the leaves inside the pages of large phone books, lining both sides of each phone book "sandwich" with a paper towel.  Let the leaves thoroughly dry in this flattened state for at least several days.  I usually keep the leaves sandwiched undisturbed inside the phone books for a whole week before carefully taking them out.2) To laminate the pressed-and-dried leaves, I set up the laminator on a table or on the kitchen counter.  I stack some books, magazines, or phone books in front of the laminator to create a platform that is 1.9" to 2.0" high and then place an inverted baking/cookie pan on top of that stack.  The baking/cookie pan should be place right up against the laminator, and its surface should be aligned and level with the laminator's slot where the pouch is fed in.3) I place a new laminating pouch onto the cookie pan, with the folded sealed edge pointed toward the laminator's slot.  Since the pressed-and-dried leaves are very brittle, I carefully place leaves onto the back sheet of the pouch using one hand while holding up the top sheet of the pouch with the other hand, filling up the bottom side from the folded sealed edge first and working my way down.  As I fill up the sheet with leaves, I progressively lower the top sheet onto the leaves; this holds the leaves in their place.  I position the leaves so that there is 1/8" to 1/4" spacing between the leaves and a similar distance away from the edge of the laminating pouch.  Also, try to place the leaves so that each leaf is pointed towards the folded sealed edge and each leaf's petiole (leaf stem) enters into the laminator AFTER most of the main leaf has already entered into the laminator's rollers.  The reason for not having the leaf petiole enter the laminator first is that if you have a large leaf with a thicker petiole, when it hits the laminator's rollers first, the rollers may push back on the leaf petiole, nudging and moving the leaf inside the laminating pouch.  But if most of the leaf has already been rolled through the laminator before the rollers go over the petiole, this does not shift the position of the leaf inside the pouch.  If a leaf has a really thick petiole (e.g. a large maple leaf), you should cut some of that thick portion out before placing the leaf on the laminating pouch.4) After the laminating pouch has been filled up with pressed-and-dried leaves, I CAREFULLY slide the pouch along the surface of the cookie pan into the laminator's slot.  I do not lift the laminating pouch up to insert it into the slot or else the leaves inside the pouch will move around or fall out.  Once I have slid the laminating pouch into the laminator's slot, the rollers will start pulling the pouch in.  As the pouch is going into the laminator, I use my fingertips to lightly press down on the areas of the pouch that are just about to go into the rollers in order to hold the leaves in place and prevent the possibility of any leaves shifting or getting nudged inside the pouch.  I continue pressing onto areas of the pouch until the last one or two inches of the pouch are about to go through the laminator's rollers.  Even though I have not tried laminating pressed-and-dried flowers, you could probably also do that as long as the flowers are not too thick.For both laminating documents and leaves, I find that there are a few things that I can do to minimize the possibility of ending up with wrinkled, buckled, or bent laminations.  First, I minimize how much the laminated pouch has to curve downward when it exits the rear slot by stacking a book or phone book behind the laminator to about 1.5" height.  So as the laminated pouch exits the rear of the laminator, it stays relatively flat instead of curving downward onto the table or countertop.  Most importantly, as soon as the sheet has completely come out of the rollers, I IMMEDIATELY place it on a flat surface.  I then also place a clean cookie pan on top of the still-very-warm laminated sheet and I place about a one-pound weight (e.g. soup can) on top of the cookie pan to keep the sheet flat as it cools.  I find that the laminated sheet is most prone to bending, wrinkling, warping, buckling, and curling when it is freshly laminated and still very warm.  So it helps to immediately place the warm sheet on a flat surface and keep it flattened with something placed on top of it while it cools.The laminator comes with a "Laminator Cleaning Sheet" which you are supposed to use after each series of laminations to clean the laminator rollers and remove any excess adhesive that may have exited the pouch onto the rollers while laminating.  I have not used the 'Laminator Cleaning Sheet' yet, but I have gone through two boxes of GBC 50-count 3-mil 9x11.5" laminating pouches and four boxes of Scotch 50-count 3-mil 9x11.5" laminating pouches (Amazon had a cheaper price on them at the time :-) so far, and not once have I encountered a jam where I had to use this laminator's "Jam-Free" feature that would have let me simply pull the jammed pouch back out of the laminator.

Summary: Overall I'm pleased with this printer. It was simple to set up, simple to install, and it works well. That's not always the case with printers these days (especially in terms of the installation when you have multiple operating systems) so Epson deserves kudos for that. My quibbles are: it lacks a couple of convenience features (especially wireless networking); and the print quality, while good, is not stellar.Review: I've used Epson printers in the past and have always been satisfied with the initial setup. No exception with this printer. While it's large (as you would expect given that it is a wide format printer) it is easy to work with right out of the box. It's packed well, with lots of easy-to-remove tape holding the parts together for transit. There's a clear "getting started" sheet that walks you through the setup steps. The only issue I encountered during setup was that it took what I felt was a long while to prime after inserting the print cartridges. Everything worked fine, but the time it spent chugging along to complete that task made me concerned that something was wrong.The build quality is decent - everything feels substantial and certainly appropriate for the price point. No problems running the software on Win 7 32-bit, Win 7 64-bit and Win 98 machines.The print quality is good. It is not high-end, but it makes the most out of the 4 print cartridges. I would not consider this to be professional quality, but perfectly fine for home or small office use, general snap shots, and the like. Speedy printing and quiet operation. No paper jamming or feeding problems even though I ran several sheets of paper that were damaged/crumpled on the edges for my initial test prints. That was impressive.The downside of this printer is the lack of some convenience features. I also have an Epson Artisan, and love the LCD screen. Really missed having that on this printer. I also missed having wireless networking capability, especially since this has such a large footprint. My router is in the living room, and running a cable to it was a problem, both in terms of the cable itself, as well as having to have such as large printer in the living room. Although I hooked it up to see how it worked (no problems), this printer will not be networked since there is no room for it in the living room. It's going to be hooked up to just one PC in the rec room. It seems really odd to me that wireless networking was not included - it's so common these days to have it.With the exception of the two issues listed above, I'm satisfied with this printer. It should definitely be on your short list if you're looking for a wide format printer that won't break the bank. Just remember that it will need to be hardwired into your router if you want to network it, so check the size (especially the width) to make sure you have room for it.
