I had have never laminated before, but went from set-up to a completed, laminated document in minutes.Set-up is basically unboxing and plugging it in. The laminator comes with a few laminating pouches in a few different sizes. If you already have a project, buy your needed size when you order this. You select a "cold" or "thermal" laminating option. If you go cold, it is immediately ready. If you want hot/thermal, the unit takes a few minutes to get ready. You then select between 3 mm or 5 mm. The instructions here could have been a bit more explanatory, like the difference between "cold" versus "thermal/hot", when you choose one over the other, and what the difference is between 3 mm and 5 mm. But, even without such an explanation, I was able to laminate a two-sided recipe document as easy as pie. (pun intended)This is a really affordable laminator. I always assumed laminating at home would me more expensive. The only downside? I can already think of dozens of things I would like to laminate! (kid's artwork, achievements, etc.)Nice, easy to use laminator if you have a need.

The Westcott iPoint Evolution electric pencil sharpener works well. It has a sleek design and doesn't take up much space. It sharpens pencils quickly and quietly.  I did not have to keep checking to see if the pencil had a point. The sharpener automatically stops on its own. My only sticking point is that it has to be emptied more frequently than a standard pencil sharpener. (I tried using it in my classroom.) It is better suited for personal use. I give it 4.5 stars.  I highly recommend it.

My son has had binders fail on him within a week.  Dollar store binders and Walmart quality are not for him.  I bought him this Avery binder.  He throws everything in it, lugs it all over the place.  It gets heavy usage.  Seven months later, it's still in one piece.  There are no tears and the rings are still aligned.  He gives it a thumbs up.

These black ink pens are terrific: fine point, smooth but not runny. They have a comfortable feel to them and I love that they're waterproof.  I did a small test with my watercolor paints to see if they could be used with pen & ink paintings and there was no smudging at all.The only suggestion would be to have some in more masculine colors.  My husband really liked the way they wrote but didn't care for the pastel colors.

QUICK SUMMARY:  This headset works well with my laptop computer.  While using Skype, the sound I heard was very clear, like the person was sitting next to me.  The other person reporting excellent sound, too -- much, much better than when I used my laptop's built-in microphone.  The fact that this set is foldable and more easily transported makes this a great headset to own.  Highly recommended!WHAT I LIKE:- Comfortable fit.  I didn't feel pressure on my head or ears after wearing them for a while.- The sound I heard was excellent for voice (I don't use headsets for music)- The sound captured by the microphone was excellent (as reported to the one who heard me speak)- Foldable design makes them easy to stow or transport- The microphone boom kept away from my mouth (other headsets I've owned tend to bump into my mouth)- Plug-n-play performance.  Windows 7 recognized it right away for me.  No drivers to install.Usually I can make a comment or two about what could be done to improve a product I review, even if there was nothing I particularly disliked about that product.  With this headset, nothing really comes to mind about what could be done to improve it.  A headset should be comfortable to wear, provide good sound through the earpieces, capture and deliver sound well through the boom microphone.  This headset does all of that.  As long as there isn't an issue with reliability, I have no qualms about recommending this Plantronics headset.

These moving boxes arrived just in time to pack up my 1 bedroom apartment.  They are the perfect size for pillows, clothing, bed sheets, towels and will accomodate loosely packed electronics or sports equipment.  The best part is that they don't need ANY tape, not even to seal the top.  Putting them together is extremely quick and easy - just follow the blue bubbles marked 1-4 on the panels to flip them down in the correct order.  The cardboard is sturdy and thick and you won't have to worry about the bottom falling out...unless you're filling it to the brim with heavy books maybe.  Of course, then you'd hardly be able to lift the box.  They do take up a little more space than most boxes of the same size when they first arrive unfolded, but are packed efficiently.EDIT:  I recently received a shipment of same-sized (though cheaper) boxes from Uhaul and they arrived in a simlarly huge box, but were of noticeably weaker construction.  Plus, you have to tape the bottoms of the Uhaul boxes very well in addition to putting tape on top to keep them closed.  These Fellowes boxes win out, despite the price, especially if you are planning to reuse them or move them around a lot.POST MOVE:  Having finally finished moving, I can say these boxes were easily worth the extra expense.  I loaded them with heavy pots and pans and though they sagged a  bit at the bottom, they held together.  I put a little tape on the bottom just for extra security on the heaviest two boxes, but I doubt it was needed.  It may not seem like a huge hassle to put together standard boxes and tape them up, but you'll appreciate skipping it.
Easy to use, inexpensive, and quickly received. As an artist, this comes in handy for more solid pencils that aren't hand chiseled with an exacto-knife.

My youngest child is 4 1/2 and in pre-K.  She's learning to write, but has had little to no interest in writing numbers.  I figured we'd give this book a try and see if she'd be game for learning to write her numbers.  Surprisingly, she loves this book.  She'll happily sit and listen to me read the cute playground themed rhymes that explain how your write the number correctly.  Some of the rhymes seem a little odd to me, but she enjoys them, and since she's the one learning to write her numbers, I'm not going to complain.I like that each number (from 0-9) has a page with four practice lines. Each line has ten spaces for practicing the number.  This is nice because most other books like this only have a few spaces for writing practice.  With four lines, your child can practice writing each number on four separate days.The math in this book goes from very simple counting exercises to basic addition and subtraction.  Several of the exercises involve cutting and pasting.  Adding tactile exercises like this is nice because it can make the math concepts easier to grasp for some children.  My daughter was very excited when she saw the pages with items to be cut out and went paging through the book to find the lesson the corresponded with it.My only gripe about this book pertain to the use of only one side of the paper for each page, which I think is wasteful.  It makes perfect sense to do this for the pages where you'll be cutting things out, but not for the rest of the book.  Other than that, I think it's a pretty good resource.

To be honest, I just like the tape. Unless the dispenser is bad, it is kind of just an invisible, not-thought-about item. In the case of this "designer dispenser" it works just as effectively as the old fashioned kind to hold, dispense and cut tape the way I expect it to and the color is kind of fun, so I'm in favor of it.

I've been a fan of these rollerballs for quite sometime. I like how comfortable they are to use - writing is smooth and flowing. I've not had one skip on me or drip or otherwise make a mess of what I'm writing. They are just easy to use and easy to write with for a long time. Unlike traditional ballpoints, as you're writing you don't feel any (significant) friction between the tip of the pen and the paper. It's more like gliding than writing.These new colors are wonderful. They're darker versions of the last round of colors: dark green, dark red, dark blue, dark purple and a chocolate brown (dark orange, I guess). I like wild colors, but sometimes feel like I should have some more "normal" colored pens. These are close enough. ;)The ink in these pens are dark enough for check writing, faxes, or other writing that will be copied or digitally transmitted. (I've had banks complain about lighter, crazier colors.)These pens are not inexpensive, but I find I don't lose them because I'm always using them.

I began using these pens over 20 years ago for home, and office. These pens were always packed in my canvas bag for work, as I needed them frequently for chart work, and outlining. They last a long time, and I never had a problem with them. I've used them for several jobs I worked through the years, and could always count on them.In addition, I like the 4 colors at my fingertips when needed to make life a little easier, instead of searching for different colored pens. Today, they are just as handy for my office, as they are for home needs when labeling.Since I've used them for several years, I depend on them. Good quality, fair price, and extremely useful. Highly recommended.

The Five Star Flex Hybrid 1" Notebinder is a very durable binder that has a 1-year replacement guarantee for everything except abuse. This binder has a 200 sheet capacity and comes with 5 smoke-colored tabbed dividers (3 sleeves and 2 folder-types with pockets), 60 sheets of college ruled paper, and 20 sheets of grid paper.One of the things that I really like about this binder is the flex rings and the ability to fold over the cover like a traditional notebook. It truly makes this binder easier to use. The flex rings take a little getting used to if you haven't used them before, and it's note as quick as a traditional binder to add (or take out) paper as you need to open each ring individually.Overall, this is one of my favorite binders due to the durability and unique hybrid approach that combines a binder and notebook into one. If you prefer to customize your binder cover, this binder is also available with a customizable cover option.

It appears that Amazon has resolved the problem of some companies shipping this product without placing it in a separate container (as reported in some earlier reviews). The "Quickpack" box is an advertised feature of this product. Any company that sells and ships it should be aware of this fact and pack it inside of a separate cardboard shipping box. That said, this is an average quality paper with a premium shipping cost. I only recommend this product for those who prefer the pull down side panel feature of the box itself.
Bought for personal use but I've got a ways to go before I try my hand at colored pencils. My friends daughter likes them though. Maybe they'll still be around when I want to try them :-)

I guess if you don't have space for a larger dispenser like the Duck Brand Standard Tape Gun with Foam Handle, (Includes 1 Roll of 54 Yard Standard Tape) then you can pay about the same price for 22 yards in the throw away dispenser that isn't very sturdy.So, if you have to travel with packing tape, or want your packing tape to fit into a small drawer, then buy this.  The tape is high quality, thick, is easy to unstick from itself.The plastic dispenser is a bit flimsy though.So, go with a larger tape gun if you are able.

This is a great, multi-purpose memo board. I was actually interested in it more for the magnetic feature than the dry erase board, as I wanted something to replace a very old bulletin board.  This magnetic board is perfect, as it is a good size (14x14), and very lightweight.  I love the frameless style and the silver color--both look more modern.The board comes with two cute, rainbow-colored magnets as well as a black dry erase pen with a built-in eraser on the cap.  It also comes with self-stick pads for hanging.  My only complaint is that there is no alternative method of hanging.  I want to hang the board on my wall, but I don't want to use the self stick pads and risk damaging my paint.  I have no problem with using a small nail, but as far as I can tell, there's no place to attach a nail to the board.  I'm sure I'll figure it out, but a small hanging loop or hole would have been helpful.  Otherwise, this is a great product, and I would definitely recommend it!

This is a good idea with problems. An inexpensive, well built file box made out of cardboard is a good idea.  The problems include cardboard that is not very strong and a bottom that did not hold together without the aid of packing tape.I like the idea of a light file box that can be put in a file or desk drawer.  I have a plastic one that is bulky.The problem with this is that the cardboard seems thin.  It bent easily when I grabbed the side of the file box with my hand. The bottom of the file box did not hold together well  when empty and once I put a couple of files in it it opened. I had to take some packing tape to reinforce the bottom. The Amazon web page says this will hold 750 sheets. I am not sure if the bottom will hold up with that many, even with the packing tape to reinforce it.The top front and back portions of the file box, which have handles, have two layers of cardboard.  These hold up okay. I wish the entire file box had two layers of cardboard to make the entire item stronger.I have used this for a week keeping it in my desk drawer and taking it out and putting it on my desk at times. It is okay if left alone in a desk with the desk bottom and sides supporting it. Once I took it out the sides bent a little and as mentioned I needed to add tape to the bottom so it would not open up. This is not holding up very well.

I had an old Brother fax/answering machine that finally got too expensive to operate (the imaging film is no longer made), so I decided to replace it with this Panasonic unit. I couldn't find too many alternatives that could be used for everything from faxing to an answering machine, so in the end, I pretty much settled for the Panasonic. So far, I'm happy with the choice.Positives are the ease of setup, the construction quality and the fact that you get everything from a cordless phone to a network scanner in one box.To use all of the features, you'll need a wired Ethernet connection (really not sure why WiFi isn't built in) as well as an analog phone line. With these two items connected, I had no trouble getting up and running in under ten minutes.There are print/scan/fax utilities for Windows (of course) as well as Mac OS X.With some fine-tuning of the settings, you can automatically forward faxes and voicemails to your email system, so you don't have to be right in front of the device to receive your messages or faxes. You can also scan directly to a networked PC, assuming you have the Panasonic software installed. These are all great features for a low-cost unit.On the negative side, the built-in web configuration program is quite poor...it works, but it's just a blur of settings with no explanations, and clearly it looks like it wasn't developed in US English originally.Print quality is only fair, but I have other printers for when I need high-quality print.Scanning speed is quite slow for a device of this type, but I don't do so much scanning that it's a problem for me.Final negative is that like a lot of other manufacturers, Panasonic ships this unit with a part capacity toner cartridge. Replacements (which are fairly expensive) have toner for an estimated 5000 pages, but the one you'll find in the box is only good for 2000. Still, the cost per page is quite a bit less than older style film units.Overall, Panasonic has squeezed a lot of function into a small product, and even though none of the functions are stellar performers, if this is what you're looking for, it's worth a try.

I wrap a lot of gifts year-round, especially at Christmas time. It goes with the territory of coming from a large family and liking to give a gift instead of a gift card. If there's one thing I know about it's the main problems with the art of gift wrapping. My biggest problems have always been cutting straight lines on the paper (even with paper that has marked lines) and tearing off scotch tape while holding the paper that needs to be taped. I consider myself a pro at gift wrapping after 50 years of practice since my childhood, but I still always wish for new products to make this skill easier and quicker.A couple years ago, I bought the Scotch Gift Wrap Cutter. When I  tried it, I had hopes of cutting straight lines every time, but after 50 years of using sissors, it took me a few times to get used to this new blade cutter. When I finally got the hang of it- getting it started and then holding it on the correct angle for a smooth cut, I can tell you- I will never go back to sissors. My paper is always straight and I love this product, as it does save paper when I don't have to constantly go back to re-cut a crooked piece!When I first saw this new Scotch Pop-Up Tape Handband Dispenser advertised on television, I couldn't wait to try it! I have wasted so much tape in my life trying to tear it off with whatever fingers were not holding the paper. When the tape twists, and it always does using just a couple of fingers, it's garbage, and you realize that about a fourth of your tape ends up in the trash. Not to mention you have to try tearing a perfect piece of tape all over again- meaning you are losing time as well as tape! I tried this new dispenser just at the tail end of my Christmas gift wrapping this year and what a difference! I don't have to pull twisted tape any more that ends up in the garbage can! The dispenser is light weight with an elastic band that you can use on your wrist, hand or knuckles. The pop-up tape is easy to load. Once loaded, you merely touch the piece of tape sticking out with one finger and it's out and ready to tape! No more twisted tape or struggling with holding the paper to be taped! Each piece of tape is 3/4" by 2 inches long, which I found to be adequate, but I would love it if they could make the tape 2 1/2 inches long, which is more what I am used to! Scotch has made my two main wrapping problems disappear, which is cutting straight paper and now, no more wasting of time and tape with this great new Pop-up dispenser, which is practically hands-free and really does save tape!

These oval labels are gorgeous.These are thick, super glossy labels. The adhesive is permanent, so removing the label after it's been adhered for a while will destroy the label.Avery has figured out how to help a person cleanly peel labels off their backing. There is a vertical dent in the backing paper that when folded, a small tab on the left side of the oval label is exposed. This makes it just too darn easy to peel the label off the backing paper.These are a really nice size and shape. I was surprised how many words I could type on each label. The oval chosen is very pleasant looking.The paper accepts inkjet ink very well. I printed some photographs onto the label, and they were sharp, clear, and had bright colors. Once dry the labels don't bleed ink.The Avery Wizard add in for Word is really only one way to use these labels. Setting up a table of cells, exactly the right size would be a lot of work. The one pain with that wizard, the labels are represented as square cells in Word. Avery should have added a hairline oval in light gray that exactly matches the size of the label. As it stands, I had to guesstimate where things would land on the label. Using line centering and centered for inside the cell, I was able to get text to lie down correctly on the label.These are beautiful labels with a well thought out method for using the labels.

We check Avery's website for templates.  There are a few cheesy options and also a blank tempate.  The blank version seems to be lined up perfectly as it printed well (just make sure you put the paper in the right way).  The paper feels sort of like a thin cardstock, which did not get stuck in our printer.  This has sometimes been a problem with thicker paper.

I had given up on Pilot pens because they usually leaked ink.  I saw this one and thought I might as well try it.  The writing is fairly smooth, the barrel is somewhat thick for my hands.  The spring clip is rather large, but I realize that since it is tailored for work applications, it probably has to be larger to clip in pockets or on folders.  I was anxious to see if the pen would write on moist paper, so I misted a piece of paper (a shopping list) and tried it out.  The pen did not roll smooth enough to consistently write on the surface. The price of the pen, the bulkiness of its presentation, and the ify claims about writing capability makes this pen one that I will skip and go for a less expensive ballpoint.

I generally like this organizer -- it is attractive and colorful.The gray plastic "base" or whatever is very good quality -- tough and durable.  The colored plastic folders are a little on the thin side, and I wouldn't remove them and carry them around, etc.  It's better if you only plan to use this organizer to keep the folders inside all the time (for example, for commonly used forms, to organize mail, etc.)I would like it better if it had two loops at the top, to help keep it steadier -- with just one loop, it swings from side to side.I would not use it to fold up and take with me, by the way -- it's just not going to hold up for very long used that way, in my opinion.  Overall, though, I like it for keeping frequently used forms and a calendar in.

The company I work for has offices all over the place, so many of our meetings include participants connected to our conference room via video teleconference (VTC) cameras.  It's nearly impossible to see the whiteboards when you're dialed in via VTC, because the dry erase pens are too dim to read.  These bold pens are incredible though.  They are bright enough to show up even for the remote attendees.These pens also have a window where you can see the ink level, so you won't be surprised when your pen eventually goes dry.These pens are easy to write with and they erase easily too.  They're very handy.

I seriously love this product and have used it for everything and almost everywhere. It's ridiculous how many items I find myself using this on, it's crazy! I love the great bright color and the quality of it and am already ordering more!

This tapes goes OVER existing packaging tape.  It will not be strong enough to use as tape on its' own.  It is great if you are selling stuff online, and need to ship it and want to make sure it was not tampered with.  It rolls off easily and applies and cuts easy.  It's basically just a clear type tape with text on it.  It does it's job and is a great value.  If you need it, I recommend it.

I like to use a lot of different supplemental materials at home with my children to boost what they are learning in school.  I'm partial to the books put out by Brain Quest because they're colorful and fun unlike most other workbooks like them.  I was unsure what I should expect from this Problem Solving book by Mead.  I'm actually impressed with this workbook.  It covers a wide range of problem solving and logic based skills.  Most of the material is presented in such a way that my first grader thinks it's a game.  It's a fun book that does a good job at building up critical thinking and problem solving skills.The quality of the workbook itself is also pretty nice.  The tear out pages are a nice weight so they're able to stand up to erasing without ripping.  The book has bright and colorful illustrations that will catch the attention of young learners.Overall I think this workbook is worth considering if you're looking for a book of logic based activities for your first grader.

I received the pink package- which I really was hoping to get pink.There is 2 sheets of stickers and they are fairly thick and are like rubber and actually have a plastic odor to them when first taken out of the package.The odor faded  and within a few minutes it wasnt noticeable.I used some of the stickers on the fridge to hang up items.I am also using some holding up random notes I have on my computer monitor.For me they are useful- not really needed, but they are useful.I could see children/teens getting a lot of use out of them- locker decoration- hanging up art - etcThey are also stickers on both sides- if you peel off the clear plastic on the side you wouldnt really think would be sticky- it is a sticker also so both sides can be usedThe price is a great price too!Under $4!

We used these for some kids crafts.  We made a recipe book with lots of cool pictures in it for a birthday.it was nice, the kids felt that they could really make a "real book".  And it was easy enough to use.Its certainly better than a binder for most things.I could also see where it would be useful for procedural manuals at work.  It keeps things from being bulky.  Normally we use a three ring binder and those can be annoying because they are always thick no matter how little we put in them.I would recommend it for anything where you want to have a slightly upgraded feeling of quality.Here is the direct link to more paper if you need it.Fellowes Twist and Bind Machine-Free Kit, Pre-Punched Paper Refill, 50 per Pack (5226101)

I have the 3M Dual-Swivel Monitor arm mounted to my 5' Ikea Galant desk and it's working perfectly. I've uploaded a few pictures of post installation. I tried this with my Dell Ultrasharp 27" and 24" (pictured) monitors and both held up just fine.There are multiple mounting options included. The desk mount can either be mounted as a "clamp style," which is most common, to attach to a flat surface or via "Grommet Type" to go through a hole in the desk. Depending on the type of mount you use, it can accommodate desk thickness all the way up to 4.25" when using the standard clamp style mount.The assembly and installation was pretty straight forward. The included instructions are basic, but the pictures pretty much give you all the information you need. I will add that in regards to assembly instructions for the "Clamp Style" mount, when you get to Step 2, skip to Step 4 instead and complete that first. Then back to Step 2. This will make it much easier to use the included Allen key to tighten those screws.Putting the arm together is rather easy as it snaps together. There are quick-release latches to easily remove them in the future. For final adjustment, there are 2 additional Allen Key points to tighten at the pole and the swivel point at back of the monitor. To prevent unwanted movement, I had to tighten mine down more than it expected as it did cause the cap on one of the nuts to snap off. This is only cosmetic and nothing you'll ever see in the future, but a little surprising.As this is a standard VESA mount, it worked exactly as expected with both Dell monitors I tested it with. It has a place to run cables through the arms, although be sure to check your cable length to make sure there is enough slack for future movement. These stands need more "excess" cable than you might think to make sure you don't break any cables or connectors.Overall, the mount appears to be sturdy and allows for much more movement on my work surface than I had before with the original monitor stand. It's also a bit pricey. Otherwise, I'd consider this recommended for anybody looking into a single monitor swivel arm solution.

I like the idea of this magnetic marker board. It is small but not too small. It's perfect for a grocery or reminder list to hang on the fridge. And it has the cutesy little magnets with it. But the magnetic stickers for the board are not very strong. It wouldn't stick on the surface of the fridge well at all but kept sliding down the front.Eventually we tried the washer, and it stuck a little better. (Of course people aren't opening and closing it as much.) So it sticks there, but it isn't an extremely practical place to have a marker board.Summary: It's cute and a good idea, but I wish the magnetic strips were stronger.

It will come as no surprise that these labels are easy to use.  They're an Avery product, so the templates for using these labels are built into almost every application you're likely to use with them, so formatting the print data is a snap.  What makes these labels different is their construction.  They're thicker than the typical mailing label, with a white front and a dark gray sticky side.  This makes the labels truly opaque, so that they block any previous writing or labels that they are applied over.  I've tried to see through them, and I haven't been able to.  This allows envelopes to be re-used while protecting the privacy of the previous addressees.

I never thought there could be much innovation with regard ti hanging folder tabs, but I was wrong. Although the tabs that typically come with folders work fine, these are made of a thicker plastic and really do go on and come off easier than the tabs that attach with wings. These attach using three bumps that fit into the slots in the folder. Once attached, they stay on much better than the standard tabs. They are easy to remove when you want to remove them by gently lifting them off the surface of the folder. You can also slide them side to side while lifting them. The included card stock inserts are easy to insert and remove. The only problem I found was if you over-flex the tabs they get opaque lines at the flex points that are permanent. They seem brittle, but I have not yet broken one.

I purchased this little machine about 10 years ago. I really needed one for a few quick labels. It was cheap and since I didn't think I would be using it for a long term I would try it. I did buy several replacement tapes at the time ( I was positive I would not be able to get any in 6 months) Well it is at least 10 years, The machine works as well as it did new and labels are still available. If I had a need for one I would not hesitate spending what they are asking for this one. A trick I've learned  is to run the front of the tape gently across your thumb and a dull knife then flip the label over and with a bit more pressure run the tape on the paper side. Like curling ribbon, but not as much pressure. It works like magic. Any stiff, smooth, straight edge will do. If you are in need of one of these I highly recommend this one. I have gone through about 25 tapes, the cutter still works like it is supposed to. I'm not sure how many labels you can get out of a refill but they seem to last forever. I just popped the last one in my machine, so I am replacing my stock. I will only buy 2 this time because they seem to be available. I will look to brother the next time I need a machine that they make. I am no longer angry about the 6 month old typewriter I couldn't get a ribbon for 30 years ago lol.

I put this on the back of a  closet door in my home office and use it for organizing receipts for tax purposes.  The pockets themselves are pretty deep, but they do not expand our very far.  I labeled the folders using a label maker, and recommend that you use something like a 3M removable adhesive to hold it up.So far, so good - it does the job and looks pretty good (even though it does live in the closet!)

I recently received a dozen Letter/Legal Size Bankers Boxes through Amazon's Vine program. While this might seem fortuitous--as you will soon learn, I have need for such organization--in actuality I noticed this offering some months ago and hoped it would become available again. I already have more than sixty record storage boxes* in my basement and thus plenty of perspective for comparison, not to mention a continued need for organization and storage.Just to be precise, I am reviewing the Presto Model 636. The shipping box was deceptively heavy at almost twenty pounds! If you cannot comfortably lift that much, be sure to get some help or else open the shipping box and carry a few at a time.I was amazed at how quickly each of these Presto Bankers Boxes assembles. It is *much* quicker than others I have tried, even other boxes from Fellowes. Evidently the "Instant Assembly" is Truth in Advertising. You simply pull on two opposite corners and the box essentially assembles itself. That's it! The lid assembles much the same as other Bankers Boxes (and thus takes far more time than the box itself in this case), however the locking lid is a nice touch. This feature is not essential, especially because in my experience the weight of stacked boxes tends to keep them in place, however I will admit that sometimes a lid can slide around when carrying boxes around. That shouldn't happen with these. The only slight drawback to this feature is it can be a little difficult to remove the lid when you actually want to!These storage boxes are also very sturdy. Surely the double wall construction is to thank. They are sturdier than the non-heavy duty offering from Fellowes that I already own (the self-effacing "Basic Strength" Stor-File Model 703), sturdier than either of the Perma choices I have tried from Wilson Jones (Stor-All Model 3325Q or even the deluxe wood-grained Supreme Model 5010Q), and certainly sturdier than any of the knock-offs from the office stores (for example, Office Depot model 63325).Unlike some of the other office equipment I have tested for Vine (Smead SuperTab Folders,X-Acto Electric Pencil Sharpener,Triton Storability LocBins: all of which I rated three stars), these Bankers Boxes really are better than the competition and truly do offer real features, not just gimmicks. Superior quality. Made in U.S.A.There is plenty of space to write on the side of each box, though personally I print my own organization labels. :-)I will not allow price to affect my rating, but let me say this: I would never pay ten bucks for a single Bankers Box. Maybe I'm a cheap basterd but the cost really adds up, especially when you buy them by the dozen. This then is high quality at a high cost. Personally I would make do with slightly less heavy duty boxes, but that's your call as the customer.* I never realized that Fellowes, Inc. is in fact the copyright holder of the "Bankers Box" trademark, and indeed the company was founded as the Bankers Box Company back in 1917. These pencils are beloved of colored pencil artists. I normally do watercolor, but I also like colored pencil and you can get some dramatic results. They give you the buildability of pastels without the issue of the dust, and the result is more durable. There are some hints for using these that will really help you develop some amazing artwork.1. Sharpen these pencils with an electric sharpener. I like theX-Acto, because it has the ability to take fatter pencils, if you want. Some brands come in larger formats. THe electric sharper lets you sharpen frequently (you will need to) and does it quickly and well.2. If your lead breaks after you sharpen it, and keeps doing this, your pencils were dropped or mashed during shipment. You should try a few more pencils. If the same thing happens, return them. These pencils develop cracks in the leads if they are treated roughly. They are packed well, so normally, shipping is not an issue. But anything can happen from the warehouse to your doorstep. Likewise, keep them on your table, and punch them into a strip of styrofoam between uses--don't let them roll around on your art table. They will just roll onto the floor and they can break that way, too.3. Paper is important. I happen to like Stonehenge paper, which has a sort of suede-like feel and enough tooth to grab the pigment. It comes in various shades, including black. TRY BLACK! As with pastel, you can get some glowing results by penciling in your highlights and using the paper as shadow.4. Burnishing; aburnishing pencil and blendermelts the pigment more thoroughly into the paper. After you lay down sufficient pencil to cover, burnish and blend.5. Be inspired! There are many great books. I favorAnn Kullbergwho has written a number of books and also has workshops, kits and demos on her own website. There is also an author locally here, Nancy Carol Willis who has written some wonderful children's books about nature. HerRaccoon Moonis a terrific children's book and all the illustrations are in colored pencil. She has one about robins and one about the Red Knot, a rare bird that relies on the eggs of the horseshoe crab, both being special to our shore in Delaware. Her illustrations glow and you will see how wonderful colored pencils are for illustrating.

Panasonic KX-TG6632The KX-TG6632 is a DECT 6.0 "Plus" digital phone kit with an answering machine. The DECT 6.0 network is one of the more advanced cordless frequency systems and is fully digital. Because it is a network, your satellite handsets do not require any physical connection to the base station. They simply sit in a cradle to charge up anywhere in your house and you can expand this system up to a few extra units, although it comes with 2 handsets.The range for the handset is about 100 feet or more. At 90 feet, I started to hear some minor interference but nothing dramatic. The audio quality during calls is exceptional. There is an Eco Mode that gives up to 13 hours of talk time and decreases/increases signal strength based on the proximity to the base station, but I haven't tried talking for 13 hours straight. It comes with Ni-Mh AAA batteries instead of proprietary battery packs. This gives you the option to buy replacement AAA NiMH rechargeable batteries in most grocery stores, which is both cost effective and convenient! I'm glad to see more OEMs using Ni-MH batteries instead of NiCd, NiMh is cadmium free and has better performance (resistant to the memory effect).Before I used the handsets, I put the batteries into my special charger to discharge and recharge them to break them in. While my charger said they were fully charged, I put them in the phone and the cradles kept charging them for another hour or so until the orange LED shut off. The Panasonic chargers must be quite an advanced charging circuit to top off the NiMH cells!The keypad on each handset is fully backlit, which means you can actually see the numbers in total darkness. The LCD is backlit as well by white LEDs and resembles a Nokia cellphone from about 5-8 years ago. The Caller ID system and address book is fully networked, which means all of the handsets in the network will read the same Caller ID logs and the same address book. Changing the address book on one phone will ensure the entire network has access to the updated info. This makes it convenient in not having to set phone numbers in each of the phones.Unlike other phones, the Panasonic shuts off the charging LED once the batteries are charged. This helps reduce light pollution in your room at night in case you wanted to sleep better. I had an older GE DECT 6.0 phone that kept its blue LED on all the time, and this blue LED was bright enough to act as a night light. I had to use tape to cover it, so it was very thoughtful for Panasonic to use a more subdued orange LED that shuts off after the charging is done.The ring tone choices are limited, but at least they offer a few creative ring tones based on popular overtures, but it is nothing advanced. The talking Caller ID function is very helpful but the pronunciation programming needs to be improved.Another awesome feature is that your satellite handsets will play incoming calls to help you screen calls if you're not in the general vicinity of the base station. You can also play messages via the satellite handsets and erase messages as well, so you never have to be at the base station to check/play/erase messages!The only negative aspect I can report on these phones is the slow interface of the menus. Scrolling through the address book takes a split second longer than I'd like, the same goes for dialing. With my Motorola Droid2 smartphone, I can setup pauses for passcodes to voicemail boxes which dial blisteringly fast. With these Panasonic phones, the auto-dialing is painfully slow and the menus are slow as well. The address book entries also allow a limited number of characters, making it impossible for setting up an entry to automatically log onto certain voice mail boxes or other phone menus. That said, my complaints are minor compared to the performance, ergonomics, and overall design of these phones. I'd highly recommend them to friends, families, and co-workers.Overall: 4/5 stars, the menu/interface could be faster. Now 3/5 stars because of the problem below:UPDATE: 31 DEC 2011The speakerphone on one of the handsets has started to intermittently produce sound. I've isolated it to a failure of the speaker itself, and not the wiring. The coil must have broken somewhere inside the speaker. I use the speakerphone a lot on this particular handset, and it must have broken because of this.UPDATE: 4 MAR 2012I found a speaker on eBay that physically fits the phone but the impedance is not matched properly. I am able to hear the button tones and the speakerphone audio, but it is a very low level. I find it disappointing that the speakerphone died in the first place, and second, it was impossible to order the correct replacement via Panasonic's horrible web site. If a product requires an electrical engineer to try and find a replacement speaker online and to fix it himself, then it's not a very good design.

This printer replaces my HP C6180 All-in-one.  That was a great printer until the pipes dried up because of non-use.  I learned my lesson and intend to use this printer on a regular basis.Well, it's got everything as far as AIO printers go.  It's wider than the HP, but that's fine.  Yeah, this needs some space so be sure to take into consideration these dimensions: 19.25"L x 15.5" W x 9"H closed.  Add 6.5" to W for open output tray, additional 3" to W for pulling out the paper catcher extension.  Of course the paper trays at the bottom add around 6" if you just want to load additional paper and about 12.5" if you want to pull the entire tray out.  Add 4.25" to H if you want to open the Auto Document Feeder Cover.  Add 13" to H, separate from the Auto Doc Feeder, if you want to open the Flatbed Scanner Door.  But hey, after all that measuring, you don't have to leave any rear space for cables because they've designed it in a way that it does not protrude from the back, yay! (not gonna add how much space you need to open the back in case of paper jam because most people will figure that out on their own ;) )Ok, that's done....phew.  It looks great since it's got that Samsung-like "Touch-Of-Color" thing going on.  Google for pictures to understand, but basically it's that burgundy on top of black coloring scheme.  This thing prints FAST!  Word documents are printed with half the speed of a laser printer, but it's still too fast to notice the difference :D  Built-in duplexing will make the tree-huggers feel good.  I don't use it because most people prefer one one-paged printouts.The scanning utility for Windows is pretty smart.  It even divides multiple photos that you put into the flatbed scanner into multiple scanned files rather than one big fat picture file of multiple pictures in one.  So like this:  You put 4 pictures on the flatbed scanner and you click "Photo" scan option.  It scans all the photos on the flatbed, but saves each photo to individual files!  Nice, right?  If you don't like that, well make a custom scan option or use the "Document" scan button.Needless to say this works on networks, wired or wireless.  I couldn't find the Bluetooth connection if it even exists on this machine.  There's also cloud printing support, but never bothered to set it up.  Fax works as expected.  I've set it up to listen to the answering machine and when it hears the fax beep, it will pick up and print out the incoming fax.  That way I can leave it connected on the phone line.I'm not a good judge of print quality.  All I know is that the photos print out good to me and the documents are just fine.  The CD direct printing functionality works great...no leaky ink yet.  Just dry CD label prints.Issues:  When the printer is about to print and automatically opens the output tray, the tray itself sounds like it's crashing open.  I don't like the sound in my office...sometimes it startles me!  So before I click print, I manually open the tray.  Not that anything seems wrong with the mechanism, but I just don't like the crash open sound.  I'm surprised Canon couldn't come up with a soft open option.  Either that or I have a faulty mechanism.Another issue is if you set it to "Preview before Printing", it won't preview the next job until the current print job is done.  So you have to wait for each print job (not each page) to finish before you get the next preview window.  Annoying, so I don't use the preview before printing option anymore.  Maybe it's a Windows 8 thing? I dunno.The occasional auto cleaning cycle feels too long.  Gets in the way of fast printing.  But hey, it has to clean, right?The online utility has a very old interface (like 10+ year old) and very limited in settings.  So most customizations have to be done through the menu settings on the printer directly, which can be a hassle.  There was another settings issue but I forget what it was, lol.  But it's no big deal for most users.So putting all things together, the printer is an excellent buy.  The minor things do bother me, but not enough to disrupt my printer usage.

I bought this stand for the opposite reason from most people: I wanted to LOWER my Acer X223W monitor to avoid neck strain. My desk is one of the old steel/formica desks, and I guess it's higher than the newer ones. My monitor was right at eye level with the top, but this proved too high. This stand really did the trick. By using this stand, I was able to get the bottom edge of my monitor 1.75 inches from my desktop, which now puts it just below my eye level.The stand is really nice, obviously well built, nice heft, easy to put together.A few things you should know:1. You have to decrease the tension screw in the bottom quite a bit to get the spring loose enough to allow the monitor to go down and stay there. Keep on turning that screw counterclockwise and eventually you'll get the tension down to a reasonable point.2. Likewise, there is a tension screw in the top that you have to screw counterclockwise to allow the monitor to tilt with some ease.3. The hardest part of this process was getting the old stand off my Acer. Disconnect EVERYTHING electrical and computer connected before you start trying to remove the monitor's original stand. When you turn the monitor face down to remove the stand, put a towel under it to avoid scratching it. TAKE YOUR TIME.After struggling fruitlessly with the factory stand and not moving it at all, I finally read enough to learn that on my Acer X223W there is a plastic cap located on either side of the factory stand that LOOKS like it is a part of the monitor--- but this is really just a cover cap for the screws that hold the stand onto the monitor. These caps are recessed down into the back of the monitor, so they look like they are part of the monitor but they aren't. You have to use something sharp to pry off these caps and then under each cap is two short screws that are the stand's attachment to the monitor. A sharp file or screwdriver would probably get the caps off, I used a tiny file. Once I got the old stand off, putting on the new stand was a no-brainer, they give you these nice finger turn screws to put on the new stand, you don't even need a screwdriver.See my customer uploaded image for a picture that shows where the plastic cover caps are located on the back of the Acer X223W monitor:[...]I'm really happy with this stand, it rotates side to side and also up and down. I don't know why I didn't do this sooner.Oh, and I had to buy my stand somewhere else, because Amazon took my order and then a few days later told me they could not get the item.

THIS WILL JAM IN THE PAPER FEED!  The Epson NX430 will jam on the right side of the feed. HERE IS HOW TO FIX IT: get a sheet of acetate, cut apprx 2.5"from the right side bottom up on a 90 degree wedge about3 inches and print on that. You need enough "center sheet" to get it through the feed and doing this will force the rollers to once again grab and print in unison. WORKS. Now, given that, this printer ROCKS for color and copies.Epson's NX430 takes little footprint space, so an unexpected find was that it sits next to my desk where books once stacked like a growing pile of lost souls; but wifi'd up, this sweety can go anywhere, even remote. Wifi enabled, it is sweet for sending from the Apple bunch of machines and other wifi devices, yes, even a phone.  Scanner resolution is 2400 dpi: 4 times the best of my last one at 1/3rd the space. Without question, the prettiest, and most petite printer we've ever owned.It uses very small ink cartridges, and so far, no refill, but supposed to give 124 copies per, so there's that, but colors are individual and easy to load, so less waste. There is no paper tray: paper loads from the top and a feed extends from the front: be aware of that as that adds height and forward space, but minimal. இ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:ѾѾѾѾ Recommended with warm fuzzies.I bought this unit to replace an old AT&T; 1710 digital answering machine that was still working okay, but I wanted its ability to record 40 minutes of messages instead of my old 1710 model's recording of only 10 minutes of messages.  So much of this review is based on comparing the 1739 with my old, and far more basic, 1710 model...ѾѾѾѾѾ Excellent 5-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾѾѾ The amazingly unbeatable $18 low price!!!  A lot of electronic features for far less than what some people pay for a few months of voice mail service (and far less than what many people spend at coffee shops during a single week).ѾѾѾѾѾ Lots of features and configuration options for the low price.  You can choose English or Spanish language presentation, the number of rings before the machine answers, a 3-digit user-defined remote access code (the 1710 only used an unchangeable 2-digit remote access code), whether to be able to listen to your outgoing announcement when the machine answers a call, whether the machine announces the caller's number when the phone rings, whether the incoming number is stored and announced prior to message playback, whether to accept blocked (private number) calls, and whether to have the machine audibly beep every 15 seconds when there are new messages.ѾѾѾѾѾ Easy voice-narrated setup of all features.  You just press and hold the [Setup] button and the machine guides you through all configuration settings. A recorded man's voice actually speaks to you and guides you through the setup process.ѾѾѾѾѾ When you press the power button to turn it off, a voice speaks out, "The machine is off".  And when you turn it back on, it tells you, "The machine is on. 40 minutes to record", telling you how much recording time is left on the unit.ѾѾѾѾѾ My old 1710 model required 4 AA batteries to retain stored messages in case of a power outage.  The 1739 does not need batteries to retain both the outgoing announcement and stored messages during a power outage.ѾѾѾѾ Good 4-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾѾ The machine does not record blank messages or messages consisting of just touch tone beeps.  My old 1710 answering machine would often record my 2-digit remote access code touch tone beeps as separate messages every time I called in to retrieve messages, but this no longer happens with the 1739.  Furthermore, my old 1710 used to record blank messages where someone (usually a wrong number dialed) would not say anything and just hang up.  But with the 1739, I no longer have to wade through blank messages consisting only of silence on the other end.  In addition, if the caller has not spoken up 6 or 7 seconds after the beep, the unit will disconnect the call, and not include the silence as a recorded message.ѾѾѾѾ The 1739 has better phone keypad ergonomics when accessing the answering machine remotely.  On my old 1710, you had to remember a non-intuitive layout of keypad commands, or carry the pocket-sized command reference card with you when you were away from home.  Now with the 1739, all of the most common commands are placed between phone keypad numbers 1 through 6, and if you do not have your command reference card with you, you can always press the '5' number on your phone to get a narrated help guide that describes what all possible remote commands were available.ѾѾѾ Average not-good not-bad 3-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾ The clarity of both the digitally recorded announcement and incoming messages is not much better than my very old AT&T; 1710 digital answering machine.  I can still understand all words and phone numbers left by callers in the messages, but they can sound somewhat garbled or a bit muffled sometimes, requiring me to replay a message a few times every now and then.  Perhaps a cruder digital recording approach was used in order to make the unit very inexpensive, but I would have gladly paid $20 or $30 more in order to get better sound recordings!  If you are getting static on your recorded messages, you should try plugging the answering machine into a DSL filter; this will improve the overall sound quality, but, as mentioned, I had hoped that the clarity of both the outgoing announcement and incoming recorded messages would be noticeably better than what I had on my old 1710 model... instead, the sound quality between this new unit and my old model are about the same.ѾѾѾ My old AT&T; 1710 answering machine used a less-bright LED digit to display the number of incoming messages.  But 1739 uses a much-brighter red LED display and, in addition, has a red On/Off button that always glows red when the unit is turned on.  Depending on where you place this unit, the amount of red glow that emanates from this machine can be annoying in a darkened room, especially if this machine is placed in a bedroom.  You can turn off both the LED display and glowing On/Off button by turning off the unit, but then you no longer record messages.  It would have been nice to be able to either turn off the two sources of red light but leave the unit turned on or, better yet, have a dimmer option to reduce the glow that comes from the unit.  Of course, you can always place something over the unit to cover up the red glow, but...ѾѾѾ My old 1710 had two phone jacks for connecting the unit to the phone with one phone cord and connecting the unit to the wall jack with another phone cord.  But for some odd reason, AT&T; decided to use a non-removable telephone cord to connect the unit to the wall jack.  This is okay if the supplied 5-foot cord is long enough to reach your wall jack, but you will need an extension cord if you need to place the unit farther than 5 feet from the wall jack.ѾѾ Bad 2-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾ As a test, I tried calling into the machine and leaving five kinds of short messages: "ET call home", "This is just a test", "Just a test", "Call James", and "Call me".  The machine properly recorded "ET call home" and "This is just a test", but it did not record the "Just a test", "Call James", and "Call me" messages.  I repeatedly tried these short 2, 3, and 4 word messages and it consistently did not record them as messages.  This is bad!  You may thus never receive messages left by callers who only say a few words and then hang up.  There appears to be some minimum syllabic threshold required in a message in order for it to be recorded. This may present a problem if you have someone who quickly and tersely leaves a message of "Call me" and hangs up, resulting in the machine not recording the message and you not getting such a message.  But, overall, I myself would consider the risk and consequences of losing such brief messages to be small since I expect most callers will leave at least a full sentence as a message, but it is definitely a potential problem with this product and I do wonder if I ever lose any quick short messages left by someone.ѾѾ When the machine announces the time-stamp for each message, it only announces the day of the week, time, and year.  During Setup, you can only configure the unit's clock for these attributes also.  But knowing that a message was recorded on "Monday 3:36PM 2009" or "Thursday 6:03AM 2009" only means something if (a) you check your messages on a weekly basis, and (b) you do not keep old messages stored on the unit that were phoned in over one week ago.  Otherwise, you may not know which "Monday" the message is referring to!  This is a huge blooper of a design flaw that the AT&T; engineers chose to track the day of the week but not the day of the year.  I would have much preferred the unit to say "April 12 2009 3:36PM" instead of the far more vague "Sunday 3:36PM 2009".

I got this printer to replace my old HP Photosmart C4635 so there will be some comparisons made between my cheap printer and this new one. First off, I am not sure why HP does this but they tend to NOT include a USB cable with their printers. I can understand it a little bit with my old printer since I got it for so cheap but I think paying the price on the D110A should at least include a USB cable, they are not expensive to make, at all. It is a generic USB printer cable so if you are replacing an old printer then you should be able to use the old printer USB cable. However, if this is your first printer, you would need to buy one and they got some cheap ones on Amazon. I was able to use an old USB cable that was hooking up to my Western Digital external hard drive.Here is what I got in the packaging:- printer- power cord (at least you get this)- Bag to hold the printer- Bag for the cables- Printer Ink- 100 photo paperNow, onto the features of this printer. The printer is extremely light and fairly easy to set up. Loading the ink cartridges is pretty easy and I was glad to find that the ink used in this is the same as my C4635. It uses HP 60 or you can pay a little more for HP 60XL so the ink lasts longer.SETUPI turned the printer on and it was pretty straightforward. It asks for your language preference as well as your country. This part got tedious as I had to state my language then it asks you to confirm if this is the correct one. Then after getting the latest updates on the printer, I had to go through the same thing again. I then set up wireless and it was pretty simple. You can have it scan for a router and then enter in the WEP/WPA key. I found this part a little bit tedious too as you have to use the left and right arrows to scroll to the characters you want. It would have been a lot simpler if HP include up and down arrows on the printer to easily navigate the keypad. You are then asked to calibrate the cartridges by printing out a piece of paper and scanning it. I had to do this on the C4635 as well so no surprise there. It will then print out a page telling you how to access the HP Eprint Center, which is a big feature on this printer.PC SETUPThe installation disc was easy to use and pretty quick. Only bad thing is that it doesn't let you do a custom installation. I always like to uncheck all the toolbars these software install on my computer. Alas, I got the Yahoo toolbar anyway. I just removed it afterwards so not too big of a deal for me.PRINTI decided to try and print out a picture. Quality came out a lot better than my C4635. It took just as long to print a picture as my old printer so I am not jumping for joy at the speed but still doable. For anyone coming from laserjet printers, this is definitely some getting used to. It took a long time for my picture to dry, probably because of all the colors in it. I tried printing a few other things and stuff with less color came out much faster. If you do print out a lot of pictures, you will probably use up the ink fast. Otherwise, it is pretty conservative on the amount of ink used. Again, it is only slightly faster than my C4635 so to me it's not really an improvement on speed but it is an improvement on quality of pictures.COPYCopying was faster than my C4635. It comes out almost like the exact document that is put in, so I was very pleased with that result. For my testing purposes, I scanned my AT&T; bill. If it wasn't for all the writing at the top, and the crease that also got copied, it could pass as the real thing if the original is not sitting right next to it.SCANI love the scan function on this. With my C4635, The only format the scan comes out in is in a JPEG. Now, you can scan it in as a PDF or a TIF. It was easy to use and you can either scan from the printer itself or use the software that comes with it on your computer. I tried the scanning to PDF and again, it looks great. It is very clear and easy to read. Another improvement for me over my old printer.APPSThis is a new feature in this printer where you can register your printer to HP Eprint Center and be able to print forms and puzzles and all sorts of things right off the printer. After setting up an account, I was easily able to print out a checklist, a maze, etc. Plus, there are even coloring pages that you can print out. It was easy and very fast to use. Right now, there is only a total of fourteen apps, including Yahoo, Weather, Sudoku, etc. I believe it will expand as this is a fairly new feature. Furthermore, they are suppose to add a feature where you can send an e-mail to your printer's e-mail address from anywhere and it will print it. However, at this moment, it is still not up yet so not sure how well it will work.Overall, I am pretty pleased with the product. It is about where my expectations lay and some aspects of it surpassed my expectations. Printing to me is still about so-so but I love the scanning and copying feature. The setup was a bit annoying and again, no USB cable is included. This is not a dealbreaker for me but may be for some people so I wanted to throw it out there. Happy printing!EDIT: The eprint feature now works! I tested it out and you get an e-mail address where you can send your e-mail and attachments to to print. I tried it and it worked super fast! This is a great feature as long as there aren't too many bugs along the way. Right after I hit send in my e-mail, the printer came alive.EDIT 2: I found a way for user to not install the Yahoo Toolbar. It's a little bit hard to see but it's something that looks like a blue link and it says something about installed components or something and you can select what to install from there. Again, it's a little hard to see whereas usually, it will just ask you if you want to install a toolbar or not.

And for the most part, her frugality was right minded, and it became ingrained in my mind as well.So when I had the chance to try Scotch's Pop Up Tape dispenser I found her in the back of mind saying "a regular role of tape would be cheaper..." I like it a lot!The dispenser comes with a supple suction cup (that you don't need to wet before you use it), so the dispenser sticks to smooth surfaces, and it does it with just enough effort to stay affixed - but on smooth surfaces, you can slide it around as your work space demands it.  The other thing is that it uses scotchs pre-measured tape supplies, which I also like because its tape in a uniform amount that works for nine out of ten.So I am keeping this one at work and I am getting one for home, too!

I had owned this shredder for about a week when it suddenly stopped shredding, so I requested permission to return it.  Then, it hit me that there might be a reset button on it.  Sure enough on the back of the shredder there is a power switch.  Apparently, a power surge had knocked out my power.  I  flipped that little switch and it was perfect again.  So, of course, I cancelled my return.  It says it will take 17 pages.  That's a bit of a stretch.  If you want to clog your machine, you can try 17 pages; however, about half that many will work better.  I have had my beast for three months now, and have done some pretty heavy-duty shredding--shredding a bunch of old income tax returns, etc., and she is humming right along.  I also love how quiet it is.  I have a smaller one that is much louder than this one.

I use hook and loop dots and tape mostly in duct tape items like composition notebook covers and purses. These are the ones I like for notebook covers. I'll make a small tab that folds over from the back to the front to close the notebook.The adhesive on these is ideal for that purpose. 3M knows their glues and since this is made to be well adhesive even on smooth plastic, the dots don't come loose with opening and closing my notebooks. For purses I prefer theScotch(R) Heavy-Duty Fasteners, 2 Sets of 1 x 3 Inches, Strips ,Black (RFD7091)because they are a bit stronger for the regular use and the bigger rectangles are more secure.I've also used these on vinyl bracelets. The small dots stick well enough for fashion use.
The wrist rest is great.  I got it to use with my laptop, but since I have my laptop at an angle, I can't use the wrist rest.  Would probably work best with a desktop computer.

I LOVE this pen.  My wife got it for me some years back and it still writes well, of course I don't use it all that much so I'm not draining a lot of ink.  The writing is smooth and does work upside down, horizontal, however you want to use it.  The only annoyance I've found is sometimes there will be a little clump of ink at the point that I'll have to wipe off.  Otherwise, I can't say enough nice things about the pen.  It'd make a really good gift for anybody who likes to do puzzles while they're in bed.

I use these continually to mark my fathers clothing with his name. He resides in a rest home and needs all his clothing marked with his name on it. Ive found these to be the best. Great for anyone who needs to mark their name on their clothing for whatever reason. I just ordered several more.

The pad is very thick and almost gel-like (reminds me of a gel bike seat cover), and it is very easy to use/adjust. Each side as these knobs that you loosen to adjust the height of the footrest, and it is colored coded for each height and even comes with a guide to help you determine your own personal ideal height. Then, to move the footrest back and forth, one simply has to push down on the front, and it easily glides to the desired position, then you just hit the front again, and it's locked into place. If you are a neat freak like me, you like everything organized. instead of using the laminator, you can use this pocket to display your Most Valuable Award (etc) in your office. That way, you won't have to commit to the Award, or your calendar schedule, and it will still look nice and shiny.The price, however, only makes it affordable for the office.

Usually I use the Avery Brand of labels, and when these came I was so excited to see that they have printed the compatible Avery label number right on each sheet. These particular labels correspond to Avery 5366. This makes it so easy to use with Microsoft Word.These labels are the perfect size for labeling file folders, but can also be used for return address labels. They measure 2/3" tall x 3 7/16" wide

These are small but they hold really well for their size. I use them on my whiteboard to hold announcements and notes for the classroom.  I like that I can hold a note/announcement and then change out when the announcement expires.

If you are looking for a good quality printer, this canon wireless would be a very good option.
