Not hard, but might take more than you are used to.Second, while this is heavy duty and that's a good thing, its also bulky. Make sure you measure your printer space and that its wide enough for this. Wider than your average $200 printer.All in all -- Recommended, as long as you have the space for it.

The Swingline stapler is a great size for my home office. While it does not include staples, the best feature of this tool is the fact that it is customizable. One word of caution - be sure to check the product packaging for your "skin" code to create the customizable skin for your white stapler.

Don't get me wrong i do like this printer a lot.but the honest truth is the ink the ink the INK!imagine spending 30 dollars on ink and more than half of it gets completely wasted because you are trying to figure out how to work the damn printer.The printer manual only gives the bare basic information and the rest you have to figure out on your own. But be careful because every single action you do wastes ink. KEEP YOUR PRINTER OFF AT ALL TIMES WHEN NOT IN USE AND ONLY USE IT WHEN YOU NEED IT. Keep that in mind and you will be happy with this printer. Also if not bad enough the ink eventually fails after 6 months to 2 years of being in the printer. and unopened ink fails after about 2- 2.5 years. So if you don't use it you loose it. In addition the images are not as clear and crisp as i would have hoped, You'd think after paying so much for ink and a printer that the print quality would be wonderful but this isn't the case. images are HORRIBLE to print on regular printer paper. but I'm sure they would be good on image paper.This IS A GOOD PRINTER. just be careful not to waste ink, only print text based documents on printer paper, and use up all ink in printer within 1 year, and out of printer within 2 years, and you should be fine. I give this printer three stars because it is MADE TO WASTE INK.Only buy this printer if you don't have to money to invest in a good laser printer, or you don't mind managing the INK.also try buying the extra high capacity inks, instead of the regular capacity, saves more money.

I'm a long time user and fan of Avery binders and found this one to be a good quality mid-grade binder with very strong D-shaped rings that are fairly easy to open and close. They clasp together perfectly so there's no gapping or losing your papers once they're in place. This two-inch size binder is spacious enough to hold large amounts of material and still easily turn pages. There are two flat interior pockets along both the front and back walls of the binder for holding additional materials. The clear plastic view holder for slipping documents or labels into the front cover, back or spine is a nice feature. In my particular binder, the plastic view panel on the front was a little puckered looking. Not a big deal for someone using it for home, school or work projects, but for a professional presentation I'd prefer a cleaner look and might purchase a higher-grade model. That said, I'm still very happy with the functionality of the binder and the sturdiness of the materials compared to other binders in this price range.

I use these all over the house to label things or put reminders on things.I've found them useful for:--Labeling garage sale prices--Putting on gift cards so I can record the balance--Label things when the batteries were last changed--Label remote controls so I know which device it goes to

60x sheets shredded at a time sounds impressive. And it would be if actually worked. However, the shredder I received shreds no more than 10-15 sheets at a time. The 60x refers to the capacity of the auto-feed drawer. You can put 60 sheets in there and they will get shredded (providing the machine doesn't jam; more on that later), but not simultaneously.The auto feeder works awesome if you have flat, unfolded sheets of paper free of staples, tape, or thick envelopes. It becomes nearly useless for my main purpose: shredding the insane number of credit card offers, Discover checks, and other junk mail that I receive. To successfully shred these items each and every one must be opened, flattened, and placed carefully in the auto feeder. If the shredder gets through half without jamming up, you're very lucky. Designed to save you time, I've found it takes MORE Of my time to use this shredder than a standard design. Frustrating.Another issue: the shredder is huge. 20-25% larger than an equivalently powered top-down shredder. Too large for my taste given the fact it doesn't do that great a job shredding junk mail.For stuff like computer print outs without creases or folds, the shredder works fantastic. If you're an accountant or tax preparer or someone else printing and shredding a lot of unfolded paper, this unit will work well. Otherwise, I'd recommend a standard, top mounted shredder.

Given the advertised special features of this Scotch tape, I was expecting it to be thicker and stickier than duct tapes I've used in the past, but it seems about the same as most in these respects.  (Note: Scotch doesn't advertise this as "duct tape," but I'll use duct tape as a comparable product for the sake of this review.)  In fact, some brands of duct tape I've used before seemed a little beefier and stickier, for whatever that's worth.  I rate this about the same as good-quality packing tape in these two categories.  The Scotch tape does not have perforations to assist with tearing as some duct tapes do, but it still tears just as easily as good packing tape if you use your teeth to get it started.I put the water-resistant claim to the test by filling a plastic jar with water and taping the opening closed with two strips of overlapping tape.  The tape was only stuck to the circular rim of the jar and not the sides.  When I flipped the jar over, not a drop of water escaped.As a control group, I repeated the same experiment with some clear (Henkel) packing tape that I bought at Costco.  The packing tape did start to leak water slowly in two areas when I flipped the jar over.  Although the Scott tape doesn't feel any stickier than the packing tape, it did indeed do a better job of holding the water in.  That said, I don't think I would trust this as anything more than a temporary patch for something like a leaking pipe, but at least in this experiment it seemed to do the job.The color is pretty true to what you see in the picture: Red with a slight touch of orange.Be advised this tape is about twice the price of regular duct tape, so unless you need the color or special features, you can save money by going with another product.  Otherwise, this Scotch tape seems to work well.

I have 2 kids that go through at least 10 pencils a week. Not to mention their friends that come over on the weekend it seems as if it's always sharpening. The good thing is that we haven't had any problems. It's so good that I purchased 2 for the math classes at the school. Great product worth the price.

This tape is different and much better than the standard tape of this type.  It's strong, tough and tear-proof.  It is also surprisingly flexible. It sticks very well to boxes and envelopes.  Where it's put, it stays.  It's a pleasure to use.  I don't know if it is a good value compared to lesser tapes that require more product, but the quality can't be beat.

This is a fantastic stapler. I've been using a mini 2" stapler for my home business, partly because it was cute and partly because it was dead cheap. I had no idea what a difference going up in size would make! With the mini, I struggled to staple a stack of pages, it always took a lot of effort. With this stapler, it was effortless! I was really shocked at the difference. And it's not a huge stapler, either.The downside, for me, is the stapler's appearance. It claims to be modern, but it looks "retro-cheap" to me, which is okay---except it's also very, very green. In the description photo, it looks like a pale lime green, very subdued, which happens to match my office decor. In person, it's a glow-in-the-dark neon green. We are talking BRIGHT! It reminds me of something I might have owned back in the 1980s!I will subtract a star for the fact that I hate the color. And I was disappointed that it didn't come with any staples. Fortunately, my mini stapler uses full-size staples, so I was able to load and test it right away. The staples went in easily, and stapling with it was absurdly easy! I'm already in love, I just wish the color wasn't quite so bright.Four stars, definitely recommended.

I used to use these types of pens in '80s. Glad to find them again. These pens work well in terms of mechanism. But, they are not high quality writing instruments. All colors write well but ink flow is typical of cheap ball point pens.Very happy with this product and I would recommend it to friends.

I teach ESL for young adults, and I'm always on the lookout for good organizers and new ways of communicating with students. Even young adults like the eye-catching colors! I use these to label my own work and write notes on homework for students. Very handy item!

Thirty dollars for a mouse pad? I asked myself.  Really?  I had to see what could possibly warrant the cost.  What I received surprised me.  This is probably the most comfortable, durable and resistant mouse pad I've ever used.  Oh, it's also huge.No, really.  It's huge.  Too big, in fact.  As you can see from all the reviews here, this thing is massive.  But look at the measurements for a moment.  It's almost a foot and a half by a foot, in length.  It's too big for my desk, which has to house a very large G19 keyboard, a G13 gameboard and now an almost two foot mousepad.  Be prepared, when you order this, for losing a good portion of your desk.That said, what we have here is a very, very nice mousepad.  It's made from cloth, with a rubber back so it doesn't slide.  So it's very comfortable rest your wrist on, but it's also incredibly durable.  I intentionally spilled a variety of liquids (water, Coke, etc.) on it and they pooled up, didn't soak in (even when I left it for an hour) and easily wiped away, without staining.  Very cool.  More importantly for competitive gamers, it offers no resistance.  You can swipe your mouse across it with ease, with no hiccups.I don't really know what else to say.  This cloth mouse pad surprised me.

First, as every other review has pointed out, this stuff is strong and capable and it's just not going to give way. And it's infinitely better than duct tape for almost everything duct tape does (so long as you ever want to remove it, and it's the King Hell of packing take (except that you can't use it to tape over labels as it would obscure them).I use it as packing tape but only in two cases:1) I sometimes ship heavy computers in boxes and even if the boxes are double-thick carboard, no amount of regular packing tape seems to me to be storng enough to make sure the bottoom (whichever the bottom may turn out to be during shipping) will hold. Carefully applied, one strip of this can do it, and maybe not all that much more expensively than numerous runs of a good quality clear packing tape.2) What I use it for more often is just to tape the edges. For instance, if I put a short piece of this at each end of the bottom of normal shipping box, I feel as though I'd made sure the bottom won't give way and then I can use regular packing tape that won't have to take much of the load just to seal where the flaps meet. This also makes it almost impossible for someone to catch on the edge of the box and pull it open.I can see that this would be good for places where you might want duct tape but want something more permanent, but I've always liked that duct tape can often be removed leaving only residue to clean and that's sure this true of this.Still at $22 I can't being myself to give it 5 stars, though I definitely would if i find it cheaper, and I assume buying in quantity wuold do that.
Buy HP ink and never get screwed, they just work as promised, the same goes for their printers too best in the business.

I wish I had something more positive to say about this file case, but it's very blah, especially for the price.  The cardboard seems sturdy enough, but I don't think it would hold up to long term and frequent use.  I think the case wrap would be very helpful in protecting the file case, and I think they should be sold as a set.  On it's own, the file case feels awkward to use. It's just not worth the high price.  If they cost 3.99 then I would likely buy several of them.

I love the wireless technology of this XP600 and the print quality is excellent. The ability to print on both sides of the paper is also an extremely helpful option. The photo tray is sturdy. The Swingline Standard Stapler, "Eco Version" is as a very cheap stapler that works well. It is very lightweight, and is mostly recycled plastic. This cork board is very basic but it works perfectly. There are no bells or whistles here but the price is good and it hangs easily with the included hardware. The frame is basically the same color as the cork which is something I really like; it doesn't stand out from other hangings in your room and blends in nicely.This also happens to be the best size; it's not too big, not too small and pretty much fits everywhere without overwhelming the area. I did notice that the punch pins will go through the back of the board if you push them in all the way. I generally angle my pins down so this isn't a problem for me but it may be for others. I already own a laminator but is only 6" wide.  I work in a college library and sometimes I have to make signs and this laminator just fit the bill.  You can laminate a full-size page. This stand is sturdy and provides two shelves to organize your items below the printer.  I like that it has wheels to give the option to move around.Installation was pretty straightforward.  The box didn't come with adequate packing though so my husband had to adjust one of the sides that got bent in the mail. This label maker is very easy to use.  After inserting AAA batteries, you simply drop in your desired tape cartridge, consult a Quick Users Guide, and you're ready to start printing.  You can change fonts, add graphics, frames, etc.  The print quality is crisp and clear, and there is not a lot of empty "wasted space" on either side of the printed text. Expandable Desk File Sorter offers a quick, convenient and professional organization for on the go or as a sturdy temporary filing system, great for household bills, or small business invoices and receipts.

I love this idea! Precut pieces, 2" in length, and easy to lift off.So this particular package comes with two desk dispensers and 2 wrist dispensers. The wrist ones need loading with one of the 6 refills included, the desk ones come preloaded. Note: the desk dispensers say they are not able to be reloaded, though they seem like they would be able to.I gave the wrist dispensers to my kids for their craft boxes, and they love it! No more fussing about how the tape won't cut properly, and no more me worrying about their fingers getting cut on the sharp part. Yes, it runs out, but I have a few refills to tide me over for now.The desk dispensers are cool because they don't need adhesive to stay on. Just put them on the desk, and the very light suction cup action works as you pull straight up on the tape. A cool concept.Overall, a great product!
these things hold like two drops of ink! soooo small and pro9000 printer wastes last bit of it. wish tanks were bigger and used up all ink before you have to change it.

One of my former coworkers kept a balance call in her office and most often used it in place of her office chair.  Great for keeping your core active and not slumping into bad posture while working.  But there are drawbacks to having just a ball for your chair, including that it can roll into things and possibly get a hole.This chair combines the good parts of sitting on a balance ball and a chair that will stay put.It comes in a much smaller box than you expect and that is because there is some assembly required.  It was easy to put together.  It took a little care to make sure the deflated ball went into the fabric cover facing the right direction.  A little hand pump is included to inflate the ball.  If you have some kind of electric air pump it will be much faster to inflate.  Once the ball is inflated and the plug put in place, you screw the legs on and you are done.I find it comfortable for my home office.  I periodically think about bringing it to work but don't want someone to walk off with it to another building so for now it stays home.  I have cats, including one who still has her claws, but they have so far left this alone.The only downside is that the only height adjustment is to let air out of the ball so you sit lower.

Overall a very comfy chair for a tall/large person.  Looks great.  However the back can occasionally become dislodge from the seat and you have to put it back together.  It has a very simple hook & clamp that attaches the back to the seat and for whatever reason it pops out of place about once a week for me.  It's great that assembly is so easy but not at the cost of the chair falling apart time to time.

Avery Self-Adhesive Laminating SheetsI've used self-adhesive laminating sheets in the past with great success, so I decided to try Avery's brand. These sheets are not overly thick and are easy to use. I love the guide lines printed on the backing paper, this helps with trimming the sheets to fit your project. I first used two of these laminating sheets to protect a fastener torque chart for use in the garage. I frequently come across fasteners on cars/motorcycles where I may not have the service manual to tell me the recommended torque, so I found a sheet with recommended values based on the grade of the bolt and thread diameter. The laminating sheets help protect the chart so I can keep it handy in the workshop.Air bubbles seem easy to expel using the Avery sheets, and it was easy to trim without leaving any gooey adhesive.Overall: 5/5 stars, great value for a small box of 50 sheets. Very easy to use.

This is a very nice cork board.  It does not feel cheap or flimsy in any way.  It's quite large and you could fit quite a good deal of pins on it.  The cork stays very nice even when adding and removing pins and doesn't show much signs of wear.  If you're looking for a cork board, this is a good one.

What's not to like?  The Inspire has a small footprint, a relatively quick warm-up routine (mine takes just under 6 minutes), and it laminates effectively.  You're out of the box, plugged in, and securely and cleanly encasing cards, paper, and other thin stock within moments -- there's little to no learning curve here -- turn it on, slide your material(s) between the plastic sheets, when the green light comes on you insert the pre-sealed end first so as not to suffer any bubbles or jamming.  Moments later everything is out the other end, cool to the touch and impeccably sealed.  Unlike some other laminators I've used, the plastic seals right up against the edge of the cards I first tried (with very little variance) allowing a nice close cut and a minimal amount of plastic 'bezel' around the edges.  After each use it's recommended that you run the included cleaning media through (a thin piece of cardboard, effectively) a couple times to remove any run-off/waste, which likewise takes no time at all.Hard not to glow about an economical unitasking device that serves its purpose efficiently.

When I got these labels, I set them aside until I wanted to make labels for some ring binders. When I grabbed them I was surprised to find that they were totally blank. I guess I thought they'd have the pattern you see on the front of the package. Actually, they can have that pattern, but I didn't end up printing out labels until a few days later when I had more time because I first went to the Avery site where you can design your labels online, I entered the product number and nothing happened. It just didn't work. So, I downloaded the actual on-your-computer software (PC only) and came back later to install it, only to find that there were zero templates for these labels. I think it was probably just because they are so new, and when I later went back to try the online version AGAIN the product ID did bring up a number of templates.I guess I'm somewhat of a design snob, I have a lot of experience with Adobe and other graphics programs and I feel it's better to make it yourself otherwise you FEEL like you're creating something when really you're just pasting in the same permutations that everyone else is. AND YET, I had more fun than I thought I would using the Avery Design and Print interface. They have quite a few options, the interface is pretty easy with just a little poking around, and you can add your own images, work in layers and really just design the heck out of it. Then, you can save your file to your computer OR save it in your free account on their site (which is easy) and access it later from anywhere.After designing my labels, I printed them out from my browser print dialogue and I thought they came out looking really nice! I put them on the spines of some 1 1/2" binders, as well as on the fronts, and that worked pretty well for me although these labels are a little taller than 1 1/2", causing me to curve the edge around the binder a bit and the next day I found that part of the label had curled up a bit. Maybe the labels stick better to some surfaces than others, but they are supposed to be designed to wrap around, so I was a bit surprised. I think Avery makes other labels just for binder spines, so that might have been a better option for me.Finally, I downloaded the app to my iPad mini and tried using it to design a label. It does a good job of imitating the look and feel of the website. I did find that you are going to have problems using it without an Internet connection, so that's too bad since my tablet only has wifi and I imagined it would be fun to design labels on the train. Once you are ready to print the label, the app saves it (remotely) as a PDF and opens it in Safari for you, and you can print it out from there, assuming you have a printer already set up to print with your device. Otherwise, you can always save it and print it from another computer or device later.

If you are looking for a basic home printer that will print the kids homework assignments, pictures, and don't need a lot of the heavy-duty processing power that you expect from your printer at work, this is an excellent cost-effective choice.It detects and connects easily to home wireless networks -- you would think this would be a given but my last home printer ... a Canon PIXMA constantly had to go through the set-up cycle in order to get it to work each time you wanted to print -- and half time time you had to go through manual setup for that.However, Epson continues to need to do better quality control of their install software.  I also had the opportunity to test and review the big brother of this printer:Epson WorkForce 840 Color Ink Jet Wireless All-in-One with Fax (C11CA97201)and I reported problems with the install software giving an "error" most of the way through the install process.Specifically, "no matter how many different computers I installed it on (2 running windows 7, one running Vista), the install software always ended with an error. Fortunately, it got far enough to where I was able to add the printer using the Windows 7 utility and everything works perfectly. So if you are comfortable trouble shooting and adding devices on your own, this won't be a big deal. If you are not, then you will get frustrated and have to call tech support (which I did not do)."As with the Epson WorkForce printer, the build quality of this feels rather "light weight" in comparison to other printers oriented towards the home office user.  However, I have not had any problems since I don't tend to expect to slam paper drawers closed or expect printers in this price point to take the kind of abuse that we would subject our "work" printers to.Again, if you want a printer that just plain works ( at least once you get it installed on your network ) for a reasonable price point, I'm a new convert to Epson printers.  I will not buy another Canon product and while the build quality seems less durable than HP printers, the ease of use outweighs any features that HP could put forth.[NCJVR]
These 3M labels perform as expected and secure nicely to the envelopes.

I tend to read a lot of non-fiction books.  These Notetabs are perfect when I want to mark pages I find worth reading again.In the past I have tried those yellow sticky pad squares or transparent page markers.  I would also bend the corner of the page or just tear off a piece of paper and leave it in the page.  None of these worked very well. The yellow sticky pad squares fall off easily and the transparent page markers get me to a page but do little else and they tend to fall off the page as well.These Notetabs are great. I can stick the whole Notetab on a page and just leave it there.  Because of the size it will not fall off. If I plan to leave it in a book permanently I can even highlight the Notetab without damaging the book. I actually placed one of these in a book and put a yellow sticky square on it. I then wrote on the yellow sticky square and reused the Notetab after I was done with the book.I do find these a bit thick for some books. Instead of repeating what many other long reviews have already said, let me just point out a few things:1) The MX model name stands for Multi-function with faX.  This is also known as a 4-in-1 printer, as it prints, scans, copies, and faxes.  The fax part works both incoming and outgoing.2) Photo print quality is simply excellent, as with all Canon inkjet printers.  I had an HP that cost almost as much and it not only lacked many of the MX870's functions but printed photos rather poorly.  That's what made me come back to Canon.3) Text print quality is very good.  I use my cheap (under 70 bucks) Brother laser monochrome for text printing.4) Canon is the company that started using individual inkjet tanks which is convenient and may save money.  I say "may" because inkjet cartrdiges are cheap nowadays so having individual tanks is no longer a big cost advantage as it used to be.  Still, the convenience is worth something.5) You can do double-sided scanning, copying and printing.  Both source and output can be double-sided.6) Initial setup took me 10 minutes mainly because it was a pain to remove all the orange protective tape as well as install the print head, which comes sealed in a separate package and not pre-installed.  Installing the first ink tank was a little scary but after that it was a breeze to install the other ink tanks.7) Software installation, on Vista and XP, took about 15 minutes for the Easy Install option.  I connected this to one laptop using USB and the other laptops (XP and Vista) via wi-fi.TIP: if you have a Vista or Win7 PC, use that PC to set up the initial wireless function on the MX870.  Vista and Win7 have this awesome Windows Connect Now feature which makes wireless setup of the MX870 a complete breeze, no matter how your wi-fi network is configured.You only need to set up the wireless function on the MX870 once.  You do need to install the printer driver and turn on wireless printer connection on each PC, but the software installer takes care of that.8) Canon's software suite is just great, making scanning and printing very easy to carry out.  This is something that really distinguishes Canon multi-functions from other brands.9) I did a lot of research before settling on this Canon and I've been very happy with all aspects of it.

Who was the idiot who came up with the idea for whiteboards in the workplace? What exactly was wrong with blackboards and chalk? Every company I visit, no matter how how high tech or cool, has nonfunctional whiteboards. The markers are inevitably dried out - which one does not find out until they are tried, followed by a frantic search for fresh markers. This little dance is repeated a million times every day in conference rooms across America. Then the marks are impossible to clean by dry rubbing. Even at their best, whiteboard drawings look ugly compared to elegant, organic chalk on slate. But they're cheap you say? Cheap to buy maybe. But let's compare the time and motion involved in erasing a blackboard vs. whiteboard. Ready? Here we go:Need to erase blackboard. Implement the following steps:1. Rub eraser on blackboard. In a pinch, use your hand.Need to erase whiteboard. Implement the following steps:1. Root around until you find your 3M Whiteboard Eraser. Take it to breakroom sink.2. Run water on it.3. Your hands are now wet. Dry them with paper towels.4. Walk back to conference room trying to hold dripping 3M Whiteboard Eraser without getting water on your clothes.5. Wipe whiteboard with dripping 3MWE.6. Whiteboard marks have now been, not removed exactly, but rather smeared into large wet diluted splotches.7. Go back to breakroom for more paper towels.8. Back to conference room to wipe up and dry whiteboard. Discard paper towels.9. Back to breakroom to wash your hands again and dry.10. Need to erase again? 3MWE has dried out, take it back to water faucet ..Let's see, assuming average industrial cost of a professional with overhead of $100 per hour, and we estimate the company has just spent about 25 bucks (not counting the paper towels, water and trash removal) to ERASE THE WHITEBOARD ..

I am reviewing this product for what it is, not what some people think it is. This product is a fire box, not a true safe. What that means is that it will keep your items (documents, etc) safe during a fire and perhaps a flood, but it is NOT a secure container designed to defeat straight-up theft. Anyone with a screwdriver or stout knife can defeat the locking mechanism on this product. Again, as a fire box, it is stout, sturdy and rated to last quite a bit of time. Note: I have not personally tested this item under those conditions (and never hope to). The product also has a cool, professional design to it. All I ask is that you know what you are buying and what you are hoping to get out of it. For what it is, it's perfect!

I love Sharpie products, but this is the first one that really disappointed me. The pencil is ergonimically designed and looks very chic, but the graphite ink delivery is very inconsistent; lines of written out will be solid or choppy depending on how the ballpoint can deliverthe ink.  I have tested the pencil on different types of paper and it works the best on the yellow business pad.  It does not write well on glossy paper like all liquid gel inks and will smear.  Erasability will depend on how much force is exerted when you write, if you write lightly, then it erases cleanly, but if you writing leaves impressions on the paper then residue is left on the paper and you cannot fully erase the ink.  You can use any type of eraser to erase the liquid ink which one of the good characteristics of this pencil.  If you want improvement do not hesitate to contact Sharpie, it's a company that seems to emphasize improvement, which is why the retractable sharpie writing instruments have improved, they do not dry our as fast as the initially pens.  I look forward the the next redesign of this new pencil, but currently the pencil just does not measure up to the original lead or barrel based pencils.

Documents of 6 sheets seemed to be the (lower) limit for consistency.I have had no problem with smudging, even with a slightly moist hand trailing over the lines as part of my drawing lines from right to left (I am right-handed) -- A real plus for the sinister.As claimed, these pens did start quickly, even after having sat unused for 4 days (unlike many of the other stick pens I wind up with).-- Douglas B. Moran

I like this printer despite my vow to not use Cannon again.  I had a run-in with the company when I purchased their Pixma Pro-100 ($400) a year ago.  Canon failed to honor their rebate (others had the same problem) and I couldn't get any response from the company when I questioned it.  But wonderful Amazon refunded my money and my old Canon Pixma was resurrected and still works like a charm.Computer - iMac OSXConnection - USBImage Editor - Photoshop CCPapers Types - Canon Pro Luster 13x19, Plus Gloss II 8.5x11No problems with setup.  I work in an IT setting and you never use the software that comes with hardware - always download the latest version from the manufacturer's website before you hook up the hardware.  As of today, the latest driver version for Lion is 10.85 (1/6/14).First I printed a test page from dpreview and used the Glossy II paper that came with the printer.  Perfect print.No problems printing 13x19.  The size choice was clearly labeled under Print Settings - Paper Size, and the paper type was selected under Print Settings - Quality and Media - Photo Paper - Luster, Print Quality - High (via Photoshop).  It took maybe 15 seconds to move the 180 mb image to the printer, the printer took over a minute to warm up before starting the print,  and it took less than a minute to print.  I printed a family photo and it was just spectacular.  The colors were true to life and details were sharp, despite my having to slightly increase the pixel size of the photo.After printing the two photos, I was down 20% on my inks.  That explains why I reserve the photo printer for photo-quality prints I have to have right now.  Otherwise, I use my color laser or send the prints out for printing.No settings for Vellum and I didn't have any at home to test with. No problems printing borderless.I don't like mixing functionalities so the lack of duplex printing, scanning, and faxing is perfect.  Given the ink usage, I also won't miss a paper tray for printing multiple copies.Size - This printer is bigger than I like but I occasionally make 13x19 prints so the size is necessary.Weight - as a former owner of an HP-1 (1991) that weighed about 100 pounds (and cost around $1000), this is like styrofoam and a third of the height.I really like this printer and think the price it great but would use it more if the ink didn't cost so much.  Assuming I can get 5 each of 19x13 and 8.5x11 prints from each set of cartridges, and I replaced them with Canon cartridges sold here for $26, it would cost me, on average, $2.60 per print for ink.  Seems reasonable but still a factor.If you want to improve your printing expertise, I highly recommend the online training course "Inkjet Printing for Photographers with Ben Long" at lynda dot com. I take about 10 hours a month of software training there and this was the most useful course I have taken in years.

I am always finding things I want to remember in books I'm reading and these page markers are the perfect size. I needed some letter size file folders, so I thought I'd give these a try. I find them to be sturdy, with handy larger size tabs and cutouts.Pro:+ These are constructed of pretty heavy stock. They do a good job of holding the paper.+ 10% recycled content - not much, but it is something.+ The material holds both indelible and normal ink well, with no running.+ The tabs are wider than normal. I was so disappointed that the biggest setting was not big enough for my Lyra Color-Giants colored pencils used by my child. It is quite heavy -- much heavier than my other Safco drafting chair, but rolls easily on its closed casters. Just plugged in the dongle and worked great with Powerpoint 2013. Battery pre-installed with a pull tab was a nice touch too. And easy to open blister pack to boot. Would definitely buy again.

I would call these average boxes. They're sturdy enough to stack a couple high (though if I was packing them solid with paper, I wouldn't go 4 high) and they're nice looking boxes. The finish of the outside of the box is not glossy so you can write on it with anything - marker, pen, pencil, brush...However, "attached lids" mean you need a razor blade or utility to score/detach them neatly. All I had was a pair of scissors. I tried both pretending one scissor half was a blade and cutting with the scissors properly - both messed up the edge a little. Just tearing them was a nightmare. The other perforations that needed to be cut to assemble the box actually tore without problem if I was careful.The cardboard is a little thin - the sides bent a few times during assembly. At this price point I would have expected thicker cardboard.

Out of the box, the machine was slightly bulkier than I expected; but it had a nice aero-dynamic shape and fit nicely in the palm of my hands. The LCD screen is kinda small and not backlit but still clearly visible. The plastic on the unit is of good(but not great) quality.The rubber buttons on the unit are placed kind of close together so it might be easy to mispress an unintended button. There are many different options for styles, borders, sizes, and colors. With the middle navigation button, it is a breeze to shuffle thru the variety of font options and sizes.The machine automatically stores/saves up to 30 different label designs. Installation of the print cartridge is quick and easy. You just pop open the back compartment and pop in the label cartridge. The unit has an A/C adaptor slot but does not come with an A/C adaptor.There's an included symbol list illustrating all the designs available in the machine. The actual printing is pretty quick. The results look nice and solid. The label protective paper is a little tough to peel off from the label sticker.The label itself sticks securely to most surfaces. The only potential negative is that the machine does not come with an A/C adaptor. Overall a versatile machine that is fun and nice to play around with. You might end up spending a lot on replacement cartridges though.4.5 stars

A very nice product to review for the Vine this time, and pretty much the top of the line in this class.  I had one unfortunate experience with it, and that was due to my router, not the printer.  After setting up the basics of the printer function, I was going to network it.  I understand, (a friend said he did that is the last model) in the past it had to be networked first. I was hopefull to use the easy method, because my Netgear router had a network WPS button.  It didn't work unfortunately. After a few frustrating hours, I did a websearch for someone to answer the issue, and paid one of those online firms to set-up my network. It cost me $24.00, money well spend in this case.  Had I known what I was reading in the checklist for the printer, and that I even had a Mac filter, I could have fixed it. Sadly, the router didn't explain the checkbox in one of the screens that turned on Mac filtering.  All this to tell you that, as soon as he unchecked it, pushed the connect button on the router, the printer network request worked perfectly, and I was wirelessly networked.Now ready to go, I put paper in the paper tray, scanned a photo, it opened up the software on the PC automatically. Then I sent the image back to the printer to print it. It came out great, very fast, after the printer did it's warm up dance.  I've always wanted an ink jet with this ink feature, this since I saw the Brother about 10 years ago with the single color cartridge method.  Ink is cheaper, and you don't throw away unused ink, when you run out of one color.  My other printer is a compact HP, so that it fits underneath my keyboard in a compact computer kiosk.  I don't use the Cannon there, but surprisingly I could have fit the same compact space.  I don't like those big things, with all the fancy paper feeders, that look like office printers.  This has the one office printer feature I do like, a paper cartridge.Being able to network wirelessly, makes it able to use it as a copier, without going to the computer all the time. BTW, when I was running Explorer 8, there was a nice connect toolbar to use the printer on the web.  Unfortunately, it would not connect to Explorer 9. There was a marker on the Explorer 9 install, showing Cannon was working on the software changes, but It's not out yet as so this review.  Not a problem, just a temporary inconvenience.  This printer has all the bells and whistles, data cards, USB, etc. I give it a thumbs up.

One of the main things I like about this tape compared to others I have used is that it is not overly sticky so you don't have to muscle it off the roll. It is flexible but just sturdy enough to not fold over on itself.  This is polypropylene film reinforced with glass yarns with specially formulated rubber resin adhesive. The foam wrist wrest is very firm, though comfortable enough.  It's just not soft like some other gel products. This mouse pad has a no-slide mat that does keep it in place.  The surface has an antimicrobial coating, which is claimed to reduce stains and odor.I hadn't had the wrist rest before, and it is worth the extra few dollars.  Overall, this product worked just fine for me.

I wanted to like this product.  In fact, I wanted to love it, because it's a well-known name and I love their other products, but this fell short...badly!  It could have been that I had a defective product, but why take a chance in the future?I love that the product itself is bright and colorful.  It's tactile in the way that it has finger grips, essentially telling you how to hold this and how to maneuver it.  It is re-fillable, easy to open, and it looks like a product that would be great for craft projects galore!When I went to use this, it would give about 50% of the time. Projects then take twice the amount of time they should.Then I thought, I must be holding this wrong or something, so I played around with it. This is supposed to come with alphabetical, numbered and monthly tabs so you can customize the dividers, but it only came with alphabetical tabs. There are two little pockets for index cards, but only one index card was provided. These are minor quibbles, because it's easy enough to make your own paper labels and insert them in the tabs. Some of the nice things about this organizer are: alternating dividers are blue and clear, which helps when looking up items; there's a textured exterior, which makes it easy to grasp and doesn't show fingerprints; since it's plastic, you can wipe it down and not worry about it crumbling the way old Kraft paper organizers did over time; there's a clear inset on the cover flap, so you can see your labels without having to open the organizer. If you have multiple organizers, this saves time and is very neat. It's an attractive folder overall. One small note: unlike those old accordion folders, the bottom doesn't expand, so if you stuff this to the brim (it claims to hold 600 sheets) you won't be able to fasten the cover flap. The fastener is an elastic loop and plastic button; the elastic doesn't go all the way around the folder like those accordion files. Overall, this seems like a very useful tool. I'm using it to temporarily store papers until I get around to formally filing them, instead of letting loose pages pile up on my desk. For that, I'm not using alphabetical, numeric or monthly tabs - instead, I made my own tabs for topics like Bills, Bank Statements and the like. I think this is pretty handy and it looks fine on my desk.

When I first reviewed this chair I kind of came down hard on it only giving it three stars because although it was a great looking chair, the seat cushion is a little bit harder than I would like. I find that if I sit all the way back with good posture it is just fine. I looked into chair cushions to add on top of it, but decided I can live with this the way it is. It's tough to find something in black leather, and then if you place some tan cloth thing on top it makes you look like you have back problems even though you don't have any.Ok now that we got that out of the way, there are things I do love about the chair. It is hydraulically controlled to lift the chair to the height you desire, and it has a handy release mechanism that allows you to lean the chair back. My old chair leaned back no matter what and it leaned so you were always working in a leaning position.The overall look of this chair is first class. It has the aesthetics down pat. For a chair of this price range it looks top drawer. Assembly was easy. Always start all bolts leaving them loose in order to be able to properly align them all, and then when you are done tighten them all up. After saying all of that, if I could find a super comfortable chair pad I really would love this chair a lot. The one other concern is that although it is leather, it is a very thin variety of it. Already there is a small poke through tear on the side. This isn't something like Texan raw hide leather. I like the idea of "Fine Italian Leathers" soft to the touch but tough enough to withstand normal treatment. I don't plan on abusing this chair, but until I find the special seat cushion I am having a "Hard" time cherishing it. If I find one, or if anyone has any suggestions please leave a comment. Amazon has some right here but with mixed reviews. They even have them in faux leatherTUSH CUSH Home Office Orthopedic Large Computer Ergonomic Seat Cushion Original - Carbon Executive Faux Leather VinylThere are several different cushion models available and that is just one of them.UPDATE: It is a year later. I have found the hydraulic cylinder that supports the seat height which is adjustable all of a sudden decides to slowly let go. It gives you a steady ride down to the bottom position within it's range. So you are sitting there adjusted to the height that you like, and every few days it does this 5 second time period drop. Just like letting air out of a tire. It is not a health hazard like a sudden drop but a drop nonetheless. So I am going to see how good their customer service and warranty is since it is under warranty, and request a new cylinder. I will let you know how I made out.PS: I have grown to love the chair and sit on it daily as I am now typing this.BINGO UPDATE 2: Hon is now on my favorite best chair company list. I called them out of the blue and told them of the hydraulic problem. All the customer representative did was ask me what the serial number was on the bottom of the chair. He didn't know who I was or anything, and he just said, "That is still covered under warranty, and please provide me with your name and address in order to send the replacement part to." Bingo I should expect to receive it within about 5 days. When I was on hold the recorded message was playing saying the following, "We can repair it, or they will replace the whole chair, or refund the full purchase price". This is their standard warranty policy. That's a WOW. It says this is a 5 year warranty. I ordered this on May 17, 2012, and it is now May 22nd 2013 so it has been over a year. I didn't have to produce an invoice, etc. etc. etc. So this is a company to deal with. All of a sudden my chair feels a lot more comfortable.

8/29/2013:I am editing this review to state that, since I reviewed it, the price of these books from this seller has skyrocketed. + Pros:+ Three different settings for notebook height.+ Latches keep riser in place.+ Swivel in the back to rotate the notebook.- Cons:- Cannot adjust height while notebook is on the riser.I usually use the desktop computer in our house because our Dell notebook is hard for me to type on. Using a flat keyboard on a flat surface never worked well for me, so I was eager to try this out.The riser is surprisingly light, and in all honesty I didn't think it would hold our 10lb notebook, but it held up with no problem. I was able to move the notebook from side to side on the swivel base, the latching was very sturdy, and my posture felt better looking straight ahead at the screen, as opposed to my usual table hunching.Logitech's instructions were very easy to follow - I've uploaded some samples, they're all in picture format. This will take you no time at all to set up.The only flaw with this product is the riser height cannot be changed without removing the notebook first. When I tried, it was very uncomfortable.Overall, this is a great product and I would definitely recommend it for notebook users.

I've used these to print a few sheets of return-address labels, and I really like them.Ease of peel: Almost perfect. They do come off easily, but not so easily I can bend the paper back and get 10 off at once. For single-label removing it's great. Tearing off the side leaves a tiny bit of each label free, enough for you to grab so you don't have to scrape off every label.Look: I love how they are translucent. The ink stands out nice and sharp, and the address seems more clear. It looks professional and pretty.Printing: (HP LaserJet) No problems. I was surprised at how crisp the ink was, and how there was no smudging right after it came off the printer. (I'm used to getting ink on my fingers.) Also, using the 'Mailing Labels' 'US Letter Small' presets printing from Address Book (on a Mac) the labels were all printed right (makes my life easier).Price: There are labels you can get for half the price. If you do a lot of printing these may not be economical. But if it's for rather infrequent use, I favor the performance and look of these labels over saving a few dollars.I recommend giving them a try.

There is not much to say about labels. You expect to be able to print well onto them, and have them adhere well onto packages. Unfortunately, these labels only accomplish the latter. They are promoted as accepting both ink and laser toner, but in my Brother laser printer, I tried to print both UPS and USPS labels onto them and the print quality was so terrible that I had to reprint onto plain white labels. I feared the carriers would not accept labels with degraded bar codes. It seems the printing surface of these labels is too fibrous to accept the toner well, and it even smudged a little after printing. In non-critical situations this might be fine, but not when printing bar codes. The adhesive seemed strong and durable, however.Having labels that blend in with corrugated boxes is a nice idea, but not at the expense of usability or print quality.

First I'll get out my gripe: I've installed over half a dozen wireless printers over the past few years, and I can say that this one was the least intuitive. With my Epson printer, I just went through the network setup, let it find my router, and then typed in my WEP password. This won't let you do that - or at least I couldn't figure out how to input alphanumeric keys - so I ended up having to connect to the printer via USB, and then for some reason with the software on the disc I couldn't get my computer to recognize the printer, until I went to Canon's site and found the right driver and downloaded and installed it manually.  It works fine now, but took a lot longer than I'm used to.Apart from that, this is a nice low-end printer, suitable for the home office or small family. One of the advantages of going with a Canon is that their color printouts and photos are quite good. If you print on photo paper, it looks like something that was professionally developed.  I can't say that for my Epson printers, which are faster, but tend to botch photos.  Otherwise as far as ordinary printing goes, this is a decent low-end printer, not too fast but not slow either.  It won't do two sided, and it doesn't hold a very large stack of paper, so you have to get up and add paper every 20 sheets or so.  It scans just fine, and you can send a scan directly to your computer wirelessly.  I haven't tried the fax since I don't ever need to, but I'd say this I'm overall quite happy with the quality of the output on this machine and would gladly recommend it for someone with moderate printing needs, especially if those needs include printing the occasional photograph.
I order this glue for my 1st graders and they love it. It holds the projects very well and they seem to last a little longer than RoseArt and the dollar store brands.
Staples are Staples... But the packaging for this box of staples is wonderful! Since this is for home use, I doubt I will need more staples for the next 50 years, but I would order more if I did!

Excellent Post-It notes. For me these are the right size, useful & practical. This sample pack came in multiple colors, not bound to each other, which I appreciated. Whoever invented these had a great idea. I did not notice them being more "stickier" than older Post-It notes. They work great.

...this all in one does an excellent job at all four of its tasks: printing, scanning, copying and faxing.Way back when, audiophiles were convinced of a direct relationship between the number of separate components you had and the quality of sound that came out of them. The concept of an "all in one" anything meant none of the functions would be done well. Nine years ago, when I bought my first inexpensive all in one, this old audiophile concept held up: it was pretty bad at all of its functions (print, scan, copy).Good news, everyone: those days are gone.The Workmate 635 does all of four of its functions pretty well, and offers three connection options (USB, Ethernet and wireless). I chose Ethernet (to free up a rear USB port on the desktop it's paired with). It holds 250 sheets of paper, and lets you print from memory cards and make copies without being connected to a computer. This is the fastest inkjet printer I've ever used.Image scanning offers options to save as .jpg, .bmp, .pdf or .tif formats. Bundled OCR software allows you to scan text documents into editable Word and .pdf formats.Two small things keep this from five stars: printing may be fast, but is also rather noisy...especially when printing text. Also, even though the included drivers on the installation CD claimed to have installed successfully, they did not. After visiting the Epson website, I was able to download the most current drivers, and then it installed fine.Overall, an excellent performer at this price.

The MFC-9320cw Digital Color All-in-One prints, copies, scans and faxes with high quality up to 600 x 2400 dpi, contains a 35-page capacity auto document paper feeder and provides easy access to install and replace toner cartridges.  But its key features are what makes the 9320cw ideal for small office or business where value and performance are required.Flexible networking means you can share documents  via Ethernet or wireless connectivity as well as with the standard wired connection.Fax flexibility with stand-alone or PC faxing.Direct Print/Scan means you can print from or scan to your USB flash memory drive (not included in package)Copying occurs at a speedy 17ppm with black and white or color, and the paper tray has a 250 sheet capacity, however, for business cards, posters and other thick papers, there's a nifty manual feed.This all-in-one replaced a trusty HP Deskjet workhorse, and I can say the results have been surprisingly good.  I have tested it in print, scan and fax mode and found it fast and efficient.  I even printed two sheets of my business cards with better-than-average results.  Does it print as well as my HP photo deskjet?  No, the first copies were a tad disappointing, however, after tweaking the advanced adjustments, I got color that is almost as good, and since most of my work does not involve photo printing, this is quite acceptable.Installation was a snap. (I used the wired hookup.)  Directions are easy to follow with screen prompts.  Setup was accomplished in less than fifteen minutes and this for a person who has never before installed an all-in-one printer.I have only two nits: this unit does not offer duplex printing, so two-sided copies must be done manually and I occasionally get a message that the yellow and cyan toner cartridges are low, when this is not the case.  Another reviewer has made similar comments.  The message disappears when I reboot so is not a problem, but rather an annoyance.  I would give this printer two thumbs up.Addendum:  the above based on initial review.  Now, less than six months later and with only about 250 sheets of paper copied, already the color toner cartridges are empty.  For a machine that's supposed to give 1000 copies per cartridge, this is pretty dismal, given the price of cartridges.Addendum 2:  I replaced the toner cartridges and am again getting the "Toner Low" message after less than 100 copies run.  What's up with that?  Also, the Manual Feed works abysmally with thick paper.  I get a "Jam Inside" message whenever I attempt to run business cards or any 90 weight paper.  Powering the machine off and removing/reinserting the toner cartridges/drums 10 or 12 times for each sheet run is frustrating to say the least.  At first Brother Support told me it was my word processing program that was causing it but it happens with every program.  I am still waiting for another response from Brother.  In the meantime, choose this machine with reservations.Addendum 3:  I hate to keep adding edits but felt this is worth knowing.  Google "Toner Override" for the Brother machine and choose the solution offered for each affected toner cartridge.  I did this, and voila!, I now have the black toner working perfectly.  I am surprised Brother Support hasn't mentioned this.  It sure saves $$ on a new cartridge bought prematurely.

இ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:ѾѾѾѾ Recommended with warm fuzzies.I have been using this Lapinator Plus! for almost four years now.  Since then, I have acquired two more laptop pads/stands equipped with cooling fans, but they are sized for my 15-inch and smaller laptops.  My original requirements consisted of three needs when using my 17-inch laptop on my lap: 1) the portable pad/stand/desk had to securely support my fairly heavy 17-inch laptop, but still be portable and light enough to pack into my large-sized Timbuk2 messenger bag, 2) the platform had to provide some way to keep both my lap and my laptop cooler, and 3) even though my mouse does work adequately on uneven surfaces such as moving it across my bare or clothed lap, sofa armrest, chair, or carpet, I wanted a flat platform where I could move my mouse for situations where I needed finer mouse control.  For brief periods of casual usage, I am okay with using laptop touchpads.  But I would MUCH rather prefer using a mouse overall, especially when it comes to working with graphics and photo editing software for extended periods.  And so this larger-sized "Plus!" model of the Lapinator combined with the removable Mousitizer mouse pad works well for me.More of the Lapinator Plus' features are described and rated below:ѾѾѾѾѾ Excellent 5-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾѾѾ This is a light, portable, simple, and durable design.  Unlike some laptop pads and mats that utilize cooling fans, there is no extra fan noise from the Lapinator's "passive" cooling approach of propping the laptop up on its three self-adhesive bumpers.  I originally wondered how long the three bumpers would remain stuck onto the pad since these bumpers both keep the laptop cooler and also hold the laptop in place.  But so far after four years of weekly (not daily) usage and frequently being packed into my Timbuk2 laptop messenger bag or other luggage, the bumpers are still stuck on.  If a bumper did eventually fall off (and hopefully I would notice it and find it after it fell off), I could easily glue it back onto the pad.  Without the three bumpers, the cooling effects of raising your laptop from the surface of the Lapinator would be lost, and the laptop would slide around on the surface more.  If you end up losing two of the three rubber bumpers, you can replace them with adhesive-backed stick-on picture frame rubber bumpers.  Note that some of the Lapinator photos may show it with only two bumpers attached to the pad, but this Lapinator Plus! comes with three circular bumpers/risers.ѾѾѾѾ The Lapinator pad has a slight bit of flex to it and is not totally rigid, but since I travel a fair bit with my Lapinator, I happily prefer its light weight instead of a more rigid and heavier pad/desk/stand.  Its overall construction quality and durability seem to be pretty good.  The Lapinator weighs 15.1 ounces and the Mousitizer mouse pad adds another 5.2 ounces.  So compare this 20.3 ounce total weight to other laptop desks/stands/pads that can support a 17-inch laptop and decide for yourself whether lightweight portability is a factor for you.  By comparison, I have a 25.8 ounce laptop pad that only supports a 15-inch laptop; that 15-inch laptop pad is made of plastic, does not have a mouse pad area, and has one cooling fan.  I have heard of other people who had the surface of their Lapinator pad warp due to heat from the laptop, but after almost four years of weekly (not daily) usage, the surface of my pad is still smooth and flat.  Perhaps that is because after even a full day of constant usage, the surface of my laptop's keyboard still remains fairly cool (without any additional forced-air convection cooling other than the laptop's internal fan)?  If your laptop regularly feels very warm during usage, perhaps you should look at other pads that offer one, two, or even three cooling fans for better cooling.ѾѾѾѾѾ The Velcro cord strap at the rear of the Lapinator is very handy for holding onto the power cord and mouse cord (if you do not use a wireless mouse).  You would think that ALL laptop stands and desks should offer some kind of mechanism for managing cords dangling from your laptop when it sits on your lap, but most other laptop desks/stands do not offer a way to secure/tether dangling cords.ѾѾѾѾ Good 4-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾѾ When I purchased this four years ago, I had to buy it at list price and pay extra for shipping, for a total cost of almost $50.  At the time, I thought it was overpriced.  But at the time of this review's writing, Amazon is selling it for $30 with Free Super Saver Shipping, making its pricing much more competitive with other competing products now.ѾѾѾ Average not-good not-bad 3-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾ The removable Mousitizer mouse pad clips onto the right or left side of the Lapinator, so you can use it with both lefties and righties, or remove it for traveling or when sitting in a narrower armchair.  Over the years, my Mousitizer's plastic clip has loosened slightly and the mouse pad can shift and flex slightly as I move my mouse across it.  I wished that the Mousitizer had a mechanism for snapping or locking it in place on the Lapinator, instead of just clipping on.ѾѾѾ The Mousitizer comes with a molded strip of thin adhesive foam that you can optionally stick onto the outer perimeter of the mouse pad that reduces the likelihood of your mouse sliding off the pad.  Additionally, when the Mousitizer is clipped onto the Lapinator, it is tilted towards the Lapinator to further decrease the chance that your mouse will slide off the Mousitizer.  But I still found the adhesive foam to be too thin (low in height) to prevent my mouse from sliding off and falling onto the floor sometimes when I shift on the sofa/bed/chair or move around the room carrying the Lapinator.  So I bought some extra adhesive foam from the hardware store to create a taller barrier, and now my mouse stays within its corral more reliably :-)  With the supplied adhesive foam attached to the Mousitizer, when it is clipped onto the Lapinator, you have a mousing area that is 5.6" in width and 7.0" in depth.  Depending upon how sensitive you have your mouse adjusted, this may be adequate or you may prefer a large mouse pad.  For most usage situations, I find the available mousing area to be okay, even though I would have preferred at least an extra 0.5" of depth to the mousing area.௫ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Conclusion:Both four years ago and also right now as I look at the variety of other portable laptop pads/stands/desks, it seems that all of the other laptop pad/stand/desk offerings either 1) do not offer a mouse pad or decent space for your mouse, 2) are designed more to cool the laptop with fans but are not comfortable for placing on your lap for extended periods, 3) are too big for portable use and are more meant to keep at home and use around your house, or 4) are more suited for 15-inch laptops or smaller.  Some of the laptop desks that *claim* to hold a 17-inch laptop really are too small, resulting in at least 3 inches of your laptop hanging over the edges and not staying too secure on its platform.  If your main goal is to keep your laptop cooler, laptop pads like this that use passive cooling to let air underneath the laptop are not as efficient as the forced convection cooling that a pad using one, two, or three fans can achieve.  But the Lapinator's passive cooling approach does not require a USB connection and the accompanying fan noise and extra weight that fan-cooled laptop pads have.

This is the second Pilot fountain pen I've reviewed - and like the first one, the PILOT MR ANIMAL COLLECTION pen comes without instructions of any kind.  It took me a bit of experimentation (and the assistance of a number of friends and family members) to figure out how to load the cartridge into that first pen.  This time, it was easier - since I am now an experienced fountain pen user and know what to expect.  I still contend that the fountain pens I used as a child were much, much easier to load.  But once you get the hang of it, you'll get your pen working quickly.Here's how to do it (for those of you who haven't used a pen like this in decades and need some instructions):1) Remove the cap from the pen and set it aside2) Unscrew the nib (with the writing tip) from the barrel (base) of the pen3) Remove the metal and foam insert from the nib end (this is used to fill the pen with ink from a bottle)4) Insert the ink cartridge into the nib end of the pen, flat side toward the nib (the narrow end should be pointing outward)5) Press HARD so that the cartridge is punctured inside the nib end of the pen - you'll feel the puncture when you've got it right6) Screw the nib with attached cartridge into the barrel of the pen7) Start writing - if ink isn't immediately flowing, replace the cap on the pen and shake it a few timesOnce you get the cartridge installed, this is a very nice pen.  It's well-weighted, feels good in the hand, and writes smoothly with even ink flow.  It's not as scratchy on the paper as the first Pilot pen I tried, but I can't say it's a silky smooth as the gel pens common on the market these days.  But I like the feel of the pen, and it's quite attractive.  The one I received for review has a burnished silvery-colored finish to the barrel with a  inch ring of black enamel animal print (i.e. lizard-looking scales).  It comes in an attractive black presentation box.Overall, this pen would make a nice gift, especially for someone who really appreciates writing instruments.  It's priced well and writes beautifully.  But Pilot, please, make directions available to purchasers.  Not everyone knows how to load a fountain pen!
