The Brother cartridges are not refilled by a lot of the chain places around where I live.  They are however generally cheaper than the competition so it's not quite as bad a situation.  I seem to get more pages on a cartridge than I did from HP as well.  All in all, good product.

I am a colored pencil artist.  Ever since I started using colored pencils as my main medium I have gone through several sharpeners.  My first one - a Panasonic - was excellent, but it died after about six months of use.  Before I ordered this sharpener I had three (yes...THREE)different brands in my studio.  This X-ACTO sharpener makes number four.  From the first time I used it I realized that this is the best sharpener of the bunch.Colored pencils vary in diameter according to the brand.  Therefore, having a sharpener with a dial that accomodates the various sizes is a definite plus.  Part of the reason I had three separate sharpeners before this one is because they didn't have the dial openings.  I went ahead and bought each one because they got good reviews.I'm thinking that the search for a perfect sharpener has come to an end.  This baby sharpens to a nice sharp point (something that is a must in colored pencil art), does not damage the pencil, and does not eat too much of the pencil at each sharpening. The fact that it doesn't eat the pencils is a necessity since artist-quality colored pencils are NOT cheap!NOTE:  Any pencil sharpener that is used for colored pencils must be "lubricated" by sharpening a typical #2 pencil on a regular basis.

We have the Canon MG-5400 and it's great for paper printing and scanning, but it doesn't allow much flexibility as far as printing on discs, which is why I wanted it -- with all the downloadable recordings nowadays, I have to make my own packaging (it's not as good to just write on them with a Sharpie).Anyway, the Canon was limited in how much could be printed word-wise and just wasn't up to what I needed it for. Not to say it is not a superb product otherwise.The new Epson not only prints on discs in more ways, it also prints jewel case inserts. I used to have to assemble them myself. This was an unexpected bonus. Also, it's easier to access the CD printing tray.As for operation, you have to have the panel open already to print paper. On the Canon, it flips open on its own. Not a huge deal but worth noting.Because of its size, the Epson, like the Canon, doesn't hold much paper, but it seems less likely to send pages falling to the floor as the holding device is longer.

Swingline staples have been a "staple" in our household for decades.  We like that they stay stuck together in a long strip until you put them in the stapler.  Some cheaper brands break apart in the box and you end up with waste because you can't load individual staples into the stapler.We also like that these staples are strong enough to be driven through up to 20 pages of paper without bending or wimping out.  They don't rust on your documents, either.  We bought some off-brand staples once, and they rusted and left a mess in a storage box of old bank statements.This order is for five big boxes of 5,000 staples - that's 25,000 staples!  My husband will take one box with him to work; I have one in my desk at home; our daughter will take a box to college; and we'll put the rest in a drawer.  We'll probably never have to buy staples again, but I think it's a good deal when you can buy a lifetime supply of a good quality product for less than $10.
This cartridge last longer than the 41 standard cartridge. It works well with my Canon MP460 all-in-one printer.

if you need an envelope to send things in, this is the perfect one.The best thing i liked about this is the Reveal-a-Seal.  No more licking !!!it's sooooo easy.  No more papercuts on your tongue (yes, i did get them), no more awful taste in your mouth and no more worrying if the envelope is sealed.  this is perfect.  i have one bill each month that i pay and they don't give me envelopes.  six months ago the company contacted me and told me i was late in payment. i had the cancelled check that said i paid on time. i put a trace on it and it turned out my envelope seal did not hold and the contents opened up in the mailbox and spilled out.  the post office was holding my check.this will NEVER happen with these envelopes.  i sealed one and immediately opened it up and the seal was so strong, even after a second of being sealed.theya re a great weight too.  you can see through themthey make my life a whole lot easier and i wish i would have had them 6 mos. ago, it would have saved me time, trouble and a delinquent notice on my credit report.when my samples run out, i will order more from amazon.  they are worth it.

Not much to say about this.  They are rubber bands wound around in a ball.  I got this for my workshop because I can never find a rubber band when I need one.  The rubber bands are a good size for wrapping up small cords and items.  The ball makes them convenient to store.  I probably won't use this many rubber bands in my lifetime but it's handy when I need one.
This tape is great for mounting projects onto foam core as well as any other type of surface. This is way better than the spray mount.

These are excellent laminating pouches, I have no complaints. The items I laminated turned out great, they were easy to use. They're all pretty much the same, but these were a good bargain since they were free from Amazon Vine. I would buy them when I need more.

I'm currently a pharmacy student and as you may guess there are lots of drug names to memorize, which left me frequenting staples in the area and drug stores to replenish my index card supply. I can say that since purchasing this I have not had to look around to see which store has a shelf full of index cards. They are all lined which is great, and they are generously sized so you can cram as much information on the back that you need. Also you don't have to worry about the quality of the card and that what you write (as long as you are using regular ink) will show through the other side. Great brand of index cards made of recycled material.

The Canon Pixma MX420 is a solid all in one inkjet printer that will satisfy most home users but does not excel in any given area. This is not surprising considering the low price. It does all the basics, such as printing text/color photos/graphics, fax, and copying. The duplex printing capability (ability to print on both sides of a paper) is nice also. It also has built in Wifi capability, which allows you to print wirelessly from anywhere in the home. The 802.11N Wifi capability is a nice speed upgrade compared to my older Brother MFC 7840W printer, which only has 802.11g, but in most cases I don't think you'll notice the difference in terms of how quickly a page gets printed out.Print quality is good overall, with very readable text and pictures. If you are interested in the best text quality, you may want to consider a laser printer instead. Similarly, if printing photos is your primary goal, you would be better off with a photo-centric model such as any of the Epson inkjet printers. If versatility is most important, this model should be fine for you. Keep in mind that for about $40-50 more, you can get a more capable Canon printer such as the MX882. The MX882 may also save you some ink money in the long term since it uses 5 separate ink cartridges vs 2 for the MX420. This means that if you happen to run out of magenta in the MX420, you have to replace the whole color cartridge even if you have plenty of the other colors left, whereas with the MX882 you can just replace the magenta cartridge. Some folks may actually prefer the simplicity of stocking just 2 cartridges, though, so you should probably purchase based on what is more important to you.
Canon ink is very good and prints great photos. I love my inkjet printer for printing photos quickly and this ink is top notch.

It seems odd somehow to purchase boxes online, but suppose that is how things work anymore. These boxes come flattened (of course) in yet another large carton. The boxes seem nice and sturdy, and of a good size for general moving, which, unfortunately, we are going to have to do again soon. Hopefully, these nice boxes will help for a smooth transition.

We just replaced our printer after 7 years.  We had an HP printer before, and purchased another one because we loved the first one.  The new printer (C47950 takes these tiny HP 60 cartridges.  I thought for sure I was doing something wrong when I ran through the first cartridge.  When I took them out, I compared and they ARE smaller than the previous cartridges we bought for the old printer.  When I went to shop around for new cartridges, I saw the statement that it will print about 200 pages per cartridge.  They aren't kidding!  We home school, so 200 pages of printed materials for two students is NOTHING.  We are blowing through these left and right and I am disappointed.  Had I known before, I would have purchased a different printer all together.  I print everything in draft quality since my kiddos will literally see it once, color it or answer the questions and be done with it, and still, I counted 198 pages last time.  While these cartridges are definitely less expensive, I would definitely do a page-for-page comparison before investing in a printer that requires these cartridges.  At this point, we're spending just as much money for me to print one and make copies at a local print shop.  :-(  I give it 3 stars because it's a cheap alternative if you don't print very often, but if you're a print-heavy house, you may want to find something else.

These shipping labels work great for recycling mailers.  I've used them to mail several packages & it's a great convenience to no longer have to spend five minutes or more trying to peel off old labels before re-using padded mailers.With Avery's TrueBlock technology, it's a snap to quickly print a label that completely covers the old label. These labels work just like conventional laser labels--just use Avery's template to print the labels you need.  The "magic" is in the dark, vinyl-like coating on the "sticky side" of the label.  This dark screening coat completely blocks out the label underneath, so nothing shows through.  Just a clean, neatly printed new, bright white label.Elegantly engineered recycling solution; Highly recommended!

...envelopes are becoming quite amazing and just in time to be nearly obsolete. I mail just about nothing and when I do mail that nothing it happens very inseldomly. But I gave the envelope a try and sealed it and then opened it and it did like it said. The security feature worked. I'll hang on to these even though by the time and I'll need to use one, the glue will have worn out. Then I'll chuck them.
I have used these labels with great success. They print out nicely and I like the fact they are eco-friendly. They stayed "stuck" (which in my case was a good thing). I would purchase them again.

I'm a certified PMP who prefers some old school methods of Project Management when it comes to tracking action items, risks, lessons learned, etc.  Having seen many disasters when people rely solely on their tablets for note taking, I like having a paper record I can refer to and transcribe from.I like this Mead/Cambridge Action Planner Business Notebook because it lends a serious and professional look to my note taking in meetings (contrasted with a simple college ruled, spiral notebook).  The printed form has plenty of space for page number, date, headline or title, 29 numbered lines to align the salient take away points from the meeting, and a big white space margin for additional notes and thoughts. The paper is somewhat heavy, but wet inks (such as fountain pen) have slight bleed though to the back of the page; gel ink and ball point is okay.Deducting one star for the bleed through.Highly recommended

I ordered this printer because I was interested in being able to print my own photos at home rather than having to send them off somewhere or take a flash drive into a Walgreens, etc. I was expecting a photo printer that would create "quality" prints slightly below that of an actual photoshop, but the Artisan is way more than this!First of all, it's incredibly easy to set up (assuming you have a wireless connection). I took it out of the box, removed the travel safety protections, plugged it in and followed the step-by-step instructions from there. It automatically connects to your wifi (once you enter the password) and prints with no problem.It prints plain text documents quickly and cleanly (no big deal there). But the photo prints are incredible. Using the two free 4X6 photo papers that came with the printer I was amazed at the quality of the prints - they look like they were developed professionally. Secondly, and even more impressive, is that Epson allows you to set up an account online that will then allow you to establish an email address and send photos to your printer directly from your iPhone! After getting the settings right I tried this and had a professional-looking copy of a photo I took with my iPhone printed out in under a minute.Not only is this printer easy to set up it produces beautiful quality and prints from your iPhone. I don't know what else you would want from a photo printer. The ink is a little expensive but it's worth it for the quality and simplicity.
It's commonly known that ink cartridges are overpriced, but HP inks are good and this is one of the cheaper places you'll find it. I still hate paying so much, but this is one of the better deals.

This "easy grip" feature of this letter sized folder does indeed make it rather easy to grasp it and pull it out of a drawer in a file cabinet or off a shelf on which you store paper documents in folders such as these. This is definitely the best made part of the folder; it impressed me a lot!One thing I did notice, however, is that with time the bottom or the sides could become worn. Therefore I don't recommend stuffing these with documents to the point where the folder is too full--the last thing you want is for one of these to break especially if you frequently pull it out of a drawer or off a shelf and then replace it.Overall, I recommend this product. It is rather well made and I like that "easy grip" feature." Just don't overload those folders!

Finally, a shipping label that can be peeled off without ripping, sticking to the box or envelope or curling into nothingness.  This AVERY Repositionable white label measures a generous 2"x4" and prints clean without smudges.  Once placed in position, you can easily peel it back off to reapply elsewhere, or just leave it be and it will not fall off in transit.  It adheres permanently to the surface over a short time.  I actually used these to label my kids' school books and folders since the size makes them easy to read from afar.  I highly recommended Avery labels way before this product, but now that they're made with this "Re-hesive Technology" which makes repositioning such a snap, it's my number one choice for labels.

I wanted to try these labels specifically for use on a color inkjet (Epson R380) to test the print quality. They arrived today, and I made some return address labels with a photo on the side and script text in blue, and the print quality was not bad. It wasn't super crisp like when using Photo Inkjet label stock, but it was definitely passable. I tried plain white Avery labels in color inkjet and they printed horribly, not really usable. Avery does make Photo Inkjet labels which look great, but they aren't cheap, and that means buying two separate kinds of labels for text and color graphics. So, I was hoping these 3M labels would work well with color and as everyday labeling, and it appears they'll do OK. AND, there is another added benefit to these 3M labels: the instructions say that these work in laser printers as well, so I tried it out in our inexpensive Canon MF3240 laser printer, just printing black laser text. These labels worked VERY well in the laser printer! Super crisp text, and the backing paper is very flexible as are the labels themselves, so they ran through the printer with ease. If you have a color laser, I bet these would print very well on there. One kind of label stock for both laser and inkjet, nice!SO, if you need photo quality labels you'll need to use the Avery Products - Inkjet Labels for Color Printing, 1 x 2-5/8, Matte White, 600/Pack. But if you are shopping for labels that print decent in color on an inkjet and very well on a laser, these 3Ms are your one-stop shop, and at a third of the price!

The following is my fiancée's review of the labels.My fiancé and I used these labels for our Save the Date postcards for our wedding.  We put all of the addresses in Excel and we were able to easily transfer it to Word for the template for the labels.  It was fairly easy to figure out the template for the labels. I'm not sure if this is because of the template or because of the printer.  I simply moved them over in the document and they printed out okay.  About three out of 100 labels were messed up. I use this for eBay and it is perfect thus far in about 6 months of use. I have used it both on battery power and with the included AC adapter and it works fine either way. For the price, I did expect a very good pencil sharpener.  But WOW, this is it!  The finest and most versatile pencil sharpener I have ever used.  If your looking for the best, look no further, 'cause This Is It !!!Signed, Sharp and Happy

An excellent all-in-one wireless device which was purchased specifically as a Cloud Ready printer to compliment an Acer Chromebook.  The Canon prints very well, copies superbly, and faxes perfectly.  What is delightfully surprising about it is how simple it was to register in the Cloud and "connect" to the Chromebook for someone who is technically challenged and remains amazed by cordless telephones.  The design of this fine machine is both functional and attractive.  Refreshing is the ease of inserting the ink cartridges and the small red lights which report them to be making contact securely.  The only negative to be mentioned and it is not of small concern is the awful, confusing, and completely inadequate online directions that the Canon website provides for initializing the Cloud functionality of their device.  There is no mention of the Cloud at all and it is somewhat frustrating to figure it out n a hit-or-miss basis.  It should be clear and simple guide to accomplishing the task.  With that said, however, it is not impossibly difficult to find one's way without such an aid and the tremendous feeling of satisfaction in accomplishing that which seems beyond the grasp of the inexperienced is absolutely wonderful.  The first time the device prints a document at your command, without wires or cables, is one of the most stunning you will ever experience.  Not since I purchased an automobile with power windows have I been so amazed.  Overall, the Canon PIXMA MX892 is a very satisfactory addition to the Chromebook's simplicity and one which is quite good at fulfilling the potential and promise of the Chromebook's bright future.

These Pendaflex (made in the U.S.A.)  letter-sized hanging folders are excellent.  The tops are reinforced so the tabs (5 options) won't tear through.  The folders come in a five-color assortment in a dispenser box.  They feature sturdy flexible hooks and include computer compatible printable sheet on which you can customize your own tab inserts.

A very task oriented notebook that is laid out well but more freestyle (versus the MeadCambridge Limited Action Planner Business Notebook (06064)  Mead is a good name and one that most of us know for notebooks, paper, etc.This is a fancy notebook ... but it is laid out well and the lines and colors (and perforations) make for a great, more structure "scratch pad".A good way to keep track of ideas.  You could also do that with standard notebook ... but this one is kind of cool.

We buy a lot of paper each year.  Mead provides a good basic (cheap) paper that will no doubt meet the needs of most students. However, I find the paper to be thinner than expected which may be an issue for those who exert significant pressure when they write or those who rely on their trusty eraser to get them through the day. It's OK - nothing great - a good utilitarian option but for wide-ruled paper (for younger students) I think it really shouldn't be quite so thin.Pricing Note (not part of the review):The price as I write this review is $1.33 for 200 sheets of wide-ruled filler paper. That is the delivered price if you are an Amazon Prime member or combine with other products to get Super Saver Shipping. If the price is higher as you read this review you may want to consider coming back at the start of the next school season and stocking when they are on sale.

This white board is a great size for my fridge, or for the side of a filing cabinet.The magnets that keep it attached to a metal surface are very large and keep it where it belongs without any danger of slipping and sliding down the surface.It comes with decorative magnets for the front too and a marker with a cap that is magnetized on one side and has its own eraser on the other - very handy.I was going to keep it in my office at school but like it too much, so now it lives with me on my fridge where it helpfully reminds my son of his weekly chores. I recommend it for home or office use.

I got tired of paying so much for ink and decided to buy the cheapos that are advertised as being the same quality....they're not. I found the cheapos to be of horrible quality (blotchy). I only buy the HPs now, there is no real alternative. While the cost could be better there's no reason to subtract stars for it as the alternative is to pay less for off-brand garbage.

I use this laptop lift with my Mac Book Pro 13'' and it fits just perfectly. Because your laptop would be up from your desk, the computer then does not heat as much, so that is actually very nice to help your computer live longer. This is a great product that I do recommend as a great addition to any office to ease typing.

Most expanding files I've worked with in the past have been of the paper/cardboard variety.  This plastic/mylar kit seems like a step in the right direction.  I was able to squeeze a bunch of papers in this thing quite nicely.  The 20+ dividers give you lots of flexibility in your organizational process and the whole structure is sturdy... with the exception of the lid.  This file system deserves a better lid.  It's wimpy and earns the loss of one star.

These are a basic home office staple.  Labels that can be used to address envelopes (as they are intended) or used to mark and identify a myriad of items, files and boxes throughout the home or office.  The 3M labels match the templates available in Microsoft Word and are easy to set up and print. The 10 sheet pack is a good size for the home or small office user making a total of 300 labels.  They last me several months at home (except at Christmas time when I use them for the card mailing list).  Made by 3M they are easy to remove from their backing and stick securely to the box, envelope, blouse or file that you choose to label.  An excellent product.
This Post-it Super Sticky Notes, 4 x 6-Inches, Canary Yellow, Lined, 5-Pads/Pack is excellent and comes in very handy for everday even notations.......
Good, basic scanner. I just needed something to copy documents and this does it quite well. I have found no problems with it so far.

This is a nice little memo and paper clip holder and even comes with paper and paper clips. I really appreciate that the paper pad isn't post-it type for once. Sometimes you just don't want the back of your piece of paper to be sticky. The paperclips are pretty nice, too, if you like bright, colorful clips (and I do.)It's actually not a paperclip holder, in my opinion. There are three slots, one for the paper and then two smaller ones (which are actually a good size to maybe stick some post-it notes vertically) but none of them has any sort of barrier in the front to keep paperclips from escaping. Still, overall it seems like a good quality hunk of acrylic to use for keeping small bits of paper handy.

My two complaints about these labels are:The sheets curl quite a bit; enough that I have to manually roll them in the opposite direction to approximate flatness before I can feed them into my printer.The ink from my Canon printer smears even after allowing the labels to dry for several minutes. This makes it difficult to firmly rub the label onto a package.I used the entire package, so these labels are not without functionality, but I won't be buying these again.

We bought a Mead 5 Star 5 subject for our newly minted 9th grader last summer.  His English teacher required them all to buy one and carry it to class everyday. My son is the destroyer of binders and notebooks. His abuse of school supplies is legendary.  By the end of most years we have things held together with duct tape or replaced at least once .  This one is the only one that has every survived a whole school year.  It didn't even need any duct tape!  We are very satisfied with the quality and longevity of this notebook.  This will be the one we buy every year to get him through the rest of high school. A new one for next year is already ready to go.

I got these to use at work in the kitchen of our animal shelter. I recently bought some neon colors, thinking they would be fun. Well, they don't even show up when I use them. Not useful at all. That's the last time I go for 'cute' when I need something that works well. These colors are strong and vivid, and I can even mark the top of a can cover with the date, and it stays until it's washed off. These wipe off the white board easy peasy too!
These pocket folders are great for organizing all kinds of papers.  I really like how durable they are.  Overall great quality!

I have never used a thermal binder before, so I wasn't sure what to expect. The binder is easy to use and I must admit the binding is not only well attached but also looks very professional. I tried numerous different sizes to see how the thermal binding machine would perform, and it did a fine job on each. It only took about a minute to bind a small presentation of about 60 pages or so. The machine has a small footprint and actually looks nice sitting around the office. Although the machine is likely too small for a large business and too expensive for many individuals, it is a great fit for a small business.
Perfect printer, very easy setup, fast and there are many suppliers of toner for this one. The cartridges cost as little as $8.

I do a lot of shipping on eBay, and so I usually go through a lot of packing tape. Much of my problems come from having to reinforce boxes so that their contents don't drop out. This tape actually helps me get rid of that issue. It is super strong, and it holds box flaps together without having to tape and re-tape over areas. It also stays down from the moment you put it on the box. You don't have to worry that it will peel off. I like to use the tape also to laminate over shipping labels to keep them on, and it works wonderfully.Scotch makes the best tape, and this shipping tape is sure to meet your most demanding shipping needs. The six-pack ensures that this will last a long time. I highly recommend this packing tape for shipping anything.

I had the opportunity to obtain one of these for free, so I did.  I use it at home.  It is really much larger than one would really want at home, but it was free, so I can't complain.Anyway, this machine does exactly what it claims it should do.  My kids use it for school stuff.  I use it for things I really wouldn't need to if I didn't have it.  It does everything it is supposed to do.  It seems to be heavy duty, but this is the only one of these I have ever had, so I really have nothing to compare it to.My kids try to put too many pieces of paper in it at one time. If I am not mistaken, the instructions claim you can put 25 pieces of paper in at once.  Well, you can, but it seems to cut 15 or so much easier.  And since I am not in that big of a hurry, I see no reason to push it.Anyway, now that I have this thing, I really don't think I will ever need to replace it using it at home.  It seems like it will last forever.  I don't really know what else to say about it.  It does everything it is supposed to do, and I haven't found anything it is supposed to do that is does poorly.  Well, it is big.  Really big.  Bigger than I would really ever need for home use.

If you've ever used wimpy notebook dividers that tear off or get dogeared after a few months of heavy use, then these are for you!The whole page is the divider, so you can do a list of what's contained in the section.  That's great if you're organizing a lot of overlapping information.  I have notebooks full of master copies of poetry, reading selections, and grammar exercises and these dividers are invaluable for cross referencing so I not only know what I have, but where to find it.Love!

I do graphic work on the side, so when I had the opportunity to get a printer that can produce up to 13"x19" prints, I took it.  I've heard of Epson, but had never owned one.  I'm not disappointed.  It produces quality prints, it is as quiet as a printer can be, and it's relatively fast.  It can also hold up to 500 sheets in the bottom tray, so that is a plus.  I have an all Mac household, and have experienced no compatibility issues when hooked to my Airport.  I installed it to my main computer, and have been able to print from my family's other 2 computers by selecting my Epson connection when printing.  The only problem I encountered was not being able to to print from my iPhone or IPad - I get a "No AirPrint" notice.  I emailed their customer service and they were prompt to respond, but have not been able to resolve the problem.  If I am able to fix the problem, I'll increase my rating to 5 stars.  (PS - Please be aware that this printer is large compared to average home printers, 22 x 16.3 x 10.4 inches.  It's also just a printer, so don't expect to be able to fax or scan items.)

Love these Poly mailers for magazines and lightweight books. These are slightly thinner material than the more expensive options, but they do the job for anything up to about 2 lbs as long as the item doesn't have sharp edges that can poke through the poly.The adhesive is covered by a thin sheet of plastic which has quite a bit of static cling when removed, so can sometimes be a little tough to slough from your hand into the garbage quickly. The adhesive is amazingly sticky, but doesn't "kick" instantly so if you need to reposition you can do so for a few seconds after first sticking it down.

I like the nice clean design of this chair, the padding on the seat, and the full spin. It's a comfortable chair that's well designed so it doesn't have any weird pressure areas if you're sitting and working on a project for several hours.It went together easily and quickly. My son had it out of the box and assembled in about 10 minutes.It has a stable base, and rolls well, and it's easy to adjust the height which is an important feature in my home. The men in my family are about a foot taller than the women. I don't think it's comfortable to sit backwards on, but my kids like that feature. The hard back is comfortably shaped, and they will sit on it backwards to play video games- sort of a supported slouch.

Great printer but come on, Canon!  Can't you provide a firmware update for the Apple Air printing?  Seriously, you release this and then add Apply Air and expect me to buy a new printer a few months later.  This is what I call stringing a customer along.  Otherwise, this is a great printer.  Love it and works well.

The handset of this phone is impressive, possessing a slender, efficient, comfortable design with clear voice transmission and reception through the unit.  Note, however, that the phone is a single unit with a built-in answering machine and doesn't come with expansion handsets.All in all, the phone is fine, but surprisingly no-frills in the ringtone department, offering less than ten options . . . and none of them are anything about which to rave.  Furthermore, the ringer volume seems to max out at a less-than-desirably-loud volume.  My less futuristic Panasonic phone/answering machine (with 2 handset extensions) has oodles of ringtone options for each handset and the ringer can be made quite loud.  It's a big event when the phone rings at my house and everyone hears Vivaldi's Four Season blare out.Good phone, just not great.

I usually don't like bold-tipped pens, because the thick tips don't generally accommodate small writing in the margins of books, which I do a lot of. They also tend to dry out a bit at the tip, and the 'flow' of ink isn't always consistent. These, however, don't seem to exhibit any of those problems. The ink flow is nice and consistent without 'overflowing' or blotting, and they just have a nice, even writing feel. I haven't had any problems with 'wet ink' or smudging, either. This is one impressive stapler!  The little image of a staple on the box marked "Standard" is actually bigger than a standard staple, so I thought that they actually meant some kind of larger staple. At the price that's offered, it's no wonder that thisBelkin 8-by-9-Inch Mouse Pad (Black)is the #1 in sales for mouse pads. It's simple, basic black and the perfect 9.2 x 8.3 inches that have almost become an industry standard. There are no duckies, Hawaiian tropical flowers, basset hounds, sports team logos, photos of Sports IllustratedSports Illustrated swimsuit models, hot air balloons, comic book characters, or images of mountains that you'll probably never visit. It's just a basic black mouse pad; nothing more, nothing less.But... oh, the smell! Maybe that's an added feature, a freebie that wasn't noted in the product specs?Actually, there's a fast and easy solution to remove that somewhat noxious odor, but bear with me so that you'll understand the logic. Some of the first mouse pads were actually made from manufacturer's scrap of the same neoprene foam backed with a thin sheet of nylon or Spandex that we find in Scuba and free-divewetsuits, and some of us made out own mouse pads from worn out or badly torn wetsuits.So what does this have to do with smelly mouse pads?That's easy: those old wetsuits stunk when new, but one hoped the atrocious smell would go away by the second or third dive. However, they smelled like a cross between a wet dog and dead opossum road kill when left in a plastic bag in the trunk of a car for a few days after a dive, so they had to be washed... and quickly. Today we have products such as Sink The Stink Wetsuit Wash and others to deal with getting rid of the stench. But these cost more than the mouse pad itself, which is ridiculous.The solution is simple: wash the mousepad thoroughly with your standard kitchen dishwashing soap. Good old green Palmolive works fine. Rinse it and gently wring out the excess water, then wash it again the same way (think of it like shampooing your hair). Set it on a flat surface between layers of paper towels to blot up the excess water. Depending on your climate, it should be dry and ready to use within a day or two.  I'm not going to suggest that you try this, but there are some of us who take our mouse pads and put them in the washing machine with older dark clothes. Just remember to not put them in a clothes dryer.OK, back to the mouse pad.It's good, it's priced right, it's functional, it will work with just about any mouse, be it optical or the older one with mouse balls. Wash it and get rid of that smell that makes one think you pulled it out of a garbage dump or an old tire recycling plant and it will last a long time.9/5/2012

Judging from the blurbs and photos on the replaceable cover sheet this Flex Hybrid NoteBinder is intended for students.  However, I'm using it at work. I found that most mousepads that have a fabric surface generally provide the smoothest tracking for optical/laser/IR mice because of the low friction between the teflon pads on the mouse and the pad surface. However, typical fabric pads will start to fray at the edges due to the design, and some pads have a texture or surface that is more suited for optical/laser/IR mice.The Cyborg Glide 7 is a LARGE pad, and I mean seriously large. I cannot fit it on my tables or desks at home. I was able to use it at work because of my larger table, but even then it was ridiculously large. Unless you're playing some real-time strategy game that requires lots of mouse movement on a huge map and have a very large desk dedicated to gaming, this pad is not for the average gamer.The edges are laser cut, and it feels like it was seared or welded when you run your fingers over it. Mad Catz claims that the edges won't fray. The surface is a special synthetic that was advertised to provide better tracking. The surface is indeed slick, and it was easy to use with my Microsoft Bluetooth 5000 laser mouse, Dell opticla mouse, and a Logitech G9X laser mouse. However, I didn't feel or perceive any performance improvement over an inexpensive fabric mouse pad with gel wristpad from Wal-Mart.Given the street price for the Glide 7, it's actually a great value. Just make sure you really want such a large pad, and it will serve you well. The artwork is kind of cool. It depicts a large futuristic robot.Overall: 5/5 stars, I wish it were a lot smaller though.

I've been using dry board markers regularly for years and I like the changes in this set.  The major improvement is that you can see how much ink is left.  It was a pain to grab an old marker and find that it was empty.  The tops are anti-roll so when you set them down on the counter, they stay in place.  The eraser is similar to the older ones, and it works fine.  I really like the board cleaning fluid.  It works better than any other method I have tried - a real plus.  I have several small boards on my freezer door in the garage,  and I am constantly erasing what I have taken out and updating the contents, and a board on my refrigerator for notes etc..My older markers are smaller and each one has a small magnet on it so that it will stick to the board.  These markers are quite a bit larger, as they are meant for writing on larger white boards that have a tray on the bottom to hold them.  This is pretty minor but I have seen some plastic pen holder that you can affix to the board.

These are the perfect labels. Strong enough adhesive, wide enough to publish name, address, and the costs is great (keep in mind you get 200 labels for the price). You won't be disappointed as these have higher quality than the average labels.

I have the pink binder, and I love the color.  It just about matches the picture perfectly.  The fact that I can customize the front is also fun.  It is 1 1/2 inches deep and can hold approximately 300 pages (not including dividers).Great for school, projects, organizing and so much more.This is a sturdy binder that opens and closes nicely.  It is also backed by a limited 1 year replacement warranty.

This is a funky chair--the first chair I've ever sit on with an actual blow up ball inside. Not sure how to review a practical item like this. I got it because I sometimes have to send out packages and I need address labels. These work. They stick well. And they are easy to write on.

What can I say? This is the Scotch tape that we all know and love, in a fun newly designed case. The green snail design is quite cute, and when I compare it side-by-side to my regular Scotch tape dispenser, it's actually smaller and easier to hold. Will likely be a hit with the school-age crowd. Didn't encounter any problems when I opened it up to change the tape roll, either.

This printer is small, compact, and good for tiny rooms.  However, if you can find the space, I highly recommend one of Epson's WorkForce printers.  They're office quality and they will last you much, much longer.This printer worked for a couple weeks flawlessly, then feeder began having issues.  I had to open it up and take out a stuck page, which wasn't as simple as it should have been.  Nor should it have jammed in the first place.Epson's ink cartridges are reasonably priced, at least compared to other manufacturers.  Look for knockoffs if you print a lot.

I've got no issues with this tape.  In fact, it's pretty neat stuff, in that you don't get that deafening "Schrkkkkcksksk" noise when you pull out a section of it, which is perfect for when I need to wrap a huge package in the bedroom at 3:00 in the morning.  The tape is good and clear, thick, and comes easily off the roll. It does not split into little threads, and cuts in clear widths. If it doubles back and sticks on itself, it comes apart easily and you can still use it, which is a big plus.The dispenser is the part of this product that has me shaking my head.First, the packaging, with that cool green accent (is it really good for the environment? there's nothing on the packaging that says this, but I have to conclude that this is the marketing intent) and "Sure Start" copy seem to be forming an arrow drawing your attention to the little tabs on the red plastic dispenser.  Well, the tape does start well, in that they've cut a serrated edge, which also is not sticky.  There is no mistaking where it begins, and like a rally racer sprinting to his car, you are ready to start taping your valuable Ebay items in mere seconds.  It's a nice touch, but nothing that spectacular, honestly.At the very front of the dispenser, on each side of the serrated metal cutting bar (complete with its lightweight cardboard cover proving warning that you could be grievously injured if you underestimate is raw slicing capacity), is a slightly curved and raised set of strips which seem to be forming a gripping area.  If so, this is about as awkward as it gets.  Maybe 3M and its legions of Scandinavian ergonomics specialists have determined this is the optimum point for the maximum ratio of taping pressure to speed of rolling tape outlay, but this grip just don't work for this humble user.  I've always grabbed it by the dispenser on each side at the top of the roll, and it's all worked out just fine.  Maybe some gripping strips up top would really make this thing sing...I actually pulled the label off the dispenser, which given its heavy glue on its entire surface and not just the surface contacting the dispenser, makes a mess.  The label remains sticky, and it does not come cleanly off the dispenser, which is unsightly and a pain in the rear to tidy up completely.  But, the payoff is that the inside of the label tells you that the dispenser is indeed reusable.  It's even got directions and a little graphic to show you hot to quiclkly open it up and put it onto a new roll.  Strange in that the outside of the label does not state that the dispenser is reusable; I'd think this would be a strong selling point.Bottom line: All in all, this is a great product, as it delivers on its promise.  The tape is fine, but the dispenser is a bit over-engineered.

This is a neat looking notepad of about 8  X 6 inches. There are about one hundred sheets and each sheet has a header for date and "to do" section. I use this notepad to write things I need to do each day. I use this in my office and in my home. It is pretty pad to carry around. At the bottom, it has tear-off section on which you can write your laundry list like groceries to buy or phone numbers to call. I have been using this for the past three weeks and I find this is a pretty useful notepad. I have rated this product four-star for its design and usefulness.

I have 3 laser printers, two in my office at work, one of which is a very expensive color HP laser printer and the other a Canon office printer and lastly a Brother printer/scanner at home.  When I got the Ricoh I was kind of expecting the worst and was pleasantly surprised to find out that it's right up their if not surpases the printers from the big boys.Build Quality:The build quality and the fit and finish of the 204SN is very good, it is right up their with my Canon and just about as good as the HP.Operation:It takes about the same time to warm up as most laser printers and the noise emmited from it during printing is no louder that my HP so I consider that a total win by Ricoh.  The scanning speed is not bad, it's not the fastest I have seen but it's good enough for most home office situations.Print Quality:Very good, it's surprisingly good.Negatives:Well I am already looking for a replacement Toner cartridge and all I see are OEM units so this might be a more expensive printer to operate than a more main stream printer (assuming your the kind of person who uses 3rd party toner) if not it pretty  much on Par with typical OEM cartridges.Conclusion:It's a good printer any day of the week but it's a fantastic printer at under $70!If your the kind of person who only use OEM toner then this printer is a perfect match.
When ours arrived, I was pretty excited to get it out of the carton. This is so sturdy, and looks good, too.

These are what you would expect them to be; heavy duty board, with a writable plastic film and a full backside magnet. There are two in the pack and a small marker. I got them for my daughter that loves to make lists. She loves them. She can carry it around and write on  it, then stick it on the fridge. They are very small (5x8) and that means you need a fairly sharp tip to the dry erase marker used to write on the board.

The biggest problem I've had with using some pens and markers is they smudge especially if your hands are damp. The first thing I checked when I received these is whether they smudge. They don't even when your hands are wet. When you write using just the tip you get a slim print, when using the whole end you get a thicker print. I like that they are retractable so you don't have to worry about losing the cap. I haven't used them long enough to know how long they last compared to the more typical sharpies. I would have liked one in black as well

These are great if you need a sticker in an unconventional size or shape. You print what you want or need to be a sticker and cut it out into the shape you desire. It is nice that these are repositionable (Just in case you don't get it in the right spot the first time.) I also thought the wall sticker idea another reviewer had was a great use of these.

Simple and cheap mouse pad I had a glass desk and was using a book as a mouse pad but this mouse pad works way better.  I have spilled a lot of water and other liquids and was thankful it doesn't hold water.  Its still in tip top condition and is still holding up great.

Sharpie makee a superior marker and these cool neon fine points are no different.  The yellow is a little hard to see on paper and blue is a little on the dull side, but those are minor quibbles.  Great pens in colors that pop.

Many things are nice about this set of labels.1. Once these labels are put on a paper envelope, they are staying there. The adhesive really sticks. Peeling it off  results in destruction of the label.  Placing the labels on a shiny surface, such as the packaging the labels came in or on a CD case, results in being able to peel off the label, but in my opinion, this is okay.2. Providing you with an Avery number to create the label is essential.  As many programs including MS Word work best with an Avery number, creating labels becomes a breeze. I've tried the alternative and it is a lot of trial and error.3. Small label size is great for a return address.4. Easy peel off feature; gaps where there is no label on the backing paper, is a nice idea. I admit I only use this as an oversized scanner, not as a copier, printer, or fax machine. However, it works very well if you set everything at the defaults; it gets very slow if you do things like apply descreening. It may not be possible to get a cheaper 11x17 scanner, but it seems well made and does the job pretty well.

This is a great little pen that combines four different ink colors plus a pencil all in one writing implement. If you have reason to need multi-color ink, for example, if you are a teacher, or a student who likes to take notes in color, you can carry 1 pen instead of four different ones and a pencil! The drawback is that the pencil leads do not feed as easily as I would like. Plus, the pen itself really is more of a novelty item. Truthfully, considering its expense and the likelihood of getting lost (or stolen) I am better off with four cheaper colored ink pens, than one super duper one!

Between labeling sections in my 3-ring notebooks and marking places in my textbooks, I go through a lot of note tabs.  I've been on the lookout for some that were a nice size and which could be re-written on if pencil was used.  Usually, the biggest tabs I can find are about 1.5 inches wide, so the added width on these Avery tabs was very nice.  I was also able to write on them in pencil, erase, and re-use them without any problem. Overall, they were very strong and sturdy, but I would use them only for permanent uses and not as removable ones.

Was skeptical at first.. I mean, with the price being ridiculously low compared to what the official Brother toner would be?  It's a generic toner, packed really well, and I'm glad to say, it's been chugging out documents for weeks (I print orders, Fedex, UPS and Post Office airbills day after day. I've used several of Avery's Easy Peel products. I use a laser printer to do all my black and white printing, but I needed a photo printer with a small footprint for my wife so she could print color photos for her Girl Scout projects. I gave it 2 stars because it does not have a warning label.I had purchased this at another store and when I first used it I cut too much off the nozzle and spilled some on a trash bag. My cat started licking at it and had to take her to the vet because the bottle does not have any warning stickers. A better explanation is in my response to a user's comment.

On first glance these labels look very small, and they are small, but they are "Return Address" labels.  While they could be a little bigger, I was able to fit my address on them with a small picture in front of it (street and apartment number on same line).  You are realistically only going to be able to fit 3 lines on a label (at about 8pt font), so don't expect more than that.  The labels I printed on my inkjet printer were very clear and the colors looked great.  The template allows you to print several styles on a single sheet, which I had printed a few different ones including a small picture to the left of my address and ones with a faded picture in the background.  I am using these as both customized return address labels and address correction stickers on my checks (they are the PERFECT size for that).  I have only used them on regular envelopes and checks to which they applied easily and did not peel at the edges.The "Pop-Up Edge" is a very interesting idea, and is a time-saving way to peel the labels from the sheet.  You simply fold the sheet a little along the perforation and the edge of the labels stick out for you to grab.Word of caution:  Depending on your printer, the printing may be off center or higher on the label than expected.  I'm almost positive this is my printer because I have had this issue with mailing seals as well, but just wanted to advise others to check this before printing many labels.

I've wanted a label maker forever, and when Amazon Vine offered this one for review, I was excited, but a little concerned that it had to be connected to a PC to work.  I was afraid I would have trouble setting it up, but I plugged it in and within minutes I was printing labels. I couldn't believe how easy it was to use because sometimes I can be electronically challenged.  After playing with it for a while, I installed the P-Touch editor software on the CD-rom that is included with the label maker.  While the basic software was sufficient for my use, the P-Touch editor software was fun to make really creative labels and even upload small pictures that I used on some.  The 180 DPI print quality doesn't make for detailed pictures, though.Refills for the label maker come in a variety of colors and widths for various uses. The back is easy to peel off and the labels are laminated and high quality. The only complaint I have is that it wastes a bit of tape each time it prints, maybe about 3/4 of an inch that it just lops off and spits out.It takes 6 AA batteries or you can use the A/C adaptor cord that comes with the label maker.I'm very pleased with the unit and I've used it to organize my pantry shelves, and to label the fifty or so storage tubs in my attic.  Next, I'm going to work on the kids' closets!Update: I've frequently run my labeled containers through my dishwasher and while I expected them to come off, they haven't so far, and still look the same as the day I put them on.

For use as a tab on divider pages or to make folders stand out beyond the built in tab, these work great.  You have about 2.75" of space to write on the tab.  Pencil erases but pen is permenant.  Enough room on the non-tab portion to provide stability for the adhesive surface and give you extra space to write.  A handy thing to have in your desk drawer to mark those things you want to be able to find in a hurry.

I have theprevious Saturn SL 125 Laminatorand this Saturn 2 offers some nice upgrades.  Most noticeably, the top panel buttons are all electronic touch buttons now, and they light up to let you know power, warm-up status, and the selected pouch thickness.  The new back-lit buttons make the current status and selections very easy to see, and offer nice visual cues for warm-up and ready modes.  This would be very helpful in the office, home, or school, since the lighted buttons make the laminator much nicer and easier to use.  The nifty wrap-around power cord feature has been omitted, but I don't think I'll miss it much.  And this new Saturn is noticeably longer than the previous model, yet it still handles the same laminating sizes.  This new model offers cold lamination which the previous model was lacking; basically, "cold" lamination means you can use self adhesive laminating sheets and just feed them through this Saturn so the rollers give you a nice even seal.  I haven't tried the cold lamination, but the heated lamination works quite well.  It took me less than 10 minutes to create 3 perfectly laminated signs.  I turned on the Saturn to warm up while I printed my documents, and it was ready for laminating by the time I was done printing.  My three 8.5" x 11" signs all fed through the laminator in a couple minutes and were almost completely cool to the touch when they came out.  The Saturn itself was almost completely cool to the touch as well, and barely felt warm.  I hung my laminated signs outdoors and we've had several heavy rainstorms since, yet the signs are in perfect condition since they were perfectly laminated with this Saturn.Bottom Line -- this is a great laminator and I'm really happy with it; the updated look and layout is a big step up from the previous model.  My only caveat, is I wish it were a little more compact, but I believe Fellowes offers other models that may be smaller, though I'm not sure what the trade-offs are.  Overall, no complaints and I'm really happy with this new Saturn laminator.

Couldn't find these pens anywhere in my town. I love the med tip and the gel type ink. Dries quickly and works great.
good product priced well and works as described, ill buy my ink here again for sure. The price of this ink is fairly low relative to that of many black inks on the marke

This is a nice, sharp, cardstock constructed organizer.  Basically a folder with A-Z dividers built in.These are great for certain projects that you need to keep organized.  The folder isn't too big, and if you need a long term large volume organizer, you should get a larger item.  I find this item is well suited for deadline type tasks, emptied monthly or quarterly.  Because of the little hole in each section, it's easy to make sure it's emptied, and even better suited to this sort of regular tracking task.  If you hang on to receipts, this is also a pretty good size.Even though it's cardstock, this is overbuilt and looks very nice.  I expect it to last forever.

I was hoping for a bit larger girth on these as they are meant for sorting larger files by allowing you to break them down into sections within the same folder.I found the limit of about 100 pages, after that it seems a bit overloaded.. As I have a background in criminal law, I was pressed into service by a friend to assist in designing birthday activities for her CSI crazed son. This tape worked well.  Designed for forensic use, it is clear and appropriately sticky. The tape is easy to tear and use. It comes in rolls, not in the sheets that are pictured and there is no dispenser included.  I can envision it as part of a fun curriculum at schools or parties in addition to its professional purpose. If you are not familiar with forensic evidence collection, there are many resources online which provide the basics for free. Like most things it is not quite as easy as it looks and practice makes perfect. This tape functions as it should. I cannot speak to its archival qualities but it is moisture resistant. Over the years, Avery Dennison has been known for the proverbial "Hello, My Name Is" stickers, as well as for other paper office supplies.  Like the company's other products that I've used, the Avery Flags do exactly what they're supposed to do.  These would seem to compete directly with 3M's Post-it brand flags; however, there are some important differences to note.  The 3M Post-it flags that we use at home and at work come in a little, very convenient paper and plastic "case," if it even merits being called a case.  However, they are more conveniently packaged than the Avery assortment pack.  These Avery flags are also approximately half the width of the 3M flags, which, for me, is a positive, since I rarely actually need to write anything on the flags.  Another positive is the assortment of colors.  The 3M and Avery flags are comparable in texture, stickiness, and ease of removal.  In case it matters to you, for one reason or another, the 3M flags we're currently using at home were made in the U.S.A., while the new Avery product is imported from China.  While some potential purchasers may find that to be a significant negative, it is offset somewhat by the fact that Avery Dennison is an "Official Box Tops for Education Brand" and these flags come with a 10 cent Box Tops for Education coupon.

It's hard for me to rave about a practical product that does exactly what it should do, so I won't.  The Quartet Dry-Erase Marker Kit has everything you need to supply your Dry-Erase board.  Within the set, there is a 1.68 ounce bottle of cleaner, an eraser, and four markers (black, blue, red, green).  It is not the fanciest set imaginable, nor does it have to be.The markers don't have a strong smell and clean-up is easy enough.  I might have liked a few different size options (some of my dry-erase boards) require an especially fine tip, but there is certainly value here for the cost.  An easy recommendation if you need what the set contains.  KGHarris, 6/14.

The big deal: wireless.  The other similar model by Epson, the 7010, has a cable.  This being wireless puts it over the top for convenience.LOTS of PROS:easy to understand operation, visual display is intuitive, and it's easy to figure out. Just between model numbers, this has an easier learning curve even though it contains more options and versatility.The flatbed top lifts securely and is sturdy.  You can scan larger documents, which is helpful for textbooks and large cookbooks.  It prints even larger, but note there is a difference between widest scan and widest print.Heavy weight plastic throughout, all supplies come with it, including paper samples. (Make sure you have a good paper source, the 13 x 19 wasn't easy to find...) Nothing feels cheap.  My older HP had very shoddy plastic that eventually snapped through lifting the flatbed lid often.Not a big fan of multiple color refills, as even when one runs out, you'd think the others would continue working (my previous Epson turns all the colors off, even black, if one of the colors runs out...not convenient if you still need b/w and don't want to run to the store).  This isn't laser, and it's similar to the 7010 in many ways, but I like this better. Even the 2 sided prints feel different on this one.  I didn't notice as much of a color bleed on heavier weight paper (it wasn't huge on the other but noticeable on some finer details).The fax is convenient but I doubt I would use that.  I'm assuming most people are going for the wide print capability, which is incredibly helpful...more than you'd expect at first.  And given that it's wireless, rather than Ethernet, makes it much superior to the others, even in the EPSON line, without a huge upgrade in price.It used to be said to buy components separate: scanner, fax, copier.  The multiple use copiers always seemed problematic, like they didn't do any one thing well.  This does all of them quite well, and you'd save space and money.

I'm very impressed with the Wilson Jones View-Tab Extra-Wide Dividers.  I have worked in an office for years. Great ink. Used it for my Lamy fountain pen and it writes smoothly with a great dark blue color. No clogging, beautiful bottle. Highly recommended!

Much better than the $0.99 a roll stuff you can find on sale at some local store !  It is stronger and stickier, so packages bound with it will stay bound :)  I am using it to bundle rolls of old carpeting, a couple of turns is plenty to do that well :)

stands are wonderful for my two monitors although the legs need to have a different type of tip on the legs too keep it from moving so easily.  My cat does not like them because it alters my desk setup.

Having used anEpson B11B178011 Perfection V700 Photo Scannersince 2006 to scan over 10,000 photos and slides, I decided to try this unit as a potential "more modern" replacement.  Verdict:  I'm going to keep using the V700 for reasons that I will get to in a minute.The V700 is top-notch photo, film and slide scanner that I reviewed on January 21, 2007.  Despite giving it only 3 stars at the time due to some quirks, it has been a very reliable and flexible workhorse for the past 6 years, and I continue to use it for all of my photographic scanning.  Being that old, it uses fluorescent tubes for illumination, making it quite bulky by modern standards and also requires it to warm up for a period before use.  In contrast, the V370 uses LED technology for illumination and thus is only half the height of the V700 and has virtually no "warm up" delay.As a photo scanner, the V370 works fairly well and with one exception, produces scans of a quality that will be just fine for most people.  It also uses the same software and scanning concepts as the V700, so if you are used to the Epson way you can just carry on.It does have some things I didn't like:* The cover opens "sideways".  Every other flatbed scanner that I have or have owned has a cover that is hinged on the short axis and thus opens away from you if the scanner is positioned with the short axis facing you (which minimizes the amount of space it takes up on my desk).  But the V370 has the cover hinge on the long axis, on the right side.  This might be great for some people, but I find it unhandy, as will most right-handed people.* The V370 comes with only 1 insert or frame for holding slides and film (a combo unit that can hold 4 slides or 1 strip of 35mm film), while the V700 came with a set of 5 different types (of which I have used every one). Like the previous point, this will probably not be a problem for most people who typically don't have a lot of 6x6 negatives and other oddball formats to scan anymore.* Continuing a negative Epson tradition that I pointed out in my review of the V700, you can't buy replacement or additional film holders directly from Epson.  Their web site gives you a list of distributors to contact - Is that the best Epson can do in this age of buying online?* I should also mention that I could not get the drivers to install from the CD included with the product.  I am running Windows 7 64-bit and have never had trouble if this nature, but this CD would not autoplay, and when I tried to browse the CD and manually execute the setup.exe program, it would just hang.  Only after a considerable amount of fiddling around did I finally manage to get through the install process.  I was unable to determine if the problem was the Epson CD, some quirk with my computer, or the fact that I already had the Epson V700 software installed.But here's the real problem:  It doesn't always keep the edges of photos flat while scanning, thus you will likely see places on one or more edges of scanned photos where the photo is not totally pressed flat into contact with the glass of the scanner.  This causes some scans to have a slightly wavy edge and a tiny but wavering shadow in places.  Inspection of the scanner design shows the cause:  Because the V370 can scan both reflective materials (e.g. photos) and transparent materials (e.g. slides and film), it has illumination in both the base and the cover as would be expected.  For scanning photos, you slide an insert into the cover that provides a white background ... AND that should also press the scanned photo flat against the scanner glass.  Unfortunately, the white background is only backed by a plastic rectangle that does not support either the center of the background or its edges, thus fails to keep scanned material pressed flat against the glass.  I see no easy way for the user to fix this, but Epson could easily just re-design and replace this inexpensive item, which is not attached to the scanner unit itself.I also have a Canon LiDE 110 scanner on my desktop for doing quick document scans, so I had hoped that perhaps the V370 could have replaced *both* the V700 and the Canon, but that wasn't feasible either.  Without going into the details, the V370's drivers didn't work well with either of the document scanning applications I use.  I don't consider this a negative since the V370 is marketed as a photo scanner - I was just hoping to reduce the amount of stuff on my desktop.So I'm going to stay with my current scanning set-up of the V700 for photographic scan and the Canon LiDE for documents, and find a new home for the V370.
Super good printer which prints on both sides of paper and joins your network without cables, all for the cost of taking your wife to dinner at a good restaurant!

This is my 5th printer currently in my home.  I'm not eccentric either - well, not in that particular way.  Can't everyone answer faxes in the bathroom? - I've just had the chance to evaluate several printers for Vine, and yes, most things about Epson's line keep getting better.Likes:- setup: easy peasy. Even without a handy extra USB cable, I managed to quickly hook the XP-610 up to our home network. I was inattentive to the installation interface (busy with other stuff), but all was setup within 10 minutes, except for...- Epson connect: getting setup with a dedicated email address in "the cloud" at Epson and printing from my windows phone took a few minutes more. Airprint it's not, but it was very satisfying to *finally* be able to print from *my* devices.- Photo quality: absolutely on par with the behemothEpson Artisan 730 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner (iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible) (C11CB18201)I also have, and I was skeptical, yes, considering that it is light and has a *very* compact footprint. FYI, the Artisan has two shades of magenta and cyan (light and dark), yellow, and a single black cartridge. By contrast, the XP-610 has one yellow, one cyan, one magenta, one black, and then a "photo black". That would seem to be a significant difference, yet I can say that it is tough to impossible for me to differentiate between two prints of the same image, one from each printer. I can *sometimes* tell with monochromatic and gray-to-black dominant shots - the tiniest bit more depth and subtlety is there with the XP-610, to my untrained eye. And sometimes I can see a bit more warmth in the Artisan prints, but would hasten to add that the difference is extremely subtle.- A separate (non-photo) black for text printing: We'll see if that actually makes things cheaper, but I dislike using up hi-tech photo ink for text documents on general principle.- Epson Claria ink. I've finally taught my analog self NOT to print every pic I like "just because". But if something is going on the wall or into the album, I want it to last.Things I don't like:- opaque/un-guessable ink costs. Time will tell -- the cartridges in the XP-610 are bigger than any I've seen with other printers, and I can hear the reassuring sound of ink sloshing around inside on installation, but I'm not convinced that anything has really changed, as concerns ink capacity or per-page costs. The printer industry, born of the principal "give away the razor and get rich selling blades", has as though one entity shied away from making truly comparable cost and cartridge volume disclosures, and the whole industry gets a negative star rating from me, for that.- without an ADF, it's not truly an all-in-one, capable of scanning multiple pages in an efficient manner. I'd spring for one of its "big brothers" in Epson's 800 or 900 series, if I were looking to replace a printer. That's just me.- Paper handling (and CD) trays appear flimsy. I haven't had an actual problem with paper handling yet (light-duty printing) and haven't had the occasion to use the CD tray, but I had a similar complaint with the Epson Artisan 730. If you quickly deplete paper - and I figure that the full sheet tray can hold 20 sheets of standard weight multi-purpose paper at best - this is going to be a nuisance. Why go for cutting-edge photo tech and then make the actual box a tinker toy?- Epson connect: yep, that thing that is also on the "like" list. I don't like ordering the firewall to not do its job, which was a necessity for letting Epson print direct from email. I regretfully give up this functionality and hope for an airprint equivalent for windows or my Kindle. Sorry, Epson, but home data/network security trumps convenience, no matter how much I trust you.Things I don't much care about (but might, later):- The SD and MS Duo slots. I'll not soon get around to printing from my phone, because however great the app, I can't see preferring to edit from teensy phone screen over my desktop. Eagle eyed youngsters may beg to differ.- Printing direct from my camera - for much the same reason.- Photo correction features in the print interface - maybe one day I'll give up on Photoshop Elements, Corel Photo and the rest...but I'm not looking to "marry" a printer brand so I suppose I resist these kinds of extras as part and parcel of the printer.- Dedicated CD printing tray. (One of those things you'd probably be wild about, if you actually needed it.)Bottom line: I'm impressed that Epson has gotten this kind of print quality into such an unassuming little multifunction printer. I really really really reallyREALLYwish they would set a standard for per/print costs and stand behind it. I'd probably recommend the Expression 800s or 900s to those who truly want this for all-in-one usage, but if you've already got a laser printer with fax and ATF, the XP-610 could be a very reasonable and versatile *light duty* alternative to a dedicated photo printer. (Certainly, it beats making a trip to the lab to develop one or two snapshots to snailmail to family.)

These mini dry erase markers are definitely 'mini'.  The colors (excepting the yellow) are all bright and easy to read, and the magnets are useful for sticking the marker to the refrigerator side. I had read the many negative reviews on this sharpener... and after receiving it myself, I do understand some of the frustration, but have nonetheless found the sharpener decent & workable. A few comments:-- I think some basic directions would solve many of the problems identified, and save Wescott many of these negative reviews.-- The sharpener has an "auto-stop" feature when it believes the pencil is sharp enough. It does not sharpen to 'hypodermic needle' status (which usually snaps anyway), so you don't feel like you've walked away with the sharpest pencil possible. That being said, it is still sharp; probably the just-right sharpness for usage.-- It is unclear how to take the clear plastic cover off to empty! Fortunately, a good reviewer (dare I say "sharp?") figured it out... the plastic clear casing is actually two pieces. The top disc rotates counter-clockwise to screw off easily.-- I sharpened six pencils straight and only had one with too much wood left on one side, and it still was usable nonetheless.So, this is a useful, "adequate plus" sharpener, but the question as to whether it is worth $25, I am not sure. Another electric sharpener that I have used for a few years with some success is an X-Acto sharpenerX-Acto Electric Pencil Sharpener (1818)and the Bostich is probably the highest rated one for the price range atStanley Bostitch QuietSharp6(TM) Classroom Pencil Sharpener With 6-holes And Quiet Motor, Blue (EPS10HC)

It’s a little bit difficult to think of things to rate on envelopes, but I wanted to address a concern I saw. These envelopes are security envelopes in that they have a security lining. Yes, if you put just a check in the envelope you can see it quite obviously. However, you cannot read what’s written on the check or on any correspondence you put in the envelope. In that way they are “security” envelopes. In so far as the price, yes it is a little bit higher than the discount stores, but the extra dollar it costs me to have them hand delivered to my door is worth it. There is not what I would say is a significant different in price. Finally, I do love the self sealing feature (this probably adds to the cost). It is wonderful not to have to lick yucky envelopes anymore. The seal is very tight and lasting too. You don’t even have to put tape as extra security. All in all I like these envelopes for all my correspondence – personal and personal-business. Please remember, you mileage may vary and this is just one person’s opinion.

First let me start off to say this machine is very simple to put together and use so even if you are not very electronic saavy I think this machine will work for you. The steps are really easy to follow for binding as well. However, I want to say that this purchase does NOT include the binding sheets so please make sure you purchase them as well or the machine is pretty useless.Now for the review of the machine. This machine is good for small binding project. I got it for my fiance since he is a school teacher and it works really well for what he needs it for. I would stick to the lower end of the binding pages though because if you use too many pages, it doesn't turn out well. The quality is decent and the pages and very secure in the binding as long as you don't use too many pages and to me that's all that really matters.Now on to my suggestions. This item is great for a safer box / package opener.  Sure this item has a very small tip that will do the job for cutting plastic on packages like CDs.  It's also handy for opening boxes.  But, if you are looking for something to open things larger than that - look elsewhere.  This is not designed or even able to cut through carboard or anything thicker than a few millimeters.  This product has somewhat of an ergonomic grip, but really this seems unneccessary.  As for the safety switch, it doesn't lock very well and shouldn't be relied upon as a way to prevent children from opening the small blade.  This is not as dangerous as a box knife, but this does have a small razor point - so parents beware.  As for the point itself, I'm not for sure the life span.  But I can say it made easy work of several boxes so far and will be useful to leave near my desk.  Overall, it deserves 4 out 5 for what it does. Avery likes to call these gems Note Tabs Round but I have know the brand so long I still call them labels.  They are perfect for what they are.  They tell me where I want to be when I need to find something in a book or file.  The round edge makes it easy to use and the color makes it easy to see.
