There is a weight limit of 250 pounds, so this would not be your best choice if you are on the heavy side.It's a good chair and worth considering if you are looking for a genuine leather office chair.

With no instructions, it was a little confusing figuring out how to load this stapler. Turns out there is a button on the back and then the front pops open.When using premium staples, this works great. While some force is still required for stapling - it is less than your normal stapler. I'd say it only takes about half the force. Cheap staples will buckle and jam the stapler so buy the premium ones. They don't cost that much more.This stapler is good for a single user, but since it has some unique "features", like the awkward loading and the assist bar on top, I don't think it would work well in a group setting. I had to give a quick demonstration to my own family so it didn't get misused.THe glossy black & gray exterior looks nice on any desk.

Well designed and looks nice on any surface. The marker is not very good and you will want to get a different color for the darker board. The purple color hardly shows on the purple background. Other than that, it serves its purpose. Its a nice size for quick notes and to do list. Be careful not to accidentally brush a hand across it. You will lose all your notes.

Amazon has a lengthy description of this paper cutter on this page.  If you want all the intricate details of this paper cutter, you will want to read it.For the hands on evaluation:*This cutter is a smooth rotary cutter*The LED lights at the cutting line are a real bonus.  It has an on/off switch on the side.*Fiskars claims you will never need to replace the lights.*I am a big fan of the measured grid so that you can line up two sides of the paper on the perpendicular lines and get a perfect 90 corner.*I like that the measurements are protected by a clear cover so the marks never fade away with use.*It holds a nice stack of up to 20 sheets of paper to cut at one time.*It is very light making it easy to store when not in use.

The dry erase metallic silver board is great to use in the home or office. I hung it on the wall in my office. Large enough space to put notes on. The included dry erase marker is black, shows up well on the silver finish. Included double stick tape can be used to hang the board or use nails to hang it.

PaperPro 3-Hold Punch is really nice.I don't use it every day, but when I do it's perfect for my needs.It's well made and doesn't move around on the table when you're using it. It's convenient to have at home and it's very simple to use and to store.

The Avery Repositonable Address Labels for laser printers are a true boon to person wanting properly positioned address labels.  The labels use the new Avery "easy peel" technology. This feature allows you to quickly and easily remove the labels from the carrier sheet.Once the labels are applied, they remain firmly affixed to the envelope or box to which they are applied unless you actually get a fingernail under an edge. Then, the label is easy to remove and reposition on the object to be mailed. Once repositioned the label again remains firmly affixed.No more crooked, pooly positioned mailing labels!  What a relief! If you do mailings use these.

These pocket jackets help to organize documents. These are especially useful for collecting small documents like receipts, irregular sized documents or when you are transporting papers which could easily fall out of flat folders.I have a separate jacket for each tax year and when a tax document arrives, I file it into the jacket.I used to buy about 10 at a time, but it's a lot more expensive that way. The box of 50 is much more economical.PROS:- Useful for organizing papers, especially small ones and irregular sized papers.- The box of 50 is quite economicalCONS:- The one thing that would make this better, would be thicker material (paper). But then it would cost more, so I'm still giving this 5 stars.

I write a lot. I also use a lot of sticky notes to remind myself of what I forgot to include. These notes are perfect. I can stick them on over the original material, include my corrections and later compare the two. It's much better than sticking the notes on the edges of pages and hoping I remember why I put the note there.This is a great product. I highly recommend it.

We do our share of eBay selling, and Avery's Shipping Labels with Paper Receipts #5327 are really going to be simplifying the process.Each sheet is divided up into two parts--an adhesive 5 1/16 x 7 5/8 label and a perforated paper receipt.  They can work with Avery Templates for #5127 (found in Microsoft Word or at [...]), but we like the fact that we can use the templates from USPS Click-N-Ship and on eBay and PayPal Online Postage.Depending on which service you use, you may have to feed the sheets into your printer in a different direction, so we advise first practicing on blank sheets so you don't waste any of the labels.But once you get the hang of it, they're much handier than printing out plain paper that you then have to tape to your packages--and Avery's TrueBlock technology means that you can put the labels right over old ones without having to worry about the print underneath bleeding through--making recycling packaging worth the effort.  Green is good.

These are fine dry erase markers that write very nicely and fine.  They have a small to no odor and the fine tip makes the writing on the board look a lot sharper.  I've been using Expo brand since forever, but I think I might have found a new brand to use from now on.  I highly recommend it.
I have been using this 2 sided-tape for longer than I'd like to admit.  It is a staple, go-to item with so many uses.

Since we use dry erase markers frequently at our learning center, I bought a pack of these to try something different. My very young students were intrigued by the magnetic feature of these markers and by the eraser. Some became so intrigued that the markers became distractions as they played with the magnet and pulled out the eraser.The markers themselves didn't last long and don't have that bold, dark look I like in markers, not even when first opened. My short lived experiment wasn't exactly a disaster, but was far from a success either. The built in eraser is a great concept and works well as long as it stays where it belongs.

I recently created a "command center" by our front door to keep track of our schedule and "to do" lists. This vertical wall organizer has been fantastic. I use it to sort the mail as soon as I walk in the door. The files are removable and are a durable feeling plastic material. I am a big fan of the bright colors. It comes with labels that you can use to designate the different folders if you desire. I have mine sorted for bills, filing, important notices, etc. I've got mine hanging up on a nail in our entryway and it has been exactly what we needed. I love it.

This ornament storage box is very sturdy; as soon as it was constructed it felt secure and solid. The construction itself was simple, though the pictographic instructions were nearly incomprehensible. It's also surprisingly compact for the number of ornaments it holds. There is the usual problem of its inability to hold larger odd-shaped ornaments, but for small ornaments and balls it's very handy.
I have been through many sharpeners and so far this one is great. It sharpens well and is easy to dump. I hope it holds up longer than the last one.

This is an excellent printer for family use.  Now that everyone is working off of iPads or iPhones in the house, it is essential to have a wireless printing (multifunction) device.  The setup is a snap, and the footprint not too large.  We have not been using the fax feature much, but we have put this machine through it's paces with scanning, printing, and copying.  The full print client that comes with the printer on the CD takes rather long to install on each PC - but there is really no need for the full client.The ability to print photos is good, not great.  We have found that the blank ink seems to go quite quickly.You won't be disappointed - try this printer.

Perfect and quick.  I much prefer these to the plastic file label holders.  Write your folder name on it and stick it on your folder! Done! No fighting with slipping paper in little bitty slots.  These are a must have!

It's like a flashback to 1995.  The software install was horrible, multiple systems couldn't recognize it without doing a lot of manual configuration.  Has network connection but only plug, no Wi-Fi (hello, we're going into 2014).  Unit gets very hot in multi page output and puts out quite a stinky smell.  Paper magazine is very strangely configured.  Scanner is slow.  Page feeder can't hold many docs.  No fax capability so not really an all in one.  Setup interface is archaic and requires you to study the manual for basic things.Overall, this is a junker that's not going to see any more action in my home setup.  My dell color printer (see my other reviews) blows this thing away by a mile. It's like someone found a cache of these in a warehouse from yesteryear and now wants to clear them out.

I have owed the 2 line Uniden expanadable system since 2005.  One of my extensions bit the dust, and Amazon had the replacement.  Only beef I have, and this pertains to my particular base model, you cannot do the simple registration by placing the extension in the main base.  It requires a quick two step procedure.Otherwise, this is an excellent phone.  Also, Amazon has awesome prices on OEM and aftermarket batteries for these phones.
This photo paper is the best for printing photos from my computer. I chose it because HP has a good reputation. I can see why since it works great and gives me perfect pictures.

This is a very straightforward notebook.  It comes with 3 movable tabs that you can place as you wish.  It's a bit pricy, but you do have the ability to add (and remove) refills to it.  It comes with a few post-it labels, but those can be bought for cheap.  The other nice thing is that it comes with a pocket for holding paper.  I often walk around meetings with just a notebook, and cram papers given to me between the pages.  The papers end up falling out, but this allows me to fold the paper in half and slip it into the pocket.Overall, a nice notebook.

I'm still trying to figure out the "Pure White" thing. They don't write in white. The pens are not white (okay, partly white - but hardly "pure"). I guess it is the brainchild of someone in the marketing department at Pilot. I think the name is odd and confusing - but the pens are pretty good. They all write in black. It's a combination or hybrid of gel and traditional ball point ink. The point is 0.7 - which is a fine point, but not super fine. I usually like something around a 0.5, but this pen writes nicely. I often find fine points more difficult to read, but these pens produce a thin but very well defined line on the paper. Perhaps it is the combination of ink types used.The feel of the pen is a little bit "plasticky" to me for a pen that costs over $2.00 (based on the price of the five pack), but I haven't had one break. Even the "click/click" of the pen feels cheap. But it works, and writes well and feels smooth when writing - which is what really counts. It has a nice rubberized finger pad at the bottom 1/3 of the pen. On many pens, this type of pad makes the pen too thick to be comfortable, but this one is just right. A nice touch!

I filled a grip of these in my college days. Sure, other kids lugged their laptops into class and clacky clacked their notes. But some recent research suggests that the tried-and-true pencil & paper note-taking method works better for the majority of students.These Five-Stars -- not to be confused with my rating -- are classics for a reason. They are good for writing in the self-contained spiral-bound manner, or they are perforated for easy conversion into three-hole punched binders. They come in a number of colors for quick visual sorting by subject. The 8.5 x 11 size is photocopier and scanner friendly.The quality here is great. The design is simple and elegant. This is a classic for a reason. If only a college education was as worthwhile these days...

Canon's ImageFormula DR-M160 scanner offers high-quality imaging for the business or home office. The compact design assures that the scanner won't take a great deal of space.The software and design are easy-to-use. I've found that the scanner works on a variety of sizes, from legal to letter and business cards. In fact, I've used the scanner mostly to capture business cards. The software allows you to not only capture data, but also convert it to formats most useful for your applications.The data capture capabilities of this machine make it the perfect solution for legal and healthcare offices. The scanner will aid any office in efficiently managing records and reducing the amount of paper on the desk and in the office.This is a convenient scanner with the performance that one expects from a Canon product.

Fellowes Hot Laminating Pouches, Letter, 3 mil are a great way to protect your documents.  The letter size is perfect for laminating 8 1/2 X 11" sheets of paper.  I also used them to laminate an 8 1/2 x 11" sheet and then cut the sheet into index sized cards, and the lamination stayed on the paper.  This is a terrific way to preserve recipes - any spillage of ingredients, wet or dry, can simply be wiped off.  It's also a great way to protect sheets you need to study or memorize.  The 3 mil strength is flexible, yet still sturdy.  The uses for laminating are only limited by your imagination.

Pros: zips all the way around but also has an outside pocket so you can keep quick-grab items and not have to open the whole thing. Lots of pockets, some are net so you can see into them, some are not. It’s very lightweight, bigger than most legal pads so they will fit nicely. Really well thought out design.Cons: The only issues I had were two: One, it seems to show stains more than you would probably find in a plastic type binder or of course, leather. Personally, I didn’t like that it was too floppy. I’d like to have kept bulk lined paper in there, looseleaf as it were, but there is no firm backing. Just my preference!
interesting product, gets dirty, looses grip as expected, but is re usable, not forever though...

I'm giving this four starts because it works BUT takes a lot of work to remove permanent marker stains.The blue side is like a sponge to hold, the white side is the eraser.  Get it wet and you can try to erase the permanent stains.  I found out that it needs to be very wet but not soaking for best results.  (Minimal water cut through most of the dirty look but to get the deep stains required more water on the eraser.)  It also helps to dry the whiteboard or a residue/streaking will be left.I've posted pictures of "before" and "after" (where half the marks were cleaned).  I have a video to demonstrate the effort required but it's not available on this Amazon page.We've tried to remove those stains with various cleaners but the stains have not come off.  With some serious "elbow grease" and a few minutes the stains were reduced to mostly unnoticeable shadows.  Seriously, this took some work and heavy scrubbing to eliminate the permanent stains but the end result was worth it.This did not get the whiteboard totally white in some cases but good enough to not be noticed by someone who was not trying to notice.Side note... There were some permanent markings on wood and metal frames the were completely "erased" like magic.  I also got stains off (completely) several tables that had been marked.  (I know... this is not the marketed purpose but it worked so well that I'm going to try some stains on a linoleum floor as well.)

Our old calculators were fading away (and disappearing - thanks to the kids) so I decided to start new.  I was delighted to find this one with the Amazon label and price is terrific.  Bought two and we love them. Don't know why I waited so long to replace the very old dying ones (tossed the old ones to the kids to hopefully keep them off these new ones!).  This desk calculator has a surprising number of functions and is so easy to use with large keys and bright display.  Perfect for everyday math stuff and even more advanced functions.  I highly recommend it.

We got this to use in the office room at home. The cork is quiet dense and is able to hold things such as greeting cards and any reminder cards or photographs with a single pushpin. The board is also of decent size, but not too big to occupy too much of wall space. The frame is also of okay quality and strong. The corners might not be finished so well; It seems to vary from piece to piece - The piece we got had a 2mm gap in one of the corners and we had to fix it a bit.While the board itself is light weight and might not need a strong mount, the current way Quartet wants us to mount is using their hook which slides in between the frame and the board i.e. no dedicated mount holes in the frame. We used a saw tooth hanger to make sure it stays put with out sliding from side to side.

I did not purchase my magic jack (MJ) through Amazon but rather through the MJ website itself. My biggest complaint about MJ is the voice call quality and dropped calls. Often, the person you are talking to can't hear you and you have to repeat yourself a lot during MJ to landline or mobile phone conversations. The second thing I hate about MJ is the echo you get frequently. This drives me absolutely crazy when having a phone conversation. You say "hello" for example and then you hear the echo "hello" back or whatever it is that you said. This is very distracting and annoying. I suppose you get what you pay for. I have been using MJ for many years. I was even dumb enough to purchase a 5 year service contract but after it expires, I will not renew. Their customer support also sucks. They don't even have a toll free 1-800 number to call if you have a problem. You have to get online and establish a chat connection for tech. support. I know they will tell you they have to do this to keep costs down but this is horrible. I predict this company will eventually go belly up due to the poor call quality and customer support. I just purchased an Obi VOIP phone adapter to try out with google voice. I hope this will be a lot better positive experience than what I've had with MJ for the last few years. No matter how cheap the device or service, I personally still demand a min. level of quality that is acceptable to me. MJ has fallen way below that level so they have now lost a customer for life. From what I have seen and read, Ooma seems to be the best thing going but the up front cost for the unit is pretty high and there is still a nominal monthly ($3 - $5) regulatory fee each month after you buy the unit which I don't quite understand.

The Wilson Jones Pink 7 Pocket Filer is pink with vertical grooves that give it attractive texture. The pink is a little more salmon than the photo shows.  The handle is sturdily attached to the filer but when it lifts up it is meant for smaller hands. If you have large hands, you might well end up using the filer in "clutch" style because the handle is too small to carry comfortably without rubbing your knuckles.  Other than those distinctions, it is your solid run-of-the-mill pocket filer, though I will note it is fairly durable given how well it has held up with full pockets over the course of a couple of weeks, and this includes spending a lot of time stored on the floor.

These Avery labels are terrific.  I've used them a few times now (I reuse old boxes whenever I ship anything) and I am thrilled to have such a time saver.  First of all, they are huge - - half the size of a regular sheet of paper, and they are thicker than regular labels.  That means they cover just about any other label or markings you may have on an existing box.Secondly, it also means they are easy to print up using your computer.  Avery does have a label template you can download, but I didn't even bother as I can easily figure the size and placement.I like to use a large and thick font to print the label.  It shows up well on the box and, especially once you have stamps or a postage meter strip on the box, it's easy to see which end is up, so no problems there.  I've noticed a few other reviewers making a big deal out of the brown label on brown box thing making the address hard to find, but that is just hooey.  People have been wrapping packages in brown paper and writing addresses in ink for centuries.  It's no problem.If you reuse boxes for shipping, you can benefit from these labels.

In reading some of the other reviews I noticed several folks felt the assembly on these ornament boxes was difficult. I thought it was very easy to assemble them--took less than five minutes per box. If you have ever assembled banker boxes for files these assemble along those lines. I found the perforations for the folds to be nicely punched so the folds were easy. My biggest problem with the assembly were the four black cardboard "things" with holes. I know the handles were suppose to go in the holes, but when I used them, the handles were so close to the box that moving the box became more difficult. So I skipped that step. So far the handles have held!The configuration of the slats inside the box can be adjusted some what. In one of the boxes I doubled the slats on the bottom and then put the flat cardboard separator on top. The slats were strong and very protective of the Christmas ornaments. On the flat cardboard I put some lights and other items that didn't fit easily into the little boxes created by the slats. In the second box I used the slats the way they were originally intended. With slats on the bottom and the top. Unfortunately when used this way, the slats are very flimsy and in putting them together they bent and tore easily. I put nonbreakable ornaments in this box as the protection offered by the slats was not good.This is a great concept. The side with the clear plastic viewer allows you to see immediately what set of ornaments are in the box. These are flat storage boxes and will stack easily or fit under a bed. The drawbacks are the slats when used as intended--they are flimsy and you don't get much of a feel of protection for your ornaments. The other drawback is the lid - there is no way to secure it, so you have to watch how you move the boxes to make sure you don't tip them and have your ornaments falling out!
Needed an inexpensive corded phone for the desk in my wife's office, and this fit the bill. Good sound quality, very large, easy-to-read display, caller ID, speakerphone.
I like these envelopes.  They don't stick together in the humidity, they separate well, the glue to close works well.Functional.  Reliable.  Good Price.

I've been using Mead products for nearly forty years now.  My mother would give me Mead folders as a child to keep my "art" projects in and whenever I made the jump to elementary school, Mead became an almost daily part of my life.  Folders, binders, my many beloved Trapper Keepers, and plenty of other Mead products were always in my possession.Now that I have children in elementary and junior high school, Mead is still a big part of my life.  These One-Inch D-Ring View Binders have been around for a very long time, and now they are being used by my children.  Each binder is solidly constructed and feature three D-ring holders to keep papers, pencil bags, and just about anything else that has three holes in it in place.  The outer cover features a clear sleeve that allows you to slip in a title page, cover art, or just something that says "you" on it to personalize the folder.  Two interior pockets help keep loose pages and other important things from falling all over the place as well.Basically, if you need a binder that's built well and can take a lot of punishment from school-aged kids, you need this binder.  Also, while I only received one binder to review, this pack apparently features four binders, each one a different color.Highly recommended.

The Shelf Tags by Avery makes organizing small spaces easier. What I liked best about this set, is that a person doesn't need any special label software to create fantastic labels. The company has a website where you can design and create labels.

The Avery Tickets with throwaway stubs is a great idea but just didn't work out for us. I wanted to use it for the office but they came across too unprofessional. Instead we let the kids use them for a play at the house. Even then the printing was an issue.
Post It products are just wonderful.  They have never failed me.  This product is no different.  They adhere when and where they need to, and come off when I want them to.  Zero flaws.Buy it.AD2

I have a similar one with battery and solar power and it lasted over 10 years even though it says the battery only lasts 3 years.  It has a plastic cover to protect the calculator when not in use.  The numbers on the display are nice and large and the keys are just right.  It does all the normal functions without having too many keys and excess functions.  I have had Casio products in the past and they last so that is what sold me on this one.

It's not obvious in the picture, but those sides are open, and the more you shove into it it does press outward. This is mostly a good thing as it provides flexibility, especially for those large envelopes. For those who have an inclination for how things look and to avoid clutter, this may not be such a good thing because things will stick out or bulge, sort of, so it easily become unsightly. An easy fix for this is, of course, to keep things flowing from organizer to filing cabinet. Me, I like the flexibility to be able to shove a full paper size envelop in there for a few days. I have a smaller organize for the little letters that's cute for that.
We were moving and had to use a "POD" system for the move. This product kept our mattress and box spring clean and dry during this ordeal.
Very strong and sturdy tape-- great for sealing up boxes. Doesn't add misc weight on your boxes like the clear scotch tape.

So, I thought this would be a great idea for storing ornaments, as opposed to my current method of just throwing everything in the big plastic storage totes/bins. I liked the idea until I opened the package and realized all of the cardboard pieces which had to be assembled WITHOUT any real instructions aside from a shoddy diagram drawn on the box. The grid comes basically in long sheets which are perforated so you have to tear each and every strip off and then try to assemble the grid. And remember there are two layers of grid per box. Pain in the rear! I actually decided not to assemble the second box. I just did not have the patience and did not feel like investing the time. I swear it took me 20 minutes just to get the first one done.Once together though, the box is pretty sturdy and does hold a good amount of ornaments. I was able to get more than one ornament in most of the openings - depending on the size of the ornaments.I will add that it IS cardboard afterall, so if you plan to store the boxes in an area/room that is prone to dampness, mice, insects, musty smells etc, you won't want to use these, you will want to stick with plastic storage options with tight lids.

Love these pens! I love the idea that they are made of recycled material - there is even a little chart on the back of the package, explaining how the pens are made from recycled bottles.  They're also supposed to be refillable, although I have not tried this yet. The pens write very well (smoothly), are comfortable to hold, and worked well right out of the package.  The little label above the grip is slightly annoying from an aesthetic perspective, but not really something that detracts from the pens.

I will have to agree with most reviews that this is for one a little on the heavier side and that if you are not careful it will definitely hurt if your fingers get caught!!That said for an easy and compact stepping stool this fits the glove perfectly!Compared to the rest of the stepping stools available in the market i would definitely say that this is probably by far more superior and the 2 "issues' it may have can easily be overlooked if you really want or need a stepping stool that is going to be out of your way since it can pretty much fit anywhere, that is solid and secure.For eating fingers i should probably have given this a 1 star review but for practicality and safety its definitely a 5 star!I would definitely recommend this as long as its used with caution..;) And i would buy it again (i might just have to so i don't have to carry this one around and that will knock off the heavy lifting and transporting part)

The fellowes L80-95 is a compact easy to operate laminator. It's great for home and school projects. It comes with instructions which are well written and easy to follow. It is very  portable and can be taking for road trips and short journeys. I am very satisfied with the results i have had from using it. Will definitely recommend.

The adhesive is strong but the magnet is weak.  I'm using it to hold up small notepads to the fridge and had to use several strips to keep them from falling.So I mean it works, but it won't go anywhere near as far as I feel it should because you have to use so much to hold things up.
a good telephone, connected easily with my other phones and works very good in the garage.

This is a niche product that seems to works fine. The idea is that use a permanent marker to write on a clear glossy substance on a file folder tab and then if you want to change what you wrote all you do is get a white eraser and start all over. I did not have a white eraser so I just used a tissue and scratched away the marker with my fingernail, as a result I don't know how it works with the white eraser.I think this is a niche product because the white eraser and permanent marker don't come with it and I really don't know what a white eraser is. This seem like a lot of trouble to go through when you want to write on a folder. I just use a pen and a precut while label that I put on the tab. When I want to change the what I wrote I just paste a new white label over the old one and use a pen or any writing instrument I have in my office.On the positive side the tab writing area is large. I measured it at four inches across and two inches high. Most labels are not that big. If you have a permanent marker and white eraser and want to erase what you wrote on filing folders then this is the product for you.I was able to remove the marker with a tissue and the pressure of my fingernail but some people might not want to do this. If Smead wants people to use this product it should make things easier and at least supply a white eraser or say where to buy one.

This is a good binder. I like the material it is made out of as well as the way the rings are shaped.The binder is made out of a PVC Free polypropylene.  I like products that are PVC Free. I looked up polypropylene on the web and it is a plastic polymer known for its strength and stiffness which does not absorb moisture. All this is good for a binder.The rings are round at the back but flat on the front side that comes in contact with paper. Each ring looks like the letter D at an angle with the flat side of the D facing the front of the binder. As a result it is easy to take paper in and out of this and to turn pages when I am looking though the pages of my binder. The binder also has four inner pockets.I am pleased with this binder.

The highly touted ePrint feature has not yet been implemented.- Print photos, documents and more from anywhere, anytime using email - NOT TRUE AT THIS TIME !HP is being very deceptive. Avoid this printer and HP.

This is a decent binder with some good storage in a couple pockets. Since I do lots of crafting, I thought I could ued it for instructions and some pencils, notions, etc. The outside cover is a bright blue fabric and the lining is a nonwoven fabric. It feels a little more lightweight compared to the binders I am used to, but it should work for traveling with projects.

Why just one star?  Well, it's nothing to do with the quality of the printer.  Nor is it to do with the quality of the ink.  Heck, it doesn't even have to do with the expensive price tag.  So why one star?  Because although there is still about 75% left in the main black in cartridge and my printer is configured for "Use black ink only", once the printer got low/empty on the 3 colored inks, the printer wouldn't lay another drop of ink until they were replaced.  I thought this was a trick only HP used, but I guess I was wrong.  Seems like deceptive business practices to me.

I've been looking for a solution to loose files that barely get used without having to buy a durable jacket for them, which can be expensive. This product fits that bill. You'll have to expand the jacket in order to fit your average-sized manila folder. I was a little worried about the jackets tipping over were I to fit them with one or two heavily-packet folders, thinking they might lean into the jacket, tipping them over in the process. This didn't happen.  I was also wondering how these would hold up if I needed to carry them around periodically since the jackets are as thick as my medium-thick manila's. They hold up pretty under normal use, though the wear is easily seen. I do wish they had made them a little thicker than your average manila folder. I even have some manila's that are thicker than these jackets, which I didn't expect. The purpose these serve may outweigh the cost you'll pay for them if you were looking for a solution to loose manila's like I described above. It also appears that all similar  manilla jackets are priced around the same amount per folder, so why not stick with the king/queen of manilla folder's, Smead. I think the price you'll get on here makes them worth it. If I were asked to purchase them in the store, I'd spend a tad more for more durable one's. A, for me. Happy filing. Unless you're job involves filing all day, in which case, I'm sorry. Keep your chin up! *slowly walks away from computer*
Always a quality binder that withstands heavy use throughout the years.  I would recommend this Avery binder for office or home use.

****The 3M Easy-Adjust Dual Monitor Arm (MA260MB) does what it says, at least according to the Amazon description page, with one exception, and it does so at a price you might find too high.First, it is made of substantial materials of a good fit and finish that bespeaks the manufacturer's desire to offer a high-quality product as opposed to medium quality.  The market for these products will eventually decide where the sweet spot is between quality and chepth.(If depth derives from deep then chepth derives from cheap, right?)You can mount only one monitor if you like, although if you aren't anticipating adding a second one then you should buy a different model.You can mount the base using a simple clamp or by going through a grommetted hole that's been cut through the top surface of your desk.  Assembling the pieces and installing the result are pretty straightforward; the manual is imperfect but with the idiot-grams it serves the purpose.****ATTACHMENTSAttaching monitors to the two arms that attach to the mast that attaches to the base involves a rather complicated series of steps involving the following:-- 6 ounces of construction adhesive or 1 ounce of superglue (supplied)-- 72 - 144 inches of duct tape, depending (supplied)-- an oxyacetylene welding torch or equivalent (NOT supplied)-- two 10-inch and four 24-inch bungee cords (supplied)It's the bungee cords that I object to, and for which I subtract one star from five.  According to the instructions, which I admit I was translating from Spanish, which I learned everything I know about from eighth grade in dreamy Miss Swanson's class, because they didn't include instructions in English, the last step is to wrap the bungee cords around the monitor and the product under review in such a way that substantial portions of the screen are obstructed.  Now, I admit, the instructions do go on to say that I can solve that problem by reaching up and moving the bungee cords out of the way as I like because, as they say so proudly in their ad copy, "No more solid straps of steel that won't move away from those rows and columns of your spreadsheet, forcing you to scroll!  We use ELASTIC."  Still, I think there must somehow be a way to affix a monitor to an arm without using ANYTHING that wraps twice across the screen in both directions.  But I dream.****The height where each arm attaches to the base, one above the other, can be adjusted only with the use of an Allen wrench, so if you buy this product you'll want to take a while to figure out which heights you want before you lock them down for non-wrench good.The monitors attached to the arms can be rotated from portrait to landscape.  And, yes, back again.  Also, you can stop rotating at 45 degrees if you want, although if you have any use for such an orientation I'm sure we'd all like to know what.The mechanism that allows you to re-position the monitors "with just a touch" does not meet my standards for that exact phrase.  The phrase "with just a touch" implies to me that all I need to do is move the thing around the way your dentist moves around that light that she shines into your mouth.  She moves the whole light in any direction and then points it in any direction, and when she lets go she needs only another moment to see where it will settle and make a final adjustment, and then it stays there.  This product's articulations are not that good.  You cannot always re-position a monitor "with just a touch."  For this hyperbole in the description I subtract another 1/2 a star.The product offers a nifty way to collect the various cables, which neatens your deskular region, but be warned that thicker cables will fight back.The ratio of maximum weight in pounds of monitor (20) to maximum monitor width in inches (27), a critical factor in most of the professional reviews of such products, is 74.074%, which when expressed in metric units (9.07185 kg / 68.58 cm) turns out to be that same 74.074%.  Spooky, huh?****It has been brought to my attention that the section above titled ATTACHMENTS, while 100% accurate, applies to a completely whole 'nother product, so please ignore it.  Also, obviously I add back that 1 star I subtracted from 5.As both fans of my Amazon reviews (Hi, Mom and Dad!) already know, I like to perform off-book tests, which most readers find not just useless but a waste of their time to read.  If you aren't my mom or my dad then skip down to the last paragraph.-- When shot with a .22 caliber long rifle round from 30 feet, the product under review managed to deflect the bullet while suffering only cosmetic damage.-- The product under review works perfectly well under water.  The monitors attached it, as I should have foreseen, don't.-- If you have a little duct tape left you can remove the monitors and attach a candle to each arm and use the product under review as a candelabra.  Warning: Even though you can, you should not switch from portrait to landscape.The 3M Easy-Adjust Dual Monitor Arm (MA260MB) is pricey compared to competing brands' offerings. for which I subtract another half a star, which leaves a grand total of four.

I like to make lists so that I can cross-through or check-off when the task is completed:  Makes me feel a certain sense of accomplishment--for whatever that is worth. If I find that the battery life of my wireless mouse doesn't last any longer when I use this mousepad, I'll update my review.
