-Always on the search for a pen that works right. Happened to pick up a pack of these at one of the big box stores and have been pleasantly surprised. Here's what I like: they aren't hard to get started writing, unlike others; ink doesn't normally clump on the tip and smear until wiped off - unless, of course, I manage to write through a bunch of lint and then I'm asking for it; I can see the amount of ink remaining through the pen's translucent body; and they're slim enough to be slipped into the wire coil of a notebook or clip part of a clipboard or my purse or pocket. They're also inexpensive.The only places I might not use these would be when writing checks (want a certain kind of ink for that), when writing upside down when a gel will flow better or for those who need a fatter pen to grip.Other than those situations, this is now the pen of choice.

The Fellowes Smooth Move Moving Boxes are sturdy, well designed boxes.  While some people might see them as just another box, these are built to stand up to plenty of moving and multiple uses.  The walls are made of thick cardboard and will withstand some punishment.The boxes are very simple to assemble and with their self locking (no tape required) lid, it is easy to use and reuse.  I would not recommend carrying very heavy loads without tape though, so play that one safe.  The boxes are just as easily collapsed as they are assembled, so you can store them for future usage.  Or use them as more permanent storage.

Should I be complaining about something that was less than a dollar?Yes, absolutely.The top layer of material, the red layer, is coming off from both the top and bottom of the muse pad after about a week's worth of normal use. The adhesive or bonding process isn't holding the two layers together.The size of the mouse pad is very good.It tends to slide around on my desk with very little effort.Waste of time with this mouse pad. Surprised at the lack of quality from Belkin.

I love the D-ring feature.  It keeps paper from bunching up and getting that hump that often comes with binders if you don't move every page over before closing the binder.  It's pretty hard to close the binder if the pages are not totally lined up, so it makes the hump all but impossible to achieve - SUPER!  The cover also got wet, but because the water didn't get under the plastic outer sleeve, everything inside was fine.  What I don't like is that after what I consider normal use - putting the binder in a bag and taking it out - the cover is showing obvious wear.  It looks like the outer plastic cover / sleeve may pull back in a few more uses / replacements.  If this is going to sit on a shelf or not be rubbed up against other binders / books, this will probably not be an issue for you, but if you're using it for college or something, you may want to find one that's more rugged.

Quartet Magnetic Pencil/Pen Cup Holder has a strong enough magnet that it sticks well to metal surfaces.  I have mine on the front of the fridge, and it stays put most of the time.  The cup itself is sturdy, not thin and cheaply made, and it holds a nice amount of pens/pencils/markers.
These chalks have lovely bright colors that show up well but wipe off my son's easel chalkboard easily.  Very happy with these!

Okay, the super duper thing about these are how cute they are. The are printed on one side with a cute and modern print while the back of each is a solid, coordinating color.The are basic but the standout feature here is just how cute, girly and fun they are. They do not come with labels so you will need to provide your own or just hand write on the tabs.They contain a minimum of 40% recycled materials and are printed with soy ink.

These manila file folders are much stronger than average, and they manage to create a larger space for writing/labeling the tab at the top without significantly sacrificing the height of the folder. This box is the letter size file folders, so make sure your file container or cabinet is designed for letter size rather than legal size if you want a good fit. Unless you need to find the cheapest file folders you will want to consider these Smead folders for their convenience and durability.

**The good features of this chair are that it only took 20 minutes to assemble today and the assembly process was very easy, the directions very clear. Also, the seat height can be adjusted. Unfortunately, that's about all that I can say that is positive about the chair.The chair that I was sent through Amazon's Vine Program does not look like this chair at all, so I'm not sure what your chair will look like if you order it. The chair I received was labeled correctly as "HON Boda HMH01" but is a cheaply-made office chair, definitely not something that retails for almost six hundred dollars. It has a mesh backing that is not adjustable for the lumbar region, nor adjustable for tilt. The arms are hard molded plastic without any cushioning at all and also not adjustable for height nor position; the left arm rest is already starting to pull apart where the glue is failing. The cushion is poorly made and already wrinkled by the ill-fitting cloth cover.The tilt of the chair is fixed and cannot be adjusted; however, you can loosen a knob below the cushion so that you can rock on the chair. This could not be called a tilt because the position of your back cannot change while sitting in the chair--the angle is fixed at 90 degrees and when you're rocking the seat rocks right along with the back. In addition, the seat has a slight downward slope to it instead of being parallel with the floor; I found this very uncomfortable.This chair would honestly work better as a prop chair for a theater set, not something to be used on a daily basis.Not recommended.**

My Mom likes to can things like Jelly and apple sauce.  However, her hands tremble a bit and she can't write very clear labels anymore.  So, I volunteered to create some labels for her and these did the trick.  I am not a huge fan of the brown color.  I think that they could be a bit lighter, but they did the trick.

This Scotch tape is a very thin tape that is fairly adhesive but doesn't have a whole lot of tensile strength - it's akin to some of the really flimsy packing tape you'll find for $1 a roll.As such, it's not really something you should be using to tape up a box.  It's best used on top of an already existing seal, or as a replacement for a label that just says "fragile."  If you're using this to replace multiple labels, this might actually be fairly cost-efficient as you could likely get several hundred 'fragile' pieces from the tape.  As tape itself, it's rather expensive for what you get.4 stars.  It does a job, although it's a bit expensive for its purpose.

These are divider tabs made of light card stock and designed for 8.5 x 5.5 binders. They come with a sheet of clear labels for printing on laser or inkjet printers.The current Mac OSX version of Avery DesignPro (free at the Avery web site) has dozens, if not hundreds, of templates for Avery label and divider products. It does not, however, include one for the Clear Label Dividers with White  Tabs (11426). This may be owing to non-standard paper size (5.5" x 8.5") of the label sheet. Fortunately, the Avery Design & Print Online web site does include a 11426 template. In order to use the label sheet, I had to create a custom paper size on my printer (HP C7180), Once this was done, I cut a piece of letter-size paper in half (using a paper-trimmer to get a straight, square cut). I filled in the template and then printed on the plain paper. I held the printed paper against the label sheet and then up to the light. The alignment was nearly perfect, so I went ahead and printed the labels. The labels printed neatly with no smudging (sometimes a problem on media not specific to inkjet printers).The all-at-once method of peeling and applying the labels (described on an insert) is somewhat tricky, but it works if you're careful to make sure the labels all stay attached to the strip as you peel it from the backing.My only concern about these divider tabs is I think they are too lightweight for frequent or daily use (more durable solutions are available). They should be fine, however, for reference binders. The printable labels give the tabs a finished, professional look.

This is the only kind of wire bound notebook that I will buy my daughter (high school).  The wires have never snagged her clothes and the cover is a very strong plastic type material that won't shred or fall off after a couple of months.  She likes the vibrant colors and the durability, knowing it won't fall apart where she'll lose notes or important information.  In between each 'subject' there is a 2 pocket filing page that is also very well made and never ripped apart.  I highly recommend the Five Star brand for Jr High and High school kids since they are throwing their books in lockers and dropping them on the floor and who knows what else these books go through, just spend the extra money to make sure their stuff is safe from wear and tear!

The 3M mouse pad is a little small for my own personal taste, but the gel wrist rest is wonderful I have been using if for the past week and a half and offers support which lessens the strain and has reduced wrist pain which most often this pain is related to carpal tunnel.  The only think I would change would to have the item a little larger. I think if this was offered in the small, medium, and larger sizes would accommodate more peoples preferences.

There's a phrase from the Mad Men era that goes something along the lines of "give away the razor, sell the blades." This kind of gets at the heart of the label maker business these days. The hardware is cheap, the labels not so much. And I guess that's the fatal flaw with the new DYMO LabelManager 160 Hand Held Label Maker: It's so capable of doing so many things that you end up making mistakes - lots of them - as you learn to use it. I'll grant that the folks at Dymo did their best to keep the user interface simple, but in the end this is not the most intuitive device, and that lack of simplicity costs you money in the form of wasted label tape. I'm not sure there really are any simple label makers anymore. These companies keep trying to out capability each other with every new device, but they've passed a threshold where common sense and ease of use have been trumped by unnecessary bells and whistles. If you need this many features and options, fine. But if you're like me and you JUST WANT TO MAKE SOME LABELS WITH A FEW WORDS ON THEM, then prepare to spend time studying a manual...and spending a lot of cash on labels as you learn!

This pen is not an ink gel, which can be notoriously hard to write on certain surfaces.  This pen will write perfectly until its dead, and in four colors, too, each color bold and brilliant.  I do a lot of editing and anytime I can get my hands on colors other than black or blue is appreciated.  You can even use it to color code your calendar.It's not a pen to use to write a novel, however.  It's better for the smaller projects, because the one thing it lacks is a good grip.  But it's not hard to write with -- it would just get tiring during long stretches.

Ordered this to secure my headphone ear pads. Works well, does the job. There is a protective leader for the first several inches. Tear that off and the rest of the tape is unbacked, double sided with adhesive.

I love office supplies, especially labels.  I used these to label totes of toys that I am rotating out of use for the time being.  I also used some to print out little pictures of what is inside different toy cabinets to help my daughter put her toys away in the right order.  It was fun for us to pick the photos and then put them on the cabinet doors.  My daughter loves the bright colors for her play room, and I love the fact that they come off when she's older!The ink didn't run, and the label sheets were able to go through more than once without coming off and getting stuck in the printer.
Since I buy my cartridges from Amazon (prices are better), I have written several reviews in the past. HP is a good brand, and they work well in my HP printer, enough said?

Not sure what it is about mechanical pencils these days, but tween boys seem to be fixated on them.  Our youngest and his friends all use them and beg for the latest model.  So I got him this set through Vine and he loves it.  In particular, he said that the thickness was more comfortable than in other models.

I'm not sure how to write a review of address labels, but I can say this:  They stick excellently, are "green" friendly, feed perfectly into the printer without smudging, and are the best in the business.  I've been using Avery products for over 30 years and they have yet to disappoint!

This looks like a good idea, thePost-it(R) Pop-up Laptop Notes Dispenser, 3 x 3 Inch (LND-330-3PK), but it's not what I thought it was going to be.  Post-its are great!  This is a smaller package of Post-its that are fanned, every other way in the pad.  I really like Post-its, and I am loyal to the original 3M brand (the other generics that are out there don't stick as well as the original ones do).  But the holder is just a very light weight cardboard, or a heavy weight paper that the Post-it pad is inserted into.  The holder has tape on the back, remove the protective film that covers the tape, and stick the holder anywhere.  It will hold there, and can easily be removed and re-stuck elsewhere, at least a few times before the stick-em no long holds well.So, why only 2 stars?  It's the holder!  It's just a light weight piece of paper that is folded to hold the pad.  I expected something a little more substantial in weight or design.  You know you are paying a premium for that holder, on top of the price of the pad of Post-its.  But the premium is not worth it.  Sure, the holders are colorful, might look nice in the ad, but come-on, it's just a piece of paper folded to hold Post-its.  I would have rather they used a plastic type of holder, even light-weight plastic, then I would have felt the premium that you pay for this would have been worth it.

I recently bought this phone after several two more expensive models failed; his telephone by AT&T; and Lucent works better than the other phones I bought when I had to get a new phone for my home. The construction of this telephone reflects great engineering; and it's very, very reliable for a price that's very inexpensive these days for a phone. Yes, it is corded; but when all you really need is a basic phone this really does the job. Besides, the fact that this is corded means you'll never misplace the cordless handset!The phone has back lit buttons which are desirable for those of us who are elderly or in any way sight impaired. The buttons could be brighter but the back lighting does improve upon no lighting. The phone offers well known features including "last number redial," too. The phone has a mute feature, adjustable ringer volume and more. These functions never disappoint me. It also has a small knob that lets you switch between touch tone and pulse (rotary) dialing. I use touch tone dialing as most people do. I am particularly impressed that a phone in this price range even has a twelve number memory feature for speed dialing. Cool! However, as another reviewer correctly notes, when you program the phone to remember frequently dialed numbers, you need to actually dial the number--so hang up fast if you don't intend to speak with that person at just that moment! I don't care for that so I will take off one star for this.If you want to take a nap without the phone ringing, just turn the ringer off by using the knob at the base of the phone. That's an incredibly useful feature!I highly recommend this telephone for people who merely want a basic, inexpensive phone that still has a few "frills" to like including memory speed dialing and mute. The extra features give you all you truly need to make this a well constructed telephone at a rather inexpensive price. Sure, the back lighting for the buttons on the phone could be brighter; but overall this is still quite a good phone for the price. The phone takes up little space and it can even be wall mounted to completely save counter space in a kitchen or any other room.

I have tried several different scanners to archive old photos but have never before had a method of digitizing the huge file of negatives I had accumulated over the years. This scanner performs in an amazing manner and can handle 35mm and 120 film and photos as well as 35mm slides.  I have color negatives and positives and this scanner handled them all.  The software that comes with the scanner is very user friendly and I was able to pull the scanner from the box, load the software and go to work.  I am very impressed and can recommend it to anyone that has old negatives and prints they want to convert to digital format.

The ratio of the white board section compared to the cork board section of this was just right.  (The overall size was perfect to hang above my desk, also.)  Installation (on to drywall) was very easy - it took me maybe 2 minutes to install.  The clips that are included were very helpful because you can level those first and then pivot the board into the bracket.  You can also adjust it side to side from there.Having the options to either write on this board, or attach papers with either the enclosed magnets or tacks make it very versatile.  Overall, this is exactly what I needed and it looks very professional.

A very nice arts and crafts tape from the Scotch brand. There's only 1 patterned tape and 2 solid ones. The tape is translucent.It's like regular Scotch tape, just with colors or patterns. It's not as sticky as regular tape so you can reposition it. You can cut it or tear it.  You can write on it like regular Scotch tape. It can be torn.I think it's a neat tape for projects, scrapbooking and other fun activities, just a nice variation from regular Scotch tape.

We finally switched to a Canon printer last year after many frustrating experiences with hp. We thought it was a great printer until this this baby arrived and blew it out of contention.  The ink cartridges are the easiest to load ever.  The print quality is amazing.  All in all if you have a need for a new printer of this caliber consider this one.

This Samsung laser printer handles all my home printing needs. It is quick and the resulting printed page has clear, crisp text. I generally don’t print out much of importance, so the Eco button to save on ink is a very nice feature. I also get much use out of the duplex feature which allows me to print on both sides of the paper. The printer has the capability to take jobs from a tablet or phone. I don’t use this option, or I haven’t yet, but I’m sure there are many people that could make use of it.Setting up the printer was a snap. It’s footprint isn’t that big compared to my old printer. I had to do some finagling with my space though because this Samsung printer isn’t wireless and I had to connect it to the computer. If your desk or home office is big enough, it shouldn’t be a problem. I have an awkward space to work with, so it took a long cable and some rearranging to get it going. But if you’re looking for an easy, cost-effective laser printer with good output, this Samsung should do the trick.

I have plenty of notebooks with plain lines, like everyone, and sure, that's... fine. But this is much more satisfying for working on actual multi-step projects. I particularly like to use the unlined "notes" column on the left to comment on how things went, for future reference.The paper is decently thick, but not super fancy. The covers are flexible textured plastic, which feels nice but makes the notebook hard to use without a desk. Also, this notebook looks EXACTLY like other styles of Cambridge Limited notebooks (like ones with just plain lines or the meeting planner, or whatever) so having a few different ones is confusing if you don't mark them somehow.Still, I kind of want to collect them all. And I don't even have any meetings to plan.

Being that I've taught Art for the past sixteen years, I've used a lot of paper trimmers in my time, and there were things I was concerned about with regards to keeping one in my home, mainly centered on the safety of my pets and any visitors, and any natural curious tendencies that might provide a deep cut or three from the standard super sharp blades that hang down from your average office/studio/Art room cutting board. Westcott covered that base with this cutting board, along with plenty of others!The Pros, for me:*The blade is easy to lever up and down, without being too loose to effectively cut even a small stack of papers, or a single sheet. As a rule, I don't try to cut more than five sheets of any standard-weight paper at a time - it's just too easy to wear the blade out too quickly this way, and a dull blade is no one's friend! This paper cutter can handle more than my requisite five sheets, but I probably won't push that envelope too often in my home use of it. Of course, the titanium coating on this blade probably renders that concern a non-issue, but some habits are hard to break, and I think I'll just keep this one...*The clear plastic guard on the cutting board also makes it easy to quickly guide the paper exactly where you want it to, and it's easy enough to press down on the wide plastic edge to hold the paper in place as you cut, if need be.*The rubber grip on the handle makes it comfortable to use, even for long cutting jobs, and I really have no complaints there, either. It's a thoughtful change from the standard hard plastic grip that I've grown so accustomed to using in my classroom, and the fact that it's likely to fight germs with the Microban coating goes a LONG way towards bumping up the stars in my rating! Until you've been exposed to countless germs and gotten sick every six to eight weeks (literally!) because of them, something like that might not seem that important to you, but if you plan on allowing multiple people access to your paper trimmer, this feature WILL prove its value to you!*The board is lightweight, and therefore SUPER easy to just pick up and move around to wherever you want to use it, without having to struggle with it. The lock for the blade is vital for this, and easy enough to flip down with a thumb to open the blade and get to the cutting! Placing the lock back into position is also easy, and the fact that it's made of metal means that it'll last for the long haul, doing what it needs to do to keep the blade exactly where you want it to be, especially if you have little ones running around with roving hands!*The ruler and guidelines on the board's surface are clearly visible, and cover all the bases, even including a centimeters ruler on top of the standard inches ruler that I'm so accustomed to.*And, my favorite feature - the lip that comes down to protect the edge and keep it from slicing fingers in the moving of it! I LOVE this feature!!! Others might not get as excited by that as I do, but over the years, the relocation of any paper trimmers in my classroom have ALWAYS factored in my very real fear that I would slice my fingers on the exposed blade in just picking it up to move it from here to there! When you've done that more than once, as I have, you'll find that you, too, appreciate that lip that makes the blade a non-factor in moving your paper trimmer! LOVE that!!!The Cons (and I have to nitpick to really find any at all...):*Really, the only thing I can find to gripe about at all is the fact that this cutting board is made of what I know as fiberboard, but even that isn't really a big issue. From what I can tell by just looking at it, this cutting board's main surface is made of a super thick Masonite, which is something I'm all too familiar with using in my artistic pursuits. It's thick, and while it wouldn't be wise to stack a tall pile of super heavy hardcover books on it, this board is more than thick enough to withstand your needs for its intended purpose. At over half an inch thick, it's not going to give under the weight of anything you're going to cut with it, and, really, if that's not enough, you need to use something other than a paper trimmer, 'cuz you're just gonna trash the blade cutting anything super thick anyway.*Another non-qualm: the size of this board will not be enough for you to cut any crazy-large sheets of paper like the occasional 24" x 36" sheets I have stashed in my art room, but it's more than adequate for trimming the 12" x 18" sheets I purchase as a standard for use with my Elementary art students (all 700+ of them), and it's definitely big enough for home use.At this price, with its awesome features and Goldilocks-perfect size (not too big, not too small), this paper trimmer is perfect for scrapbooking, use in a home office, as well as use in a personal studio space. It's not too small to stash in a corner somewhere, easy to lift, and the blade is fully covered and locked into place, making it perfect for the home user.I really can't find a thing wrong with this trimmer by Westcott, and there's just so much that's right about it! If you're in the market for a good one for your personal use, this will address every need you might have!

This is a great product from Logitech, which makes a great companion to your laptop. Very sturdy and doesn't look like it would break easily. However, you only have three settings: 20, 30 and 40 degree angles. Why not have more angles? What was stopping them? Surely they could've made room for more angles (From 10 to 50 degrees, in increments of 5 for example.) Aside from that, no complaints at all!

There's not a lot to add to what others have said. These pens were surprisingly colorful and a pleasure to use - not that I got to use them much since as soon as my artist (and picky) daughter found them, she said "wow - these are nice!" and promptly stole them. I would buy these.

I bought this for a small homeless drop-in center.  5th Panasonic system I've bought in the 8 years.  Works great.  And since you can make calls from the base using the speakerphone, it's like having another handset that can't get misplaced.  It's perfect for its use.  (Bought it used from Am____ Warehouse and saved money.  The phone system is in great shape.  The only thing is that the batteries are cheapies, not Panasonic.  This could be a problem, in which case I will file contact Am___.)

Likes:>Easy assembly: unfold the folded and flattened cardboard boxes and tape the bottom flaps with strong packaging tape.  Same for the top flaps after items are secured in the box.>Relatively sturdy and should be able to handle most 37" x 27" x 4" or smaller pictures, frames, mirrors, or anything else that could fit in it.>Recommend getting theseCorrugated Frame Protectors 4 x 4" - 400/cartonto protect the frame/mirror corners.  Main idea is to pack the box nice and tight to prevent unwanted movements that may cause damage.>Printed with "FRAGILE, HANDLE WITH CARE, DO NOT LAY FLAT", and large "Up" ARROWS to prevent moving/storage snafus.>These boxes are also large enough to store my extra bicycle tires (700c, non-foldable with wire beads).>Original outer box could also be used: just cut the sealing tape carefully at the end of the top flaps and peel open the outer box.>Recyclable.>Made in the U.S.A.!Slight Concerns:>I appreciate these samples but $26.67 for a pack of four large cardboard boxes is a bit high.  Check around your local art supplies/ hobby shops for free/low cost boxes that are usually just thrown away.>Strength and durability of of lower flaps highly dependent upon strength of packing tape used.  If in doubt, use heavy duty duct tape!Overall:Good moving/storage boxes for pictures, frames, mirrors, etc.

There are countless less-expensive alternatives to Canon Photo Paper Plus Glossy II, but this paper not only gives the best initial results for printing photos, it resists fading much better. When I want the best results from my Canon inkjet photo printers, this is always my first choice. This paper and my Canon printers were MADE for each other and it shows.  Although 8 1/2 X 11 size paper is gaining acceptance, this size fits most traditional photo frames and albums and is ideal for printing wedding album photos.  What doesn't make sense is why the same number of sheets of this smaller sized paper costs more than the larger size paper.

I love the size of this laminator, but its uses are limited. I have several laminators, and this one warms up and is ready to use at an acceptable and competitive speed, but  will only work with the thinnest pouches, producing results that may be fine for casual use but lack durability. It is incredibly easy to use but users must be precise when loading pouches. The worst problem I encountered was that the bottom of the pouches came out scrunched. It does not measure up to my $30 Scotch laminator which is more versatile.

This printer replaced a Canon all-in-one that I loved, but is no longer available. This one prints OK but is really noisy and kind of slow. Print quality is fine, I think the ink consumption will be all right judging on what I've used so far. I haven't done any color printing to speak of so I won't comment on that. Hooking it up as a wireless network printer was simple.Scanning is very slow compared to my old Canon. The ADF works well and it does give you the option to add more pages to a PDF file. The copier works fine.It has 3 paper sources, which was a big selling point for me as I use different types of paper for various tasks and also print checks. That's about useless. You can only put one sheet of paper at a time in the rear feed, which was where I had hoped to print checks from. Half the time when I try to use it with one sheet of paper, I get a 'paper jam' error and have to go through all the rigamarole of pretending like I'm clearing a non-existent paper jam and start all over. I've folded that thing up and don't use it at all. You have 2 cassettes in the front, which each hold a ton of paper - that's a plus. It defaults to the top tray, which is the one you have to push the output tray in to access. I am forever forgetting to pull the dang thing back out so it's spitting paper all over the floor. The bottom tray works, but you have to select it every time you want to use it and it is twice as noisy as the top tray for some reason. I print some invoices on half sheets of paper. Not with this printer. It sucks them in sideways. If you attempt to use the paper alignment edges in the paper tray to feed it straight, they center up your half sheet and it only prints half of your invoice. I will have to redo those invoices to suit this printer. Not real happy with paper management.For no apparent reason, it frequently stops printing in the middle of the page, sits and thinks about it for a minute, and then spits out your half-printed page. You then have to go and cancel the document and start over. It does this to me on almost a daily basis. If that weren't irritating enough, this morning I'm printing away and it stops in the middle of the page (of a multi-page document), a pop-up comes up and asks me if I realize that I'm getting low on ink and would I like to order some. After I check the leave me the heck alone and get back to work box, it spits out the half printed page, and I have to cancel the document and start over.I am using this for a home business and I will probably use it for awhile to justify spending $150 on it, but I would never buy another Epson printer. I'm going back to Canon, I don't care how much ink I go through - time is money and it makes my dogs uncomfortable when I swear.A footnote: When looking at the 4 1/2 star rating, bear in mind that there are twice as many Vine Program reviews than there are unbiased reviews from people who actually purchased this printer.Changed my review to one star. After giving up on the wireless network, there is no improvement in printer function. I never go a day without getting an error message and having it stop in the middle of a print job, spitting out the half printed page, and requiring me to cancel the print job and start over. I have been attempting to print holiday newsletters printed on both sides with photos. I can't begin to guess how much high-end paper and ink I have wasted with this boat anchor today. It also told me I was low on ink so I thought to replace that cartridge before starting the next round of printing to avoid more mysterious errors. It refused to allow the carriage to move to the center position for cartridge access. Another reboot and more swearing.

I judge a printer on cost per page, reliability, output quality and features. This printer scored high in all areas. Error free installation from the software Cd provided. It is always a pleasure when all goes smoothly. In office use the the text is high quality and very economical with the super size black pigment cartridge. Another feature that I likes color photo quality on plain paper. It is nice to have great color on plain paper so one does not have to always use expensive special finish papers.It has every feature one could possibly want!All around pleased!

I wanted a small flatbed scanner to convert nearly all of my paper documents (four lateral file drawers full) into PDF files. I've now scanned well over 1000 pages now with no problems. It could be a tad faster. Even as it is, it finishes scanning before I have the next page ready at least half of the time.I'd give this scanner five stars were it not for the fact that the Mac OS X software included is so obviously an afterthought. The CanoScan Toolbox does not even have a standard  OX X interface (It's not Win XP either, it's just something else entirely).  Another minus is that the software which ships with the scanner is several vesions out of date and it's not as easy to find updates on Canon's web site as it should be.Overall, however, it is an excellent value.Follow-up 2/27/08: The Canon software is not compatible with Mac OS X 10.5, notwithstanding what it says on Canon's software update page. When I contacted Canon, they basically admitted the problem and offered to sell me a newer scanner at a discount. Instead of replacing the scanner, I replaced the software with VueScan. I have had no problems scanning a couple of hundred pages using VueScan in Mac OS X 10.5.

This is very simple to set up, easy to mount to the refrigerator, and easy to use. It's a little strange how the post it's pull sideways to come out but it seems to work well. I would recommend this to anyone with limited kitchen counter or drawer space.

The Wilson Jones Ultra Duty D-Ring View Binder I received has features to recommend it and one flaw that disapponted me.The binder itself is stonger than your usual binder and holds up under weight which is a nice feature, as we all tend to sometimes stack books, etc. on top of binders.  The D-Ring system opens easily, smoothly, and quietly and secures closed the same way.The four internal plastic pockets hold up, even when you pull on them with some minor force.So what is the disappointment?  The plastic pockets on the outside of the binder arrived damaged and alreay ripping.  These are the parts where you'd slide in your front and back pages/images and the spine title piece or image.  Since this plastic seems to be of the same quality of the interior plastic, it apparently doesn't have the strength to endure the wear and tear that the outside of a binder experiences.  Obviously, since it arrived damaged, it perhaps jut "snagged" on something before or during packaging.  Whatever the cause, the fact that this outer plastic covering didn't hold up to the minor figor of being shipped out in a box to me, it makes me hesitant to recommend the product as the outer plastic should be able to endure some contact and usage before ripping.If you need a binder to store papers in that doesn't endure a lot of rigorous usage via transit, stacking, etc., this would be a good sturdy product but if you need a binder that holds up  to a lot of wear and tear and maintains some external appearance as it travels with you, this may not be the binder for you.

This book was very fun and educational for my daughter. She really enjoyed learning and the way this book is formatted. I think it is a good tool for early education. Excellent tool for beginning to write.  Highly recommend.

Let me mention that this shredder replaced an Aurora I had a bought a few years ago. I can honestly say that this has got to be one of the best shredders on the market. It does not overheat or jam (given it's used as recommended) and can easily handle credit cards and thicker cardboard stock. It is quiet and looks quite attractive in my office with the glass window (which easily allows you to see when it is getting full. It is easy to empty and does not spill all over the floor when the top is removed (with paper stuck in the top like my old one. This unit may cost a little more than others, but you really get what you pay for when it comes to shredders. This is a must have for any home office.
Not very easy to assemble but the boxes protect pretty well. It is quite difficult to get the tab into the slit and you will need to tape the box before sending (it does not have the sticky backing).

Though this is by far the largest printer I've ever had, setup was easy (give yourself around 45 minutes for the whole process though). Unpacking is simple enough, with the normal amount of packaging foam and tape to remove. There are two print heads to install, and four ink cartridges, all of which are simple to put in. Once the printer is ready to go, plug it in and turn it on; this is where the time comes in. The initial printer power on takes around 20 minutes or s, where the printer aligns the print heads, etc. Once this is done, the configuration screen comes up. My connection is wireless, and the printer quickly found my router. Entered my security key and that was that. Once the printer is connected to the internet, it checks to see if an update is available (in my case, it was). After the printer was up and running on my network, both my Mac and Windows PCs had no trouble finding/adding it.I've had other HP printers, and this one is the best by far. Good sturdy machine, and not as noisy as other models I've had. I like the top loading paper feed for copying/scanning, and the capability of printing on both sides of the paper is good both for the bottom line and for the environment.5 stars.

I must be nuts.  I'm a crafty person in an obsessive sort-of way, and I have never laminated anything other than by the old-fashioned method of using clear contact paper or the Iron Ages method of wax paper and ironing board (what...you never pressed leaves in school?).  What have I been doing?  I could've been laminating my daughter's special artwork all this time!  Not to mention lined paper for use with dry erase markers (handy for a kid who's learning to write), lists of which foods are safer (mercury, pesticides, etc.) to put in my wallet, and of course, business cards, birth certificates, etc.The laminating pouches can be purchased anywhere (check out laminator d-t com), and you do not have to use the specific brand, which was my main concern in purchasing a laminator.  Smooth, relatively quick, and easy to use, this is a wonderful addition to my craft table.  I highly recommend.

The 3M Gel Wrist Rest works well for me.  It has cut down on aches in my wrists.  My old keyboard had a built in wrist rest, but when I bought a new keyboard, I realized I needed a wrist rest.  This one does the job well.  It is heavy, so it doesn't slide around too much.  The rest's padding is fairly hard, with just a little bit of give.  It runs the length of my keyboard and extends to the mouse, so I can also use it when I use the mouse.Overall, this is a great wrist rest, but I do have one concern - the backing plastic.  I am worried it will bleed into my desk.  My computer speakers had similar plastic pads and the black dye ended up bleeding into my oak desk.  To avoid this issue, I have kept the clear plastic film that is supposed to be removed on the rest.

this is a really good phone for the money. It has a nice digital display. Now if I could only find it in black, i would have bought two of them.The phone is wall mountable or desktop. It has every feature I can thing of minus an answering machine. It rings and you can talk on it : )  everything a phone should do. Great for the kitchen.

This 3 drawer unit is very practical and can be used for so many different things. We use them under our bathroom cabinets to better organize the area and eliminate clutter. They work well and have lasted years already. It's nice too because they are really easy to clean because you can just take the drawers out and put the whole unit in your dishwasher.

I've been using this pad for a couple of weeks and so far it has been very comfortable. It provides a nice cushion and good support for my wrist. I was not having any movement or pain problems before so it wasn't like this cured anything but it does provide very nice support.  The gel pad is smooth and soft.I'm not crazy about the artwork but this was a Vine sample so beggars can't be choosy. It stays in place, the mouse is responsive to the pad surface and rolls easily, and the quality is very good.  My only negative is that the gel pad acts as a stop or barrier at times, meaning I can't roll the mouse far enough to move the cursor to where I want it on my monitor screen so I have to pick up the mouse and put it at the top of the pad again.Nice product.

This is a decent paper trimmer for the price. It's sharp, and it seems to stay sharp with the self-sharpening mechanism. It cuts up to 10 sheets of paper at a time, though half or less is most likely to give you the best results. It is a rigid plastic product, but it will flex and break if used with a bit too much zeal. It is lightweight, and has a built-in carry handle, which makes it nice for educators and on-the-go office job types. I feel a rotary blade would have offered a better cutting solution as opposed to the guillotine style blade, with little impact on overall production cost, but it still gets the job done without mangling heavier weight papers. Lighter weight papers are more likely to get mangled by this guillotine style in my experience, so keep that in mind when choosing a trimmer.

I wish I could separate my star ratings for these labels because the labels themselves get 5 stars all the way, but are they really worth the price??  I don't think so.  A Sharpie costs what...$2??  And you can reuse that over and over and over again to mark out old labels or barcodes on boxes you want to reuse.  Sure, smack one of these labels on it and it looks prettier, but is sending mail a fashion statement these days??  The only time I could see that as being appropriate is if you have a business and want to reuse a box to send something to a customer...but then again, some customers would take offense to a company reusing a box (I on the other hand would find it awesome that a company was reusing or recycling something).These labels print nicely on my inkjet as well as my laser printer.  They do curl a little if I use my laser printer, but every label does that due to the heat they generate.  The template works perfectly and I haven't had to throw any of them away due to coming out wrong.  I sell a lot of stuff on eBay, so these got used up rather quickly.  With some labels I have purchased, the label has come off of my brown packaging paper resulting in the post office having to open it up and try to determine where it needs to go.  I REALLY don't like when that happens, so I always tend to add a strip of tape over labels...but these are stickier than your normal label and I haven't had to add extra tape.Would I buy more?  Probably not due to their price.  If you are concerned with your boxes looking "ugly" when reusing them, try going into the paint section of your local Wally World and buying a roll of the brown paper you are supposed to lay down when painting.  Don't get the roll from the office supplies section, it is the same paper...yet you get 10x as much on the roll in the paint section for about the same price.  You can rewrap your boxes with this and have that "pretty" box that some are going for using these labels.  :-)

My current white board came with a marker that velcroed to the board, which was nice until the ink ran out. My daughter and I enjoyed printing some samples of what would be the invitations for her party this year.  The template at Avery website is very simple and easy to use. My job forces me to use the mouse, almost non-stop, for most of the day. I paid $65ish for this and this is of great value.  I love this laser printer.  It even came with ink, and I'm still printing strong.  I've gotten through a couple of summer classes already.  I'd say about 200 pages or a half-ream of paper.  It was really easy to install and it's fairly straightforward to operate.  Another reviewer did the math and came out with (I believe) two cents a page once you replace the starter ink cartridge.  This pretty much pays for itself.  SWEET!!!!

I'm a big fan of Neat products and love my portable receipt scanner along with their award winning software.  The NeatDesk is the grown up desktop version of their popular portable product.As a desktop scanner it was great.  It handled business cards and crumpled receipts with aplomb.  Removing the business card and receipt guides from the scanner allows you to quickly scan 50 pages at a time.  Note that it is not a flatbed scanner so you can't scan anything that won't fit through a sheet feeder.  No scanning from a book or any delicate documents.The software is also very user friendly.  If you scan a receipt, it autodetects the amounts and vendors via OCR and can easily export to third party financial programs.  Exporting to PDF and other formats was very easily but ironically it won't allow you to export to text only.  The fact that the OCR functions only work within the Neat database is disappointing.  I was also disappointed the Neat scans are stored in a database that must be exported (similar to a Outlook PST file).  This makes backups of the database take more time and should the software every go corrupt, recovery is much more difficult.You should note that although the device works on Mac or PC, you must specify which version to purchase as you will be charged another $99.99 if you buy the PC version and later want to use it on the Mac.  That's a poor business decision to charge such a high price for someone who wants to be cross platform.My biggest complaint, besides the cross platform Mac tax, is the pricing.  It's a great product and a great scanner, but it is quite pricey and proprietary.  For that same amount of money I could by a sheet fed and desktop scanner along with third party software (that stores each scan as a document rather than in a database),If your primary goal is to scan copious amounts of documents that need to be exported into financial software, this is a great hardware and software combination.  Other users might get better value piecing together their own software and hardware combinations that would be cross platform on Mac and PC.

This is a three-ring binder that is very sturdy and has a great capacity, with what looks like a good 3 inches worth of paper room before things start to get tight. The rings are opened by depressing two levers simultaneously at the top and bottom ends of the spine. There are two slits in the rear and front inside covers that allow you to slide a few sheets into, which is very handy for any notes that may accompany the contents of your folder. The spine, front and back covers also have a clear plastic film over that allows the insertion of cover pages or a spine title. There's room to slip a large spine or cover page into these locations and there are no irritating brand labels or other markings that might detract from the presentation. The spine rings open and lock back together with a satisfying clonk and they have a very sturdy feel to them, so I expect that they will endure many years of opening and closing before even the slightest sign or wear might occur.I am very impressed with the quality of this folder and I have been using it to store copies of some of my favorite role playing books, so I don't have to wear out my original versions. The folder is useful to keep all the books in one place and the sturdy construction means that I will not be replacing it for a very long time, perhaps never. I am also looking forward to adding a bit of an artistic flair to the covers and the spine, so it will look very presentable on my bookcase!

I was about to buy this phone but had a couple of questions.  Called VTech. A ridiculous system that took too many entries only to end up on hold for a period of time that exhausted my patience.  No way will I buy a VTech phone with that kind of support.

The track pad on this is amazing:  I have aLogitech MX Revolution Cordless Laser Mouse (Black)which has laser tracking, and it moves so smoothly on this pad I actually felt I needed to slow down the tracking speed.  Very nice.I chose the white.  The appearance is nice, but there is something unfinished-looking about seeing the inner "guts" of the pad.  Strangely, I also think it's kind of cool.  Didn't affect my rating, but it's an thought.The pad material is very soft, almost velvety (not velvet in actuality), and seems to be made of some kind of foam with a soft top layer fused to it.  I cannot say enough about how pleasant and good this feels.  I'm a tactile person, and in this I give five stars.  I do question how easy it will be to keep clean; if that becomes an issue I'll update.The reason for four stars is the pad itself - it's really good, but not perfect.PROS:--The feeling of malleability under your wrist is very nice.  I have a gel wrist rest mouse pad, and this is far superior in comfort.  It's sort of like having your wrist on a supportive - yet flexible - air pillow.CONS:--The angle of the wrist rest is not quite right.  I have mild (i.e., manageable) carpal tunnel in my mouse-using-wrist, and the ideal angle is where your wrist is completely horizontal until it tilts slightly downward towards the mouse.  On this pad, your wrist is tilted slightly up (not horizontal) before it tilts slightly downward towards the mouse.  This is off just enough that even though the material and cushioning is superior to my gel pad, the angle is not.  The pad upon which the mouse moves is deep enough that if I move my entire forearm forward so that my wrist is at the apex of the curve instead of following the entire contour, it keeps my wrist more horizontal.  But in this postion, the pressure point on my wrist (where it feels good to have pressure applied when you have carpal tunnel) is not engaged, so it's not perfectly comfortable this way either.SUMMARY:For people without a specific wrist issue I give this five stars:  I don't think the slight curvature will make any difference, and everything else is super-fabulous.  But I really think if you've got a wrist-issue, this is just imperfect enough to make one look elsewhere.  Overall, I really think this is a great product, but for me it's sadly not going to be my go-to wrist support.

I'll admit, I didn't think I could be impressed by a mechanical pencil, but I was using this pencil all day, and I sharpened it once: the first time I used it.I will also admit that I was wary about the eraser, it was quite small, but the quality was such that I never had to use it overly much, and it never left those annoying marks that my minor OCD goes crazy over...The only real negative about this pencil is that it uses 0.5 mm lead, which means I can't usually borrow lead, but that's hardly an issue as I'm always prepared with an extra case. I just wish I'd gotten this sooner, it is a huge improvement over your standard mechanical pencil. I highly recommend.

I used these image transfer pages to make specialized onesies.  I started with white 100% cotton onesies that I prewashed/dried.  Following the directions, I preheat my iron (a no name cheap brand) with out any water inside for 5 mins.  I placed the onesie on a pillow case on a chair, applied the transfer paper and ironed for 20 seconds right to left, then another 20 seconds up and down pushing down while I ironed.  I allowed each onesie to sit for 5 mins before I pulled the paper off.  Each onesie came out perfect.As a tip, I would recommend that you make sure no dust or hair falls onto your item... I had a hair that is now part of the beautiful artwork I made for the onesies.
These are original equipment and work well in my brother all in one printer. There is nothing to complain about.

Man I wanted to like this product so bad it hurt! The ease of going paperless seemed to good to be true and in the end it was. First and foremost the 50 page maximum scan at one time is a joke. That's only IF it counts all the papers correctly, or doesn't jam, or doesn't miscount. The clarity on this thing was awful for black and white documents. Even after I fooled with the settings. The Scotch pop up tape dispenser is a nice space age solution to the old fashioned plastic dispenser that not only needs two hands most of the time to operate, but also has to be cut off manually which sometimes sees the end result of your efforts being a twisted tape stuck to itself. (Don't ya just hate that).  This handy item is very well thought out indeed.  The bottom tread design sticks nicely to most surfaces, and the pop up gizmo seems to never have a misfire.  Each piece of tape dispensed is around 3 inches long and is easily grabbed and pulled out without flaws.  It certainly takes up much less room than the old style heavy tape units that aren't all that portable.  This can be picked up and moved anywhere.  The only possible downside to this dispenser is the cost for the amount of tape you actually get.  No question you can get a lot more for your money picking up the old fashioned role style we are very familiar with.  However if money is no object, or, you just favor the idea of this handy space saving unit that makes grabbing a quick piece of tape really easy, this is a nicely designed alternative well worth your office space.  Recommended...

Had it on my wireless network within 20 minutes out of box, Nice quality in in the photo printing and nice to include some sample photo paper in the box. The scanner works very easily also. All in one package at a affordable price. It is nice to share with two computers on opposite sides of the house.

Avery labels have been the industry standard for fifty years or more. I used Avery labels in the mid-60's when I did mass mailings for local businesses.  Their product is always high quality and problem free.  TheseAvery Textured Wraparound Labels, White, 7.85 x 1.75 Inches, Pack of 50 (08217)are certainly no exception.The labels come five to a sheet, each just short of 8 inches wide and about 1.75 tall, plenty big enough to use to make a splash.  In years past one needed to download special templates to use with your word processing program, but these days Avery has a special design tool right online at their website, one that works no matter what computer you may have - no software required, though you can download the program to your machine if you prefer. Note that you will need to register with your name and email address.The design interface is exceedingly simple to use.  After entering the product number (8217) you can choose from 56 different design styles.  Do not be fooled into thinking that you are limited to those 56 exact designs. Each is merely an example of the way that things will be laid out.  Each and every element can be customized, either with something from Avery's gallery or something from your own computer. You'll also find dozens of fonts and several hundred colors to play with. Once you've finished your design you can print as many or as few labels as you need, so none will be wasted, and can then use the same design on a different Avery product if you would like. (You can also save your designs for later use.)The labels are suitable for either a Color Laser or Inkjet printer.  (10 sheets, each with 5 labels.)Grandma's $0.02 - This is a great imaginative way to have custom products for your event or business!Highly recommended

Being in the world of accounting, I staple a lot in an eight hour work day. A lot. On a busy day I can easily go through one strip of staples and more, and I really do love theSwingline Optima 45 Electric Stapler, 45 Sheet Capacity, Silver (S7048209)that I got from Vine, but that's a bit spendy to have on every desk in the office, so I found this handy for the back room where the files are stored (plus it's a lot less expensive), and it's a much cleaner staple than most of the older (much older) Swingline staplers in use in this building.The Lightouch worked right out of the box (just put the staples in), and it is very light to touch the top and get your reports stapled. These 1/2" x 1 3/4" inkjet/laser style permanent adhesive return address labels are strong stick, assuring your label won't peel off in transit.  They come with 80 labels to each sheet and they work perfectly with my new Brother all-in-one printer,  and now I can create a return label with my business name.  They are compatible with Avery's 5167 template or use one from [...].  The printing is dark and crisp using either template, however, the Avery template gives more flexibility for centering.  My test address was perfectly centered on the label using my WordPerfect program.  Since the labels are only 1/2 inch high, I recommend you set your font to sixe 7 to assure you get the complete three-line name and address on the label.  Just copy/paste and hit the return key to move on to the next label.It's necessary to make sure the paper edges are smooth and uncurled which will happen if the same sheet is repeatedly inserted into the printer.  I printed two sheets of labels, half with my personal info., the other half with my business name.  Office printing is a snap thanks to the great products from 3M.Highly recommended.

I did not use the Wireless setup and did use the enclosed CD for installation.Upon receiving, I was oohing and aahing about how sleek and pretty it looked.  Once I started unwrapping, I immediately started comparing to my HP C5280.  Yes, it looked nicer, but it's obvious functions lacked in comparison.First off, it doesn't print CD's, which is not a major concern of mine, since the Sharpie is my tool of choice when needed.Secondly, it doesn't scan negatives or slides.  This is an option I do like to have, since I do happen to have old negatives that I'd like to scan one day, somehow, someway, eventually it'll happen.  Just not with this All-In-One.Setup with the CD was easy enough, but slow.  The calibration process and printing process is slow and noisy, although no more noisy than my C5280, but definitely slower.  I'm an impatient person, when I hit that print button, I want the paper to load right away and get the ball rolling.  This doesn't happen here, nor does it with the C5280.As for the HP software, again, I'm not a fan of HP Photo Essentials, which also came with a previous printer.  I haven't given it much of a chance to give a good rating, as I hate it that much.  It's not user friendly and doesn't cooperate between printers.  I also have an HP Photosmart P1000, which yes, it is a dinosaur, but has been reliable for a good 6 years.  My printing software of choice, I believe, came with that printer, and is just called HP Photo Printing Software (v 2.2.0.4) and is a wonderful basic image editor (excellent for adjusting color/brightness issues).  You can also choose the paper size and what standard size photo is to print on that media (for example, an 8.5 x 11 page can print 4 3x5's or 3 4x6's or more 2x3's, etc).  I don't know why HP found it necessary to deviate from that software.  Another option is to install 'Windows Live Photo Gallery', which I'd rather have a root canal than install any more bloated Windows products, even though I've been a Hotmail user for years.  I also don't like the browser additions that they felt were necessary to add to my IE7 and Firefox toolbars.  I don't appreciate that kind of intrusion by ANY software manufacturer.  Yes, it's simple enough to remove them, but it would've been nice to have been asked first (which some installer programs will do).It was nice of them to include a 100 pack of 4x6 photo paper.  I'm stocked up for life as it is on photo paper as it is, so I doubt I'll ever get to use this package. I've used a small Fiskars paper trimmer (Model 95907797 - still available here and elsewhere) for about 10 years. That model only accommodates 8.5 inches, but it is also designed to fit into a ring binder. Last year, I bought a larger model (1298937797) so I could trim 8.5 x 11 paper vertically if I needed to do so.I've been happy with both of these trimmers. They meet my needs: one or two sheets at a time, precise, straight, and (most importantly) perpendicular cuts. If you need square corners in a one-off or low-volume situation, these trimmers are the way to go.The Fiskars SureCut Recycled Titanium Portable Paper Trimmer, 12-Inch (01-005454) adds a feature not on my older trimmers: a guide wire that helps if you are trying to cut along a line already on the piece your are trimming.I decided to try this out on a pile of coupon supplements from the Sunday paper. These are printed on cheap, thin paper that tears or starts bunching very easily. The SureCut trimmer worked perfectly on this task. It made long and short cuts without hesitation, and the wire guide allowed me to literally cut on the dotted line.The SureCut wire is spring-loaded, probably to make it less likely to get bent or broken if the cutter blade gets jammed up somehow. It also looks like the wire could be user-replaceable (the black end caps are removable), but it is not available on the Fiskars site.Fiskars markets these trimmers as craft rather than office products. They are not intended for frequent or heavy-duty use. They have a line of rotary trimmers and an anvil trimmer aimed at office users. This trimmer uses Fiskars Blade Style I (eye, not one). Though hard to read, this is thoughtfully embossed on the bottom of the trimmer. They also make a scoring blade. I've never had a scoring blade, but I assume it's intended to let you score paper to be folded instead of cutting it. Replacement blades are available here and at many office supply stores.My slightly older 12-inch trimmer has rubberized caps on each corner that also act as non-slip feet. The Fiskars SureCut Recycled Titanium Portable Paper Trimmer, 12-Inch (01-005454) has no such corners or feet of any kind. This leaves it up to you to hold it down a such a way so as to prevent sliding around while you're using it. To me, this is a design oversight, given that other, less expensive models do have non-slip feet. One star off for that.

I bought this printer back in October of 2003.  So far, this Canon has proven itself to be very fast, reliable, and economical.  There is an option to use "draft" mode for the purpose of conserving ink.  This is a great feature to have if you print a lot of text, like I do.  The black ink cartridge is also relatively inexpensive.  I bought this particular printer because I print a lot of text.  My main criteria was keeping the cost per page as low as possible.  I rarely print photos, but the few that I have printed on Canon's paper looked very nice.I like the design of the printer.  You can fold the paper holder in the back forward and it will act as a dust cover to keep the inside of the printer clean.  You can also close the front of the printer as an added measure to keep the inside free of dust.  The i560 is a little bit more expensive than comparable printers from other brands.  However, I believe that the lower cost per page will more than make up for it in the long run.  There are individual ink cartridges.  And the ink cartridges do not have a smart chip built into them.  It might be possible, although I have not tried it, to refill the cartridges yourself if you can find the right ink.  However, I think the cost of the ink cartridges for this particular printer is low enough that I would recommend buying only the genuine Canon ink, that way you can eliminate most of the problems that people experience with generic or refilled ink cartridges.  I was told that a lot of problems that people have with their ink jets are due to using generic or refilled ink cartridges.

This is a great little printer.  No printer cords needed if you have a wireless network.  Unlike wireless printers I've used in the past, this one is super easy to setup (I didn't have any of the problems listed in the other reviews and I have a Mac and a PC).  It has a view screen so you can print photos directly from the printer without even having a computer.  It also copies quickly for an inkjet and can scan to any computer on your network.The scanning has led to some issues with my family sending the scans to the wrong computer, but that's user error and not the printer's fault.  Just be aware that your family may need some lessons in scanning if they aren't that computer savvy.  "Copy" is pretty idiot proof.I love that it is wide-format.  It can actually print scrapbook sized pages.  It also prints on both sides of the paper without reloading.  These are all excellent features to have on a printer.  I've used it to print cards, envelopes and 4 by 6 prints and it does a good job on all of those odd sizes too. One tray is very adaptable and can fit many different sizes and papers.It should be noted that this printer is huge and heavy.  Check the measurements before you buy it.  It's an office sized piece of equipment and it is even bigger than my home office laser printer.  It wouldn't fit on my printer stand and I had to find a new spot for it.  Since it is wireless, it doesn't need to be near your computer.The only drawback is that it is an inkjet.  After my last inkjet, I swore I would never own an inkjet printer again.  I use a color laser printer for most of my general office stuff and have my photos printed.  Because of all the other features on this one, I decided to try it when it was offered on Amazon Vine.The first 6 or 7 prints were very, very impressive.  I was entering a photo contest and I had some photos professionally printed.  For fun, I decided to reprint them on this machine.  The colors were outstanding and I actually preferred them to the professionally printed photos.  I was singing the praises of this thing at the contest display.  None of the photographers could believe my prints came from an all-in-one.  Had I finally found an inkjet to love?Love/Hate I guess.  Don't get me wrong. I still love it, but my next two prints were streaky.  I checked nozzle alignment and cleaned the heads  (a necessary evil with inkjets).  They reprinted awesomely.  A few days later, I decided to print some flyers.  Streaky again.  Aligned/cleaned: Awesome again.  The streaks only happen when you print color, not black and white.I have started just cleaning the print heads before I print color.  At least I won't waste paper that way (photo paper is expensive).  You can clean them from your computer with one of the provided utilities. My guess is that this is a problem on all inkjets, so I'm not taking any stars away for it.  It's the reason I gave up inkjets to begin with, I just hoped after all these years they would have minimized it.Aside from the general drawbacks of inkjet printers, this is a great little printer that is very versatile and can handle almost anything I can think of to throw at it.

I love Avery Sticky Notes! They work really well with sticking them in books to take notes or just to keep a page to go back to later. I would buy these in the future! They also come in bright colors, which make them hard to miss!

This is a medium-duty stapler suitable for office, home, or school use. It has a steel frame, with a few parts, such as the hinge assembly unit in translucent blue plastic (although the hinge itself is steel). The pusher block inside the mechanism is red plastic, and the spring is steel. The stapler weighs 11.5 oz and is 6.5” long by 1.25” wide by 2” high. The bottom is steel but has 2 small rubber  feet for traction on slippery surfaces. It accommodates a 4” strip (125 pieces) of standard staples (#4). This will allow you to staple up to 20 sheets of paper with one blow. The base plate folds back just over 90 degrees, enabling you to staple onto soft wood items (but not walls—you would need a full 180 degrees of open movement to do that). The product was made in China.I like the feel of this stapler in my hand. It fits well, and it staples papers with ease. There is a precision fit with the base plate, no mushy wobbliness like you find with some cheap plastic staplers. Staples come out one at a time and I haven't had any trouble with jamming. The fact that the stapler doesn't open to 180 degrees is a bit frustrating. I'd like to use this stapler for hanging posters on bulletin boards, but it seems it was designed specifically not to do that since it cannot be used flat against a wall. For simple paper stapling, though, this is a fine implement, easy to use, and likely to last many years.

I am a 7th grade teacher. I have a lot of students and a lot of pencils to sharpen each day. I've had this sharpener for 3 years, but I never let my students sharpen their own pencils. Why? Because they break it. I sent this sharpener to the "Doctor" two times and the last time it almost didn't make it back. Students looove to stick the wrong end of the pencil in or just keep the pencil in and sharpen it down as low as it goes. So I'm the only one that uses it now. Kids bring me their pencils between instruction and the system works great.But...the pencil sharpener...not so much. It's annoying because the "standard" size doesn't fit 99% of pencils. First of all, I also have aFujitsu ScanSnap S1500 Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for PC, and I will be comparing this Canon with my experience with the Fujitsu.Both scanners have a nice small footprint and can scan a variety of paper sizes (although not large), including business cards. Both scanners do a very fast job at scanning the documents (duplex, in one pass - woohoo!).What does separate these scanners from each other is the software. The Fujitsu comes with its own snapscan software coupled with Adobe Acrobat (standard version). This allows for a pretty standard setup with a large range of compatibility and support. The Canon comes with a 3rd party suite of software from Nuance. The pdf pro software is good and also has a wide range of options, maybe even more than the Adobe software. However, the Fujitsu snapscan software is just more user friendly and seems much easier to use. I have an easier time getting documents into and organized with the SnapScan software than I did with Canon's software. Again not a severe difference, but a little easier for sure ....Overall, both scanners are very, very capable, but the software really seems to be the defining difference. Either of these scanners can do a great job of digitizing your life, and do it with accurate OCR software at incredible speeds. Both scanners can handle roughly the same capacity and page sizes. I have not "raced" them both side by side, but both scan at incredible speeds and create great looking images.Again, the main difference is the software that comes with it. Both are very capable, but the SnapScan just seems a little easier to use, with a little more polished integration.Bottom line: if you can get both at the same price, I might go with the Fujitsu, but if you can get the Canon at 50 bucks or more off, go that route. Either way, you will have a very good scanner to help you digitize your life and toss your file cabinets. Not to mention the ease of sharing documents with others and being able to find documents with a simple text search. Once you have the experience of finding a document that you need that way - you will never want to go back. These scanners are simply awesome and the Canon delivers alongside the Fujitsu.** One of the comments listed on this review pointed out a very good issue: Unlike the Fujitsu, (which has a scanner and software made separately for mac and pc) the Canon has software that can work with PC and MAC at the same time. So if you have a "mixed" environment, then the Canon may win on this fact. That is a huge bonus .... Thanks!

I have had a couple of different HP Officejet printers, one of which I got on sale for a little under 500. That is the only other printer of this type I have to compare the Epson to. They all worked well: scanned fast, printed quickly and evenly, sent and received faxes. The Epson 630 does these things at least as well, possibly a little better, and the price even when not on sale is only 149.What I liked best about the Epson is the size and weight and overall sleekness of the printer. It has a small footprint so it fits well on my desk. It is light enough that I can just snatch it up and move it forward, backward or over to another table. It, like my much larger, heavier HPs prints on paper up to 81/2 x 14 inches. The printer came with full cartridges of ink - all of them - unlike the usual trial size that accompanies a new printer.What I didn't like about it was that neither I nor a second user of the printer could ever get it to load and operate as a wireless unit, which was to me the most attractive feature of the Epson 630. We both have new laptops with Windows 7 and we share a network, so it could be something with our internet? I doubt it, though. We must now take the time and headache of seeking assistance with the problem. Another problem I can't find an answer to is that when I used an inkjet printer transfer paper in the printer, it printed with white stripes instead of solid. It was only on this type of paper that it did this.Other than those small issues, I like the printer just fine, and I can't imagine how they produced it for this price.

I have to agree with other reviewers who find the Lamy Vista (or Safari - they have the same nib and feed)to be one of the most reliable, smooth, crisp, fine pens out there.  Additionally, the Lamy uses an ABS plastic that is very durable - stays shinny even if thrown in with other pens.  What I really love about these pens (I have four) is that they are so incredibly smooth on most any paper - from low-end Staples/Walmart notebooks/paper to Moleskin/Clairefontaine or Rhodia.  What I find frustrating is the nib - there is significant variation in the nib production such that an extra-fine can be anything from that to a fine or medium.  The good news is that the nibs are readily replaceable and available - so I buy additional extra-fine nibs (since I like a fine line) just to find the really good ones (extra nibs cost about $10).  If you are considering between a Vista vs a Lamy 2000 - I suggest you save your money and get the Safari - the 2000 is a piston filler meaning it holds more ink and is easier to fill but its not as consistent with its writing as the Vista in my experience.  I like fountain pens but don't like having to fuss with them when I'm writing and I find the Lamy pens to me most reliable and trouble free.

I find this stand to be surprisingly functional, stylish, and well constructed.The stand works by placing the laptop on the sloped surface. I found that it fit even my small 12.5" ultrabook. Note that the device is strictly for use on a desktop, since the stand has support only on the front and rear - I do not recommend it for use on the lap.Pro:+ It is nice to look at. The design is sweeping, with no sharp corners. When not in use the main bottom plate is a transparent smoke color.+ When the laptop is in place, I found that I could actually type very well. I find this a bit surprising, because I generally keep my keyboards flat or only slightly  tilted. I think this one has about a 10% slope. How well this will work out over the long term is another question - the wrists are bent upwards. But it seemed fine to me. You will want to have your chair height such that the forearms are level with the table for the device to work well. I think that this device might be useful for someone with a laptop on their desk; switch off using it and not using it periodically to make the wrists have different positions during the day. I'm not sure I'd want to use it all day.+ The laptop screen is at a better height for viewing when it is on this stand. I found that the added height was easier on my neck than looking down.+ It is plastic, but at least it is thick plastic. It seems sturdy.Con:- The device is advertised as keeping the laptop cool, but the bottom plate that holds the laptop has no vent holes. The laptop is actually kept off of the bottom plate, but there is only a thin amount of air space between the laptop bottom and the holder. I think some air holes would have been useful.- When using the laptop, if yours is thin you may find yourself having to rest your wrists on the two plastic pieces of the bottom plate that are nearest to you. These keep the laptop in place, but they extend above my thin laptop, and they are right where my hands will go. I have suspicions that the device may not be that comfortable to use over a long period. So if you have a thicker laptop (about 1 inch thick on the bottom) it may work OK, but for thin ones it may not be advisable.Summary: This is a useful device for periodic use at work as an alternate position for the wrists when typing on a laptop. Recommended.
