I use this machine to organize my office papers, customer reports, tax reports, etc into attractive notebooks that are easier to store or mail.  So far it's been a dream to own.After adding up the cost of purchasing comb bound notebooks printed at Staples and OfficeMax, it just made sense to buy the machine and do it myself.  100 pages bound in a notebook costs over $50 each from these stores.  For less than the price of 2 books, I can own the binding machine, purchase a 100 pack of combs (Fellowes Plastic Comb Bindings, 0.5 Inch, Black, 90-Sheet Capacity, 100 per Pack (52326)orFellowes Plastic Comb Bindings, 1 Inch, 200-Sheet Capacity, Black, 10 per Pack (52383)orFellowes Plastic Comb Bindings, 0.5 Inch, Black, 90-Sheet Capacity, 100 per Pack (52326)), and a 500 sheet ream of paper.  Two notebooks from these stores and I've already spent more than the machine?!?!This Pulsar Plus 150 is a well made machine.  The punching handle extends over the entire machine.  I can punch paper from any location around the unit.  The punching is smooth and doesn't require much muscle at all.  Just follow the instructions: insert the sheets of paper to punch the holes (up to 10-12 sheets), then insert the comb plastic and all the sheets you wish to bind (up to 150).  This is all very quick and easy.  I could print and bind my notebooks in less time that it would take me to drive to Staples to pick up my order.In my work, I need to make my workbooks and presentations look professional.  I have been usingFellowes Transparent PVC Binding Covers, Letter, 100 pack (52089).  These covers can be punched with the Pulsar and bound with the combs.  I found the placing the plastic cover in the middle of a stack of 6 sheets of paper gives me the best punch through.  Punching the PVC sheet alone sometimes creates wrinkles in the PVC.  In the notebooks, I use 1 Transparent Cover on the front and a thicker black (or colored) sheet of art paper for the back cover.
I don't have any problems with them. And they stick well, no peeling or curling. They work well. Very happy.

I just now printed out a test copy and WOW!  what a beautiful copy!  I've got four other printers that I use (3 Epsons and 1 HP) and this printer's printing is fantastic. I will try later to connect it wirelessly but for now I didn't want to deal with any hassles, just in case it wouldn't connect, which seems to be my bane with printers lately.I'm only giving it 4 stars right now since I want to test it out further, but when I saw the brilliant colors of the test copy I knew this printer was something I've always wanted. If you have a small office, or need to do higher quality printing but not reams and reams of it, then this printer might work out nicely.  I have a home business (I teach classical guitar) but I don't need to do a lot of high-quality printing.  I do like to print out a LOT of music, but the Epsons are fine for that.  I really mean that the test copy was fantastic.  I'm sitting here looking at it and feeling it....I just used plain printer paper (the cheapest I could find at Wallmart) and the test copy has a slight glossy feel and sheen to it.  I occasionally will print out flyers and have them professionally printed, but this time I will print them out using this printer.Also, it was extremely easy to set up.  I used the directions that are pictures only and was able to complete the installation process in about 15 minutes or less.  I really like that part being so easy.UPDATE: 11.21.12Just read a comment sent to me by Samsung saying that this printer does NOT have wireless capability.  That's fine if you don't need to place it somewhere away from a computer, but if you need to have a central location for other people to have easy access, then I don't think this would work out very well.  It works out fine for me since I keep it right next to my PC and have it connected to a USB port in the back.

Envy 4500 is # 4 in Amazon electronics which says a lot for its performance. Geek Roger Meyer has tested and reviewed Envy. Here is his report:The HP Envy 4500 has a very appropriate name (Envy).  Other printer manufacturers should be envious of this printer.  I would like to think I am being objective, but there are so many great things about this printer, this review may seem to be biased.  It looks good, works as advertised, is feature rich, and the user manual (on line and downloadable) is one of the best I've read.The printer is elegant in appearance and has an LCD interface that is easy to read and operate.  The menu items are easy to understand and are intuitive.  There is an auto-off function that powers down the printer after a preselected time that is supposed to aid in saving ink by parking the print heads.  All the functions, print, copy, and scan, were tested and worked flawlessly.  Print times were quick and the quality was excellent.  The same can be said of the copy and scan functions.One of the things I liked most about this printer was the ease of setup.  With a history of laborious hardware and software installations that involved extensive interactive dialogs, I was impressed with the simplicity of this setup - even the wireless functions.  It was painless, and everything worked as advertised upon completion.  I especially love the ePrint capability.  With the free HP ePrint app downloaded onto my Android phone, I was able to print directly to the printer through my home WiFi network.  Also, since the desktop PC I was using had wireless connectivity to my network, I could print wirelessly to the printer.  One less cable to clutter up the desktop!  The printer can be connected to a PC via USB cable also (not supplied).I find it difficult to find any big negatives.  It does have a larger footprint than some other compact all-in-ones.  The ejected paper holder slides out of the paper tray "pocket knife" fashion.  The little flip up paper stop seems a little flimsy, but during the evaluation, I did kept it closed and let the paper eject onto the desktop.For the price (less that $100 at Amazon) this printer can't be beat.  It looks good, has great features, works well, and is built by a company with a long history of quality printer manufacturing.--Roger MeyerLife is not about how fast you run or how high you climb but how well you bounce.

I love love love myFujitsu ScanSnap, so I was interested to see how well a device that retails for 1/3 less would stack up against it.  In short, the scanning hardware seems pretty comparable, but the software and Mac support suffers in the comparison.Both the ScanSnap and this WorkForce will quickly devour documents that you feed it.  With the Fujitsu, turning a paper document to a text-searchable PDF is nearly instantaneous (in Mac OSX on a recent iMac), and can be done with a single press of the button on the scanner.  With the WorkForce, the software titles (Epson Scan and Document Capture Pro) are clunky, slow, feel hopelessly out-of-date, and it's difficult to find where the PDF option is (not in Epson Scan), let alone the slow-as-molasses OCR.  I can't speak to the experience in a Windows environment, but for a Mac user, the extra money would be well spent to get access to the Fujitsu's much better software environment.  Should there be third-party software available that could benefit from the rugged hardware (I don't have Acrobat Pro, so I can't speak to this), then this might be a great deal.  Otherwise, three stars for Mac users.

WHAT A GREAT IDEA!!!!Treads have "100% Nylon Non-skid Latex Backing" but I just didn't want to take a chance to fall down from the stairs with these treads...  Anyway, this tape made everything so perfect.It sticks to the back of the treads so well that I think they should sell it with the treads as a "set" deal.Now I don't have to worry about treads moving off the wood stairs, it made me feel much safer.  I originally thought it was a little pricey, but this comes in good length (still have some left over) and after using it, I can say it's totally worth it.  Very happy about my purchase!

I really like my new calculator,I have big clumsy man hands and the keys are perfect for me.This is a really well built calculator that I'm going to be using for balancing my checkbook.My aging eyes have no problem reading the numbers on the display and my lumbering fingers find the keys just right,big enough to tap out my numbers without making this a huge calculator.I've been through several calculators and I really like this one,it feels good in my hands or on the desktop and it's easy on my eyes.Oh!  I forgot to mention price,It's a winner and a heck of a good deal at this low price.

These are really cute,  and I like that they are recycled material and soy ink. However they can only be used once really,  because you have to write directly on the tab.One of the included dividers is a dark color so its hard to see what's written on it.  There are definitely more affordable,  and more practical options out there ( at least for me anyway).

I waited for the e-print functionality to be enabled before writing this review.All in all, it's an OK printer for the price point.Text prints clear and sharp, and it didn't have poor alignment when printing in draft mode.  Unlike my all in one HP 6500 printer.  The system aligns itself with a scan of a printed page, which was kind of cool. The photos print out fairly sharp, though the ink usage will likely cause you to spend about 40 cents per print.  I would go with a store that can do it for 10 cents a print unless it is an emergency.Eprint works well for text.  I just send an email with an attachment like Word or PDF to my printer and it prints. Eprint doesn't work for photos as you can only load one type of paper in the tray.  Most of us will set it for normal printing anyways, so it's more annoying than necessary.The negatives of this printer are numerous.  There are only four input buttons, which cost me to 15 minutes to change the setting for wireless.  The advertised 1 watt drain in off mode doesn't really apply because the printer has to be on at all times for wireless print.  The photo software was horrible.  I couldn't get a decent photo print after the first round, and I consider myself a techie.My advice- this is a decent printer if you just want to print/ scan/ copy.  If you need a good photo printer, I'd invest a little more.  If you need fax or double sided printing, the same applies- invest more for a better printer.

There are those who don't mind spending a lot of money on pens and those who think the first kind are crazy when you can get boxes of Bics for the price of one of these.  To each his own; if you're in the latter category, these pens are not for you.  If you're in the former, they just might be.I'm a big fan of these sort of pens--I love the smoothness, the fact that they constantly and consistently dispense ink, and that the colors stand out easily, an important aspect since I use them for grading. I also like the sharpness of them as I'm often forced to write small on student papers.These pens do an excellent job in all those categories. Smooth, constant, consistent delivery of ink, silky smooth movement across paper, standout colors.  I also like the way the pen cap clicks on very securely and noticeably, which sounds like a minor point but as I often grade on our spare bed and am constantly putting the pen down, it's nice to know the ink won't be bleeding into the sheets.  These and the Pilot Precise extra fine rolling ball are my two favorite grading pens.If you don't mind the price, highly recommended

I bought several of these in Germany before they came to the states. I was impressed by how well they hold up and the smoothness of the roller ball and ink. I think this is a great product made of recycled plastic bottles. The pen also has a similar plastic bottle look. It's just an all around cool pen. I have only used the black pens, but I imagine that the other colors they offer work just as good.

This is a great stapler for those heavy duty jobs, even though it is really big and clunky and a bit funny looking.  It is easier to use since the big handle takes some of the pressure off the person using the stapler by giving some leverage.  My only complaint is that I had a couple of different types of staples at my office, none of which worked with this stapler.  You have to buy special staples specifically, and it doesn't even come with one starter strip.  To me, it seems like a good business decision, if you're stapler is great, to send it out with one row of staples so the buyer immediately finds out it works like a dream and then goes out to buy the staples, instead of just being annoyed right off the bat.

I just got the 420 up and running from an Inspiron 1520 with XP3.The driver software installed with no problems, the toolbox did not.The computer hung up on the toolbox which you don't need anyway, soI uninstalled it.I have noticed over the years, that this happens a lot with this extra fluff theseprinter, hard drive, disk drive, Etc., Etc. manufacturers throw in, just to makeyour life a little more miserable.They actually think they are doing you a favor, when in reality they are just P...ingyou off.I can remember when black and white lasers were going for close to a grand; boy have things changed!The machine is fast, and I can reduce and enlarge as I see fit.Great machine for $70.00

I am having new floors put in my downstairs, and that means that the whole two walls lined with books in bookcases must be removed, stored, and then brought back in and put back on the shelves. I'll be glad when the new floors are done and we can sit back and relax, but meanwhile, it's a lot of work.These boxes were easy for me to load, and the handles, along with the sturdy construction, make it easy for the stronger folk here to move them out of the living room and into storage. I have no doubt they will be intact once they are brought back in to be unloaded.I am usually flexible about delivery dates, but for this, we are on a strict time line. Two other types of boxes I ordered are LATE, and that is really irritating. It means we will really have to hustle--and do a lot in a couple of days rather than piecing the job out more comfortably--than if they had gotten here in a timely manner like these did.The fifth star is missing because the price seems high for what are, after all, just a dozen cardboard boxes.

When I picked up this laminator, I thought, "Why would we need this thing?" Well, I soon discovered that this was really a useful tool to have around the house. I have since used it for many laminating projects, including school projects and office projects as well. We have used this for laminating larger items such as charts, and smaller items, such a labeling storage bins. It is ready to use pretty quickly, and is only takes seconds to laminate your item. Great product.

This is a decent stapler as are most made by Swingline.  No staples at all come with it but the standard staples required are easy enough to find.  The sparkly stickers were a little tough for me to put on in an attractive manner though no one has ever accused me of being overly "arts and crafty" and um I really don't see the need for them.  This might be a nice gift for a tween aged girl at its current on sale price on Amazon of $6.73. It is not worth the full price of $14.99 as it is simply an ordinary serviceable stapler with a few glittery stickers that you could buy more cheaply at a hobby shop if you are really intent on adorning your office supplies.

I love the color and the idea of this product, but it is actually pretty hard to use because the plastic is so stiff that it makes it hard to open it and keep it open with one hand while putting papers in or taking papers out. I can appreciate why traditionally this sort of product was made of heavy accordioned paper which is more pliable. If it were easier to get stuff in and out it would be an easy 5 star winner, but as it is, I think 3 is fair.

For the simple quality of being square this label seems, automatically, more elegant.The 2" x 2" size is perfect for printing an attractive label that includes an ornament (or logo) and a few lines of text in a comfortable-sized font. I see that there is a slightly smaller size, but I'm very happy with this particular size and format.Note that the labels are square, with square not rounded corners. Rounded corners would have been nice, too. They are white but, since they print edge-to-edge you could color them. They do take ink well and dry fast. You can start applying them almost as soon as they come out of the printer.I was on the committee for an alumni dinner gala at my son's old school. We used it on the clear party favor bags we had for the ladies to take home after the gala dinner. We were able to print the school logo (which is a long coat-of-arms type design) plus 2 lines of 24 point text in the school colors and still allow for an uncrowded placement. The same label was used in some shopping bags that contained prizes and they "dressed up" the wrapping very well. We also used it on the displays at the silent auction tables to indicate the name of the donor and the starting bid. Someone suggested that it could have been used as name tags for the people in charge of the auction and raffle tickets.Since we wanted to print in color, we used the inkjet printers, but I notice that they could have been run in a laser printer as well, which is good to know.I love the size and shape. I love that they are easy to remove from the backing, that the adhesive works well, that the corners lie flat, and that they feed into the printer smoothly and without jamming.My only wish is that they were slightly glossy (or less flat). A little gloss effect would have made them just a little more dressy and they would have soaked up less ink. (And taken longer to dry, I realize).However, this little objection isn't going to keep me from getting them again next time; it isn't going to keep the school from stocking them for other events; and it isn't going to keep me from using the remainders to make my own custom Christmas gift tags this year.

Other than during the month of December, I seldom need and use a packaging tape dispenser such as this one. It is certainly an improvement over others (including other Scotch products) but it seems ludicrous to pay $9.99 to Amazon for a single-roller version when, for the same price, a three-roller can be purchased at Costco, Sam's Club, and Walmart*. So I charged the product one Star. That said, it seems sturdy, easy-to-use, and will be especially appreciated in about seven months.

An adequate all-in-one, but with not-so-great print quality.  Like most large inkjets, the printer rocks/vibrates a lot, especially on a lightweight table, and is noisier/slower the color lasers I've used-- this isn't unique to this HP, but is still an annoyance.  Replacement ink is surprisingly expensive especially if you're used to the cost of toner.  None of this unit's functions (I didn't test fax) are particularly exciting, though they are all "adequate".I've owned and liked my HP monochrome printers, color lasers, and photo printers, although their software has been problematic (in OS support and reliability), the product quality has been high.  It may be that the jack-of-all-trades "multifunction" is more challenging to get right.  Not recommended.

Mead Early Learning Idea builders claims to be the building blocks for writing success.I'll be honest, I like the idea behind it. It definitely has lots of exercises to get the kids creative juices flowing and moving. There are pages and pages of ideas to stimulate the idea flow, but it's not something that a first grader can sit down and knock out in a day. Unlike the math workbook that my son did very well and pretty much ran right through, the idea builder took much longer, averaging about a page a day not to burn out.It only dedicated one page each to capital and lowercase letters, which for a 2nd grader, and even a first grader might be appropriate (a kindergartner would need more I think) given how long it took us to go through it, a few more pages like these inter woven in the book would have been a good idea.Overall this is a great workbook for getting ideas flowing and letting them use their words that they learn in school. It is not intended to teach new words, but the phrases are mostly (a couple of exceptions I thought) good starter sentences to allow the child to think about what they want to say and use the vocabulary that they do have.Unlike the math book in this series, this book was definitely out of the reach of my pre-k student. I think that a second grader would have fared better than my 1st grader, but it was still a nice, occasional break. The price is right and I like hearing some of the things that he came up with, so overall I would definitely say that I like it. I'm just not sure that I love it quite enough for the full 5 stars.

Easy to put together. Better directions than Ikea Directions. Has a lift for computer tower. Didn't use. Also has a try for keyboard. Being that I am long legged I did not use that either. I prefer my keyboards on the desk any way.

This printer is great. This was my first foray into a wifi printer, and the cable management has been fantastic. Both my girlfriend and I can print from pretty much anywhere easily, or by USB, and yes, I've used the scanner (which is a pain to use via the limited dial functions)Aside from the clunky onboard software, the printer is also an ink hog. My older canon printers used ink sparingly, which I loved. However, third party inks have done me well. I'm worried because the printer is currently in storage, so the ink tanks might leak from disuse. Will update further when I take it back out of storage.I have not had any printer jams, and have been able to feed a variety of paper through the multiple trays (of which I print from several regularly). The printer has it all, and is compact (paper feeds into the bottom tray, older printers used to have the tray sticking out, how times have changed!)This model is relatively simple, there are much more complex ones out there that you can look into. But I do quite a lot of printing work, and I can tell you that this one is more than adequate to suit my needs.
nice bold colorful push pins that are versatile,can even hang small pictures with them I use them in school art shows.

The Lucia Ink Canon makes for it's Pro Pixma printers is outstanding, the fine art prints I can produce on my Pro9500 MKII printer are no short of stunning. For whatever reason, the Gray cartridge empties quickest of most so buying extra of these along with the full 10-cartridge ink pack is not uncommon. It's 5-star ink that can never get 5 stars because of the PRICE. If you do the math on these 17ml cartridges you'll discover that inkjet ink costs $3100 per gallon. I suppose I can't complain at the pump any more! Anyway, it's an industry thing, there are products that can and will be a good profit margin. I will say, however, that the research into getting excellent ink can't be cheap. Third party inks don't come nearly as close in quality or accurate color reproduction, so I will still buy the real thing (I've argued with enough third-party ink and carts in my life, lol). I just wouldn't mind if the cartridges were more like $8-9, especially in the cartridge packs.

I have a great holder for these pop up post it notes and it's fun to load with matching pink notes. I wish the pale pink were a bit more bright, but they are still pink so thats good. Practical and pretty.

I have four older Mead spiral notebooks, two wide ruled, and two college ruled, and I have to say that the quality of the paper has remained high. The paper on the older ones, as well as the new ones, is smooth and easy to write on. Unfortunately, as other reviewers have noted, the back cover is not as thick as it used to be, so when the pages are turned all the way around, it flops around when it's held. I understand that times have changed, and costs have to be cut, but this change lowers the utility and quality of this notebook. As soon as I looked at these notebooks, I noticed that the horizontal lines aren't very dark making it difficult to take notes in lower light. I compared the new notebooks to the older notebooks, and, indeed, the lines aren't as dark. I checked all four of the notebooks I received thinking it might be a printing error, but it's the same for all of them.Mead has always been my go to for quality notebooks. With the changes they've made, I think I'll be looking around for something else.

Simply my favorite pen. It's something about the way it rests in my grip. Makes my writing look better since the pen glides on the paper instead of dragging. And you can turn this model into a $200 Montblanc if you want to. This accepts the Montblanc rollerball refills. Try it!

This is not one of my favorite printers. The setup is lengthy, tedious and not intuitive. The instructions are seriously lacking. The printer starts with English checked (shows this on the touch screen) but none of the keys will work and all report as invalid operation. Even though English is checked, you still have to activate it through the touch screen to get to the rest of the setup and I could not find this anywhere in the instructions.The print cartridges are the easiest loading of any printer I have tested but it takes 10 minutes for the printer to ready them for printing.  The printer will not install without using the Epson CD. The software also tried to install programs that were unrelated to the printer that tried to access the internet but my firewall blocked and reported this. One of the programs was the Epson Customer Participation Program, I guess Epson expects you to participate whether you want to or not.  The printer was connected via my ethernet and should only needed to go to the internet for the latest update.Another issue is that you cannot load photo paper in the main paper tray. You have to load it at the back of the printer. I have never seen a printer before that had this odd requirement. Color photo print quality was good but not as fast as expected, it also was darker than expected. My less expensive Brother printer seems to print as fast and as good and costs 1/3 of what this printer costs. This Epson is also a very large printer.Another issue just found and that changed my previous review of 3 stars to 2 stars is that sometimes it prints crookedly. Apparently it must draw the paper in at a slight angle but I checked the paper tray and set exactly for letter size. I cannot recall any other printer that had this problem.Considering the claims made for this printer, I expected a lot more. I think here is another case where when the hype meets reality there is a serious mismatch. On the plus side though, it has USB, WiFi and Ethernet. Overall I would not recommend this printer unless you absolutely require some of the features and can live with the idiosyncrasies. If you are just looking for a good quality printer, I have found the Brother line of printers to be excellent.

This Epson LabelWorks is not only a lot of fun, but it is very practical. The well-designed and well-made plastic case leads you to a keyboard operated iron on label maker and two rolls of labels. Batteries are not included, though (I still can't figure why some products do not include batteries. Is the profit margin so low that the manufacturer cannot afford to include them?). No matter. This label maker has dozens of uses. I'm using mine to personalize some of my shirts and jackets. I'll make labels for my (first) great grandson (soon)! There is a nice selection of type fonts and numerous 'dingbats'. The styles let you customize the label to suit the intended person. There are two rolls of labels included... black on white and black on blue. It would have been nice if one of the label cartridges had been black on clear but I have a roll on order now. I really like my new iron on label maker and I feel sure that you will, too! It's well worth the price.

It's too bad that Canon doesn't make this printer any more. The color match with my monitor is great. It is easy on ink, too. I print a lot of photos and have been surprised at the quality and that I don't have to replace the ink cartridges often.

Just installed the wireless driver on 4 different computers running MacOSX and XP, Windows 7, some running BootCamp. Everything worked great - noticed that the Windows installs needed a hard connection via USB for setup when installing Wifi.Printer is made in Malaysia and comes with USB cable (a bit short) and a power cord (not brick). Especially liked that the paper tray is large and the height is short for my setup.

I moved four years ago and expect another move soon.  The quality of these boxes are similar to the Duck brand that I used for my last move.  They served me well and I don't expect these to be much different.  There are no large boxes, so you are limited to what you can fit in these boxes, but they are a great size for many things you may find on shelves or in drawers.  And having 14 boxes total means you can pack a good amount of items.  For my next move, all I am going to need is a few larger boxes in addition to these boxes and not much more.The tape that is included in this set is sort of thin and not too strong.  But it should be fine for the size and weight of these boxes when they are full.  There is no tape dispenser, which would have cost very little to include a simple one like what comes with 3M tape.The bubble wrap is a nice inclusion, but there isn't a whole lot of it.  I expect that I will need more.  The marker is also a nice inclusion and a necessity.  I usually write the name of the room that the box will go to so the movers know where to bring it, and I put a number on each and I keep a list of what is in each box so I can easily find what I need after the move.For around $40, you are getting a nice set of clean, new boxes... which beats having to ask your local stores for their used, dirty boxes.
We needed a new 2 line phone for my office and this one is just what we needed..wow!  Looks good, works well, etc...recommended...

Actually, it's not. Leather fetishists, maybe. This thing just isn't spiky enough or able to do any kind of lasting damage to be in a sadomasochist's kit. But if you're looking for a thoughtfully designed and very comfortable wrist rest for use with your laptop, computer, etc., you'd be hard pressed to find a better suited and better crafted product. What I like most about this is that it is well made and doesn't feel like it's going to fall apart anytime soon. The leatherette is very soft and the pad itself is very comfortable the moment you put it to use. I'm looking forward to chucking my old wrist rest, the one with the fabric cover that's torn from the base exposing the rather nasty looking and feeling gel inside. This product is quality and an easy recommendation as opposed to my old one, which feels like a rotted length of sausage that has started to take on a life of it's own.

I have had trouble with this printer since I received it  11/16/11.  First I couldn't get it to print in color than the  ink ran out in after about 3 weeks.  it was the ink that was in the box with the printer.  I purchased new ink and since it isn't Canon ink it doesn't print everything or it  says I am low or out of ink and they are new cartridge.  I did call customer service in Dec. about about the color (which was their ink) and they couldn't  help.  I got new ink.  the  printer  only prints sometime and says  it is low in ink or there is no ink.  I called again and they  said they couldn't  help this time because I wasn't their ink.  I told them I even had trouble with their ink too but since it was over  15 days they couldn't  or wouldn't help me help me.  I  DON'T  recommend this printer or company too anyone.

These storage boxes are the perfect size and they go together easily and without having to use tape.  When filled they are still light enough to move easily and they can be stacked and not fall apart.

I've loved the multi-color pen option since high school and college for detailed note-taking.  I still use these pens for taking notes and `highlighting" or underlining different parts with different colors.  This `new' version works as well as the old, but in a sleeker more compact and thus more comfortable to hold version.  I really appreciate the comfort of the `soft grip' barrel.  Additionally, I found this a nice compact option for carrying in my purse for my son to be able to draw detail pictures with a single pen rather than carrying around several colors! I really like the `classic' multi-color function in a new, updated and highly improved style.

I got so tired of looking for a letter opener or using my fingers to rip open an envelope that I decided to look on Amazon to see if I could find an opener that would make my life easier. Well, this is it!!! It shears off the edge of the envelope quickly, evenly, and I have yet to damage any contents in any of the envelopes I've opened. It can be used as a hand-held opener or used when sitting on your desk. The biggest plus is that it's easy to find. It's not huge, measures about 6" x 2", is attractive, and battery installation is quick and easy. I highly recommend this frustration reliever!

There's nothing fancy about this document holder, but it gets the job done. I've got it mounted to my wall now, holding a printed calendar that I plan to swap out each month. It seems secure, though always with these products I don't think the adhesives will hold forever.

As a standard inkjet printer with copy/fax functionality, this hits the mark.  Pages are clear, relatively fast to print, and actually pretty quiet too.  The scanner works well, and the copy function is really simple.  (I couldn't test the fax function, since I don't have a land line phone).Where the trouble starts is in the wireless functionality.  First, while setting it up, I found that it simply would not find my router that was sitting right next to it.  It found all of my neighbors' routers, but not mine.  After numerous attempts at setting it up, I nearly gave up.  In the end, I lifted my router about six inches and tilted it over the printer, and viola, I had connection!  Unfortunately, I have to hold the router just like that in order to maintain the connection.  As long as you set this printer up in a different place from your router (like your neighbor's house, perhaps?) you'll have no problems.  Unfortunately, that isn't an option for me right now.The next issue comes with iPhone/iPad printing.  The box prominently shows printing from iPad and iPhone, but the printer is NOT airprint compatible.  As usual, you need a special app (that doesn't work) in order to print from an iOS device.  This isn't a special feature.  Any printer can do this.  In fact, if you download FingerPrint to your computer, then any printer becomes an airprint printer.  In this case, it is just a printer.

Because of the spring loaded nature of this stapler, you use same effort to push through 2 sheets of pager as you do with 28.  And, since they give you a big lever to work with, that's not much effort at all.It has solid, mostly metal construction.  Works reliably.The only negative comment I can make about this is they didn't include directions on how to load it!  Sounds silly but it's not obvious like other staplers. (other reviews here say how it'd done.  Very easy once you've done it once)When you push the stapler to it's  limits with thicker and thicker stacks of paper the performance gets erratic - but any stapler has a limit.  I was able to reliably punch through 28 sheets of thinnish paper (calendar notepads) and usually staple 16 sheets of thick paper (from large envelopes).It's like a power stapler that you don't have to plug in!

I requested this just to have on hand if I should need it. The day after it arrived, I had occasion to use it, and I'm very pleased with the quality. This is far superior to the cheap little narrow rolls of tape we've been using for many years. I found the "stickability" of this tape to be better than some of the costly, wider packing tape I've used in the past. Of course, this tape is only one inch wide, so you might have to use a little more of it, but I do like it better than the wider stuff. Definitely recommended.

I've got several Epson printers, both at home (Artisan 837, Epson C810) and at the office (Workforce 3520).  I've had great luck with them (other than an annoyance with the workforce that it forgets the date and nags every time it's powered on).  They've been quick, trouble free, and have printed very well for everything I've done.So I was curious about this one, figuring I would replace the WF-3520 in my office with it.First thing was the size of the box - large.  I was surprised.  The shock and awe continued as I unboxed things and got to the ink cartridges.  They are over 5" long, over 2 1/1 inches wide, and just look insanely big compared to the other Epson cartridges I'm used to using.As usual, they have a big advertising sticker across the top. I will never understand why they do that for these things.  You don't need the advertising and bragging in your face - you already PURCHASED it. I wish they would limit that to ones destined specifically for floor models.Opening the ink cartridges requires something sharp - there is no notched spot to just rip.There was an irritating instruction card in the pull down hatch that shows in pictograph format how to go about changing the ink.  But it was loose and slid around, you have to snap it into these little feet that will ultimately hold it into place.The initial setup takes they say about 10 minutes.  In my case it took about five or six.  Normal odd noises and groans as the system primes everything and sets itself up for use.  They warn you in about three or four locations to not interrupt, don't turn off power, don't open the front cover during the process.This printer will replace my Epson WF-3520.  I have limited space on my L shaped desk in my office, since I have to squeeze the printer along one end, tucked behind my SoundFreaq bluetooth speakers.  I was expecting, from the size of the box this came in, for it not to fit.  But it actually fit just fine.  It's taller than my WF-3520, but measurements for front to back and side to side are actually just about the same for both printers.After setting the ink, it prompts you to tell it what kind of paper is in it, and then it's ready.  My immediate disappointment after using an Artisan 837 at home for so long, is the same I had with the other workforce printer I had by Epson - the screen doesn't tilt at all to different angles.  I love that in the "home" models, but the business models I've used so far have all been fixed.  Since I have it sitting on a desk so that the screen ends up nearly at eye angle, that very "up" tilted screen is a bit awkward.Getting on the wireless was simple.  Since I have a combination of numbers and letters in the randomly generated code, usually I have to do things like hit the 1 button a few times to get the small A or the number 1 and such.  The onscreen here is a "normal" keyboard so you can hit a button to change numbers to letters and back to numbers then.  Quick and easy.Oddly, the configuration sheet you can print with the status of everything will tell you the MAC address, but nothing about the IP it received.  You have to go to a different spot to view/print the IP separately.As is my habit, I elected to download the most recent driver from Epson's website.  There is one there listed for Windows 8.1 64 bit.  I downloaded it, and got the error that this app can't run and I need to find the right version.  I tried to redownload it again in case it was a problem with the download, something corrupted, but had the same problem.  I tried to extract it, and I received a bunch of errors that the file was damaged.  So I ended up having to use the CD, and hope the update process works as it checks for new versions down the road, since clearly Epson messed up with their driver download files for this model.  At least the CD install lets you skip their "special offers and links" since I really dislike it when an install utility doesn't let you opt out of their junk.The firmware installed on the unit from the factory is the same build (GM22E4) that's available on the website.  So hopefully the software on the CD is current.  This model is apparently new enough that it's not even listed anywhere for registration or support.  I was actually surprised to find it listed for downloads (although maybe it shouldn't have been as their files are bad and won't work at least on 8.1 x64).The install went as all the Epson routines go, no surprises, found the "already set up on the wireless" printer just fine.My previous Workforce printer had an issue with losing the date and time.  Every time it was turned off, when it was turned back on (without ever losing power, the plug was in 24/7) it would prompt me to reset date and time.  I finally got tired of it and got with support, who troubleshot it for a few minutes with me, and replaced it outright.  That new one worked fine for a week or so, then started doing the exact same thing.  So I hope I don't have similar issues with this one.The registration process after the install hung.  And when I killed it and tried to run it direct from the CD again, it hung again.  Couldn't register it online via their website, couldn't register it with their disc.  I tried a few more times over the course of the next couple hours, and eventually the registration utility on the CD finally didn't hang, and I was at least able to complete the registration.When it was time to print the test page, it nagged me that I'm out of yellow.  Since these are the brand new cartridges, I know I should NOT be.  Removing it and replacing it did nothing to get it to show any ink in it, although the black, magenta, and cyan all showed full.So even before I can start testing printing, I've had several failures and problems.  This is not even remotely acceptable for something at this price point.The software updater found four updates, the firmware (a newer version than the website shows available actually), scanner driver, fax utility, and document capture pro software.  I updated them all, in hopes that it fixes whatever is causing it to think the yellow cartridge is empty. Unfortunately that made no difference.So I thought I'd try scanning, since that won't be impacted by the empty yellow cartridge.  If you hit the scan button on the device, you have option to scan to memory device (i.e. usb stick), cloud, document capture pro, and a computer (WSD).  Since I'll be generally scanning from the Epson Scan software, though, I don't need to do any of those regularly.  The software has an "office mode" or "professional mode", basically the office mode uses the basic options and gives you some choices, the professional mode opens advanced settings, such as specifying that the source document type is reflective, or to use unsharp mask, and backlight correction and such.  It scanned fine for me this way, both when it's placed on the glass and when I use the document feeder.But in a normal client type of office environment, they don't want to scan from thier PC and have to click through things, they would prefer to just dump something on the printer, and select a destination from a list and have it just scan to a preset folder.  But there is nothing that works for me that way on this unit.  Business class printers generally let you specify a network share and authentication to access it, or an SMTP server and authentication so you can scan straight to an email address.  There are no options for that kind of a setup here, it relies on the WSD option in Windows 7, and for me on Windows 8.1 it doesn't work.  The scanner just can't see my computer.  I tried to set up the cloud option since I figured I could at least pull it from the cloud to my comptuer.  I have an epson connect account already due to the three other Epson printers I have at various locations.  The web interface (http://ipaddress) is much more fleshed out to get to advanced settings, and is the only way to register for the epson connect link.  And I actually liked the options there.  I was afraid I'd be limited to just something in the Epson connect network, but the destination options include email, evernote, google drive, BOX, and dropbox.  I would have liked to have seen Skydrive/Onedrive as an option though.  I set up dropbox, email, and google drive.Once that's configured, I actually like the simplicity of the scanning to the cloud.  You select "Scan to Cloud" from the main menu after picking SCAN.  It offers your choices of locations, so I picked Dropbox, and then the screen is dominated by a big PDF button under FORMAT.  Just touch it, and you can easily change to JPG.  That's a nice interface since many of my clients with business class scanners have to go through a few more hoops to change that on the fly.  Right there is also the option to easily change if you're single sided or duplexing two sides per scanned page, the type of document, density, and orientation.  You can also create easily accessed "presets" here as well to have all those various options saved as single click choices to make the changes as you do different document types.  I did a 9 page test with various papers - hand written, typed, some with logos, and scanned them in the auto document feeder.  It scanned and uploaded, and I realized when I looked at Dropbox and saw a PDF with all the blank pages that I didn't put them face up in the feeder.  I tried again and it was fine.  I had PDF, so it scanned all pages and made a single multi page PDF.  Unfortunately I see no way to change this option, since I've had clients who need it all to be a single document, and others who need it to scan each page as an individual file.  Granted, you could feed each one at a time and have individual files for each page, but that isn't practical.  But since most people need the "multiple pages in a single PDF" this is probably the best option to have as the only choice.  If you choose JPG it does put each paper into its own file.Scan to email had the attachment in my Exchange server's inbox within about 10 seconds.  As with the dropbox and google box, JPG scans are individual files per sheet, PDF is all sheets in the one file.Scans are crisp and clear, very accurate to the original, and are named EPSON_ and a string of numbers indicating the time/date stamp.Duplexing worked as advertised, I had no issues with either double sided scanning or double sided printing.I couldn't accurately test photo printing without one of the cartridges unfortunately.  I did put in a support email to Epson asking about it since a new in box system shouldn't have an empty ink cartridge.  They replied inside of about 1.5 hours requesting my address information, saying they will ship me a replacement cartridge.  Meanwhile the rating will be based on the issues I've had that I've never encountered with the other three Epson printers I own, and the fact that a new in box unit ships with either a defective or an empty ink cartridge.  If I get the replacement and it works and I can further test things out I will adjust my review accordingly.  But as of this writing it's 16 days and just before the holiday weekend they verified it hasn't even shipped yet, so we'll see what eventually happens.If it weren't for the setup issues, driver problems on their website, and the bad yellow cartridge they shipped with it, this would've easily earned at least a 4 star rating, but if you're going to have to jump through that many hoops to get something up and running in a business environment, you may as well spent a little more and get something with truer "business class" options such as network share abilities and the rest.But if you're looking for something simple for a small home office, and this is in your price range, it's certainly a nice unit to work with.

I had picked up a different similar sized whiteboard from the Vine program a couple months ago. However, that bulkier frame is part of what makes this one such a better build quality than the other one, so it's ultimately a wash.The magnets came with some horribly tacky glue holding them to the surface of the board, and that stuff was a real pain to get off of both the board and the magnet, but more so the board because of how that residue interferes with the marker. The Epson Expression XP-600 Wireless Small-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner is printer packed with features in one small configuration. Unlike other all-in-ones, the XP-600 is smaller, less than 6 inches high, around 13 inches wide and 15 inches long. The small configuration is perfect for a clutter-free work space. The smaller dimensions of the XP-600 means that it can be placed plainly in a little corner of a room or your work space. The fact that this printer is also wireless means that it can be integrated into your home/office network without bothersome cables to worry about.Further thoughts on the XP-600:Design: The Epson Expression XP-600 Wireless Small-in-One printer is small and compact, can be placed unobtrusively in a little corner of your work space or computer table.Flexibility & Functionality: Though lacking a fax function, the all-in-one printing flexibility of a printer, scanner and copier pretty much covers the basic printing needs a regular consumer would ever need from a printer. The ability to print from flash/memory cards adds to the functionality of this all-in-one printer. A 2.5-inch LCD with a touch-screen panel adds to the functionality of the XP-600. Airprint compatibility and Epson Connect are another big plus on its functionality. You can print wireless from your tablet or smartphone, whether it is by apple or android. You can also now print directly onto a CD or a DVD, giving your burned copies nicer looking labels with your own personal touch to it.Wireless: As more and more home networks adapts and transitions to wireless protocols, the Epson Expression XP-600 Wireless Small-in-One printer meets that demand by having the ability to be configured to function wirelessly. Needless to say, setting this up to work wirelessly with your network is also very easy.Performance:With printing speeds of 12ppm for black or plain documents and a 9 ppm for documents requiring color, the Epson Expression Home XP-600 doesn't belong to the top-notch scale as far as printing speeds are concerned. Nevertheless, unless your task requires you to print numerous copies of paper documents, the XP-600 satisfies the average printing needs. Scanning is also a snap, with a quality rating of up to 2400 dpi, you are assured of the highest resolution this printer can output with its scanner. Photo printing is another noteworthy feature of this printer. Printing a 4 X 6 photo from the XP-600 and the results were very good. Not as sharp as you would get from other high-end larger printers but the results were good enough to satisfy my needs. Plus, Epson inks are known for retaining their details and non-fading.Needless to say, the Epson Expression XP-600 Wireless Small-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner has exceeded my expectations. The compact size packed with great features makes this truly a home-based printer. Highly recommended!

First of all, I have to say I have no idea why several other reviewers have trashed this poor little $8 stapler. It is *not* difficult to load, it's perfectly simple to load (more on that in a minute) and it does *not* fall apart, in fact, it seems beautifully made. Why all the anger aimed at this stapler?I find the stapler very easy to use and it has such a soft touch that the first time I used it I didn't think it had stapled anything--I was surprised to look and see that indeed it had worked. You barely have to rest your hand on this and it staples things together. (You might want to tell teenager boys that before they mash it down too hard.) Compared to my old Swingline staplers (I probably have 10 in my house/office) it takes almost no pressure and for that reason, I would highly recommend this to old folks or people with a hand injury, etc. that might have trouble using a normal stapler.As far as loading, give me a break! It takes all of about three seconds to load this. First, you remove the paper tab that is there only to show you *where* to press at the back of the stapler (and you toss that tab away, it's only packaging). Then you remove a little strip of green tape up front that is, again, just there to secure parts in shipping. To load the stapler you push down the little lever at the back of the stapler and pull out the staple tray up front. Then just drop in the staples, close it and you're done. If someone can't do this in under five seconds they're doing something wrong. Someone had trouble loading this? Really? Kind of makes you wonder about the veracity of some of the reviews.It's a great stapler. It's easy to load and use and it's less than $10. Of course, only time will tell if it's durable, but I've been using for several days and I see no sign that it will have any issues.REVIEW UPDATE: I've now been using this stapler for more than two months and I have to say, everything that I said earlier stands: this is a great, lightweight and durable stapler. I love the ease of using it and even though it sits on a shelf next to my desk with two other staplers, this is the only one that I ever use. And it goes through 10 or more sheets of paper like nothing. Great stapler.
