However, when you compare to other printers in this price range (like the Brother MFCJ825), you realize that the Canon isn't that good a deal - other printers in the $90-$125 price range have fax, document feeder, Ethernet, touch screens and more.But my biggest gripe is just how cheap this thing feels - everything is cheap plastic that flexes all over the place. The paper tray, the paper output tray, the scanner lid - it just all feels too cheap. Also, the lack of an OEM ink option is a downer - a full set of Canon cartridges will run around $75, which is just $24 less than the entire printer cost.B/W quality is good - on decent paper, definitely one of the better producing printers I've seen in a long time. Photos (on premium paper) are just ok - despite all the new technology touted in their ink, things just don't pop as nicely as on an OfficeJet Pro or Epson Artisan.So, as much as I love the print quality from Canon printers, this one is not a winner in my books. It is definitely a decent option for a home printer if you just need an occasional print, but only if it is on sale, I would not invest $100 in this machine - plenty of other options out there that offer cheaper ink and more features.

I use this for my printer at home - I am not writing business letters and don't need high quality paper - just solid paper and it works well for my every day uses (printing out mapquest, children's homework assignments, etc.).  It is standard 8.x x 11 letter size.  This item cost me $16.47 (2500 sheets - can't beat the price), no shipping or handling cost (I love PRIME!) and is delivered to my house very quickly. For basic comupter printer paper, it is a great deal.

I've been using this binder to sort and keep track of receipts for the holidays. Last year I found that my system of throwing them all in an envelope wasn't really working. I really like the bright color of this binder as it makes it easy to keep track of and lets me have a little fun with decorating it. The rings come apart easy enough, but also snap firmly together so that you won't worry about losing anything. Additionally the binder cover and back are nicely constructed and should stand up well over the years with average use.

I use these every time I need to mail something. Most shipping websites default to this size of label. Some of them use the other half of the sheet as a packing slip, which can feel a little wasteful to also print on label paper.

Fine point BRIGHT markers!The uses are endless.  I've been using them to mark labels that I need to see right away. Other family members use them onbirthday cards, coloring, etc.I like the "chisel" type tip as  you can use it to write fine, or sideways large.When using a marker, it seems to dry quickly, thus it does not come on the side of your hand.The month I've had them, there have been to leaking or smudging.  Also items I've used them on have not faded or had the color run off.Nice markers!!

I don't know how they determined that it prints 14 pages per minute in color... More like 1PPM color... But otherwise it's a fantastic printer. Took about 10 minutes to get it set up, connected to my wired and wireless networks and start printing.

Label makers have sure come a long way from the ones I remember years ago.  I had a great time playing around with this and learning how to use it. I just took a quick glance at the manual that it came with and had no trouble at all figuring out all the features. What I liked the most were the fun borders you can put around your labels, such as making the label into a text bubble, a little scroll like an official announcement, a border with a flower on each side, etc. There is lots of clip art you can add to the labels too, which make them a lot of fun.  There are all different shapes - hearts, thumbs up and down, flowers, you name it and it's probably there.  It was very easy to change the font style and size, and very easy to add numbers and punctuation.  One feature I really love is that you can save your labels in case you want to print the same one over again. There is a little cutting blade on the side of the label maker and all you have to do is push the button and it's cut.  The only problem I had is the layout of the keyboard - it's not like our cellphones are, but in the order of the alphabet.  I had a terrible time typing even the simplest words!  That's really minor though, compared to everything else.  The size of the unit is nice too.  It fits nicely in one hand and will be very easy to store in a drawer.The labels themselves are really nice and sturdy (I'm not sure what material they are, but kind of a light plastic) and very easy to remove from the backing.  The label maker comes with a 10 foot starter cassette, which was super easy to install.  I checked and Amazon has several varieties of labels for this machine and the price is very reasonable.If you need a label maker, I would look no further than this.  I think it would be perfect for either the home or the office.

This is excellent tape, thick and sticky, much better than the conventional tape I buy 6 rolls to a package in bulk. It is easy to find the start, difficult to tear/cut (which is good, scissors/knife work fine), and adheres well. However it isn't so much better that it is worth the current price shown here. I'll use it for specific cases where more strength or time is anticipated (storage in the attic) but continue to use the cheap stuff for routine shipping of light or medium weight items.If you search, you can find some more detail at the website for an orange colored nationwide home improvement chain. They have the same item for about half the price and they have some different detail. Specifically of interest is its ability to work well over a broader range of temperatures and adhere to boxes of varying composition."Premium Packing Tape that features Corru-Grip Adhesive technology, developed specifically for optimal closure of high percent content recycled corrugate. Provides excellent performance, superior adhesion properties, holding force, tensile strength and easy unwind. Perfect for demanding box sealing applications, under or over stuffed boxes, package repair and bundling applications, and packages exposed to more challenging shipping hazards and stress. For extra heavy boxes, up to 70 lbs.Adhesion level  HighIndoor/Outdoor  Indoor/OutdoorUV/sunlight resistant  NoMaximum application temperature (F)  120Minimum application temperature (F)  35Moisture Resistant  NoProduct Width (in.)  1.88Recommended surfaces  General Purpose"I am giving five stars because it does appear to be of high quality and likely to live up to its claims. I'll let you judge if these qualities are worth the extra money for your specific application.

I was intrigued by these hybrid pens; the idea of combining gel and ball-point ink sounded great. I love gel ink pens, but they do tend to smear. The Pilot Acroball pens have some drawbacks, however.The color is bolder and deeper than regular ball-point ink, which I liked. On regular paper everything was great, but when I tried to use the Acroball on a medical document, heavier stock with a shiny finish, the ink didn't want to flow properly. I had to switch back to my regular ball-point. Be warned.Not much else to say; if you like gel ink, need pens only for regular business paper, and want to minimize smearing, these pens are fine. The price seems a bit high to me for the limits of what the Acroball hybrid pens can do. They certainly aren't "fashion forward", as claimed in the description. That's just silly.GRADE: B

Smead has always been the go-to brand for hanging file folders, their quality is top notch and these colored folders are no exception. The bars are made from strong metal that doesnt flex like the cheap ones do, and the paper is thicker and doesnt tear like others do.These are bright and colorful, so it is easy to grab the file you are looking for without having to read the chicken scratch you wrote on the tabs.Recommended for people who want to simplify their file organization without being too drastic.

We used these markers to entertain some teenagers and gradeschoolers, making designs on t-shirts.  We just bought the cheap-o package of t-shirts from the store, and washed and dried them before using.  The kids put cardboard inside the shirts, which made the surface a little sturdier for writing on, and kept the markers from potentially bleeding through to the opposite side of the shirt.They truly enjoyed using the markers, and so far they have stood up to several washings.  As the "stained" part of the name implies, these are permanent, and it took a couple of days to get the color off the hands of the youngest users (who weren't particularly concerned about the marks on their hands...).I'm not sure how long these markers would last, but despite being used by half a dozen kids for a couple of hours, they didn't appear to be running out of ink.  Overall, highly recommended, and I plan on keeping them around for more practical uses (labeling clothing and beach towels, etc.).

For those who want a rather large daily meal planner, with a good quality marker and board, this would be a good buy. It gives you ample space to give a detailed description of what you are planning to have each meal for the day, any ingredients you might have left to buy, and how many calories each part of the meal will be. The marker is good quality, the board itself is a little flimsy but once mounted via two sided tape to a wall or via magnets this is not an issue.On a practical level, I suspect many people would have been happier with a weekly meal planner. Sure you would not have as much room for detail. But having a plan for the week and a reminder of what you need to buy etc. for an entire week would more than make up for most people the space here devoted to one day. I think a review of what you had on a weekly basis would be more powerful feedback than having to erase and start over every day.However this is a DAILY meal planner so I have not knocked it down to 4 on that account. Where it does lose a star is that for the price and for the name 'biggest loser' they should have included a meal book or something else of value. Since they did not, my advice would be to get a white board and marker and customize your own board. Print out headings on a computer and tape them to the board. That way you can have whatever kind of board you would like, a combination of daily/weekly, whatever so as to be the most useful to you.

I viewed the video review on this product before putting it together.  The guy makes it look very easy with his air compressor and it probably is, but it really isn't necessary.  It comes with a pump and it takes much less time than you think to blow it up.  So far I see two problems with it:1) I don't know the weight limit.  I am overweight and it makes me very nervous.  There is sufficient air in the ball but it sinks in a lot when I sit on it.  (2) My back hurts a bit when I get up.  Because of my slipped disks, the motion that you use to stabalize yourself on the ball seems to aggravate the spine. If your spine is healthy then I imagine that this is wonderful, but if yours is already messed up like mine then it may be a little painful. I got this ball because I used to love those 'kneeling' chairs, where you're forced to sit up straight with support for your knees and your bottom.  I thought this would be the same kind of sitting experience, but it really isn't.

This package is made up of 8 Colored Ink Pens: black, blue, red, purple, green, turquoise, orange, and magenta.  All eight colors have ink that perfectly matches the pen's plastic casing, all of the colors are bright and vibrant and easy to see on white paper.The ink flows smoothly from the pen with no globs or smears. Approximately one quarter of the pen (towards the bottom) is coated in a textured rubber that makes writing comfortable and easy.Will purchase these for home, school, and work.

Got these to pack dishes for a move.  They are extremely light and mail in the bag like the image.  We ended up using only around 1/3 of the whole bag and the rest is just chilling in the garage.  Still a great value and highly recommended to protect your stuff.

This is a very nice four pack of pens. They are light weight, write very smoothy and efortlessly as the description says. I don't get a hand cramp when writing as I do with some other brands of pens if I am writing for more than a few minutes. My favorite part about this pack is that is has four different colors. I like to use different colored pens depending on what I am writing (grocery list, to-do list, letters, and official paperwork). I will buy these pens again!

This mouse pad with gel rest was necessary for me because I spend many hours at a time on the computer. I normally would have to take several breaks when my wrist would get sore. My wrist used to hurt so bad that I had to massage it for 10 minutes to get the feeling back. I'm 26 now, but I shouldn't have these issues and I no longer do thanks to this mouse pad.I like the non-sliding. My old mouse pad would constantly move which was annoying, but this mouse pad stays in place. If you are a person who is on the computer for several hours at a time, you'll appreciate this. The hand/wrist position may take some getting used to, but it's worth it. I recommend that you buy this mouse pad. It comes in a few designs which is a plus. Not a lot, but a few. Just search for "3m mouse pad with gel wrist rest" to browse through their collection.

These dividers are exactly what I wanted. They are thick, sturdy, and durable, and I expect they will last a while. The colors are muted but still attractive. It's easy to print the labels--though I actually prefer using my label maker to stick labels right on the tabs. The dividers are extra-wide, too, which means I can see the whole divider label even when the binder is full of papers. Overall, I am really happy with these!
OEM in original packaging, plugged in and it works, what more can i say? This is just what I needed.

I run a small business through my home and print off about 75 invoices per month plus minor everyday printing.  My total for the month is about 100 prints for this printer, an Epson Workforce 840.  I just looked at my last order for this cartridge and it was January of 2012.  It is January 2013 and my printer is not completely out, just low and I wanted make sure I had a cartridge on hand when it did run out.  The cartridge that came with the printer lasted for 5-6 months.  I was very happy with that length given the ink vampire printer I had prior to the Workforce.  A year in between refills is awesome.Edit:  December 2013 and I am running low on ink and ordering another.  Again this cartridge lasted about a year with the same work load as the year before.
Avery makes great quality office/home products.  These are no exception.  Good 'thickness' which means durability for years to come in my scrapbooks that I am working on. Buy them!

I sent a few packages with these labels, and from reports from the recipients, the labels arrived intact and did not easily lift from the packaging. Having the labels in a pad format is nice because the single labels won't get scattered or lost, but labels are not really the sort of things I would carry around in the first place, so the point was somewhat lost on me. Still, no complaints, so 4 stars!

A problem I've always had with Scotch packing tape is that it is not sticky as the bargain brand tapes.  That issue is mostly overcome because it is thicker than the bargain brands so you don't need to go over everything twice to ensure a hold.  The scotch tape comes off the roll near silently which is nice, yes, but for how little packing tape I use I don't really need to be silent every time.  The BEST thing about this compared to the bargain brands is the dispenser.  It has the "sure start" which is great, but so do most tapes.  The thing that sets this apart is that the dispenser is designed so that the tape will not "fall back" onto the roll after you've started the roll.  With most tapes if you're not careful the tape will roll back onto the roll and you'll spend 10 minutes getting it started next time you use the tape.  So overall, yes this is great tape, but I'm not convinced I even need tape this nice.  You will have to decide for yourself based on current pricing.

If I could do live over, this would be the only filler graph paper I would buy. It does everything graph paper is supposed toi do, but there is one important thing it does that the others don't do: No busted holes! Yep, that little reinforcement bit makes all the difference in the world. I recall countless nightmares of having pages fall out of my binder or getting wrinkled because the holes got busted on my paper. And if you've ever taken a high school or college math course, you know that you'll be taking the same graph paper sheets over and over again out of your binder. I'm so glad someone invented this, as it means the next generation doesn't have to suffer.

Most importantly this laminator does a fine job at laminating.  I do have a couple of gripes.  First, from the time you first turn it on it takes a really long time to warm up and signal it is ready to go.  Close to 10 minutes.  The second issue is the size.  It can accommodate up to 12.5 inches but the machine itself is 22.5 inches wide.  Although it is only about 6 inches deep you need to move it far enough out to let the stuff you are laminating to exit without hitting anything.  As I said it does do a very fine job of laminating papers, pictures, drawings, or whatever.

his folio is perfect for coupon organizing. I have my coupons organized by the isles of the grocery store I shop at. Each of the compartments represents coupons for products in a particular isle. It's a breeze to shop and to take maximum advantage of coupon use when I shop now.The product is very durable and has a nice closure as well. Fits in purse perfectly.

In good conscience, I can't rate this chair any higher than 3 stars.  There are simply too many detracting aspects about it for me to give a more enthusiastic rating although I will acknowledge it is a justifiable purchase at its' current price point.Once assembled, a process that took longer than I anticipated after a quick glance at the "picto-instructions" since I decided to follow them and use the only required tool  - a manufacturer supplied Allen wrench - rather than swap out for a ratcheting drive, the padding of the seat and backrest is pleasingly plush.  The challenge with assembly is using the supplied implement and when tightening the arms on the backrest the top screw cannot be turned more than 1/3 of a full rotation as the protruding arm supports inhibit any more of a turn on the upper screw.The instructions also fail to indicate it would be suggestible to anchor the screws for the armrest rather than fully tightening as the backrest cannot be mounted if the arms don't allow a few millimeters of movement.  This step might also be expedited if two people are available for assembly; the backrest needs to be centered in order to fully tighten and sitting the chair on its side is not the best option to accomplish that task.  Granted, this annoyance is not uncommon with most items requiring assembly, but it doesn't make me any more willing to accept it.The chair seating is constructed of moderate grade soft leather not radically different in appearance to an upper range vinyl covering, with breathable synthetic meshing on the side panels of the seat and lower portion of the backrest. It is a grade of leather that may scuff or puncture easily if the chair scrapes against a metal desk drawer or the arms become lodged under a rough finish desktop underside. It may be an aberration with the unit I received but the right arm rest padding is noticeably less abundant than the left. The stitching on the side panels of backrest already looks like it has undergone a degree of stress so I might be looking for a sewing kit in the not too distant future.  I'm also not real impressed with the plastic components of the chair base or the armrests, which are already scratched from tightening the assembly screws.The lift/tilt mechanism seems to be adequate with pretty good range. It is primarily constructed of steel as is the center tubing. For my preferences, the lumbar support is good although some potential customers may desire a chair with greater adjustment capabilities.  I'm using the chair in a Berber carpeted area and the wheels seem to have free movement without any squeaks or squeals.

She said:The ability to remove a single label from the sheet is absolutely wonderful.  The sheet then goes back through the printer without a problem, so you can print one label or a few labels as needed without waste.The tooth works perfectly on inkjet printers.  You can print inkjet lapels in color or black and white and they come out as well as the printer is capable of producing an ink output.But the best thing that the labels have is exactly what they advertise, the "Easy Peel".  Peel one label off a sheet, and keep the rest on the sheet.We will buy the easy peel labels even if they are somewhat more than the competition.

I have a small 2 shelf rack that holds my printer/flatbed scanner on the top shelf and this sheetfed scanner fits perfectly on the bottom shelf. I absolutely love how easy it is to get my work done! And did I mention, my shredder fits right next to the rack. I just wish EVERYTHING in life was this easy!

Worked ok for the first few months.  Now I get really bad color prints.  I have researched it on the net with mixed results.  Samsung has few real troubleshooting resources.  I paid $89.00 with free shipping.  Its not worth that.

Purchased through Amazon. Very good price here  on Amazon. The picture shows three different colours but we recieved three blue ones, not a big deal really just thought I'd mention it. They work nicely.

Easy to assemble - no tools necessary except for a rubber mallet or hammer & block of wood.Very sturdy and the large wheels roll over door sills with little resistance. Be sure to locate handle as pictured so the handle bracket is flush against the bottom of the top shelf.When installing wheels on the legs just invert the leg with the open end up & position the wheel shaft in the leg tube and tap the leg on the floor a few times and wheels seat themselves.Good product at a reasonable price & quick Amazon delivery.
Great little printer. Takes up minimal space on the desk. Easy to set up. Easy to add more users. Works like a charm! Prints beautifully in color and black and white as well as printing my photos.

I've had a canon 500 series for a while and its a very solid printer.  Not a speedster at all, but the print quality is great, reliability has been perfect, and software support is very solid (e.g., t-shirt transfers which need to be inverted were included via one choice in print setup).The issue with this (and probably other color inkjets) is that the price is very misleading.  It's the cost of ink that will really be the cost, they run out pretty quickly, and the replacement cartridges are very expensive.  If you don't mind that aspect, its a great printer.

Very nice permanent marker set, and everything stays organized in the tri-fold plastic case.  The markers are high quality and come in a lot of fun colors.  My nieces loved using this set when over one weekend.

I have a bit of an office supply addiction, so I'm always eager to try out new folders.  These Smead folders are unusual in that you can file them vertically or horizontally.  Tabs allow you to label the folders regardless of their orientation.  If filed horizontally, then these folders are slightly taller than the average manila folder, but they fit into filing cabinet drawers.  If filed vertically (or upright), then they cannot be used in the typical filing cabinet.  However, I can still see many uses for these folders.  For example, they would be perfect for open-top desktop filing boxes.  In this manner, your documents are filed upright and can be read easily when flipping through files.  Smead offers a vertical filing case for this purpose.  I also have been using them to transport materials to meetings; because the folders are closed on two sides, they are perfect for carrying papers without worrying about things falling out of them.The folders come in three earth tones - blue (stonewash), brown (nutmeg), and green (leek).  The neutral colors will look great in most offices, and the colors allow the folders to stand out well.  I have been using them on my desk for various projects, and I can always find them in a pile of manila folders due to their color and size.  The folders are made of a sturdy water-resistant 100% recycled material; I think that they will withstand use.  They are a bit pricey for a package of six but novel and well-made enough to merit the extra cost.

Bought these after reading the great reviews on them and how well they perform.  All in all, I'm very happy with them for specific uses.  However, they do have some downsides.In particular, the ink still goes through paper.  Not sure if it is the amount of ink it releases, or the overall type of ink, but my hope was the UF tip would limit this issue.  Wrote a check today, and when I went to tear it out, the check underneath had the black ink on it.  This also happened on the notepad I had used.Overall a solid pen, just know that these will go through your everyday paper writing products.  If you need one that doesn't go through paper, get the Sharpie pens that are grey/black in casing and don't bleed through.

This roll of post it sticky note paper works like a roll of scotch tape.  You roll out a strip of low tack sticky paper and write what you want on it, pull to remove (like any post-it note).  It is simple, strong, and very basic.  Not much to complain about here except the price.

The concept is pretty cool - put down a sticky note without obscuring the text or pictures below it. But in action, the texture of this sticky note isn't fantastic. It's basically a thin sheet of plastic with some stickum on the back, so when you try to write on it, you need to use a non-running ballpoint pen, no gel pens, and press harder than usual because of the lack of traction you get when writing on a sheet of plastic.I think this is an innovative idea, and if I had situations in which this was truly critical and needed, and not just kind of a neat feature, then I'd forgive its flaws and be enthusiastic about it. But so far, comfort and ease in writing on my post-it has trumped seeing through my post-it. I suspect many users will feel the same.

I'm glad someone finally thought to make sticky notes that have two sticky strips, as it can get really annoying to have paper curl - which in turn promotes the note falling off the surface.  These are well-designed and hopefully just the first of many such products.  I stuck one on my son's door a couple of weeks ago, and it's still there!

We never seem to have enough of these around my house, especially before school starts in the fall.These are nice quality binders. The ring is attached to the back, not the inside spine. Easy to load. My 11 year old daughter reports that it was easy for her to insert spine labels, but the label also easily slips out, so she had to tape add a piece of tape to the top to keep it from slipping out.

If you have a picture, calendar o any other lightweight picture(1 pound or less,) don't reach for the hammer and nails.  Instead use Scotch Reusable Tabs.  You get 18 of these little guys, which can be reused as well.  They can easily hold up a calendar or a lightweight picture with no trouble.  Aside from that they are also very subtle because they are very thin.  For small jobs that need a hanging, use this product and you won't be disappointed.

I complain in the review title that the directions for this device could be better but then I have to laugh at myself a bit and ask why a relatively simple piece of equipment needs directions at all.  In reality this shouldn't need much in the way of directions, but if it is going to include them, well, those directions need to be clear and to the point and they should clearly note what everything that came in the package is for and where it would be used.  Minus a couple of star fragments in the review for that (somewhat) failing.In terms of does this device work the answer is clearly yes.  You put it together, put it in the intended spot and put your monitor on top of it and you're done.  It gives you some additional space below the monitor that will stand on it and helps to raise that monitor to a more appropriate viewing height.  If the monitor you have is on a stand that is fixed height (we use a bunch of fairly inexpensive Acer monitors at my work, all of which are on such stands) this can be of great benefit.For me, this piece of equipment somewhat replaces an older monitor stand that I had been using.  That being one of these: (Allsop Metal Art Monitor Stand (Black)or one very similar).  I like the Allsop stand though I would note that it seems to have always been "bent" a little with the shelve that the monitor is supposed to sit on always tilted forward rather than sitting level.  The design of this Fellowes monitor riser precludes that from happening as the flat surface is equally supported on 3 legs.  Having the back leg for this riser may make it less convenient to put items under the stand/monitor, but there is still a decent amount of space under there to place things.In the end this seems to be useful piece of equipment that is priced reasonably enough to make it worth recommending for those that need something like it.

These are amazing! How clever that someone devised a way to bend thin strips of shiny metal in such a fashion that they can be used to clip several sheets of paper products together so they don't get lost. They don't work as well as my stapler, but those with commitment issues will find the paper clip a great alternative. They can also be bent into fun shapes when you are faced with idle time sitting at your desk. However, it seems that once they are altered from their original shape, they do not perform their intended task very well anymore. Sure glad that I purchased 1,000 of these little buggers.

Is it hard to get excited by staplers? This is not your run of the mill red swingline. Of course there will be allusions to "Office Space", but this stapler takes it up a notch. It's labeled "Business Pro"; it feels beefy and substantial. This stapler really can staple 25 sheets of copy paper together with little fuss (yes, I tried it, along with stapling bristol board and cardboard together). It has a compartment underneath for holding more staples. The one deficit here is this is covered by a synthetic rubber cover - that while it fits into place fine - still leaves me wondering how well it will hold up over the years, but this is a very minor issue.Otherwise, this is one of the nicest desk staplers I've seen. It's squared off look combined with it's red color and black rubber accents looks great - almost Ikea-ish. It's one of those common tools that works fine with no fuss, and it doesn't jam. I appreciate these kind of common objects that just do their job. It is easy to make something that is "good enough". This is better.

By now, you surely know what the function of the sticky-note (or Post-it) is.  If not, then you don't need this product and a review of it is of no use to you.  These square pads are essential for the office setting, and darn near essential in many households.I'm also not really prepared to wade into the debate over GM vs. Avery.  GM invented these, but in my opinion, Avery's quality is just the same.  At least in terms of stickiness.  Identical, IMO.  Others have different experiences to report.In the case of this specific product, the selling point is the fact that they're made from recycled materials.  I like that...but for my tastes, I prefer the brighter colors.  I usually want my sticky note not only to stick but to "stick out" in terms of being easy to notice.  These recycled squares are very subtlely colored.  Some folks will probably love that...again, it's all personal preference.If recycling and "green" is very important to you, you'll like these because they say they are 100% recycled.  That IS nice...so often, green paper products are only a small percentage recycled.  So in the end, I can heartily recommend these...but I can't recommend them more than any other 3" x 3" adhesive note pad out there.  Too much personal choice.

These sheet protectors are perfect for anyone using them under stage lights. As the music director for my church, I have given all of the musicians three ring binders, but we had trouble with the glare from the stage lights obscuring the music. These eliminated the glare from the sheet protectors.They have also proven to be sturdy and easy to use, without much sticking.These are great anti-glare sheet protectors.
Been wanting one of these for years to replace a very old Dymo tape labeler.  This works very well and is easy to use.

After being generally unimpressed with the quality of this printer on normal paper (there are visible offsets from one print stripe to the next, though the color is well done) I tried it with glossy photo paper. Hello, antiquing! The ink pools and separates on both HP and Kodak premium glossy paper (both of which are rated for inkjet printers) and is notably wet when it emerges from the printer, and for several minutes afterwards. Though it was a new printer, I tried head cleaning and nozzle checks to no avail.  In my opinion, there are btter printers for the price point and this model should be avoided.  A commentor to this review pointed out that Epson paper could avoid the issue with the photo paper.  My Canon printer works fine with this photo paper, and personally I do not like having to be locked in to a particular brand of photo paper.  If buying a particular brand paper does not bother you, it could improve the print quality for photos.  I still do not think that the printer does a great job and it is relatively pricey for a desktop printer.  We also own this printer and prefer it to the Epson for regular and photo printing.Canon PIXMA MX922 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax

No question about it, Avery makes the best adhesive labels for computer printing.  Avery offers a vast variety with a size or type for just about any common use.  How can it get better? Or to continue the car analogy, like watching a Yugo struggle up a highway ramp. It will eventually get there, but it's a slow struggle and sounds horrible. So first a shout out to packaging: product was packaged so well (wrapped in plastic then surrounded by foam so not even touching cardboard outer box) that even when my UPS delivery guy left the box out in the pouring rain all day, none of the components were even slightly damp when I unpacked it.Assembly instructions were clear and easy to follow. Anyway, was able to access HP Solution Center and downloaded a separate set of manual set up instructions that were not quite as easy to follow.  My computer crashed 3 times trying to back out the auto install files. 2 hours later, I was able to clean my hard drive to follow the manual install instructions and got the darn thing set up.Now, after all that... here are my thoughts/grades on how the product works.Physical Design: AOverall, the product is sleek, pretty and compact.  It has a shiny black color and sits comfortably on the corner of the desk.Ease of Use: B+There are clear picture icons on the buttons to identify the different options: color vs bw fax, color vs bw copy, etc.Paper is easy to load. I tried running a copy job while talking on the phone and found that the noise level was not at all distracting.Quality of Output: BSo I thought the quality was good. Certainly document printing (both color and bw) were fine. I did try to print/copy a photo and found that photo quality was not at the level of a dedicated photo printer (like my Canon Pixma). But it's great for standard printing jobs.Overall I'd give this a B/B+ (my installation/set up issues did not factor into my rating). It would not replace my beloved Canon printer, but I did find it to be a competent and compact solution for home office/personal use.

STRIP-SHREDDING: The size and ability to shred credit cards and CDs really appealed to me, but I was disappointed to find the paper shredding was only "strip shredding." Strip shredding makes 1/4 inch strips and the full length of the paper which, with enough patients can easily be puzzled-pieced back together, taped, and made completely legible. (I have done this on something that I needed to put back together again.) Your paper and credit cards run through the same feeder. You run the risk of someone getting your private information off any of these items you run through this shredder. For this reason I marked down the unit. For the old cross-cut shredder unit I have (see link below) it make the strips smaller than 1/4 inch by 2 inches which makes it just about impossible to piece back together.STAPLES: I was very pleased with its ability to handle staples (they stay in tacked). It will not stop paper from flowing right through and just bypasses the staples. I even tested an envelope folded several time was several stapes and the unit was able to handle the metal staples just fine.JUNK MAIL: I ran a standard thick envelope of junk mail and it handled the load just fine. But one word of warning, one of the other reviewer's says that you can almost run 16 sheets through this shredder. I tried the maximum shown on the unit (8) and it was struggling at that. I would not recommend you try and run more than 8 or you may make the unit unusable.CDs: As far as shredding CD, it did a WONDERFUL job! I have in the past tried to cut my old CDs with scissors, only to have shattered pieces flying all over the place. With this unit it cuts the CD in 4 strips which makes them unusable. You have to press a separate button to make the CD go through it's own separate feeder (there is not an automatic shred setting).SIZE: Love the compact size too: 12" tall and 13"x7" structure. It is fairly noisy, but has an automatic shred setting for the paper feeder so only makes noise while shredding. For the price it isn't a bad unit, but you still run security risk without the cross-cut!CROSS-CUT SHREDDER: I will still use my cross-cut shredder I've had for years and it's on sale on Amazon now for the same $30 price (although it doesn't do CDs or credit cards).Fellowes PowerShred P600C Paper Shredder

INSTALLATION PROCESS:*** Smooth and intuitive. I have a home network, and it was detected perfectly, much to my relief. The three laptops in the house (2 PC's and 1 Mac) are online wirelessly. I have no idea how that happened, since I don't understand the concept very well but, luckily, it went without a hitch.***  I have it connected via USB to the desktop which is located in a room where the wireless connection is so weak it required bringing in wires through the attic from the dsl modem to the computer. It works even faster via the USB port.***  All the drivers and utilities (printer, scanner, fax, and event manager utilities) are contained in the CD and it installs them sequentially with minimal user involvement.AS A PRINTER:*** It is designed for better quality business use. It's geared at people who want to print more professional and elegant documents, brochures, business cards, hand-outs, small booklets (it uses only letter or legal size paper), and business presentations in house.*** It's hard to believe it's an inkjet. The colors are rich and well defined; the black is deep and dark and sharp. Gradients and color transitions are smooth and clean.*** The quality of the print is equal (if not better than) what you pay to have printed at Kinko's, etc.*** I can't say how much I appreciate having a larger black cartridge! I've looked for this feature ever since my Epson Stylus 400 died. It saves a lot of money and aggravation since--regardless of what color you are printing--the black cartridge is a always contributor to the total color. Since it is the most used ink, it makes perfect sense that there should be more of it.*** This is the first printer I've ever had with individual ink cartridges for the Cyan, Magenta, and Yellow. Our company logo is in green (cyan and yellow and no magenta) and we often print the text in dark blue (cyan and magenta, no yellow). So we each time we ran out of Cyan, the whole color cartridge had to be replaced. I think we'll be saving money.*** The ink dries fast and doesn't curl the paper (we use 94% white, 24 lb stock). Haven't  tried it on 20 lb paper, but doubt it would be a problem. (There is an option for draft printing which lays down less ink and an option for grayscale if you want to test out your document without using color.*** Black and white printing is (at least) equal in quality to black and white laser printing: sharp, well-defined edges, smooth curves, excellent contrast, no haziness or blur anywhere.*** Color document printing looks completely professional, even in areas of color transition or gradation. Same sharpness and definition as black and white printing.*** It is not specifically designed for printing photos, but it does a very good job. I have an Epson Stylus 900 photo printer and the quality is fairly close. The problem is that it does not provide profiles for any non-glossy photo papers. Most of the profiles it supports are for presentation papers or regular papers. Photos will print very well in these papers as part of a presentation, but if you want to print a photo (as a photo) on non-glossy photo paper, you won't get as good a result as you would if the printer gave you a wider list of papers to choose from. I checked online, and there isn't any way to download additional profiles for the printer, so you have to pick one of the "wrong" profiles and hope it's close enough. It also doesn't provide a paper profile that would be applicable to printing something on heavier paper (such as cover stock or card stock). I did try to print an invitation on 64-lb card stock using the "Premium Presentation Paper Matte" option and it came out fine, but I can't help wondering if a more paper-specific profile could have given me an even better result.*** Having stated that this is not a specifically photo printer, it does provide some options for adjusting photos (such as converting to sepia, auto corrections, scene-specific corrections, and gamma and color space choices). Personally, I prefer to edit in Photoshop on an image-by-image basis rather than applying the same editing formula to all images, but I played with a couple of the options and they aren't bad.***  Curiously, sRGB, the most common color space, is not an option. You get to choose between AdobeRGB and Epson Vivid (whatever that is). I noticed no difference in print quality or color when sending the document to the printer as ProPhotoRGB, AdobeRGB or sRGB. But, if you work in a wide color space in Photoshop, you don't have to convert (or reduce bit depth). The printer makes all these conversions for you, apparently. I'm assuming this is a good thing.*** Since I was unable to find specific information about the optimum resolution at which to send photos to the printer, I assumed that the usual 360 dpi that most (or many) Epson printers prefer applied to this printer, too. I printed at 300 dpi and at 360 dpi and could tell very little difference, however.AS A SCANNER:*** I was already familiar with the Epson Scan software as I have used it for years. It is intuitive, dependable, easy-to-learn, and effective TWAIN software and it works either from within Photoshop or as a free-standing software.*** It is possible to do considerable editing from within the software, and is excellent for all purposes from photos to documents. Scanning in "Professional" mode gives you a lot more options, and isn't as intimidating as it sounds. The default mode is "office."***  The scanner works perfectly and you can control the function from the computer and save to the computer or a memory card, you can save as jpg or tiff, or create a PDF from your scan. You can even scan to e-mail (the scanner scans, opens your e-mail program, and attaches your image to the e-mail).AS A FAX:*** Works as a free-standing fax machine, where you would load the paper, dial the number, and send and receive faxes using the machine's controls just as you did with your old fax machine (except that this one is a little more interactive and the little window keeps you informed and keeps giving you options and instructions).*** Works as an `attachment' to your computer, where you can open a document that you want to fax, and proceed as if you were going to print (except you select the Epson Workforce 840 FAX as your printer option) and proceed to fax the document or you can use the control panel to select the fax icon and open a faxing dialog from there.*** It has options such as saving a list of numbers you fax frequently; creating a sender identification header; setting number of rings for fax to pick up; faxing from either the scanner glass or the automatic document feeder; faxing in color; redialing busy numbers automatically, etc.*** Of all of the above, I find the faxing a document using the "print" dialog to be the smoothest workflow--works like a charm.AS A COPIER:*** It copies perfectly well. The print quality of copies is, of course, dependent on the quality of the original. With an excellent original, you will get an excellent copy. Having said this, it is probably not the most cost-effective way to make multiple copies.*** The automatic document feeder on top makes your life a lot easier since you don't have to keep raising the lid to copy each page and you can send a whole stack of pages as a fax.SUMMARY:*** It REALLY is an all-in-one unit. It is user-friendly and has a logical interface that is easy to learn and use.***  For a machine that performs so many functions, it has a very small foot-print. The only caveat is that it needs clearance space on top to open the scanner lid.*** The instructions are clear, the operation is smooth, the response is immediate, the status display keeps you informed, there is easy access to status and maintenance information (such as remaining ink supplies) and trouble-shooting tools and information.***  You can load the machine with a whole ream of paper at one time and the two paper trays give you a lot flexibility.*** All in all, a complete winner!

I have used a Hunt Boston pencil sharpener for years.  The Hunt Boston sharpener is relatively quiet and efficient.  I think we have used it for at least five years or more.  I am also a huge fan of X-Acto knives.  I have a bunch of X-Acto knives along with dozens of blades.  X-Acto brand knives and blades are great for woodworking, building plastic models, and other hobbies.  Thus, I was excited to try a pencil sharpener from X-Acto.The pencil sharpener looks like a high quality product.  It feels solid and sturdy and rests firmly and flatly on my workbench.  I was initially impressed and almost ready to sharpen pencils.  Before I did, I removed the tray that holds the wood shavings.  The tray seemed a little cheap, but hey, it is a plastic tray to hold trash, so how fancy does it need to be?  The problem came when I tried to put the tray back into the pencil sharpener.  The tray would not go back into its slot.Surely, I was doing something wrong.  I took the tray back out to make sure I had not missed some sort of adjustment that needed set to get the tray back into the sharpener.  After all, I am a typical guy and I only read the instructions after figuring out how something works, if ever.  However, I had not missed anything.  The problem is that a plastic prong on the back of the tray, which I think engages a safety switch that enables to sharpener to work only when the tray is in place, did not properly mate with the hole.  It takes some jiggling of the tray to get it in place each time I remove it.  The inability to easily mate with the pencil sharpener subtracts one and a half stars.After finally getting the tray back into the pencil sharpener, I was ready to sharpen a pencil or a bunch of them since I seem to accumulate dull pencils on my workbench, where I do not have a pencil sharpener.  Into the sharpener went a pencil.  The good news is that the sharpener did quickly put a nice point on the end of my pencil.  The bad news is that I thought the sharpener was broken.  The sharpener makes a horrible grinding noise every time I sharpen a pencil.  In contrast, my Hunt Boston sharpener makes a humming noise when the motor operates.  The X-Acto sharpener seems to be working well; it is just relatively noisy compared with my current Hunt Boston, and a former electric sharpener that the Hunt Boston replaced.  The noise is also obnoxious and sounds like something is operating in a way it should not be operating.  I subtract a second star and a half for excessive and unnecessary noise, which may be an indication of something that may break in the long term.I must to admit to some disappointment.  X-Acto is a brand I associate with high quality.  The shaving tray is hard to install and the motor sounds like grinding gears.  It is possible that my pencil sharpener is defective.  However, I would have thought that routine acceptance testing would catch a defective product prior to shipment.  That leads me to believe that X-Acto considers this product typical production.  If that is the case, I have to recommend against purchasing this product.I looked at the ratings on Amazon for this product and, unsurprisingly, learned that this product has many one and two star ratings.  The one and two star ratings tell a story.  Many of the ratings are because the sharpener failed to sharpen either well or at all.  Many of these ratings are because the sharpener failed immediately or within days, weeks or months of purchase.  What I wonder is whether someone thought it might be a good idea to involve Amazon Vine reviewers in the hope that Vine reviewers might be more favorable.  If that was the thought, the thought was in vain because I am only slightly more impressed than previous reviewers are.I hoped the X-Acto name was an indication of the quality of this product.  It is not.  I am disappointed with the shavings tray and with the noise level and the type of noise. This Canon PIXMA PRO-100 from Amazon Vine replaces a seldom used Epson 1650 Photo printer which replaced an earlier Epson. We do a lot of wild bird photography and like to make up cards and prints of the superior shots. How disappointing to find that the recommended printers fail to deliver realistic and vibrant color images. (The problems with both Epson photo printers was getting the color print to approximate the color of the image on the monitor.) Each printer was, in that respect, disappointing.I have to admit to a bit of skepticism when setting up and testing the new Canon, however, my fears were unfounded. As stated on the website, "The PIXMA PRO-100 Wireless Professional Inkjet Printer possesses the functionality and technology you need to achieve high-quality output so your prints can look as good as the images you capture." How true. The 8-ink dye based ChromaLife100+ system provides the user with a wonderful palette so each print is vivid and true to life.Setup was a bit time-consuming but not difficult. Our other printers use a USB setup, but this time I decided to try the wireless mode. The printer is set up in my husband's studio on a home network with the router directly below. The associated computer is an HP Laptop running Windows 7, 64-bit PC.A quick-start illustrated sheet guides you through the initial set-up (removing orange protective tape, placing print head, installing the 8 ink cartridges. All this is done wirelessly until you get to the hardware installation from the accompanying disk. Then you need to plug in the USB cable and follow the on screen directions. This is a first for me, however the instructions are easy to follow. When the software and drivers are installed, you are instructed to disconnect the USB cable.As stated by others, the footprint on this is large, 25% bigger than the Epson 1650. Fortunately, the printer and scanner share a six-foot table so accommodation was easy. Having Wi-Fi, Ethernet and USB makes it versatile for any work situation.Some pluses: you can print various media up to 13" x 19" at 4800 x 2400 dpi with FINE technology for outstanding detail, the Print Studio Pro Plug-in software allows seamless work flow (compatible with Digital Photo Professional (ver 2.1 or later), Adobe Photoshop CS, Adobe Photoshop Elements, and Adobe Photoshop Lightroom).Another feature I like is the two-way paper feeding for various types and thicknesses of paper. Also, built-in CD and DVD printing allows you to print directly onto your CD, DVD or Blu-ray discs.AirPrint allows you to print photos, email, Web pages and documents from your Apple device directly to your printer.Lastly, there's computer-free printing where a PictBridge connection lets you print photos directly from your compatible digital camera, DV camcorder, or camera phone.I ran test prints following the setup, then tried a few color images of birds. I was blown away by the print quality. Very hard to tell these were not done in a photo studio. (Note: I did not use the provided canon paper but rather sheets of semi-gloss from Epson which we bought at Costco.)Haven't tried B&W; printing since we use a laserjet for text, but for photos, this machine is outstanding.The only negative might be paper cost, cartridge cost and life, but all photo printers use a lot of ink, so it should be expected.Overall, I highly recommend the Canon PIXMA PRO-100.WHAT'S IN THE BOXPIXMA PRO-100 Wireless Professional Inkjet PrinterCD/DVD Disc Printing TrayManuals and other documentsSetup CD-ROM  (one for PC, one for Mac)Setup Ink TanksPower CordPrint HeadUSB Cable

I was tempted to title this review "When a good brand goes bad", but that wouldn't be fair, because the HP Officejet Pro 8000 does print beautifully and has relatively long-lasting ink cartridges.  If my two HP Officejet Pro 8000's are any guide, serious reliability problems show up after a year or so of ownership.I've owned my current one for a year and the previous one for 18 months.  I loved both of them at first.  I've been buying HP printers faithfully since 1993.  As a writer, I use my printers a lot and need one that's reliable and durable.  In the past, HP always was both.  Over the years, it became one of those rare brands that was a no-brainer to buy.I bought my first HP Officejet Pro 8000 after I had to discard my faithful HP Business Jet 1100dtn because HP did not release a Windows 7 driver for it, with the result that I could no longer do duplex printing.  For the first year or so, the HP Officejet Pro 8000 printed beautifully, just as well as my older HP, but then the problems began.  There were two problems:1. Sometimes the printer would just not print.  I did everything suggested in the manual and online, but it would not print.  I'm a computer professional and am fairly good at this sort of thing, but nothing I did would make it print. The next day, however, it would be fine.  At first it was just occasional.  Finally it because too frequent to ignore.  I still believed in HP and thought I had just gotten a bad printer, so I bought another of the same model.  So far the problem hasn't happened with it, but a friend with the same printer is having this problem regularly, so I expect I'll experience it sooner or later.2. Paper jamming or misaligning.  This became a problem after about a year with both of my HP Officejet Pro 8000's.  It began yesterday on my current one, when it took me several hours to print 24 pages of an important and urgent document that weren't torn or misaligned.  Very frustrating.I don't share some owner's complaints about the printer's noise, but I am unhappy with the warm-up time, especially because it's using up ink in the process.  I was having a problem for a while with a surge protector switching off randomly.  During this period, when the printer was being switched on several times a day, it used an enormous amount of ink even though I did very little printing.  If you want long life from your ink cartridges, don't turn your HP Officejet Pro 8000 on and off very often.If only one of my HP Officejet Pro 8000's had gone bad, I'd accept that I just had the bad luck to get a defective unit.  Even the best manufacturer occasionally mades a lemon.  But I've owned two of this printer, and a close friend owns one also.  She has had the same problems I had with my first one, and that I'm beginning to have with my second one.After 18 years as a loyal HP customer, my next printer will not be an HP.  I've ordered a Brother HL-2270DW monochrome laser printer for printing text and will save my HP Officejet Pro 8000 for printing photos as long as it continues working.  It seems to have fewer problems with photo paper than regular inkjet paper.

UPDATE Nov 2012: I upgraded to Windows 8 a couple of weeks ago the day after it first came out, and I wanted to say that this printer has no problems in Windows 8.  Works perfectly.Old Review: This printer arrived a few days ago, and it was like Christmas Morning.  What tech guy doesn't like playing with new tech stuff?  There was so much to play with on this device, that setting it up was just FUN.  That's not really an issue with the printer itself, more my perceptions and experiences with it, but I wanted to say it anyway.  NOTE: I am using Windows 7 64bit Home Premium.First off, the thing is BIG.  Now I wasn't expecting a tiny little compact thing, mind you.  You don't get a full function device like this and expect it to be small.  But it was way bigger than I anticipated.  It's roughly 18 inches wide by 17 inches deep and 14 inches tall.  It didn't fit where my old printer was - the table the old one sat on is JUST too small for this, which made for some shuffling of furniture and whatnot.  Additionally, anything other than your default paper gets loaded via a backside paper loader.  Your primary paper (for me, 8.5x11) is loaded in a tray that disappears completely inside the printer.  But anything else (manual feed, envelopes) go in via the back paper loader, and it extends out the already large footprint of the thing.  It's not much, just an inch or two, but you will need some sort of extra space in the back, you can't just push it against a wall, and expect to be able to use the back paper loader.  Additionally, anything the device outputs comes out the front.  Which also has an extender to cradle the printed papers. Which extends the front of the thing out about another eight inches when fully extended.  If you don't do that, the paper will NOT stay in the printer and falls on the floor.  Additionally, the box it shipped in is itself even larger. It's all protective foam and whatnot inside there, but the box the UPS guy delivered was quite large.Once you take it out of the box, you'll find a ton of little bits of blue tape all over the outside (and inside).  This is pretty much to keep all the sensitive bits from sliding around and getting damaged.  You need to pull all the blue tape off first, and once you get the ones off that let you access the inside of the printer, there's some on the inside two, and two bits to remove from in there that were protecting the scanner guts.  There's a piece of paper taped to the outside of the printer showing you what to remove from the inside.  There is an instruction sheet showing the order of getting stuff set up.  I followed it, as since this is a brand new printer (as of the time of my writing), I assumed Windows wouldn't have proper drivers for it, and let the ESPON install disk do it's thing.  Normally I just hook up a device and let Windows find the drivers, to bypass all the crapware that most install discs put on there, but this one wasn't bad. Installed the printer, got it setup on my network and all that.  The four ink cartridges come in vacuum packed seals, and you're recommended not to open them until you're putting them in the printer.  You're supposed to shake them before putting them in the printer, but I missed that instruction.  It didn't seem to affect anything though. During setup, you're asked if you want to set up the printer wirelessly or via a "temporary USB connection", that is labeled as "recommended".  Yet they don't include a USB cable for you to use.  Odd, that.There are two parts where the initial set up really slows down.  One is the priming of the ink cartridges.  You follow the instructions on the little screen on the printer, and once you get the cartridges in there, it has to initialize them (whatever that means).  This does mean a 12 minute delay (felt longer, but I didn't time it) while it gets itself ready.  They tell you not to interrupt it, or open any doors while it's going on or it will "waste ink".  While I did as I was told, it did bog down. Additionally, I updated the firmware during the install as well, and that was another 10 minute or so "twiddle my thumbs watching not much of anything" moment.  Necessary I suppose, but don't expect to be printing five minutes after you get the thing out of the box.  I set up wirelessly. I do wonder if the speed of setup was slowed down because I did it via wireless.The printer works either via a hardwired connection or wireless.  There's a hardwired network jack on the back, or it works over your local network via 802.11/b/g/n connections.  The printer didn't see my "N" connection, so it connected to my "G" one.  Not a huge deal really, just odd that it didn't see the "N".  The wireless is nice because the printer can more easily work over your network as opposed to the older fashioned "shared printer" concept.I'm also an iPad owner, and earlier this year when Apple introduced the concept of AirPrint, I thought it was gonna be cool to print from my iPad.  Then I discovered the number of printers that worked with that was limited to a handful of HP units, and nothing else worked (easily, anyway).  There was a small paper inside the box here saying this printer worked with iOS AirPrint, but only after a firmware update (which is the aforementioned one I talked about earlier).  Once I got everything set up, I was quite surprised to see that feature work.  It will stop quite a few things my wife would forward me and say "Please print this".  :)There's also another cool feature which I doubt I'll use much, but it's nice that it's there.  Print via email.  During setup, you get a page printed telling you about the printer's capability to print stuff you email to a specific address.  That address is printed on the paper.  I tried it out, and it does work.  It's kind of cool that you can do this, I suppose it's a way if you're away from the printer and need to get something to someone where your printer is that you can do that.  The email address is quite long and complicated, but I do wonder about the spam capabilities there.The auto feed scanner will do double side scanning, which is nice.  I don't have many print and scan jobs that require double sided stuff, but it's nice to know it's there just the same.Here's some remarks about the various sections of the device's functionality:Scanner:  The EPSON Scan software that gets installed during installation does the job.  It's certainly better than the stuff that I was using before on my old scanner, which was the stuff built directly into Windows.  This has a lot more detail including dust removal & back light correction, which is a big deal to me, as I have a boatload of old pictures that need to be scanned, and that definitely helps.  The speed of the scanner was quite good.  Sure, you can jack up the DPI and really slow things down, but for standard scanning, it does the job quite well. The resultant quality of the scans is good as well. Don't know how to compare that to other scanners, just that what it scans looks good, so I guess that's OK, eh?  :) There is OCR software on the install CD, but I opted not to install that, so I can't remark on how well it works.  A nice upgrade on what I was using before, which was well, not good.  You can also scan to email, scan to PC, or scan straight to a PDF.  It's a nice selection of options depending on what your needs are for that particular scan.  The resultant scans of photographs came out quite nice.  Obviously if the picture is too old and too beat up, that's not the scanner's fault, but it does seem to do a good job at auto removing some damage to old photographs.Printing: I tried printing several different kinds of things during my setup and initial testing.  The standard "test page", and a few photos and various documents and whatnot.  Despite not having "custom" paper to print photos on, I printed 'em on plain old printer paper, and they still looked pretty decent, so I imagine proper printing paper for photos would look quite good.  The printer is quite fast, even when printing photos. Granted, printing a photo isn't as fast as printing just a page of black and white text obviously, it was still snappier than I thought it would be.  Word documents are quite crisp and easy to read. Pages with color accents on mostly black and white printed pretty much as fast as an all black text page did.  Given printing is the majority of what I'll use this device for, I was impressed at all my attempts to throw print jobs at it. EPSON claims the printer ink will look good printing pictures on any kind of paper.  It does seem better on standard paper than special paper, so I'll buy that.  Again, plain text and document printing looks quite crisp.  Their tech claims that the documents printed will last 118 years. I seriously doubt I'll still be around to check that claim out for myself.Fax: Initially the print to fax didn't work right out of the box.  The setup disc added two printers to my "Devices" tab.  One for the printer, and one for the fax.  The fax one was greyed out and didn't work when I tried to use it for the first time.  I looked into the settings, and Windows (or the EPSON Setup) had assigned the port to LPT1:, the old style of printer port.  The "printing" area of the new printer was working fine, and it was on some new EPSON port.  So I manually changed the port for the Fax to the same as the printer, and it worked fine.  I was able to test it by faxing a dummy fax to 1-888-877-1655 (a toll free number for a site called faxtoy daht net). You can look on that site and see your test, as they post everything they receive there.  An inbound test worked too via the site faxzero daht cahm.  So the fax worked quite well.  I really liked being able to "print" to the fax machine.  A fax machine is generally an antiquated concept, but for the times you HAVE to do it, I prefer being able to just print my document via fax as opposed to the old way of printing it out, and faxing it via physical paper.  This gets a thumbs up for sure.  EPSON claims it can send a page as fast as three seconds.  My test faxes were pretty short, and were "Print to Fax", I'm unclear if that speed claim is for physical paper faxes, or the way I did it.  Still, given how infrequently I fax anyway, I doubt the speed of the faxing will be an issue, much less how fast it goes.Ink: The printer came with four individually colored toner cartridges.  Black, Yellow, Red, & Blue (although they call them Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, & Black).  The ones in the box have a smaller capacity than the ones you would buy as refills.  The marketing says that the thing can get a couple of thousand pages out of a set of toner, but the ones in the box say 1000 for Black, and 900 for color, so they're not the same shipping with the printer, I believe they're referred to somewhere along the line as "starter" packs.  A check of the Epson site shows refills aren't exactly cheap. The three color cartridges are $24.99 each, and the black one is $38.99.  Gah!  To replace all four of them would cost $113.96 (plus whatever tax and shipping you'd tack on).  Granted, a manufacturer toner cartridge for my old black and white laser-jets isn't cheap, either.  I'll be doing MOSTLY black and white printing, so the colors won't go down as fast, but still.  Given this printer sells for $300, spending over 1/3 of that price on a single complete ink refill is a LOT.  I'm sure there's replacements a lot cheaper, but it's always a gamble with cheap/no name toner/ink.Paper: For me, the overwhelming lion's share of printing jobs will be on standard 8.5x11 inch printer paper.  This printer has the capability of printing on a lot of different types of paper, but I doubt I'll be using a ton of them.  So I don't have a lot of say about that kind of stuff here, except..  I can stick a lot of paper in this printer at once.  The big sticker on the printer that was there before I took it off said you can stick 330 pieces of paper in there at once.  Now I didn't break down and count it obviously, but it did feel like a substantial amount of paper in there.  That's a non tangible thing, getting up and refilling.  And that's the front loading cartridge.  Other kinds of paper are loaded via a back loading tray, including envelopes. I would have preferred the envelopes be in the front and not the back, but oh well. The printer is marketed as having 50% lower printing costs.  There's a massive sticker ON TOP of the printer when you take it out of the box that says this.  Problem with this is I'm not sure how to quantify that claim - it's probably down to ink anyway, and not paper. I've never owned a printer like this before (my home office printers have always been smaller type things likethisorthis).  Still, even if it doesn't come near 50%, the fact that it probably will be more conservative with ink and whatnot is good.Problems: As I've only had this a couple of days as I write this, I've yet to run into the dreaded paper jam, so I have no idea how hard it is to fix problems like that. Every printer gets them, so I know I'll run into it some day.  But it's too early in the life of this printer for me to judge how hard it is to fix paper jams.So to summarize, the printer is more than sufficient for me in what it does.  It's quite large, so don't expect it to substitute in cleanly for a smaller type Laserjet printer if you're upgrading from that.  But it appears to be a workhorse from my initial testing.  As I use this going down the line, I'll update with any relevant issues I might run into.  If you're in need of a good small business printer to handle all kinds of duties (scan, fax, print, etc), this is a good option for you.P.S.  Yes, I realize the ink for this printer is more "ink" than "toner", but I've been saying toner for the stuff you put in a printer that lets it print so long I have a hard time forcing myself to say something other than the word "toner".  :)UPDATE: I saw where the four ink cartridges are available from Amazon.com as well.  They are:Black:Epson DuraBrite Ultra Ink, Black (T676XL120)Yellow:Epson DuraBrite Ultra T676XL420 Epson DuraBrite Ultra Ink, Yellow InkMagenta:Epson DuraBrite Ultra Ink, Magenta (T676XL320)Cyan:Epson DuraBrite Ultra Ink, Cyan (T676XL220)UPDATE Oct 20: Today I noticed an update to the firmware and software for the printer.  This new update brought with it the ability to hook up to Google Cloud Print.  Got that up and running - was pretty easy.  So the printer now has the ability to print with Epson's own "Epson Connect" as well as Google Cloud Print, and iOS' AirPrint.  It's a very well connected printer.  :)
