I chose this printer mostly because of the features like wireless printing, high-quality ink and the compact size. My other printer was way too big and heavy, but this one isn't bad to move around when needed. After using this Epson for a few weeks, I've yet to have any complaints. It has been a pleasure to use and trouble-free.Set-up was fast and easy, just follow the enclosed Quick Start sheet. It doesn't include a USB cord, so if you don't have a wireless internet connection in your home or office, you'll need a cord. I installed the software on a Mac, which was simple with a CD. You will also need an internet connection to install the software if you're using a Mac. You don't with a PC.If you have portable devices like tablets (iPad, etc.), you can also print directly from them as long as you have a wireless network in your home or office. It was just a few additional steps at set-up and then I was able to print from these other devices. It's so convenient to print things even from your smart phone or tablet. I love this feature and use it often.I'm very happy with the quality of the printing in both color and b&w.; No smearing or smudging and the print has a nice, sharp look. Photos look great too, especially if you use the right kind of photo paper for what you're printing.Like another reviewer mentioned, it has a 250-sheet of paper capacity. If you do high volumes of printing or copying, this might not be enough for you.I use the printer mostly for printing, but the photocopy, fax and scan features are very useful and all work well.The touchscreen menu works well and is mostly self-explainatory. I'm glad the menu panel on the front of the printer doesn't fold in and pull out like an older Epson model I have. This is a design improvement because my old Epson broke because of that feature. This one feels much sturdier and more solid.From the touchscreen, you can customize your printing/scanning/faxing/copying, set up your wi-fi connection, check your ink levels, do printer maintenence, check job status and more. The printer has auto 2-sided print, copy and faxing as well.Epson has a comprehensive online user guide so you can see the many things you can do with this printer. There are videos too if you want to see how to set up the wireless connection. I didn't find it necessary because the Quick Start page was very clear, but if you have trouble at least you can see how to do it or do troubleshooting.For the price, I think this is a really good value if you want a compact everyday printer with color printing, crisp b/w documents, photo printing and the addition of convenient features like faxing, scanning, copying and wireless printing directly from your computer, tablets and smart phone. The easy set-up, simple operation and printing without hooking up cords have saved me lots of time and aggravation. Very pleased with everything about this printer!

Scotch's restickable shapes for mounting are a great little product.  The package comes with 18 shapes and is available in different colors.  The shapes are hearts, stars, and circles.  The shapes about an 1" by 1" and can hold up to 3/4 lb without being intrusive or cumbersome.  They do work on a variety of substances (they advertise that they work on steel, plastic, concrete, glass, wood, painted walls, etc.).  We've successfully used them on glass, wood, walls, plastic and steel - we've not yet had the opportunity to try concrete.A neat little extra (that is stated in small print on the back) is that the shapes have a double-sided adhesive, the front of each shape has a plastic coat that can be peeled up so that it can have something adhered to its front while it holds up another item with its back.  This allows you to create a layered or three-dimensional effect on the fridge or other surface.If you like scrap-booking, you'll love decorating the fridge with these and if you are tired of magnets, these make a nice alternative for tacking things up at a moment's notice.  You'll probably even want to get a couple of different colors to be creative.

This is a very nice dispenser for use with Post-it notes.  It is quite heavy and sturdy, so you don't have to ever worry about the dispenser itself being lifted when you grab a note.  The top cover can be changed between either a blue or red pattern.  It looks nice on my desk and has a low profile so that I can keep it under my monitor.Just make sure that you purchase Post-it notes that are specifically for dispensers (accordian-style), not just a regular note pad.  Otherwise they will not work in the dispenser.

We had an old Ooma handset which is not compatible with the Linx. So a call to Ooma got us a new H2 handset at a great price and they even picked up the shipping.Once set up we are now using the Linx for a dedicated fax with our second number yet we retain the instant second line for both incoming and outgoing calls.For anyone wishing to have excellent phone service with dual lines and the Ooma in combination with the Linx is clearly the ticket.Ooma is the right solution at the right cost of any phone system regardless of provider. The best part is it has a dual ring feature so you can ring your cell phone and pick up your call while shopping or traveling.Ooma tech service is absolutely the best. They are professional, courteous, knowledgeable best of all call wait times are typically five minutes or less.

Okay, there are some pretty basic reasons I use these particular notebooks.  First and most importantly, they are cheap!  I go through dozens upon dozens of these things a year, to the extent that cost does matter.  I use them for everything...more about that later.  Secondly, they are college ruled.  I have a real hang up about that and have almost a phobia about using the wider ruled note books.  Thirdly, the quality of the paper is what I want...it holds ink pretty well, are better than some about ink bleeding through, but most importantly, it holds simple old graphite from my pencils.  The white color of the pages makes my feeble attempts at penmanship readable and does not stress my eyes in the bright sun light.  For me, these notebooks are simply work horses.Now if I were setting on the Board of Directors of a Fortune 500 company, I probably would not use these things during meetings (well, actually I would, cause I am me, but most people would not), but as I do not hold such a dubiously exalted position, and it is a pretty good bet that I never will, I need not worry about appearances in that particular setting.I do use these things for everything else though.  As I read, I take notes.  I am a list maker and manically and obsessively create list of just about anything you can imagine.  I have lists dating back for well over 60 years, many of which I have no clue as to what I was listing or why, but never-the-less, I have my precious lists.  These books are ideal for making shopping lists, chore lists, things to do lists and more.  Having different colors is a big advantage when you are a multiple list maker like me as it helps to organize things a bit.  I also use these to "write things down" as I have problems with my memory at times.  I wish I could say that this was because I am getting a bit long in the tooth, but that would be a lie.  I have been forgetting things since I was a wee lad and learned a long time ago that it is best to write things down. I have boxes and trunks filled with old notebooks of things I was an am suppose to remember...never look at most of them of course, but they are there if I need them! I am also an obsessive drawer and these are ideal for making rough sketches and strange designs.I like these thinner 70 page models over the thicker three or more subject ones as I tend to lose many of these notebooks and it is nicer to lose a few pages versus many pages.I must have hundreds of these things filled from cover to cover from my school days.  My children will no doubt have a wonderful burning one of these days.Are these books a pure class act?  Hardly, but they are cheap, serviceable, easy to find and extremely functional.  It has been years since I felt the need to impress anyone with my writing materials (actually, that is a lie also, due to the fact that to the best of my knowledge, I have never felt this need to impress anyone as to the aspect of my life), and I seriously doubt if I will change my way as I have gotten worse about such things over the years.This is a very good buy here on Amazon and it is good to throw a few of these things with your order so you can hit the no shipping fee zone.I highly recommend this serviceable product.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks

These little tabs come in three different colors - the blue and green are bright and easy to spot, while the khaki color blends in if you are looking to mark something without being distracting. The sticky on the back of these is light, so it doesn't peel anything off if you decide you want to unmark something you had previously marked. The perforated edge of the tabs make it easy to bend the edge of your marker without bending the whole marker, and can also be removed if you don't want it there anymore. There's not much to say about office supply markers like this, but they work perfectly for my purposes.

As a proponent for square objects opposed to the standard everyday rectangle, this was a must buy for me. I've been cutting regular labels square to fit my product, so for me this was a prefect solution.Not only are these an awesome shape, but the quality is definitely better than, say, a normal office address label. They are thicker and seem to stick longer, so they are perfect for sealing packaging or placing on your shopping bags for advertisement.You can print on Laser or Ink Jet and there are a lot of them in each pack (300!). I just can't say enough about this product that is essentially a sticky, printable, square!The only thing to consider - and this wasn't a big deal for me - was that I had to download the template from a website. Microsoft Word didn't seem to have this specialty label in it's list.

Even though only one roll of tape shipped, I can say this is typical super tape from the super tape company, 3M.  How do they do it?  I do not know but sorta do not care either.  It's the tape that counts.  For years, long years, I've used Scotch tape but it has always been the type that had to be cut with either a dispenser or other cutting device.  Now, we have a tape that can actually be torn without any difficulty.  Reluctance filled my mind when attempting to tear into the sealed package.  It amazes me to find a plastic covering so strong that a knife is needed to get into the tape.  Alas, I finally opened it and could not believe my eyes.  Pull, tear and tape!  Done is an understatement.  I can see an empty spool soon with all the wrapping left.  The first flock has been put out of sight and fully tapped with ease.  I planned to get 50 full yards according to the promo; however, the one roll came with 17 yards on it.  I hope the 3M folks are not advertising 2 rolls with 50 yards or maybe they just sent the wrong one instead of the right two.  No big thing, however.  I'm a Scotch fan and will use the few feet left and get another roll of something.  Regardless, I highly recommend this tape and will buy more later.

I upgraded from a plastic case to this one and I am rather pleased. The material feels very sturdy. It doesn't collect as much dust as the plastic case did and it is incredibly spacious (as in it will hold 1,000 cards). I'm still considering a steel case or switching to a Rolodex (throwback!) to keep my information at hand but this is a great little box. And the price is right.

TEKwriterUSA Gel Pens are really nice to use. The colors are bright, beautiful, and sparkly. I love the fact that the pens have a comfort grip on them, and that the entire pen (grip, cap, etc.) matches the color of the ink. These pens write very smoothly, and are a joy to use. I ordered these staples to go with the Stanley Bostitch Contemporary Full Strip Stapler for my classroom. I have not had ONE single jam since I bought the Stanley Bostitch stapler and staples. As a teacher, I will not go to another brand now. I have found the perfect combo for high usage.

These are nice color pans from Paper Mate, a trusted pen manufacturer.The pens come in 8 different colors, or course the blue and black ones will get the most use in my household.But it's nice to have the other colors as well.I find these to write nice and smoothly, a very nice product IMO.

My only disappointment is that it can't be wireless and plugging in at the same time -- at least that's what I read in the instructions. I have had very good luck with AmazonBasics products, including these. They say they are photo safe, and my experience with some irreplaceable family photographs, is that they are. I am using these with the AmazonBasics laminator and appreciate knowing that these work as the price for more is reasonable.
This is a great product and is what I wanted. Just sucks I have to buy my own supplies for work.

The stated specs state 30 feet line of sight.  While testing this with fresh Duracell batts, I got > 50 feet line of sight with excellent consistence responsiveness from the pointer to computer screen.  The reason I did not test longer is because I did not want to exit my house in the middle of the night in February to get an even longer line of sight.  So, this pointer should be good to go for any usual conference room or classroom, and I think it opens up the possibility of roaming a really really big room (i.e. hotel ballroom) while presenting.The design is simple, ambidextrous, and seems like a lot of design thought went into it.  Examples:1.  The USB dongle is very flat and can be stored in the unit itself.2.  The USB dongle has a bright blue light that flashes with each click so you know when the signal is getting through.3.  Comfortably fits in your hand, yet is small enough to stash in a pants/jacket pocket.  However, if your front pocket is too tight, people might wonder why you are so happy to see them (J/K).4.  The red laser pointer will not work unless the USB dongle is out of the storage slot (safety mechanism).5.  The buttons all have a nice grip feel to them and are easy to push.6.  The EZ presenter program is great!Why I like the EZ presenter program:1.  Very easy to install and doesn't slow my computer down, can be accessed from the right bottom system tray icons.2.  You can easily preload up to three files for quick launch and the EZ presenter will open them up simultaneously.3.  The ability to draw CHECKS and actively draw horizontal LINES with one undo/complete eraser works like a dream.  Also, it seems to work in any program or desktop (that I tested) as it directly "draws" onto your screen.Two improvements for future versions:1.  Need a another button for ENTER.  Sometimes, a window will pop up and you have to close it by hitting ENTER or moving the mouse pointer over to it and clicking.  Obviously just hitting ENTER is a lot faster and easier, less disruptive when presenting.  I don't expect a keyboard on this thing, but a dedicated ENTER button would be grand.2.  A more secure lock for back panel.  When pushing the pointer button up (cursor to top of screen), the back battery panel has a tendency to open.  This is slightly annoying.  Should consider a small plastic tab like a lot of TV/stereo remotes have.Still, I think it is a well designed product and elect to give it 5 stars overall, especially for the great functional range.

In the beginning there were no staples and if you do not have any S.F.4 Swingline Staples, please spring for a box of them.  I paid a little over $3 for 5,000 of them from Amazon.  While waiting for them to arrive, I attempted to use a rack of B8 staples and they do not work.Now, let me rave about the Swingline LightTouch stapler.  It is indeed light and it takes so little effort to complete up to a 20+ page stapling job.  (I stopped checking at 22 sheets, because the staples are not long enough to penetrate much thicker paper.)  Then I thought back and cannot recall the last time I had to staple anything that exceeded 20 sheets of paper.The head or where I put my hand to push is large and that aides the stapling.  The physical body is at first glance bulky but that is a favorable factor.  My old, Viet Nam stapler is small, light and ineffective except for being able to staple 3 or 4 sheets with some effort.  While the 'art' of stapling is moderately intuitive it did not arrive with instructions.  Opening it full width so that it can be used for a tacker requires patience and a modicum of hand strength.  Once there it tacks well.  Many of the old time staplers came with a staple remover, usually on the outside near the rear of the body; however, this stapler has none or if it does I cvould not locate anything that resembled one.  So what, it is a fine stapler and does a superb job.  If it lasts as long as my old one I'll be happy.

This is the largest printer I have ever owned.  It won't even fit in the printer cabinet that every other printer has gone into.  Fortunately, it's wireless, so I can store it anywhere.  Right now, it sits under an unused desk and takes up most of that space.SETUPSetup was extremely easy.  I just turned it on and it practically ran itself.  It even told me I forgot to take out the packing material from inside.  There's an installation disk for the PC.  Wish I didn't have to go that route, but they all seem to have that and it was relatively painless.I set up my HTC One by scanning the QC code and that was very simple.This was the most user friendly setup I've ever encountered in a wireless printer.  Nice.SCANNINGThere's dual-sided scanning, and a document feeder.  I always use the document feeder.  Scanning to computer is ultra slow.  It would do in a pinch, but I would buy a dedicated document scanner if you have to do more than the occasional scan.Scanning to print is much quicker.  It can do double-sided scanning to double-sided print.  Cool.PRINTINGThere's double-sided printing and large format printing.  Two paper trays, so we don't have to keep changing the paper.  I keep letter size paper on top and 11" x 17" paper on the bottom.Printing is so fast and the quality is very good.  I tested a photo on printer paper and there was no pixilation, lines, nor flatness to my photo.  The ink did not smudge.MEMORY CARDThe beauty of the touchscreen is I can see the photos right on the screen using my SD card and flash drive.  I don't need the computer and I don't need to remember what file number to print.  It's right there.The only caveat is it reads only JPEG and TIFF.  If you use any other format, it will not print.OTHER CONSIDERATIONSThis printer has a fax feature I have not used because I have no one to fax.  Nice to know it's there, though.I have three other Epson printers, including an Epson Workforce 7010.  They all use the same ink tank.  This one doesn't.  It uses 252 ink cartridge.  Sadness that I have to stock more than one type of ink in the house.PROS:+ two front paper trays plus one paper feeder in back+ large format capable+ document feeder tray on top+ easy setup+ faxing+ Wi-Fi network capable+ print from mobile devices+ automatic double-sided printing+ automatic double-sided scanning+ touchscreen display+ fast startup+ fast printing, good quality+ print from memory cards or flash driveCONS:- very large and heavy- scan to computer file is very slowOVERALL IMPRESSIONI like it, except for the size.  It does everything I ever want a printer to do, but I wish it was smaller.  It is ideal for businesses or anyone who has room to fit it.

I've only owned one label maker before this one, so I haven't done a comprehensive review of all that is out there.But I really love some of the features of this one:- Rechargeable battery- Detailed graphic display to preview the label before printing- 6 different font sizes to print with- Ability to save commonly used labels and recall with "one-touch" button- Can be held in one hand- Printing/cutting wastes very little label tape (others waste a lot!)Only a few cons:- Have to scroll through the on-screen menu to access most symbols- Limited selection of fonts- Weird/small keys for the numbers, somewhat hard to push down- Non QWERTY keypad

If you have a list of mailings to send and are ready to print address labels you'll want reliable label sheets.  That's what Avery offers with this item.  Just prepare the labels in your Office software and set the template for Avery 5160 - then with these sheets loaded you can print and have these ready to peel off and slap on the envelopes.  This item contains enough labels to last awhile.  These kinds of labels can be used for a variety of projects, not just for mailing addresses.  Avery is a leader in offering convenient office supplies - this address label package is one of many of their offerings that you'll find useful.

The Epson Expression Premium 810 was surprisingly easy to install.  It was wired to an 12 year old desktop running Windows XP along with simple, intuitive installations via WiFi to laptops running Windows 7 and 8 and an Ipad,  The Ipad required the download of an app, but it was easy.  The printing was clear and the colors bright on regular paper.  I have not yet tried to print a photo. The only downside to this printer is the cost of the ink, as with all inexpensive printers these days.  Although it does have the benefit of each color or black cartridge can be purchased separately.  Even so, a complete change over is about $65 using Epson cartridges.

Whether you work in an office or have files in your home, if you're like me you go through piles of folders.  Every now and then I need to replace one because it's either worn out or I want to change the labeling.  For example, when I'm tucking away my tax receipts I need a new folder every year.  Once I'm done using the folder I can turn it around to label it, but can only do that so many times.  The tabs on the Smead folders are most certainly larger.  They are 1/4" wider and taller than the ones I usually use.There's no problem now if I want to write more on the tab.  Some things just need a bit more space than others.  For example, you will be able to add things like the complete date on a tab instead of having to go through several folders to find the one you want.  Keep in mind these tabs have an erasable section, but you'll need something like thePentel Hi-Polymer Block Erasersin order to make full use of them.  You are buying folders and if you use the wrong eraser it's not the fault of the folder.Almost everyone has permanent markers around the house, but the fact that the Pentels are an Amazon Add-On makes them easy to put into your cart.  Do they work?  Yes, and quite well.  I wrote on a folder and then used a polymer eraser to remove what I had written.  If I let it set a bit I had no problem.  If I tried to erase immediately I had a bit of smearing.  With normal use, you most likely won't be immediately erasing so that's not going to be an issue.  If you need hanging folders, Smead also offers the erasableFastab Hanging folders(assorted sizes) with built-in erasable tabs.  These are great "SuperTab Folders" that are step-savers and very user-friendly.
It's hard to get quad rule paper.  I was glad to find this, and while it's not cheap, it's a better buy than driving all over town looking for it.
I thought these were the B2B gel pens when I ordered them. my mistake. But I kept them because they are partially recycled. But no one likes to write with them

You must use these pencils for a while before you make up your mind.  My initial thought upon just looking at them were that they were a little clunky looking; however, upon using them for a while, the shape, size and form of them are really well thought out.  The pencil lead gets better once you've used them for a while.  The first few writings were a bit thick because of the chopped off lead.  The lead is thick and it makes that cut off top even more prominent because of it.  I actually tilted the pencil to the side and did a rubbing to make the tip have a bit of a point.  That little extra step made writing much nicer.If you have a heavy hand when writing, which my husband is, you will be gleeful when you realize that you cannot easily break this lead like most other leads.The only improvement I can recommend is that the pencil eraser be made of a different material.  It doesn't erase well enough for me.  It appears more to blend the lead into the paper than actually erase it.  This could be because the lead is so much thicker and more lead is actually deposited onto the paper.  Maybe one of the white erasers would do a better job.Overall, a very nice mechanical pencil.

I got this 23.2-inch organizer and the 11.375-inch model too. Both fit perfectly into my file cabinet, but I prefer the 11.375 organizer because the spacing between the wire spacers is smaller. I put just one folder in each space so that they stand up straight, making the folder label very easy to see and identify. I ordered another 11.375 organizer to put in the same file cabinet drawer. I have the 23.2 incher down below in the lower drawer for bigger file folders like ones stuffed with old letters and product manuals, as well as folders I don't access very often so I can bunch them together with other folders in the same space. It's not as easy to identify them that way, because they tend to lean into each other, but if they're folders you don't access very often it doesn't matter and the folders take up less space.

These stickies are not your grandfather's stickies.  The stickies, which measure 2 X 3 1/2 inches, are sticky over almost the entire backing.  Gone are the days when you have to post your sticky but add some Scotch tape to ensure that the sticky will stay in position. The kit comes with four pads.  Two of them are chartreuse colored.  The other two are flaming pink.  These bright colors scream out and ensure that all potential readers take notice.An interesting feature of these stickies is that one border is devoid of stickiness.  This makes it easy for the user to grasp each paper, and remove it from the pad.  Moreover, the narrow border region is perforated, for those users who have a need for the entire backing of the sticky to be in direct-contact with the target surface.  On the other hand, the user has the option of leaving the perforated border intact, and in this case, the adhering sticky will have a narrow region that flops about because it has no sticky backing.The container (bag) has a re-sealable zipper.  It is the same kind of re-sealable zipper that you find on grated cheese products from the grocery store.  The advantate of this bag is that you will never lose your pads of stickies.  They are all safely in the bag.  It is my guess that the bag will also maintain shelf-life of your sticky pads.

I was provided a set of Shacke Magnetic Push Pins for testing and review and was asked only to give my honest review, so this is what I found.What You Should Know Before You Buy:♦ Very strong magnets for their small size.  They give a satisfying little snap when attaching to metal.♦ This is a set of 24 in 6 different colors (white, black, red, orange, yellow and blue).  Four of each color.♦ They are slightly larger than standard push pins.♦ These types of strong magnets are not toys and can catch little fingers if not careful.♦ They should be kept away from anything that is sensitive to magnets (computers, phones, TV's, etc.)Conclusion:These are great, high quality magnets in a great design.  They are easy to use because of the size and shape.  They are perfect for your fridge, or a metal hanging file like I have on my wall.  The magnets are incredibly strong and can hold up a lot for their tiny size.  If you are looking for some strong, push-pin style magnets, these are a great choice.  Highly Recommended!

I have medium-sized hands, and find these pens too thin. They are not as comfortable as a regular size pen and are harder to hold. In addition, the plastic is very cheap looking.They write very smoothly, however. I can see these being good for school children as they might be a better fit for their small hands. You also don't have to worry about them being lost as they are economical. But for adults, you are better off getting normal-sized pens.

We've moved on from the thick mousepads of yesterday and graduated to what's more functional-- thin. You don't hit the edge of the wall on this, and it works great with optical mice. Many thing mouse pads are plastic top and cause issues with optical mice.A good price and works as expected.

As others have pointed out, this lapdesk is plastic, cracks and breaks easily (this is my 3rd), does not provide much insulation, and is nothing special.  That's why I much prefer it to the expensive and expansive all-wood lap-desks that I've received as gifts.  They're large, cumbersome (lousy traveling companions), they're never there when you need them, and when they are present they're simply too large, unwieldy (often because of accessories that are missing or malfunctional) and user-unfriendly to present themselves as preferable alternatives to computing on one's own God-given desk-less lap.The pictured lap desk is simply light (weightless, practically), quick and handy.  And if you still occasionally write notes (some correspondents prefer them to word processed-documents--bad penmanship is no excuse), this is the one to have.  The cushioning on the bottom may not be ample but it's adequate, and it's securely attached to the plastic slab--adjustments are never needed.My only reservation is the price, which is twice that of the similar ones I used to go through (a year's use is good).  On the other hand, recently I haven't seen anything as good for less.

No longer will I have to go cubicle to cubicle trying to figure out who "borrowed" (without returning) my stapler! No more! With its fashionable blue leaf pattern, it will be visually obvious as I search the office to find out who stole my stapler. No more sneaking into cubicles and checking the bottom of the stapler for the label with my name on it. Now, it will be obvious. You won't be able to get away with stealing my stapler! No more begging the office supply manager for yet another stapler.This Swingline is plastic, not metal, and is lighter than one would expect. These dry-erase markers are really nice!  They have a fine point, so you can use it in tight places like dry-erase calendars, and they're great for color-coding.  They maintain a good inkflow instead of getting tired out halfway through a word (so far). Also, I didn't notice any odor from these markers, unless I practically shoved them up my nose and took a big whiff, which I don't think is something one would do when using this product in a normal fashion.  I like these!

Identity Theft often happens through your mail or in your mailbox. Always shred your financial documents.Put the mail out if it applies in your town close to when the mailman comes. Write with an indelible pen so they cannot wash your checks.Reveal-N-Seal envelopes also are a must to protect against prying eyes.Jay Adler

We have had this phone system since it first came out over 5 years ago.  It is the best wireless phone network we have ever owned. Being able to print wide format 11 x 17 borderless is great, and the printer does an acceptable job at prints up to this size, although I still like Canon colors better, they seem more true to my eye. Epson has a tendency to "pop" reds and greens, and some people like this because it seems to make some pictures look brighter and crisper, but I like colors to come out more true to life, so I'm having to fuss with my settings in Photoshop and Lightroom to make that happen with the Epson. I also like Canon inks because all the colors have the same sheen on glossy photo paper. Epson inks show less gloss in the blacks, which is visible when looking at the photo from a bit of an angle. I also had one 11x17" print with some slight streaking, not to the point of being visible from more than 6" away, but definitely there when you're looking at the image close-up.So, yes, it's great to have a big format printer, but it only scans 8.5" x 11"? Why have all that extra space just for printing when they could have easily made the scanner bed large also? If you have a need for a larger format printer, you're probably going to want the ability to scan larger documents also.This printer also seems to use more ink (or has smaller ink cartridges) than my Canon Pixma MX922, which isn't exactly an ink miser itself. I've used up the original cartridges printing eight 11 x 17 images and a variety of other basic documents in the past 10 days, and the ink levels on the new (Epson OEM brand) cartridges are already down about 20% after printing five 4x6" and one 8.5x11" photo.Scanning is relatively quick and results are equal to all the other scanners I've owned over the past few years. The "innovative" scanner lid isn't exactly a new thing, we had copiers back in the 1980's that had rubber lids that were actually great for copying books, this bi-fold lid does a little better at holding down books, but not enough of an upgrade to call it "innovative".Copying is simple and quick, and the document feeder works well.The touch screen feels good, works well, and the menus are relatively quick to navigate.The overall look and feel of the machine are pretty much what you expect from any printer today, sleek looks but paper trays and other accessories feel exceptionally lightweight and cheap.Setup and wi-fi connection were quick and easy.I'd actually give this 3.5 stars if possible. I think it deserves more than 3 stars, but the lack of wide format scanning and only moderately impressive photo quality don't really deserve four stars. That said, if it did have a wide format scanner and was available in the same price range, I'd definitely give it 5 stars.

I was SO happy to find these in this size (2 inch round). They fit perfectly on my tins for my lotion bars and look wonderful. very happy with this purchase.. there are enough card spaces and overall its compact and stylish! i would recommend this to others

I've used Post It Notes for years.  I always keep a pad by my computer.  What I like about this product is, first of all it came in a set of 2, in my 2 favorite colors of hot pink and hot blue, the color of the notes, as well as the base and back of the dispenser.Secondly, the dispenser is thin so it doesn't take up any room, so I just have it on my desk, but you also have the option of mounting it on a wall if you so choose. The last time I was impressed by a printer was 1992 when I saw a 600 dpi printing coming out from an HP LaserJet 4.  I cannot believe I could make professional  quality printing at home.  Ever since, there have been many breakthroughs in the printer technology including a high resolution color printing, I have not been  surprised much. Finally, I meet a printer that makes me amazed and it is the Epson Artisan 800.  Here is the story I have for you.When I first got the printer, I was surprised by its size and look.  It is big and beautiful.  The color LCD touch screen is gorgeous and is very intuitive.  The  motorized CD/DVD tray is cool and the finish of every angle of the printer is awesome.  What I like most about this printer is its wireless capability.  I print wirelessly, copy wirelessly, and scan wirelessly.  I can put this printer anywhere in my house and my family really likes it.  The setup for the wireless connection is pretty straightforward.  If  you know about your wireless network (security setting and SSID), you can do it by using the menu on the LCD display.  Once I put all the wireless network information by using the LCD menu, it is recognized by the installer as if it is connected by a cable.  The installer works great and is very easy to follow.  And this printer does all of its jobs without connecting to a computer.  Specially, a scan-to-memory card feature is my favorite.  By plugging a memory card (SD, SDHC, MMC, CF, or  a USB thumb drive), a document or a picture can be scanned and stored in a memory card in either a JPG or a PDF format.  This is so convenient.  I could convert any document I have to a PDF file with just a push of a button and the files are saved in a memory card.  I could do this job by using other scanners that I have, however, there are several steps that I have to follow to do the same job.  My wife, who is not computer-savvy, can scan and convert a document without my help.  She does not need to ask me any more to scan her documents.The Epson Artisan 800 comes with all the ink cartridges full.  I know that most of inkjet printers come with cartridges that are less than half full.  And it has an additonal black cartridge as a spare.  I really like Epson's consideration to give one more black ink cartridge.  There are 5 color ink cartridges that are separate so you can buy an individual color when it is out.  The color printing on a 4 X 6 photo glossy paper is breathtaking.  Although I know  that the photo inkjet printer these days can produce outstanding results, I am still amazed by the quality coming out from the Artisan 800.  I tested the photo printing by spilling the water on it and yes, it is water proof.  I used a premium photo glossy paper from Epson and it worked beautifully.  I do not understand why the other reviewer got such a miserable result.  I used a default setting and pushed a button on LCD screen to print out from the memory card directly from my digital camera.  And the result was one of the best I have ever seen.  I compared a photo from the Artisan 800 with the photo came from the Canon Pixma MP610 side by side and the photo from the Artisan 800 is a little more yellowish and darker if I insist to find the difference.  However, the quality of the picture is amazing and many of my friends were surprised by the quality (I printed many pictures and gave those to my friends as gifts).The feature that I also like is a CD/DVD printing.  I ordered a printable DVD from Verbatim and it produced remarkable results. The printing on the DVD dried very quickly and it never got smudged. The CD/DVD printing software that came with the Artisan 800 is not the best but it is OK to use.  Most of my friends that I showed the printed DVD thought that the DVD was pressed from the factory.  It is that good.However, the Artisan 800 is not perfect.  It still jams paper sometimes, not frequently though.  And sometimes it gets frozen when I insert a USB memory stick.  It seems like it gets frozen while it is reading many files that are not recognized by the Artisan 800, however, I am not 100% sure.  Once it gets frozen, I have to power cycle it.  And scan-to-email and scan-to-PC only work when the Artisan 800 is connected by the USB cable. Because of these reasons, I give 4 stars, not 5 stars for this product.Overall, this is the best printer I have owned so far.  I have had many printers at home and at work and no other printer amazes me like the Artisan 800.  I have never had any printer that leaves all my family members impressed.  My 8 years old daughter loves to play slideshows on a beautiful LCD screen and my son likes to use the scan-to-memory card feature to send his homework assignment to a friend who forgot the sheet.  I heartly recommend this printer to any one who is looking for an all-in-one printer that does all the job wirelessly and flawlessly.

Much more durable than I thought it  would be. At first I thought I would use it on my desk for all of the normal functions-holding pencils, pens, etc...which it does but then I split it in half and realized it has magnets on the back so I now have it on the side of my Dell computer collecting all sorts of goodies. I'm a big Epson printer fan and have had many models over the years. I finally get to have a large format from them now. The printer is able to handle 13x19 size paper and can scan 11x17 paper. WOW!! Purchased from Asus and Panasonic Specialists. The printer is excellent. I love all the features like automatic duplex (dual side) scanning and printing. My wife is enjoying this sketch book very much. The paper is very nice quality and it is great to have a sketch book in a larger format.

Although I could not think of a reason why I needed this product, I use a lot of sticky notes and was intrigued by the idea of them being "see-through". I got these boxes to store old tax files and old financial documents that are taking up too much space in my large filing cabinets and I'm very pleased with them! In my younger, less gray haired years, I took many, MANY, 35mm shots of my travels throughout the U.S. and Europe. HIGHLAND PRODUCTS"Highland" is a brand under which 3M sells products which fail quality control, overruns of special products (e.g., made to military specifications), and overruns of industrial products not meant for retail sale.  Therefore, "Highland" products are only intermittently available in retail outlets.  Many (failed quality control) Highland products sell for half the price of corresponding "Post-it" or "Scotch" equivalents, and are usually of the same quality (except for the reason they failed, if any).  The over-runs and industrial product are usually first quality---but maybe not exactly what you were expecting.SHORTCOMINGS> I've bought packs of Highland pads which were poorly cut and not perfectly square.> Some packs have "lines" on the cut edges---evidence of a dull or dirty cutting machine>> Obviously if the pads are just cut poorly, that is probably the only defect---and otherwise the pads are perfect "Post-its"> Many batches Highland notes are less sticky than "Post-its".  "Less sticky" is the worst "defect" I've ever found in a Highland pad.> I'm not sure if it is a fair generalization that Highland notes are usually a fainter yellow, because I've purchased Post-its just as faint.> At least half the packs of Highland pads I've bought have been indistinguishable from corresponding Post-its.  I suspect that entire batchs (or "runs") of Post-its are "condemned" if a defect is discovered with any part of the batch.SOMETIMES "LESS STICKY" IS A GOOD FEATURE> Some batches of Post-its are so sticky that they are hard to pull off the pad.  With larger pads that isn't so much an issue.  With these tiny pads, it is---the pads are hard to write on (because the pad is much higher than the surface your writing hand is on).  So, the normal thing to do is pull on off the pad then write on it, but they curl up as you pull them off the pad, and the stickier they are the more they curl. If, to overcome the curling, you stick them hard to your desk to write on, you compromise their stickiness.  Arguably, for these small notes, the less sticky Highland version are more convenient (because they don't curl up so badly as you pull them off the pad, so you don't have to stick them to your desk to write on them).> Very sticky Post-its used as bookmarks can be hard to remove---sometimes impossible to remove from newsprint (including cheap "paperback" books) without damage.  Arguably, the less sticky Highland version are more convenient for use as temporary bookmarkers. (Albeit: You can intentionally reduce the stickiness of Post-its, if you want to, by sticking them to your hand first.)> In my experience, you can't depend even on a true-branded "Post it" to stick when you really need it to stick.  So, when I need a note to absolutely stick until I take it down---I tape it up with Scotch blue painters tapeScotchBlue Painter's Tape for Multi-Surfaces 2090-.75A, 3/4 Inches by 60 Yards, 1 Roll.  If you think blue painters tape is just for painting, think again, it is amazing stuff with hundreds of uses.EVALUATIONIf you can get Highland pads for half-the-price of Post-its, then they are usually worth buying.  To some extent whether Highland pads are acceptable substitutes for you, it depends on how you use the notes.  I mostly use the notepads for general reminder-note taking, rarely sticking them up to a bulletin board (or refrigerator)---so the Highland pads work just as well for me, even if I get a "less sticky" batch.VALUEChances are at least 50:50 that you'll get pads indistinguishable from Post-its.  So, at half the price of Post-its, you can't loose.  And that doesn't count the fact that the "defects" (if any) may not matter to you.  So, at the typical 1/2-the-price-of-Post-its price, Highland notes are a bargain.  However, Amazon prices don't always follow this rule.  Currently, the Highland notes are $4.99.  Until recently, the corresponding Post-its were over $10, making the Highland notes a bargain.  But currently, the corresponding Post-its are $5.49 from Amazon---I'd probably go with the Post-its.Post-it Notes, Original Pad, 1-3/8 Inches x 1-7/8 Inches, Canary Yellow, 12 Pads per PackTRIVIANote the name "Highland" means "Scotland".  "Scotch" is the brand 3M uses for most of its tape products.  "Scotch" is synonymous with (to be as inoffensive as possible) "thrifty"---which is clearly the implication of "Highland".  I happen to be "thrifty" and of Scotch ancestry (the Bruce clan), so I'm "allowed" to mention things like this.

I had a Fellowes shredder that I purchased hereFellowes Powershred W-11C 11 Sheet Cross-Cut Shredder (3103201)about 7 months ago so I was happy to compare this Swingline shredder.  Boy, what an improvement!!  Here's what is so much better on this one:1) It can truly handle 12 sheets of paper without slowing down.  I am shredding old financial documents and I always remove staples no matter what, but this shredder actually shreds 12 sheets with ease.2) The removable bin is SO EASY to use -- I simply pull out the bin while the shredder stays stationary.  The Fellowes was a pain because  I had to remove the top shredder part to empty the basket beneath it, usually spilling some paper along the way, then placing it somewhere while I emptied the basket and then placed the shredder back on top.3) The window shows when I'm filling up the basket; no guessing and having to lift up the shredder top to see how full the basket below it.4) The ability to shred CDs and credit cards is nice, although I probably won't be shredding any CDs soon.  And so I've removed the CD receptacle inside the bin to give me more space for paper shredding.5) The styling is sleek and I can place it against the wall horizontally so it takes up less room in my office.  And because it is heavy it doesn't want to tip over easily.6) I like that it has an "overheat signal" but I just shredded pretty continuously for about 20 minutes and had NO problem.  I did have little pauses while I removed some staples or a stray paper clip but this thing ran great.Yes, it is quite expensive, and I will definitely update in 6 months.  One thing I learned the hard way two shredders ago:  definitely buy the recommended shredder lubricant and use it.UPDATE 2/5/12:This shredder has definitely met my expectations in terms of continuous shredding time.  However, I wish there was some kind of WARNING LIGHT to notify me when I need to empty the bin.  More than a few times I've been going along, and then remember to check the bin--only to discover that it is a bit over-full.  Then I shut if off, and have to slip my hand & arm in the bin and pull down the shreddings before I can remove the bin all the way.  Invariably, it drops some shreddings in the bottom which I then have to scoop out by hand before replacing the bin.Also, it would be much better to have the entire shredder the silver color instead of black on top, since the process of shredding produces a lot of fine white dust which looks awful coated all over the shredder; the silver color would make that much less noticeable.UPDATE 3/1/12:I purchased a Fellowes Powershredc 79Ci for the office.  It's $30 more than this Swingline--at least here on Amazon--but to me it's more than worth the extra money.  It's much quieter; it DOES have an indicator light to let you know when the bin needs to be emptied and it won't shred until you either push down on the shreddings or empty the receptacle; and it even has indicator light to warn you if you are trying to shred too many sheets of paper at once.  For my money, there is no comparison--Fellowes Powershred 79Ci is the one to buy.

The Fellows Pulsar Plus 300 Manual Comb Binding Machine (I wonder who comes up with these names... Is there a plain Pulsar?  A Pulsar Minus?  How about a Plus 299??) is, as the name says, a manual comb binding machine.  It's very easy to use.  You stick the paper in the top slot, making sure to align the left edge with the positioning stop, and pull the long lever.  (It takes a bit of force if you're punching more than ten sheets, but I've tested it with the rated eighteen sheets and it works fine.)  You then place the proper size comb behind the vertical pins and pull the short lever to open the comb rings.  Drop the punched paper over the opened comb teeth and lift up on the short lever to close the comb.  Voila!  Instant binding.The base has a tray for comb storage, along with a handy-dandy comb size measuring tool.  To keep the janitorial staff happy and crud off the floor, there's also a tray to hold the punching chaff.If you have moderate binding needs, this is an ideal machine for your office.  If you're doing a lot of binding, you might consider the next size up or an electric version.  OTOH, this will still work after aliens attack and destroy the power grid.Highly Recommended.

Sharpie Accent Gel Highlighters are excellent for use on light-weight papers such as those used in Bibles.  They do not bleed through to the other side of the page on which you are highlighting text.  Further, the markers do not spread out as do liquid markers, but highlight only the area chosen.  The gel highlighters also do an excellent job on slick papers that are used for magazines; they do not smear since they go on dry.  Sharpie Accent Gel Highlighters do not dry out when the cap is left off; I've done so for over a week just to test this claim.If I like these highlighters so well, why do you ask did I not award them five stars.  These markers are essentially translucent crayons.  If used on heavier papers such as those in textbooks, they highlight unevenly.  The texture of the paper is very visible to the naked eye and, if one likes evenly colored highlighting, is a distraction.  The highlighter consists of only 1/4" of the gel material; any individual with a heavy hand will quickly wear it down to the end.I recommend the Sharpie Accent Gel Highlighters for use on light-weight or slick papers, but cannot recommend them for regular, frequent use.  They are an expensive alternative for everyday highlighting and, thus, receive only four stars from me.

Parker pens have been a staple in my pen-collecting life from the beginning. This, the JOTTER model, is an absolute must for any serious Great Old School writers. It's up there with theFisher Space Original Astronaut Space PenorFisher Cap-O-Matic S200 Chrome Cap w/ Black Barrel Ballpoint Pen - S251BKand the immortalCross Classic Century, Lustrous Chrome, Ballpoint Pen (3502)(which in my aristocratic youth was a gift to show a boy had become a man).The Jotter is interesting because of its heft and excellent 1950s construction. I own several, one in chrome and the rest like this one, with the half plastic barrel. The Jotter, at exactly 5" in length and a bit chubbier than most pens, is an excellent, non-fatiguing ballpoint pen. It is the opposite, for example, of the now-unavailable old Papermate Stick, which is just over 6" in length (and thinner than a No. 2 pencil).Something I have noted from other customers is they are addicted to the retraction (clicking) mechanism of a pen. Parkers have a tendency to 'slip' or malfunction a bit, due to the fact that a Parker refill is configured funny, almost like a "key" that fits into the cap's "lock".Aside from that little freak-out, a Parker will really be the only pen you'll ever need. I have to say, my sister bought me one as a gift, and the refill in it lasted for over a decade. It was the only pen I wrote with - it was really a bit scary. That was an all-chrome satin textured model Jotter. It never quit on me or wore out in any way: it was stolen at almost 11 years of age. (The PEN, not me, dummy!)The only warning I will offer in all seriousness is you may find it difficult to find genuine ordinary ballpoint refills for it; Parker seems to be leaning hard to get people to buy their Parker Gel refills, which are excellent but they last about 2 weeks!Since this is about a pen, I must get on my soapbox. Schools are poised to cut out teaching cursive altogether, instead training children to type on computers. Penmanship is already down the toilet - why teach it? The PC is the new "notebook".Anyone familiar with the Good Old School - I am a proud alumnus - knows that we obsess about the quality of our paper, notebooks, pens and pencils. Think it is insignificant? Think again: every law enforcement officer is issued a notebook which is numbered and catalogued. Military branches have something similar to this practice. This is a vital element of the practice of the authoritative professions.Reporters, both media and court, are even pickier about the writing implements they use. They all file their notebooks, for future reference among other reasons. Scientists are no different and file their hand-written field data plus other research along with the transcripts. Authors and even poets are extremely picky about it too, if they are the Old Schoolers. Yep: it IS that important.So it ought to be as important to the ordinary person, the civilian who is not an author, reporter or scientist, because what you have to note is no less important! Always give this some thought before buying any stationary - especially your pen.As one very excellent reviewer here wrote, a great pen boosts your morale at work, makes you feel enthusiastic about writing, and even encourages your colleagues/clients when you need them to sign something. Just don't fall prey to the Biggest Scholastic Evil in the World: having your favorite pen stolen.

I have a lot of paperwork at my job site and within my home.  I use colored folders to prioritize paperwork for filing and to distinguish work projects.  The clear nature of the folders makes it easy to quickly ensure that I have selected the appropriate file.  I appreciate that these are readily reusable.  I've been using them for several weeks and I haven't had a folder tear (most of my folders have less than 20 sheets in each). I like that I can use a pencil to write on the tabs and then erase the project heading when I need to change it.While I think these are great for facilitating organization in the home or office, I would point out the following:1) These are not made for 100 sheets of paper -- The product description claims that 100 sheets fit in a folder.  Yes, the papers fit but not securely.  To keep the papers from spilling, be prepared to harness a binder clip on the outside of the project folder.2) I would have liked more utility -- I like traditional sheet protectors because I can file them in binders.  What I don't like about traditional sheet protectors is trying to remove the sheets of paper when I need them. These project folders easily permit the removal of paper because they are open on two sides.  Sheet protectors are usually completely clear.  The colored features of the C-line product allows projects to be quickly identified, which is why I wish I could file them in a binder.  When flipping through a binder, I would love to be able to find the colored section pertinent to my needs and remove the project needed folder and/or material.3) All the tabs are the same height -- If you only use the 25 folders that come in the box, it is probably going to be easy to quickly flip to a colored folder and identify whether it is the project you need.  If you are seeking to employ 100 of these, additional identifying features would be a plus -- like staggered tabs.  Because all of the tabs are the same height, the colored folders blend together.4) Not green -- Polypropylene, while durable, is not readily recyclable in most communities.  Additionally, C-line makes project folders that come from recycled sources, but this particular product does not appear to have been created from recycled components.This product is made in China.

I print a lot of copies for my writing and research work. I was using a basic laser printer, very cheap toner and so very user friendly to me. But it didn't have a lot of flexibility. I had to use another printer for scanning and copying, and have been looking for something to do double sided printing, so as to save paper.This printer fit the bill perfectly. It was easy to set up and easy to use. This model doesn't have the wireless access of other models, but I didn't need that.  It can be networked, however, so that is enough for me.It has a pretty small footprint for its capabilities.  Everything is tightly packaged and engineered so that there's no wasted space. It is very functional and works great in all of its capacities that I used it for.  It was my go to printer, the one that I used the most (I have about 4 other printers each with their own speciality).  This is an all around workhorse--not the best at any particular job, but competent at a lot. I even was able--in this day and age--to use the fax feature.  Had to fax a form to our insurance company.  Plugged it into the phone line, dialed the number, everything worked quickly, smoothly with absolutely no bumps.  This printer really is just plain easy to use.My one complaint about the printer itself is that it's really surgey.  Meaning that when it turns on, it really draws in a lot of power. I couldn't plug it into my UPS because of that. It kept tripping the power circuit.  We have an old house and my office is an old add-on room off the side.  So the wiring isn't the best. When I turn this printer on, it has a tendency to trip the circuit breaker at times, and otherwise affect other things that are plugged in. I've not had that problem with other printers or devices.Still, the bother was worth it to me. I liked this printer a lot. Note my use of the past tense.The trouble I am now running into is not really one connected to the printer itself. But it radically affects my use of the printer.  I am a PhD student and adjunct professor. My home office budget, thus, is pretty bare bones.  While I need functional equipment, I can't pay the frankly outrageous prices charged for the manufacturer's stock toner.  I've long relied on other manufacturers who make generic brand toners and cartridges for my printeres.  So, when after printing about 1200+ pages the toner that this printer came with needed to be replaced and I looked on Amazon for generic substitutes. Found one, got it, installed it. The printer didn't recognize it. Called the company (Inkers). They were great, said I had the right model of cartridge, so they sent me another one. That one didn't work either (got refund quick by the company). Tried another brand.  Also didn't work. Cartridge fit, but the chip wasn't right. Tried a refill company. The replacement chip they sent also didn't work.Meaning I can't find a cheaper generic toner for this printer and I can't quite get to paying the full toner price. So, for now, this printer sits unplugged and unused.ADDED (April, 2013): First an update about the generic toner. They seem to have worked that out, so now I can print using the cheaper toner. However, I've run into another problem. If you're printing large amounts, this printer really starts slowing down. I'm printing out my dissertation, and when it hit 140 pages, it apparently overheats and prints five pages, stops for about 12 seconds, then prints another 5 pages, stops for 12 seconds.  So, this really makes printing out long documents extremely time consuming.  Given that I need to print out 5 copies of my 332 page dissertation, it means I really, really don't like this printer right now.

Epson is a top-notch name in scanners.  I have been using an Epson v500 photo scanner for home use for the past 5 years, and we have had zero problems with it, so when I had a chance to check out the Epson V370 I thought, sure, let's see what it can do.First of all, if you have used Epson desktop flatbed scanners before the controls and control screens will look very familiar...er...probably mostly identical to what you are used to.All right, I'm getting ahead of myself.  First things first...What you get in the box.  You get the Epson V370 flatbed scanner, two compact discs containing drivers and program files for the scanner (one for Apples and one for PCs) a 3-prong power cord, and a USB cable to attach your scanner to your computer, plus a quick start instruction and installation sheet.  Follow it!  Install the software before attaching and powering up your scanner.Anyway, it took about 5 mins to install all of the programs needed to interface with and run the scanner (I have a iMac desktop computer).  I then attached and powered up the scanner, but the computer didn't automatically pull up the control screen.  I had to go into the Applications and activate it manually.  I then added the scanner application icon to my dock for easy access.  Once I got that all arranged I scanned a photograph and then a B/W document, using the fully automatic mode, and the scanner readily identified the document type.The Epson V370 Photo comes with four sets of scanning options: Full Auto Mode, Home Mode, Office Mode, and Professional Mode.Full Auto Mode is exactly that.  You place your document, activate the scanner, and it does the rest.  You can set the document type - Photo/Doc and the resolution between 50-1200 dpi, and the same for film mode (slides, negatives, etc) and 50-1200 dpi.  This mode's default is to automatically send the scanned image to your "Pictures" or "My Pictures" folder - which I frankly found a little annoying.  I want to send things where I want.  But with this option you have to go to the default destination folder find the scanned image (e.g., img001.jpg) and move it where you want it to go.In Home Mode you have more options you can select.  This mode is designed for someone who scans a variety of things and who wants more control over how the scanner works.  In this mode you can select the document type from several different options (photo, newspaper, color positive film, color negative, B/W negative, etc.).  In this mode you can also select the destination for the image...to a degree.  You can choose whether the image goes to your screen at 96 dpi, a printer at 300 dpi, or you can select "Other" and select the resolution at anything between 50-4800 dpi.  You can also choose color, grayscale, or B/W for the output regardless of object type.  You can also do dust removal, backlight correction, color restoration, etc.  This is a good mode for someone who may be doing family history, or scanning family photographs for archival purposes.Office Mode's pre-sets are set up, well, for office-type work.  Figures.  These defaults are set up mainly for scan to print at 50-300 dpi.  You can also control contrast and brightness, but that's pretty much it.Professional Mode is where you can access all the bells and whistles this scanner offers.  You can select image type, e.g., B/W, or 8-48 bit color.  You can set the resolution at anything between 50-12800 dpi, and set the document size.  You can also adjust all of the things listed above, plus color, tone, intensity, set the tone using a tone curve tool, gray balance, etc.The scanning screen is 9x12" (slightly larger than the usual 8.5x11.7" size of most scanners out there.  Though I hardly think that this warrants the claim that it can scan "oversized documents".  It can, however do something that many digital cameras can do and even cell phone cameras can do, and that's stitch together multiple images into one large image.  That's pretty neat, but this is not what I'd call an "oversized document" scanner.The fact that this scanner has a side hinge makes it tougher to scan books as easily as when the lid hinge is at the top of the unit (like in the v500), and the V370 has a larger footprint than the v500, so if you have only a small area for your computer work you might want to take that into account.I'd say that if you are on a budget, that this scanner is worth a serious look.  If you are a professional who relies on top-notch, professional grade scanned images you will probably want to climb the scanner scale to a pricier scanner that produces even better digital images.I'd easily say that this scanner does a 5-star job for a scanner on a budget.Happy scanning!

This scanner is marketed to small businesses, and while I do not happen to run one of those, it does appear to be a really nice item for organizing business expenses.  Since I am very fond of 'tech' of all sorts, I offered to test and review this item.The description says it does not support 64 bit windows, and in fact the included installer CD refused to run on my 64 bit system.  Not to worry though, if you go to their web site ([...]) you can download a 64 bit version.  It installs a database as well as the scanner software.  There is a special piece of paper in the package which is used to calibrate the scanner, and the documentation recommends occasional recalibration, which means you need to NOT lose the paper.  I am not sure what you'd do if you lost it...I guess ask them to send you another one.The NeatWorks software is really nifty.  It interprets the scanned documents, and if they are receipts, it picks out dollar amounts for later use in expense reports.  I did not have any business cards to try, but the application will scan them and produce an update to several types of 'contact list' that you might use.  There is also an option to choose to file an item as a 'document' which means it is largely uninterpreted (though you can do text searches on them.  One suggestion made by the developer is that you file recipes as documents so they can be searched for ingredient lists).I wanted to give this scanner a good test, so I fed in a bunch of stuff just to see how it would be handled.  My results:1) I fed in a grocery receipt that had been folded a few times but wasn't badly crumpled.  This was handled just fine, and the software was easily able to pick out the correct dollar totals.  It even figured out that the receipt was for groceries and tagged it as such.2) An Amazon purchase receipt that was in the box from a network hard drive I recently purchased.  This scanned correctly as 'hardware' but the software read the dollar sign on the total as a '1' and thus added a thousand dollars to the purchase amount!  Yow!  Luckily, this is simple to fix in the application and you are in fact prompted to verify the numbers before they are filed in the database.3) A receipt from a recent American Airlines flight to Texas.  The application did read it as an 'airline' expense, but the dollar totals were completely misread.  Again, I fixed them easily.4) A receipt from a recent trip to Best Buy.  If you've seen BB receipts lately, these are receipts with an attitude!  They've got a lot of 'stuff' printed on them, advertisements, phone numbers, etc.  The scanner processed this perfectly and the software read everything correctly.5) For chuckles, I fed in a MegaMillion lottery ticket (a loser, sadly).  This ticket had really light print on a colored background, and of course it had numbers everywhere.  Not surprisingly, the software was completly flummoxed by this one.  I filed it under 'documents'.6) How about a 20 dollar bill?  It scanned perfectly, and the software indicated it was 'cash' (hee hee) but did not indicate the denomination.7) Since I was testing it, I decided to do something of a stress test.  I took a longish grocery receipt and I crumpled that sucker up BADLY.  Then I flattened it out as best I could and fed it in.  For good measure, as the paper disappeared into the scanner, my cat leapt onto the desk and whacked it.  Now THAT is a test... This receipt did not fare well at all.  It was completely chewed up and caught in the scanner mechanism.  I was afraid I'd done some damage but I picked out the pieces and then got the last of it out of the works by scanning a blank piece of paper.  This jam-clearing exercise was simple to do, since the scanner top pops open at the push of a button to allow access to the internals.  The scanner was undamaged and I fed in another document, which processed just fine.Now I tried out some of the software options...Once the receipts were in the scanner database, there were numerous export options.  I exported to a MS Word document and got a very nice 'expense report'.  An export to Excel gave me an xls file that produced a nice spreadsheet.My final scans really tested the NeatWorks interpretive software, and that application exhibited a level of functionality that might be an indication of why this scanner is so expensive.  I tore a page out of a paperback book (the 'about the author' page at the end, because it contained two different font sizes and some bolding) and scanned it in as a document.  Then I exported it to a PDF and opened that PDF in Adobe reader.  I exported it to a text file and it was a perfect text representation of the words on the page!  I could wish it had the option to export to MS Word format because I can't begin to afford Adobe Acrobat...I then printed out an adobe document I already had on my system, a knitting pattern with smallish text and color pictures.  I scanned the printed document back in and then used the NeatWorks software to export it to PDF.  I ended up with a PDF that looks really close to the original, allowing for some quality loss from printing the color images.All in all, I liked this scanner and as I said, if I were running a small business, I'd find it really useful.  It's also really nice for folks who scan in regular documents because it saves them in a handy database for later searching or printing.The newly added 64 bit support means this will be my 'main' scanner in the future.

Summary: A very handy all purpose mounting tape.Ok, so I'm a tape junkie.  No joke - I must have at least 150-200 different types of tape in the house.  It's amazing what you can make or fix if you have the right tape or glue.  I consider double sided foam tape to be one of the key "Must have" tapes and this 3M/Scotch version is pretty much the gold standard.  Note that this tape does have some "Creep" so I would not rely on it to keep heavy items on a wall or mounted where they are likely to eventually fall.  Tips on use for this tape:1) Works best with clean surfaces2) Does not work well with textured surfaces3) Works better with surfaces that are somewhat flexible4) Does not adhere well if the surface is cold5) The foam is not UV stable - if you use it in an external environment it will yellow and get brittle6) To remove the tape, use a thin wire to cut the foam between the layers of adhesive.  A little bit of WD40 or oil on the wire helps cut through.If you want a tape which is even stronger and suitable for outdoor use, try 3M - Super Strong Automotive Attachment Tape, 1/2" x 60" (03609)Besides masking, duct, scotch and packing, here are some other tapes you may want to consider:Painter's (Blue or Green) masking tape - The blue is much easier to peel off and won't leave adhesive residute while the green gives a much crisper line if spray painting.Aluminum foil tape - what you really want to seal ducts with, also great for high heat or any area you need extra strength.Gaffer's Tape - A stickier version of duct tape with a lot more cloth and a lot less plastic.Fiberglass strapping tape - if you're using this, you better have scissors!Velcro Tape - The underlying adhesive is very very strong, so it works well with textured surfaces - great for securing things you want to take apart later.3M 465 Adhesive Transfer Tape - Basically very strong double stick tape - without  the tape.  Make any decorative paper, fabric, etc into tape.If this review was helpful or if you have any questions / comments, please let me know!

Wood, painted surfaces, some metals, and other non-packing material surfaces do not bond well with this tape.This tape ages well. A lot of other tapes don't store well, or loose or gain stickiness over time.  Some packing tapes can turn into a real mess after a few months in a warm attack.  This tape does not exhibit any of those problems.When shopping for packing tape, I make my selection based on what bad things it doesn't do, rather than seeking any particular 'performance' attributes. They have measure approx. 3" x 3.25" and have 7 lines each with lots more room to write than the old divider Tabs. Also these Post-its have a larger glue surface than I have seen before.  The Note Tabs have glue on 2/3s of the surface so they should be quite secure.2.  Also new to me are the 2 Label Pads in bright pink and green.  Being labels they are fully adhesive and measure 2" x 3".3.  The 1" Tabs(really 1 1/2") are bright transparent pink,green or orange and clear.  The colored part forms the 1/2" Tab and the 1" clear function secures (adhesive coated) but doesn't cover text in your book. The transparent colored Tab doesn't block, or prevent you from reading other Tabs. All three came in one simple clear dispenser and are easy to retrieve and post.4.  There's another single handy clear dispenser for all three Flags: Again, transparent bright Pink, labeled "On Test", bright Green, labeled "To Do",and Blue labeled, "Study".  They are 2" long x 1/2" and you can while slicker than paper, you CAN write on them.  The bottom of the colored part forms an arrow so you can place the Flag to point specifically to a certain section, or even word, all while being able to read the text under the Flag.5.  The third product that comes in a single handy clear dispenser for all five colors are the Arrow Flags. They pop out very easily from the simple, well-designed dispenser.  They also are bright colors on transparent slicker-than-paper, that you can write on, although here there's not much room for that as they measure 1/2" x 1 3/4". The Full Adhesive Notes are like regular Post-its except 3/4 of the paper has an adhesive coating, so they won't curl up.  They measure 3' by 3", and there are approx. 30 sheets.7. There was at least one reviewer who had indicated the price of this lubricant was reasonable.  I am not sure he calculated its cost which is roughly $87.00 per gallon.  At that price it may be cheaper to never lubricate your shredder and just replace it when it wears out.  I am not advocating that you should not lubricate your shredder, but just plain motor oil will be nearly as good and a lot cheaper considering that you can lubricate many items in your home by using an inexpensive oil can filled with inexpensive motor oil.  Some may want to use a light grade in one can and a heavier grade in another, but you can save yourself a lot of money over the years by not buying "special purpose" lubricants when they are not really needed.  Of course you would want to use higher priced synthetic oils like Mobil One in your Ferarri or Mercedes that is required for their warranty, but even that standard for high performance engines is still more than 10 times cheaper than this "Shredder Oil".  Decisions on the use of certain types of oil are not going to make or break you, I am just suggesting putting such small decisions into perspective.  Its similar to the example of the guy who buys a new car every two years and trades his old one in, but he will change his engine oil every 3,000 miles because that's what his father told him to do.  The only reason for changing the oil so often is if you are selling your car to your father who will keep it for years.In conclusion, if it makes you feel better using the "special $87.00 per gallon shredder oil" I think you should do so.  But you may want to acknowledge that at least some of your decision is based upon how you feel as opposed to how you think.

I was excited about upgrading my "all-in-one" printer to this new high performance Wi-fi all-in-one printer. The following will be an ongoing blog on the printer:Day 1:I started installing the software at 8 p.m. At 11 p.m. it was still installing.  I went to bedDay 2:When I got up it hit a stopping point.  I continued to install for another hour and a half.  It rebooted, and then it wanted me to register a number of applications.  After another half hour and no end in sight, I went to work!After almost six hours, it still isn't ready to print, fax, scan...Additionally, I was assuming that since it was "Wifi" ready, that it had its own router.  No.  You will need a wireless router to use the Wifi.  I was able to use my internet router but in a business situation this might not be available.  So take this in mind if that is a reason you are choosing this.While trying to set up the Wifi, the printer could not download information to the computer, so I had to set it up manually!When I got home I started the registering process and more software was added.  Then I found out that some of the software was out of date and had to update it.  The update was date 2009!  Why did the disk not have the most current software?!But after 8 hours of setup and registering, it appears to be ready to test!!I first tried to print using a cable and it worked.  The print quality and color quality are very good.  So far, so good!  Next I wanted to print wirelessly.  I got an error message that the model was incorrect but it printed.  So I am not going to fool around with it anymore, I don't know how many times I tried to fix something minor and wound up screwing up something major.  I will live with getting an error message, as long as it prints!Well, I have not tried to scan or fax yet but I will let you know when I do!!Faxing:I needed to fax some information and decided to use this.It is not simple.  Each funcition (fax, scan, copy) has its own area.  You need to select fax then use the fax part of the dashboard to complete it.  I decided to try it without referring to the instructions.  Most fax machines are very similar.  It took five attempts before I got everything right. The fax appeared to go through and after looking through a couple of menus, I found the one that showed me it went through.  The next day I called the place where I faxed the info and they received it.  Therefore, it appears the fax is fully functional.The downside is that if this is being used in an office, someone could not easily fax something and would need to walked through the process at least once.  Also in the set-up instructions, there was a note that the fax may not be compatable with certain phone service providers including Verizon Fios (which I have but I did not have a problem.  This is just a warning.)Well that leaves scanning!!  Will update again when I use it.
