This label printer is approximately the size of 2 VHS tapes, so it is big but not cumbersome. This is not a stand-alone label-maker and absolutely MUST be tethered to a PC. It is not Mac compatible, although it did run fine on a Mac running Parallels Desktop with Windows 2000. It started up fine on a PC running Windows XP as an external USB drive. If you open it, you will see the stand-alone software, no additional install required.Pros:-Can save label layouts-Laminated labels are nice-Multiple widths nice-One button horizontal to vertical orientation switch-Comes with power adapter, but also uses batteries-Uses computer keyboard and all fonts you can come up with-Labels seem durable - stuck in a freezer at -80 deg C and had no difficulty with peeling or brittlenessCons:-Not Mac compatible-Bulky but can only hold 1 tape at a time-Spits out extra piece of label (almost the size of my 0.95" labels) with each label (-1 Star, even my cheap LetraTag or Brother PT-80 do not do this)-Margins cannot be adjusted down (but can be made wider)-Smallest label size is .95" with a lot of white space-Text easy enough to read, but can see "dots", suitable for barcodes and simple line graphics, but not for pictures-MUST be tethered to a computer - cannot print saved layouts from unitFor home use, I really enjoy my thermal printLetraTag Plus, which can also print on iron-on fabric labels. Honestly, I would continue to recommend the LetraTag for most purposes. However, this is convenient for work, where I have to label dozens of small tubes each day. The fact that I can type text into a pre-formatted and saved label box from my computer versus typing everything out on a small pad is very convenient. If a small keypad or ability to print saved labels from the unit in a stand-alone fashion had been included or had this been Mac compatible, this would be a 4 star item. These laminated labels are durable and continued to stick after freezing (although applied to dry, room temp surface), which could be applicable to home freezer or restaurant usage as well.Edit: Microsoft Plug-ins/Optional PC SoftwareI am less than delighted with the plug-ins. I anticipated being able to format labels for my needs (I print about 30 at a time) and update only the fields (like date and an ID number) that change. I use Excel for tracking and hoped that the plug-ins would update from the Excel formulas. However, be warned - once you have exported your data OUT of Excel or Word onto the label sofware - it will not update if you edit your Microsoft document. You still need to format from the label software as it automatically prints it all on 1 line. You can only export one label at a time to the software (there is no way to make it detect multiple rows as multiple labels, however columns are preserved on the same label). So, I see absolutely no benefit to using the plug-in in Microsoft versus using the installed (from the CD) editing software unless you have tons of data. You can also NOT print say 5 of label 1, 3 of label 2, and one of label 3. You can print 5 of all labels or 1 of all labels, but not independently control them and have them print all at once (to save on the "extra" label it spits out). One good thing about the software, is it does allow you to EDIT the MARGINS and EDIT the SIZE of the label down further!Saving layouts: this would VERY useful for business apps. However, problems have arisen saving multiple layouts. Basically, it opens the last saved layout regardless of the one I am trying to open even though they show correctly in preview mode (thus effectively overwriting my other saved layouts). I have not found a work-around.

Our new headmaster this year favors that all of us teachers use a uniform way of storing our lesson plans, so I switched from the usual spiral-bound planner to the 3-ring binder the school provided.  I inserted the usual dividers for lesson plans and gradebook, and the semester got underway.  But I recently discovered these slash jackets and find that they help me resolve a number of organization issues.First, though they are designed to hold unpunched papers, I find that I can anchor my "go-to" memos (school schedule, "scan-a-score," yearbook staff contact info, etc.) by lining up their punched holes with those of the jackets.  Now I always know where they are and never have to fumble through stacks of paper to find them. And--big bonus!--I can still insert other free-standing papers on top of them.Second, if I have items that I need to remove frequently, I find the slash jackets superior to the plastic sleeves I used before, as the upper right corner of the papers is exposed by the slash, making it easy to whisk them out when needed.Third, since my classes are relatively small, I can print out hand-outs from my home computer in the morning and insert the stack in a slash jacket.  Since I always pull out the notebook first thing upon arrival, I now have my hand-outs immediately accessible so that I no longer have to fumble around in other folders looking for them, and--again--they slip right out since they are not anchored by notebook rings.Fourth, I tutor a part-time student on Friday afternoons.  I can prepare her materials and insert them in a slash jacket, which means I do not need a separate folder for the work of one individual.Fifth, the slash jackets can serve as a "literature display" case.  I can run off a stack of "Requests for Make-up Work," insert them in a slash jacket, and use a punch pin to secure the slash jacket to a bulletin board.  This gives students easy access to what they need without requiring additional expenditures on my part.  (If you teach, you know how much money we teachers spend on our own classrooms every year!)Sixth, the "Student-Family Handbook" for next year has just been printed.  At 53 pages (duplexed), it still fits easily in a slash jacket!Seventh, we use 8 " x 11" green and red papers as signals during a fire drill.  If all students are accounted for, we hold up the green.  If not, red.  I now keep these in a slash jacket as I always grab my binder on the way out of the classroom anyway.  I don't have to fumble through a file folder to find it now, so I am ready to display!Eighth, sometimes I take CDs or DVDs to school with me.  I slip them into the first slash jacket in the binder for quick removal upon arrival.  Even if a disc is in a simple paper cover, the disc is protected and does not break.Well, I could go on, but you get the idea.  These things can really make a teacher's life easier, and I certainly plan to buy more!

Every time I need to buy one of these and stop in my local office store, I am always amazed at how many different varieties of 3-ring binders there are in the world. What is even more amazing is that I actually seem to think about which ones are right for each use.=== The Good Stuff ===* These seem sturdy and well made. The covers are made out of vinyl, and are pulled tightly enough that there is no slop or sag to tear. The "hinges" in the vinyl are made out of what appears to be a thin transparent sheet of plastic or vinyl, and based on previous experience, these are often the first points to fail.* The D-Rings open and close cleanly, and are aligned.* There is a clear cover on both the front and back covers, so you can slip in a sheet of paper to serve as a title or label for the notebook. There is also a flap along the spine for a label (so you can see it on a bookshelf), but this is pretty tight and took a bit of effort to get a strip of paper in there.* There are flaps on the inside of both front and rear covers, so you can hold a few more pages.=== The Not-So-Good Stuff ===* The edges are a little rough, and the clear pouches for the front and back covers hang a bit loosely at the top.  You won't cut yourself, but you will notice an edge to the vinyl.=== Summary ===I would consider these perfectly acceptable as everyday "working" binders- in other words something that I use for myself. For anything being presented to a client, I think they come across as a little cheap, and I would use something more upscale.

Great gizmo.I was born in the early part of the 1960's, and as such I'm now in my early 50's.  What does that have to do with a document scanner? Not much other than I have a whole lot of boxes filled with 'important stuff'. Stuff I feel a need to keep, but it would probably be better if I threw most of it out. Now with this ScanMate scanner I can do both.The scanner itself couldn't have been easier to set up. As is typical for most things today, all I had to do is put in the CD and install the software/drivers - and then plug in the scanner when prompted. I'm running Windows 7 Professional and the installation went without a hitch. To turn on the scanner you simply pop open the cover on it - and the cover becomes the input tray for the scanner. The controls on the scanner are simple - there is a large numeric display that shows numbers 1 to 9. Beneath that there is a large button, which when pressed cycles the numbers on the display. The numbers represent the nine different scanning modes that the scanner will do. The different modes allow the scanner to scan to a color PDF, a B/W PDF, several image formats and also to an OCR text file. You can easily change the settings if need be. There is one other button underneath the mode button and it has a big bright illuminated arrow on it - and as you might guess it's the start scan button.The way the scanner works is you place a stack of documents face down (top side down) on the scanner input tray, select the mode you want and then press the arrow button. The pages are quickly pulled through the scanner and drop out the bottom part of the front. Scanning is fairly quick, and the way the scanner is configured out of the box - it will scan both sides of the document at the same time (you can change that setting if you don't need to scan the back of stuff). Once the scanner has scanned the pages, you get a pop-up box on the computer screen. Here is where my experience might be different than other peoples'. The scanner comes with some business card management software - which I did not install. I've got a full installation of Adobe Acrobat Pro X on my machine and when I scan something to a PDF, that is the software that gets launched with my new PDF document. There are a number of document management software packages out there that would work with this scanner - but for my needs Acrobat works for me.So how does the scanner do - Great! so far. One of the first things I did with it was to go to the kitchen and pull out that one drawer that I know pretty much everybody has. You know the drawer, the one with odd plastic lids that you don't know what they fit - and under those  lids all the manuals and warranties that came with every single kitchen appliance /  gizmo that you have ever bought or were given as a present. First thing I did was to weed out the ones for all the gizmos that are no longer with us (R.I.P). The rest, I ran them through the scanner and made PDF files out of them. Some of the manuals I had to take apart and cut the splines so as to get them to fit the 8 1/2" width of the scanner's input tray. After I made the PDFs, I put the files where I could find them and even made a backup of them on one of my USB portable hard drives. Then I tossed the paper versions in the trash with the other stuff (and threw the old plastic lids in too). Now I've got a whole new drawer of space in my kitchen. It's surprising how good that feels.My plan now is to repeat that with all the old boxes of documents I've accumulated over time and different careers. To end - I really recommend this Kodak ScanMate to anyone wanting to get back some of the wasted space in your closets / garage / attic or even just your desk drawers.Kodak ScanMate i940 Scanner

But I was unable to reproduce such fancy designs with any degree of accuracy.  These are not "paintbrushes" -- the tip seems to be a little more flexible than a standard Sharpie tip, and it comes to a fine point, so they allow a bit of variation in line width, but not much.  The line is pretty thick, except when you pull through to the point to lift it from the paper.  And I think that the tips could get squished of flattened fairly easily.These were a lot of fun to play with and would be fun for art projects, making labels, etc.  But I don't think they're significantly more fun or more versatile than standard Sharpies.  I sometimes use sharpies to write on my calendar or address envelopes -- but these would not work well in those situations, because they line they create is generally way too thick.  The I also found the pen a bit awkward to hold.  The barrels were just a bit thicker than standard barrels, and they were shorter, making them a bit awkward to hold.  These are a fun addition to my collection of art supplies, but I'll probably stick to the standard Sharpie design for future Sharpie purchases.

The Epson Workforce 840 is Epson's flagship All-in-One printer. It has duplex scanning, duplex printing, faxing, and copying capabilities. It also features a 3.5" LCD touch screen, dual paper cassettes, and WIFI connectivity.-SetupWireless setup was problematic. I ran into a hitch when the printer reported an IP conflict: "A router/access point channel conflict has been detected." The Epson printed just fine, but it took an inordinately long time (~3 minutes) to scan a document at 300 dpi. I managed to resolve the conflict by bypassing DHCP and manually assigning an IP address to the printer (MAC Address) in my Linksys router. After restarting the router several times, I was able to get the scan function working flawlessly.-Print SpeedsPrint speeds are astonishing. I put the printer through the paces by printing 6 copies of a mock document (which simply contains the pangram "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" repeated 145 times). It completed the printing in under 35 seconds -- or equivalently, over 10 pages a minute, or 5.83 seconds per page - in High Quality mode! My Canon MX870, a high-end all-in-one with comparable features, took a fair bit longer even in Draft mode -- 48 seconds (7.5 pages per minute, or 8 seconds per page). Photo print speeds are equally impressive. 3M has designed a great dispenser for it's post-it notes. The dispenser lets you pull off one post-it note at a time, as they are accordian folded- one note comes off to the left, then the next one comes off to the right.  This is a very clever and convenient way to easily remove one post-it note at a time. The plastic holder is a lovely two toned design that comes with adhesive strips so you can mount it on a wall or appliance where you will need the notes the  most.Everything is perfect until you come to the pen holder. They placed a pen holder next to the note holder, only this pen holder is an inch lower, making it barely 2 inches tall. The average pen is 6 inches tall and it would have been better to make the pen holder an inch higher than the note holder, making the pen holder 4 inches high. The pen is too wiggly and unsupported in a two inch holder, falling over and out too easily.I hope 3M redesigns the pen holder, making it taller and more supportive, as this is a great dispenser for the post-it notes, but it will be better when I don't have to keep picking up a pen off the floor!

I use the Logitech R800 which I recommend highly. It also tells you when you are moving out of range before you look silly clicking the mouse with nothing happening. Update, April, 2012.  I just had to replace my Photosmart printer.  It was about 3 years old, and I have "upgraded" to a new model through HP, for a small amount of money. Have not managed to "break" another one...but I do safeguard my stuff and my clothes whenever I am opening the new cartridges, because they have not changed the design so far. Actually, I did a LOT of printing with them.  However, when replacement time came, I took out the black xl (not the photo black), twisted the "arm" off of it (I HATE this system they use to get open their cartridges for placement in the printer) and ARRRRGGGGG...the entire "cap" thing came off, spilling black ink everywhere.  RUINED my yellow LL Bean shirt, ink in my keyboard, ink on my synthesizer (Kork workstation which sits beside my computer table)...it was a dreadful mess, and three days later, my fingers are still stained.Anyway, I called HP tech support, who referred me to the design department (which is, I hear, working on a DIFFERENT design because of this problem.) This is an amazing foot rest.  It was easy to set up and changed my situation immediately.  While my feet are on this, my posture in the chair is improved by sitting all the way back in the seat. I am 5'8" tall (while wearing 4" heels) and most office chairs need a lot of adjustment before I can use them.  Then, of course, the desk is too high.  It took very little setup to put this foot-rest to use under my kitchen table --which is currently functioning as my office.  (My office is a mess of work to do and I don't like going in there.  It's dangerous.) I changed the height setting to the higher setting by unscrewing two thumbscrews and then tightening them and tilting the rest to the angle I like.  It was an extremely easy set up.This product makes an immediate difference in the way I sit in my office chair.  Sitting in the chair incorrectly causes me some lower back pain and neck pain so I try to correct myself whenever I notice it.  For some reason, it has always been more comfortable for me to sit on the front half of my seat, leaving the back half of my chair available for all kinds of pranks and incidences.  On an extremely highly polished floor in a classroom, my chair once shot out behind me.  The worst indignity?  I could have gotten over falling, but hitting my chin on my desk and falling on my butt...not a good day.  And it added to my reputation for being a clutz, not that I needed any help.  All in all, it's probably much safer to properly sit in a chair.The immediate consequence of this foot-rest was that I have been much more comfortable sitting at work for long days.  My lower back does not hurt and I have not had to get up constantly to walk around or play with my hula hoop.  While I am working, I am playing around tipping the angle back and forth - toes and heels, toes and heels - which also provides some entertainment.This is heavy and sturdy and seemed like it would stay in place.  Its only flaw -- that it does not have non skid below it.  This foot rest does shift on wooden floors.  My solution for this minor problem was to put a piece of carpet non-skid below it.  That worked.Yes, it is still under my kitchen table and it annoys everyone but me.  They are currently working on making it fit under my desk because it is about half an inch too wide.  In the meantime, I am perfectly happy with it.  '

I'll confess. This is tricky. I haven't been in a formal school environment for almost 65 years. I have attended a few seminars and workshops over that time, and even a convention or two, but the school environment is different. When I became a freshman at Winthrop University a little over a year ago, I learned very quickly that I was going to need notebooks. Not so much the kind that I would write in, although they were important, but more needed to store class handouts, syllabi, plus a bunch of stuff totally new to me -- flashcards. Things needed to be organized, categorized, tabbed and indexed. And the conventional three ring binders (whose rings seemed to go all too quickly out of alignment) would trap some pages, and refuse to open out in the allotted space without intruding on my neighbor's space. Someone needs to reinvent the binder -- especially for college use.Well, somebody did. Those nice folks at the Mead Company really took some time to think things through. Every one of the things I found lacking in the conventional binder seems to have been thought of in this amazing product. I can get them is a rainbow of colors, so I can have a different color for each subject. The front cover wraps around to the back so in use it only takes up a fraction more space than a single sheet of notepaper. The first two pocket-dividers are amazingly well thought out. Little tabs to keep the top of the pocket closed once it is filled, plus a fairly hefty top corner tab that holds an item in the pocket's outer pocket from getting dog-eared. Additional small pockets on these same pocket-dividers where flashcards could be stored.If I have one reservation, it is not really a "fault", rather it is an unfamiliarity. The rings for inserted papers and pages are relatively soft plastic, and must be opened one at a time rather than with a single snap of one opening all three together. There is also the consideration that an external ring might tangle with other stuff in my totes. The flip side of that story is this: I only have to add and remove pages on occasions that are relatively remote from one another, but this is a "wait and see how it works out" feature. Offsetting the concern, however, is a one year warranty on the whole binder, so should any part of it fail (other than by abuse and misuse) the company will replace it.For me? I'm buying another in a different color for my needs for the summer semester, and two more again in other colors, for the four classes I will be taking in the fall. I can't think of anything more five star than willingness to return and buy more, can you?

I have been a fan of Pilot pens since the mid-1970s when I discoveredtheseas a replacement for Bic pens or the standard crappy government issue pens while serving in the Navy.This pen, from Pilot's Metropolitan Collection, is a bit of a letdown.The pen looks nice and comes in a handsome presentation box. You have to press the cap hard onto the top of the barrel to get it to stay in place, or else it tends to fall off while you're writing. We both thought the pen felt a bit top-heavy with the cap on the top of the barrel. While I had no complaints while using the pen, Mrs. Boilermate's natural grip on the pen placed her fingers on the ridge where the two halves of the body thread together, which she found extremely uncomfortable. Moving her grip above or below this ridge made the pen awkward for her to use. When you're done writing, the cap fits back over the point with a satisfying "click."The pen writes very smoothly because it uses Pilot's G2 refill. If, like me, you prefer an extra fine tip with blue ink to the black supplied with this pen, they are availablehere on Amazonat two for $1.48. If you want a smooth writing, skip free pen, I would recommend one of Pilot's ProGel, Dr. Grip, or Q7 Gel pens that use this refill. For the same $18 that this pen lists for, you can buya dozen G2 penshere on Amazon and have change left over.

I've already read two OTHER reviews of this printer that had the exact same problem out of the box: namely, the paper jam signal is blinking (indicating a paper jam - duh) and will not clear no matter what you do. The EPSON support was timely (I had to wait 5 minutes on a weeknight for tech support) and some of the best I've had. In the end, they determined the bogus paper jam light was unsolveable and they had to send me a replacement. I received it by FEDEX 2 days later. They also let me keep the original printer's ink cartridges and sent me 6 new ones, so I was able to do some "free" testing as to ink capacity (see below). With the replacement printer I had ZERO problems with easy setup; no horizontal striping on the prints; all colors solid and vibrant.Pros:* Excellent tech support and hand holding.* Stunning pro quality prints onEpson High-Gloss Paper* Beautiful prints onEpson Matte Presentation Paper* Problem free push one button setup with WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup)* Included copy ofAdobe Photoshop Elements 9 (Win/Mac)* Some of the best, friendliest, and fastest support I've ever receivedCons:* Obvious bad initial batch of DOA printers WHICH MUST BE FIXED* Power cord has tendency to come out of printer* Sparse documentation in box (newbies beware)Things to note:* Big footprint (which is necessary for a big format printer)* If you don't have WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) capable router, wireless setup may be a problem* USB printer cable is NOT included but would be useful* Specialized ink and paper is more expensive than usual home printing supplies (don't be surprised)* Paper feed support for 13 x 19 inch is a bit short for thin matte paper which "flops over"I set this up with WPS before I installed any software, which was not in the included documentation. My experience told me to set up with WPS before installing drivers as the printer is just registering with the router. Just push the WPS button on your router (if it has one) and then push the button on your printer within 2 minutes. When I subsequently installed the included software and commenced setup, it asked me if I knew where my printer was and finding it on the network was trivial. Nowhere does it say to do WPS first, and I suspect some people will have setup problems if they don't do WPS first (or don't have a WPS router). I had no need of a USB cable for setup.Also, though the wireless connectivity is nice, you may have issues with it later as I did. It's likely that the printer  was too far away from my router and the connection may have dropped (yes, my fault). So, out of 25 wirelessly printed posters, 2 stopped printing in the middle and I wasted a couple of premium photo sheets. (NOTE ADDED: Large files printed in high quality on glossy paper cause most problems. Same photo printed on matte paper is no problem. Wi-fi bandwidth or packet issue? Maybe.Problem does NOT occur with USB connection.) USB cable connection was rock solid. I highly recommend getting the inexpensive matte paper while you setup and learn to use the printer. Alternatively, just do setup and testing with regular 8.5 x 11 inch inkjet paper.When replacing my printer, Epson let me keep the original six cartridges and sent me six new ones as well (like I said, nice support!) so I experimented with quantity. I was able to print thirty 13 x 19 prints before two of the cartridges ran out: light cyan and light magenta. The other cartridges are at varying levels, with black being about one quarter full. It's difficult to say what mileage you will get since it depends upon what you print - I did black and white prints, color photographs, and movie posters (Wikimedia Commons has a great high def Boris Karloff "The Mummy" with some complex coloring). Each of the six ink cartridges will be individually replaced, not all at once. You might want to invest in a second set, and then replace each individually as they run out. Light cyan and light magenta are the colors most likely to need replacement the most often. Black if you do a lot of bitonal printing (large text posters).I printed on one sheet of non-Epson glossy photo paper and 2 hours later the ink was smudging. When Epson recommends that you use their own paper, take that to heart. The Epson papers are dry and solid right out of the printer.Based on my experience so far, I have a rule of thumb that a single 13 x 19 inch photo quality print on premium paper will cost about $3 to $5. That might be higher than reality, but it still gives me a good feel for single print expenses.I love this printer and would have probably given 5 out of 5 stars had it worked initially. The hand writing is on the wall that there's something awry with some of these early shipments, but Epson responded like a champ and replaced it quickly.Lots of friends and family are going to get gifts this year of beautiful 13 x 19 inch prints of houses, babies, and cats. Cheers!

Before I ventured whole hog into the land of refillable fountain pens, I started with the Pilot Varsity. One of the most important things with any fountain pen is that it write smoothly, without and skipping, hard-starting or scratchiness. I've purchased two of these pens, (one black and one purple) and each of them wrote quite smoothly.I did notice that the nibs are very easy to damage. Slipping this pen back into it's cap while tilted on a slight angle (yes, completely my fault) caused me to bend one of the nib tines to the degree that it was unusable and had to be thrown away. Nibs on regular/refillable fountain pens are made of a much stronger material, and while they still can be damaged, are not as flimsy as the material used on the Varsity nibs.The next thing I noticed, wasn't until I bought my first, (2nd, 3rd, 4th , etc.) non-disposable fountain pen. The Varsity nibs write really, really wide and on cheap paper, the ink bleeds and feathers all over the place. It's just not suitable for all kinds of paper.Keeping in mind that it's a disposable pen, it's actually a great way to test the waters before venturing into the land of fountain pens. Fountain pens in general require very little pressure to write and the Varsity is no exception. A light hand will deliver a solid line. Being able to write with light pressure allows a person to write for longer periods of time with less hand fatigue and cramping - which is why I use a fountain pen 98% of the time.Once you decide to take the plunge and buy a refillable fountain pen, check out theLamy Safari Charcoal Fountain Pen w/ Extra Fine Nibwith an optionalLamy Safari Converter Z24so you can refill with any kind of fountain pen ink you choose. If you want a classier looking pen, try thePelikan Tradition Series 150 Black GT Fine Point Fountain Pen - 993535

Over the years I've made use of countless three-ring binders, and never really gave it much thought - when one worked. Really the only time I would think anyone would give one any attention is when you had to use a bad one. Luckily, this Wilson Jones binder is one of the good ones.Back when I was teaching, I usually had the students in my classes keep a classroom notebook using a 1-inch binder. So over the years I've seen a lot of them. One of the things that I noticed during that time, is when a binder fails it is going to be for one of two reasons. Either one of the cover hinges is going to break, or the prongs that hold the paper in the binder are going to develop a gap and let the paper slip out. This new design that Wilson Jones had developed seems to address both of those issues. The hinges for the covers are wider than the standard ones, and they have a pattern of welds running the length of the hinge. The effect reminds me of a continuous piano hinge. I've only used the one binder I was given for about a month now - so I really can't say that it's holding up better than one of the standard design. But I imagine it will. They have also used an interesting design for the point where the two prongs come together to keep the paper in the binder - one prong end has a peg and the other prong has a hole that the peg fits into. When closed the rings feel really solid. Just don't get a finger in the way when you go to snap the rings closed.I also like how the bar for the rings has been attached to the back cover and not to the spine of the notebook. I think that makes the pages work better when using the notebook and when you go to store it on a shelf. The side pockets on the inside of each cover are handy.If I have any complaint for this binder it might be that the plastic transparent cover feels a bit light-weight for something that is being sold as 'Heavy-Duty'. I don't see any issues if the binder is being used in an office situation, but if I were to give a student one of these, that cover would probably be stretched out in no time.I could see myself buying and using these.

I've been very pleased with this chair so far. It came disassembled, as expected. Assembly was relatively simple, and took around twenty minutes. The only tool you need comes in the box. This chair has tons of adjustment options, from the height of the arm rests to the cant of the seat, along with the usual adjustments for height and recline. The fabric seems well made, and the chair is quite attractive. My biggest surprise was the weight: the chair is quite heavy, but this is probably a testament to the solid construction of the base and the many mechanisms needed for the adjustability. So it's not a problem (and maybe more of a sign of a good chair), just something to note. In all I'm quite pleased.

I wanted to like this stapler. I truly did. But, I'm afraid that it's cool future-retro design just doesn't hold up in the functionality department. If anyone has used staplers for several years, they'll know that there are some that tend to jam more than others. Unfortunately, it looks like Swingline's Green Fashion Stapler falls into that category. It worked well enough the first few times it was use, but before it even needed to be refilled, it started to jam. Try to collate more than 10 standard weight pages and you're asking for trouble.I use and have owned a number of quality Swingline staplers. While jamming is always a potential issue, this lightweight model seems to have a predilection for it. Is it the fault of the staples or the stapler? I'd have to go with the later because my  old747 Black Classic Desk Staplerhas no problems and keeps on chugging. My"Office Space" Rio Red Staplerworks reliably as well -- also based off the 747 design.I suppose the bottom line is to go with proven models when it comes to stapling. While this model is cute and compact, if it doesn't perform, what good is it?~ Kort

As someone who has gripping issues, I found the width of these to be wonderful. They are easy to manipulate, hold things to the cork board with ease, and are actually rather attractive. A huge improvement over the standard narrow clear ones I had been using for years.

Canon calls the new Pixma Pro-10 Printer a "Professional Inkjet Printer" and if ever a device like this deserved the title, it's this one. In a word, I am stunned at the quality of images I can produce with the Pixma Pro-10. I don't know if it's the quality of the printer or the quality of the inks (likely both) that creates such stunning results, but everybody who sees prints from this machine is knocked out. I do a lot of black and white photography, and the new 10-color Lucia pigment ink system uses three black inks (!) to create prints that are as good as I can get from any commercial service bureau. If I consider the time I used to waste driving back and forth to my primary print lab - time that is now spent on more productive work thanks to my Pixma Pro-10 - then this beauty has paid for itself about 10x over. That return on investment makes this purchase a no brainer.

I did not find this tool easy to use on gift wrap, which was the primary reason I bought it. It might work better on thicker wrapping paper (mine is a little thin, which is about all I can find these days) but I could get it to cut a sheet of printer paper, just to prove to myself that it wasn't a broken item. Went back to scissors for the Christmas wrapping.
I ordered these and have installed one.  I have yet to discover how many copies I will get, but the quality of the ink is good.

So I got this through Amazon Vine's program, but it sat in a box for awhile.  Then came a Saturday when I was sorting through my infant son's clothing, toys, and other items, and the nesting urge just overtook me.  I got out this label maker.All along, I'd assumed that it would be complicated to use, which is why I didn't really ever try to use it.  It so wasn't.  It came with instructions, but I didn't need them.  Loading the label paper was easy -- totally intuitive.  Then, you just type what you want it to say, hit print, and it does it.  The lettering looks great, you've got tons of options for styles, and it's pretty simple to cut the labels evenly (another worry).There are also tons of different colors you can get, so if you want it to look color coordinated, go ahead.I love this thing.  I'm going to label everything in my house.  Then, I'm going to go to the Container Store, and buy more stuff, and then label all that, too.

Loved it so much, I bought a two more immediately after assembling first. Very quick assembly. This particular model allows 3 seat adjustments: seat height, seat angle (leans forward or back), and seat-back angle. Only other adjustment is for the spring tension for the seat settings (which is default VERY stiff, and for my petite staff, made adjustments to seat impossible as their weight was not enough to overcome the springs). Armrests can be installed variably for height and width. The seat feels as though it is tempurpedic-like material. Very comfy. My staff is in heaven! Armrests are solid plastic material and don't seem to want to be torn out in chunks against the counter tops like the foam-rubber type we had previously. The variable adjustments, to me, make this seat worth the extra money compared to the less expensive and less adjustable model.

Like everyone else, we're always looking for ways to declutter and organize the unending flow of paper flowing into our house.  My latest solution (and it seems to be working) is to keep important stuff (checking and savings accounts statements, property tax receipts and bills) neatly tucked away in a three holed binder.  Hopefully at the end of the year (after the taxes are filed) I'll just be able to shred everything.  I ordered the box of four (in red -- makes them nice and visible) and have started a system -- one for medical stuff, one for checking and savings, one for tax deductible expenses and one for my son.  The great thing is that you can print a title for the end of the book (use large print and landscape orientation) and slip it into the clear plastic pocket.  Then, you can also print out an 8.5 x 11 sheet for the front and insert into that pocket.  There are also pockets inside the front and back cover for stowing stuff if you don't have time to 3 hole punch it right away.  The other great thing about these binders is that the D-ring holds 25% more pages than a conventional O-ring -- these hold about 250 pages, which I hope is enough to get us through to the end of the year.

Let me start out by saying I love, love, love this product. The Scotch Adhesive Dot Roller is a terrific product. It's a great, no mess, way for doing paper projects. My daughter loves to make little projects/crafts all the time with paper and she would normally use a glue stick. We all know how messy those can get and how much of those glue sticks we have to clean off the table when our kids are done with their projects. This product put an end to that mess! It was simple and easy for her to use and she even liked it better than her normal glue stick. The items she glued with the adhesive roller stuck well and her projects came out looking great with no spill over on the sides from the glue. The only reason I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 is the price. I feel it is a bit expensive for what you get. If it was half the price that they are charging now, it would be a much better value. In the future we will probably go back to using glue sticks for most projects and save the Scotch Adhesive Dot Roller for special projects. That is unless the price on these drops considerably.
Perfect school supplies for my second grade student. We go through so much of this Wide- Ruled Loose Filler Paper each school year.

The typical sticky note...glue works well but doesn't leave residue, the size is just right, and the colors are pretty (the pink, blue, and green note variety in the pack is nice).  There is no loss in quality or thickness of the paper due to being recycled, and I like that the company offers box tops to benefit schools...nice gesture that credits this particular company.
The eraser is first to go on a pencil so it is good to have a supply of rubber erasers.  My wife is also an artist and can use these erasers to touch up sketches that she makes.

I've written my share of pen reviews (I have an ongoing love affair that swings me between the Pilot G2 series and The Uni-ball Signo Gel Pens) so imagine my excitement when I saw an 8 pack of retractable colored ink gel pens at about 25% off the cost of a similar G2 colored ink gel pen set.These are good pens - for plastic pens, they don't feel as solid or look as sleek as the G2 or the Signo, but in my college note taking days, these would have been the pen of choice for price and variety.  All the colors wrote nice and dark except for the hot pink which was a bit too neon and could have been darker. I also personally prefer the fine point tip for Gel pens, however these medium point pens still had a nice steady flow that didn't bleed off the line so I wasn't bothered by the medium point at all.Very pleased with this pack.  I'll probably stick to my G2 and Signo pens for my regular black and blue purposes, but for fun colored inks, this is definitely the pack to go with.  It's a great price point for some really solid pens.

I've had the original 602 when in high school and loved them. The price was fair back then and the quality was great.These new 602's seem different and the lead just doesn't seem the same, as if the formula changed. The price is a bit too much, but the quality make is on par with the originals.If you're wanting the pencil for the name, fine, but the lead just doesn't seem like the old 602. Might just be me.
These are great!  Bright colors that are dark enough to read, pretty consistent ink, and easy-to-use style.  If you're looking for some great color pens to add on, I recommend these.

I like to keep a box for things on my desk that are bothering me.  At this time of year it usually has to do with deductibles for health insurance with notes all over them from talking to insurance people and all kinds of similar junk.  But then there are also all of the tax pieces coming in and paperwork on children...  These are all things I don't like to LOOK at.  I have a wire box for them at the moment but I can still SEE them.  This is a SOLID good replacement for THAT box.This box has reinforced corners that make it stronger than some boxes of its type.  I compared it to another box of this type that I have, one that ended up as a catchall in a drawer and realized it is not stronger.  Probably, this one is much better because I knew what to expect.Not bad.  Nice color.  I wouldn't pay real money for it though.

This product gets an A+ for convenience, but I can't help but wonder if it's worth the cost of the refills. I could just as easily use regular tape and pre-cut it into strips on the edge of a table.That being said, the dispenser itself is durable, and the tape pops up quickly and without hassle.A great gadget for the holidays, but it won't be replacing my regular old-fashioned tape dispenser anytime soon.
I use these to print my logo on. They are smooth and a nice size so these work for what I need. No issues with printing.

I love these.  The colors are bright and sharp.  The tips are narrow so you can write and draw.  I like to draw on whiteboards, but the dry-erase markers with the fat tips make it impossible.  No bleeding, running or smuging.The only thing that would give these five stars is if each of them had an eraser on the tip instead of the oddly shaped cap.
Since Dymo offers the Stamps service for free (well... it's paid for by the sale of labels) I felt a little bad about buying these labels cheaper.  But then I got over it.No issues at all.

Our household is home to educators, family members into board games and arts and crafts, and other folks who might find a home laminator useful.So needless to say, we all gave this a whirl.The first thing that struck me was how easy it was to set everything up. We had some board game rule sheets to laminate, and getting the items prepped and the unit ready to go was a breeze. Took just minutes.Even better? It was ready to start working in under a minute. No waiting for a lengthy heating up period. We were feeding in our sheets and laminating them in no time.And even better than THAT? The results were actually very good! Just as good, in fact, as you'd get from a visit to your local Kinkos. No complaints.This unit accommodates several sizes/thicknesses of pouches, and includes a cleaning sheet to keep it functioning nicely.Not many households will have a need for their own laminator, of course, but for those who do -- especially people involved in civic organizations, volunteer clubs, crafts, or education -- this model would make for a nice purchase.

The Five Star Zipper Binder Plus is certainly sturdy and well designed, but is in organization features that this binder really shines. There are not one but two different compartments containing file organizers, moreover, each file organizer contains 5 file transparent file separators for a total of ten different places to store your items for school. Each file organizer can be securely fastened separately from everything else so you don't have to worry about your files falling out if you accidentally drop the binder while the main compartment is open. There is also a large internal pen and pencil holder and an internal compartment for storing a cell phone but which is big enough to store a scientific calculator also. Of course there is also a spacious two inch ring binder in the main compartment also.  All in all, I would say this is a pretty cool binder, I only wish they had had these when I was at school!

I will admit it here.  I'm a big fan of Avery.  The keep coming up with fantastic products that I enjoy getting.  These sticky notes are no exception.  I'm a major reader of books:  ebooks AND printed books.  I also like to take notes, bookmark and highlight.  The nice thing about this product is the size.  They're big and see-through.  The size allows you to write notes or you can use them to mark where you're at.  Use them along the edge of what you're reading to bookmark where you're at. The surface is just right for allowing you to take notes-the type of surface and the size of it as well.My only complaint?  Sixty per package just isn't enough.  :(

These quartet liquid dry erase markers do exactly what you want them to do.  They write on a dry erase board without a problem; they erase easily, and there’s no weird offensive odor with them like you find with some dry erase markers.  The fine tip is especially nice for writing in small spaces, like a dry erase calendar, and the ink flows easily and smoothly.  I’m very pleased with this product and have no complaints.  If you are looking for fine tip dry erase markers, you can’t really go wrong with these.

Just the right size for a single 14mm DVD (even with its O-Card if you're careful).  Easily fits dbl. Blu-Rays.  The outer surface is a moisture-repellent plastic.  Ink will smear, but we tape our labels to the package with no problem.  Easy seal pull-strip is also very secure.  Using these mailers, we sent numerous orders for about nine months without any shipping damage reported.

I love the quality paper, the hardback cover, and even the larger rings that allow me to keep my pen inside the binder. The lines on the paper are a light gray. When copying/scanning the paper, the lines barely appear, allowing the notes, drawings, etc. avoid distraction.  Overall a GREAT notebook that makes note-taking very enjoyable and convenient.

This uni-ball twist and turn mechanical pencil is surprisingly sturdy,durable, and terrific. It comes with diamond infused lead that resists breakage and maintains a continuous sharp point. You will no longer need to buy the fragile mechanical pencils that are currently available in the market, because this uni-ball will outlast them all.
The oil is needed to keep your shredder working properly.  Trust me, I messed one up by not oiling it.This bottle will last a lifetime.

The Papermate Inkjoy set contains eight pens of assorted ink colors. Despite the low price tag (under $5) the pens are not cheaply made. The clip is metal (not flimsy, breakable plastic), the buttons are sturdy, the gel grip comfy and the ink transfer smooth. The picture shows the barrels being clear, however, on the actual product, while still transparent, they are tinted to match the color of the ink they contain.One note of caution: the pens are packaged with a protective wax ball on the tip. Make sure to remove it before attempting to write with them.All in all, for everyday use, these are some of the best pens out there.

The Epson Artisan 837 is probably more than the average user would need in terms of features and quality, but does it all very well.  Color photo printing quality is excellent and does 4x6" pics as well as the drug store digital photo printing when using the same quality paper.  I have also used some cheap thin photo stock which even provided very good results (although longevity may be the issue with this paper).  The scanning capability is excellent, and the included scanning software is easy to use, as is the character recognition (OCR) capabilities for scanned documents.  The document feeder for scanning and faxes is a definite plus -my last all-in-one didn't have this and it was sorely missed.  The ability to copy from the touchpad with computer off is also handy, and the copy quality is excellent.  I also like that you can print from memory sticks and cards without having to run everything through a connected computer (this was a major drawback to my last printer/scanner/copier).All in all, the Epson Artisan 837 is extremely easy to use and intuitive for both the touchpad features and included software.  The output quality is excellent (and adjustable in terms of resolution and color/grey/B&W;).  On the higher settings, I have reproduced older developed 35mm photographs with no apparent loss of quality.  If I take the time to scan them into Photoshop or PSP first, some of them even come out better than the originals.

I am an office supply sucker. I love labels, notebooks, and paper products of all kinds. The Ampad simple sort was a new idea to me.  I think the idea is fantastic as I often use legal pads and then end up with sticky notes trying to point to information since I cant move the sheets.  This seemed like a perfect option.When I snapped back the top of the writing pad, the top of the pad was on the desk and the bottom was hanging off creating a slight curve.  This pushed the papers up. So when I snapped the top back, the papers went every where.  So the top is easy to use and the papers are very very repositionable.  The dividers are simple manila pages with primary colored tabs on them.  They work well too.But the disappointment is the paper.  It is thin and has almost no tooth. It is not fine to write on. Some pads just have such great paper that you love using them.  This is not that pad.  I am actually considering seeing if I can use the nifty top mechanism with nicer paper.

Although we were content with our previous printer, this multiple use machine (printer/copier/fax/scanner), is far better than any in our experience and the touch screen is very enjoyable as well as practical to use.  The 901 comes with a five-year warranty and the sole time we had to telephone for assistance, we received prompt action.  Since most of our printing requires black ink only, the $5.00 cost for replacement cartridges in black is a real saving.  The scanning function allows for oversize documents, while automatic two-sided printing is a boon. All in all, this has proved to be a superior product.
The packing was completely inadequate, the board was out of the package and broken at two corners.

When it comes to advertising budgets Neat must have one of the largest.  I don't remember flying on a plane and not seeing it advertised there.  I don't remember reading a business magazine and not seeing it there.  This is in stark contrast to Fujitsu whom when I am recommending a scanner to someone I usually get a response like: is that a real brand?The Neat device itself is slick I'll give it that.  Neat when to the same design school as Apple I think, Fujitsu went to the IBM school of function.  There are only two buttons on the Neat scanner - PDF and Scan - so there isn't much to the physical layout to be scary to those easily scared by tech. There are different size slots for different sized documents - clever.What I don't like about the scanner is software.  It just annoys me.  I am used to putting a document in the scanner, it is scanned, Im asked where I want it saved and then it is saved directly into the file system. Im not much of a fan of proprietary software. Im sure its great, but what I don't want to do is learn another program. I installed it and played with it. I then promptly moved back to my easier Fujitsu workflow.The scans themselves are on par with the Fujitsu so I have know comment to complain there.  They both will scan a document fine.I just don't like the software.

I know there is a calculator on my computer, but I still love regular calculators and this one is a convenient, compact size. Since this is dual powered, it will last longer and you can recharge it with solar power.The size of this calculator is nice because it fits in your hand while you calculate away. I find I make less mistakes, although I do sort of miss my calculator with the larger key pad.~The Rebecca Review
These boxes are easy to assemble, sturdy and are great for storing my old manuscripts and old taxes.  They look like they'll hold up during any move.  A good value.  Recommended.

There's not much to say that hasn't been said before. This is an excellent product that keeps my MacBook Pro nice and cool. There is indeed a notch cut out now toward the bottom so you can now open and close the lid without lifting the laptop out of the holder.Well worth the money, and probably the best MBP stand out there. Lowered my idle temperatures about 6 degrees over the Logitech Alto Express stand. Boy did my MBP get warm sitting on that puppy, plus you couldn't eject discs while using it. Wish I hadn't wasted the money... You live and learn!Bottom line: Buy the Mstand. It's superb.

I really like this set of dry erase markers in assorted colors. They are so bright and such vibrant colors.  They are very easy to use and don't smear on a dry erase board.  I just recently purchased a Dry Erase Board and our son liked it so much I gave it to him.  Don't know how we ever got along without one.  I've always used a small note book to write down the things I needed at the store.  NOT ANY MORE!!!  I have a new Dry Erase Board coming to me in the next day or two.

I've used binders like this for years and they have always performed well for me.  The D ring design accepts a lot of pages smoothly and the snapping mechanism is secure and easy enough to use.  Just get the right size for your application.  The smaller sizes also hold a lot of paper and the 2 inch size seems bigger than it sounds.

I needed a laptop stand that was portable enough for me to take in the car on a near-daily basis, and into different conference rooms and computer labs.I'm glad I found this. It's very lightweight and seems to be sturdy enough to hold my laptop (although it is rather light).  The surface area is generous -- giving me room for my 17" widescreen display plus another 2-3 inches.It's a far better alternative to lugging around a 10 lb, expensive table lectern.Although it comes with a mousepad attachment (which I wasn't expecting) which must be attached to one of the legs. Doing this prevents you from folding up the legs for travel. So, each time I want to use the attachment, I must screw it into place and remove it when I'm done and store it separately. Not brilliant.If I were left-handed, I wouldn't be able to use the mousepad attachment at all, as there is no hole on the left side.The stand is SO lightweight, it easily slips around on whatever surface you've stood it upon and risks being tipped over. It's entirely possible you could accidentally knock the stand and send your laptop flying or falling. To counter the slipping, I've stuck four little rubberized pads on the bottom legs. Still, it would be nice if the bottom leg segments had optional weights to prevent tipping.The stand is a bit wobbly, due to the inexpensive construction. Not a big deal. Some of the pieces of plastic or aluminum arrived scratched and looked used, though everything functions fine and it came in an original box.The "English" language on the box and instructions is laughable.

I recently discovered these pens and love them. I had been using Uni-ball gel pens but found those to run out of ink too quickly. Even though I could still see plenty of ink in the pen the uni-balls stopped writing. Someone else in my household bought a bunch of these Pilots and I decided to give them a try. These Pilots write better and are more smooth. For some reason, they seem more flimsy and are lighter than the Uni-balls. Now, only time will tell if they last longer, but for now I really like them.

Honestly this wasn't as nice as I'd hoped it would be. While not super expensive it's expensive enough that I had hoped it would be a decent quality since it really is pretty small 14" x 14" sounds bigger than it really is, think just a bit bigger than a piece of standard scrapbooking paper for an accurate estimate. I love the modern look/feel of the silver borderless board and picked this to hang in my 10yr old daughters room (she actually ended up deciding she wanted it on her door so we could leave eachother little messages which it does work well for).Mine also arrived with some scratches & dings, not bad enough to make me want to return it.... just enough to annoy me a bit. The included magnets are junk, we honesty just tossed them, you can purchase inexpensive "rare earth magnets" here on Amazon and make your own really cute magnets with some imagination, my daughter likes to use small plastic toys, marbles, etc. just put a bit of e6000 glue on the magnet and apply it to your choice of things and they make really unique strong magnets that look really great with this board. The included marker is nothing great, but nothing horrible either... we have a whole collection of mini dry erase markers & crayons so this just went into the pile, all seem to work fine on the board and erase easily (with a bit more effort required when writing over the scratch ours arrived with).If you can manage to get one without damage I think it's a nice option when you want a smaller board with a more modern feel.
The amount of paper is just enough for anything my school age kids and I need (and I'm a full-time college student). I use it with an HP printer and it hasn't jammed once.

This is the best phone we ever bought. It's replacing a 7 year old Sony system and it does so much, I am amazed it has such a reasonable price.1. The cordless handsets--you may want a few more. They show the Caller ID (assuming you have that service) and they also have built-in phone books on each handset. This means that if one person tends to use a handset (say in their own home office) they can set up a phone book from frequent callers or frequently-called numbers.2. The base unit has a very easy to use menu. Absolutely intuitive.3. The phone base for the cordless handsets recharge the batteries. Since we store them in their base, they are always ready to go.4. The base unit (answering machine) also has a speaker phone.5. The units show missed calls, but of course, a missed call can be one that was picked up on another handset or the base unit.6. The handsets can be located with a signal.7. The phone ringers have a variety of nice tones and tunes to choose from.8. The units light up and are very readable.The only criticism is that the speaker phone is not all that loud, but I hardly use speaker phone, so I don't really care about that.Bottom line, for the price, this is a great deal and a phone I enjoy using a lot.

IMO Avery continues to dominate the do-it-yourself business advertising market.  The quality of the paper is superb - thick enough to not feel homemade, yet not as substantial as a professional business card.  It would be nice to see a heavier weight paper offered, with the understanding that some home printers malfunction when the paper weight is too high.The Clean Edge system is where this business card paper really impresses.  The edges on these cards are simply amazing.  The perforation is so tiny that the edge looks nearly smooth.  Other brands tend to leave a ridged edge that has feathery bits of paper jutting out.  Also, the fold-back method to separate these cards is terrific.  Never does a card edge rip and the process is very fast.Compared to any other brands that I've tried, these Avery Clean Edge Business Cards are my clear favorite.  I have printed 3 packs of cards and will continue to purchase more as needed.My only gripe is that Avery release printer templates for more software than Microsoft Word.  In print design, Microsoft Word is at the far bottom.  Avery should consider that software from Adobe, Corel, and others have been mainstream for many years and release templates accordingly.  It is possible to find Adobe and Corel compatible templates online, however Avery really ought to step up and release official templates on their website.

I ran this product past our teen, and we agreed that this is a functional product that would be good if you have stuff that fits the pockets, but is not hugely stylish or adaptable.What's good:- The magnets on this thing are great.  It snapped right to the locker and refrigerator we tested, and they're strong enough that they won't come off unless you want them to.- The neoprene pocket material is nice and stretchy, with no sag so far.What could be better- This isn't very adaptable.  It's 8" wide, so if your locker is narrow, it might not fit.  On top of that, it basically has three pockets - one is divided into two <2" pen pockerts, and one is left at an <4" phone or note card pocket.  If those fit your needs, this is a pretty good way to keep some pens and pencils in your locker door, plus maybe a pad of post-its or a phone, but if they don't fit your needs, there's no adjustment.  (We might have liked this better if the two halves could be separated.)- It's not very stylish.  You can get the inside accent color in a variety of colors, but the outside neoprene is flat black.Overall, this does what it says, but we felt like it could be better.  Recommended if it meets your needs.

I don't know if the second layer of adhesive makes all that much of a difference in the function of this office/classroom/home staple. However, I really like the idea of "100% recycled paper" and the "Box Tops for Education" logo on the package. Avery is environmentally and socially responsible with this product. That makes the product superior to its competitor in my mind.

This is really the first desktop laminator that I've seen (and used) that doesn't take up 1/2 your desk! I love how quickly it warms up, for the last minute needs! The handy beep when done warming allows you to walk away for a few minutes and come back when it's ready! Though I do recommend using it for the first time outside, as the first time the rollers heat, there is a definite burnt plastic type smell. It was totally gone by the 3rd use.I love the FRONT feed, as that way you can be sitting and see that your item is feeding properly, and not going in sideways at the last minute- as the top and bottom laminating sheets HAVE to touch, or you don't get a seal in that area! You do need to keep the typical 1/4 inch side seam allowance, again because the two sheets have to touch. I do recommend the Swingline pockets though, as they seem to go through easier, and have no bubbles or marks. They were what I had on hand when this came in, so why I used them. For the price, they should include at least 2 with the machine, so you can make it works out of the box. But they aren't too bad in pricing.My review is really 4.5, if it came with trial sheets, it would be a 5!

Similar to correction tape, this product was extremely easy to use.It's too bad that I didn't have this type of product before for my Kindergarten grade child. I wouldn't have had to deal w/ all the messes of glue sticks, paste, or drip glue for her homework.It's a great product for grade school children or for scrap booking. The bonding isn't extremely strong, but it makes it perfect for school age children where you can still remove the glued item and fix it again w/o a huge mess of paper tearing.
What's to say except that these do what I want them to do?  The product comes out smooth and shiny, protecting the item you've laminated.  Works great with my Fellowes laminator.
I needed something that would hold out a lot of handouts for meetings I hold.  These are perfect.  They hold a few to a lot of sheets at one time and are very sturdy.

Epson WorkForce 845 color inkjet multifunction printer has a lot going for it. In particular, its above-average capacity and paper handling, top-notch performance, and very good output will fulfill the needs of a small office or home office well. A few setup and interface miscues are all that stand between this product and SOHO nirvana.Paper handling on the WorkForce 845 includes a generous 500 sheets of capacity (split between two 250-sheet stacked trays), automatic duplexing, and automatic two-sided scans of documents placed in its 30-sheet ADF. Duplexing is fully supported on the Mac, as well. The scanner is letter/A4-size, and the lid telescopes almost a full inch--after a solid tug. Looking for full legal-size support? The HP Officejet Pro 8600 Plus has a legal-size platen (and a higher purchase price).The WorkForce 845 processes plain-paper documents in a hurry. In our tests, text at default settings printed at 11.5 pages per minute on the PC and 11.3 ppm on the Mac--far faster than the average. Our snapshot-size photos printed to plain paper at an outstanding 5 ppm, though they slowed to a rate of only 0.9 ppm on glossy photo paper. Printing letter-size glossy photos on the Mac proceeded at a middling 0.4 ppm, and scan times were about average.Though fast, the WorkForce 845 produces output that appears anything but hasty. At standard settings, text looks black and sharp. When you choose the slower (and more ink-intensive) "fine" mode, the results are nearly laserlike. Color graphics printed to plain paper are exceptionally accurate, and closer than usual to the quality of their glossy-paper counterparts. Said glossy-paper photo prints have a slightly cool color temperature (and an ever-so-slightly pink bent) but show exceptional detail. Overall, subjects have a bright but realistic appearance. Epson's printers also feature economy and fast-economy print modes that accelerate print speed and can save on ink costs, at the expense of print quality.The WorkForce 845 is nonconformist in one good way, shipping with Epson's extra-high-capacity cartridges (model 127), a 945-page black and 755-page cyan, magenta, and yellow. Few inkjets offer anywhere as many pages right out of the box. Replacing those cartridges will set you back $29.49 for the black and $20.39 apiece for the colors. That works out to 3.1 cents per page and 2.7 cents per page per color, or an economical 11.3 cents for a four-color page. I recommend that you replace spent cartridges with the same extra-high-capacity tanks, as the merely high-capacity (model 126) tanks are just average in cost: 4.8 cents per page for black and 3.6 cents per page for each color, or 15.7 cents for a four-color page.The WorkForce 845's other departures from the norm are less appealing. Why force users to select 'Change ink cartridges' from the Maintenance menu to move the ink carrier into position for removal? On most printers, that action transpires automatically when the user lifts the hood. In addition, the power button requires a nearly 2-second press to cycle the unit on, yet the MFP reacts instantaneously to a power-off press; for most printers, it's the other way around.Another problem I rarely encounter with other printers is difficulty setting up push scanning--that is, initiating scans to a networked PC from the printer's control panel. This is a must-have capability in an office environment to avoid running back and forth between the PC and MFP to feed new documents. The WorkForce 845 fully supports push scans via USB, requiring no tweaking--but when I tested the unit via wireless, I had to add an exception for the Epson Event Manager software to the Windows Firewall manually, restart the PC, and then double-check that the exception stuck. And in our case, I had to redo the exception after the restart. You may simply elect to disable the Windows Firewall instead, though this move is dangerous unless your router has a firewall. Epson's documentation on this process is vague.The Epson WorkForce 845's annoyances pale in comparison with its strengths: speed, capacity, high-quality output, and affordability. It's a bargain for a small-office MFP. Just make sure to deal with the wireless push-scanning issue at setup time so that you can confirm early on whether the unit will work in your environment. If you'd prefer an alternative, another model worth considering in this price range is the Canon Pixma MX882, which has comparable features but is somewhat more compact.

I have always used HP printers in the past, in particular the HP Photosmart series but decided to give Canon a try. What drew me in was the duplex printing. Here's how the whole process went.INSTALLATION: Installation was fine on the first computer. It was easy to set it up and easy to set up the WiFi but when I went to set up the other computer with the printer, no matter what I did, it would sync up once via WiFi and then never again. It just did not recognize the second computer no matter what I did whereas there were no problems with the first. I ended up having to use the USB cable to hook the second one up whereas the first computer is still using WiFi.WIFI PRINTING: This is a great feature since it means both my computers can print, except that only one of the printers was really using the WiFi printing. What I've noticed is that there is quite a bit of lag to print when using WiFi and I never really had this problem before. I think it's almost a minute before I hear the printer start to move.DUPLEX PRINTING: This is what initially drew me in. Be sure you actually set the settings to use duplex printing or it won't print on both sides. Most of the applications did not set the duplex setting as a default. What the printer does is it will print the first page out then feed the paper back in and turn it around and do the second side. Make sure the paper you're feeding is not too thick though. I was trying to do this for printing out a card but it jams the printer when it is anything but the standard letter paper.SCANNING: I was a little bit disappointed with the scanning feature of this as when I scanned my pictures in, it just didn't capture all the colors and sharpness that the actual picture had. I have to admit that my HP printer/scanner combo did a better job of scanning the kind of quality pictures that I expected.COPYING: Copying worked fine and I didn't have any problems with copying something. It is just like all the rest printer/scanner/copier combinations in this aspect.INK: I will say that the ink does seem to last a little bit longer than HP printers but the ink itself are also a bit more expensive. I think I've seen it for about $45 for both color and black.Now for the kicker, I have been using the printer fine until just a few days ago when I tried to print something and it suddenly jammed. I didn't do anything different. The paper was still the same kind that I've been using and nothing has changed. The feed just suddenly crinkled the paper together so it jammed. I removed the paper jam but now, the printer doesn't work anymore. I've submitted a support ticket with Canon as I've already cleared the paper jam, powered it off and back on and still getting an error message. The error message even tells you that you have to contact support if it is still not fixed. This is pretty aggravating as it was the only functional printer at the moment in my house and now I cannot print until I get in touch with support and try to figure out what happened. But to have this kind of issue from a simple paper jam? I would've given this one more star if it wasn't for that issue. A paper jam should be something where once it is removed, then the issue is no more.UPDATE: I got in touch with Canon's customer service and I will give them props for a prompt response and getting me a replacement in the mail very quickly. I didn't have to pay for shipping or return shipping and the item worked right out of the box. Now I just hope I don't run into this issue again.

I applaud the effort to create a reasonably priced, ergonomically superior chair for the sub $200 market. Bad chairs create bad backs and all the problems associated with that. Unfortunately, while this Basyx chair has better than average built quality, the chair lacks in a few significant ways that make it an imperfect solution.First, the good:1) Built quality is excellent. Solid, heavy gauge, metal parts for the chair frame including a powerful pneumatic lift. The casters are large enough to roll freely even on office carpeting. This is a heavy-duty chair and won't fall apart easily.2) The adjustable arms are comfortable and well designed to accommodate variously sized people.3) The material quality of the seat back and seat are reasonable.4) The mesh back, while not as good as the nicer chairs from Global or HON, offers solid lumbar support and breathes nicely.The not so good:1) If you're a taller occupant (I am 6' 3") the top bar of the seat back meets right at the shoulder blades, creating a pressure point. This is especially noticeable when leaning back in the chair. A a major annoyance, and and enough to knock the chair down a whole star for this single issue. The problem would have been easily addressed by warping the back bar with some sort of foam or padding.2) The seat, while firm (which is what you want from anything you plan to sit on for a while, including a bike, believe it or not), creates pressure points under the sit bones (the two, narrowly spaced bones in your backside). I discovered this after sitting in the chair over a few days. The seat needs better contouring to alleviate this issue.Overall, I'd rate this chair as average. If you're taller than six foot, it's probably not the chair for you due the to the top bar issue. For under $200, it's worth considering and will absolutely destroy the cheap junk they sell at office supply stores in the same price range.

My wife loves a foot massage. She's had foot massages in no less than five different countries and tried many types, including Shiatsu, Reflexology, Thai, Deep Tissue and foot massage machines. So, when I asked her if she would like to help me review the Foot Rocker from Fellowes, she flashed two thumbs up.After two weeks of tests, her enthusiasm diminished into a dismissive hand gesture.Touted to improve circulation and reduce fatigue, Fellowes' Foot Rocker is a bit underwhelming straight out of the box. The Foot Rocker is plastic--one big, piece of black plastic with two matching plastic wheels. The simplicity of the design takes time to appreciate: approximately 10-15 minutes, or the same amount of time it takes to figure out to lock the wheels in place without breaking one or more plastic parts. The instructions are rather cryptic on exactly how to lock the wheels in place and how much force to use. I slapped at the wheels with the palm of my hand but a rubber mallet would work much better.You can flip the Foot Rocker over to adjust the height (from 2-3/4 to 4 inches) but that's the only adjustment provided. I recommend spraying a coat of WD-40 where the wheels lock into the textured platform to reduce the squeaking. Using the Foot Rocker on carpeting or a throw rug instead of a bare, wood floor will also help reduce the noise.The rocking motion took a while to get used to before it became comfortable to operate while we worked (we tried it under the dining table and a desk while working on a computer).In summary, does the Foot Rocker work? Yes, although many customers might expect more features and a wider range of adjustable options. The Foot Rocker could do with better instructions and less squeaking. The product is sturdy, easy to clean (the Microban protection is a nice feature) and relatively simple to use. I would be more inclined to use this in my office than at home, where I'd look for a more expensive model that included vibration and foot warming.Rating: Three stars.

This Accuteck ShipPro digital scale works very well and is easy to use. Like any scale, this one works best when sitting on a hard surface like a counter-top, desk file cabinet, or a hardwood or tiled floor.If you would like to see pictures that we took of the scale in use, please go back to the scale's main sales page and scroll down to where the "Most Helpful Customer Reviews" section starts -- look to the right of that area for the "Product Images From Customers" section. Nice looking, functional unit. The 10 pound with that you see in the pictures weighs about 10 pounds and 4 ounces... with the three scales we have showing 10 pounds 4.3 ounces, 4.4 ounces and one with 4.6 ounces. All in all, a very acceptable deviation for parcel post use.The scale's documentation notes that there is a ten year manufacturer's warranty, which is amazing, so if an issue arises before that ten year period expires I will return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. I did receive this scale gratis from the manufacturer, and have put it through the paces to objectively find out how well it performed. My statements here reflect that testing.If you are looking for a scale of this style and size, for use similar to what I have described above, then we recommend this Accuteck ShipPro scale to you. It is easy to setup & use, easy to read, and we found it to be very reliable.Go for it.
