The HP Officejet 4500 is a printer that ranks as a basic All-in-One in my book.  It contains Printing, Scanning, Fax and Copy capabilities but lacks many features you might find in more expensive printers... but of course you are paying for those advanced features after all.  What the HP 4500 is, is a printer that gives you great performance and the bare necessities at an affordable price.UNPACKING + INITIAL SETUP ( A+ )I was very impressed with how HP packs their printers.  I used Lexmark for the longest time and there is a world of difference.  The Printer came boxed with foam, and enough tape/cardboard to fill a small garbage pail.  They really wanted to make sure nothing broke in shipping or got dislodged.  As for unpacking the printer itself, it isn't hard to un-box and all the tape and pieces of cardboard you need to pull out are in easy reach with no surprises lurking.Setting the machine up initially isn't hard either.  Just follow 10 simple steps, most of which are just undo the tape.. plug it in.. put in the ink etc.ADVANCED INSTALLATION ( C- )After the initial setup it will be time to install the software drivers / software for the printer.  This is where I have my gripe.  HP software is insane bloatware.  Lexmark printer's I owned would install in maybe 2-3 minutes.  HP installation took 10 minutes to do just a "minimum" installation and that was 47.2 MB ... if you do a recommended FULL installation you are looking at up to 600 MB of garbage being put on your computer system, some of which is not even compatible with current computers (some of the programs do not work in IE 8, Google Chrome or Firefox 4.x.x or higher)  *** HP has updates on their website for some programs ***Anyhow I recommend doing the following to avoid bloatware and unnecessary software to be installed on the system.  When you start your installation process simply select MINIMUM. This installs the driver and basic software such as Tools and Uninstall feature.  Follow the steps and test the printer to make sure it can copy/scan and print properly. Now when finished select to install additional software from the driver disk.  Select "CUSTOM" You now will be allowed to select what you want and do not want.  It saved me about 300MB worth of software and bloatware yet the printer still has full functionality.*** NOTE: Even with MINIMUM installation, the HP software will forcefully install Yahoo Print Toolbar.  If you do not want this, just go to toolbar and inside settings is an Uninstall optionQUALITY OF FEATURES ( B- )- Scanning .. B- ..  The scanner is quiet and fairly quick at lower resolutions and produces nice images.  I did notice some pixilation occurring on sharp angle corners, but going to a much higher resolution resolved it.- Printing .. A .. This is a great printer,  it is much faster than my previous printer and has more options when printing a page.  The rated 22ppm seems a bit inflated though even if it is being taken AFTER the first page.  It seems more like they are rating that at "Fast print" not Normal.. but still the printer does a great jot printing fast and without bleeding colors.- Fax .. B ..  The fax portion is actually quite impressive for the price.  While it is not really mentioned you are getting a 3G capable fax modem here. (33.6k baud)  You can use 9600, 14400, or 33600  which is very helpful in speeding up faxes for some small business owners.  The fax portion is very simple to understand and is much higher quality than the one on my old Lexmark- Copy .. B+ ..  Copies are very accurate though sometimes can come out a bit lighter than anticipated.SOFTWARE QUALITY/INTERFACE ( B- )I was very impressed with the software.  While a bit bloated yes... the software is very easy to understand and use. My parents figured it out in no time and the software can be quite powerful in a simple way.  The solution center provided by HP has a small, clean interface that tells you everything you need to know; easy to use buttons and features.  My only gripe is that the software is a bit bloated.  With it running and the HP desktop solution option (boots on start up) you can have up to 6 processes running on your system using 80 - 120MB of system ram.  It is a hog of a software package.  As for the printer interface, simple and efficient with the use of just 3 buttons to move around menus and very readable text.  There are much more advanced interfaces out there like the LCD color interfaces or the touch screen interfaces but you also are paying a premium for those.INK CONSUMPTION ( C )Not sure exactly how ECO friendly this printer is unless I suspect HP is not rating their ink on NORMAL.  I find the cartridge 901 black is rated for 200 pages, I can get over 300 if I print on FAST...  around 150-180 on NORMAL  yet the 910XL black is rated at 700 and I maybe get 600-650 on FAST.  No idea if there is some magical feature on the printer I just can't find or if the ink cartridges perform randomly.  As for the STARTER cartridges you get with the printer, they barely have any ink in them.  Enough for maybe 20-30 prints of black and colorOVERALL ( B- )I've used plenty of printers and so far this HP one appears to be the best in the end. While it does suffer from bloated software and inconsistent ink cartridges you are getting a lot of bang for your buck here.  The printer is essentially a "BASIC" 4-in-1 here... there is NO WIRELESS, NO MEMORY CARD SLOT, NO Two-Sided Printing etc.  However you are still ending up with a quality scanner, quality fax and quality printer  just without all the additional bells and whistles.  With all that said I would recommend this printer to someone who does not dabble with photo printing/photography and does not need a networked printer.  It is perfect for just the average Joe who wants a printer/scanner/copier that can also Fax if needed.*** NOTE: The Web clipboard plug-in feature(on the CD) that gets installed with the scanning software is not compatible with IE 8, Chrome or Firefox 4.x.x .. for some people it can crash the browser and for other people (like myself) the program never closes. It just keeps opening itself over and over again.  To uninstall it just uninstall it in your add/remove programs in the operating system*** NOTE: This is the WIRED version of the 4500. Below is the link for the WIRELESS version of the printer. Same exact features just with built in wirelessHP Officejet 4500 Wireless All-in-One (CN547A#B1H)** NOTE: This printer requires a USB 2.0 A-B cable to hook up to your PC.  It is not included with the printer. If you need a printer cable here is a cheap yet quality solutionMediabridge - Hi-Speed USB 2.0 Cable (6 Feet)

This Display Pocket is sturdy and professional looking but with a few additions could be really a neat product.First, what is is. It would be nice if it had a magnet to allow it to be hung on a refrigerator, file cabinet, etc. It also would be handy if it came in different sizes which would make it much more usable for photo's of various sizes as well as newspaper clippings, etc.All in all this is a handy item but it seems to be a bit overpriced. I guess when compared to a picture frame it is reasonably priced but the price did give me a pause when considering four or five stars...I ended up giving 4 considering the price issue. Perhaps Scotch will increase size offerings with future products of a similar nature.

First, the storage case -- VERY nice -- long-lasting (we hope) plastic that folds out into a tryptich, so that all the pens are on display and within easy reach. Just press the back of the panel and the pen you want pops out. The display then folds back into itself for ease of carrying and protecting the pens as well.The pens themselves are visually BEAUTIFUL. Each has a color coded clip and color-coded rubber grip. The array is a delight to behold.The range of hues and colors is exceptional.But -- as for "Marks on just about everything, including glass, metal, plstic, photos, foils, coated paper" -- I tried this and found that the DARKER colors WILL mark on just about everything BUT the paler colors will not (especially on plastic, glass and metal) -- unless maybe some of the ink in some of the pens is drying out (which I doubt, because they ALL work fine on paper).These are VERY fine points and are GREAT, so I discovered, for working with colored pencil and watercolors/acrylics washes on paper (smoother papers - vs- the heavier nubbied watercolor papers).Since this is PERMANENT ink, ther is no way (using water anyway. I will try a solvent to see what that does) that they can be blended, but fine cross-hatching and also stippling help to create a blended look.Some of the paler colors were a bit on the weak side. I have taken a couple of these pens and stored them upside-down in the display case/carrier to see if Gravity will alter their flowability and color strength (I am using a rubber band to keep it closed as the pens stored upside-down are inhibiting total closure of the case).They CERTAINLY are fun to doodle with or sketch. And the Acid-Free Ink is a VERY positive PLUS. for longevity of the finished artwork (just be sure to use Acid Free paper too)As for comparing them with Sharpies -- there is no comparison -- Sharpies still are better but BIC is a good brand name and well-loved, so there is certainly no harm in getting these and enjoying them and -- HEY -- Using them along with your Sharpie colllection too!!!UPDATE Dec 2012 -- I am using these for very fine work -- on paper -- and find that they cover flawlessly (and depending on the porosity of the paper, the color may come out darker than indicated on the pen top). The points do not get stubby (especially if you use a light touch, as the ink flows effortlessly)

I use a decent amount of mailing/packing tape, and half the time I don't have scissors handy, so this tape really comes in handy. Before I got it, I didn't believe it would actually be tearable by hand, but it is! YAY! The only reason it doesn't get five stars is because it is quite expensive.

I have been using these Sticky Notes for a while now. They stick just as well as Post It Notes, if not better. I like the colors better with the Avery, they are slightly more vibrant. I was shocked that the Epson ink for my Workforce 840 is so expensive. I was dismayed at this. I have tried refills on other Epsons in the past but the ink jets clog rendering the printer useless. I purchased this printer in February 2011 and was initally excited to have a wireless printer that I could scan with. This feeling was short lived as I was only able to scan without incident for about 2 weeks and then I begun to get the error message that :"the scan cannot be performed because another program or computer is using the networked HP device." So I uninstalled and reinstalled the software(after rebooting my computer, the printer and the router) thinking that maybe something was forgotten or I did something wrong. Once I did that I didn't use the printer for a few months (had a baby) but I figured after the uninstall/reinstall it should be ready to go as I hadn't used the scan function in over 2 months. Well, it wasn't I again got the above error plus some new ones, went on the HP website which instructed me to uninstall/reinstall from the website and try again. Well it did work for about another month and then again, nothing. So then I put it together that each time Windows 7 had a Critical Update that caused the system to reboot the scanner would stop communicating with the computers in my home. So this time I contacted HP because I was sure they would be able to help me all the tech had me do was reinstall without uninstalling which caused another issue. So then I had to uninstall/reinstall and I contacted HP again and they told me to take the printer back to the store that I had purchased it from over 4 months ago (ha). Finally, I got someone at HP who upgraded my case and right now as of July 15, 2011 my scanner still does not work, HP still has no clue they are making me troubleshoot my own printer (when I told them it was a software issue) and they said the only assistance I could get beyond this is I could get a replacement C410a...with the same software lol. So as I sit here and shake my head I wonder are they just trying to buy time until my HP warranty expires or are they really trying to help.SignedFrustrated

We homeschool and use pretty much any available surface to write on during lessons; white boards, sliding glass doors, windows, the glass on the table, tile, and Oilcloth. If it is handy, non-porus, and previously tried then we will use it. I needed a new laminator since my previous one was no longer with us, [R.I.P.]. So when I was able to get this one I jumped on the chance. So I have had the chance to use it a few times but others have made more use of it. So far it has done everything it was said to do. It warms up pretty quickly and does its job fairy quick as well. This fiberglass tape has thin fiber strands in two directions.  It is therefore almost impossible to tear.This is the perfect tape for wrapping boxes that you absolutely want to keep sealed, and which could otherwise rip open, due to weight, or bulkiness.  It also has great tensile strength and will hold itself together (when wrapped completely around something) far longer than regular tape.  This is not going to snap or come undone easily.On the negative side it is very expensive (probably 4 times the cost of regular good packing tape) but you are buying a "specialty" tape, which should not be used for regular packing.Use this if you worry that someone might open your box.  A box securely wrapped with this will not be able to be opened with anything other than a sharp object -no nosy college roommates (for example) tearing it open with their fingers.  Also, use this to securely large cardboard boxes that you are checking in for airline travel, or that you are shipping overseas.

I have some fine china that I need to store for a while and this bubble wrap fits the bill perfectly. The roll is perforated every 12" and is easy to separate. The 12" sheets make an excellent cushion between the china plates. They are thick enough to provide protection but not so thick as to be cumbersome. They also wrap nicely around the china cups and saucers. I use them for all the other items that I need to store as well and they provide a feeling of comfort that everything is safely stored.Excellent product at a reasonable price.
Am trying this out to see if penmanship improves for a 2nd grader.No results yet.  Will update.

I love these boxes... first off, there's no need for tape and with ordinary boxes, you end up folding the bottom, taping and praying it holds so your stuff doesn't end up coming out the bottom when you move the box - no worries about that with these - just pop that box open, push down the flap at the bottom, load it up and go.  The handy hand grips are perfect too... I hate trying to grab onto the bottom of the box or even the sides to move it and constantly worried about it slipping because my grip wasn't good enough.I've packed up lots of storage stuff in the past couple of weeks and it's so nice to just grab a box, fill it up, fold down the top and go - there's no worry about finding the tape, or the scissors, OK, so you do still have to find the pen to mark the box (which if you're like me you misplaced anyway) but these boxes are super simple to use and sturdy enough that packing your prized possessions is practically worry free.The best part is, once you've unpacked your stuff, just fold the box up (assuming it's not wet or some other disaster hasn't occured to it) and you can use them again.

SOOOO SOOO glad I bought this!I'm a teacher with basic technology in the classroom. I bought this set because I was tired of the classic red/blue/green/black dry-erase markers and I'm so glad I did.My board looks like it has life, a story and best of all it always looks cheerful now..:)I use the fuchsia as a substitute to what I would use the red for example for something very important/urgent/etc. and it still gets the point across but without my eyes feeling violated and my blood pressure going up from the red burning away..LOL..Just kidding!Honestly if you are looking for a set for your kids room, teenager its great but I use it for my board everyday and I love it just as much (it might even make you want to draw a butterfly).The colors really do make all the difference in the world to me (even though I would like to substitute the yellow with something else because you can barely see it when the sun is shining).All the colors last long, are vivid, bright and happy, they wipe off easily without leaving a trail of color or stain, the magnets are pretty strong, the sponge erases very well, and the markers do not smell.I definitely would buy the set again and I do recommend it.

As a sticky note junkie, when these came up on Vine, I of course ordered them! I had never really considered the idea of a retractable highlighter but they really solve the biggest problem with highlighters in general: Dried out tips. Additionally, being able to retract the tip between use means fewer stray marks on paper, clothing, etc.The colors are really excellent too, vibrant and a pleasure to use.The one issue with these highlighters (and the reason for a 1-point deduction) is that the writing on the side of them quickly wears off. Like, within a day. It's probably not a sure deal, but it's kinda sad to watch the iconic "Sharpie" logo quickly flake off, leaving you with generic-looking pens. Not a huge deal, but Sharpie could probably stand to use a better printing process.

These folders are much nicer than paper ones.  The write on section does readily accept pencil and regular pen (it is not completely smooth).  I was also able to readily erase the pencil, making reuse possible.  They are not as heavyweight as I would have expected, think heavyweight page protectors rather than stiff plastic.  It is nice to be able to see what is in them from the top as well.  However the top of the place you write on is about the same height as my regular tabbed paper folders, which means that if you file them with paper folders you will not be able to see the tab on these.And they really do not hold 100 sheets of paper.  What they mean by "gussets"  is that in the corner the very edge is not sealed all the way down to the bottom.  A little more than a half inch at the very bottom corner is not attached, which does allow more paper.  However, with one hundred sheets the edges of the folder do not reach the edge of the paper stack, so I would not say they "hold" 100 sheets.  With 50 they do.  This is with typical 24lb laser printer paper.I can see these being useful for carting papers around,  as they are sealed on two sides, so paper is less likely to fall out.Overall a nice product for projects you are working on, I am not sure I would use them as file folders because of the fact that the tab does not stick up high enough and because of the expense.

I was pretty skeptical about this product... it seemed to me that the only way to improve a stapler was to make it powered by someone other than me (and I have an electric stapler, too!)  However, this stapler does what it claims to do... it makes it a LOT easier to compress the stapler enough to cause it to staple.Although the information says the stapler is smaller and "standup," it is still hard to believe that a little stapler can have any power -- intuitively, you just figure it will be *harder* because there's not as long a lever.  However, this thing is engineered differently and only very light compression is enough to drive a staple quite as well as when one "pounds" one of those traditional desktop staplers!  I was able to staple through 25 pages of a textbook, one with rather heavy paper.  The desktop stapler could only manage 22 pages, and I had to "pound" it a couple of times to get that.Although the stapler couldn't manage more pages of my test book, it didn't jam... the staple just didn't go through the paper.  The desktop stapler, a name brand, did jam, with the staple stuck in the output slot, requiring the needle-nose pliers to remedy.I like it and intend to get one for work, too!

I have 3 kids in school and run a small business out of my home, so we tend to print a lot.  Before owning this printer, we also used a scanner to make copies and the modem in my PC for faxes - which were kind of a pain, but still saved quite a bit of money over using an ink-jet all-in-one.We've had this Panasonic KX-MB2030 printer for about a month now and have been extremely impressed with it.  Here are the things that we've liked:1) As with most laser printers I've used, the print speed is very good.2) The print quality, at 600x600 dpi, looks great.  My Brother HL-5240 is a bit better at 600x1200, but I don't typically use that higher resolution anyway.3) I LOVE the copier that is built into this printer.  What was once a pain using my scanner and printer together has become very simple.  The document feeder also works great for copying things that are multiple pages long.  For example, just a couple of days ago, an ATF agent was at my house and I was able to run off some quick copies while he waited - this would have been an embarrassingly long process before I had this printer.4) I don't receive or send many faxes, but I've found that this printer works great for that too.  This is an area where it's worth it to spend a few minutes with the product manual (which can be downloaded from Panasonic) to see all the features that this fax machine is capable of.5) The network interface is very handy.  I've gotten to the point where I hate plugging printers into a USB port because of problems that can occur when sharing printers.  I know several other reviewers have knocked this printer because there is no USB cable included, but I suspect many business users would probably just discard it anyway.Although I love the printer overall, there are a couple of things that could definitely be improved.1) This printer turns itself on every day at noon and runs through a loud warm-up cycle.  Even though it's been a month, it still catches me off-guard pretty much every day.2) These laser printers are much more economical to run than pretty much any ink-jet printer, but this particular model isn't the best laser out there for economy.  My Brother HL-5240 is quite a bit cheaper per page, although it doesn't have all the additional features of this printer.  Because of that, I'll probably continue to run both printers and mostly use new Panasonic KX-MB2030 for copies, faxes, and for my wife when she's in the upstairs office.If you are looking for a very easy to use, and low-cost multi-function printer for a home office - then I highly recommend this Panasonic KX-MB2030.
Great lead that actually writes smoothly and breaks less.  I have used a lot of lead in my mechanical pencils and these last the longest. I recommend them.

I really like laser printers compared to inkjet, because of the appearance and durability of the printed product.  I especially like that you can use a highlighter on laser printed documents without the ink smudging or running.  Try that with an inkjet.  My affinity for laser printers usually comes up against the high cost of color laser printers and the lack of Laser all-in-ones on the market.  Before getting this Samsung all-in-one, we used to have a black-and-white laser printer and a separate color inkjet all-in-one.  That combination took up way too much desk space and was a lot to maintain.  It also required a decision each time versus printing to color inkjet or gray laser.  A hard choice on some projects.  With this offering from Samsung, you don't have to make those trade-offs.This, CLX-3305FW, is fast (for the size and price), prints well, and has a very compact footprint.  After a couple weeks of use now, only thing that I don't like about it is the short life of the toner cartridges, especially the ridiculous 'starter' cartridges that came in the box.  You should price out the cost of replacement cartridges when you consider this printer's price, because you'll be replacing them soon after it arrives.Other than the short life of the cartridges, I like everything about this system.  It is extremely compact for a laser printer, especially for a color all-in-one.  Getting it set-up was fast and easy, and each of its functions work very well.  I had no problems hard-wiring it into my Linksys router and getting it installed on all our Windows 7 machines.  It scans, prints, faxes, and copies very well.  It isn't super fast, but is fine for home use.  The image quality both on prints and copies is better than I expected and as good as any other printer out there.  My opinion is that they are all pretty perfect at this point.  I haven't seen a functioning printer that didn't make wonderful prints in the last three years or so.I really like the compact size, which is perfect for home use.  If you know what you are getting into with toner cost (over $100 per 1000 sheets), and the numbers work for you, then I recommend this system.  It is very easy to use and does a great job.

3M has made the perfect foot rest that I've been looking for, for literally decades! Sitting for hours has always caused such terrible cramping, leg, ankle and foot pain, that I've always preferred standing jobs over sitting ones! Pretty much everything about the ordinary characteristics of this product, Post-it Notes, Original Cube, 3 Inches x 3 Inches, Fruit Design, 3 Cubes Per Pack (C300-F-3PK), that can be said has been said -- by many reviewers, and quite well -- so I thought I'd go after less ordinary characteristics.FIRST, you're not going to believe this but you do not have to lick the backs of these to get them to stick to many surfaces such as other pieces of paper and glass and plastic.  It's probably because of a manufacturing glitch that my particular batch turned out this way, but it's true.  That strip of adhesive on the back, like on an envelope, will stick to stuff without any moistening whatsoever!SECOND, to put to rest any dispute about how large these Post-it sheets are, I whipped out my calipers and measured the living heck out of them.  They are 70.19 millimeters square according to the average of the several measurements I just now took for each side, and I was being pretty careful.  70.19 mm divided by the number of millimeters in an inch, which is 25.4, means these sheets are 2.763 inches on a side, which is 7.9% smaller than the 3 inches advertised.This starts to add up.  A 3 by 3 sheet would be, of course, 9 square inches.  A 2.763 by 2.763 sheet is only 7.634 square inches, which is 15.176% smaller.  Another way to look at it is to consider that each sheet is smaller by 1.366 square inches (9 - 7.634).  Multiply that by 900 such sheets in the package and you get 1.229.4 square inches, or 8.538 square feet, or 94.9% of a square yard, which is the equivalent of 161.043 more sheets, for which I subtract one star.  (If they'd been advertised as 2.5 by 2.5 inches, I'd have ADDED a star.)THIRD, one virgin block is 39.39 millimeters tall (which means it is by no means a cube as advertised), which means that each of the 300 pages averages 0.1313 mm in height.  I wanted to know, as I'm sure you do too, how that compared to the width of a human hair, so I plucked and lined up several hundred of my hairs and measured the distance, which worked out to 100 micrometers each on average.  That means these sheets are 31.3% thicker than one human's hair, so now you know.This information is handier than you think.  For example, if by measuring you have determined that a particular table or chair leg is short by 3/7 of an inch (10.8857 mm), you can calculate that at 0.1313 mm each you will need 82.907 sheets to shim up that leg, which I would round up to 83 sheets.  I tried it, and it worked.  I cut 3/7ths of an inch (well, OK, 27/64ths) off of one leg of what was a perfectly level four-leg table and then shimmed it with 83 of these sheets.  No wobbling whatsoever.  Cool, eh?FOURTH, one virgin block weighs 146 grams (5.15 ounces), which means each sheet weighs 0.48666 grams.  This fact can be used to great advantage if you need to weigh something on a simple balance scale and you don't have any standard reference weights.  You simply place the object to be weighed on one pan and you place as many of these Post-it Note sheets as it takes on the other pan to get them to balance.  For example, if you want to know how much a quarter (5.7 grams) and a penny (2.5 grams) weigh, you'd drop them onto one pan and start removing these Post-it Note sheets one by one from the pad and dropping them onto the other pan till the pans balance.  In this case the number turns out to be just under 17 sheets, which times 0.48666 grams is the 0.289 ounces you would expect.  Test it yourself to see whether I'm right.FIFTH, at the price of $11.96 not counting any shipping charges and handling fees and sales taxes and import duties and international tariffs and sales commissions the price for each of the 900 sheets is 1.3 cents.SIXTH, taking testing to higher limits, I can tell you that if you duct tape one whole entire 300-sheet block of these Post-it Notes against your chest and allow your even drunker friend to shoot it point-blank with a .22 caliber pistol, you should cover your ears first because it's LOUD.Five stars for meeting all the other requirements of a Post-it Note minus one for not meeting one is 4 stars.

This lap desk was just the thing I needed for my netbook. I have a Dell Mini 9, and it gets very warm in my lap, as well as becoming more difficult to handle. As much as I love my netbook, it does have flaws that needed fixing, and this desk is the almost perfect solution.I don't think it would be very fun to use the textured, padded bottom with bare legs, but with legs covered with a thin sheet it's quite comfortable. The fan noise is hardly noticeable, and it keeps the computer cool enough. I previously had a cooling pad I picked up at a local bargain store, and while it kept the netbook cooler than this, the fan made a LOT more noise, and it didn't have speakers.The speakers have good sound quality-- maybe not home theatre caliber, but I can certainly hear them better than my netbook speakers, and the volume has the potential to blow you away. The side controls are clear, easy and convenient.It does have a couple of flaws. First, I can't leave this plugged into the netbook and use headphones simultaneously with the lapdesk on mute. I'm not sure if that's a result of my operating system or what. The other is that while there are tabs you can pull up in the front for a regular size laptop computer, they are inadequate for a netbook. When I use it at a more upward angle, I do experience some sliding around. The netbook needs to sit higher up for typing, and there is no way to secure it there.Overall however, it was a great purchase that I know I'll use for a long time. There's really no other accessory like it, and the flaws are not enough to keep me from using and enjoying it with my netbook. It's perfect for a 15 to 17 inch laptop, and still quite useful with smaller computers. Four stars for a great accessory that I'll probably appreciate even more with a full size laptop.

The Zowie G-TF gaming mouse pad is endorsed by noted Swedish gamer, "SpawN" and features speed mousing over a cloth material, rather than PVC.  It is enormous in size and provides ideal features for gaming.PROS:- Large mousing surface- Smooth and fast- Durable- Water resistant- Non-slip rubber baseCONS:- PriceyWhen Gamespot, an old vendor connection I had, provided me with my very first gaming mouse pad, I was only beginning my foray into heavy FPS gaming (think Unreal Tournament and Half-Life).  That mouse pad was made out of a PVC material (plastic) and was textured for easy gliding.  At the time, the best mice were optical, and I had a dual-optical Logitech mouse.  Needless to say, that combination allowed me to frag my share of foes and become very very good at UT.  Fast forward ~10 years.The idea behind the PVC mouse pads of yesteryore was to provide a slick gliding surface for mice.  Then came the large surface areas to allow wide swipes of the mouse without running out of space.  Alas, the hard PVC surfaces were not that comfortable but there were no other options until recently.  Now we have manufacturers who have combined the comfort and convenience of cloth mouse pads with the performance and large surface area of PVC pads.  Also keep in mind that we are two generations removed from optical technology, having passed laser only recently with Blue Track from Microsoft and Darkfield laser from Logitech.  These tracking advances have probably contributed to gaming far greater than any mouse pad before or since.The Zowie G-TF cloth mouse pad is very good for gamers and I highly recommend it.  I have used it with my Logitech G9 gaming mouse (laser) as well as a Microsoft Darkfield laser mouse.  Both mice glide nice and smooth and the cloth feels nice on the wrists.  The special coating is water resistant as well.  The edges are rolled and triple stitched for durability and comfort.  The surface area is enormous and can fit the largest of laptops on top of it with room to spare.  When I initially looked at it and was gathering my thoughts for the review, my eyes wandered to my cloth drink coaster on my desk and could not help but think that the mouse pad was essentially a high tech drink coaster :)  Except that the G-TF will help you become fragtastic!

I am currently enrolled in college, and I like using pens to take my notes. Unfortunately, I tend to need to revise my notes a lot, and pen simply doesn't allow for that. Pencil is fine for math class, but for other classes, I prefer pens. I have tried MANY erasable pens before, and the results were not satisfactory for me. They would write OK, but erasing was always touch and go. Sometimes the pen would erase fine, sometimes it would leave ink residue, sometimes it would smear the ink all over the area I was erasing, and sometimes it would rub a hole into the paper.I gave up on using erasable pens until I heard about these. They use gel ink, so the issue with not writing well would be solved. I was skeptical still of their erasing ability, but I decided to give them a try anyway.These pens are AMAZING! First, they write no different than any gel ink pen. The writing is smooth and bold. But what I really like is that they erase perfectly clean without smudging or rubbing a hole into the paper! The pen has a rubberized eraser that uses friction to remove the ink. So not only is the erasing clean, but because the eraser itself isn't removing the ink, the eraser produces no by-product and does not ever need to be replaced. So this pen will write and erase until the ink is gone!The pens are not refillable. That is the only downside that I could possibly think of. These are my preferred pen for class now! I highly recommend this product if you want to use an erasable pen that is truly erasable!

Thankfully, their template program is incredibly easy to navigate and very user intuitive.  Avery's template program also offers some wonderful graphics to help customize your label as well as the option to upload your own photos or graphics.  When it comes time to print, another window opens up with a PDF file that you can save to your desktop for future use.After creating the designs I wanted, I printed off a page of labels.  As the label color is that of medium-brown kraft paper (think a couple of shades darker than a paper grocery bag), not all colors will work well; some of the lightest ones barely even show up. These kraft brown labels are more for dark and shaded graphics.As I mentioned earlier, these labels are thicker than Avery's typical white mailing labels.  Even peeled off of the backing, they feel quite substantive.  For crafters who make and sell items like soaps, candles, canned/bottled/jarred goods, etc. these labels are very professional looking and stick incredibly well to almost every surface.  Removing them - not so easy.I've already used up most of the pack I received via Vine, and am hoping that my local office supply stores have them in stock.  Reorganizing the pantry was made a little bit more fun by designing and using my own labels.  I've also used them for address return labels, which makes for quite an eye-catching letter.  These labels also make very pretty and professional looking book plaques.  At first when I received these labels, I wasn't sure what I would use these labels for.  Now? Previous to requesting this tape to review through Vine, my experience of tapes had been limited to duct tape, transparent adhesive tape, and packing tape of various thicknesses and strength. I had never before encountered a vinyl tape like this one.I requested the color red, and it is a bright, clear, very attractive red.According to the Scotch website, this tape is made of uPVC with a rubber resin adhesive. The initials "uPVC" stand for unplasticised polyvinyl chloride. The good news about uPVC, compared to PVC, is that it contains no phthalates or BPA, making it much safer.  Because it outgasses far less than PVC, uPVC is used to make dental retainers and mouthguards. I have an extremely sensitive sense of smell, and tend to easily get headaches from outgassed chemicals. When I put this tape right under my nose, unlike for PVC products, I barely smell it, and what I do smell doesn't bother me.A resin adhesive such as this tape uses is very durable and strong. It forms a tight bond very quickly when it is applied to a surface. It is highly resistant to damage from heat, cold, UV rays and many different chemicals. It is so resistant to moisture, it is ideal for underwater applications.The main reason I wanted to try this tape is for applications when good, old duct tape is failing me, because the adhesive doesn't stick very well, in particular, on my plastic,split keyboard. It has harsh, jagged edges, and I had unsuccessfully been using duct tape to put over those edges to protect myself from scratches. Unfortunately, the adhesive on the duct tape very quickly would wear out, and I frequently had to replace it. So far, so good, with this vinyl tape. It looks a lot better than the duct tape, and its adhesive is holding up well on the plastic.In order to cut this tape, I used an inexpensive pair of kitchen scissors. It cut easily. Even better, unlike many other types of tape, I had no trouble pulling it away from itself when I used the tape for the first time. The manufacturer obviously knew this, because there was no special starter tab of cardboard or other substance to help the consumer find and detach the tape from itself. On the other hand, that does make me wonder: What does that ease say about the durability of the adhesive on vinyl that it is so simple to detach the tape from itself, a vinyl surface?

This review was carried out by connecting the 4540 to my Mac Pro running Snow Leopard and to a MacBook Pro running Lion, both through a WiFi connection. iPrint capabilities were tested using an iPhone 4.Setup was fairly quick, with installation of software under Snow Leopard via an included CD-ROM, then by upgrading to the most current drivers from Epson's online support site. Under Lion, all the drivers are automatically downloaded from Apple, so there's no need for the CD-ROM. Finally, with a USB connection to the laptop, I upgraded the firmware in the 4540 so that the printer would work with AirPrint.Once all the software was installed, the ink cartridges inserted, and the additional paper tray added to the base, we were ready to go. The connection to the wireless network was a bit less than intuitive as the password requires entry on a telephone pad equivalent on the touchscreen. The telephone pad has buttons that read things like 8 TUV. To choose the letter "T" requires one touch of the button, but where are the lower-case letters? "t," as it turns out, requires that you push the same button four times. To get to "8" requires 7 pushes of the same button. To choose "t" twice in a row requires that you push the button four times, then hit the space bar, then back up a space, and then hit the button four more times. It took some trial and error to figure this out. Anyway, we got through the password entry and the unit was now available wirelessly for all computers on the network.Printing itself is fast, as advertised. Remember that inkjets aren't laserwriters so small text is not brilliantly perfect as it is with a laser. That said, this is as good an inkjet printer as I've seen in terms of overall clarity and consistency. Two-sided output was particularly quick. Paper choices include two separate 250-page lower trays as well as a manual feed slot in the back that can hold a smaller number of pages (about 80).Printing from the iPhone was simple, and the Epson app also allows scanning. For instance, let's say I have four double-sided pages to scan. I'd place the four sheets in the ADF (automatic document feeder), which can hold 30 sheets. From the iPhone, I can give a scan command, instructing the unit to scan B&W;, grayscale, or color, and single or doublesided. I can also adjust the resolution if desired (75 or 150 dpi). The scan takes place quickly, with the unit easily handling the double-sided scans. Everything then outputs to my iPhone from which I can store the document, email it, or print it (perhaps on another printer if so desired). Naturally, I could do this from my Mac as well by simply running Preview software (which you may not have known allows for scanning).Incoming and outgoing faxes can be handled easily from the front panel or from your Mac. Copies can be made in either B&W; or color using the two buttons on the front panel. I found it particularly nice to have this as a hard-wired button - a quick color copy here and there is a perfect application of this unit (recognizing that each page will cost you about 8 cents). For B&W; copies, again, this is a quick solution, though if I'm making 10+ copies of a page, I'll use the Canon laser copier that I have next to the Epson.Photo printing: I printed several 4x6's from iPhoto. On the good side, this printer is incredibly quick, generating a full color 4x6 in high definition in under 40 seconds. The prints are perfectly acceptable, but this should not be your printer if your plan is to use it primarily as a photo printer. The prints look fine at arm's length, and the color spectrum is accurately reproduced using high quality ink, but on close inspection, you'll quickly see inkjet artifact (lines and dots that make it clear that the print was made using an inkjet). For sharing prints with family, or for business purposes, this is fine, but these are not the very high quality prints that you'd get from, say, Epson's Professional Imaging line. Given the speed, though, this printer is very good at running off quick prints to determine if you want to take the time to print something in higher quality elsewhere.The overall build quality of the unit is good - better than low-end inkjets, but there's a lot of plastic here, so some of the adjustments within paper trays are a bit on the lightweight side. That said, I had no paper feed difficulties, even with doublesided scanning and printing, and out of the box, everything worked as promised. The manual is provided in printed form, but is a bit brief. Additional information is available from Epson's support site, and I visited that site to determine, for instance, how to choose which paper tray to use from within the Mac's print command window. I noted a brief problem trying to install the Fax capabilities under Snow Leopard initially, but this problem vanished after I installed the latest software that I downloaded from Epson's support site.In summary, there were some very minor issues as described above, but overall this is a strong entry from Epson that will work quite well in both a small office and the well-networked home office.

Scotch Bi-Directional Filament Tape is "heavy-duty" by the company's own description. This packing tape is reinforced with fiberglass yarns, encased in the tape in a grid pattern. The tape is impossible to tear, which is the point, but you will need scissors to cut it. It is 5.7 mil thick and clear, apart from the fiberglass grid, so that graphics and bar codes may be read through it. At least that is what Scotch claims, but I think I will stick to using clear packing tape to cover bar codes and addresses.The filament tape is intended for strapping, bundling, and reinforcing boxes for shipping, particularly if the contents are heavy. I intend to use it for boxes of books, but this tape would be helpful for any box whose contents are heavy enough that the box is in danger of losing its bottom when picked up or of bursting if it is dropped. I've had a few of those delivered in a mail bag after the contents spilled. If you seal all of the edges of the box, this filament tape should prevent that problem. Reinforced gummed paper tape also works, but the filament tape is more convenient.I compared it to Scotch Shipping & Packaging Tape and found that the filament tape adheres a little better. Scotch claims that it will adhere to "a wide variety of surfaces, including metal, plastic, and fiberboard." If you're worried about adhesion, you can always wrap the tape completely around the box. The Bi-Directional Filament Tape is expensive but probably worth the cost if you ship or store heavy items. It may save you having to file a few insurance claims.

I got rid of my last scanner about 12 years ago. Back then, they were slow, worked poorly with slides and negatives, and the drivers caused unmitigated grief for your computer. So it was with some trepidation that I installed the V600 onto our MacBook running Snow Leopard and HP laptop running Vista.I need not have worried. The included software performed flawlessly, and the scanner creates amazing scans even when using the fully automatic settings. I have uploaded three scans, all using the automatic settings:* White horse, scanned from a print made from a digital camera* Candy scanned from objects on the scanner bed* A dog's tail, also scanned from the the live objectAll three scans (especially the candy and dog's tail) are courtesy of my 12-year old daughter, who is getting very creative with the V600. Epson has delivered software that makes the whole scanning experience easy while still delivering high quality results.The film scanner uses special trays (included) and a separate light source, and delivers 6400 dpi. The automatic results are decent, actually a lot better than my neighbor's scanner that cost three times as much as this one. But for great film or negative results, grab a copy of VueScan on the web. Scanners are actually very complex animals, with color profiles a myriad of available settings (which are mostly kept under the hood of the included Epson software). If you want to tweak your results, VueScan is the best solution. It directly supports the V600, and includes profiles for dozens of different negative and transparency film stocks. The results are substantially better than what you can get with the included software.I haven't found a flaw with this product yet. 5 stars for sheer delight.

I have been using mechanical pencils for many years, as I prefer them to wooden pencils. Specifically, I have been using 0.5 mm lead pencils for drawing fine lines and graphs which was a necessity in math classes when I was in college. This is far and away the most amazing mechanical pencil I have ever used. It's not perfect but it comes close.My very first observation about this pencil is that it is very light which for me is a very minor negative. I have always liked writing instruments that have a little weight to them, whether it's a pencil or pen. This is a personal preference, though. If you really like a pencil that is very light and easy to hold, this pencil may very well meet your need. If you prefer a weighty pencil, though, this might be a small disappointment.The claim to fame for this pencil is a rotating plastic gear inside that turns the lead when you write, so that no chiseled edge forms and the tip stays uniform and sharp. You can actually see the gear through the clear plastic grip on the barrel of the pencil though it takes a close look to see how it works. It is not dissimilar to the way a clicker pen works in that opposing sets of plastic teeth allow one-way rotation of the mechanism. When you write you do have to lift the pencil from the writing surface periodically and the change in pressure causes the mechanism to turn.By tapping gently on the tip of the pencil you can watch the gear inside turn - it really does rotate.I did a side-by-side comparison between the Uni Kuru Toga and another mechanical pencil I have used for years. The old mechanical pencil works fine, though the lead does form a chiseled end and slowly the lines become wider and softer as I write. To maintain a sharp, crisp edge, I have to rotate the pencil in my hand. The Kuru Toga, however, maintained thin, precise lines no matter how I held it, never once needing to be turned to adjust for a flat end because the flat end never formed.I do have a tendency to bear down with my writing implements and as such I frequently break the tips from the leads in my other mechanical pencils. So far I have not had that problem with this pencil, though I am not sure if this is a function of keeping the lead short or the lead being better - the pencil comes with a cartridge of leads that are supposed to "diamond infused".The Uni Kuru Toga does not have a comfort grip, which is unfortunate, though there are foam grips out there that will fit this pencil without too much difficulty. Adding a comfort grip would be the one real change I would make to this pencil.The Uni Kuru Toga is far and away the best pencil I have ever used. It maintains a sharp point and the leads are harder to break (at least they seem to be). It is more expensive than typical mechanical pencils but the higher cost is not unreasonable and I would consider well worth the cost. If you need a pencil that maintains consistently fine lines no matter how long you write, this is an excellent choice.

There are pockets for each month to put them in.  It is also a great place to build a budget, meaning estimate the amount of money in each category that you are going to spend. So, just speaking for me, this is a duplicate record and doesn't help me.There is also a checklist at the top of each page for things you may want to do each month. Hmm, how to do a serious in-depth review of tape? Let's start at the beginning.  This three-pack of Scotch GiftWrap (the solid spelling is 3m's) comes in a purple carton that offers its own review: ". . . . features a unique satin finish that disappears on most gift wrap papers. Makes your gifts look great! Easy to dispense and sticks securely."The first thing I noticed is that the purple starter strip on each roll of tape lines up at a different point. I managed to grab one and pull the tape across the inch long gap so I can scrape it across the jagged plastic teeth for severing it. Why do all tape dispensers have this long gap between the roll and the cutting surface? Invariably, the exposed tape picks up dust, lint, dirt, even small insects and then has to be discarded (and the extra size seems a wasteful use of extruded plastic). Plus I tend to leave a fingerprint on the tape no matter how hard I try not to do so. 3M has a chance here to innovate instead of just replicate, but I'll expect a cut from the production savings.Now in my tests, the unique satin finish actually disappears better (if there can be degrees of disappearance) on darker paper but shows up quite clearly on very light paper and on light areas of patterned gift paper. Are most gift wrap papers dark? I'm not sure 3M can substantiate its claim here.On to "Makes your gifts look great!" I have to take issue with the semantics. This tape is not going to be applied to most gifts, so it really does not affect how they look. I know that 3M means the wrapped gift, but honestly, nothing makes a wrapped gift for me look that good. I've never mastered the folding and sizing of the wrapping paper, and it is a running joke in my family that my skills in this area are marginal at best.But this extra-wide tape does make it easier to seal gift wrapping, whether one folds the paper with the precision of an origami expert or needs to span a revealing gap where the ends of the paper do not quite meet.Except for the inevitable fingerprints and occasional insect carcass, this tape is pretty easy to dispense until it detaches from the front of the dispenser, reattaches to the roll along an invisible seam, and triggers a torrent of cursing. It does stick securely as long as adults, not toddlers or cats, tug on the seams.Here is another point that may matter in some situations: this tape shares a quality with Silly Putty: it will lift ink from newsprint and from documents printed on inkjet printers, and sometimes it transfers that ink to other surfaces.When all is said and done it's good to have a few rolls of this tape handy, and I'm sure we will run through a couple of rolls during the flurry of gift giving that occurs throughout November and December--several family members had birthdays and of course there is Christmas (sometimes lamely called "The Holidays" as if these were the only holidays over the course of a year).

The C4280 has been in my home office for ten months now.  I've got the software loaded on three laptops ranging in age from 4 years to six months old; all of which are running Windows XP.  We've been using it for work, personal and school projects without any problems.The scanner has a couple of modes.  The document mode had a couple of surprises. I'm on the faculty at a university where thankfully (almost) all of our classrooms have been updated to use whiteboards instead of chalkboards, but unfortunately the only whiteboard markers they provide or sell in the campus stores are the lowest end Expo ones. I've been trying these markers out in my class this quarter, and the students I both agree that these are a huge step up. Why?* No bothersome odor at all. Even some of the ones we've had marked "low odor" from other brands have still been a problem, but these haven't bothered any of us.* The colors are vibrant and dark enough that you can see them across the classroom. I've tried some brands where only the black and blue ones can be seen from more than a couple feet away, but in this neon colors set, every color except the neon green was dark and clear from across the room -- even the orange and pink, colors which are often hard to see with most brands. Having a variety of good colors to work with is really helpful when we want to be able to color code what we are putting up on the whiteboard.* The markers glide more smoothly than any others I've tried -- it's like they have more of a wet feel than most dry erase markers -- but they don't smear easily, either.* All of the colors erase easily from the board, without needing to scrub, and without leaving streak marks.* We also appreciated being able to see how much ink is left in each.My only concern is that the design of the markers sometimes makes me afraid they will spring a leak in my bag, so I've started carrying them in a plastic bag that can be stashed in my bag. Probably a good practice anyway. I've never actually had one leak at this point -- and it may just be that being able to see the ink wells makes them look more fragile than they are -- but I feel as safer carrying them that way.

The concept here is a single file folder with three dividers (making four separate sections). Many times, I have gathered a bunch of related papers that I'd like to file in one folder but the papers still need to be organized into subdivisions.  For example, in my "Car" folder, I might want a section for insurance, for maintenance, or for the pink slip and other purchase information. In the past I have used paperclips, which always seem to fall off eventually. The folder is open on three sides, so it could be easy to lose a tiny scrap of paper.Smead touts these folders as "expandable," but I'm not sure how useful that particular feature is. The folders are stiff and if you try to put something thick in them, they rebel. Could they be to help pull the sections apart? Are they vents? I was mystified, so I wrote to Smead and asked.  Here's the response I received: "The holes in the organizer folder are there so the user can quickly and easily see which sections have papers in them and which sections do not."  There you have it.

Speaking as a loyal Panasonic phone owner for years... I'm a bit surprised by the flood of good reviews on this phone, my experience has been the opposite.When I saw some of the negative reviews, I glanced over and then dismissed them, figuring they were just the exception based on a purchaser getting a lemon or folks that didn't understand the technology very well.  The minority seems to have it right in this case.PROBLEM:The primary problem was an issue with the sound of my voice cutting in and out when I was on a call (your voice is fed back through the handset speaker normally). Many people may not realize that phones normally feedback your voice into the ear speaker until it ceases to work properly (as with these phones).  When it happened, my first reaction was that the line had dropped and I would start saying "are you there, are you there?".  When the other person invariably said "yes", I began to realize it was the phone malfunctioning.  Another problem is static on the phone occurring randomly on calls.  We've never had that problem until these new phones were put in.I am returning the phones because of these two issues.  However, there are some pretty glaring design issues I'd also like to draw your attention to.DESIGN DISAPPOINTMENTS (design points that make me wonder, with lots of frustration, what Panasonic engineers were thinking):-- Unlit keypad (I knew about this from other reviews, but seriously, previous Panasonic phones had lit keyboards, what genius decides to go backwards on a key feature like this)-- Non-dedicated key for voicemail (yes, this phone has an answering machine, but I can't buy a non-answering machine phone anymore, thank you Panasonic... they could at least recognize that a fair amount of people will use voicemail and design with that in mind, their previous phones had that)-- Cheap feel to the phone itself (felt and looked like a cheap plastic kids toy)-- Clunky menus.  The menus on the handset were not natural to flow through.  It is not that hard to take the time to make use and flow of menus an easy and non-confusing thing.  These felt like an after-thought.The sad thing?  I am going to stay with Panasonic since they still have the best quality phone in my mind, it just happens to be a phone they no longer produce and sell, the KX-TGA520M series phone.  Looks like I'll be shopping eBay and Amazon marketplace.Really disappointed with the direction Panasonic is going in with their phones.

I love Avery products and this ticket stock is fantastic.  I have a Brother color laser printer connected to my Windows Vista machine and it fed through the printer fine and goes through the duplexer without falling apart. Also, the ticket stubs come apart wonderfully after printing.  Where Avery seriously fails is in the ticket template design.I had wanted to try this on both an inkjet and laser printer since it is rated for both. Therefore, I planned on using my boyfriend's inkjet printer with his MAC OS machine.  However, for some reason I was unable to locate the 16154 label at avery.com/print using Safari so I nixed that idea.  So when I got home I tried my computer and printer.  At home with IE 9 I was able to load the template. The problem is the template is not totally intuitive and that started the below problems:- I was only able to edit either all the tickets or one ticket at a time.  What I really wanted to do was edit several tickets at a time because I wanted a quantity of 3, 3, 2, and 2 tickets all with different designs on the same page. I had to do that individually unfortunately.- After I thought I was finished, I previewed the results and got a PDF to print.  However, the first set of tickets printed in black and white and the PDF printer settings were grayed out for the color so I could not change the options in the dialog box.  I had to cancel out and reload the PDF for some reason and then I got the option to change to color.  However, for a while I was fussing with my printer thinking the problem was on my end when it wasn't.- Once I was able to change the print settings in the PDF to color, I printed all the tickets. That is when I noticed another problem.- I made a mistake and although I thought I was done when I previewed my tickets, I did not realize a ticket numbering sequence was missing.  There was nothing that warned me I wasn't done. However, I did not notice this until I used up all 20 sheets in the package and I went to separate the tickets - now I'll have to number both sections by hand.- I also feel that while the template is created and before printing starts, there should be a warning to remind users to insert card stock correctly - just in case.In summary, the product itself is of high quality but because the template is so poorly designed and non-intuitive, there will be a lot of frustration and waste of product until some controls are instituted to ensure one doesn't forget anything and ease of use is refined.  The card stock gets 5 stars and template gets 1 star from me.

If using a POTS or VOIP line at home/office, this isn't a bad choice for you. It's a dial-pad you can use with any headset with a 2.5mm jack (the one that's included is OK -- I prefer other styles.) Parties I've chatted with on the other side report generally good call quality, though this unit, unlike many corded headset amplifiers, does NOT provide the option to adjust your outgoing (read: microphone) volume. The voice quality is clear (thanks to the DECT 1.8GHz technology) -- and you won't pickup any of the interference common on the 2.4GHz band. I was able to take this phone at least 300 feet OUTSIDE of my home -- and that's with the base being placed on the floor far from any exterior walls. That's definitely impressive and on the better end of cordless phones.Also realize you MUST use a headset when using this phone (it takes a few seconds to put a headset on, compared with just picking up a handset.) There are decent cordless phone systems, despite being larger, have a headset jack along with a standard handset and provide similar call quality -- at the same or lower price.I'm personally only using this with basic, metered rate phone service at home for LONG calls, so I have little use for the caller ID/voicemail options that are presented on the phone. On the surface, however, they don't appear very difficult to use. The LCD screen readout is clear with the backlight and it isn't terribly difficult to navigate the menus. On the other hand, however, the buttons (including the numbers and TALK/END) are very small, even smaller than some itty bitty mobile phones I've see around.Bottom line -- if you're going to be spending a lot of time on the phone, looking for cordless freedom, and don't mind having to put a headset on every time you use the phone, it's a good choice. But there are other quality DECT phones with a headset jack (though you'll have to purchase the headset) that provide a similar experience.
