Tipping it back and forth in your hands like some kind of new-age yoga exercise. The only guarantee is that you will make a mess. HEY, FREE CONFETTI! Why not locate the access door on an end so you can simply tip the hole puncher and empty it out? Or make the entire bottom cover removable. But, no. This is such a stupid design flaw that it ruins what might have been a decent product.>>Convenient ruler with paper guide.The paper guide is non-adjustable, just like the rest of the product. And would it have been that difficult to include metric measurements? Maybe I'm still in a bad mood about the last feature.>>Non-slip rubberized base.If we're being honest, it's a plastic base with two small rubber feet. But it doesn't slip much, in any case.

Even though one of the corners was damaged during shipping, it still did its job in organizing desktop clutter. Although it has labels for the slots, this convenience is not apparent on the Amazon photo of the product. Manila folders fit easily. All in all it is a handy simple design.
it served its purpose but was a bit sticky. they are needed & were used properly. nothing big to complain about

I bought this paper after reading the reviews and wanting a slightly heavier paper for my Epson workforce 840 printer/copier.  I'm in love.  This paper is so smooth and such a beautiful white (100).  Whether I print color or black, it comes through clearly and crisply.  I will never go back to a cheaper paper.

I receive boxes daily which contain heavy items. Most contain staples on the outside to  reinforce them, A regular staple remover won't work well and even heavy duty ones, till now, haven't done well for me. To be fair, I think that when it come to staple removers some just have the right heft for a particular user. Not all feel the same. This one simply works well for both me and my spouse (who deals with his own share of boxes, although not nearly as many as I do.What I like:1. The lower part slips easily under the staple. No wasted time maneuvering it into place.2. It has the heavy duty strength to remove staples easily.3. Finally, it has a satisfying heft and that is an elusive but important factor for me. Just like a pen which just feels better than others, becoming a favorite, this remover just feels right.

Brilliant ideas usually have simplicity in their kernel. This product is not an exception.There is always the good old notepad application on your computer, you might say. You'd think you don't need paper when you're working on your laptop in a public place, like a coffee house or a bookstore, and suddenly someone you know happens by, or someone you just met, and you find yourself not feeling very comfortable for anyone to be touching your keyboard to jot something down. Or to simply draw up an idea, you may find yourself needing for a piece of paper. Wouldn't it be great if your laptop had a simple, unobtrusive, yet elegant container unassumingly strapped with non-damaging adhesives on the back of your computer's screen? One that you can pull out a post-it sheet like a tissue paper with another one popping out right away. That's exactly what this product is.In fact, I need a post-it right now...There! I got one.Does...does anyone have a pen I can use?

These boxes assemble easily and the best part is that no tape is required.  They are made of sturdy cardboard with handles on the sides and large areas for writing in the contents.  I like that the assembly instructions are hidden on the bottom of the box so that you don't have to look at them during storage.  The boxes are great for storage of heavy items like books and file folders (I have the small size) but are not so good for frequently accessed items since the top is not that easy to open.  The design is great for long-term storage or for moving items.  They should hold up to be used multiple times.

Cleverly designed moving boxes that require no tape, and fold up flat for storage. I love that these are designed to be reusable!They look like a typical bankers box in the picture, but they are much sturdier than the ones I've purchased in the past.

Bought this stapler at a local office supply store and love it! This stapler is just perfect for a large or small office. And I have found that I use this as my dependable, everyday stapler. Most of the time, I just have to staple less than say six sheets of paper together, however, I recently tried this with a small manual that I printed that had 17 pages, it stapled it very well.And since this stapler does not jam, and it is of superb quality, this is the best stapler I have used ever!Highly recommend this to all!

I purchased the holder with this twine and loved it so much I just had to get more. This is much denser that the twine you purchase at the grocery store. That could be a pro or a con. I use it all over the house and for different purposes. Gotta love Cotton. Now I need to get another holder so I can have it in my craft room too.
I got these to mark up wall calendars in the office for various events. The colors are visible from across the room.

I'd thought that it would be easier to wrap presents with this, and then as I was wrapping a small gift that soon looked like I wrapped it in duct tape because the strands are so long (2 inches).For larger packages it worked fine (though ti fell apart on me a couple times), but overall, I did not think it was vastly superior to the much more affordable scotch tape that I normally use.

I truly like the ability to print labels and stamps from one printer without having to change rolls.  I found the new version 8.5 software buggy and frustrating.  Some parts of it simply don't work, period.  Note that I am using this on Mac systems, so maybe this is not true for Windows.  But, I wanted to move addresses from my Mac contacts list to a new Dymo list.  The software manual says you can select multiple addresses, choose "Copy to Dymo Address Book," and you will get a Save As box and be able to save them to the Dymo book.  Not so.  It simply moves one label at a time over.  It simply will NOT move multiple selections.  Very frustrating.  Other aspects that are annoying are how the selection features work in the editing screen.  If you open up a new blank label, you cannot select and remove the original text box.  Trying to click on it does not work.  Adding an "address object" field still does not let you remove the original text square, and they print overlapping each other.  So, if you want to do an address label, for example, you really have to open up one of the sample designs and modify it, there's no easy way to create your own from a blank slate.  Annoying.I am personally not troubled by having to use Dymo brand stamp labels.  The other major stamps by mail company, Stamps.com, wanted 15.95 a month and still required me to use their labels.  I see this as the classic Gillette shaver marketing technique.  Charge little for the razor/printer, sell the blades/stamp rolls.  I do not have to pay any monthly fee with the Endicia service.  Works for me.I just hope they sometime get all the bugs out of the software!

This binder has a 5 year guarantee on it, which is nice to know the manufacturer stands behind it (albeit wether it makes it to 5 years or not is a different story).  It's built quite solidly, the cover folds away instead of being attached to the rings.  The rings are D shaped to hold paper more easily and better.  It's a good quality, really thick binder.

Great size. Quality is good. The pattern is nice. The plastic that holds the cards seems sturdy. I feel the hinge may be a problem in the long run as it has a bit of give to it, which is worst if the organizer isn't completely full. Also the term organizher is annoying and completely unnecessary.

When this arrived I was surprised at how heavy the box was because I expected it to be a flimsy plastic piece of equipment. Boy was I wrong, this is actually heavy duty and of great quality. It seems to be mostly made of metal. It's not too heavy to move around or anything, but it's not something that is going to break easily. This thing will take from a 6mm to a max comb size of 12mm, but I used Fellowes 8mm plastic binding combs for my first project along withFellowes Transparent Presentation Binding Cover, PVC Material, 8.75 x 11.25 Inches, Clear, 25 per Pack (52309). The instructions are illustrated perfectly and the captions underneath the illustrations explain step-by-step exactly what to do, and that's what I need. The instructions show to insert the comb into the device first and stretch them out, but I suggest punching all the holes in your covers and documents first. I found that my comb was a bit stretched from me leaving it stretched open while I figured out what I was doing and punched all the holes. I adjusted the guide to where I wanted my punched holes to start. The instructions suggest putting no more than 7 sheets of paper in the punch part at a time, so that's what I did. I punched the front and back covers at the same time with ease and they were the thick plastic kind. The paper and plastic from punching the holes went into a neat little waste drawer underneath and not all over the place. So, I just could dump it when I was done. It also has a storage drawer for the combs with a sizing part to tell what size comb you are using. I inserted the comb to where the loops faced me and the binding was facing the back, then I slowly pulled the lever down to open the comb up. It was really easy to operate. Don't open the comb all the way up. You have to have enough of the ends up to put your covers and paper on, so take that into consideration when you're stretching it back. Lining the paper up to get the holes on the comb was a little tedious at first, but it didn't take me long to get the hang of it. Since I had left my comb stretched open so long, I had to kind of squeeze them back tight with my fingers once it was out, but that's completely my fault for leaving it stretched too wide and for so long. Overall, I really recommend this for home or office. It's a high quality product for sure. I'm a huge crafter and I can't wait to use it to make books for my son and cookbooks for Christmas gifts. The possibilities are endless.

Avery Removable Label Pads are great!  I used the label pads to label my file cabinet folders.  I change my mind often while organizing files and with these labels, I can just remove and rename a folder easily.  They are also large enough to fit several words written in large font, which helps me easily spot the folder I am seeking.Each pack includes three different color labels.  They are all attached together into one pad, which helps keep the labels organized.I found these simple to use and quite helpful with organization and recommend them to anyone who needs to label files.

These are a super tough, attractive version of the familiar paper dividers we had in school.  They are Multi-color 5 tab dividers for a three ring notebook.  The tabs are extra wide so you can actually fit your entire heading on it.  If you have a presentation binder these make it look professional, clean and neat, and separate out the various subjects.There are two ways to format, print, the titles onto the tabs.  You can let Wilson Jones format your pages for you at their website.  Just type your tab titles into the website template and print.  It's fast and easy.  Or you can use your own word processing software and follow the directions included in the package.  These aren't labels you want to write on.  These are for a really professional look to a presentation binder.If you are creating a professional, sales or other type of presentation binder these will add the impressive finishing touch

These boxes are not the best for moving.  We recently completed a 1300 mile move across the country.  We boxed our own items using a combination of these boxes and Amazon shipping boxes, and then packed them into a semi-trailer to be hauled across the country.  It wasn’t our first move, so we have a general idea how to pack, and used lots of bubble wrap and other packing materials.When we opened the trailer at our new location, I was disappointed to see that the majority of these boxes looked pretty rough.  They were dented and smashed, far more than the Amazon shipping boxes.  I was worried about the contents, but the items inside fared better than the boxes.  In all, we ended up scrapping only a single lamp.Usually we save our moving boxes…cut them down, fold them up, and then hand them off to the next person we know who is moving.  These went to the recycling bin.  These would not be our top choice for future moves.The one nice thing about these was having everything shipped together in a single kit.  Although we had lots of bubble wrap, tape, and a marker, it was convenient to have it all arrive together.  Plus, we were able to use the shipping box as another moving box.

Note that mine came damage, most likely because it was rattling around an Amazon box with no padding or air bubbles or anything - all the corners were bent.But, overlooking the packaging mishap, this is a nice binder.  Very easy to open with 1 finger (just a bottom snap, not the top and bottom ones you have to do at the same time.  And, very difficult to open UNLESS you're using that bottom snap, which is very good - it probably won't come open when you don't want it to.  The 2-level pockets on the inside are also very nice - everybody always wants a couple of those; not sure why they aren't just standard in every binder.  It's not hi-tech...Overall, very nice and quality binder.  Corners aren't quite strong enough to be tossed around in an unpadded box, though.

These are the best mailers and very reasonable.  The tackiness of the peel and stick is so strong I do not need to add any extra security tape. So I am saving even more money in not buying more product to mail.

This tape is thin, and arguably not as sturdy as the last roll I had from another American tape company (I don't recall the brand).  But, the adhesive is wonderful, allowing the tape to both come off the roll easily and then stick wonderfully.  The tape also has a weird pattern in the roll going side to side.  If it is not a defect, then my guess it is there to keep the tape coming off easy and not losing a thread portion on the edge as duct tape and cloth tape is apt to do on occasion.
This is my second order of these cartridges and they work, but do not last long.  We went through these in a month or two and they are not refillable.

I love this whiteboard because it's the perfect size to travel with. I've had recent occasion to have to do several presentations where I had need of a writing surface and didn't want to have to carry reams of chart paper, much less a full-on easel board. This board has been the perfect solution. The surface is large enough to offer a significant writing surface that is smooth and erases easily. It's also lightweight enough to travel easily. I pair it with theAluminum Folding Table Easel Holds Canvases, Signs Etc. Up To 24" High, which allows for a quick set up and take down. I haven't attached it to a wall, though it comes with adhesive labels that would allow the board to be attached to a flat surface.The only issue I've had with the board is the white frame. My daughter got a hold of the board, and wrote on the frame with a dry-erase marker. She didn't think it would be an issue--it is. The frame is plastic and it takes quite a bit of elbow grease to get even dry-erase marks off of it. Still, it's a great board for every day use.

This light-duty sharpener does a great job on my kid's desk keeping their homework pencils sharp. It's fairly quiet, and works well with both graphite pencils and wax-based colored pencils. The clear reservoir lets you see when it needs to be emptied, and the design is such that you can empty it without making a big mess on the counter. My only complaint is that the opening is small and cannot accommodate oversize pencils.

This "deluxe" model is a bit heavier and sturdier than usual. It works about the same as my old, smooth stapler. The ridges make it a little less prone to slip from my fingers. It doesn't seem to be much more expensive than any other staple remover.
I think this is great option. Although, it's notquiet when I sharp the pencils. However, itdoes sharp quickly. I get high quality sharppencils out of it.Takako Masuda

I found this binder to be one of the best that I've ever used. It is very handy in my job as keeping my notes organized. If you need a heavy duty binder I would suggest that you spend a little more and get this one. But this is not my main reason why I like the binder, because you will soon understand why I love it as you are about to find out.After my middle school age daughter saw it she asked for one. After ordering her this Avery binder she is more organized because she uses it for a complete or "all in one" binder for her 5 subject classes at school. She no longer needs to keep 5 smaller binders as she has placed tabs for each individual class in her one Avery binder for easily finding what she needs.I love this single Avery binder as I no longer must drive back to her school because she has forgotten a specific homework assignment that was left in her locker (parents of pre-teen or teens know what I mean)...She now brings home only one "all in one binder" AKA... Avery Nonstick Heavy-Duty EZD Reference View 2 Inch White Binder. Her school does not allow bookbags/backpacks as well as all her textbooks are not allowed to be taken home.She now has this binder packed full of her school work, homework, school papers, etc. The Avery binder now weighs about ten pounds and she has used it for over five months. I am amazed how well it holds up after roughly being carried all day, often dropped on the floor, thrown into the car at pick up time, opening and closing the binder rings constantly, etc and after 5 months it looks and works like new. She as added her own theme by placing her decorative drawings in the clear plastic pockets within the outside cover. I work  for a school and often suggest this binder to parents that ask me advice to help with their child and organizational skills.

Wow, all I can say is that I did not expect these to really work, but I decided to give them a try. I installed the first 3 of these today and followed the advice of another reviewer when installing.  They work PERFECTLY.  I will write a follow up review if in fact they fail in the near future.  But I just printed a photo and it's beautiful.  They are well packaged and fit my Epson 410 printer perfectly.  All you have to remove is the piece of tape and a tiny spacer between the cartridge and the clip.  If you get confused, just compare the old cartridge to the new one.  Insert the cartridge. CAREFULLY read the prompts that show up on your printer so that you say OK to the right questions.  Epson does not want you to use this cartridge and will try to make you feel afraid for putting it in.  Just keep saying OK, and in the end it will ask you "are you sure you want to install this cartridge" the DEFAULT ANSWER is NO - BUT if you want this cartridge to work you need to say YES.  Good Luck!

Canon paper is some of the best. I got great prints using my Canon MG5200 printer,Canon photo paper and cheap $14.88 ink. I'm not sure how long they will hold up but i guess if you handle photos correctly & store in a dark box/envelope they should be fine. I got paper for $12.99 which I think is not bad for 100 4x6,20 5x7,20 8x11 good deal.

I never much thought about whether premium tape is a thing that exists, but I guess it does!I've found this to be very nice overall. I can use it to tape things down for a few minutes when I know that I'm going to want to pull it back up. A couple of times I've used it to make quick temporary labels for things as I was reorganizing stuff like cables. I could keep the cable in place and mark a letter or two to make sure I remembered what I meant it to be for, and then pull it all back up afterward and everything was kept simple and clean.I'd probably think it's worth investing in something like this when you know you have a big job ahead of you. If I were going to put in all the time it takes to paint a room very  nicely, it's worth spending a few more dollars to try to get tape that's going to do a very good job of helping you get nice results. More generally, though, less expensive brands will get the job done adequately.

These laminating sheets work as advertised. All you have to do is peel off top strip, peel off rest of the liner, place what you want laminated in between and it's done. Easy to use and quick laminating for your photos or documents. Highly Recommended.

This binder is really cute...the front is pictured, the back is mostly brown with a little pink and green.  The inside lining is more of a white and green pattern...not really damask but reminds me of that.  Seems like a solid piece, is more paper than plastic (so if you got water on it that wouldn't be great).  Goes really well with the Wilson Jones binder dividers (more cute patterns).  The only downside for me was that the inside binder ring opener (outer part) is a little small and harder for me to open and close, but it's probably normal for this size.  Also, I didn't like that the sticker that comes on the front does not come off easily.  I actually couldn't get it all off.  Otherwise, a really fun binder!

Anyone who runs their own business is well aware of how valuable filing folders are, which are used for several reasons, especially if you have many clients. These Manila folders have a few good advantages. They are large, letter size, with one-third cut tabs. I appreciate the light color for writing not only on the tabs, but the folders themselves. They contain a 90 per-cent larger, erasable label area. They are strong enough, durable, and don't easily tear apart. You can revise and reuse these folders. They are also easy to organize. I've already used 18, out of 24. The disadvantage is that it doesn't come with a permanent marker and white eraser, which I do not have at home. However, I've used them immediately by writing with pencil directly under the tab area. Overall, these folders are very handy, and make life a little bit easier. I would indeed use this product again, and I know many people already have permanent markers at home. I know if I look hard enough, I'll find one in my desk drawers. The eraser to me is worth the one-time purchase. However, I'm already using them, with no additional problems. Recommended!

Over the years, I have had two electric pencil sharpeners, and weren't impressed with either. They were extraordinarily loud, and never seemed to do a good job of sharpening the pencil. I don't know if I was holding the pencil at precisely the correct angle, or what it was.Anyway, when I saw that this "for heavy-duty use in the office or school," I jumped for it. Sure enough, at least so far, this sharpener really seems to do the trick. It is quieter than my "Wal-Mart Specials," but not what I would call silent - still it is a marked improvement. Also, it does a quick and efficient job of sharpening the pencils, making them nice and sharp in just a few seconds.The kids and I all like this sharpener, and were more than happy to heave our old one into trash. It really works!(Review of Westcott iPoint Curve Axis Electric Pencil Sharpener for School or Office (15511))

Yes, they're great! We love Tabs for our home school work - we mark where we are, what needs to be done, etc... These particular tabs are thick, heavy duty, and have great adhesion. I've found them to have a much stronger adhesion - they even curl the paper when removed, but not enough to do damage though. As others have remarked, the rounded Tabs don't catch on things and are more pleasant to touch. The citrus colors are pretty too.

I misplace my post-it notes often (and people take them and run off with them) so this seemed like something helpful to have on my desk. It is heavy enough to also use as a paperweight.One thing I didn't realize until I got it was that you do not use regular style post-it notes in it. You need to use a special kind which has a symbol on the package that sort of looks like paper folded in an accordian style. This dispenser comes with one pad like that.I tend to buy post-its at dollar stores so I won't be able to do that for this. The accordian style post-it notes cost around $9 for 6 pads, but it varies, depending on where you buy them or how many in a pack you get.It's pretty handy and people are much less likely to walk off with it if they ask for a post-it to jot down a note. It would make a nice teacher's gift or gift for a co-worker.

Note:I've just moved this printer down from five stars to one star. It was a great printer while it worked. Less than 100 pages into its print life it suddenly lost the ability to recognize that paper is loaded to print. A printer that won't load paper is about the most useless thing you can have around.The original review follows:****************************************There is a lot to like about this printer. First and most important, it is top notch at its basic job ... printing in color. Using good quality glossy paper, you'll be extremely pleased with the quality and color accuracy produced by this printer.I also like the Wi-Fi network connection. That makes it simple and convenient to get everything that will talk to your router to have access to this printer.The color touch screen makes it convenient to view and print photos directly from memory cards with your photos.You get duplex printing (both sides of the paper) which is unusual for a printer at this price point.The Epson Connect service allows you to easily print from phones or tablets, which is confusing or inconvenient for many people.If you print a lot of color, you're going to spend some money on cartridges, to be sure. You'll need to keep extras on hand, as the various color cartridges will run out at different times.

This chair has a lot going for it.  First, assembly out of the box is a breeze, and the base comes with the casters already installed.  I liked that.  (Anyone else hate putting in casters?)  It took longer to open the box than it did to assemble the chair!One thing I liked immediately were the adjustable arms that allow you to position them to best suit your work environment.  In fact, if you don't like the arms, you can leave them off completely, and you wouldn't be able to tell the chair was supposed to have arms.The adjustable range seems to be about 4 inches by way the the standard under-seat type of lever.  While the back is not adjustable, and it can't be locked into place, it is nicely molded and padded, and provides good support. Adequate padding in the chair cushion makes sitting for a few hours quite comfortable. A down side is there's no way to prevent it from tipping back when you lean back.The chair's five legs provide more stability that most four-legged desk chairs, and the color is benign enough to fit well in most any decor.I would have given this five stars if it weren't for the price.  $549 retail, $379 Amazon's price at the time of this review. Seems overpriced for the features.

The Brother QL 570 is really nice, and prints on a wide variety of lengths. There is a company called [..] who offers great prices for the replacement labels at a much better price.The continual rolls (no pre-cut) label is really better, which allows you to chose the length of the label, rather than pre-cut and somewhat confining sizes. Importing pictures from your hard drive or scanner ads a nice touch. The images are B&W; but produce great results.The software included is very good and Brother's website is always updating the additional add-on's for the consumer. A great machine with a lot of choices. Thermal labels eliminate the costly replacement inks, and with a few companies making the labels now, the prices are more and more affordable.

LOVE this organizer (which ZIPS close to hold everything in)!  Works way better than a ring binder or one of those files that closes with an elastic band.  My son carried this zipper file to and from school in his back pack EVERY day this past school year.  No problems with the zipper, or anything.  He kept all of his school work in here until it was complete and ready to be turned in.  The one we have is still in great condition (given its enormous amount of use), but plan to purchase an additional one for next school year.  Highly recommend!!

If you want a stapler to keep on your desk for occasional use in a busy office, this is a good choice because it is distinctive looking and is unlikely to disappear.  But it is not very sturdy, so not a good choice for frequent use or stapling more than a few sheets of regular-weight paper.

It's almost like having the adult version of stickers.  Write, peel, and stick, just as advertised.  I also like its texture.  It's very well made.  It's easy to use.  And it does stick to most objects well.

This Academie Wirebound Sketch Diary ("14 x 11 ") is a very fine 70-paged book of high quality, acid-free drawing paper. The paper has enough grit to hold color pencil work; yet it is still comfortably smooth. I have enjoyed rubbing my hand across it while working.Each sheet had fine perforation dots for easily, but carefully, pulling the paper out of the book. You don not get those wirebound paper tags when removing these large sheets of paper. It is also a good size book to fit into my larger bag. But, I really only have used it at home.So, why not 5* for the rating? I have an issue with the cover. Although it is shiny and smooth for easily slipping in and out of a bag, the cover design is so ugly I want to glue another design or even blank paper over it. I plan doing that soon. I have a similar criticism about the smaller 6" x 9" version of the Academie sketching diary.If they want to sell sketch books to artists why not make the covers more appealing?
I have never had a problem with this scanner.  It will copy anything I want to copy from bound pamphlets to single pages or photos. I use to struggle with a HP never again. Canon is for me.

These labels worked perfect with my laser printer. I have a very very old HP printer. I went on the 3M website to download the template for the labels. Just be sure to tab over twice to get to the label on the right hand side after typing out an address on the left hand side.I had no trouble feeding the paper through and printing out the labels. They looked excellent. The only downside is to make sure you wait long enough because even after a minute, the label still smudged a little bit when I ran my hand by it. The labels themselves stick to all types of surface great and is secure. These are definitely worth it.

This wireless All-in-One is beautiful, compact, and easy to install.  You unpack it, careful to remove all the protective tape, including inside the printer (don't forget that).  Then you set the printer on your desktop, raise the paper support and connect the power cord to the back of the printer and plug it up to an electrical outlet. Next you load the ink cartridges and put paper in the printer.  After that you insert the product CD and follow instructions on your computer screen.  It took me a few minutes to install then check all of its functions.  I'm not very tech-savvy so it might take you smarties less time.  :o)  Excellent print quality.  I haven't tried printing any photographs yet.  However everything else works perfectly fine.  This size is what I needed for the limited space in my home office.

I had really high hopes for the Winsome Alden Lap Desk.  Even after seeing some reviews that were less than glowing, I decided to give this lap desk a try.  My largest concerns and problems with it have been the build quality and design.  The finish of the lap desk, plus the flip up top were two big selling points for me.  It's a shame that the lap desk lacks in quality, because it could have been an awesome product.As someone that often uses a laptop in a chair or bed, I thought I would get some great use out of this.  Truth is, I still do use it, but the quality has been lacking.  First, it arrived with a minor scratch/ding.  Second, it also arrived with a small splint starting the wood.  I could have returned it, but it was difficult to find to begin with.  Another large disappointment is the fact that all of the edges are sharp and rough.  You would think when they designed this they would have realized that you would have your arms and hands resting on it all the time.  The sharpness and roughness of the edge can be really irritating.  Plus, I hate putting an expensive laptop on a lap desk that could easily scratch it.  While the color the finish is a nice color, it could have actually be finished better.  it's not smooth (although you might not want it too smooth to avoid items sliding off of it) at all and the feel of it is not appealing.After minimal use, a portion of one of the legs came out.  It's nothing that a little wood glue won't fix, but it shouldn't be happening.  The drawer is very loose and opens easily.  A simple magnet or anything would have prevented this.  It would have also been nice to have the legs lock in place with a simple mechanism.  Otherwise, it makes it difficult to move off or on you.  The flip top is nice, but again, a simple mechanism would help.  You pretty much need to remove your laptop before you can let it back down. COMPARISONThis is good quality strapping tape; sticky and with plenty of fiberglass filaments.  In comparison, the STAPLES store brand has half the filaments, which are the whole point of strapping tape.  The more filaments the better.STRAPPING TAPEStrapping tape is primarily used like metal or plastic straps around boxes with heavy contents to prevent them from bursting open, because the embedded fiberglass prevent the tape from stretching.  It is not meant to seal edges or gaps---it will work for such use, but not as well, mostly because it is less flexible.USE>  A band of strapping tape (even narrow tape) around each side of a box (that adds up to 3 bands for the three dimensions of normal space) is the best insurance that a package will not open in shipment.  Use two bands for each side if the contents are heavy.  Why not use "packaging" or "shipping" tape?---they will stretch and then let go.  Packaging/shipping tape is for sealing boxes, not for preventing them from bursting open.TIPS ON USE>  The tape sticks well to most cardboard (of shipping boxes), but sticks much better to itself.  So, overlap by at least 3" on a small box, more on large boxes.>  The tape sticks so well to itself, that it may be hard to "start" pealing off if the end has stuck to the roll.  The best strategy is prevention---fold over a tab every time you cut a length of tape from the roll.>  The tape absolutely will not tear laterally (because of the filaments), but tears easily parallel to the filaments.  To "start" a roll when the tape is stuck on the roll, it is best to use a flat knife to scrape/pull up a short length.>  When sealing a package with strapping tape that you want to open at a later date, leave tabs (1/2" of tape folded over on itself)HOW WIDE?Of course, it depends on weight, but for "average heavy" boxes:3/8" is good for up to say 10" wide boxes1/2" is bood  for up to say 12" wide boxes3/4" is good for up to 15" wide boxes1" is good for up to 20" wide  boxes---but two 1/2" bands (equally spaced from each other and the box edge) on each side are usually better than one 1" band2" is good for or big or very heavy boxes---but multiple thinner bands (equally spaced from each other and the box edge) are usually better than one 2" bandThis size (0.7") is a good compromise---you aren't wasting much on small boxes, and can use multiple bands (which are better anyway) on almost any size larger or heavier box.  I generally keep 3/8", 3/4" and 2" rolls on hand.  I use the 2" strapping tape for large boxes of rocks (I'm a geologist).

I'll start off by saying that for what I paid for this, I really think it should have come with an adapter cord, or at least a loop since there's a spot there to tie a wrist loop on there.Now that that's out of the way, I like this overall. But when I read someone else had to get out a manual to even capitalize a letter, I laughed. Most of the buttons are self-explanatory like this.  The button with the frame around the letters lets you choose a frame.  The button with the letter A in different fonts lets you pick a font.  The button that has two different-sized capital A's controls the font size.  It's not rocket science.I think it does a great job of keeping the waste way down.  The unit has a nice feel to it, and the buttons are easy to press.  The preview feature doesn't really give an actual preview of what will be printing out, but that's not a big deal to me. Clear is great but if you have semi-clear containers, you'll probably want a white or black background on your tape.  The choices of fonts are fine, but some are more pixelated than others.  As mentioned previously, this really isn't a great look.  Not sure why Epson doesn't fix this as it's such a huge turnoff for so many people.  I don't have a problem with Epson tape.  It sticks on anything for me, even after removing and repositioning several times.  It's very easy to take off, but doesn't peel or curl up on its own.  I read someone somewhere complaining of labelers that didn't use split tape.  I don't know which brand that was, but this was does use split tape which makes it much easier to remove the backing.  Use a gentle hand though because the tape is so fine, you can easily crease it down the middle while removing the backing.I would get a Brother label maker and pay even MORE for Brother tape if they would make a machine that didn't waste it.  It's partially about the money, but it's mostly that it just irritates me.  I know they know about this problem but refuse to fix it.  As it is, I'll put up with the poor type on this and just stand back farther to read my labels.  Not so noticeable from a few feet away.  :)

Also, it doesn't require line-of-sight, which is good since you have to have the receiver in a usb port.4) It installs and XP and Vista with no drivers needed.5) The 1 gig of storage is nice as you could fit most Powerpoint presentations on it and thus not have to carry an extra thing.6) I almost failed to notice: There's a little compartment into which you slide the receiver/flash drive. Unlike some laptop mice, it should be hard to lose the receiver.7) The light that flashes green on the receiver when you use it flashes red when the batteries are low. I haven't had it long enough to run down batteries, but if this works it's a nice feature.The negatives:1) This won't fit into all hands.2) It's *very* basic: forward, back and stop. That's it. That's fine for very straightforward presentations, but no more.3) Price: When I first opened this and started using it, I was guessing that it might cost $40 on amazon. When I confirmed that it was RF rather than IR, I thought $50. But $75 seems high. It's great that you don't have to have an IR receiver, and the memory is a clever touch, but it just doesn't convince me at that price.Conclusion: I'd wait and see if the price drops once it's been available for a while.Dave

My only previous experience with hot lamination was with the cheap, thin stuff that teachers use.  Lots of creases and bubbles.  Yuck! I always see this at teacher's desk and in my office. I finally decided to get one for home, even though i don't use it much. It is very well made and hard to find anythign wrong with it. Does its job well.

Labels are thick and strong. Adhere well but are also easy to peel off if necessary and don't leave that sticky residue. I bought this for use at work and have not been disappointed at all.  This support my multi-monitor setup for document comparisons and keeping quick references open. These are serious moving boxes.  You fold them out, put the hanger in place and you are ready to put a bunch of your hanging clothes in them. I don't use this extensively as I have another black and white printer that I use for most printing jobs, but I have used this for scanning documents to the computer, and making quick copies.  I've also used it for a couple color printing jobs, using premium glossy paper, and it does a nice job of that as well.I like the pop-up feature of the control panel.  I have this printer installed in a bookcase and having the ability to pop up the control panel makes it so much easier to see than getting down on my knees to get the panel at eye level.I find it pretty intuitive to use and haven't had to refer to the owner's manual so far.The only complaint I have, and the reason for docking a star, is that the paper carrier is kind of flimsy.  I originally had the printer sitting on a pedestal with a drawer in it where I kept the spare printer paper.  I pulled out the paper carrier, filled it, and pushed it back in, but because the pedestal wasn't quite as wide as the full width of the printer, the paper carrier jammed and I could NOT get it unstuck.  I finally had to deinstall the printer, flip it over, remove 2 screws and flex the frame slightly to release the paper tray and reinstall it correctly.  I ditched the pedestal at that point and haven't had any further problems, so mostly that one was my fault, BUT the tray is not very sturdy regardless.  I hope it stands up to continued use.I've had other Epson printers in the past and overall find them to be of good quality.  This one is very easy to use, have scanned documents and then faxed using a USB fax modem without any difficulty.  I've not burned through the original ink cartridges so far - they seem to be holding up well.I like the USB interface capability, as I don't have wireless in the house.  I also like that you can directly insert memory cards and print from them as well.  And, I like that it doesn't take up nearly the room that my old Epson RX500 photo printer did - it's much less tall than that one and slightly smaller overall footprint.Overall I'm pleased with it.

I bought this as an auxillary phone.  We've got an answering machine and a fax machine, but I needed an additional phone to be by the computer in my downstairs office and I wanted a speakerphone so when I was telecommuting I could call into meetings and listen to them without holding a receiver up to my ear.I was convinced to buy this phone by the string (until recently aftet I placed my order) of rave reviews for this phone, combined with the terrible reviews for so many other speakerphones that cost less.I've only had this phone for a few days, but I can say that it is attractive and seems to be built well.  I called in to work and tried out the speakerphone and it seemed to work well on both ends.  I heard the other party fine and the other party did said I sounded good.I like the uncluttered controls with big number buttons and big buttons for volume and speakerphone.  I didn't have to pay for a lot of features that I don't need.This phone also has the added bonus of a headset input, so if I ever need to talk a whole lot from my home office, I could get a headset and talk while keeping both hands free.  So far, so good.Postscript:  It's September of 2007 and the speaker volume is now impossible to control and the unit seems to be buzzing.  I can't use it for conference calls anymore.  I guess I'll buy another one, but I'll look around first.OOPS! I forgot that this phone is powered by three AA batteries.  They need to be replaced on occasion.  When they start running down, the speakerphone gets squirrely.  So, I replaced them and now the phone works fine.

Just got my Avery Durable View Binder and am already putting it to good use.  I needed something to organize all my catalog of video files I have done lately and my DVD and Blu Ray sets. (ok, some HD DVD sets too, I was impetuous! )  All my materials fit nicely in this thing. room to spare. ON the inside , both the front and the back have two pockets in the vinyl covering to hold more papers or whatever you want. A nice and compact calendar. Although it comes with a pin, there is no way to attach it to the calendar. It has magnates, which is the only way to hang it. As a dry erase calendar, it is nice and works well.

Love writing with this pen... one lasts me about 2-3 weeks, as I do a lot of writing at work. I have a favorite pen and this refill fit perfectly!!!! Nice smooth writing, and quick drying ink!!!
I have photo's from my didtal camara that I want to print out and this paper is great. We are making a alblum of our cat that pass away after 15 years he was very special.

More like 25-50 pages.  This is so misleading and so frustrating.  HP has got to come up with a better solution, I hate running out so frequently. Of course this is a great binder for business use, but there are home projects for which this binder is very useful as well.  I like to make personalized cookbooks as bridal shower gifts and love the one I have for my own use.  The binder I use needs to be sturdy and easy to use and these have served the purpose for me.  It helps that this particular binder is a bit wider than the standard ones, so my page protectors and divider tabs don't stick out and are protected.  While the rings of this binder are 2", the spine is 3" wide, which is pretty big, but perfect for my own use.  Usually however I use a smaller version for gifts.  Because the printed document inserted in the transparent cover overlay and spine won't stick, the bride can switch to a larger size binder when she needs to.This size binder holds a lot of pages and the back mounted rings with easy finger tab for opening and closing make loading and turning pages easy.  My cookbook binder has stood up to a lot of handling and I like that there are two pockets on the inside front and back covers instead of the usual one.To make the cookbooks I have a computer file with a cover page and a set of section divider pages that I can customize for the bride.  I print these on pretty stationary and insert them into page protectors with Avery stick on tabs for section names, then decide on recipes that I think the bride would like and print those on normal paper which I then put in more page protectors.  I include lots of empty page protectors for her to add more recipes she finds over time so the cookbook becomes very personal.  It's easy to add or remove things, including pages printed from the internet or torn from catalogs, and of course the binder and pages are easy to clean if they get splattered.Another project is a favorite of my grandchildren.  I use a smaller version of this binder because I don't want it too heavy for them to handle.  I insert an enlargement of a favorite picture of one of the kids on the cover of each and insert picture collages in page protectors. Since printer paper is way cheaper for the kids to draw on than drawing pads you would buy for them, their pictures and stories fit well in page protectors and can be added to the binders. The children love to look through the albums and there is no worry about the pictures being damaged by sticky fingers.  I can change the cover pictures since they don't stick and while these are not fancy picture albums, they are the most beloved and looked at in my house.  Because the thumb tab in this binder is so easy to open and close, the oldest child is now making his own album of favorite art and pictures.  These binders are really great.

Costs about the same as buying a rubber bands separate, but with twice the fun. Has a wide variety of colors. Fun to toss around and squish. You can even put them around your wrist to use them for later use.

The Scotch Sealing Tape Dispenser H122 is durably constructed. The cutting blade is excellent, and my favorite thing about this dispenser is that the tape guides between the roll and the cutting teeth have a broad, flat face that I press the tape against between uses, and I don't have to fidget with tape that falls back onto the roll.This dispenser is easy to use. Its lack of a handle is something I worried might be a disadvantage, which in a commercial setting as "the box guy," it certainly would be. From the perspective of the home user, it turns out that being able to draw the tape across the box and stably rest the dispenser at the opposite end while I draw the cardboard tight without the dispenser flopping to either of its own sides, keeps the tape from folding over on itself, and for this, I feel that this is an excellent tape dispenser for non-commercial use.

I use both Post it and Avery sticky notes and I can't tell any difference between the two. I even put one of each on the fridge and peeled it off and on 30+ times and both had equal stick. I would buy either brand based on price alone, both are good.

Laser Multifunctions like this Brother are the Swiss Army Knives of small offices and businesses.  Like most Brother printers and multifunction machines, this one is easy to set up, has good print quality and very reasonably priced toners, particularly withBrother Printer TN780 Super High Yield Toner Cartridgewhich gives 12000 pages, the cost per page is 0.91 cents, as of now. One of the least expensive laser printer costs per page. Works well as a fast printer, copier, fax machine and scanner.Setting this multifunction apart, in a sea of Brother and other multifuncion machines, are the following 3 things:1. SPEED: fast print speed of 42 pp improves the efficiency of a busy office.2. COLOR TOUCH SCREEN CONTROL: instead of hard to read monochrome menu trees nested within trees. Having multiple features in a machine is useful only if you can use the features easily - and large color touch screen makes it easier to change settings so you can use more of the features.3.  PRINT FROM MOBILE DEVICES: using AirPrint, Google Cloud Print, Brother iPrint&Scan;, Cortado Workplace, and Wi-Fi Direct. I personally have not yet printed from any mobil device or Google Docs.Although it is a network multifunction, when I hooked it up to a Windows SBS2011 server, the CD that came with the printer did not have drivers for the server! I got a screen message to download the drivers from Brother web site - which has a lot of stuff like manuals, drivers etc. but very poorly organized with no clear explanations as to which driver is for which purpose. There was no driver for Windows SBS2011. On calling Brother technical support, they answered within 5 minutes (prompt by tech support standards) and Wilma told me that I needed to download Windows Server 2008R2  "Add Printer Wizard" driver and I was able to get at least the printer working with the server. Setting up Fax server and scanning server is even more complicated. Scanning and fax functions are easy to set up with a USB connection.How can you sell an ethernet and a Wi-Fi multifunction and not send the network drivers with the machine? There is hodgepodge of software available for this machine on Brother's web site but without much explanation as to what the software does and which driver to use for which machine. It is hard to figure out what to download.If you get faxes on the computer, then Brother saves them in TIFF file format, not PDF. But software CD that comes with the machine also comes with Paperport 12 SE which you can use to convert TIFF to PDF files, but it is just an extra step and a hassle.Except for these glitches, Brother 8950DW is one of the fastest and least expensive print per page cost multifunction machines out there and can be a workhorse for a small business.

I like this document organizer pretty well actually. It holds a lot of papers and has a Velcro pocket on the front for the smaller items which is handy. I needed a portable, light, and inexpensive sharpener for my pencils- regular graphite #2, a variety of drawing pencils (including charcoal and graphite in assorted soft/hardnesses), colored pencils, and watercolor pencils. This sharpener has done a perfect job on all of them. I haven't had any problems with tips breaking off or shattering, and the pencil tip is always a perfect razor-fine sharpness with a good balance of wood to graphite/lead. I especially like that I no longer have to use an X-Acto knife to get my pencils to a good sharpness for the different grips I use when I draw.The only caveat to this sharpener is you must hold the sharpener in one hand and the pencil in the other, unless you manage to secure it to your work surface. The motor is powerful that either the pencil or the sharpener will try and spin when you insert a pencil and it turns on. Smart tip for all users: download the software from Neat's site and install. You're sure to get the latest version that way. When you install, you'll be prompted to sign up for a 30 day trial of NeatCloud, which sounds fine, but once I saw the monthly price I'd be charged, I opted not to go further. This cloud option is really for the extreme neat freaks - those of you who live for organizing and would get a thrill from accessing your receipts anytime, anywhere, including on your mobile devices. I'm not one of those people. There is, of course, something to be said for keeping your receipts safely stored off your computer, but at the price of a deluxe fast food meal every month, it seems a bit costly. That said, using the scanner to take care of my messy habits is all I need, and I can back up Neat's documents to my Time Machine and Dropbox.It's as simple as can be - start up Neat's software, feed a receipt into the long slit of the scanner, and press "scan". Neat takes care of the rest, including reading as much of the receipt's contents as possible. It was generally able to pick up most clean, clear text, but had trouble on any receipts that printed even the slightest bit blurry. That's easy enough to fix, just click in the box, select the text, and retype the amount.From there, Neat lets you organize the receipts into folders that you can set up for your needs pretty much just like you would in the Finder (as a Mac user - I would assume it's similar for Windows users). There are also Smart Folders, but I haven't quite worked out how they function. The software itself is noticeably scant on details about how these work or how to make custom ones...One strange note for Mac users: I can't for the life of me figure out why the Neat software wants/needs access to contacts in my Address Book. Weird. Perhaps I can send my receipts to them...?What's also nice is the unit is tiny and comes with a soft sleeve in which to store it, so it can be neatly stored out of the way. All in all, it's a pretty thoughtful system that I will be putting to much greater use to get much more organized in the future.

Before receiving the Canon PIXMA MX860 printer, we have been using multiple printers, anEpson Stylus photo R1800 inkjet printerfor photographs and aCanon PIXMA iP6220D printerfor other printing needs. From there the basic set-up is pretty simple but slow going.  For instance the printer takes 4 minutes after installing the ink to align heads and such.  Lastly the printer is connected to a computer LAN or wireless network.This machine prints documents pretty fast when used as a printer, with excellent quality printouts.  The copy feature does an excellent job, especially with the auto duplex function for single or double sided originals.  This is a slower process than printing documents, but is reasonable considering the complexity of the job.  The fax is simple to use and produces excellent quality transmissions.  The scan function provides good scans but doesn't include attachments for scanning negatives.  While the scans have their usefulness, they are not of sufficient quality for scanning images. When Canon came out with their Bubblejet printer back in the 1980s, it changed the face of inkjet printing. For a few hundred dollars, they offered a printing solution that took the world from dot matrix quality to "near laser quality" text. The secret was micro fine quality nozzles that had precise control over ink. Since that time, quality has improved, colors were added, prices have dropped, and you can now get something that produces top quality 13" by 19" prints for less money than the original Bubblejet. If you factor in inflation, it's even more of a bargain.People are used to inkjet printers being inexpensive, since companies use the "razor blade" model of making the printer itself cheap and the ink expensive. This is no exception. In fact the ink that comes with it consists of a set of starter cartridges and isn't even as much ink as you'd get in standard cartridges. The replacement high yield cartridges aren't cheap but will last far longer than the ones that come with the printer. There are also aftermarket cartridges that can save you money. But with this printer in particular, I wouldn't recommend it. With cheaper printers you might be willing to sacrifice some quality to save some money, but you shouldn't buy this unless you are looking for top quality results.As with other Canon printers, some starter photo paper is included. Unfortunately they don't supply a single sheet of 13" by 19" paper. I bought someCanon Photo Paper Pro Platinum, 13 x 19 Inchespaper to test the printer with, and the results were spectacular. I don't print large prints every day, and was willing to spend more for the Platinum paper. It's not a question of the price per sheet but whether spending that amount of money is in your budget. The Photo Paper Plus is also an excellent photo paper.As far as features go, this printer is best suited to a single task: printing high quality photos. Canon makes it so that it will work well with everything from text documents on up, but I'd recommend a cheaper printer for everyday tasks and using this one if you truly want higher quality photos, especially large ones. And it's the large ones that are the most impressive.Setup is simple, and if you have WPS on your router, it comes down to knowing how and when to press a single button on each, and the instructions tell you that. The only physical hookup you need is plugging in a power cord. The printer comes with a quick setup guide made up of pictures for the most part, with limited text. The seven major steps have numbered minor steps, and the minor steps have numbers in them too. It doesn't get to the point of major confusion, but the numbers with white outlines, the plain numbers and ones in pink circles walk you through the process. They don't necessarily tell you everything that's going on. For example, one step causes a page to print out that looks like a head alignment page, but with no text telling you that. Then later with the software setup it tells you that you need to align the heads. When the paper prints out from that, you realize that it's the same thing it had you do already. But it really comes down to unpacking it, plugging it in, pressing some buttons and putting in the cartridges.It comes with a CD containing everything you need to print photos and CD/DVD labels. The suite essentially works with all Canon printers and is the latest evolution of their software, with the added caveat that it checks to assure that you have genuine Canon ink for the "premium content" that will allow you to print everything from greeting cards to calendars. Of course it will let you print photos and print on disks as part of the standard suite.The printer also supports AirPrint, which allows you to print easily from your iPad, iPhone or Mac. These features work well and nothing needs to be installed on any of these devices. One of the frustrations of owning an iPad was the inability to print with common printers that were around when it came out. You also get Pixma printing to print with an app from other mobile devices.The printer features "Wireless PictBridge," which will allow you to print directly from compatible cameras without a computer. This is an extension of the similar previous capability offered by Canon, which allows you to print directly from a compatible camera with a USB cable. I can see why Canon added all these features since the software and corresponding firmware features were already in place. But personally, for such high quality photo printing I would just as soon print from a computer after having a chance to get things exactly as I want them. Of course you could also print photos with other software such as Picasa or any photo editing software.CD printing is nothing new for Canon. It was supported on my iP4200 printer back in 2006. But back then, they didn't include the tray for the disk, they blocked the slot, and they disabled printing in the firmware for the US market. So they've had plenty of time to improve the software for printing CD/DVD/Blu-ray discs with printable surfaces. The latest improvements let you select a small or large spindle size, select your own background or choose from a variety of backgrounds, use one of many templates, and place the text of your choice on a label. It has limited capability for spinning, curving or stretching text, so you might want to use different software to produce the image and simply use it as a background with nothing else. Then again, if printing on disks is your goal, you might want to select a cheaper Canon or Epson printer, since many current model Canon printers will have the same capability for less money. And having the ultimate control of colors might be much less of a priority on a print medium that's not optimized for high resolution.For me the bottom line is that this is a high quality printer that's best suited to somebody who wants to produce larger prints or who wants an improvement in print quality that is gained from a good design and more cartridges. I wouldn't recommend this for document printing, birthday cards on plain paper or the printing of snapshots from a cheap camera. It's not that it won't do these tasks as well or better than a cheaper printer. It's that it would be overkill.  I'll save it for when I need the best quality printing for display purposes and use my other printers for everyday tasks.

Reviewing Scotch tape is like reviewing Kleenex, or Coca-Cola. Is there anybody who doesn't know what this is?On the other hand, this iconic product could use a bit of updating.Pros -- Matte finish, so it "disappears" on paper (even more so if you rub it with your fingernail). It also won't show up as much on xeroxes (oh, excuse me, "photocopies")- Two-sided clamshell dispenser. Cheaper tapes have a one-sided dispenser, and yes, the open side of the tape gets cruddy. You wind up with a dark line on the edge of the tape. These are better.Cons -- The greener alternative to this package would be one refillable dispenser and a bunch of refills (at least for a home office). Scotch does in fact make a desk dispenser package with refills (Scotch Magic(TM) Tape Deal), but the dispenser is clunky and big. I would totally go for a slightly more robust version of this dispenser instead. I do recognize, however, that most people are going to use up the roll and throw the dispenser out. So...- There are only 18 yards on the roll. That's ~650 inches, not the 1000 inches in the refills (Scotch Magic Tape). Shipping these with the full 1000 inch rolls would also be a greener alternative - it would mean 1/3 fewer dispensers thrown away, and about 1/3 less energy used for packaging and shipping. I'm sure, when these dispensers were first designed, some marketing guy figured out the price point and decided on 18 yards. But that was decades ago, and consumers think differently now.Great tape. Needs a packaging upgrade[Update - on Earth Day, 3M announced a green alternative to this tape, namely a tape base and glue made from renewable materials. They also have started a dispenser recycling program (the dispensers are polystyrene, which most local programs won't take). Amazon does not yet carry this product - I'll update when that changes. (Still want more tape, though)]
