This printer produces great quality output, and i've printed over 300 full color pages without any problems.  I bought this printer specifically because it can print on heavier card stock using the rear load feature.  The ink is VERY expensive though.

I've been using these pencils for about a month now, and I like them.  I like the rubber grip on the barrel, I like the pencil's action in extending new lead, and the eraser works great.  I also like that there is another eraser in reserve once you wear the first one down.  All you have to do is pop the eraser holder out of the top of the pencil, flip it over, push it back in, and viola - another eraser.The eraser doesn't leave a lot of debris on the paper, and it picks up pencil lead very well.The HB lead together with a 0.7mm lead make it likely to smear relatively easily, but it doesn't bite into the paper like 0.5mm leads sometimes feel like they do.All in all, a great pencil.  The flip eraser is really just a gimmick, but a good one.  Way to go Paper Mate!5 stars.

I'll admit it.  I am a degenerate Post-It addict.  I like them small, tiny, medium, multiple colors, clear, I even like them HUGE.  And this Big Pad is truly gigantic.  And while the small ones have a myriad of uses- bookmarks, reminders, tabs- the use case is virtually unlimited- I can't really think of what I'll use these enormous ones for.They are exactly square, 11 glorious inches by 11 inches.  They have two wide strips of adhesive on the back, not just one on the top like you would see with the lilliputian "regular" Post-Its.  So, with the double strip on the back, you could stick this entire square on a white board, a desk, or a wall and it should stay stuck.For now, this mammoth is just resting on my desk, awaiting it's dharma.  And I can't think of what I'll use them for, but I do admire them.  More than that, I appreciate and marvel at the fact that I live in an era in which there are 11" x 11" Post-It notes.UPDATE:  I FOUND A GREAT USE FOR THESE!If you have a glass-top desk and your mouse won't work on it, and you don't like having a thick mouse pad, which will slip around anyway, you can just lay one of these down and you have mouse magic- thin and light, and sticks to your desk!

I love this chalk and if you are looking for a holder, "Rikagaku Dustless Chalk Holder" works perfectly and it has a clip/cover that is also magnetic. This chalk writes so smooth, much better than anything else I've tried. It is also easy to erase, even when I haven't chalked my porcelain board. I do keep my Prang chalk as a backup and in holders for the kids to use, but I use this almost exclusively. Yes it soft, but that is what makes it so wonderful. My set arrived in perfect condition and I have ordered more.

I am really impressed by these Paper Mate InkJoy pens.  They are smooth and effortless like a gel pen, and they do not skip or get blobby like regular ink pens.  Best of all, they can stand up to my heavy hand unlike some gels/rollers which write and feel more like felt tips.Don't be alarmed when you first open the package and see what looks like red blobs of ink at the tip of each pen.  This is just a protective wax bit, and you use your fingers to easily remove it.  (I tried "writing it off" - like one would with an ink blob - and that does not work!!)Very nice surprise, pleasing colors, medium/thin 1.0 mm line, and it feels good to hold.  Definitely worth a try if you love writing the analog way!
This is sturdy packing tape and at under $3 a roll, a good deal.  I don't know what else to say.  It's clear, it's sticky on one side, it's good for securing boxes and envelopes.  It's packing tape!

I won't go on and on about these, they're little post it tabs, after all.  But I will say that they are great to have on hand to flag items in your planner, book, etc.  I especially like to keep them nearby as I'm looking through magazines, I stick them on the edge of the page that I'd like to remember for the future.  Very handy for me.  No more mental notes that I can't remember after 2 minutes.  When I want to find something of importance in a magazine or book, I just go to my little colored tab and there it is.  No wasting a half hour scouring through issues of magazines or craft books to find the page I'm looking for.  Obviously, they can be used for all sorts of things, I'm just relating they ways I like to use them.  Great to have on hand.

I'm a student so I'm constantly printing things (as much as it pains my wallet). My little dollar store stapler was no longer cutting it, especially as I started to have to split my packs of notes into smaller portions of 5-7 sheets so my stapler could properly staple them together. Well, no more! This stapler is great and so easy to use though I will admit I haven't stapled 65 sheets together (mostly 40 or so). It's light weight, but heavy duty, and is great for small office or home use.

My kids love to write notes and stick them where we will find them.  I like to write my lists on small papers.  So these sticky notes are perfect for my family!  (Good thing it comes with 400 sheets!)These sticky notes are everything I would expect:-Just the right amount of stick-Standard 3 x 3 inch size-4 bold colors-The boxtop label was an unexpected bonus since our elementary school hounds us for them.  Just be aware it is on the plastic wrapper.  I almost shredded the label while opening the plastic.

The impossible-to-ignore color, combined with heavy-duty adhesive make this tape a virtual alternative to painting surfaces that you want to highlight for reasons of safety or identification. Mark a square of tape with a permanent black marker and you've created a customized label.I had no idea it would be so useful - like an optically-biased version of duct tape. Its clarity is industrial in quality and its usefulness for identifying/marking boxes and other stored items, as well as highlighting stair edges and creating other lines of demarcation is unsurpassed.
Loved this! I used this as the binding on a mini photo album. Has not lost it's seal yet. I want to get this in shades of pink.

Had to replace my really old, wonderful Lexmark as it was not compatible with Windows 7. I really shopped before deciding on this Brother. Very happy I made this call. It has worked well, no problems. Has many features that my prior printer didn't have that I'm enjoying. Only thing that I'm not really happy about is the color quality. Just don't get a bright clear color print. But that's not real important as I send pictures out to be printed.
This scale is a great value, it works perfectly every time.  It is ready within a few seconds of turning on, and gives consistent accurate weights.

I have enjoyed using these in cookbooks, to keep notes on recipes. They stick well and remove easily, and really, what more can you say about a product than that it works well for its intended purpose?

A stapler is a stapler, right?  I mean, how different could they really be from one another?  This is the conventional thinking, but I inherited, as most people do, somebody else's 1940's model stapler when I landed a great new job with a new employer recently. After removing the mysterious gummy residue from the top of it and sanitizing it with alcohol to kill off any disease the gummy goop was harboring, I was good to go, as they say.  Still, when the opportunity arose to try out a brand new stapler as an Amazon Vine member, I jumped at it.  Actually owning a stapler seemed like a big commitment and a lot of responsibility for somebody who has spent his life using the standard-issue staplers passed down through generations of workers, but I was ready for it.  So, here is how things worked out for me:POSITIVES+ NEARLY EFFORTLESS: This stapler employs some kind of advanced physics--like quantum physics or some other physics that regular people do not understand.  Anyway, a baby could staple 20 sheets with this stapler--seriously.  Clearly, no lawyers would approve of this review, but let me be clear, I am not suggesting that you give a stapler to your baby.+ SOLID CONSTRUCTION: It seems to be well made, based on my initial usage.  Have you ever had a stapler that you wanted to hurl as far as possible, due to constant jamming and poor performance?  This is not one of those, though it is fairly streamlined and might sail a good distance should it ever reach the end of the line and face a projectile experiment.+ SHORT LENGTH: Size does, indeed, matter.  In the case of staplers, oddly, shorter seems to be better--easier to handle and takes up less space in your drawer or on your desk.  My old one was nearly 7" long, but this one is only 6.25".  OK, is there anything that strikes you as odd about me measuring the length of staplers?  But I digress!+ COOL NAME: Being a marketing professional myself, I applaud the people behind this one.  To give a cool name to a mundane office item is to change the world forever.  Well, not exactly, but the attempt is worth recognition.  Next time somebody asks to use my stapler, I will say, "Oh, you want to use my EVO!"NEGATIVES- MARRED PLASTIC TOP: OK, so the thing is brand new, and the plastic top/handle arrived fairly marred up.  Shouldn't a new one be in pristine condition?  If you were to buy one of these, wouldn't you expect it to look like a sparkly new sports car, not an old Datsun with a few door dings?  Anyway, it is looking better since I took some desk cleaner to the handle.  Besides, it is only the handle (though the most visible part of the stapler!).- AWKWARD STAPLE REFILLING: We were born with a human instinct to lift the top of the stapler to insert the staples.  Anything other than that feels like riding a bicycle backwards.  So, rather than reading the instructions (who reads the instructions?!?), I attempted to lift the top to insert the staples.  NOPE!  Does not work.  After fiddling with it for a while, I got the back of the stapler to slide out.  I then proceeded to attempt inserting staples in the back of the stapler.  The engineers who designed this stapler must have known that idiots like me would try this, as they put a little picture of staples back there with a line through it--you know, like DON'T PUT THE STAPLES HERE.  Well, I either did not interpret the symbol correctly or wanted to prove them wrong.  In either case, I gave it a shot and failed.  Finally, I figured out that you need to insert the staples underneath the stapler after sliding out the back.  OF COURSE!  NOT!  This was not intuitive, but I did manage to figure it out, even without reading the instructions.- FIRES BLANKS ON OCCASION: If you bought a gun and it sporadically went BANG when you pulled the trigger but shot no bullet, you would be unhappy.  When the same happens with a stapler, it isn't quite as consequential, but still a little disappointing.  It has happened 2-3 times out of the first 25-50 staples I have used so far.  Not a major deal, but if you expect perfection, then look elsewhere.
Check the size before buying

Cork Bulletin Board is the go-to standard for all around postings. The cork will take push pins and staples making it the perfect place to  attach notes, photos, flyers, and maps. It comes with the hardware so it can be hung vertically or horizontally. Perfect for the home, business, shop, dorm room, or office.

I usually use Hallmark's greeting card paper and like it a lot.  Avery's product is equally good.  It is a true matte finish, so if you want a little more shine, this isn't for you.  The stock is thick enough that the printing doesn't show through and the fold is neat and professional.  No need to buy pre made cards if you have these on hand.  I use American Greeting's printable option a lot but my kids like to make their own cards with it.  They look much better than trying to fold your own card stock.  I would highly recommend these.

I have desired and wished for a useable FAX machine for years but thought that they would be too costly or complex for my tastes. After a LOT of research and reading of reviews on various machines, I ordered this one from Amazon. One of the best decisions of my life! This little guy was just the right size, was very affordable, had every feature that I could imagine, and was a dream to set up and learn to use. Everything went like clockwork and within a very few hours, had it purring. First test was for copying and it just took right off and gave me perfect copies at the push of 1 button. The next day, had to send off 11 faxes to close a financial deal and again, lickety split, it sent off all the faxes first try by just reading the manual (the recipient immediately verified receipt).For the uneducated on these machines, you don't need a separate FAX telephone line or number to send faxes. It did it's thing right over our normal phone connection.I highly recommend this little guy. It does everything a FAX machine should do and does it easily and well.For the record on 'Brother', the manufacturer, I had a question that the user manual just didn't quite answer and I called the customer support number listed in the manual and very quickly had a knowledgeable service rep on the line that quickly, patiently and courteously took care of my problem. It's been a long, long time since I had such good service for a new product.Thank you, Amazon and Brother!

These pens are great.  Smooth writing, and I really like a "clickable" pen, versus a removable cap that I always loose.  The ink is also erasable, which is really a good feature for when scrap booking with children, who always need to "fix" their writing.  :-) The best part is the fact that they are ultimately wonderful for use on marking fabrics.  The ink will disappear when ironed.  Now I am not promoting the fact that one should mark all over the front of a quilt, for stitching lines.  But for the small marks that a person needs to do, to mark a spot for joining a corner or such, these pens are the best.  This assortment allows for a contrasting color on whatever fabric I am using.  Many quilt shops sell these exact pens at a much higher price.  I've been using these for over a year, and have had no complaints or problems, and the pens still good.  As a caveat: always test your pens on your fabric!
I cant complaini am really happy and it works well best of all is the price!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! nothing more to say

Ominous Title, right?These are fine, just normal erasers.  Nothing great, nothing terrible.  Depending on when you hit Amazon, you might or might not be getting them cheaper than your local office supply chain.  But really, do you want to put on your pants, spend your time, and burn the gas needed to go get these, or do you just want to click a few buttons and have them show up at your door.Lazily recommend buying.
This clear Display is well made hard plastic will not fold or lose the shape, easy to use and maintain, very useful and it does what it is supposed to do, I like it a lot.

This printer offers the highest print quality and the most features of any multifunction printer under $300.  It can do things that other competitors (i.e. Canon) cannot, such as print on CD-Rs right out of the box.  The output quality of photos is also superior to Canon.  However, build quality is a bit iffy, specifically in the paper output tray; it feels flimsy, sticks sometimes, and I do not have great faith that it will hold up over time.  Still, overall this printer and its successor (Artisan 837) cannot be beat and would recommend it in a heartbeat if the primary user is an adult.  With all of the features and superior output quality, it is hard to match... Just be careful with the output tray, might not want to let little ones around it! :)

I was having a hard time trying to find a planner that fit my needs -- until I saw this one. I love how there are lines on 3/4 of each page on the right side and empty space on about 1/4 of the left side of each page. There are only a couple small headings, such as date, and several blank spaces, so you can really customize this planner to fit your exact needs.I really liked that it has a side perforation to make page removal clean and easy. However, should you not wish to remove the pages, they stay firmly in place in the notebook, which is spiral-bound. The black linen cover is flexible, yet durable, and looks professional. The pages are a slightly larger than many other planners, (8 1/2" x 11"), and the paper itself is slightly thicker (20 lb, of which 30% is post consumer waste) than many other planners. I have not had any issues with ink bleeding through the pages.I have no complaints about this Planner. If your needs change, this planner can change right along with your needs. I highly recommend this item.

This copier/printer/etc/etc makes sharp and beautiful color copies, crisp.  Mind you it works much better on illustrations are opposed to photographs.Set up was a breeze. There are simple drawings and step-by-step instructions. It took only about 15 minutes. Do note that the unit is rather heavy, I suggest two people for lifting. OTOH, it's rather compact.There is one issue, and that is endemic with this sort of color copier. A resupply of OEM printer ink in all the colors comes with a very hefty price tag. Don't let the kids play with this, and use grayscale or the Eco feature as much as possible.Easy to use, simple to set up, great copies, what more could one want?

It's simply packing tape with the message Fragile Handle with Care printed on it.  I use it to wrap around the outside of a box whenever I'm shipping glassware, as well as helping me identify what moving boxes have fragile items in them.  If your moving, or if you ship fragile stuff regularly this tape is an excellent investment.  It sticks great, and Scotch doesn't make a bad product.  I don't know if I would use it exclusively to tape up a box, but a quick circle around the middle of a box makes it easy to identify.

I have this in the hall by the front door and it is great to jot down appointments and such as I make them over the phone. I can then add the dates to my google calendar when I have a minute, but it nice to not just be writing stuff down on bits of paper to enter later. This way, if my two wacky toddlers somehow manage to distract me, everything is in one location for when I have time to get to it.I like the cork strip to tack up coupons, lists, outgoing stuff, event tickets and such. The side column is good for jotting down dates beyond the current month and a good place to write the day's to do list.I think the price is fair and would replace this if it got damaged. Nice little mommy's helper to make sure everyone makes it to where they need to be.

Each school year I find myself buying a score more replacement binders because those purchased the prior year have been destroyed. I have finally realized that the extra money spent on Avery products actually saves me dollars in the end. Some of the cheaper binders don't even last six months around here. Not worth the money or the headache.This 2" binder is sturdy, closes nicely, is long enough so that the divider tabs don't stick out the side and has "ez-turn rings" so pages turn smoothly. The rings open easily enough and snap closed nicely. Inside are four pockets into which you can slip files or extra papers.A good quality binder.

What I like about this organizer is how heavy duty it is.  The tools that I find most useful are the clipboard and Envelope.  The clipboard is a handy place for quick access to work in progress.  The envelope is great to fit odd sized documents.  I was impressed that the envelope had lots of room.  I keep a few magazines in it that are of fairly heavy weight and it has held up very well with the weight.  I didn't like the pocket on the inside of the front cover much--any item that I put in there falls out whenever I open the binder.  But I do appreciate the elastic closure that keeps everything secure when the binder is closed--I've never had any items fall out when the elastic band is secured.

This stapler arrived in its box, tucked inside a padded envelope. At a mere 4.5 inches long, it really is compact, however, it will effortlessly staple through a maximum of fifteen sheets. With one finger stapling, it operated with ease while sitting on a desk. I find I prefer to hold the stapler in one hand and squeeze it together. It works well being hand-held and is easier to operate for me with my arthritic fingers, but it's stable and doesn't move about on the desk or table.Directions for reloading are shown on the outside of the box (it comes filled with a supply of staples and takes the standard 1/4 inch ones. Simply hold the stapler upside down and slide the anvil arm toward the rear to expose the staple chamber. With the stapler pointing upward, fill the chamber with one-half a strip of staples and then slide the anvil arm back into position.All in all a nice light-to-medium duty stapler for home or office that has a very small footprint.

I bought this printer since it is not advisable to use stick-on labels for blu-ray players.  It was very straightforward to set up, specially the wi-fi, a little bit more difficult with the CD/DVD/Blue-ray disc tray, but once I got it going, it produces crisp and clear labels on the printable blu-ray discs.  The discs labels look just like store-bought ones. It also works great as a general wireless printer.

This is my 3rd Canon printer & I really like the results. Set up was super easy, love the wifi less cords to deal with, being the separate color ink tanks I see ink purchase either being easier or more expensive not sure yet on which 1. Don't let the 5 color cartridge info fool you, there are 2 blacks, 1 for photos 1 for text printing & not all 5 come in 1 easy to buy package! Photos are more vivid then my MX512 which has been my photo printer for 6 months now, the other canon we have is my 1st photo printer now the kids homework and my paper printer, and I love the paper try being in the printer rather then with the MX512 sticking out from the front. Still can only print 8.5x11 tops so if your looking to print bigger this is not the printer for you. I will update as time goes on but for now this is for photos, the MX512 is the only scanner with a paper feeder which is great when you have to scan more then 1 thing and still can print a mean photo when needed for something less then framing like for a school project, and the MP490 will keep on being the everyday printer! The feature I love the most on this printer so far is the 2 paper trays so I can have 8.5x11 & 5x7 photo paper loaded and print either size without having to change paper!! Great touch Canon!!

These are really nice dry erase markers!  They flow very nicely and don't "skip" like some of the other markers I've used. The colors are very vibrant and they are easy to erase even after being left on the board for extended periods of time.  Would definitely recommend these!

With a 3-ring binder, you often get to pick between these options: do the rings hold together if dropped, or are the rings easy to open?This one is a hold-together. It's a bit tough to pop the rings open, but they have held up when I knocked the binder off the counter and it had 400 sheets of paper in it.It does hold well, up to 500 sheets. I didn't test it all the way to the max, because really that max is an ideal. If you need to store 600+ pages, you should split it up for ease of access.This binder had a good fit at 400 pages plus dividers.View cover was not perfectly crystal clear, but clear enough. Holds tightly to the paper. I'm not sure how easy a printed page will come out after a few months, though.All-in-all, this is more of an archival/reference than a working binder to constantly be putting things into and taking them out of. But it's great for that storage/reference purpose.

This is extremely high quality graph paper. The lines are clean and precise, without being overly intrusive, and remain so even after erasing. It's thick enough to stand up to even marker use without bleed and the reenforced holes on the edge are brilliant, meaning this could last for years of page turns in a binder, without interfering with the page itself. Perfect for students or those who need to freehand graph professionally, this is one that's worth the extra cost for better quality.

I didn't read the description carefully when I chose this notebook.  I assumed it was a regular sized (8x10 or A4? sized notebook) so when it arrived and it was the size of a hardback book, I was a little confused.  But that confusion quickly led to delight as I opened it up and saw all the good stuff packed into this little thing!Pros:-each page is lined with a spot to write in the date on the top-the cover is plastic (like 5 Star) so it's very durable-there is a see-through vinyl pocket in the front-another vinyl pocket in the back-three vinyl tabs/bookmarks that can be moved around easily by snapping them in/out and putting them where you like/need them-it comes with two refillable post-it note pockets and another set of pockets with the post-it bookmark type tabs (the multi color)-the spiral part that holds it all together is a thick, solid plastic so no wires to get bent or to catch on something. Also since they are solid and the paper, folders and pockets are what snaps on & off, there is none of that dreaded gap that always seems to happen with regular binders-everything is refillable and very easy to move around/personalize how you wantCons:-none I've been able to find!My 15 year old son immediately claimed this as his own, he said it is the perfect size to use as a planner/organizer for school.  He likes how everything snaps in/out and is right there at his fingertips, easy to find and use.  Since he commandeered mine, I'm ordering another for myself :)

These badge reels by Swingline are a mood lifting addition to my drab work badge. Sturdy, they seem to be the type of reel that will last for a while so with five in the pack, I'll be set for a long time. They have a little clip on back suitable for clipping to a waistband. No pinching or irritation whatsoever.No problem recommending these at all.

Brother continues to amaze me with their combination of high quality and lower cost. Here is another great product from Brother that works as well as products costing 2-3 times as much. I need to scan and print from the road so this item is a lifesaver. The size is super small and it works perfectly. Also, the setup could not have been easier. I Highly recommend this portable scanner if you are in need of one.

I loved the concept of these labels, as I do a lot of online shipping. The half-sheet sized labels make sense because that's how large the labels are on popular shipping sites such as UPS.com and USPS Click-n-ship. However, it is not possible to print just a half sheet of paper from the shipping sites because they are un-editable PDF files. Therefore you must print out a full-sheet worth of text (mainly redundant 'shipping instructions') thus wasting the 2nd label on the other side of the sheet. Overall a nice label product but you might as well buy the more widely available full-sheet labels.

This is a must have you do you Power Point presentations. I was using my wireless mouse to advance slides, then another presenter introduced me to this. It seems expensive for what it is, but it is very useful.
This is a very simple system for making spiral bound reports. The hardest part is making sure you set the paper in the printer to print with the binding edge correct.
Pentel Super Hi-Polymer Lead Refill , 0.9 mm thick lead is just what a grade school child needs if using a mechanical pencil. This was given as a gift. The feedback as been very positive.

Wilson Jones produces a practical binder that any student or anyone seeking out a way to keep papers organized.  Three features provide the ease of placing materials in the three-ring binder, first, accommodates up to 220 pieces of paper and within the left-side of the binder, a pocket where three or four pages may fit, second, the binder is recyclable and the metal rings may be removed; simple instructions to how to do that are conveniently printed inside the binder, and third, it is plastic and may not lose its form or tear.  Overall, for this reader, the binder is somewhat reminiscent of the denim binders made by Mead of years gone by but the only thing missing is the rugged denim blue exterior texture, the big three-rings, and a blank schedule that would be printed inside the binder where you may write your name.

I ship dozens of items a week many requiring bubble wrap to protect the contents of the inclosed materials. The cost of shipping so many items does tend to get expensive and so I do my best to find great deals on shipping materials that are the best bang for the buck.Scotch 3M is a name brand product. Their bubble wraps are consist with one another and so, when ordering each time, you know what to expect. The wraps are durable and I have had no issues with the rolls easily puncturing or tearing like tissue paper.Several comments were made about the price. Yes, the price of this item has gone up but there is a trick to it. Put the item in your cart. Next, edit your cart by clicking "Save for Later." Log on Amazon and click on your cart. If the price of any item you have in your cart or "saved for later" either increases or decreases, you will receive a notification at top. I log on amazon several times a day to monitor the price of items. When the price for these rolls drops by several dollars, I quickly place an order at that point before it increases back again. Prices fluctuate for all products on Amazon. You just need to monitor for the deals.Overall, a good investment for those that require durable and dependable bubble wrap.

Love that it's made of 100% recycled material.  Sturdy cardboard holds up well on a shelf with other binders.  The metal ring is very strong and secure.  Will use this for household bill sorting and other monthly projects.  I would go with a plastic binder if I needed to carry this in a backpack since I'm sure the cardboard won't withstand daily bumping and crushing.  The design is simply lovely and will add a touch of "spring" to the drab solid colors of our existing office binders.

~This is quite a handy little tool when wrapping multiple or difficult gifts.  You can wear it around your hand just under your knuckles, or around your wrist, (I like to wear it around my hand) and is secured with a flexible, soft elastic band, which is adjustable to fit a very small hand or a large man sized hand.  When you need  a piece of tape there is no fumbling with a tape dispenser while trying to hold the paper to the package, you simply give a gentle tug to an exposed pre-cut two-inch piece of tape and it frees itself from the dispenser. It's great!I would imagine that this would be a great do-dad for a parent who is allowing their young child to help with wrapping.  I can remember when my kids were young and they would try to tear off a small piece of tape for me and end up with a piece as long as their arm.I've priced it per inch with Scotch tape in a regular dispenser, and surprisingly the cost for the pop-up refills are comparable to the same Scotch tape in a disposable dispenser.The down side is that the tape is all pre-cut into 2" strips, so if you wanted less or more tape, it might get `sticky'.

Good tape if you need to secure heavy packages. This is thick and reinforced so it's meant for something heavy.  Costly, so don't want to use it on packages that don't need it (lightweight stuff).  It does not rip with your fingers so you need to have something to cut it with.  Other than that, not much else to say about this.
I ordered this twine to keep on hand as it is very useful both inside the house and out especially in the garden.  I use it to tie up tomatoes and it is a safe and biodegradable product.
Great labels!  Use them for work daily.

This monitor arm is very well made, it's built like a tank, I love it. It took about, 30 mins to assemble. However the height of the monitor is not adjustable after setup. Doing this requires an elaborate system of shocks, which is expensive. I don't see the point of not being able to adjust the height. I've also had VERY good luck with the ergotron'sErgotron LX Desk Mount LCD Arm, Tall Pole (45-295-026), and they're somewhat cheaper.

This is a great product. I have used it with both a connected mouse and a digital mouse, and it works great each time.What I like most about it is the very, very thin design. It is so compact that it travels well with my laptop. Also, the surface is easy to clean and stays clean in comparison to the soft foam-type mouse pads. I used this for a few days in a computer lab where I work with many other people who are not always as clean as I would like them to be. There's not much to say about Post-its at this point.  If you haven't used them, they stay where you stick 'em (on smooth dry surfaces) and they're easy to remove and re-stick.  These colors are very eye-catching when placed in strategic places.  I've always found Post-its to be expensive and these are even more expensive, but I've never found a generic substitute that works as well.The difference with these particular Post-its is that you get one month of an Evernote subscription, and these colors work with the Evernote app and your device's camera.  If you're already an Evernote user, these will add a bit of functionality for you.  As you buy refills, you'll get more free months, but you can only apply one month per year.If you've wanted to move to Evernote, this is a good way to pick up a month and try it out.What I learned with my free month is that I'm not the Evernote power user that I'd need to be to justify the $5/month fee to myself.  It may be that I'm not that organized, or that my odd schedule doesn't benefit from the software.  But that's just me, and current or potential Evernote users will get something out of these Post-its and the free month that I couldn't find.So the Post-its are just fine, but expensive.  They coordinate with Evernote, and you'll need to refill with these colors to continue to use that feature.  Several other refill packs are available, and there's also aquad note holderto allow you to easily access any color you need.  The Evernote feature is probably great if you're already an Evernote user, and the free month will be handy if you're thinking of trying it.But if you just need ordinary Post-its to stick on the side of the computer monitor, cheaper options are available.

There are multiple criteria upon which I evaluate any piece of hardware and those which need to interface directly with the computer require one to throw in a few more. First, there is ease of set-up. Second, there is the functionality of the device (does it do everything it's supposed to and how well does it do it). Third, there is the quality of the user experience when using any interface software.Note that I initially set this up with an HP desktop PC using Windows 8. I further set it up to share with other computers on my network. This included a laptop running Windows 7 Professional and another laptop running Windows 8 on a touchscreen laptop.In terms of the ease of set-up, this went relatively smoothly. I read the sparse manual and followed the instructions to the letter. Note that you can't just randomly connect things. There is an order to how Epson wants it done which will probably impact whether things go smoothly so read the manual. Installing ink was a snap, though I'm increasingly tired of the instructions with pictures model that seems to be the norm. Sometimes the pictures aren't 100% clear and I get nervous about whether I'm doing things right. However, everything went okay.The onscreen instructions did the rest. My network couldn't be found initially so I had to use a USB cable to help the process along (note: no cable is provided so you'll need your own if you have this same issue). Once I connected via USB, the network was discovered and the device worked properly. It printed a test sheet and I was able to scan. I did not set up the fax as I didn't have a long enough phone line to reach the printer and I didn't expect to use the fax anyway. I will update this review when and if I use the fax function.Note that installing the driver software over-wrote my default printer choices and set the Epson as the default. If you're running multiple printers on your network as I am, you'll have to reset the default if you don't want to use the Epson as a primary printer. Changing the default, fortunately, didn't create any issues with the scanning utility. Also, if the scanning utility is left open on any PC on the network, other PCs won't be able to access it because it'll be considered in use by another PC so you'll need to instruct other users to close the utility after they use it in order not to lock others out.I'm a little less pleased with the scanner interface than the set-up process. Though the scanning software allows you to select either "office" or "professional" mode to offer either a streamlined or more complex interface, there were a few bugs in it that I found annoying. The primary one is that there is supposedly the capacity to name a file before scanning so that you don't have to settle for the string of numbers after the "img" prefix that are a part of the default naming scheme, but I couldn't edit the name either before or after clicking the "edit" button. This function seems to be bugged, at least in my versions of Windows 7 and 8.You can print images directly from a device (such as an iPad) or an SD card (you insert them into the front). I tested this only with a thumb drive and SD card and the process is more byzantine than necessary. You insert the device, you are told that a device is recognized and have to press "OK" and then you have to further press the drive icon in the lower left hand of the panel. It will then ask if you want to look for jpegs or tiffs and after you make that selection, it'll load tiny thumbnails on the screen that you can scroll through. I think any time a device is plugged in, it should automatically load the images rather than make you go through two selections to load them up. Users aren't going to plug in a card, drive, camera, etc. unless they want to do something with it. It could be more user friendly and streamlined.You can perform some low level manipulation to adjust images on a storage card, drive, or device, but one of them is not "rotate". The corrections are very rudimentary (red eye is one of them), and you really can't see what is going on until you print something out. All in all, you're better off not printing directly as you have fewer options, but it is good in a pinch and is a nice feature to include. Note that SD cards don't go in very far. You may feel you need to push it in until it clicks, but it just barely goes in and feels like it's not complete. There is a light that lets you know it's in properly though, so that is helpful.The functionality of the printer and scanner are quite impressive. I found the scan quality to be superior to other all-in-ones (such as Brother or Canon) and that made it worth the higher price point. The resolution says it goes up to 9600 dpi, but that is interpolated (that means that it is created with software and not actually scanned in at that resolution). It really only scans in at 2400 dpi, but that is much better than most users require anyway as few printers can benefit from resolutions higher than 600 dpi.  The top of the box claims that this is "beyond laser" and I don't think it quite lives up to that claim, at least for plain paper printing (which is mainly what I do). The text is impressively crisp, dark black, and sharp on plain paper. Color and image printing aren't nearly as good as a color laser printer. You can see dots and gradients are not smooth. I'm guessing this would be greatly better on photo paper, but I didn't have any at the time of this review to test. However, as a test printer for images or for solid color graphics or low resolution proofs, this would be fine.I looked into replacement ink prices and color is $13 per cartridge and black is about $20 and there's a multi-pack for 56 dollars which includes cyan, magenta, yellow and black. Epson offers ink for sale at the best prices at the time of this review and is offering free shipping. OfficeDepot and other outlets are actually more expensive for ink or offering it at the same price. At this time, I don't know about the longevity of the cartridges, but the sites that sell the ink claim 300 pages per color cartridge and 350 per black cartridge. The question I am curious about is how often the printer runs auto-head-cleaning and wastes ink. I had a Brother inkjet which seemed to be running maintenance once a week and burned up a lot of my ink doing this routine cleaning.All in all, I think this is a very high quality inkjet with a better than average print and scan quality compared to cheaper models. It's the middle ground between a basic inkjet and a good quality laser printer. If you want something with business quality capability, but not for a graphics company, this might fill the bill. The networking capacity is solid and set-up is fairly easy.

I am glad I purchased this Label Writer for labels. By the way, it comes with a roll of starter stamps. I set up a "free" account with Dymo's Endicia postage. Using their software, I assigned a cost center or client for each postage transaction and printed stamps on the machine. Then I discovered a major problem. Endicia modified their policy at the end of 2012. If you have a "free" account, you must purchase Dymo stamps to print postage. You must enter an activation code every 200 stamps. Dymo stamps are sold in rolls of 200, and are accompanied with an activation code. The Dymo stamps are grossly overpriced, and it costs between seven and ten cents for each Dymo stamp compared to about one cent for generic stamps. It is easier and smarter, to purchase post office stamps.Although Dymo advertises the Endicia account as a "free account." A truthful description would be a "pay as you go account" rather than a "free account." In my opinion, the company might benefit by being a little more honest. Ostensibly one is forced to purchase the Dymo stamps prevent  use of counterfeit stamps or inferior stamps that are rejected by the postal authorities." Yet,  if you pay between $10. And $20. per month for a subscription account, they don't care... in that case you are free to use generic stamps. As if by magic, paying a monthly subscription makes the problem of counterfeit or inferior stamps disappear.  I am not that dumb, nor am I that easily duped.I no longer use the machine for stamps. I do use it to print labels. I loaded a roll of large labels on the left, and smaller labels on the right. I use the large labels to mail flats, and the smaller labels for file folders and some envelopes. I am still happy I purchased the machine. If you live very far from a post office, you may sign up for a subscription account. You will then pay between $10. and $20. per month, and you can purchase generic stamps at about 1 cent per stamp.

Number Stories is a collection of colorful worksheets which begin with number formation and include counting and basic arithmetic exercises. The cover text states it prevents reversals of numbers (in the practice pages, not every page) and this is accomplished by including a numbered dot where you begin each stroke. There are paper manipulatives in the back of the workbook to be cut out and used in the activities: set the table (count the cups and plates, add), counting coins (counting and addition),etc.  For more counting practice there is an activity to count the number of times you can perform an activity, how many sit-ups, how many times can you hop on one foot. This is good for practice when the kiddos are to hyper at the moment to sit still. :-) You can turn this into addition or subtraction exercises by having more than one child participate. Other activities: using a ruler, counting backwards, calendar, clock, graphing (simple stack charts), number words, addition, subtraction. There is a total of 40 sheets. I question the grade level because I think this would fit for K and 1st, but I would expect many second graders to be beyond this material. Our pre-K kid is still early for the handwriting but liked the counting activities.

The VTech CareLine phone is being marketed for an older crowd, and that makes sense. It's got big numbers and audio assist, and most importantly, it comes with a safety pendant that can be worn around the neck and used to dial preprogrammed numbers in the event of an emergency. If you're looking for a phone for your elderly parents, for example, this would be an excellent choice. But the point I want to make here is that the Careline would also be a great phone for anyone of any age.Here's what I like most about it:- The Careline comes with both a landline and a portable phone. Maybe I'm wrong, but I don't think this is a common combination, and it's a great idea. You get the security of a landline, which won't cut out during power outages, and the convenience of a portable all in one unit.- The safety pendant can be used to dial numbers you've preprogrammed into the phone. These could be emergency numbers or whatever you'd like. That's handy, and could be life-saving in an emergency situation. But it's also handy for day-to-day use: keep the pendant nearby in the shower or while you're working in the yard, say (provided you're close enough to the house), and you'll never miss a call. The pendant rings and you can answer it by pressing the button on the front, then have a hands-free conversation through the pendant. The clarity is fine.Those to me are the most important points in the phone's favor, but there are other pluses as well: it's attractive; it has a built-in answering machine; I like that I can put pictures alongside my four preprogrammed numbers. (If you have kids, you might like the idea of having easily understood buttons on the phone for contacting the police or fire departments.) The phone, in addition, was a snap to set up.As far as I can tell, then, there's nothing not to like about the CareLine. I'm very impressed with it.-- Debra Hamel

The name itself, "3M(TM) Foot rest, Adjustable, Extra Wide, Steel Construction," should deter any reasonable person from taking a second look at this foot rest. I'm not sure who gets the blame---or credit---for that exercise in corporate marketing, but let's move past the inelegant to the more refined.Many of us, myself included, spend too much of our lives typing into keyboards and reading words on computer screens. And for anyone who is tethered to a computer day in and day, out, sitting is something we take for granted. Our posture and position while sitting is important for many reasons and having a foot rest can help prevent back, leg, and neck problems that come from pixel herding.This 3M foot rest is wide enough (I don't know about the "extra-wide" claim) to allow ample space even for folks with large feet (that would be me again).  It is made with steel so the platform feels durable and stable. Though there is some sort of material on the bottom to create a bit more friction and hence more stability, you will need to protect wooden floors from both that material and the metal frame.The angle adjustment requires just a bit of tweaking, but the height adjustment takes a bit more work for just a minor difference in height. Both adjustments allow more options to help improve one's sitting posture, and I do think the long-term benefits are worthwhile.The manufacturer offers a five-year guarantee for the product. I'm guess 3M is not too worried about one of these heavy duty foot rests breaking but I am wondering how durable these devices will turn out to be, so I am holding back one star just to hedge my bets. All in all, this seems like a very good product despite its unwieldy name.

We (my wife and I) printed up a photo which we already had in a frame because we wanted to send it to someone and were absolutely astounded by the quality difference which came out of this printer versus the professionally produced ones from the photo counter at CVS we had been using before.  The photos from this printer are bright and true to the colors, contrast, and brightness of the actual subjects we shot--our pet rabbit of 11 years in this case who died last November.  The Canon prints aren't just slightly better, they are very obviously better.But just to make sure we weren't fooling ourselves, we then printed the photo again on the cheapest grade photo paper, and again on plain (multipurpose) paper.  There was no notable quality difference in the images coming out of the Canon on these three types of paper, and they all far outshined the prints from the photo counter.So then we printed again, using the same make and model of photo paper on both the PIXMA MG8120 and our other Canon printer, the MP495 (which costs only about $79 compared to the MG8120 which sells for just under $300).  While the image quality in terms of sharpness was better than the MP495 on both the MG8120 (of course) and the Kodak system used at the photo counter of the drug store, the lower price MP495 prints were still brighter and truer to color than the photo counter prints.OK, so now the question is, is it worth it to buy the MG8120 over the MP495?  It depends on what you're into.  If you're really into photography or even just an avid snapshot photographer, then absolutely you should get the higher priced MG8120 featured on this page; but if you want prints which are still excellent--and I mean 'excellent'--at an incredible bargain price, then get the MP495.  Both are Canon PIXMA printers, and they both blow away getting your photos done at the drug store, or Wal-Mart, or wherever it is you've been comparatively wasting your money on professional photo printing until now.We have since reprinted every single digital photo in the house and they are all shockingly beautiful--like going from analogue TV to 1080p Hi-Definition.OTHER FEATURES: Of course, the MG8120 also has a lot of features it's lower price cousin does not such as: a preview and system screen and ports for various kinds of input devices and cords most notably.  You don't need your computer to print with the MP8120.It's also multilingual--including Japanese, Chinese, and Korean (which have completely different writing systems of their own), but also a lot of languages you don't usually find options for on electronics devices like Croatian and Polish.Add that this printer also has a paper tray included in the bottom, whereas paper has to be fed in the back of the MP495.BOTTOM LINE: If you're buying a printer for school, then get the MP495 which will far exceed your needs for an incredibly low price; but if you're running a small business or you're some other kind of heavy user of a wireless printer/scanner or you're really into photography, then you should treat yourself to the MP8120--which is still a remarkable deal for all that it does at the high level of quality it delivers.Either choice will have you never going to an outside source for your printing needs again.

When purchasing binders, one needs to consider the use you have intended for them.  There are two things I look at,  the cover and the rings.  As a teacher and a mom, I have a lot of experience with binders.The cover:If I am simply going to put papers in them and store them on the shelf, I like the hard binders.  I use this type for filing recipes and documents I need to access.  Since they are stiff they are easy to shove back onto the shelf.  In the classroom these also work better, as they are less likely to slip off the shelf than the flexible cover binders.However, I find that buying hard binders for my kids leads to problems.  The kids like to stuff these into their backpacks, and the edges where the plastic is sealed quickly start to peel off, and the covers get folded over.  For them, I have found that a flexible binder in general will make it farther though the school year.  They will sometimes crack along the spine, but usually not enough to make the binder unusable, and a little duct tape will fix it.The rings:The second thing to look at is the rings.  The best ones (in my opinion) are the D shaped, as they hold more, with the little dimple on one side that fits into a depression on the other side.  This prevents papers from getting caught as you flip through.  They also hurt less if you snap them onto your fingers!  The other closure (a zig zag) tends to get misaligned over time with hard use, and the sharp edges hurt more if you close them on your fingers.This binder has a clear front in which to slip a cover, and more importantly if you are filing on a shelf, an insert area along the spine.  I am a fan of this extra, and have found that printing on cardstock, then laying the binder on a flat surface makes it easy to insert the label.  It also has my preferred D rings with the dimple closure which work very well.  However, the binder looks cheap, the cover being wrinkled.  I would not use it where presentation matters.  The price point is reasonable.

This Fellowes replaces an older Aurora strip cut shredder (AS1200MSB), whose basket filled quite fast. I generally hold all of my shredding (receipts, shipping sheets, banking statements, credit card offers & their respective checks they try to get you to use) in a basket and shred after the paperwork starts piling above the basket (about 3" worth). With the strip cut, the basket filled very fast and had to be emptied frequently, I'd say about 6-7 times with my 3" pile. With this cross-cut, I've only done a little more than 2" of paperwork and have only emptied it twice, and both times the basket wasn't packed full.The shredder itself is a lot heavier than the Aurora, and a few inches wider (also, odder shaped; wider up front & thinner down back, unlike the rectangular Aurora). I have encountered 2 instances where the JAM INDICATOR light had lit. I personally didn't think they were too thick, but I reversed it out of the shredder, and tore into 2 pieces to reshred.Credit cards shredded perfectly, although I think I'd prefer to dice them up angled rather than straight in. I could still read my full name on some of the shreddings.To test their claims, I took 9 pieces of Staples Multipurpose Paper (20lb) from the ream, unprinted, and halfway through, the JAM INDICATOR light had lit and the shredder stopped. Copy paper is relatively thinner than the bank statements & sensitive "junk" mail I receive, so I don't see 9 being plausible, unless it's really thin paper.  I had to work at getting those jammed sheets out while reversing, they were really in their tightly.The basket opens easily, but if you have the shredder on a carpet, it doesn't go back in easily without a little adjusting.  Putting the shredder on my chair mat made opening & closing the basket a smooth process, for the most part.  Dumping the basket can be pretty messing, especially if you're dumping the basket into paper shopping bags like I use.  Once you turn that basket to dump it, shreddings go all over the place; I had plenty to clean up off of the floor.This machine is quiet, does a nice job of cross cutting, but when it comes to the sheet limit, keep it lower than 9. Also oiling is recommended, and it would have been nice if they'd provided a small container of oil. I have always used the shredder sheets in the past, so I'm going to use those up.Overall I'm happy with this shredder and happy that the shredded waste pile considerably smaller than my old strip cut.

I've owned a lot of printers over the years.  Most recently inkjet printers from Epson, Canon, and HP.  Even though this printer has more capabilities than most of the printers I've owned, it's probably been the most frustrating one that I've owned for a number of reasons.o It's a bear to use.  They've crammed so much functionality into it (most of which you'll never use) that the UI is just ridiculous.  Buttons, buttons, and more buttons everywhere.  I feel like I'm piloting an airplane everytime I try to interface with that thing.o The wireless networking feature works really poorly.  I was originally excited by this feature.  I have several computers in the house, and have a wireless router.  The problem is that the printer frequently gets "lost" and for whatever reason decided not to join your network periodically.  Then you have to bring out the USB cable, and re-initialize all the settings.  After having to do this a dozen or so times I finally got fed up and just plugged it into the ethernet instead.  That has worked *much* more reliably, but it is less convenient.o the power-saver functionality works really poorly.  Probably the most frustrating thing about the printer is what it does when you leave it on for a while.  HP obviously put some consideration in to saving energy, which is fine, but it has bad side effects.  If you leave it on for a half hour or so, it will power itself down into some kind of power saving mode.  The problem is that it doesn't waken from that mode!  The only remedy seems to be to power-cycle it, at which time it often scolds you for doing so.o out of the box, it doesn't work with system 7.  This was a surprise to me, since I bought this printer in 2010, months after system 7 was shipped, and this was one of HP's newest printers.  Fortunately, they came out with updates on their website that you can now go get.  Still, it makes the cd that comes with the system worthless as anything but a very small frisbee.o The ink sensors are not reliable.  I'm also frustrated with these.  On the canon printers for example, there is a really clear display that shows you the status of the ink.  On HP, the display (like everything else) is ambiguous and deceiving.  It's been telling me that it is out of ink for weeks now, yet all the pages I print out continue to be flawless.  I guess the synic in me says that they don't mind so much in being "convervative" in their ink estimates and having you throw out your cartridge long before you actually need to in order to sell you more ink.  But who knows, maybe it's simply a legitamite defect.All in all, this printer has too many warts for me to recommend.  My next printer will probably be a Canon.

This little gizmo is a convenient and interesting tool for dispensing pre-cut lengths of Scotch tape. It is designed to be placed on a desk or other smooth surface, freeing up a hand while working with the tape. In theory this is a great idea. The implementation, however, doesn't work out so nicely unless you are very mindful.Loading the pre-cut "stack" of tape strips is very easy. Though there are instructions for loading the tape, most people likely will not need them. Slide off the tab on the top of the disk, pop in the tape (making sure the tab sticks up) and slide the tab back into place. In less than a minute the dispenser is loaded and ready for dispensing tape.The length of the tape pieces is very close to ideal. Whenever I have needed a piece of tape, 2" is a fair average for the size of piece I need and this dispenser saves the aggravation of figuring out when to cut the tape. The tape comes out easily, eliminating the tearing across the cutting teeth used in most dispensers, which has the benefit of providing smooth edges when applying the tape instead if leaving a serrated edge that can stand out against certain packaging materials.The mounting mechanism for this dispenser is simple. It is a flat rubber gasket between the desk and the hard Styrofoam base of the dispenser. It is not a suction cup, though it does create a vacuum - sort of. Once the dispenser has been placed on a smooth surface like on a desktop or counter, the gasket does create a simple seal that makes picking the dispenser up very difficult. However, sliding the dispenser around is effortless, so placing the dispenser near the edge of the desk can prove frustrating if you slide it right off the end of the desk...Because of the mounting, tape must be pulled straight up from the dispenser, not at an angle. If you pull from an angle, the dispenser is likely to slide.The Pop-Up Tape Dispenser is really a nice idea that can save some aggravation when working with clear tape. The pre-cut lengths are convenient and provide a smooth edge for application. The user must be mindful of how the tape is pulled from the dispenser, though, or using this gizmo may be mildly frustrating.

The 3M Gel Wrist Rest is a very comfortable product for resting your wrists as you type at your keyboard. I have a laptop at home, so I brought this to work and used it to replace the default hard wrist rest that we have on our keyboard trays. This was definitely more comfortable. Because of its gel, the 3M has a slight give as you set your wrists down on it, making it very comfortable to place your wrists on. I was able to type all day without having any sort of discomfort. The bottom of the 3M is a skid-proof surface which adheres to what you place it on without actually *sticking* to it. Therefore you won't have to worry about it sliding around as you bring your hands to and away from your keyboard. The top of the 3M has a nice, cool surface. It is 18" long, about 2" wide at the ends, and 2.75" wide in the center. It sits about 0.5" high. The black has a bit of a dull light reflection, giving it a little bit of character as opposed to just straight jet black. It also has an antimicrobial agent which is supposed to "inhibit the growth of microorganisms, such as bacteria, on the product surface, that can cause stains, odors and product degradation." I did find that the 3M was slightly shorter in length than the keyboard I have at work, so I had to slide it to the left side of my keyboard tray to get the maximum amount of wrist rest where my hands are normally resting. You may find differently or you may find that you have the same issue; it's not a big deal and it doesn't affect the performance at all, but I thought I'd point it out for those of you who may be more concerned with aesthetics and uniformity. I also found that since the ends are narrower the edge of my left hand was hanging off the rest slightly relative to my right hand; it was a little awkward. Overall this is a good, comfortable wrist rest for those of you who type at your computers a lot and are concerned about wrist issues.

A long time ago, I met someone who worked as a summer intern for 3-M. Her job was to test adhesives. They would take a standard size weight and determine how And thiswell the adhesive worked by determining how long a specific sized adhesive patch would support the weight - and they would also determine how it would release - would the release be sudden, or would it be gradual?  Would it slide?  Would it damage the test surface?  Would it leave residue on the test surface?The chemists would make tiny differences in the formulation of the adhesives, and they would send out batches of coated test strips for her to test.Whenever I see a product like this, I am reminded of the engineering and experimentation that goes into the development of such a product. I'm reminded of how much it takes to make an adhesive that releases after weeks - unlike, say, masking tape, where the adhesive drys and sticks and leaves residue unless you remove it before it drys.  The wikipedia article has a lot of detail on the type of testing that is done on adhesives.And that is what we have here. Something that is a "Label" has to have a stronger adhesive than a typical post-it because you don't want a label to fall off.  I believe that these labels have the right adhesive quality for their use. The labels do not have the adhesive strength that you would see on permanent labels, and that is a good thing.  When I removed the labels, if I was at all careful, they did not tear.I didn't write on them with as many things as the other testers did.  I basically feel that labels are the sort of thing you write on with sharpie markers, and those worked fine.  Nor did I try as many removal and replacement cycles.  My feeling is that you will rarely want to remove and replace a label - you would want to place a label, on, say, a cd case. The most important thing is for the label to release cleanly when it is removed. And these do - they don't damage the surface that they were stuck to (I tested plastic, paper and cardboard), and they don't leave adhesive on those surfaces.What I think these labels might be good for is, well, supposing you have some storage boxes and you have things inside the boxes. Use the labels to indicate what is in the box. If you take something out of a box, remove the label and stick it on the item. When you want to put the item back into a box, stick the label back on the outside of the box - even if it is a different box than it was the last time.  Or suppose you want to organize your kitchen. Put labels on the outside of your drawers so you do not have to open the drawers when you are looking for something. If you decide to move the item to a different drawer, move the label with the item.Or, supposing you have a re-recordable dvd which you record programs on until it is full. Write the names of the programs on the label as you record them. When you watch the programs and erase the dvd, remove the label from the case and throw it away.I would not use this sort of label to label a DVD or a CD, the label would unbalance the disk, the spinning would almost certainly release the adhesive and when the label came off it would destroy the drive.A product that I'd like to see is sheets of these labels that could be printed on with an inkjet printer.One thing that I'd like to emphasize is that these are not postit notes, nor are they a substitute for postit notes. They are labels, and should be considered as such.

First of all, it has a number of pockets: it has a large zippered pocket on the front; opening the item, on the left side are two pockets, one that secures shut with a Velcro strap, and another mesh one that zips shut; the inside back has a large pocket that does not secure, but it has a loop to place a pen or pencil. However, if one were to get a spiral notebook with a heavy, rigid backing board, one could slip that backing board into the large vertical pocket on the inside right, making the top remaining pages suitably supported for writing. I cannot recommend this item; it attempts to fulfill too many needs, and it fails consistently.
