Somedays I find myself staring at groups of women enviously wishing that my guy friends and I could stand around giggling and twirling her hair at the local Starbucks. But again men don't have the complex emotional feelings like women do.That was until I found these pens. As I started using them I could feel my emotional void in my heart filling. I found myself talking about my emotions to complete strangers. I found myself giggling more and even acting bashful. All thanks to these pens, they may be made for her but they'll work on him. So if your a guy like me who always longed to have his inner girl tickled and always long to babble about any random things that happened to pop into your mind then all I can say is BUY THESE PENS TODAY!  They will change your life.I love you all so much you mean the world to me I appreciate you taking the time to read my little scribbles and I hope that you have an amazing wonderful cheerful day!Love Chuckles.

Absolutely (so far) doesn't leave crud on my MacBookPro. Is kind of difficult to not catch on things (like shirt sleeves). I stuck one on my desktop printer... very handy! Anyway, these are light and thin, and do work. Just a bit awkward while moving your laptop. Too bad a slot cannot be in the laptop for stick-up notes ;-)

It's a dry erase board, it has a decent build quality now...Let me get to the point. The included marker is awful.  The magnet isn't strong enough to hold it to the dry erase board without it sliding to a vertical position which BLOCKS THE CALENDAR.  Very annoying.  I ended up just lying the marker on the top of the calendar.  Second, the week is set up Monday-Sunday.  Meanwhile, nearly every other calendar I've ever seen is set up Sunday-Saturday.  It took a few times to remember to write things in the correct 'column' because its not what I've been trained to use for the past thirty years.Otherwise, yeah, its a cool idea.  I enjoy using it.  It's a perfect size and very easy to clean.

This pen is perfectly adequate -- it writes smoothly and is comfortable in hand. However, the lack of instructions for loading the cartridge is a definite negative (it took me quite a bit of time to figure out how to get it to work!) and the pen doesn't have the heft that really nice pens have, that feel of something substantial. (That said, that does make this pen an excellent choice for people with arthritis or other health issues that make gripping a heavy pen a burden.)

I love these colored labels! I've used them for organizing everything from what's in my boxes of Christmas decorations, to my kids' craft items, and even stuff in the kitchen. They're not just for files! They have good sticking-power and nice, bright, noticeable colors. They are standard sized, too, which makes printing on them easy.

My wife uses this pink filer to carry work papers. This has seven pockets and expands to hold a number of letter size sheets. It measures about 1.9 x 9.9 x 13 inches and easily fits into her hand bag. It also has a carrying handle on the top and works as a perfect mobile file. It is durable and works for carrying the work for school, college and office. I rate this product three stars for design and overall satisfaction.

We have had an Epson 630 printer for over a year and have been very satisfied with it. However the 630 does not allow for duplexing a feature we needed so we were delighted to upgrade to the Epson 845 which does provide quality duplexing.  The 845 has a large paper capacity with two trays for a total of 500 sheets.  Like the 630 it has  scan, fax, copy and print with Wi-Fi.  It also has a very easy to use touch screen panel.One of the things we like the most about the Epson 630 is how long lasting the ink cartridges are.  In fact after a year of relatively heavy use we are still using the print cartridges that came with the machine!  Since we have only had the 845 for a couple of weeks I can't vouch that its ink will be as long lasting though the manual made a point to mention that Epson provides fully loaded ink cartridges with each new machine.The Epson 845 is a quality product that should fulfill the needs of any home office or small business.  I highly recommend both the Epson 845 and the Epson 630.

These are so nice. When I was growing up in school, gel pens were really big. I had a ton of them in every different style and color and I used them on everything. I remember they would dry up very easily and a lot of times they would skip while you were writing, so you'd have patches where the ink didn't show up. These gel pens are nothing like those. These write so smooth, and the ink never skips. They are comfortable to hold and they come in a ton of different colors and styles. The stand is also very sturdy and is great for displaying the pens out on my desk. I am a scrapbooker and card maker and these have come in handy for drawing accents and writing messages on my projects.
After being a long time gel user, this is my new fave. Something about it just works for me. Bought a box. Happy with it. Seem to last a while.

I got this for my 9 year old daughter. She likes the attractive cover design and is using it as her diary now. There's not a whole lot to say, good or bad, about a notebook so there's not a lot of criterion to go by in reviewing this one. But my daughter says the pages are nice and big and give her plenty of room for her writings and drawings, etc.; and, as I've said, the pretty cover draws her to the notebook. So we like it and recommend it to others.

These boxes are the perfect size for moving and are very durable for the move. There are lines on the side to mark the contents as well. Medium boxes are the size we always seem to need more of in a move. I highly recommend these boxes.
Avery labels are my favorite brand of labels.  The work great on my laser printer.  I use these to label my catalogs and other business supplies.
Even though this cartridge is half the price of the printer itself i guess that's brothers way of sucking you  in but the quality is great you dont need to wait for the unit to warm upvery happy!

I have used this product for at least ten years. It has never failed me. The sticky sides last and last and last. I use it for a multitude of things. My old 1/2" roll was marked by me in 2003 and is still going strong. Great product. I definitley do recommend.

You get what you pay for.. These mailers are nothing to brag about. The material is cheap and thin. I'm not 100% sure if these are even kraft branded ones. They look like the off market kinds. These are great size for cables or really small items. They provide adequate protection. You can't fit a cd, dvd, or book inside these mailers because they are just too small.

Sturdy and well made notebook is holding up nicely so far.  The cover is durable and still looks great after a month of daily use and carrying in my backpack.  The storage pockets inside the notebook are a plus and the pages tear out easily and cleanly.  I highly recommend this notebook.

This tilting foot stool comes out of the box complete, is a solid metal frame construction, and does indeed tilt to 30 degrees. It is fine quality, well made, and serves as advertized. The height adjustment is wing bolts, which are really hard to loosen, you may need a tool if you really need to drop the height down 3/4 of an inch.  I am using it right now, but I am not sure my posture is any better than before. If you are short, have a problem sitting in an office chair without your feet touching the ground or having the need to bring your hands up over your elbows too high to use a keyboard and also have your feet on the ground, this foot rest is ideal. Heavy contructed, but not too heavy to move. Overall, it is what it says it is.

While I like the lightweight but durable material and the adhesive surface of these little signs, I hate the way they're aligned on the paper. The first row of signs is flush with the edge, so if you don't have a print to edge printer, you either have to drastically modify your design (meaning you can't use any of nice templates offered with the product) or you're losing a third of  your signs on every sheet!The frustrating thing is that there's a thick unused border on the opposite side, so they could have easily set up the pages to have a perforated border on both sides, allowing them to be used on all printers.That glaring flaw aside, they are nice little shelf signs, easily printed to make your shop look consistent and professional. I'm using them with a self-adhesive laminating sheet so they product is printed on the sign but the price can be applied with wet- or dry-erase marker and updated as necessary on volatile price items, without having to run out a whole other batch of signs.But I'm so disappointed that my actual yield is only 80 signs instead of 120 because of the layout defect, that I have to take off 2 stars. I'd take off 2.5 if I could.

It says "Laser" on the package, but the inset included inkjets, which is what I use, and inkjets work fine--no problems, no smearing from the moment they're printed.I have to hand it to 3-M, they think their products through and make all the details work. The "Quick Lift" to remove the labels from the sheet is spot-on; really works well.When they say "permanent," they do mean it. Make sure you stick them where you want them as they won't come off again.

I got these markers from the Amazon Vine program to review.  We use dry erase markers in my house primarily to keep track of what meals we are going to eat for the week on a white board on the fridge.  We also occasionally use them for our adventuring map when we play role-playing games (dungeons and dragons and pathfinder).These markers worked great for all of those uses.  I really love the rounded (rather than chiseled) tip on them.  The tip has stayed nice and rounded over use and hasn't flattened any.  The markers are very bright in color and write nice solid lines.  I also love that they are very low odor, I am very sensitive to smells and these don't bother me.The cap also snaps on the back of the marker nicely so that you aren't loosing marker caps all of the time.Pros:- Rounded tip- Durable tip- Bright Colors- Write Smoothly- Cap snaps on end of marker while writing- Low odorCons:- None!

I got this laptop stand primarily because the work-desk that I got to use this summer didn't have a keyboard tray, and I wasn't in a position to add one to it. I was looking into the solutions that would allow me most of the keyboard tray experience without having to spend too much money. This stand seemed to fit the bill, and I have been very satisfied with it. It is relatively cheaply built, but it gets the work done. When fully folded it is extremely compact, and it can easily fit in a largeish messenger bag. SEtting it up can be a bit annoying, as each leg has to be fitted separately. This makes it extremely hard to get the exact level surface with this stand. I would definitely not recommend using it on soft or uneven surfaces, such as thicker carpets. Once assembled though, it felt pretty sturdy. I have used it both as a laptop stand and as a keyboard tray. If you use it while sitting down you will not have too much room for your legs, so be aware of this when deciding whether to buy it.Overall, it performed more than adequately for my needs, but you really get what you pay for. I would still recommend it for casual and infrequent use, but if you rely on a laptop stand on a regular basis I would suggest that you look into soem other sturdier options.
The cartridges are not as expensive as most of HP's cartridges. Ex. My laser jet cartridges cost over $100 each and there are 4 so these are quiet a savings. I am very excited about this!

Helps making life much more organized and stress free when you can quickly fin something makes life much easier. I find the green is bless to use if you have any problems with your eye sight and it's less of a distraction !

Athough it does require being connected to a computer or laptop, it does an excellent job of scanning photos and documents.  Much better than another similar scanner I own.  The other does scan without a computer and saves the scans to an SD card which is convenient for some situations.  I am very pleased with this model.  I use it with a desktop and a laptop.  It works fine with both powered through the USB connection.  No other power source is required.

How many times have I used a magic marker to cover an old package label... lots! I was surprised and very pleased to see these labels with TrueBlock Technology! It works! A real time saver and no more ink on my fingers from the marker. Add a package of these labels to your shipping arsenal. And, if your word processing software doesn't have a template for them, you can download it from Avery's website.Once you use them, I bet you'll be sure to keep a supply on hand. Highly recommended.

A while back the electric pencil sharpener in my office died. Instead of purchasing a new one, everyone just automatically switched to the mechanical pencils we had in stock. Nobody even questioned getting a replacement sharpener until this beauty showed up on my desk.Pros:* Provides a sharp pencil, without over sharpening.* Compact design made it easy to fit on my desk.* Price is reasonable for a Stanley Bostitch branded product.Cons:* For being named a "QuietSharp" it is not nearly as quite as I expected.* Doesn't hold enough shavings before needing to be emptied in my opinion.* Co-workers always at my desk wanting to use the new sharpener. (This last problem was solved recently with the purchase of a new office sharpener and I took mine home!)Overall a 4-star item, losing the 5th star due to the noise level.

I like this product, not necessarily because it is clear but because it is sturdy. The plastic is thick and not wobbly at all. It is extremely functional on my desk, but not too big. The only complaint I really have (and it isn't much) is the extra bit of clear plastic at the bottom front of the product which probably increases stability but also kind of gets in the way. It would probably be easier to deal with if it was not clear because sometimes I forget it is there and bump it.

My friends know that I love all types of "Post-it" notes.  However, I was leery of these "Super Sticky Removable" labels.  Please note that they are labels and not really notes as the entire back is sticky.  I let me dad use them in his garage to label the 50+ gray bins he has stored stuff.  As we started to label, I begin to mix the labels up (to aggravate my dad and to see how "removable" they were...to my surprise they were GREAT!  The thicker labels are great with permanent markers but using the new no bleed through markers are best.

This calculator has pretty much everything in the world you would need from a calculator but why oh why did they leave out a fraction and mixed number buttons??  The process to enter fractions is frustrating when you have to do it over and over and even the most basic calculators have these buttons.  Even the simpler TI-34 has these buttons.  It's an omission of such a basic feature like this that looses stars from me.  Otherwise it is a great device I just have no idea why something so basic and common isn't one of the buttons.  If I wasn't required to own it I would return it for a device with the same features but with the fraction buttons.

I know, like the first time I saw a Rubik's cube, I just sat and stared at this thing for about five minutes to figure out how it works. At first, I thought I received the wrong shipment: I thought this was some sort of unpopular female grooming device. I called Amazon customer support and a really smart agent, Hareesh, told me how to use it. Many thanks, Hareesh from New Delhi.It works by gripping the staple with those jaw-like teeth, then this device gently plucks staples out of paper. Already used staples loosen their pincer grip on the paper, and fall out like thin metal whiskers from a giant robot or something. The staples, alas, cannot be re-used. A suggestion for a future version of this device would be to somehow crimp the staple when it's being withdrawn from the paper to be re-used in some fashion. That would make the device more ecologically friendly. I took a star off my rating because if even I, who has been using this now for about three minutes, can think of ways to make it better, then something is definitely wrong in Who-ville. Plus the fact that it only comes in one color, black. I think a rainbow of colors would be reasonable and would make this a focal point of the desktop. For instance, I would have chosen fuschia, if it was a choice.All in all, though, it gets the job done. It takes staples out of paper. I wish it had a letter opener and maybe a Scotch tape dispenser build in...or better yet, a stapler! The pulled out staples could somehow go back into the stapler and be reused on the spot, you know, like when you put the staple in at a funny angle and you wish you could re-do it. Well, you could, if my idea works. If the manufacturer wants to take my ideas and run with them, that's fine, I don't need any money. You can just name it after me.

I love the colors, nice, thick and sturdy, the prongs are great, make fastening documents very easy.  We use them at home and at the office for all our filing needs, would definitely buy them again.  Everything you need in a good folder, you can't go wrong with these!

Conveniently sized to hold a good amount of mail, this organizer is sturdy enough to use in a home or kitchen and professional-looking enough to use in an office. The good points:* Quality construction. The durable plastic will stand up to wear and will not break easily* Label-friendly. There is a small notch in the center of the file to place a label, in case you use multiple pouches* Strong magnet. This is actually my favorite feature - the magnet is so strong that even when completely filled with mail, the pouch will not lose its seal.My only "wish" for this product would be closed sides - with the open sides, mail can (and does) easily slip from the pouch. Convenient for removing it, but not good if you don't want to risk losing something important.

I hesitantly took this gel wrist rest, because I have never had luck with gel wrist rests. In the past, I have bought wrists rests that were either too cheap, too short, or poorly made (Yes, imagine gel leaking all over your desk and you having to clean it up and fight with cleaning the stains left behind). To my surprise, however, I love this wrist rest. It's not incredibly soft nor is it too firm (there's a compromise between firmness in this wrist rest). I also love that it's super long; I don't think I have ever seen one this long. The only minor issue is the thickness of the rest; I find it just a tad thicker than other rests, but it certainly gives me comfort. I recommend this wrist rest for your wrist comfort!

Noodler's Heart of Darkness is a very dark ink.  The only other Noodler's ink that seems as dark is Noodler's Black.  Given the chance, Heart of Darkness will bleed through notebook or copy paper.  Heart of Darkness is waterproof on cellulose based products.  It cleans off fairly easy from other material.  Ink flow is good with dryer nibs.  Noodler's 4.5 ounce bottle is a lot of ink.  The glass eyedropper and tall bottle make for a more difficult filling of piston or bladder converters.  This is a very good dark ink.  This product currently comes with a free Noodler's clear (demonstrator) eyedropper fountain pen.

This is a nice pen that works great. It reminds me of something I used when I was in school. It actually come in handy now because there are times when I am signing something or filling out a form and I want to switch from blue or black ink without changing pens. The red comes in handy when I want to underline something in a document I am reviewing. I honestly have no idea when I will use the green ink.The pen is made of plastic.  The price is reasonable. If you want a four color pen at a good price this is a fine choice.

The Swingline Heavy Duty Staple Remover does what it does best & it removes the staplers excellently. There's a sharp tip in front of it & this tip is used to remove the damaged stapler. Lastly, it is easy & fast in removing staplers & it catches the unwanted stapler under it's tip.

Not that packing tape is so hard to work with or anything, but if you have lots of boxes, this does simplify your job.  I've tried other tape dispensers and I don't really have any complaints with them, but this one is particularly easy to load, feels well balanced in your hand, and is overall easy to use.  I like that the tape is totally covered--that's a nice touch.  I also think that the part that presses down on the tape as you dispense is better than average.  I couldn't find anything to dock stars on, so this product gets all 5.  Another good product from 3M.

This Study Kit is a variety pack of Post-it products geared to organizing a student's materials for study -- or for anyone wanting to sample an assortment of Post-it products to see which are most useful.The kit contains 10 products, but they're variations on a theme of just 5 items -- listed here in descending order of their usefulness:-- 1 Highlighter Pen with a built-in stash of Flags (a great idea, although the highlighter ink is a pale shade that's hard to see);-- 3 more types of Flags (in different shapes/colors/sizes, including one that's stiffer and can be placed to extend off the edge of a page and serve as a "tab");-- 2 colors of Note Tabs (one oriented horizontally, the other vertically; of heavy paper, with lots of room for writing plus a tab that extends off the page as a place marker);-- 3 shapes/colors of Notes (all of which have full-surface stickiness and can't be easily lifted to read what's on the page underneath);-- 1 pad of 4x5-inch Grid-lined Paper (it confounds me that this is a universally useful-enough product to include).All flags are transparent; all papers are mostly or fully opaque. All can be written on with pencil or pen (though gel-ink smears until fully dry).The first three items might have wow-ed me if I weren't already a fan. I keep them on hand, plus a large supply of traditional (top-sticky) Post-it Notes. But this kit doesn't wow me; it seems duplicative and redundant. And distracting! -- whereas my goal when studying is to distill and simplify, these products and the illustrations in this kit look incredibly "busy," more like scrapbooking.

3M's shipping labels are a strong stick self adhesive label designed for laser printers. This 2" by 4" size can be used for shipping purposes and to label household items or make name badges with.The labels come in a sturdy cardboard package containing 25 sheets. Each sheet contains 10 labels for a total of 250 labels. The labels are white with slightly rounded corners. Easy printing instructions are also included.I like to recycle packaging materials. However, tearing off the package labels sometimes weakens the structure of the box as it usually takes some of the cardboard off. I stick these labels directly on top of old labels and write the new address on them. This helps save the environment.As an added plus the 3M company offers free templates at their website.Great product.~ Lee Mellott

My classroom is in our partially finished basement. The concrete, textured walls are part of my room. It has been difficult finding the right product to hold up my charts, alphabet letters and various other things. My posters would hold for a while, but then fall.This product holds my posters and things firmly on the cold, concrete wall. The sticky squares are very easy to apply and are also reusuable. There are plenty in the package for many things to hang. I am very happy that there is a product that addresses the needs of those of us who use wall space other than drywall.

This is the product that came with my Swingline GBC Fusion 1000L heat laminator. The plastic looks fuzzy before it's heated. Once it goes through the machine, it becomes clear. The ends tend to curl a little but my projects have turned out nicely. An inexpensive way to archive or preserve my paper documents. I am very pleased with this.

These waterproofed arched labels were created especially for use in make your home brews and homemade gifts look great.  I really love that they basically print from edge to edge, and the shape is unique and eye-catching.  However, there are two issues that could be improved on.  Normally, I love using Avery labels, because the online instructions for printing and the templates are clear and concise.  You don't need to be a Graphics Designer to figure them out.  However, the instructions and templates are somewhat lacking and limiting for these labels.  I felt like they really decreased the ability to individualize and personalize your labels.  I would have really loved the availability of more options and direction.  Additionally, I hope in the future that the company will release these in a larger size.  I felt like they were not quite large enough to give wine bottles the professional, complete look we have come to expect from Avery products.  That said, I will probably order them again, if for no other reason than there being nothing else like this available on the market, at least as far as I have been able to locate.

I am quite please with my Smead Step Index Organizer.  It is not the biggest folder out there, but I have found it very useful for my kitchen organizing...  I am a big recipe and coupon clipper.  I use one of these for all my recipes, taking advantage of the easy to read dividers.  Another for coupon and rebate "stuff".  Then there is the pile of "use and care" booklets that come with every new kitchen purchase.  Because of the clear window at the top, I can tell which organizer is which.  They store in a drawer, fasten securely, and keep things at hand.  Works well for my purposes.

It's a calculator what can I say - it adds, subtracts, everything I need for the FE exam.  Excellent price and a great calculator packed with functions and features in a little package compared to my large graphic calculator.

Having your own laminator is probably up there with having your own island, well maybe not that great, but pretty darn great ! I started this baby up and it took a good 5 minutes or so to get to the desired heat level. Put my 8 x 11 paper inside the pouch and whala, a perfectly sealed sheet of paper. Couldn't be easier or more user friendly. I love it and will recommend it to everyone.Laminators are such a gift from the Universe. I've also sealed some important recipes, instructions, and favorite divine quotes which I like to carry around with me. There is so much to laminate, I can't wait to get started with more. Being hermetically sealed keeps your items free from moisture, dust, snow, rain, fingerprints and more. It's my all time *favorite* new toy which will be used time and again.

I do lots of eBay shipping and had high hopes for this tape as I do pack fragile items.  The tape is thin and flimsy and I wouldn't trust it to close boxes without double or triple sealing it if I was actually going to ship it.  For simply marking a box fragile this is fine, but the colors don't pop enough like fluorescent stickers.Poor implementation of a good idea.  If the tape were thicker and had a more eye catching contrast it would be a better deal but for now I'm sticking, pardon the pun, to packing tape and using a series of high contrast orange and black stickers to warn that packages are fragile

After receiving on myself I knew this was the perfect gift for my boss who needed a way to become more organized.  This looked great with the hardcover that it had that was really elegant and it had a 100 sheets of paper in it.  He really liked it and it was the perfect gift for someone that had it.

I've had two other Epson all-in-one printers. This is the newest model and it is so fast. It is a great printer for getting big jobs done. It's a large machine, but that is because it has all sorts of great features. It was easy to install and it is so nice to have a wireless printer. Fewer cords around is always a plus in my messy space. I have it set up to print from two PCs in separate rooms and it works well from both. The paper trays are large capacity so I am not constantly having to refill them. The print outs are fine, text is clear and looks quite nice. I do a lot of draft prints and those turn out well too. Photo prints are good, better than the last printer I had, but the colors do not come out as vibrant as a proper photo printer such as I've had with an HP. Scanning is very quick and also very good quality. I've only used the fax feature a couple of times and it faxed just fine.There are a couple of things worth mentioning, not really problems for me, but could use improvement. The power button and the touch screen are harder to press than I expected. A light touch like I use on my phone does not work. Another thing I don't like is that the tray for print outs is immediately above the top blank paper tray. If I want to change the paper in this tray, it is awkward unless I remove my print outs and fold up the tray that holds them. Lastly, shortly after I started using this printer, it would print blue lines horizontally through grayscale draft prints and sometimes yellow lines through color prints. I rarely need to print high quality sheets, so this isn't an issue for me. The speed and functionality of this machine outweigh these minor inconveniences. I am happy with this Epson and hope to use it for a long time to come.

If there's one product on which 3M has built its reputation, it must surely be adhesive tape.This Scotch Super Strength Packaging tape does not disappoint regarding its strength and itsadhesion. It's certainly pricey compared to standard packaging tape, but for those occasionswhen maximum security is a must, by all means use it. The rather cheesy "Manufactured for 3M"dispenser is another story...I have my doubts that it will last the life of the tape withoutbreaking. If you manage to accomplish that feat, the dispenser is easily refillable with atwist of the wrist. I'd rather use this tape with a quality dispenser, so... recommended withreservations.

You wouldn't think something this small could do a great job scanning but it does.  My husband had a stack of receipts he needed to scan and once it was charged, he finished in no time flat.  He likes the program with it, too.  He had a huge bulky scanner before and likes this smaller one much, much better.  It is much faster and he can take it on trips to keep up with the paperwork as he goes.  I am going to get one for myself now that he's tested it for me (smile).

This is a fast, efficient printer.The very easy to use control panel walks you through each step  and it easily scanned to my computer which was an issue I had with an earlier Epson model. I had no trouble with setting up WiFi or getting my computer to find the printer. It has both  large and dual paper capacity and because of that the printer is on the tall side. Pictures printed using the printer came out average but honestly I haven't printed any using photo quality paper. There is one thing that could be an issue, depending on where you need to put this printer.  The front panel, where the controls are,  slants out and is not adjustable. I previously kept my printer on a tall dresser, and had no problem using it, but with this one, you need to look down on the controls, so we had to move it.  Otherwise, I've used several Epson Workforce models and all are zippy and well made, and this one makes printing and scanning even easier than the others.
nice pens they work well and make doing good writing jobs earier.would give these good makes for the way that they perform and they work

The cascading organizer is great for my daughter, who is in fourth grade. She is the creative sort, so she uses it to organize the different kinds of craft papers: colors, textures, and prints.This is great for home use, but I don't think it would withstand classroom use. The construction is great for a child's use, but not for a room full of children.

I guess the answer is, why not an apple.  If you need a dispenser for post-it's, this will do the job.  But it's unnecesaarily large (even has pebbles or sand inside to weigh it down).This strikes me as one of those products no one has been waiting for or needing.  So why waste the plastic on this?

Probably the best feature of this stapler is that you can use it to tack things to a wall or such, not just staple papers together *which it also does very well) Also, the fact that it is made from 50% recycled material is noteworthy and applaudable. Other than that, it is a stapler that does its work as advertised.

The Fellowes Smooth Move Moving Boxes are innovative for the US, a type of moving and storage box that's more common in Europe than it has been in the US. The box is a hybrid between a US style "moving" box, that requires being taped together and taped shut, and the common "file" box, that folds together and creates a self reinforced container with hand holes. The boxes are sturdy and easy to fold out and together, with built in fold over lid. They may not do for "shipping" in that the tops are designed to be shut rather than sealed with tape. But all in all the Fellowes Smooth Move Moving Boxes, in various sizes, including the always popular 12x12x16 "book" size and larger, are a great idea and a good value.

The smart way to buy a printer is to go monochrome (black and white) because dealing with color, you have to continue to buy all those little cartridges that never last as long as they are supposed to.  And unless you are printing photos, there really is no point.  With this type of printer, you seem to pay more for the toner, but you get about 3000 prints for about 65 bucks. (That's about 2 cents a page).  For this printer, you want toner #MLT-D116L. I'll admit, the only experience I've had with laminators was in the school where I worked, and in other schools where family members worked.  Those old workhorses got the job done, but they were sllllloowwww to heat up, got super hot to the touch, and often creased the item as it fed through.  This laminator has NONE of those problems.It heats up in a little more than 2 and a half minutes.  The first time I tried it, I was still trying to get a laminating pouch open and I realized the Ready light was on.  Now I load at least one pouch before I turn this on.You do need a light to tell you when it's ready, because the outside doesn't really get very hot.  It's comfortable to handle even while in use.It feeds laminating pouches through slowly and evenly, and hasn't damaged anything yet.  Sometimes I'll get a tiny bubble or two at the very top of the pouch, but that's always been an area that can be trimmed.I really like the pouches that came with the laminator.  They're sturdy enough to take all the abuse I've thrown at them, including steaming them in the bathroom, and laminating an ID card, folding it in half, and stuffing it into my wallet.  The ID card still looks like new.  The pouches are crystal clear, text is easy to read and image details are easy to see through them.  They're a bit of a pain to open because they're a little clingy, but that makes them easier to load and send through the machine properly.Fellowes offers an "Idea Center" with forms and things that you can download, print, and laminate for use.  There are categories for Home, School, and Work, and include the usual things like calendars and to-do lists, and chore charts and menu planners and frames.  (The frames are probably a good idea--print the frame, cut out the middle, laminate the whole thing, and you can rotate photos on the fridge, under the laminate, where they should be protected.)  There are basic flash cards for the early school grades.  And it seems like they've added many more "Ideas" since the first time I checked, so the collection is probably still growing.For me, for occasional use, this laminator does a great job.  It's very easy to use, heats up quickly, doesn't get too hot to handle, and it produces undamaged, nearly perfectly laminated output.  I think it's a good choice for light or medium duty use.

I was eager to try out this scanner.  Several years ago we bought a Canonscan 9950F to convert all our film into digital.  At that time I converted 12,000 negatives into digital format.  Since then I have used my Canonscan mainly as a flatbed scanner, although occasionally I need to convert a few negatives, for other people or when we use a disposable camera.I set it up on a Dell Dimension 8100 on an external powered usb port.  No problems with installation, I was up and running in under 10 minutes.To compare I took a new set of negatives and scanned 6 shots in both the Canonscan and the Epson both at the same resolution and using the dust and scratch removal programs for both.  Here are my comparisonsThe Canonscan is faster, it took about 7 minutes to scan the 6 shots.The Epson took a little longer, 9 minutes for 6 shots.  The quality of the Epson was better, dust removal was more precise and the Epson software was better able to pick up where the edges of a very light photo were than the Canon.  I wonder if the LED, (being one wavelength) helps with this clarity.However, the Epson only has 2 slots for putting your negatives into on the plastic mask.  Theoretically it can hold 12 images, but that is only if that is how your negatives are cut.If your negatives have, say, 5 images each, you are only going to be able to do 10 a time unless you are willing to cut up the negatives.The Canonscan mask has 5 slots, each for 6 negatives.  In theory you could do 30,  but I found that because of how the negatives were cut I could usually do 24 to 28.Not an issue if you are just doing a few, but if you have a backlog of thousands it can make a real difference in how long the project would take.  The scan time is not hugely different but the time involved in physically placing the negatives into the slots and setting up the scan would take longer with the Epson.  The mask with the Epson is more difficult to work with than the Canon mask.  The Canon has a hinge on one side, the Epson the whole front snaps out.  It seems a bit flimsy, but so did the Canon and it lasted through the 12,000 scans.I really like the LED instant on being the impatient person that I am.  You do not have to wait for the scanner to warm up, great for a quicker scanning of a couple documents.The Epson is much more intuitive.  It took me about 10 minutes to figure out how to scan a negative (I, too, made the error of not putting the mask in the correct place).  With the Canon I remember it taking me an hour to get the general idea and a couple hours to figure out exactly how to get it to do what I wanted.I also could not get the front buttons to work, but you can do it all from the software.  Being able to scan to a PDF is really nice.

Size: First, this printer is BIG and it's heavy.You can load many types of paper including up to 13X19" which is very wide format paper. You can print onto envelopes and it comes with an attachment to print CD/DVD labels too.Setup: This printer is wireless meaning you can print over wi-fi from any room in your house and don't need to have the printer attached to a computer. We put the printer in the closet and print from our laptop, desktops, and ipad/iphones and it works great.You need a USB cable (it doesn't come with it) for the initial wi-fi setup unless your router has the WPS symbol on it (ours didn't). With the install CD, running Windows 7, and using an Airport Extreme router, installation was done in under 10min with no problems.Printing: Printing from windows or Photoshop is very easy. Photoshop CS5, and other versions, has settings for this printer already loaded and it makes really great photographic prints. Prints done directly from windows are also easy to do.The initial setting is for speed printing but if you change the default setting to the slower print and specify quality paper, it makes a huge difference in print quality. At highest settings, printing a 22 megapixel picture from my Canon 5D Mark II, with a color 8.5 x 11" glossy photo paper, it took under 3 minutes to print a photograph. I had no problem with paper jamming and loading paper is very easy.Print Quality: I used Epson photo quality glossy paper and the quality is better than expected. I get prints from Kodak online and shutterfly and these pictures are at least as good or better in color reproduction and sharpness. With the Epson premium luster paper the prints look even better. These prints are almost as good as the prints I get sometimes from mpix.com for my highest quality images and special presentations. It really depends on the photo paper.The ink instantly dry to the touch without any smudging right out of the printer.Cost: The printer itself is reasonable priced for what it is. The ink is where it gets costly. The replacement inks are 6 individual color cartridges that are easily changed, snap in and out. The cost 19.99 for black, and 21.99 for the other colors at this time. So if you need to replace all 6 inks you are looking at over $120 which is a lot of money.Mobile printing: You can print to this printer with your iOS device like Ipad or Iphones with the Epson iprint app. Using my Iphone 4GS, I printed pictures and documents. You even have access to the advanced settings like paper quality, etc. Setup was literally as easy as downloading the app, picking the printer, and pressing print. Really impressive.Conclusion:Excellent prints with quality rivaling that of professional print shops that I have used. The quality is only limited by the quality of paper you use.The setup is very easy.The mobile printing from my iphone and Ipad is really a very nice added bonus feature!

The MP610 has been phased out by Canon in favor of the MP620, but Amazon still carries the old model--and at a hefty price reduction.  The question: should you adopt a new-is-better stance?  Answer: hardly.  Consider the following:The MP610 is an extremely versatile yet powerful machine.  It proved itself for me in each of its functions long before the most popular consumer magazine listed it as #1 in its ratings.The 610 has served me most handily as a stand-alone copier, performing better than the dedicated copy machine I formerly used for printing out music.If you plan to use the 610 as your main printer, rest assured that once you've tried the auto duplex feature, you won't settle for a printer without it.  The MP620 does not have duplex printing (unless you manually flip each page to the other side).The MP620 is an "upgrade" (perhaps) aimed exclusively at photographers.  It adds another ink cartridge, provides enhanced "autofix" for those who touch-up their photos at the printer, and has slightly reduced warm-up time for the first print-out.  It also, at this point, costs considerably more than the MP610.  Don't expect the 610 to be available much longer at this price.

This notebook is made with a durable plastic front cover and a cardboard back with the Hook 'N Go feature.  Inside the front cover is a divider with two pockets.  Each notebook contains 100 college ruled pages -- perforated with three hole punch.The strangest thing about the perforated pages is that throughout the 100 page notebook, only every other page was perforated.  I'm not sure why they didn't perforate every page.  I thought it was a mistake on my second page, but then I looked.  It is exactly every other page perforated.  Why did Mead not think we'd need every page perforated?  Also, when I did tear out the perforated pages, the pages did not tear out cleanly.HOOK 'N GOI wondered why I would need to hook my notebook into a three ring binder.  Why wouldn't I just use loose leaf paper in my three ring binder?  Because Mead says I could write on both sides of my Hook 'N Go pages.  But I can write on both sides of my binder pages, too.  The rings stay in the middle and get in the way  with either method.The advantage of the Hook 'N Go tabs is that students can have several separate subject notebooks in a binder.  When they want to grab a subject, they can take the whole notebook out.  Everything is there in one place.  They don't need to take out single pages and they don't need to lug out the whole binder.  When students do need to take all the notebooks with them, the notebooks stay locked in the binder, safe and secure.PROS:+ durable plastic front cover+ two pocket divider inside front cover+ Hook 'N Go feature+ paper is three hole punchedCONS:- only every other page is perforated- perforated pages do not tear cleanlySUMMARYThis notebook would be most useful for college students who need to take copious notes.  Buy one for each class, put the ones you need for the day in a binder.  When  you get to class, take your notebook out and start writing.  When you study your notes, take out your notebook and all your notes are in one place.This is a nice notebook, if you don't mind the perforation issue.  I'm a little anal.  I do like sheets that tear out cleanly, especially if I must pay more for the feature.  Once they fix that problem this will be a great notebook.

The stand works as it should, in that it raises my monitor just under 4 inches. I use it at the office, so it actually adds more desk space.  The box it comes in makes it seem as though there's more to it. I can send a fax from home!  Can you believe that I am an IT professional and have never sent a fax from home? The Casio fx-CG10 comes packaged in a hard clear plastic case which resisted all normal attempts to be opened. Frustrated, I finally resorted to a Dremel cut-off tool and sheared off the outer case. This allowed me to extract the calculator, the hard plastic faceplate (which can be installed as a backplate when the calculator is in use), a USB cable, a serial cable, a Utilities CD-ROM (Windows only), and the four AAA batteries necessary for operation. A printed Quick Start Guide was included. The calculator, received on 1/23/13, had version 1.0 of the software installed.Upgrading the software requires a PC (not a Mac, though it works fine with a PC emulator on the Mac, which is how I tested it). I downloaded Version 1.04 of the software along with several other upgrades on the Casio site and installed them. That took a little time as I was trying to use my regular USB cable. The cable that comes with the Casio works perfectly but is slightly non-standard; don't lose it. I also added Physium, which displays an interactive Periodic Table and contains a number of standard mathematical constants that aren't otherwise in the calculator. The calculator has about 9MB of free memory once the operating system and basic components are all installed.Upon initially turning on the calculator, you're faced with several color icons, as if you had opened up a folder on your computer. There's one for statistical activities, another for financial calculations, one for geometry, and so forth. How do I add 2+2, though? It's not entirely clear when turning on the calculator how you would quickly perform basic math. Luckily, this is the first option, mysteriously titled, "Run-Matrix." The screen itself is a significant upgrade to your average calculator display. There is extensive use of color where appropriate, and the screen generally presents black text on a white background, very much like a modern computer rather than an old-fashioned calculator display (such as on the HP 50g).Although the calculator screen can be reproduced on a PC, this is not possible under the Mac OS. In either computer environment, you can boot up the Prizm and interact with its memory. Adding Physium, for instance, was as simple as dragging it from my download folder into the Prizm folder. It appears that there are many applications available for the Prizm, largely games which others have written and posted online.The keyboard works well though I prefer the HP calculator keyset, which has a rectangular shape and cleaner clicking action. The Casio's buttons yaw and tilt to some extent and it's not necessarily clear that you have fully depressed a key as there is no subtle feedback as on the HP. Each key has three potential functions, modified with Shift and Alpha keys and indicated in yellow and red respectively. The red is difficult to read in low light. I'd like to see a Clear All function that clears the entire screen, but this is not here (at least not obviously so). There is a multidirectional button in the middle on the right that allows one to choose menu options; but then to select the chosen option, one has to hit the EXE key at the bottom right. I'd prefer if the multidirectional key could be depressed in the middle to make the selection as that is a typical interface on other keypads (e.g. remote controls, typically).That said, the full manual, available for download and on the Utilities disc, is 601 pages long. This is not by any means a straight-forward calculator but rather a basic computer with a limited interface presented by the overall size of the unit. As such, extensive programming capabilities are present alongside the built-in application sets.Overall, this is an advanced calculator with capabilities akin to a computer including animation, spreadsheet, extensive personal storage, and interface capabilities to computers and projectors. It can even be connected to other Prizms so that information can be shared. I'd like to see a somewhat more intuitive UI in the future, but otherwise the capabilities are here. This should serve the vast majority of students through high school and college.

You know, I love my Canon printers.  And I am very impressed with myEpson WorkForce WF-3540 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, (C11CC31201).  But I LOVE thisEpson Expression Premium Photo XP-800 Small-in-One Wireless Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Fax, and Scanne (C11CC45201), which has nearly all of the functionality of the much bigger Workforce in a much smaller size!  Let me give you a run down of some of the features that I like best -1.  First, this Epson (as well as the Workforce linked above) is Airprint compatible.  As I found out when I bought my latest Canon, if you happen to want to print from your iPad or iPhone, just "wireless" is not enough.  You need a printer that is Airprint Compatible.  So very many iPad apps have a print function, but without the Airprint I could only print pictures using the Canon iPad app.  With the Epson I can not only print from all of my apps, I can also scan, copy, and access documents stored in the Cloud right from my iPad or iPhone.  (This printer is also compatible with Google Cloud Print.)2.  Have you ever tried to print something on both sides of the paper?  Remember the hassle of trying to remember which side goes up and which way you flip the paper?  The very first thing that I printed off was a two-page knitting pattern.  I sat on the couch waiting and waiting for the second page to print, thinking to myself that the printer must be rather slow or that perhaps the second page had jammed in the printer.  Finally I got up to check.  Imagine my surprise to find that the printer does two sided printing without any help or interference from the operator! I hadn't even realized that two sided printing was enabled!  (Yes, you can turn it off.) No more flipping of the paper or trying to figure out which way it is supposed to go.3.  You can email right from the printer or your Epson iPrint app!  Earlier this morning I was talking to a friend about making some homemade mozzarella.  When I asked whether she was going to use the microwave method or the hot water method she perked right up . . .  microwave?  It seems her book didn't mention that dead-easy method of making your own fresh mozzarella.  I put the recipe from my book onto the scan bed, tapped the screen of my iPad a couple of times and whisked the scan off directly to her email.  Mozzarella in progress!4.  TheEpson Expression Premium Photo XP-800 Small-in-Onehas some unique built-ins that will let you copy or restore photos, print a photo layout sheet, make greeting cards, copy a CD or DVD label, print on ink-jet compatible CD/DVDs, print coloring books from your own photos or even print various ruled papers - wide and thin ruled, graph paper or use your own photos to create lined or unlined watermarked paper.  Students, homeschoolers and crafters will have a blast with these extras.  You can also print on card stock and various craft materials.5.  You do NOT have to be at home to print!  The Epson Connect feature allows you or those you authorize to send documents, scans and photos directly to your printer from anywhere in the world you can access email. I checked this feature thoroughly when I tried out the Workforce, even emailing things home during my trip to the UK in early December.  NOTE:  I did notice that setting up Epson Connect was not as straightforward as it might be, at least not on a Mac.  You can access the Epson Connect Printer Setup by going to Applications/Epson Software.  Double click the icon and it is straight forward from there.6.  The Epson XP-800 Small-in-One has a substantially smaller footprint than either my Canon printer/scanner or the Epson Workforce WF-3540.  Dimensions are as follows -Canon printer/scanner - 17.5 x 12 x 6 inchesWorkforce WF-3540 - 17.5 x 18 x 12 inchesXP-800 - 15 x 12 x 7.5I've found the initial setup of the Epson XP-800 to be quite straight forward and particularly appreciated the ease of product registration.  There was no need to hunt my reading glasses to try to read the teeny-tiny product number on the printer . . .  the Epson software scans the printer and fills those blanks in all by itself.Other things I should mention:Unlike the Workforce, which can hold an entire ream of printer paper, the XP-800 has a fairly small paper capacity.  You will need to load paper more often if you are doing a large print run.  The printer does accommodate a variety of paper sizes in the trays - A4, letter, legal as well as 4 x 6, 5 x 7 and 8 x 10 photo papers.  (You can print envelopes and other sizes from the rear paper feed one sheet at a time.)This particular printer is intended to print photographs as well as general printing, so it includes a special photo black ink cartridge. Epson says this is normal, not to worry.All in all, this is a great little printer with most of  the functionality of its big brothers and lots of extras! A very useful strategy for organizing physical things is color coding.  But what if you only need to do so for a finite period of time?  Maybe you're going to re-use that box.  Or maybe you're just packing things for transport.If you use a standard label, it is likely to be a pain to remove when you want to re-use that container.  If the container is a solid surface like glass or plastic, the label leaves residue.  If the container is cardboard or paper, removing the label tears the surface.For years, people have used Post-It notes as a partial solution.  The problem is, the sticky part is a thin band, and the rest of the label - flopping in the breeze as it were - reduced the life-expectancy of the label to a matter of minutes.Post-It Super Sticky removable color-coding labels are a good solution to this problem.  The adhesive is more sticky than standard Post-It notes, and covers the entire back surface.  Yet, it is still a removable adhesive, and will not leave a residue and will not damage paper or cardboard.  It takes ink easily, and does not smear.  It can even be re-used a few times, although with degradation of performance.It seems to work best on cardboard and glass.  While it does stick to plastics, I found that the edges spontaneously came up after a week or so.  And any greasy matter on the surface kills the value - the labels pull up in a matter of days.As long as you are going to use this on a suitable surface (clean glass, paper, cardboard) you will find it a nice solution for temporary color-coding labeling purposes.

I'm inclined to say that the Avery PocketTabs are unique. In the half-page size, they're pretty much jumbo-sized note-tabs that also happen to be able to store stuff. Overall, the PocketTabs are well thought-out and seem to be quite durable.It should be noted that the dimensions that Avery gives: (5.125 x 8.315 in) are the dimension of the entire PocketTab, including tab. If you only look at the body sans tab, they're only about ~7.8 inches long. (This assumes that you would have the tabbed portion sticking off the page).In terms of capacity, the largest single sheet of paper that fits inside is approximately 5.1 x 7.3 inches. (It will hold a CD/DVD, no problem) While the PocketTab itself can hold a ~3/4" thick stack of 3x5 index cards with only minor deformation (eg. it gets a little lumpy but you can still close it), when affixed to a page, I found the maximum practical capacity is about 1/2" thick using 3x5 cards. (Approx 60) Avery has designed the PocketTab in such a way that trapped air is not an issue, and the adhesive is not edge-to-edge, which allows the pocket to expand naturally. (If you exceed the limit, the PocketTab will start peeling off on its own. In my mind, this is a good thing as I'd rather have the PocketTab fall off than my page ripping. Also, the PocketTab is repositionable) Finally, I found that the pocket is very secure and did not open when I shook it upside down with 60 index cards inside.My favorite element on the PocketTab is actually the tab itself. Even though the entire thing is made of flexible but sturdy poly plastic, the tab has a paper suface so writing with pencil or pen is a breeze. Unfortunately, the back side of the tab is just plastic so while it is the same color as the front, it's much more difficult to write on.Needless to say, your satisfaction of this product will depend largely on how strong the thing you plan to affix the PocketTab to. For example, I'm using this product in a notebook with relatively thick pages and I'm quite happy. I could imagine, however, the added weight being a problem for notebooks and such with very thin pages.My biggest issue with the PocketTab is that it more or less requires you to put it on the right side of a notebook. (If you put it on the left side, either the pocket will have to be upside-down or you won't have a tab to use. I have no problem using it with the pocket upside-down, but even then, I can't write on the tab easily since it doesn't have a paper coat.) I also noticed that it is possible (though unlikely) for very small, thin things to fall out of the corners. (For example, a common used staple, small screws, or a resistor).Overall, the PocketTab is generally well designed and quite versatile, but there is room for improvement.

It took me awhile to review this phone because I wanted to see if it would work at our new house that is currently being renovated (we've been working on it a year in January) but there aren't any land lines laid in the ground there yet. We are on a waiting list and hopefully it will be done before we move in the late fall.I wanted to see if this would work while I'm in the garden area which is about 30 feet from the house but it's also on a lower level and I'm not sure if the signal will still work or what. I'm not great with estimating distances but both the phone handset and the safety button thing worked clear out by the mailboxes. My previous phone system was a Panasonic brand which I loved but it would cut out just outside the driveway here where this phone continues to work for a greater distance.....I would venture to say it's at least a half a city block (I'm estimating....I live in a rural area and we really don't have "blocks" here).My husband has worked around heavy, noisy equipment for most of his working life and so has some hearing loss and he thought this phone was even better than the Panasonic which was good but this one seems to have more clarity and the audio assist is great because it's almost too loud for me so I don't have to cringe when I answer the phone but my hubs can easily use it when he answers the phone so we are both happy with the volume. Also it works when listening to the messages left on the answering machine and that's a huge plus for us because with the Panasonic, there was no way to turn it up loud enough for my husband to hear and if a soft voiced person left a message, even I had trouble making out what they were saying at times. Now I won't have to "interpret" for my husband because he can hear even the soft voiced people with the volume boost.I'm in my forties and still have 20/20 vision so I don't NEED the big buttons but I still find that's a nice feature because if you have long-ish nails, it's much easier to dial without accidently pressing a wrong number or two numbers at once.I can't think of one thing I don't like about this phone. You can even add more handsets so you could have one in every room if you wanted. No more 50 yard dashes to the phone, trying to get there before the machine picks up.The Panasonic phone was a bit cheaper and it came with two extra handsets but for us, the audio boost, voice activated dialing, large buttons and safety pendant make this more than worth the extra money it costs. I think this would make a great Christmas gift and most likely I'll be getting at least one and probably two more to give to my parents and my sister.Thank you to Amazon and the Maker/Vendor for giving me the opportunity to try it out.

I recently acquired a Canon MX472 printer, scanner, copier and fax machine. I wanted to upgrade from my previous Canon MP470 printer, which is just a printer/scanner/copier.The setup of this printer was very easy. Since I own a Mac I had to go online to set up the printer because the setup disc that came with the printer is Windows only. I don’t know why they don’t include a disc that also works on a Mac, but the online setup was just as easy. However, Mac setup without the Internet would be cumbersome. I chose to use my printer wirelessly and that setup was equally as easy. The included instructions were very easy to follow and the pictures make it even easier. It was up and running within 15 minutes.The printer quality is good in black and white as well as color. I do have one complaint though and that is the black printer cartridge barely printed 200 copies of normal text. The capacity of the ink included with this printer is listed at 180 copies for the black as well as the color whereas replacement cartridges are either 300 or 600 copies. I started a big print job (166 pages) right after installing this printer and it gave out right near the end of the project. My advice is to buy additional ink when you purchase the printer or soon thereafter. Once the cartridge is close to empty, the printer will stop printing until the cartridge is replaced.The copy, scan and fax functions are pretty straightforward and work really well. Copy and scan were quick and I noticed no lag time between scanning and printing as I had in previous printers. Fax hook-up was also easy, but with one caveat: you’ll need a landline phone connection for the fax and I could not find that mentioned anywhere on the packaging or on the website. I suppose most people know that? With many households going to cell phones as their only telephones, a landline is no longer hooked up in many homes, but fax won’t work on cell phones. No loss if you don’t use fax; it is, after all, archaic. Many places will accept the pdf version of a scan and this device can help with that and at a better resolution than fax.I am still getting used to the paper loading in the front of the printer, but I do like it better than the paper loading from behind. It feeds the paper more like a copy machine and you can put a lot more paper in the tray in comparison to the back loaded style. I had a big problem with my previous Canon where the paper was fed from the back. This eventually became problematic and malfunctioned a lot causing paper jams.I am hoping the bottom tray feeding with this new printer will not have that problem. Make sure you have the tray extended for the printed copies to land on; otherwise they will end up all over the floor.I LOVE the fact that this printer is wireless and I can print from my iPad and Android as well. Setting those up is easy (with patience) and differs depending on the type of mobile device you are working with. I have to say the Android was a bit fussier than the iPad.Inkjet photo printing is still way too expensive. Premium photo paper is expensive and the ink is equally expensive or more. It’s cheaper to send the pictures out for processing and pick them out while shopping. But if you have some shots that you don’t want the photo lab people to see, then this printer will create a fine print that looks every bit as good as professional processing, and the new inks are designed to last without fading for decades.Although the printer is inexpensive, the ink is certainly not! To refill the printer with all large capacity cartridges (about 600 pages of ink) costs as much as a new printer with 200 pages of ink included. So, if you print a lot, you’ll want to get a cost per copy to truly compare. Some inkjet printers use ink that is cheaper per milliliter. Laser is more expensive to start but usually cheaper to operate (even with color) than inkjet. Some cheaper, generic ink is available online and refills are available at Costco and other stores (once they get the proper adapter to fill your cartridge) but sometimes that ink is inferior, not just less expensive.If you need a printer with a low initial cost and don’t mind the high price of inkjet printer ink, this printer appears to have all of the functions and quality you’ll need; and if you have a landline and need to fax things, then that added function will come in handy as well.

In the past I've reviewed theEpson LabelWorks LW-300 Label Maker (C51CB69010), which I found easy to set up and intuitive to use. It's shortcoming, I said, was the quality of the printed label itself: jagged, dot-matrixy looking fonts.The Dymo Labelmanager for Mac has the same problem: the print is not what you'd expect from a laser printer, but I'm willing to accept now that that's the nature of the beast. Maybe it's wrong to expect more.The Dymo was likewise easy to set up. Had I realized I had to put the battery in I'd have had it going in less than a minute. (As it was I sat there dumbly for a little bit waiting for it to do something. D'oh!) Without knocking the Epson, though, I must say that the Dymo is even MORE easy to use, more intuitive. In fact, remarkably so. It's plug and play (plug, that is, into a USB port; you don't have to plug it into an outlet). And the nice thing is that since it doesn't require any software, you can unplug it and use it on a different computer just as easily. If you have it already plugged into your computer, all you have to do is turn it on. It will mount on your desktop. You click to open the app and you're in a window ready to type your label. You can then easily change the font, format, direction (horizontal or vertical) and size of your text, even within a single label. (I've uploaded a picture of the window to customer images.) Of course, some fonts don't print as nicely as others, so in reality you probably won't be getting very fancy. You can also very easily take screen grabs and add small images to your label. Again, these don't print out with stunning clarity, but given the right, not very detailed image, it can work. (I've also uploaded a picture of two printed labels to show the machine's output. I'm afraid they're not the highest quality images, though.)The quality of the printed label is probably no better, or not significantly better, than the Epson, which I gave four stars. But I'm giving the Dymo five stars because it is stunningly easy to use and more versatile than the Epson.-- Debra Hamel

Easy to move out of the way.If you like lipped shelves, then you will like this cart.  You cannot install the shelving properly, lip-down:  each shelf is potentially unstable if bumped.  That will matter if what's on the shelf is heavy or important.  As in, a computer.  For this product would otherwise be ideal for holding computers.  So, I assembled the cart lip-up.  HINT:  do the bottom shelf first, and put the wheels on last.  It's easy to assemble, if done that way.EDIT: the first cart (review below) is now deployed such that an old Win98 Dell Dimension tower sits on the lowest shelf, and an HP Laserjet 4 sits on the top shelf.  In between, is a shelf for paper and peripherals.  The monitor sits right of the cart, in white shelving.  That gives you a sense of computer station usage.  Import: it's easy to move the unit out to plug and unplug, remove paper jams, etc.Original review of the first cart, follows below.  Second is substantially the same.=====On the cart, I had placed my Optiplex 780 (SFF) with monitor on the top shelf; my huge Dell 8400 tower sits on the lowest shelf;  in between (12" clearance), are peripherals and wireless keyboards useful with either computer.  It is stable, and moves well on the house carpeting.  Thus I can wheel it forward for clearer viewing, getting behind to mess with cables, etc.I don't want to lift the tower out from the lower shelf, but merely slide it.  The lipping problem is solved by putting a large but relatively thin (1") coffee-table-sized book beneath each computer, enabling each machine to slide above the lip.  It works, but is not ideal.  I lined middle shelf with rubbery kitchen drawer liner, to keep air flow but mask the cords below.So only due to the lip-up shelving, is this five-star product rated four stars.  If you prefer a lip-down design, get the similar-quality Seville cart here in Amazon for about the same price.  I bought the Sevilles, too (and reviewed them).NOTE:  a computer chassis on a chrome chart will emit a vibration when on.  Depends on the type of chassis.  The old-fashioned tower emits almost no vibration.  But a small form factor like the Dell 780, emits a substantial hum you can feel when you touch the cart.  Due to that, the above-mentioned 'book' is more important: it nearly eliminates the vibration.

I had my middle and high-schooler look at the NoteBinder.  My youngest loved it right off, but her sister wasn’t entirely convinced that all the complex features would add up to the best durability and usability.There are five translucent gray-black colored tabbed dividers here, two with pockets for loose paper and an additional flip-in-slot closed pocket on top of that, which can hold index cards or other small, irregular pieces of paper up to about 3.5: X 7.75”.  A nice touch is a diagonal partial pocket at the top right of these two pages to help keep pocket-stowed pages from falling out.The other three tabbed dividers are open at the top to hold and display one or a few pages within.  (Why a display page would be tinted so dark I’m not sure, but it’s consistent with the overall notebinder.The 3 rubbery rings fascinated my kids with their unorthodox end-in-hollow-end closure, but it would be tough to quickly get a piece of punched paper out of the notebook, and a hurried user could easily spill out other pages and tabs by accident, we thought.  The tough nylon spine that is sewn to front and back plastic doesn’t look very elegant when the notebook is empty, but take up the slack with 100 or 200 pages and it’ll doubtless prove pretty smart.All in all, there’s a whole lot of ingenious features here but also a whole lot of compromise, not to mention added (needless?) complexity.  A notebook is more compact, a binder easier to open and close.  Add the price consideration -- at this writing, the notebinder is considerably more expensive than same capacity binders or notebooks from Mead -- and this is something you want to be sure that this really is the tool you or your student wants before making the “upgrade”.I’m calendaring to report back at the end of the school year.  (Yes, actually, I do do stuff like that.)

Presentation pointers come in a few varieties - mainly with or without mouse functions, and with or without a laser pointer, and small or large (which usually means proprietary charging or nonstandard battery vs standard batteries).  Then there are varieties of air mouse controls (trackpad vs button).If you want something really teeny, like the Genius Ring Presenter, you compromise on charging convenience, and sometimes on distance. Some manufacturers make other compromises - the ring presenter does not have a screen blank button, which is a deal-killer for some people.So what's good about this?  It has a unique shape (I refuse to say "form factor" when "shape" means the same thing).  It takes a while to get used to.  But once you do, you have a convenient tiny presentation pointer.  It works, it is responsive, and you can fit it into your bag easily when every ounce and inch counts.Would I buy it with my own money if I did not get it from Vine?  Yes.  Why four stars? The only down side, in my opinion, is the cost of the ink cartridges. I wish they were a little less costly, but I do appreciate the ink quality.WiFi was easy enough to set up. The printer didn't recognize my router's SSID when I went through the setup wizard, but I think that was more due to my router than the printer. Once I logged into my router admin panel I was able to complete the setup. WiFi worked flawlessly once it was set up.The scanner works wirelessly by connecting to the Epson Cloud Connect. I had to set up a free account with Epson to get this set up. Once that was done, scanning was fast and easy to do using the touch control LCD panel. The file was emailed to me, which was convenient. I have patiently been waiting for years to replace my six year old photo printer which does not work under Windows 7 or 8.  Based on the Amazon reviews (which are looking mighty suspicious about now), I bought this.  It is not as wonderful as the reviews would suggest.Fuzzy images.I tried printing several images of different varieties--animals, landscape, family photos.  In each photo print, the images were fuzzier than the original digital image.  The original digital images are all over 6 MP.  That's pretty large, so a print should be crisp.  There are only two settings on this printer.  They are "Text and Image" and "Best Image".  I tried both and on Ultra Premium Photo Paper from Epson.  With new ink cartridges and extremely expensive photo paper custom made by the same company, I would expect much better quality than these photo prints.No image software included.There is no photo image software included.  That's important with photo printers if you want to print different sizes or different photos on the same sheet of 8.5 x 11 photo paper and as expensive as the ultra premium photo paper is you want to utilize the entire page.  I have two software packages from HP photosmart and neither worked with this printer.  So I had to print full size photos which would not have been my choice.Ink.After four 8.5 x 11 photo prints, one third of the blue ink was gone, one fourth of the pink, and one fifth of the black and yellow.  That's a lot of ink wasted.The quality of photo printers in the marketplace has declined considerably over the past five years.  I'm hesitant to keep this because between the ink and paper each page costs around $3 to print and that's a lot considering the poor quality.  I'm also hesitant to return it because it looks like everything is made in China now and anything better is unlikely to come along anytime soon.Amazon reviews have become highly unreliable.  This was a mother's day gift and it was such a huge disappointment.  If you look at the reviews you will find the same dozen or so keep getting resubmitted every three months.  Although Amazon takes returns there's always a hassle when it's electronics and I don't feel like being hassled anymore.  I won't be buying electronics at Amazon anymore.  The reviews are bogus and the products are always craptastic.

This little product is a fair example of why I started buying 3M stock thirty years ago.  When I was a young investor, I knew I knew nothing so I said, I will buy no stock in a company that I do not use personally and continually.  That advice to myself has held up.  Hang on here for a moment.I was not in search for a tape dispenser.  I have one.  Every time I use it one-handed, I end up with it wound around my eyes.  I do not intend to do so; it just works out that way.  I am bad at planning my tape use.  I tried one made from a ship's anchor, so it would stay put as I wrestled my little strip of tape free.  I cannot stand the big lug on my desk top any more than the fly weight next to it.This is all nonsense of course.  But I cannot get over the latest in a decades long string of genius innovation.  Not the tape; 3M did that long, long ago.  It is the dispenser.  This little baby is not suction operated.  Get this straight you critics, because if it were, it would not glide like a hockey puck across my desk.  But try to clean and jerk it, and you are in for a real surprise.Not only does it slide like Ty Cobb; not only does it hold like a a teen-ager with her heart throb; it holds onto my fifty year old deep grained and distressed desk top.This is only the first application of this impressive chemical engineering.  Cheers!  Roll on, Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing.
