I am awarding this printer 5 stars for its ease of installation, quality of output, quality of workmanship, unit price and the average cost of a printed page.The Xerox Phaser 6310N appears to be a solid, quality unit. Given that you will print a couple thousand pages before you need to buy your next toner, you get a lot of value for the price. Thereafter, based on the prices currently listed at Amazon, paying $70 for 2500 black and white pages is not bad at all. In fact, on a per-page basis, you are paying significantly less vs. what you would spend on a generic ink-jet printer.I installed the printer at home, in the basement, plugged into a wireless Linksys router via an Ethernet wire. My printer is now taking jobs from 5 different computers, connected through the same router over Wi-Fi and running Windows XP and Vista.The unit comes in a nice, neat box where very little space is wasted. The unit is very much assembled and ready to go. There is a `Quick Installation', poster-sized guide (also a 'flash' animation on the CD) that explains in detail how to remove the various sticky tapes that held the printer together during transportation and lock in the toner cartridges. Once that's done, you plug in the power, connect the printer via either USB or Ethernet (USB and Ethernet cables NOT included), turn it on, set up your favorite language if it's not English and you are ready to go. On the computer side, you need to install the Xerox printer driver.The driver installation(*) was relatively quick and nearly flawless. For it to proceed, the setup program must first find the printer. Since the printer was not physically connected to the laptop, it immediately started to look for IP-based printers. You must make sure that the printer is turned on and it has an IP address(**) while this is happening. The status page, which you can print from the front panel, will tell you if that is the case. My DHCP-enabled Linksys router assigned an address to the printer so no complicated setup was required. On the Vista side, I had to give Vista permission for a couple of tasks to complete. The setup gives you the opportunity to register your printer online. I agreed and it was quick and easy even though I was surprised that the setup knew my printer's serial number but not the model which I have to pick it myself from a long drop-down list.From the moment I opened the box to the time I printed my first page off a document, it took less than one hour. I can see how some users may require help with the network installation part. I cannot say how Xerox supports end-users with more complex network setups because I did not have to call the tech support.The Phaser 3310N is a large, solid box (see Amazon's picture) and it is so because it holds large (fully loaded) toner cartridges and the fuser unit. Printing is quick and quiet and I experienced no paper jams yet. The colors are bright and both the text and the graphics are crisp - I printed some very complicated flowcharts and a colorful logo to test and I was satisfied with the result. Out of the box, over 200 PCL and PostScript fonts are supported. Other features include 128Mb of memory, support for various paper sizes and paper types including glossies and envelopes, it can be set to go into PowerSaver mode after a period of inactivity (and I reduced it from the 30 minute default to 5 minutes), can be set to produce an audible tone on various conditions, will produce Configuration pages with values for various settings and parameters including the environment's temperature and humidity.This printer should be ideal for the small office and it could be great for the home if the relatively large size does not bother you. In my case, it doesn't because it's going to stay in the basement. Memory expansion or wireless connections were not issues for me but those who have such concerns should do some research before buying.________________________________________________________________________(*) Note that you will have to install the driver on ALL the computers that are going to use the printer. Every time you install the driver, you will be prompted to register again. After you complete your first registration, ignore any subsequent invitations.(**) I can think of 3 basic way you can connect the printer without having to buy any extra hardware, other than a cable, if you don't have one already:1 - Personal printer - use a USB cable to connect it directly to your desktop computer (or your laptop's docking station)2 - Shared printer - after connecting the printer as above and you install the printer driver, share it (the specific steps depend on your operating system but it's usually easy). This way, anyone on the same network can use it for as long as the computer that's sharing it is up.3 - Network printer - you plug it into a network port or directly into a router using an Ethernet cable. Unless you place some restrictions, everyone on the network should be able to use the printer for as long as it is on and the network is up.

I've previously avoided multi-function devices on the basis that, at least historically, they didn't do any one of the functions extremely well. Things like scanning were better handled by a dedicated flatbed scanner, and dedicated inkjet printers produced sharper text and better pictures. That being said, I'm very impressed with the WF-2540. I even liked it enough to recommend it for my in-laws, though they went with the nearly identical WF-2530 model.Scan quality -- I have a old Canon CanoScan flatbed scanner than I can now get rid of. I'm very pleased with the resolution options and color quality, and I like the way the options such as "Descreening" are presented in the interface better than what my CanoScan offered.Print quality -- My other inkjet printer is an Epson Stylus Photo, so it isn't really the best comparison. The image sharpness is excellent. Understandably the colors are a bit dull compared to the Stylus Photo, but that's understandable as this is a 4-color printer (my Stylus is 6-color). As for text, I've traditionally veered away from inkjets (favoring laser printers) because it tends to looks fuzzy, but I find the WF-2540 to be reasonably sharp and will probably get rid of my laser printer in the near future.Fax quality -- Not a lot to say here. I sent a fax to myself at work and it looked good.Wi-Fi/Networking -- This is actually one of my favorite aspects of this printer. It's great being able to use it from any computer in the house (noting that the driver does have to get installed on each computer to use the printer). And it's not limited to printing: you can also scan and fax via wi-fi from any computer, with the scan result being copied to your local machine. Also available is Epson Connect, which you can set up to print from outside of your network. On the most basic level, you can forward an email to your custom @print.epsonconnect.com email address and it'll get printed. Finally, the printer also includes AirPrint, which means that you can print directly from your iPhone or iPad, which also works as expected.Driver and Installation (Mac) -- I always skip using the CD that comes with the printer because 9/10 of the time it's out-of-date, and this was no exception. I downloaded the most recent package from Epson and installed it. Important note: by default, all of the available software is not marked for install, and I very strongly recommend installing the Download Navigator (updater utility), as even though the downloaded driver was the most recent on the website, there was a driver update and firmware update available in the updater. After the driver was installed, a wizard takes you through the setup of the device, including setting your fax name and number.Weaknesses -- The only things that could be better with this printer have to do with the installation and setup. First, as noted above, the Download Navigator (updater utility) is not installed by default, and even with the most recent package from the website there are additional updates available. Second, during initial setup, you have to join the printer to Wi-Fi on the printer's front panel, which means typing in your Wi-Fi password on the telephone input panel. Third, I can't find a way to get back to the setup wizard, so there's no easy way to change the header name or number for, say, the fax settings. All of the settings are editable via the front panel of the device, but that's not as user-friendly. Finally, getting to the printer application, at least on the Mac, is a bit weird in that it's launched via System Preferences -> Print & Scan (or Print & Fax in 10.6). Thus scanning (which is handled from the printer application in the Print & Scan System Preference pane) can be a bit non-intuitive until you realize where it's hidden (however, you can scan directly from the printer and it will dump the output on your desktop). The only other minor weakness is that I find some of the functions of the buttons on the front of the unit to be a little non-intuitive when copying and faxing, but I got used them after a bit of trial and error.

This Targus lap desk is a good solution for those who want a small, portable lap desk for their laptops. When fully closed it is only about 0.5" thick, but unzip it and it springs open at an angle to be about 3" thick at its widest (in the back). The angle allows for a pretty comfortable typing scheme, rather than sitting flat. I have a heavy 17" laptop, and even though this is only made for laptops 15" or less, mine sits on it pretty well and the lap desk still supports its weight. Unlike another reviewer, I do not find it difficult to keep it propped on my legs. I am 6'3" and have my knees spread about 8" apart right now and the lap desk is sitting "comfortably." I use quotes because I've found that I actually don't find this to be comfortable to use for long periods of time, as the back flipping piece pushes into your legs and hurts a little. Because the material across the surface is a mesh, air from your laptop fans can go right through it and out the bottom without it warming you up, which is fantastic. The surface also has two non-skid bumps near the top to help hold your laptop in place, but because my laptop is already bigger than this, I don't find them to be of use to me (the front of my laptop still has to rest on my legs). When you are all finished using this, just zip it back up and it closes tightly on its own as you're zipping it. Overall a very good and reasonably-priced solution for people who want to be able to easily type from their lap without having to deal with regular laptop heat.

This is the second Hon chair I've received as part of the Amazon Vine program.  I've been using the first one (Basyx VL701ST11 VL700 Series Executive High-Back Swivel/Tilt Chair, Black Leather/Meshfor that past 6 months and have been very happy with its quality and performance.This chair, the Hon Ignition Task Chair is of similar high quality with additional features and a sold padded back versus a mesh one.  It's also several inches shorter (the back height), or so I thought until on accident I lifted the chair, heard a racheting sound and noted the back could be raised and lowered.The Pro's:+ Chair is well made and very easy to put together.  3 pieces with picture-type instructions: 1-2-3-4 you're done.+ Adjustable width for the chair's arms. You can gain approximately 4 to 5 inches on each side of the chair; moving the armrests out by pushing down on a lever under the seat.+ Adjustable arm chair height.  Raise and lower the arms of the chair independently.+ Chair lift adjustment.  Users 5' to 6' should find a comfortable height position.+ Adjustable back of the chair height.  This is accomplished by lifting up on the back of the seat; you'll hear a clicking noise as you do this.  If you go all the way to the top of the adjustment the seat back drops back to the bottom - starting position.  This took my husband about 20 minutes to figure out for me.  If you have gone too high, you have to start over.  How do you know you've gone to high?  The seat back falls back to the low position.  Offers adequate lumbar support for most users up to 6' tall.+ Seat firmness is adjustable.  Use the knob on the bottom of the chair to soften or firm up the seat to your liking.  I turned it thinking the 'tilt' feature would be there.+ The 'tilt' feature:  PULL OUT on the lever on the right hand side of the chair. This is the lever you use to raise and lower the seat.  If you leave the lever pulled out, the chair continues to have the tilt feature.  If you don't want the tilt feature, put the chair back to the upright position and push in the lever - which then locks into that position.  You cannot lock the chair into the tilt back position.The Con's:- The directions for the assembly of this item are minimal, but worse, the directions for its use are non-existent!  Awful oversight on the manufacturer's part and the reason for the 4 out of 5 star rating.  I can totally see why people might hate this chair because they think they can't adjust things as promised.  A couple simple how-to's for seat height adjustment and tilt adjustment, would probably make a lot of consumers happier with this product.- Despite the chair width adjustment, some users will find the chair best suited for small to medium frames. Not necessarily a 'con', just an issue to be considered.  I'm 5'6" & 145 pounds, and it fits me just fine.Conclusion:Overall this is a well-built, feature-rich office task chair which would be suitable for many people, but not all.  It has multiple adjustments: height of arms, width of arms, height of backrest, height of chair and tilt, which work well when you figure out how to get them to work!The chair is super easy to put together, even with the minimal directions.The worst part about this product is the lack of directions on its use.  The features of the chair are tough to discover.  No help is given in the form of 'How-To' directions or even diagrams to operate the chair's functions.  Small diagrams on a lever are the only ones you see, and they are not clear.Perhaps it was due to the Amazon Vine packaging, I did not receive warranty info on this chair, or any documentation on how to contact the company should there have been a problem.  Not sure if that will be the case for buyers of the chair.I would recommend this chair for its quality build and features, but give it a 4 out of 5 star review due to the terrible lack of instructions.  For as much as you pay for this chair, you'd like to know how the features work without a hassle!UPDATE: 5/17/13I've been using this chair for quite awhile now, and find it's good for me most of the time.  However I did find that considering the long hours I spend at my desk I needed more back support than this chair provides, so I purchased aFellowes Professional Series Back Support, Black (8037601)to go on it.  That made a world of difference, and I'd recommend it to anyone with any office chair other than wide or tall back 'executive or manager' type chairs.Features Per Hon:HON Ignition Series Low-Back Work ChairPneumatic seat height adjustment360-degree swivelTilt, tilt tension, and tilt lockAdjustable back heightAdjustable height and width armsHard casters for use on carpets and chair matsStandard black frameChair is warranted for users up to 300 poundsHON Full Lifetime WarrantyDimensionsOverall:  36in D x 27.5in W x 41in HSeat:  17in D x 19in WBack:  17.5in W x 20-23in HSeat to Floor:  17in - 21.5in HUsable Seat Depth:  17-21.5in DWeight:  50 lbs.

Close your MacBook, place it on the ZeroStand, and step back a bit and sit down. I've owned the Brother MFC-490-CW printer for 6 or 7 months. I purchased it at Staples and after rebate it was only around $70. I was skeptical that an all-in-one, wireless printer could be any good for such a low price. I was wrong.As a computer consultant, I have long recommended Brother Laser Printers to my clients. They have proven their great value over the years. But ink-jets are another beast. I've never really owned a "good" ink-jet printer that didn't clog up, or jam or just provide less than satisfactory performance.This printer is wonderful. Software installation was not complicated and installed equally well on my PC as well as my Mac. Having a wireless printer is just fantastic. You can put it just about anywhere without having to worry about wires, cables. All the functions work well. Scanning to memory card is easily accomplished as well as to your computer. Faxing is easy as is copying and printing. You can also print photos directly from the memory card if you wish.The only thing that wasn't great was the OCR software included with the printer. It worked better on the PC than on the Mac for some reason. But both platforms gave mostly unsatisfactory results with many recognition errors.Other than the OCR issue, which is probably not even a big factor for many users, this is an awesome printer. I can't even believe that a printer with this much function can sell for so cheaply. I mean, the cheapest Canon flatbed scanner you can find is selling for around $90 and all it does is scan. This device not only scans, but copies, faxes, prints and is wireless to boot. Even buying a wireless network adaptor for an existing printer is more expensive that this entire printer WITH wireless capability.I also own an HP Officejet Pro 8500 Wireless All-In-One PrinterHP Officejet Pro 8500 Wireless All-In-One Printerwhich costs over three times as much as this Brother MFC-490CW. About the only major feature that the Brother lacks compared to the HP is Duplex printing. In most other regards, it performs admirably when compared to its much more expensive rival.Ink usage and cost is always a consideration when choosing a printer. Usually ink is a very expensive component. Well, ink is expensive even for this printer, but not as expensive as Epson ink that I've also purchased. Any printer will have consumable costs and unfortunately buying third-party ink or refilling ink tanks is not a good idea because usually the ink will clog up or even damage your printer in the worse case scenario and provide less vibrant color that fades more quickly in the best case scenario. Always a good idea to stick with the same brand ink as the printer manufacturer.I would not hesitate about buying this printer again. It is loaded with functionality and is priced very aggressively...it's a great value.5 Stars.

This is a hard review to write, but this product has a number of people in my office, including myself, baffled.  I have tried other Avery Pocket Tab products - which are pockets that stick to file folders, etc, and have a tab of their own that one can write on, and think they are nifty.  But this? Not so much so.The Note Tabs are approximately 7.5" in length and they are serrated, so you can easily adjust their size - we get that. The firm gel creates a comfortable cushion to rest my hands and the leather-like texture is both attractive and appropriate for any home or business setting.The seams appear very well joined to the flexible plastic base and should provide years of gel-ooze protection under regular use.Can't yet speak to the anti-microbial protection since I have yet to lick the surface but so far I haven't caught any illnesses.If you're looking for an attractive, durable, and reliable wrist rest then stop going to the bars looking for Mr. Right, this may be all you need.

I don't have much wall space in my office, so this was the perfect size cork board for me.Not too big, and not too small, just right.Its great for holding important pictures, business cards, and stuff like that.Very Recommended!

This is my second Samsung laser and I noticed the same issues:  it has a hard time being set up wirelessly (via USB was fine).  Having said that, after some time and working with my laptop, I was able to get it set up.  Once I did, it was good to go!The quality of the print is sharp, precise and bright.  I compare it to my Brother machine and am very pleased with it.  It doesn't print photos as well as I'd like, but that's typical of lasers (stick to inkjets for photos).  I used cardstock as well as regular paper with no issues.In addition I was able to print from my iPad.  A big plus!  This can be done with or without the app.  Amazingly, it picked up the printer easier than the laptop did.  A good printer as a decent price.

...other than a copier's stapler. I found the Swingline heavy, solid, and easy to use- both auto and manual. I like the flat staple on top and the barely noticeable curvatures on the bottom. I am so happy to archive my old personal stapler for an office model. The tray in the bottom is very handy for storing additional staples rather than having to hunt for the box when I run out.
It's cheap super glue that works. The tubes are big so I ended up wasting a lot of it; once you open the tube, it's impossible to save it as the cap will glue to the tube.

Yes, this is an expensive product.  But then again this is something that appeals to a specialty user.  For those who do video or photo editing, the use of dual monitors is a necessity but one that takes up lots of desk space - particularly given the width of today's monitors.  The 3M dual adjust Dual Monitor Arm (MA260MB) opens up the desk and allows for easy adjustment of the space according to your need at the moment.  The arms are very strong and this is a product that is obviously built to last.The one drawback is that the instructions are rather difficult to understand.  You can easily end up using the wrong item at the wrong time in the wrong place because the instructions are less than clear.  For those who have ended up confused, another reviewer made a video review (http://www.amazon.com/review/R12Y3LLB5O9QPK/ref=cm_cr_dp_title?ie=UTF8&ASIN;=B009NSGO3M&nodeID;=1064954) that explains it better than anyone could in print.Normally I would dock them for the confusing instructions but the quality of this product is so high I am giving a free pass.  For those who need dual monitor capability, this is a great option to maximize space and flexibility.

This reverse design where the wider part of the push pin is toward the top makes these so much easier to remove from bulletin boards and walls!  Nice and sharp, I haven't found a single thing I don't like about them.

This label maker has a small footprint and works off USB power, so I can keep it in my laptop case and use it only when I need it. You don't need to install software on your drive, so this unit is really convenient all the way around.You don't have the ability to custom design your labels without limit, nor do you have a great variety of label sizes you can print.I use this to label all my burned disks, boxes and folders for my home business and it works really well for that. If your labeling demands are greater than this, you might want to upgrade to a more expensive unit. But for the price and my modest needs, this label maker works great.

This is a nice, solid/sturdy, and good-sized pencil cup. You can use it as a stand-alone cup or open it in two (becomes 2 half circles) and stick it on your fridge or some other metal surface, as the two halves of the cup are magnetic. We're able to put quite a few pencils, pens, and markers in there but at the same time the cup is not overly big.

As a laminator, it works okay, but the lack of instructions really had me wonder how it all works, but it was pretty self-explanatory.  Heated up okay and was a little slow, but did the job.  The price is right, so you can't go wrong with it.

I've been wanting a printer that connects to my network via wifi. It's really a drag hauling a printer around to different computers, finding a place to plug it in, etc. I wasn't sure about this printer however, since it's an all-in-one. In the past I've found that all-in-one means it does a number of different tasks, and does them all poorly.The WorkForce 635 was really easy to set up. The instructions are very clear. Setting up the wifi and installing the software was also very easy, although since the computer I was using was in a different room I had to walk back and forth a number of times as you are supposed to start installing the software before doing the wifi, and the software setup screen walks you through the WiFi setup that happens on the printer. I'm not sure all that walking back and forth was necessary, but I was just following instructions.They say the ink cartridges come with plenty of ink in them, unlike many/most printers. I can't say if that's really true since I haven't used the printer long enough, but I think it's a great concept.I'm happy with the printing that this machine has done. I love that I can print something out from my mac in one room and it's just there waiting for me in the other room when I'm ready to go get it. The tray holds a LOT of paper, too. I've also printed with my iPad using the Epson iPrint app. It worked fine through the wifi connection, the only disappointment is that I had to take a screen capture and then print out the image rather than being able to print out a web page. THAT would have been awesome!I haven't used the scanner yet, but I was pleased to find it's not a sheet feed, you can actually lift the top of the machine up and there's a flat-bed scanner there. The specs weren't listed on Amazon so I had to go digging on the Epson site, and this is what it says:Scanner Type: Color flatbed / Automatic 2-sided ADFPhotoelectric Device: Color CIS line sensorOptical Resolution: 2400 dpiHardware Resolution: 2400 x 2400 dpiMaximum Resolution: 9600 x 9600 dpi interpolatedScanner Bit Depth: 48-bit color / 24-bit outputFeatures:Scan-to-PCScan-to-PDFScan-to-emailScan-to-memory cardI think those are pretty decent specs for a scanner, so I'm thinking of testing it out by hand drawing a font and scanning it in to convert to vectors, but I'm sure it'll be fine. I still have to keep my old scanner, though, since this one doesn't do transparencies or negatives.I was a little disappointed with the software. So far I've only installed it on my Mac, and I'm used to being able to print just a selected section of a web page or a pdf document or whatever I have, and I haven't found a way to do that. If there IS a way to do that, it's not an intuitive way. I've been putting just what I want into Google docs, then downloading and printing the resulting file. Like the image capture method on the iPad, it's a tedious work-around that certainly negates any of Epson's bragging about the speed of this printer. It's still more convenient than a printer that isn't connected to the network, though.
Yes, it does have warnings, but I do no intend to chew on it, etc.This well priced binder works well.  It has a pen slot, I like the elastic that wraps around.

Personally the color of sticky note has never been much of an issue with me, but I know some people might color code the notes based on categories or something similar.  The Avery Steps Sticky Notes provides the ability to choose any color you want from the pad without breaking the set up.  They all stay together.  The premise works well, as the pad does not split apart and everything stays together.  Of course, it does add a little bulk to the pad (length-wise).  Overall, it's a new way of looking at the average sticky note.

I do frequently ship my stuff using PayPal, and this product made my day much easier. Instead of going though manual cutting, and attaching the labels using a tape, this allows quickly snapping your inkjet output on the package.The printed label fits perfectly in the adhesive area. The only inconvenience is that the labels require top margin to be 1", while Firefox defaults to 0.5". If you're lazy, you can ignore the setup, and you'll have a cutting line illustration on the right side of the label.Since the label is aligned on a letter size page, you should also be fine with other services. Just make sure the label portion of what you print comes on the correct side.

Oh these are Heaven on Earth for sticky labels.  They actually stick to items instead of falling off after a few minutes and are the perfect size for storage containers.  I buy my spices by bulk and put them in storage containers and always seem to have the problem of the labels falling off.  Well no more that's for sure.  I like that fact that they have the colors so making them easy to find.  I tend to label my spices and put them aside by baking spices and cooking spices so now it will be easier not to confuse them with baking being green and cooking hot pink.  The labels even have a tab on the end so that they are easy to remove should you need to.  These will be tops on my list for some time to come and I know I'm going to act like a three year old and go around putting sticky labels on everything I can.  LOL!

I have come to rely on Epson printers throughout my personal and professional like. Whether a large format photo printer or an office workhorse, Epson printers are generally reliable and produce high quality printing. Like HP in the 1990, Epson has become the printer company to beat.The Epson WorkForce WF-3540 is a solid printer, copier, scanner, and fax machine. Unlike some of Epson's first all-in-one printers, this is a solid unit with the bugs worked out. And, Epson has also worked out the kinks on their wireless setup as well (or it could be that we no longer have Windows Vista as a speed bump in our technology highway).Epson's software is easy to use all around from printing to scanning. There is much to like here... Setup was easy, great color touchscreen, fast printing, the duplex printing is a great feature, excellent printing output with great colors, and the ability to print from smartphones and tablets.If you are looking for a quality all-in-one printer, this should be on the short list of choices.
Very low price when compared to purchasing it at stores.  Definitely more reliable than the "remanufactured" or "refilled" cartridges which seem to have issues.  Would purchase the new ones first.

The Sharpie Accent Gel has some great features, including;PROS:- Won't dry out- Ability to highlight on paper thin sheets as advertised- Glue-stick like ability to advance the baseBut it also has some cons, which strongly detract from a potential 5-star rating.CONS:- Still smears- Nib is not rectangular shaped, and loses edges too quickly, making it difficult to highlight accurately.I found the last con to be very annoying; since the gel highlighter is crayon like and soft in texture, the tip deforms easily.  This means that the tip does not retain an edge at all, making it difficult to highlight accurately.  In fact, a crayon probably highlights better, due to the harder material texture.It's a neat idea, but could use some improvements to make it an even better product.  If they fixed the nib-shape issue, I'd happily give it 5 stars.
This is a great item to get a lot of your toner with our worry or care. I haven't even burned through this yet but I don't use my printer heavily.

Pros:-> F - A - S - T!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  I scanned a 14-page document (two-sided) and had a PDF in less than 30-seconds!-> Very good fidelity: the document was printed on myHP Photosmart C5180 All-in-One Printer, Scanner, Copier (#Q8220A)and looked fairly good in hand. The PDF generated by the GT-S50 looked a bit light in comparison to the hands-on copy, but nothing I couldn't fix in Elements if I felt the need. It's a very good copy. I plan to mess with this for the near future, just to see what I can get out of it without too much effort/time invested (assuming a home- or small-office wouldn't want to put a full time person on this to get their scans out...-> Small. No really small! I set it on top of myHP Photosmart C5180 All-in-One Printer, Scanner, Copier (#Q8220A)and if it was the same cream color as the all-in-1, it'd look like an attachment piece instead of a completely separate unit!-> Easy to set up and use.-> It's an excellent scanner for librarying photos. Stacked several of varying finishes into the doc feeder, fired 'er up and onto the computer goes the pic. Really cool! (Too bad it doesn't do slides ;-} )Cons (so far):-> Typical Epson software - lots of software! Stuff is squirreled all over my computer! It's been like this since my first Epson flatbed scanner about 12-years ago.-> UPDATE: uninstalled all Epson software. Downloaded and installed the drivers and software from Epson's Snow Leopard site. Now both myEpson WorkForce Pro GT-S50 Document Imaging Scannerand myEpson WorkForce GT-1500 B11B190011 Document Imaging Scanner (White)are available under scanners preferences.OUTDATED BY PREVIOUS: Isn't available in Snow Leopard's printer preferences to be able initiate scans from my Apple MacBook Pro 17 inch MA611LL/A over airport (testing still IP). Just found (on Epson's website) that I (perhaps) shouldn't have installed the included software onto my Mac Pro! There was no BIG RED NOTE in the box about this!!!This would be an excellent scanner for small-to-mid-sized offices.

I love organization; but, this product takes too much effort to get you there.  It definitely needs fine tuning.  The premise is great; the problem is in the execution.  It is too difficult to rearrange the papers.  Once you use the perforated pages, it's a hassle to organize the papers within the three colored tabs located in the back of the notepad.  I say buy a clipboard or folder(s) and shuffle your papers in the order of your desire.  I recommend that you wait until Ampad perfects their concept and skip this model.

I got these envelopes because I still pay bills by snail mail and every once in a while I misplace reply envelopes. These are great. They seal easily and you can't see what's in them after they are sealed. Perfect for paying bills.

This isn't what I thought it was.  I thought it was just a scanner that sucked down receipts and put them on my laptop in read form.  The software actually "reads" the receipt and helps you organize it.But I get ahead of myself.First, I am a spaz when it comes to software, so it better be easy to install.  This device has to be attached to your computer, via USB, to work (no plugging in to an outlet). There is a CD-ROM to install the device, but mine doesn't work.  After about ten minutes on the Neat Company website, I found the download. It took my internet connection about 30 minutes to download.  After a reboot, the wizard install was simple to use.  There are videos to show you how to use the scanner. I just winged it.The first receipt I did was "read" after about one minute. The name of the store, date, sales tax, and total are displayed in the Neat filing cabinet. It seems like a good idea if you have a small business or you itemize your taxes.  If the scanner cannot read your receipt, you can edit the item. All items in the filing cabinet can be printed.I also scanned a few documents and they go into another filing cabinet.  You can also scan your taxes.So why did I minus a star? Privacy. Because I had to use the website to get the install, I had to register it to my computer and I just got the feeling that I lost another bit of my privacy. I mean, I can put my taxes on here.I read some of the other reviews and apparently you can only register the device to five computers. While that isn't a problem for me, I don't think that fair.  For $177, I should be able to register it to as many computers as I want.All-in-all, it seems like a good product.  I've learn a lot about it over the last week and I have a lot more to go.

This is a very good quality stool for a good price. Much lower than in stores or even the other versions of the same item. The wood is some sort of Asian hardwood, typical of what you see in furniture these days. The finish is very smooth and even, the color of the stain is consistent and well applied. Assembly is easy, just make sure to match the legs with the red dots and don't tighten all the screws until all pieces are in place. Packaging from the factory is superb and will hold up in transit. The saddle style seat is quite comfortable and since the build quality is rather good the stool doesn't wobble or feel like it will collapse on you. For being solid hardwood, this item weighs only about 14 pounds. About the only complaint I have is the Allen wrench supplied to tighten the screws. By the time I was done it was twisted and bent, and no, I didn't over tighten the screws like a gorilla. Then again I just threw it away since I have others that I can use if I even need to retighten the screws. Made in Malaysia.

I really like this tape dispenser.  It is, indeed, much easier to hold and manipulate than most are, easy to load, feeds the tape smoothly, and prevents the tape from looping back and becoming stuck to itself.  Because I do a lot of shipping, the one thing I didn't like was that it holds only a small roll of tape.  The tape is also sized to the dispenser, so I wasn't able to refill it with another roll I already had.  I do like the dispenser enough to make a point of buying the tape that fits it in the future; it's just that it's never handy to have to seek out a specific size and brand of a staple office supply.

I found this printer to be just an awesome printer. it installed so easy , and works with the network, fast and good prints too unless doing duplex. I dont mind that tho, as I do a newsletter and really appreciate the duplex feature.I have the Canon 9000 Professional Photo Printer which I paid much more for, yet I would say these photos rival the clarity of that for only a portion of the price. I thought I would use this one for mostly printing in B&W;, yet I find myself doing color photos as well.

This is a very heavy printer and its big.  I had to have some help carrying it to my office.  It has some good features, but for the cost it should have wifi capabilities.  For all the details check out the excellent review by C. MacPhail.

As a homeschooling mom, I use labels a lot and these are awesome. Love that the top is clear and allows to stick and unstick with ease. We use these to label books shelves,for art supply boxes, etc. Great also for yard sales.I have to keep these hidde since my boys love them and want to label everything.

At first I was unsure why this split in 1/2. Then I realized the magnets and the split allow for saving of space if this is used against something metal like say a file cabinet. I simply use it on my desk. It's sturdy, well made, and large so I can even keep a scissors and a screwdriver in there with pens and pencils. Purple is not my thing but other colors are available. This was the one I was able to grab. The magnets also allow for paper clips to attach themselves to the sides so they are easily found when needed.

The markers in this set are absolutely top quality. They write smoothly and erase with ease. If I were only reviewing the markers it would be five stars, but, unfortunately, the junk eraser and useless caddy brings the whole set down. The caddy is needlessly bulky and is designed to only work with one specific board. The eraser has an odd design, with only a small strip of eraser material and the rest is the handle.I don't know how this product even made it through the design and development stage. The caddy is about 2 - 3 inches thick and heavy. All it does is get in the way. It could have been made much thinner and slighter and worked great as a magnetic caddy, but for some reason they went for this weird proprietary design that makes it worthless.In short, buy the markers, skip the caddy and eraser.
These clips are made of good metal and can bind large stacks of paper.  They are handy and easy to use.  You never know when you will need to use one so I stocked up.

I really lke this printer and especially like the fact that is does not need as much space as my all in one printer . This one has a very flat profile so unlike my Epson 2540 (also a great printer) it does not need the space of two shelving units because it is a little more than half the height of the Epson.  To be more specific this one is not quite 5 inches high and the Epson 2540 is well over 8 inches high.  This really makes a difference when you have limited space or you want to put it in another location /another room away from your usual office space. The wireless feature is fantastic and allows me to print from any computer to any room in my house.  I love this.  I also love the convenience of printing from my ipad or iphone  with or without the hp printer app. Excellent.Just to address any paper jams:This printer makes it very easy to clear a paper jam.  Just lift up the middle of the (open it as though you are changing the ink) and look for two grey dots.  You put your fingers in the two grey spots and squeeze together and it will open and allow you to pull out the paper jammed in the center of the printer.

This is a great investment for preserving any sheets of paper you don't want to get lost or messed up.  I will probably be ordering more when I get all these filled, for my personal files were such a mess.  I am categorizing personal bill files, poetry, recipes, and all sorts of miscellaneous information that I want to be able to refer to in the future.

A 1.5" binder is good for storing papers for more than one subject. Buy a set of index dividers, and you're ready to get organized. The binder comes in attractive colors and has  sturdy front and back covers.  Inside the front cover is some decorative faux stitching. The user can customize the binder by inserting a picture or decorative paper behind the clear plastic sleeve. Its rings are a little stiff to open but not unreasonably so and are unlikely to be opened in secret except in an empty house.Five Star guarantees this binder to last a year  from the date of purchase. The guarantee does not cover damage due to abuse, so don't abuse your notebook.

Here we have another great product by Post It! These super sticky file folder labels are completely removable, and cleanly removable from your file folders. I've tested it the past week now, moving labels around and they came off quick and easy and stuck on the next file with no trouble.You can write out the labels by hand or print them as I did on my inkjet printer. It does state they work on laserjet printers as well, and the template worked just fine for me.I have also used these on a plastic surface and they stuck just fine, and removed without residual. Of course they are meant for your file folders, and Post It does have other products to organize bins and such that work Perfect as well. I think these are a great way to really organize your files, and know you can easily remove a label and not destroy a folder over it.

The pages are durable and being avery you can use their template to print the tabs using your computer. Which is an excellent feature. However, the tabs are slightly longer than the insert and stick out just enough to be annoying. Stupid flaw that I never knew would tick me off so much. So I am not going to recommend them.

Great firm seat cushion.  It stays in place well, and is a good complement to the Obus Forme back support device.  You have to play around with it to get things at the perfect spot, being that they're two completely separate pieces.The front section zips off (see in the photo there are three sections).  If you're short, give it a try both ways, first with the entire cushion, then later with the one section removed.  This will help you decide which way is best for you personally.The only complaint I can think of is that the back support and the seat cushion should be offered as a set so that someone doesn't have to purchase the items separately.

For a home laminator it does its job and pretty well. Heats up fairly quickly and when used on the hot setting, laminating some artwork, provided a nice clean clear and even lamination with no bubbling. A decently close lamination to the image so no seam is noticeable between the paper and where the lamination attaches to itself. The auto feed works well without any problems. Fits pretty much everything someone at home or school would need to laminate. It's functional for what it is and I wouldn't expect anything more. There is even a cold setting too but didn't use that as I didn't have any item which required that setting. Overall it's worth its weight as a home lamination tool.
I put it on my file cabinet on the other side of my L-desk and my husband came in and complimented how organized my desk looked. The price is great. The material is really good!

First, the good part. The ink colors are really beautiful. I'm not an artist, but I found the colors to be far superior to those of other pens I've used. They're rich, intense hues that are pleasing to the eye and easy to read (I wrote on a series of different-colored paper). The body of the pen is quite comfortable and has a good balance in the hand. But those two excellent qualities are not enough to outweigh the fact that the ink blobs and smears, and some of the nibs scratch, resulting in that fingernails-across-a-chalkboard goosebump alert. The package has five pens in assorted colors. Of those five, two nibs scratched and three inks blobbed. Therefore - and reluctantly - I would not recommend them. I wish I could: a comfortable pen with beautiful ink is a pleasure, but blotting, smearing and scratching is a nuisance.

I really like this concept.  As it stands it is very functional.  fold the front panel over and it is easy to see what is inside.  Keep it up and have a easy to carry filing system.This has multiple ways to improve organization and bring flow to your office or home filing.  However it is just a basic coated cardboard.  I like the idea but would like a better quality product for my office

I got this mouse pad with the Gel pad because I work in the IT industry so I am on the computer all day.  My wrist is usually very tired by the end of the day.  This does help minimize the stress on your hands and wrist.  It is very comfortable as well.  A must have if you are on the computer the whole day.

A sturdy and artfully designed machine -- heavy -- it stays where you put it -- instructions are complete and well written. A little instruction, proper placement and punching of the front and back covers, the mylar sheet protector, and the pages (15 pages maximum-- good idea to make them double sided!), place the comb, move a lever, place the materials, move the long handle, and voila -- a binding job with a professional look!I would like to see  some improvement, though -1)I used a marker, drawing a line to indicate where to place the papaers and covers for proper punching. A mark needs to be on the loading area above the punch.2) Capacity - Only 15 pages? This would be ok if they were double sided and this was a short presentation. I realize there is another Fellowes binder that will take more than 15 pages, but is it possible to purchase an adaptor so the Pulsar can accommodate a few more pages?Aside from all that, I look forward to taking all my shorter-length printouts that I have accumulated from conferences, and binding them instead of stapling them or binder-clipping them; they will look SO much better and will last longer after getting a Pulsar treatment.

I am not a student, but a professional adult with a bad habit.  I tend to write down important pieces of information, like telephone numbers, on any loose piece of paper I can find.  I know others who do it, so maybe you can relate.  This notebook cames with me everywhere so I know where the information is.  The perforated pages allow me to easily remove it and put it in the file it belongs in,  No more frantic search in the piles of paper on my desk!

I own a HP 8500a all in one printer and recently ran out of black ink.  I had not bought printer ink in a while and was initially a bit surprised to find that the tricolor and black refill package totals around 100$.  I thought to buy the package, but my levels of the color inks are still about half full.  I would guess most people use about twice as much black ink as the colors, so it is nice that these "XL" models contain double the ink as the original cartridges. I will buy the color cartridges when I need them.  I am definitely glad that I did not try to buy the cheaper, refilled cartridges.  When it comes down to it this printer is just not that expensive to use.

This is the first "real" pen I have ever had.  I've only ever used cheapy pens that come in 10packs or that I've stolen from various businesses. :)  This pen has a nice, heavy weight to it that makes it feel substantial and solid in your hand.  I do like the way it writes.  It is smooth and feels nice.  If you were looking for a gift for an office co-worker or employee, it does come in a very nice little box.  I'm not sure I would ever spend this much money on one pen to replace this one, as I am one who loses pens regularly, but I do really like this pen.

I recently received a Fellowes Smart Suites Corner Monitor Riser via the Amazon Vine Review program.  When I chose this item, I was thinking that it would be nice to reclaim a bit of my desk space by having room underneath the monitor to store more clutter.  But overall, my impression is mixed.  It does what it's meant to do, but I didn't feel like it was a step up from my current configuration.In terms of design, the black molded plastic is OK, but the milky plastic overlay that covers the support structure looks and feels somewhat cheap.  It comes with additional rubber feet you can use to adjust the height of the stand, but I didn't use them as it would have made the monitor a whole lot higher than it currently is.  The unit comes with "directions" on how to assemble it, but I certainly had problems making heads or tails of what they were trying to convey.  Granted, I don't think you *need* directions to use this, but the pictures-only instructions did more to confuse than clarify.My biggest issue was the footprint of the stand.  Since I had my monitor set back to the edge of the desk, I really didn't want to bring it forward much.  But given the way the three legs of the stand flare out, you can pretty much figure that the monitor will end up somewhat closer to your face than you previously had it.  Furthermore, it's much wider and deeper than my current monitor base, so some things had to be spread out a bit more than they had been before.  Granted, you get some of that space back under the monitor, but things like speakers and such will end up in different places.  When I stood back to look at how things had to be placed to make it work, I wasn't thrilled with the arrangement, and went back to my previous layout.Obviously, your mileage will vary based on what you have on your desk, whether you need your monitor to be higher than it currently is, etc.  But at least for me, this riser didn't offer enough advantages to cause me to stick with it.Disclosure:Obtained From: Amazon Vine Review ProgramPayment: Free

This is a great set of gel pens for the price. The quality of the pens is great: the colors are vivid and the writing is smooth and fluid. I can't believe how many pens are included in the set: i have never seen so many gel pens together in my life! A lot of the colors are so similar that I can't tell them apart, which is a little weird. For example, I think for the forest green pen they just added some glitter to the exact same color for the forest green glitter pen, etc. Also, the comfort grip could be better...my hand stats to hurt after a while. Finally, the plastic set that comes with the set is pretty cheap and flimsy. Still, for the price, I think this is a great value.

I have been wanting a laminator for years.  I don't have tons to laminate, just one or two items a year, so I couldn't justify spending  a lot of money on something that would get used only infrequently.  However, when this went on sale for only $15 here at Amazon I jumped at it.  It was super easy to set up.  All you do is plug it in and turn it on, then wait for the ready light to turn on.  I bought a pack of scotch business card size thermal laminating pouches (5mm) that worked flawlessly with this laminator.  The seal was perfect and there were no bubbles.  I think if you are doing a full sheet it will take less than a minute to pull it through.  With the business card it was done in about 10 seconds. For my needs this laminator is perfect.

The Epson Workforce Wf-750 has become the "workhorse" of my home office. Sorry for the pun but I just couldn't help myself!Here's my input on this printer:1. Just like everybody else says: It's HUGE... but not for a scanner/printer that prints up to 13x19 prints! I have 13x19 photo printer in my house that's MUCH bigger than this. My suggestion would be to check the measurements and really see where you'll put it before you buy.2. The printer is a tad more `old-school' than many of its current competition. This is not a bad thing however: Instead of being a touch-screen printer (of which I own several), it uses good old-fashioned buttons - and plenty of them. This is great because when I want to fax, I just press the fax button, instead of having to navigate a full menu-tree of options to get to it. The same goes for copying - when I want a black-and-white copy, I don't have to poke around and find it in the menus or chose something on my computer via software, I just push the BW copy button. I LOVE doing things with just one button push, and this printer delivers that ease-of-use that I really appreciate.3. The print quality is great for a business machine. I wouldn't use it to make prints for the wall, but I may be pickier than most because I am a pro-photographer. It definitely prints well enough for marketing my materials though.4. Installation was a snap. I ran into no snags and the printer was up and running within 5 minutes.5. The paper capacity for the printer is 250 sheets. For a strictly-business printer such as this I wish it had a 500 sheet capacity. Being able to dump an entire ream of paper into a printer is a great feature (that this one lacks) because you don't have to store any half-reams of paper aroundAll in all, I think this is a perfect choice for a small-business who needs more than just the standard 8.5x11 scans and prints. If you need the extra-size options, this machine will serve you well.

I am terrible about answering my cell phone when I'm at home. It's always someplace else, either in my purse, out in my car, the other room, on silent, or charging. It also rings when some one calls the land line, as a traditional phone.The answering machine is great - I can't hear the messages. I HATE when someone calls and the answering machine picks up and it plays their message super loud - especially when we have company. This phone is super easy, you can access and listen the voice-mail from any handset.The handsets are small and light weight, but do not feel cheap. The display is large and easy to read. I had to read the directions to set up the bluetooth, but if you've set it up in your car, I would say this is easier.Earlier today I called my family and didn't have to sit two feet away from the wall because my phone was charging - those smart phones certainly don't have a long battery life! This phone is fantastic; highly recommended!

I really wanted to love this mouse pad as I have been looking at something with a wrist rest for quite a while. I'm really happy that we took time with these phones and didn't write the review as soon as we tried them out. They are flat and straight as a board  This can make it annoying to use as one can accidentally hit a button (usually the intercom button) and then blocks out the person you are talking to until you turn it off.* Since the buttons are multi-functional they can be difficult to find depending on the function you are using, so you really NEED the book to learn how to use the phones. These buttons are not self-explanatory.* Depending on how the phone is positioned on your ear, one can have difficulty in hearing the person on the other end.* When you want to hear a message left on the answering machine, it must be done using the handset. It automatically broadcasts through the speaker and you must hit the speaker button for private monitoring.* There is no option to delete a message right after it is played. When it ends and you push delete, it doesn't erase it. You must go back and delete old message or hit delete while it is still playing.* No head-set option on this model* These cannot be mounted to the wall. They are desktop/tabletop only.In spite of the shortcomings listed above, these phones have proven satisfactory for daily use.

I received this printer earlier today.  It is now set up and running.  I was surprised how effortless set up was.  We are using Mac 10.5.4.It comes with an instruction sheet that shows you how to remove the tapes over the toner cartridges and other packing materials.  All you have to do is turn a few knobs and pull a metal piece forward, then pull out 8 yellow plastic tapes.  Then you put the metal piece back and lock the knobs again.  You take off a few pieces of tape, seat the toner cartridges in place (they only need to be moved forward slightly) and then you can plug it in.  I connected the printer to my wireless router with an ethernet cable but you can also use a USB connection.Then you use the installation cd and run the install program.  This runs effortlessly, all you need to do is agree to the licensing agreement.I wasn't totally sure how to set up the printer to print wireless.  I'd never done that before.  I tried a few things involving the printers IP addresses without success.  I didn't realize I was making things far more complicated than they needed to be.  Finally I just tried to print a document.  I selected "Add printer" and the software loaded the drivers.  That was all it took to add the printer.  Now when printing I just select this printer and it prints.  It is no different than using any other printer.You can change options using the menu on the printer.  I changed the waiting time till sleeping from 30 minutes to 5 minutes  The default on this printer is to print an information page every time it is turned on.  This was easily turned off.  Everything else seems fine as it is.I've printed documents in color and black and white, labels and a few photos.  I wouldn't print photographs on this printer but it does a good job with documents that have photos.Someone else mentioned the lights dimming when they used the printer.  I haven't had that problem at all.I am pleased with this printer.  It is sturdy, with a lot of metal and is solidly built.  I look forward to using it in my home business.  My housemate teaches at a high school and they use the same printer in their computer lab.  It has been very reliable even under a much more intense use.  They change toner cartridges 3 - 4 times a year, which isn't bad given many students printing documents all day every day.Edited to add - I've had trouble with Firefox crashing when I print. This is a known issue with Firefox NOT anything regarding this printer but while investigating it I added a RAM disc to this printer.  This printer comes with 128 MB of RAM in it.  You can add to the physical memory in the printer but what I did was add a RAM disc.  This dedicates memory on the hard drive so the document you're printing is written to the hard drive and then prints.  This has greatly improved the Firefox problem (which I think is a Firefox issue) and speeded printing.  So I would recommend that you add a RAM disc.  Open the printer info, select "info" and then driver.  Check the check box for RAM disc.

The Fellowes Bankers Box set the standard long ago for cheap and sturdy document storage. This was very easy to set up though it was one of those rare occasions when the pictures were not very useful at all. If you are even a little fanatical about all things being exactly even, it will cause you to get out a spirit level because otherwise you will fuss at it for awhile.I work from home and use a variety of research books, some of which are quite large well over the 300 page limit of this page holder; however, if the book fits in the bottom lip, the holder will support it.  I have a roll top desk so by using a variety of heights and drawers, I am able to keep three laptops working at the same time, as well as having four to five research books open.  This opened a whole new level for me in a space that was largely wasted.I really liked the way I was able to get this to drop an open book at sight level between the top shelf and the desktop surface of my desk.  It created a level 1  which is incredibly useful.This is also sturdy.  I have several bookholders, one even fashioned by a metal working friend who noticed that I needed something sturdier for some of my books while she was in my office.  The only advantage over those are that I am able to use clips to hold books open as well as magnets to keep notes in place. I am not ashamed to admit that one of the primary reasons that I prefer this calculator - really the HP 12c series in general - to the alternatives is the fact that it looks like an instrument designed for professional use, as opposed to what one might find in an eighth grade science class. Of course, there are plenty of other reasons that this calculator is king.I used theHP 10bII Financial Calculatorfor years, and was quite content. It was only after I signed up to sit for one of my industry's designation exams that I realized the poor old 10bII was not an approved model. My options were theTexas Instruments BA II Plus Financial Calculatorand the HP 12c. Due to my aforementioned desire to avoid looking like I was using the same calculator I owned in grade school, I went with the 12c Platinum.While I was initially frustrated by the calculator's use of Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) - which can be switched to an Algebraic mode on the Platinum model - I have come to appreciate the much more efficient RPN. I realize that time is rarely of the value that it is in a test taking environment. However, if you are considering this calculator for an exam, I can assure you that it will save you time which, when it comes down to it, will probably be much more valuable to you than the $40 price differential between the BA II and the 12c. Even outside of the exam room, if numbers and calculations are your business, it just makes life a little easier.The manual that accompanies the calculator is great. It provides everything that one needs to understand the full operating capacity of the calculator, as well as some helpful walk-through examples. I do wish that it was a physical manual instead of a CD. Not a huge drawback, though. Again, if you are purchasing this calculator for an exam, it will be well worth the effort to spend some time perusing the manual to determine which functions and shortcuts will make your life easier. Believe me when I say that, if used properly, some of the ignored functions of the 12c can be a real boon in certain situations.I do have to say that I have had an opportunity to handle a 12c from what was probably 20 years ago. It is unfortunate that the new calculators do not possess that same feel, but the reality is that even the new 12c series calculators are, in my opinion, of a higher quality than their peers. And I don't have to run to the store or try to remember to buy one next time I am out.

I tested these labels on an HP LaserJet Pro printer and used the labels for renaming file folders - our office prints out full-page postage/label sheets through Pitney Bowes, so I couldn't test these Avery Re-hesive labels to rate their durability as address labels for letters and packages.Out of the entire sheet of labels I printed, two couldn't be removed 'easily' - or at all. The other labels worked exactly as advertised by Avery - easy to remove and reattach. There was no smear problem with the labels. I tried to mess them up, rub the ink and all that, and the labels held up under repeated abuse. Okay, I tried to make this testing and review exciting, but it's not like I could test-drive these labels at 150+ MPH on the Autobahn. Beware that while the total board is indeed 11x17, the actual cork part of it is far smaller than it appears in the product picture. The frame easily takes up a forth of the area which is much more than the stock picture would have you believe. The actual cork part works fine though.

Beeps upon power-on (button at back of machine). Lit Snowflake button tells you that the laminator is set for cold laminating; for hot laminating, choose the 3mil or 4mil button and allow it to warm up. "Wait" button flashes during warmup time, which is approximately 6 minutes. It beeps again to indicate warmup has completed.This laminator allows you to insert the pouch directly, without use of an additional paper pouch, which is required by other laminators (and is usually included with them upon purchase). Laminates quickly and the laminated item was not very hot to the touch, just lukewarm immediately out of the machine.  But always test-touch the laminated document before going full-hands-on, to make sure it is cool enough; it may need a few seconds of cool-off time.This laminator has printed-on guidelines for letter size, photo size, and menu sizes.  But make sure you insert the item closed-pouch side first, as using the open side will result in a jam.After laminating, you must allow the machine to cool down for a couple of hours before storing it, as it will remain warm for a while after use.The only real drawback to this model is that you can only laminate up to 4 mil, which means that you will be unable to use it if you desire a rigid structure.  I like having the ability to use 10 mil as I can make long-lasting outdoor signs with 10 mil laminating sheets.Comes with a starter pack of 10 letter-sized Fellowes laminating pouches in 3 mil, instructions and registration card.  It's nice to have the starter pack, but do not hesitate to purchase a full supply of laminating pouches; compared to the costs of having individual documents laminated by your local copy/print shop, you're saving money in the end.  A laminator is a long-term investment, and should last you years and many, many documents.Remember to place the document in the laminating pouch/sheet and position it perfectly! Once it is laminated, the item is sealed tight.  You can trim the laminate, but do not trim too closely to the paper-laminate seal, as this may break the seal and make your document less impervious and waterproof.I use my laminator to protect things such as park maps (3 mil pouch) so that when I go hiking I do not have to print out the same color map from the internet each time. Any hiker knows the value of having a protected map that will not crumble in your hands, or run inks, when it starts to rain, or if you drop it in a pile of wet leaves on the trail.Laminating pouches come in all sizes, so you can laminate anything from identification cards to legal or menu sized items.  Just be careful to NOT laminate legal items with raised seals, such as birth certificates, or notarized items, as these are meant to be seen and felt clearly to whomever needs to prove that they are authentic.For a party some time ago, I created "table-talkers" - one for every table, with a special message for our guests. Back then, I had to use self-laminating (sticky) sheets, which are an absolute nightmare to use!!  This machine can be used by caterers and restaurants for all sorts of things, from menus to table-talkers, to place settings.I have never used a cold laminating setting, so I did a search and came up with this: "Cold laminating film (sometimes called tape laminating) uses pressure sensitive adhesives to bind the film to the material being laminated. Cold lamination is your best option when laminating heat-sensitive documents or photos." Apparently they come in Matte, Satin, Lustre and Gloss finishes, and are available as transfer adhesive as well, so it will "laminate your document on both sides, and at the same time apply an adhesive backing. A peel-away liner reveals the adhesive. You can then stick the laminated document to various surfaces such as glass or wood."  That's pretty awesome, excellent for scrapbooking and crafting.  I will definitely try this method, along with my tried and true heat laminating.When it comes to laminating, your only limits are your own imagination; dry-erase calendars, schedules, etc. (I find Goo-Gone effective when removing dry erase marker from laminate.)  Have fun!

The teachers at school use this stuff on everything. So I bought it thinking it would work around the house too. It has been great for hanging posters up in the kids room, as well as some art projects in the house. I tried hanging a small canvas print in the kitchen and it keep on falling off the walls. I love the fact that you have a set of different colors, low odor, and a magnetic cap that does not fall off.  If the eraser seems to get flaky or dirty, just wipe it across a dry paper towel and that takes care of the eraser.

These are awesome.  Like another reviewer said, you always seem to need to jot down a note but don't want to mess up a page in your binder!  These fix that issue, time and time again.Convenient and a great fit, easy to erase and I believe they'll stand up to quite a bit of writing and erasing before they even show signs of wear. The Smead Organizer Folders are mid-weight letter-sized folders glued together at the bottom to form an accordion file. Each bundle of folders provides four areas for storage and each can be labeled.  The folders are open on three sides and can be slipped into a filing system or carried on their own.The dull red, blue, and gray colors are inoffensive and suitable for office use, but not especially attractive.Joining the folders at the bottom was a clever idea, but I have strong reservations about how they will hold up when filled to the promised 3/4 inch expansion per section.  The open sides made them easy to use in a file, but less desirable on their own (will the contents spill out?).  I am using a set for an upcoming vacation and have been able to file travel, hotel, activity, and cruise information in easy to reach folders that will stay together.  However, I will have to paperclip the sides or slip the folders into a protective cover before I leave home.The idea is intriguing, but there may issues with the execution.  Each unit would be far sturdier if it were inside one larger folder.Three Stars:  it's okay.
Nice clicker. Works very smooth for power point presentations. I have had no problems using this device. The laser pointer on it is also very bright and goes a long distance.

I go through tons of white out tape, so this deal was great for me.Pros:- quality tape doesn't tear with jagged ends- thinner tip and tape allow for more control and less waste- thumb rest for comfort- compact body makes it easy to store and carry- good opacity (covers text well)- easy to write/highlight overCons- none so far!

(Please see photos) This is a VERY nice chair, and nicely designed and put together. Everywhere you'd touch when you sit in the chair is leather, the rest is a heavy-duty plastic which blends nicely with the leather. All the bolts that hold the chair together fit into recesses and are then covered with plastic caps which match the plastic frame exactly. Really a nice high degree of finish.You might want to look at [...] to upgrade the casters, which look to be 1" x 3/8" -- swap them out for five BIG casters so the chair rolls more easily. Casters can be expensive so I can see why Hon would save money here. For most people and applications the stock plastic casters would be fine. I just like larger casters, personally.The arms DO NOT adjust, which might be an issue. An armless rocking-type chair is a lovely gift for newlyweds. The single control for raising and lowering the pneumatic tube is out of the way, you can't scrape your leg on it if you tried. The instructions were agreeably CLEAR, and the parts come in a shrink-wrapped cardboard sheet. There are eight bolts, all the same, and it comes with a hex tool AND a couple of spare parts which are labeled "Spare Parts" which was really nice. Nothing like putting something together and wondering "Are these spare parts? Did I miss something?" The instructions themselves are clear, which is a nice thing to find.Assembly went well. There is some forceful alignment of the arms and the seat and the back which you might want some help to accomplish. You need to line up the bolt holes with the bolt holes in the other piece. This is why the instructions tell you to NOT tighten things up until the chair is more or less assembled. Then you can torque everything down and put the little caps in place.The chair LOOKS great and it's comfortable to sit in. Add some upgraded casters and it's nearly perfect.

Only 4 stars due to the significant price of this product.  But beyond the price, the tape is very resilient, holding up under water when used on a flat surface.  We've put it on commercial tile, polished concrete, and other similar surfaces for floor marking and it does the job well.  The color is very eye catching and it doesn't raise up under foot traffic.As others have mentioned, this can also be used for packing or sealing -- although that's a very expensive tape to use for this function.  I would likely use another colored packing tape for that type of work.  This products strength is its hold and marking for visbility.

We have several dry erase boards at home for keeping track of chores and all the comings and goings.  This one is quite nice in that it is also magnetic so you can hold papers to it easily.The board is nicely made (even though the backing material is corrugated cardboard, I don't think it's an issue)  There are mounting holes in the plastic corners that allow you to screw the board to the wall.  The mounting holes are then concealed by cover pieces so you get a clean look.My two criticisms are:1) The screws and drywall anchors supplied are huge!  I'm not mounting a flat screen TV - I ended up using drywall screws and some much smaller drywall anchors - the board is quite light light!2) Marker tray is disappointingly small. These folders are really nice- as others have said, the fact that they are heavyweight means they'll last a long time. I'm a teacher and I use manila folders all the time. They get pretty beat up after using them all the time; I have a feeling that these will last much longer.As for the "but..." part of my review- yes, the tabs are larger, but they are mainly larger in terms of going down instead of increasing width. This vertical space gets lost when you put a piece of paper in the folder, as that space gets covered (look at the picture and think about where that piece would fit in the folder. The bottom half of the "larger tab" totally gets cut off).Again, they're nice folders, and the tabs are slightly larger in terms of width, but the increase in vertical writing space doesn't matter since papers will cover it up anyway. I should point out up front that it might be easy to make a mistake if one is in a hurry and doesn't read the product description closely. These are good for envelopes, but I wanted them for labeling storage boxes and bins. They stick well to regular paper but not very well to less smooth or plastic or other materials surfaces.

This is one of the easiest to set-up and use shredders I have tried.  It appears to be well made and I had it up and running in just a couple of minutes (mostly unpacking).  You just set the main unit into the basket, plug it in, and you're ready to go.  The "head" is well design with a great feed for paper, a built-in credit card slot, and a separate CD/DVD slot.  The paper feed has a cover piece which flips open/closed and there is a control button and four status indicators.  All in all, a nice, attractive and useful layout and design.  But how well does it work?Well, this feed is easier to use than most and I had no problems at all.  Feeding open sheets, trifold paper, odd pieces, all worked well.  When I intentionally tried to misfeed something off angle, it handled it fine.  It seems pretty capable and handled everything with ease.  The noise level was about average.This unit is a good side for side of the desk use and has a nice window/port so you can see when it is getting full without having to remove the head unit.  I must say, I'm pretty impressed with this model.  I was not sure what to expect from an "Amazon Basics" unit, but they have delivered a fine unit at a fair price.  I would consider this more of a light-medium duty unit for home or small business use, which is probably how most people considering it will be using it.  Build quality seems good and if you use it properly and oil it occasionally, as suggested, it should hold up well.  If you want to extend the life, then be selective in your shredding and don't shred every piece of junk mail you get.  Just the stuff with sensitive, personal info.  You'll have to empty it less often that way as well.I would not hesitate to recommend this unit to my friends or anyone looking for a good, full-featured basic shredder.Thumbs up!
