Very nice and made me feel very good about having a Kodak printer.  Thanks Kodak!

These mechanical pencils work well, and are comfortable to write with. The only caveat I have is that the erasers don't seem to last very long, a problem for anyone like me who makes their share (and then some) of mistakes.

These work very well with the Fellows laminators. They are easy to handle when out of the box and easy to put your paper in. They laminate well and do not bunch up, crease or fold, so your laminated paper looks professional.

I held off from getting a printer for a long time.  Why?  I live in a smaller condo without a dedicated office space so typical printers seemed inconvenient for my life style.  I didn't want something that would take up a lot of real estate on a desk or shelf or that would require me to be in one stationary place in order to print.  I also didn't want something that would be extremely expensive because I don't print from home often enough to justify something that is fancy.  With these needs in mind, this printer has proven perfect.First, the size.  Though it looks somewhat hulking in the picture, it's actually a compact 15.4 x 14.8 x 8.7 inches.  I keep mine on a small writing desk and it works perfectly while leaving room to work.Second, the wireless feature makes printing so convenient!  I love that I can be working on something on my bed and send it to my printer on my desk.  I found it very easy to set up, no more or less difficult than connecting my Smart TV or other devices to my wifi.  And the connection is reliable.  I use this in conjunction with myWD My Net N600 HD Dual Band Router Wireless N WiFi Router Accelerate HDand haven't had any problem with it not being able to locate the network or dropping off.Third, for an affordable home printer, the printing quality is pretty good.  I've been using it to print copies of work presentations, flyers, and coupons and it has handled them as I would expect.  That said, if you're predominantly printing photos, you'd probably be better off buying a printer specially designed for photo printing.  Having used those in the past I can say that while the quality of photos on this printer when using special photo paper is okay, but specialized printers seem to produce crisper printed images that have a broader range of colors.  The same has been true when comparing the performance of this printer to the printer quality we have at work.  Working in a creative industry we have fairly high end commercial printers and the printing quality of the WorkForce WF-2530 doesn't register quite as crisp or rich in color.  However, to me this is to be expected based on the price point.  As long as your expectations are realistic it performs well for everyday printing.  I also appreciate that scanning and faxing capabilities are built in.  Admittedly I don't use these functions often, but it is convenient to have them in one device if I need them.I think the only (slight) nit I have about this printer is the style of design.  It's not enough for me to deduct a star, but I do think that given how far the design of electronics has advanced I would have preferred something that looked a little less clunky and boxy.  It almost looks a tad dated.  However, given the affordable price it is less of a consideration.Overall, I think this printer provides a great value for the money, especially for those who value working wirelessly and for whom space is at a premium.

It is as claimed. A light odorless lubricant that improves the cutting of the shredder blades. After shredding about ten bags of paper I used this lubricant and immediately noticed a difference in the sound of the shredder motor and there was no "oil" smell. A hint that I learned is to put the shredder in reverse and then apply the lubricant and let it run for about 10 SECONDS. When you puncture the spout be sure to use a small pin. If you cut the tip off you will use too much.

I have had negative experiences with "generic" printable labels in the past...specifically, with the sheet getting stuck in my ink jet printer.  I have had no problems at all with these Avery labels. They go through the printer smoothly. The labels are easy to peel off the sheet as well.  I have also used these same labels in the white version, which work equally well.  However, for purely aesthetic reasons, I prefer the clear labels.If you go online to the Avery website, there is a free software download that allows you to customize the labels to your liking.

First, I must admit that I am unwilling to thoroughly test this safe. I will not load my valuables in it, then burn my house down to see if they survive. Not going to do it, wouldn't be prudent. You can web-search proofs and counter-evidence for Sentry products in real fires.However, here's what I've got:First, as is mentioned elsewhere: NOT FOR FIREARMS/AMMUNITION. There are specialized products for those--don't use this.Second, the fire insulation has a high moisture level, so you'll need to seal moisture-sensitive items in a baggy.Third, the recommendation for best protection is that the safe be stored flat, not standing up. So, look at the dimensions as you consider your location.Durable? Feels like it, though the latch pull feels a bit tight.Secure? Obviously, if you don't bolt it down, someone could walk off with it. There are directions for bolting it.Access? The keys turn easily, and if you don't store the key in it, it's not as easy to pop with a screwdriver as my older Sentry was.Size? Obviously made for the digital age, as most legal paperwork has to be folded to fit, but you can fill it with thumb drives and CD-Roms.Weight? Just enough to make you hate it when you accidentally kick it.

The 3M Tilt-Adjustable Gel Wrist Platform with Antimicrobial Protection is a very comfortable rest which can be adjusted for angle.  I found that I liked it because it is not too soft and does not impede the sliding of your wrists the way a more pillow-like rest might.  It is also finished in a smooth leatherette surface which has enough grain in the surface to allow one's wrist to breathe and to glide easily over the surface.  The overall feel is similar to the arm rests of the Herman Miller Aeron chair I have in my home office/studio.  There is also a quality stiff plastic support for the entire keyboard should you want to use it with the front overhanging the front edge of your work surface that will permit some extra space between the keyboard and the monitor should you need it.  I cannot attest to the antimicrobial protection on the pad, but if I should find any mold, moss or mushrooms growing on the pad I pledge to write a supplement to this review in the interest of those who would find these features undesirable.I must admit that I have had limited experience with keyboard wrist rests having used only several different models over the years.  However, I can tell that there was a good amount of thought placed in the design of this 3M product, particularly in the quality and use of materials that really do contribute to its usefulness and comfort.  I am not sure if I have applied the correct standards in rating this product because I do not "love it" which Amazon says is the parameter for a 5 star rating.  But absent the affectionate aspects of the Amazon rating system, I rated this product with 5 stars because in my limited experience, I have never used one that is better.

Bought this on Newegg on special for $160 with free shipping.  Ordered on Sunday night and had it on Tuesday.  I usually love Amazon but in this case Newegg was much better.  In sum, you really can't find a better combination of features and quality for the price.  The only real complaint I have is that sometimes documents fed through the automatic document feeder aren't 100 percent straight (more like 98 percent straight, but this is only a problem sometimes).PROS:  Auto-duplexing for input and output; 35-page document feeder; great quality when using high print settings; good speed at all settings (unless it's 2-sided); two paper inputs allows you to keep two different papers in the printer at all times, or to just close the top feed if you want; fast and high quality faxing with lots of features (fax isn't just an afterthought in this machine); multiple ink tanks means no disposing of partially full ink cartridges; very good driver software gives you lots of printing options through your computer; many copy, fax and scan options built into the machine and accessible through nice rotating LCD screen; no paper jams yet (UPDATED: Still no jams after over three months of continuous use!).CONS:  It's BIG, as in seriously big and heavy too; like I said above, about one-third of the time documents fed through the document feeder are just the slightest bit off; duplex printing is slow because it stops for ten seconds to let the ink dry on one side before printing the other side; text printed at low quality can be fuzzy, definitely use high print quality for important documents; it's a little on the noisy side and even has a "quiet mode" that I haven't tried yet; after two weeks of use I had to run the "unclog nozzle" routine to make some black streaking go away (I realize that maintenance is needed sometimes but after just two weeks seems a bit soon); would be nice if it came with a USB cable; photo printing gobbles up ink.Overall so far I'm quite satisfied, though if the document feeder issue gets worse before the one year warranty expires I'll send it to Canon for service.  And if need be I can always place documents on the glass by hand.  Without that issue I'd give it 5 stars.(Note, after 13 months of use this printer fell off a table and stopped working.  So be careful and don't drop your printer.)
price is right and it comes in a pack of 6 cartridges as listed. i've only used the black ink so far and it installed without issues. print outs look good and it works!

If you think I'm a nerd because I get excited about these NoteTabs, I'll accept the title willingly.  :)  These little note tabs are simple and effective - numbered simply 1 through 10. Uni-ball pens have a wide, but not too wide point. This makes them perfect for most uses. They make a bold, clear line that doesn't blend together as some pens can. I like them for writing checks and these pens with their various colors are a great choice to make a personal statement. Very highly recommended.

These are removable labels, and in my experience usually that means if you try hard enough you can get some of the label off before destroying your document or whatever you put it on.These do come off a lot easier, but as many have said, they don't stick all that well. There is a fine line between getting them to stick, or having them easily removable. These lean towards coming off easier than sticking longer.The surface you stick them on has a lot to do with how well they stick. On paper, envelopes, kraft/manilla items, they stick and remove fine. On harder materials like plastic or metal, they tend to have the edges start curling and stick less. So keep that in mind when deciding whether to get these or not.

Sometimes it's nice to find a product that's actually as good as advertised.  These 3M Permanent Adhesive Shipping Labels are as good as promised.The 2 x 4-inch white labels are a good size:  large enough for packages yet small enough for envelopes.They work with popular software packages and templates; I used the templates provided by Microsoft Word. Instructions for using the labels are both in the package and at the 3M website.Printing is simple, and they're designed for use with laser printers. There's enough space between the labels on the sheet that they can be easy removed one at a time and so that printing doesn't overlap.They're easy to affix to packages and seem to leave me nothing at all to complain about!

These Smead SuperTab folders are unlike any I've seen before.  They have all the functionality of both typical two-pocket folders as well as tabbed filing folders.  You can use them as a two-pocket folder to carry papers to classes or meetings.  Papers are secured by the pockets as well as a semi-circular 'lockit' flap at the top, which folds over and prevents papers from coming out of the top of the folder.  The folder can then be stored in a filing cabinet or open-top container by flipping the folder on its side.  A large tab on the upper-right hand side makes it function like any manila file folders.  The bright color and extra large tab really make it stand out from other files.  These would be ideal for housing papers that you want to store in a filing cabinet and occasionally transport to meetings.  There are even tabs on the inside to store a disk and a business card.  These folders could be very useful if you have the specific need for them.My only quibble is that the laminated surface makes the folders look somewhat cheap, which is not helped by the extremely bright blue color.  I would prefer a lighter color and less shiny surface.  The folders are also a bit pricy for what they are.
very very good quality for a good price. they are surprisingly smooth and thick papers great for even resumes or formal usage.
Keeps my Royal 10 Sheet shredder in good working order! Used other Brands in the past, just not as good.

Although I know that the intended use for this product is on a desk, my wife found a new use for it...on her bed.  Before, she had an awkward configuration of a laptop cooler and a pillow to balance her laptop on the bed.  This "laptop lift" proved to be a surprising and far more stable replacement.  Also, because the laptop is lifted away from the surface, she no longer felt the need to use something to cool the laptop down and having this lift on top of a pillow proved to be surprisingly stable and easy to use.As for desktop usage, it's a little awkward since the keys are lifted to so high up that it may as well be wall-mounted after all is said and done.  But you may want to consider alternative uses as my wife has and get some good use out of it.

Looking for that all in one monochrome printer for the home office?  Then look no further this one has it all and two excellent selling points besides - low cost toner replacement & high yield.  Mine has been up and running for almost two weeks now and I'm very pleased with the results.  Do hook it up with an ether net cable for your initial setup as the instructions are confusing and the best results are achieved this way.  They also separated the toner cartridge and the imaging unit so it's cheaper to run in the long run when you only have to replace the imaging unit when it's empty.  That's significant savings right there.  It prints fast and the polymerized toner gives stunning professional results from such a compact unit.  Takes all kinds and weights of paper so far (and I use a lot of different sizes and weights in my work).  You can scan, copy, print and fax.  You can print from your phone (I really like that option since a lot of my printing is done on the fly).  Has lots of features I won't go into here. Be sure and read the product page....I think you'll be impressed.  It has full duplex and supports Airprint as well.  Can't speak to toner replacement yet as I haven't gotten to that point but if there's a problem or it's not sufficiently easy I will come back and do so.  Overall I'd recommend this to any home office user (which is what I got it for and what I use it for).

I've packed and sealed enough boxes in my life to qualify me as an amateur expert.  I've used every kind of packing tape out there.  This is terrific for someone who doesn't ship a ton of boxes because it is more expensive than regular packing tape.  (HINT:  buy it in the 4-pack here on Amazon, and save yourself some $$.)  For me, I actually LIKE the dispenser-type tape, even though it takes up more room in my drawer.  This tape actually does tear easily, and seals well.  Recommend it for most people.

I think I'd rather have more sticky notes (like come in the regular products) than have a perforation so you can tear off the sticky portion.  The micro perforation works well for tearing but it is a two hand job.  If you don't hold down the sticky portion while tearing you'll just pull up the sheet with the sticky portion attached (this is good as it makes these easy to use as normal sticky notes).The sticky portion is just about 3/4".  Which leaves a little over 2 1/4" x 3".The stickiness is fine (it works fine on a good clean hard surface), but is not overly sticky.The colors are good with high contrast to normal blue or black ink.

I'm a list-maker.  Especially with lists posted on the fridge.  This notepad is right up my alley.  It's really sturdy, with magnets on the back and even an elastic band at the bottom to bind the pages together.  The pages (and three categories listed) tear away quite easily.  My only qualm is that the three categories don't leave you much space (about 5 1/2 lines) to write a long list of items.  I might not have many "To Do" items or "To Remember" items (the top 2 sections), but my grocery lists (which would go under "To Buy") would never fit in that small area.  But really, it's quite easy to just ignore the subdivisions and just write what you want from the top of the page on down.  And there of course is plenty of blank space on the page of each page as well.  So while it's not a perfect product, it'll do me just fine.

These bags provide a fairly inexpensive way to professionally package a product. I was quite pleased with how these labels turned out once put together; they give a packaged product a clean, friendly look. They're perfect for packaging groups of small items, and can very handy for small businesses. They can also be used as gift bags for parties and other get-togethers.It can be a bit challenging to print on the thick labels, and your choices for label designs are limited unless you plan to make a custom design. You also need to be sure that you fold the labels perfectly, or else the end result will be visibly off.I'm using these to wrap Christmas goodies for my family and friends. The bags really give the packages a nice look instead of simple plastic baggies.Overall, I'm very happy with this product and plan to use it again for Easter and other holidays.

This Wilson Jones D Ring Binder is a premium heavy duty binder (heavier vinyl covered cardboard & supposedly heavier/more durable than the Heavy Duty Binder). As binders go, I expect this one to hold up to general office use. I prefer the D Rings over the round rings because it is easy/faster to close a D Ring binder when it is full.The D Rings are mounted on the back cover, which makes the inserted paper easier to manage/manipulate. The hinge mechanism is a single, bottom tab & easily opens the D Rings.The 4 pockets are 2 front/2 back & they are simple, clear pockets. You will not be able to store a lot of pieces of paper in these pockets, but the 2 stacked pockets make it easier to separate important papers that you want to grab easily.This binder does NOT HAVE the front, back & spine clear plastic so that you can customize the binder with a cover sheet & spine label.Overall, a very nice, sturdy binder.It IS "Army Green", which is kind of a split pea green, slightly darker, but not much.

Not fair to the ink that I hated this printer so much, but this expensive set of cartridges dried up just as fast as the cheaper no-names... go figure.  I finally wised up and bought another brand of printer.

I got this printer to print from Bluetooth devices, and that's all I've used it for.  From unpacking it to using it, it's small, lightweight, and easy to handle.  This was the smartest packed computer equipment I've ever acquired.  There was little in the way of extra packaging, and all parts were easily found and identified.The directions are sparse but intuitive.  Quick setup is exactly that.  Within five minutes I had this printer setup and had it paired with my tablet. One minor detail: I found is that the instructions say that the device comes set to Bluetooth visible.  Mine did not.  But as soon as I made it visible, my table connected and it printed just fine.  I have not installed the accompanying software on my PC, as I don't plan to print from my PC.There isn't much documentation on the rechargeable battery.  It just clips into place; however, mine remains a bit loose after it's clipped on.  If I move the printer much it falls off.  Not a big deal, though if I ever have to rely on the battery for use that would be a problem.This printer has no bells and whistles.  Its selling point is that it's compact and mobile.  I wouldn't expect it to ever replace my fully functional printer, but it's a great little one to have on the run.

This is a pretty good board and it looks great but the problem I have is that the boarders on it are pretty thick. I have another one that's the same total size but the boarders are much smaller so the writing surface is a good bit more. Easily there the boarders could be cut back 1 inch all around if not 1.5 inch. You don't need that large of a boarder.The one thing that I really did like about this one is that it came with some nice metal hardware for wall mounting. wide metal "hooks" that will slide in behind the edge of the board to hang on the wall but allow you to easily take it off the wall when needed. I have a number of white boards all over the house to put reminders on and also to work out all the crazy formulas that I deal with on a regular basis. This one went in my main hallway as the boarder is nice. I keep my reminders there for when I come and go from the house.It is a magnetic surface as well so you can use the magnets to hold paper notes in place.For markers I have switched to only using Quartet Enduraglide markers, they last a lot longer and the tips don't dry out while you are thinking about something to write down. Working on calculus, physics, or whatever it is that I'm using to solve various issues that I'm working on I tend to have to stop and think a lot and normal markers dry out far too quick. The enduraglides just last so much longer and they are pretty much the same price....This board seems to be of good quality though and doesn't seem to be holding up to the abuse I have given it. I just would like thinner boarders to increase the writing area more like the other boards that I have.

I use dry-erase markers all the time with my tutoring students, and I'm very happy with the way this set works. The colors are bright not watery, the line is a little finer than my other large size markers so it's easier to write neatly, the odor is low. and the eraser provided cleans up my whiteboard surfaces when we are done. Usually the eraser is enough but when the board gets a little too messy the spray cleaner does its job well too. Good set.
I sell these here at my stained glass shop in Indy. These cork back rules are a very good value.

These Smead Translucent Slash Jackets measure 9-1/4" X 11-1/4". They are made of sturdy heavy gauge poly material.  There are five in a pack.  They come in 3-hole punched in five different colors - green, red-orange, yellow, blue, and clear.  They fit in standard letter size binders perfectly.  Each jacket has two pockets, one on each side.  The pockets are close on the left side and the bottom.  The opening at the top is at a 45 degree "slash" angle, which makes moving papers in and out easy.  They are translucent so that I can see what I get in the pockets.  They are ideal for organizing office projects.  I put reports, documents, certificates, notes, Google maps, and whatnots in them, one color for each project.  I may order more so that I can put one in each of the many binders I own for loose sheets.  They surely are handy.

Wide-ruled, 3 dividers, 40 pages per section.  This is great for an elementary student because of the wide rules and few pages for each section, but likely isn't enough for a HS or college student, unless you are like me, who needed all 120 pgs and then some for some classes.  I'd just rip out the extra dividers for more room in my backpack.

Honestly, there isn't a lot I can say about file folders, but here are the pertanant aspects:  This is a box of 20 mint-green, hanging, letter-size, file folders that can expand up to 2 inches.  The label-tab is built in, which is nice, because I hate those flimsy plastic tabs with the little pieces of paper that fall out.  Just use a magic marker to label it and move on.  If you should need to reuse the folder, you could just use a mailing label to cover up the tab and mark with the new label.These have an extra 2-inch wide piece of cardboard that you can place in the bottom of the folder and lock in place with some tabs.  This is a nice feature--as other expandable folders I have used tend to get rounded off at the bottom, making it hard to see some tabs on the manila folders inside.These are made in the USA and use at least 10% post consumer waste as part of the content of the durable card stock these are made from.  Also these are marked with the sustainable forestry initiative label, meaning efforts are made to make the paper production less destructive to the environment.  All in all, it seems Smead has covered all the bases in making a high quality and responsible hanging folder.

Fellowes Pulsar E 300 electrically punches up to 15 sheets of paper at a time and will bind documents up to 300 pages. I like the vertical document loading feature; it accurately aligns the punches of every document. Position the edge guide, then put up to 15 pages at a time into the slot, make sure they're all the way inserted & push the button. Very easy, no muscle power required, & you end up with  perfectly punched & aligned pages. (I suggest that you punch a test page before you begin your project).  If your document contains more than 15 pages (up to a maximum of 300), there's no need to set the punched pages aside, simply place them over the comb (that you previously got ready), punch more pages, place them on the comb, etc. When you're finished, close the comb using the comb lever.  Another feature that comes in handy for me is the storage tray which doubles as a comb/document measuring device. It not only measures comb size, but has a slot for your pages. You squeeze them together, measure them in the appropriate slot & you'll know which size comb needs to be used.  A clear window  allows you to see if the pull-out chip tray needs emptied.There are a multitude of uses for this comb binder, ranging from school reports, presentations, final exams, to business uses, menus, brochures, and even home use...make that recipe book to pass out to your kids, scrapbooking, calendars & more.The Fellowes Pulsar E 300  is backed by a limited, two-year warranty. It comes with instructions, a binding starter pack which contains enough supplies for 10 projects: 5 each 1/4"  & 5/16" combs,  oversize (8 3/4" x 11 1/4") covers - 10 - clear, 5 each white & black.
The Avery 5160 labels have been around forever, but these have been improved.  Easier to pull off the backing sheet - particularly the first label of the sheet.

Avery products are always top notch, but nothing can compare to their premium notebooks that open with just one tab and close with the same, but this comes very close.  The tabs take only a little bit of effort to work, but what I really like is that for a binder this price, the rings stay firmly clamped shut.  I got quite a few of these to use at work where I teach high school girls with learning disabilities and emotional issues; I keep copies of their mainstream class notes in my own notebook so that if they lose or forget them, they have a copy, and I can go over their notes with them and explain what they don't understand.  So I collect a lot of notes and needed more than the one inch binders that I had, so I bought these and I'm very happy with them.  My students are overwhelmed that I purchased them out-of-pocket for their use and really do appreciate it.  The binders are sturdy, clasp well, and were in excellent condition when I received them.  If I know Avery products, I shall have these for a very long time.  I definitely recommend them for anyone who does not wish to spend the money on the premium Avery binders.

I recently bought a nicer pen and replaced the ink it came with with a Fisher Space Pen refill.  To my knowledge, this was the first time that I had wrote with a space pen and I was instantly hooked.  I would say that it writes as smoothly as gel with no dry time.  This pen was only a few more dollars than the refill cost me, so I decided to buy two of these so I always have Fisher Ink pens around me.  These are nothing fancy, but they are nice hard metal click pens.  This is the only pen you ever need really.

The Westcott iPoint Evolution Electric Pencil Sharpener is eye candy and it actually sharpens pencils. There is an auto-shutoff when your pencil is sharp, but if you want it even sharper you can push the pencil in a few more times. I really like the way it empties out the shavings by allowing you to remove the shaving holder and then undo the top (although I have to confess I was stumped on how to open it until I read the manual). It's very mess-free. I had no trouble, however, operating the device and it does a very good job sharpening my pencils.I have an old battery-operated sharpener which also does a good job but is actually much smaller than this, so I'm not impressed with the size and feel it could have been smaller and still done a good job. And, much like other reviewers here, I also wish it could work with larger pencils (which my older sharpener does, even at a smaller size).It has a very nice design, however, and if you are looking for just the right office gift that will fit in with modern decor, this sleek device will do the trick.

I was torn between giving this 4 & 5 stars.  It seems kind of cheap, and I was almost disappointed when taking it out of the Amazon box.  I took it to work, where I'm on the computer all day.  I have it on the left side so I can keep my right hand on the number keypad.  I was surprised to feel how comfortable it is!  I didn't have a problem sliding my mouse around, and my wrist felt comfortable.  Some wrist rests have a covering that will eventually fray over time, and this one doesn't.  It should last a few years until I get bored and want a new one.  It looks very professional, though my office is unprofessionally cluttered, so it's hard (for me) to show off.  It doesn't seem to rock as much as the description says.  I don't know if this will change over time, but I haven't needed it to bounce around much anyway, so that's a good thing.I have another wrist rest/mousepad that I like, but the mousepad has started curling up at the edges.  This one is made curved very slightly down, so I don't think it will curl up any time soon.Remember that "torn between 4&5 stars" thing from above?  I've already changed my star rating while writing this review.  I talked myself up a star.  Though this kind of looks cheap and utilitarian, it's comfortable, doesn't slip on the desk, has a good surface for the mouse to slide around, and isn't too expensive.  And instead of cheap, I've decided it's kind of funky looking.  So there.

I tend to write smaller-sized notes on my whiteboard, and these Expo dry erase markers are perfect for that. The ultra-fine point on the pens makes it feel like I'm writing with a normal pen, so I'm not trying to keep the chisel point of normal markers rotated in some awkward position for a fine line.The low-odor claim is definitely true. I don't smell much of anything from these markers when I uncap them. So much for my jokes about liking whiteboards so I can huff the markers. :)  Color-wise, it's nice to have a variety, but some of the colors look very similar if the lighting in the room is not overly bright. Black/brown, red/pink, and blue/purple tend to look like each other when I view them from any distance.Overall, this is a good set of markers for a reasonable price, and I'm enjoying having them around.Disclosure:Obtained From: Amazon Vine Review ProgramPayment: Free
helpful if you are moving, or if you are like me, have a mobile office in the trunk of your car and need a place to store materials.  Would definitely buy again.

The shaft was too long, but it's well made, heavy and I was so sad to have to send it back. Bought a smaller desk when we moved our office to a bedroom and had to replace it with something else. I was, of course, installing it when I discovered it wouldn't work and it is truly a sturdy piece of equipment.

It was a little less than expected--it sounded like it would be an organizational system, but it's more of a mini sampler. The contents is fine and as described; it comes with a leaflet on some basics of organization, which is a nice extra. Best for un-complicated needs and very basic, this kit works for people just starting out in getting their finances together, and maybe not as much for married couples with the usual plethora of bills, cards, and accounts.

I have a lot of books on my shelf at work and am constantly marking pages I reference frequently. The plastic post-it flags work ok but are sometimes hard to write on due to color (too dark) and size (too small). I also need to use an ultra fine sharpie to get the ink to stick. It's also challenging to hold the flag still while I'm writing on it. This roll solves all of those problems. The material is paper so I can write with a fine ballpoint without problem. The color is light so the contrast with the ink is very good. since it's on a roll, I can make my tag bigger than needed so I can hold the tag in place while I'm writing. It's not all good news though. The dispenser does not have a serrated edge so you have to be careful when tearing off a section or you won't get a straight edge. A strange oversight IMHO. Also, since it's a roll the paper is completely sticky on once side as opposed to the plastic flags which have half of the flag with stick-um and half without. This means when I use as a bookmark I have to use twice as much as I need so I can fold the tape over on itself to avoid the tag sticking to something else when I put it on the bookshelf. These are fairly minor nits and overall I'm pretty happy with this product.

Teachers, you're better off buying real pencils at 3x the cost.  These are horrible.  Many have un-centered lead, so they didn't work at all.  It's almost impossible to re-sharpen them, so they're one time use.  I considered them a waste of money.

The Bostitch B875 is a super stapler.  If you find yourself having to staple large documents, this is the stapler for you.  The reduced effort mechanism makes it simple to push staples through multiple sheets.  Placing the sheets onto the stapler "bed" is easy.  The pages don't have to be squeezed underneath like with other staplers.Overall, the stapler feels strong and durable and I expect it will last for years to come.  Unlike with other staplers, I find that I don't have to struggle when stapling large documents.

I got this hoping that it would replace the old strip on my windshield for my "Fastpass."  I figured, "heavy-duty" would do just that.  What it doesn't mention in the description on Amazon but does on the packaging is that the adhesive on the back is not intended for use in direct sunlight.  That being the case, I tried it anyway and it failed within 2 weeks.  One thing is for certain though, the hook and loop portion of this is strong.

We have a lot of papers to be shredded around the house.  My husband has been talking for months about getting the ultimate shredder.  Since that doesn't seem to be going anywhere fast, and I had the opportunity to review this product for the Amazon Vine program, I jumped at the chance.My main issue is junk mail and catalogs.  The day we received this shredder was also a big mail day.  Recognizing that this product is intended to shred up to 6 sheets, I gave it a good test right off the bat with a fairly thick envelope, and, well, it might have shredded the thing eventually but the machine was making some fairly alarming noises:  my first chance to use the manual reverse switch.  It worked like a champ.  After that I had a good idea what it could handle, and the rest went through with ease.The bin is large enough to handle a few days' mail.  The shredder has a nice heft and feels solid but it's perfectly manageable and easy to cart around.  I plan to take it to my mom's place for her shredding project.  And here's something not everyone knows:  shredding is fun and satisfying!The box included an insert card stating that all products were tested before they left the plant so there might be some loose paper waste around the blades.  That made me feel really good, that personal attention was given to my particular machine.Really, the price is great for what you get.  This is an easily portable machine for home use.  I started at 4 stars when I began to write this review, but there is no reason not to give it that fifth star.  Definitely recommended.

Slim and flexible, this cable does everything it's advertised to.  We needed a phone charger in our truck for our Galaxy 4 and this cable was the perfect length to thread from the adapter up and behind the dash to the phone holder.

This little 11" x 14" dry-erase board is framed with light plastic and has smooth, rounded edges. It weighs 10 1/2 ounces without the 2 circular magnets and 11 ounces with them, so it is easy to hold in hands or on lap. The write-on surface is 10 1/4" x 12 1/2" so it's larger than most paper tablets. The small pen (with attached eraser and magnet) has a fine tip, so it's easy to keep my writing small and get a lot on the board. I've been looking for a dry-erase board to keep next to my laptop for doing quick, simple calculations and making short-term lists. This is it! Love it!!!

I used to carry fountain pens with  me, but I had to many accidental ink messes.These pens write smoothly, are reliable, and super-convenient--and don't leak.  I still enjoy my fountain pens at home for writing and sketching, but I find these a touch quicker to grab and jot down a sudden insight or to-do item before I forget it.  I like too that I can save money by buying the refills.Highly recommended.

I haven't had a working scanner since the very late 90s. I am somewhat amazed by how inexpensive these all in one devices are. It's nice to have a home scanner again. And this thing does it all. I've never had a wireless printer, so it's really nice to not have to run up to the office every time I want to print. It's even nicer to not have to worry about physically hooking my laptop up to the printer. The setup was self explanatory, very easy. It's perfect for someone like me who doesn't want to read the instruction manual.The printer is fast for a small home printer, and I've been happy with the quality of everything I've printed. It does a good job with pictures in documents, but it is not a photo quality printer. The scanner is a little slow, but I'm not sure how much more you should expect at this price point. I love the fact that I can do double sided printing! I'm all about the double side! Saves paper and the environment!!Overall, I'm happy with this printer and would recommend it as a great addition to any home office.

I have used several Epson printers over the past few years, including the WorkForce 845, WF-3520, and the XP-850.  I have been pleased with the printing quality of all the printers by Epson I have tried, including the XP-410.  This printer gets the job done both as a photo printer and document printer.  I was pleased that it only required four ink cartridges, as opposed to five or six I have encountered with some of the other Epson models.  Wi-Fi setup is, as usual, very easy and it works nicely with the Epson printing app on mobile devices that I've been using regularly for well over a year.  This is an excellent desktop printer for home use, as it takes up very little desk space, even less than the XP-850 which I already thought had a great footprint.  It also is very quick and quiet when printing which I found very nice, especially in a home-use setting.As with most Epson devices now, it has a color display menu with easy-to-change settings and options.  However, although the design is quite like many of the all-in-one models I have used, this model is not the best option for an office environment.  Other than the fax option, this printer includes the other standard functions of scan, copy, and print, but the capacity clearly fits consumer rather than commercial standards.  In other words, this is a small "everyday" printer/scanner combination.  Although more of a personal preference, my main issue with this printer is that it is a top loader for paper.  It can be argued that this helps make sure the printer size is small, but it is clear that Epson can make small front loading printers (as seen with the XP-850).  Another feature that is noticeably missing is a feeding tray for making copies or scanning.  While I know many people primarily use this when faxing documents, I also find this tray to help when scanning or copying a multiple-page document.  This device features a traditional scanner where you simply lift the lid a scan a page at a time.Overall, this is certainly a good printer for home use, but I would not recommend it for office or small business use.

The Epson software provided with this printer installs spyware on your computer in the form of the Ask.com toolbar without your knowledge.A few days ago I found that the Ask toolbar had been installed on one of my systems at a time when no one was at work or using the computers.  It took only a few minutes to find that the offending software was installed by the Epson printer software.  In fact it had been installed on all six computers in my office that had the Epson 837 printer installed.A look at the Add/Remove programs screen also revealed the following software: Epson Customer Participation, Epson Download Navigator, and Epson Event Manager.  All these programs communicate over the internet and all were apparently installed with the Epson software packageI am very frustrated with the endless task of trying to keep all the unwanted junk ware, ad ware, and spyware off my machines.I accuse Epson of sleazy business practices.  How about it Epson?  Have you no shame?  Have you no ethics?UPDATE 11/18/2013  After a recent install carefully choosing not to allow any internet access to the Epson Software, I got a popup from Windows Security Alert saying Windows Firewall  had blocked net access to EEventManager by SEIKO EPSON CORPORATION.  I chose to Keep Blocking the software.  Also got a popup from Epson requesting that I install the LTCM Desktop Client.  This is so called  "non harmful" spyware by Leader Technologies.  And yet another popup from Epson requesting that I become a part of "a new research study to understand printer and ink use.  If you choose to help, your printer usage data will be sent anonymously to Epson."I now think I understand at least a part of why they are wanting to update firmware and track my ink use.  I found one person on the internet complaining that after Epson had updated their firmware the third party ink they were using no longer worked.I would very much like to know what others are observing about Epson's behavior.===================================2/11/2014 UpdateI would not recommend this printer if you plan to use non Epson Ink.  Tried several brands with the two 837s that I own and none have performed for any length of time.  The Epson ink is very expensive.

At my home my papers were in shambles, so I ordered these.  They need a 2 hole puncher, which seems to be nary impossible to buy for a decent price.  Finally I went to Office Max and they were over $17 so I picked up one from Amazon (at a very good price) before I could even try these.Wow!  They are sturdy cardboard, and have several pages of dividers.  My receipts and bills have never been so happy.  With the prongs the papers don't slide out and I can just turn pages to get to what I want, like a book.  Who said a folder is a folder?  Nobody, I guess, but I never thought it would make so much difference what I used.When you use a folder with pockets, papers can still spill out when you drop them, same with manilas.  These just stay put, and they expand to 2" so for my simple home needs they take care of lots of clutter easily.  I'm so glad I tried these.

Feel like I paid way too much for a stapler but was tired of my old Swingline jamming. So read some reviews and sprung for this shiny chrome heavy duty stapler. So farI have been impressed, lets see how it holds up long term. 4 stars

I thought at first, "It's Scotch Tape, for crying out loud... how am I going to write a review of it?"It's the exact same tape, just in a new dispenser that doesn't work any differently than the old one...But then as I was laying it out on the kitchen table my 14 year old daughter suddenly makes a beeline to me and says, "Oh, that's SO CUTE! Can I have it to take it to school?"Sooo.... sometimes it really is the little things that matter.  And little things, like a new designer dispenser, can make a teen's day just a little bit brighter.

When the inventors of the first wave of superglue perfected the formula for a substance that will instantly and permanently bond almost any smooth surface in the world, I have to wonder how long it took before it occurred to someone- "OK- now, how do we package this stuff?"In a way, until recently, this has always been about the sole factor affecting my purchase of cyanoacrylate glues (CA). Will I finish the whole bottle before it glues itself shut forever? Or is so easy to open that it hardens in a week or two?The attempts at a solution are many, and most have no place here at the moment. One worth of note are the small, nearly single-use "toothpaste tubes" that never seem to seem to be fully useable. Then they came in in 3 packs of smaller tubes, and can almost always be completely useable. But, as of now, the glue of choice has been the Loctite brand; their long necked bottle seems to be the first plastic one I have found that is reliably there when I need it. Possibly because they were one of the earliest vendors and at it the longest.But now, I am intrigued by the 3M approach, they almost always seem to have the upper leg when it comes to intelligent, clever designs. Not to say with certainty how much they to do with the dispenser, but I am sure they oversaw its development.What we have here is, to me at least, unique. To begin with, even though it is a plastic bottle, it is sealed with what appears to be a foil membrane. I next noticed the sides of the bottle were floating- that is, free on three sides yet remaining attached at the bottom forming a hinge- no doubt of some indestructible 3M plastic tested through a million cycles. In any case, prying them back (probably voiding the warranty) I saw that it was indeed a large foil tube- the "bottle" is just a shell for it, and the hinged sides do the squeezing. Ingenious. So, unlike the straightforward tubes that work pretty well but are hard to seal and usually go missing, 3M has combined the best ideas into a package that I think will take honors for Best Superglue Container.I realize this is more than likely supposed to be a review of the product, not the dispenser. But concerning CA, what is there to say? Open time? Effectiveness? Strength? I suppose, and I am sure there are subtle differences between brands, but I also bet you don't care. Unless you are into the higher-end CA glues of varying viscosity and applications, it's all pretty much the same.So I will simply say that after a few basic tests the glue works great; but the container is simply brilliant, and unique and no doubt effective enough to turn me into a return customer.

Yet another fantastic, inexpensive AmazonBasics product. The shredder does as much as other shredders that cost twice as much. I've probably gone through twenty or more buckets of shredded paper so far, and it's still going strong,

Okay, so I love pens and office supplies in general.  I’m always trying new ones, and I especially like colored ink, no dreary schoolhouse blue or black for me except when necessary.  I have a multitude of colors and types of pens, sticky notes, et al.  So I’m always excited to try new colored pens.These are very nice pens with a nice flow.  They are very similar to the Pilot G-2, which is my favorite pen, and I would stop using the G-2 in favor of this pen if I liked the Acroball pink and purple colors a bit more.  FYI, the G-2 has a few drawbacks:  it will fade in sunlight and it will run if wet.  Those are not usually issues for everyday use.  The Acroball ink does not run if wet; I cannot yet speak to the fading issue.I also have not tested the Acroball for writing checks, as I so seldom write checks these days.  You may know that most ink can be washed off of checks using common household cleaners.  The G-2 runs, but leaves behind enough ink that cannot be washed off by common methods.  If that is a concern for the Acroball that would affect your buying it, let me know in the comments, and I will test.The appearance of the pen is nice.  The upper part has a color band reflecting the color of the ink; it also has a silver-gray shape on it, which is a bit gaudy, but not enough to get excited about.  The rubber grip has a lot of texture, sort of like a herringbone pattern.Here are some other comparisons I made for the ink colors on white paper, comparing various pens I had available at the moment.  Results will be different on different paper:Pink:  The pink Acroball is not quite as strong as the pink G-2.  It is more vivid than the pink Bic Bu3.  I prefer the pink G-2; or go with the magenta PaperMate InkJoy if you want a gorgeous cross between pink and purple (although since PaperMate does not sell the colors separately, you'd have to buy an assortment).Purple:  (Yawn.)  Acroball purple is very blue, more of a dark blue-purple than the InkJoy or the Bic Atlantis.  The G2 purple has more a more pink/red tone to the purple that really pops, and it is my favorite pen of any color.  However, if you are looking for a dark bluish, more conventional purple, the Acroball is a good choice.Blue:  Acroball blue is a pretty peacock blue, very similar to the InkJoy, Bic Bu3 or Bic Atlantis.  Not a “business” blue.Green:  Acroball is a nice green, fairly dark and easy on the eyes.  It is very similar to the green InkJoy.  By comparison, the Bic Atlantis and Bic Bu3 are lighter and brighter.Orange:  A true orange.  The orange InkJoy is much more vivid; it has a bit more red in it.  The Acroball is probably a truer orange, if that is what you want.All in all, I would say the blue and green are the best, then orange and pink, with the rather boring purple lagging a bit.

These labels are a great value when you can make use of both labels on the sheet.  To prevent the second label on the sheet from being wasted as a receipt, here's how you can change the settings on the various shipper sites:UPS: In the Complete Shipment page of UPS Internet Shipping, make sure that the receipt checkbox is unchecked.US Postal Service: Download the USPS Shipping Assistant for the option to print without the receipt (the web based checkout only has the option to either print with a receipt or to print 2-up labels).Paypal: Go to Profile / More Options / Selling Preferences / Shipping Preferences / Printer / Edit Printer Settings / Uncheck "Print Receipt" checkbox / Save.Fedex: Go to Page Setup and clear any of the info in the Header and Footer and play with the margin settings and test with a blank sheet of paper until only the extra information disappears, then print on the real label.

Didn't have any "issues" with setting up this scanner as other reviewers have mentioned. If you're familiar with Epson software (I own 2 other printers by this brand) the set up is typical of this company. I am using Windows 7 64 bit, and have not experienced any glitches in set up or output of scans. The detail of the scans (I am using for highly detailed artwork) is excellent and comparable with my flatbed scanner. "Firmware updating" only seems to be required for those not in the USA, the software will auto prompt for any updating needed for drivers (if you're a US resident), so you can ignore this brochure that's included.
it seems hard to find a normal mousepad these days for those surfaces like glass that still doesn't work well for certain mice. super thin, good 3M quality and a good alternative.

I have used many laminators over the years and was leery of this one because it is petite. I was pleasantly surprised with how easy, quickly and nicely this laminator laminates!  I laminated a sign for an outside door as well as some flyers and handouts and it was very easy, quick and professional looking. I like the height this stand brings my monitor up to, but the stand itself is a very flimsy, and very bright white, plastic. The slightest movement of the desk makes the monitor jiggle, which is hardly easy on the eyes. And, unless you have an all Apple products office, the white color sticks out like a sore thumb.

It seems as if I've used these very good blue ink pens by Bic for ages; I remember writing many a paper for college using pens like these before computers came along. Bic calls these pens "medium point" but the writing is quite clear and easy to read on the page. The blue ink lasts for months--unless you write a lot with these every day in which case they will last a shorter amount of time.The pens are compact and easy to carry with you. The pens are made of plastic with an ink tube inside them; this makes them easy to carry because they are so lightweight. As nerdy as it sounds, gentlemen can easily carry one or two in their shirt pockets. I would keep the cap on, of course.Actually, I would keep the cap on at all times when not using this pen. The ink still inside the pen can dry out rather quickly without the cap being on them. Moreover, you don't want ink to leak out of the pen and make nasty ink stains.Overall, if you want an inexpensive pen that still gives you high quality writing ink, you can't go wrong with these pens by Bic. I have used them for decades with great satisfaction.I highly recommend these pens for anyone wanting an inexpensive but good quality blue ink pen.

I keep a variety of pens on hand in the kitchen and den: for jotting notes on the calendar, taking phone messages, writing notes to myself or family members.  Today I found myself reaching for these "Ink Joy" pens over and over again.  They write smoothly.  The rubber grip is comfortable (my hands sometimes ache). They're nicely balanced for my average-sized hands.  The white, gray, and silver color scheme is very attractive.  They don't require much pressure to leave a legible mark and the ink is a nice consistency.  I can even write on a vertical surface (wall calendar) without the pen getting dry.Overall these pens are very pleasant to write with. Given the choice, I'll pick these first.  My only complaint is that the ink color indicator is at the top of the pen, where the plunger-"clicker" is and it's difficult to distinguish between blue and black in dim light.(I've edited this review and reduced the number of stars to 3 since the pens are beginning to produce ink blobs when I write.  I really liked these pens--but the blobs of ink are a problem.  Best to scribble a little to get rid of any blobs before you do any writing that you want to look neat.)

I returned this scanner after one use, and I believe that the one I received had some defects.Installation was fairly easy. The very brief instructions make it clear that you have to install the software FIRST before connecting the scanner. The software disc has a more detailed PDF guide.Pros:- It's slim, good for travel, and the carrying pouch is included- The power source is your computer through a USB cord (included)- The scanner is very quiet and barely makes any noise when workingCons:- The power button has no light or indicator of any sort to let you know when the scanner is on. My scanner was slow to power up and sometimes the button did not seem to respond, but I believe that's due to a defect.- You can only feed ONE page at a time. If you're trying to scan multiple receipts or pages into one PDF document, you feed one through, wait for a screen to pop up, click "continue" and feed the 2nd page, and so on. All in all, pretty time consuming.- The scanner does a terrible job at detecting an inserted document, especially if it's a receipt. With almost every receipt, I had two error screens pop up, one telling me the scanner could not detect a page, and the other one asking me if I wanted to proceed. When I clicked "yes", it would actually scan the receipt, but it was very annoying to have to click through the pop up screens all the time.- Other times, the scanner seems to think it's scanning something when there's no document being fed through...and it does not stop until it scans for a pre-set amount of time.- With folded and bent receipts, it took me 2-3 tries to get a semi-decent scan, and even then, the image in the PDF file was crooked and not 100% clear. The scanner seems to have an especially difficult time with folds and starts pulling through one side of the page quicker than the other.- Most documents do not feed through straight since there is nothing guiding them- Anything you scan has to be clearly printed with dark ink. This scanner does not really detect lighter ink, faded lettering, etc.
Boy I really like the way that Kodak makes everything easy to install and use. I've installed a number of printers and inkover the years and this is one of the easiest.

Using a Fellows. This is quieter, shreds more paper per run, and cuts the pieces at least 80% shorter. Only drawback is it's slower (considerably) which could be an impact if you're using it to do loads of shredding. For my use, shredding all personal financial stuff and junk mail that has my name and address on/in it... this is great! Thanks AmazonBasics.

Sharpens your pencils to a precise point. Does exactly what it needs to do. The design is cool in that you have the ability to see into it as it works and how full the pencil shaving container is. Good for what it is.

For the price this is ok. I bought the 47x35 with the lip and wish I'd bought the bigger one. With the bigger one, the constant moving around or drifting of the mat might have been less irritating. My first printer for my Mac was my old HP which served me for years.  It sort-of worked.  HP told me they no longer support the Mac drivers.  I told them I was switching to Epson.The Epson printer gave me nothing but problems.  I was always un-installing, then re-installing the USB drivers.  I switched back to HP.My last HP printer used a black cartridge and tri-color cartridge with built-in print heads, the 74X and 75X.  It had a few quirks but was usable for a good service life.  Now I searched for a replacement.  HP no longer uses the 74X/75X and have switched to individual color cartridges.  Ok, sounds good - just replace the color which runs dry to save money.  But, reviews have been dismal about ink usage and unforgiving firmware which forces the user to purchase unnecessary new ink cartridges.I have been looking for months at the new HP's, Canon, and Epson for a network printer which can FAX aka "all-in-one."  I came up empty.  None of these major brands produce a printer with good reviews.  I'm reading about poor customer service, DOA printers, horrible ink usage, and cranky firmware.I never thought that Brother would have what I needed.  I use and abuse their label maker (tip: it's much easier printing address labels than trying to feed envelopes through a printer!)  This printer is amazing.  Within half an hour, I had it faxing, scanning, copying, and printing.  It has all kinds of little features which make life easier, such as the ability to preview a multi-page FAX before dialing and printing a confirmation page for a successful FAX.  With my HP, I needed to watch the display for a confirmation.It's far quieter than my HP.  It picked up an incoming FAX and I didn't even know.  The touchscreen panel swivels (wow factor).  The ADF folds out of the way so it's nearly half the height.  As someone else mentioned, the connectors for the network, USB, and phone are inside the printer - a little weird, but more of a cord organizer to keep your desk neat.  Didn't see it as an issue.Installing on a Mac was very easy... once I found the drivers, which were not on the CD.  The installation experience was unpleasant.  Mac owners should not worry, but note you must download the CUPS printer driver from the Brother website which is easy to find.  Grab the Twain interface, too - it's amazing.  I usually skip Twain since it's so much problem on a PC, but on the Mac it seems flawless.Don't bother with the included driver CD.  For Mac, it's useless.  It kept insisting that I go through a guided wireless installation and did not install any of the drivers I needed.  If you're the type of person who likes to spend their weekends fighting with computers, by all means embrace wireless printing.  I gave up years ago.  I don't install USB printers or wireless printers, never again.  I always run an Ethernet cable directly to my router and set a static IP address.  Trust me.  Macs don't like USB devices which can be turned on and off when they're trying to sleep (may cause a kernel panic).  And, if you've got VMware, sharing a network printer between three operating systems is infinitely easier than switching USB devices.  Google bonjour for windows and CUPS.  yea, it's a painful learning process, but you only have to do it once.Even more unpleasant was finding the CD label program which is supposed to be bundled with the printer.  I haven't found it yet.  It's not easy to find on Brother's website, but it's mentioned in the manual.  Google found it for me.  I ran it - wow, really powerful CD/DVD printing program for inkjet printable media.  I usually just use a Sharpie marker.If I find anything else worthy of mention, I'll update my review.  But, I am almost ready to chuck my HP printer for good and switching to Brother.  I just wish they'd make the Mac installation procedure a bit more friendly.

This is an Amazon Vines review of 3M Permanent Adhesive White Address Labels, 1 x 2.6 Inch in size and made for use with a Laser Printer.  There are 750 labels per pack. The box of labels arrived timely and packaged securely.The package says the labels are for use with a laser printer but I tested the labels using both a laser and an Inkjet printer. The address labels are made of a bright white paper material that is dense enough that when I used an Inkjet printer to print the labels the ink did not bleed through the label. So, my experience is you can use either type of printer to print the labels.In addition, I did not experience any problem with the sheet of labels jamming in either type of printer, something that I have experienced with discount or off brand labels. If you like to print labels using a template, the Avery address label 5160 template will work just fine with this 3M product.A nice user friendly feature of the address labels is the Quick Lift design, which eliminates the hassle of trying to peel the label off of the sheet. Just bend the sheet in half and the edges of the labels will peel back for easy lift off, a nice feature that I like.Finally, the 3M labels have a strong enough adhesive on the back that when you place the label on an  envelope...it sticks, which is exactly what I want an address label to do!From my use of this product, the 3M address labels seem to be well made so I can comfortably recommend this product, and give it a 5 star rating.

Swingline claims this Light Touch stapler takes "1/2 the effort" to operate (also that it is "quiet, smooth, powerful"). As an educator and artist, I have lots of uses for a laminator.  However, my wife, who has a collection of old letters from her grandparents during WWII, was really excited to have access to one too.  The Black and Decker Fast Heat Laminator warms up in 60 seconds, it laminates photos, documents, and other documents (paper or card stock thickness) up to 9.5 inches wide.  The easy to use control panel features an on/off, cold, 3ml, 5ml, and reverse buttons, with lighting and sound alerts, as well as auto-shutoff after 60 minutes.  In addition, it has an integrated corner rounder punch, an out-feed table on the back, and a power cord wrap.  Therefore, it's portable and easy to store too.  There are a variety of pouches available for laminating, which include business card, luggage tag, 4x5" photo, and letter size.  The laminator only comes with a sample of each, so additional pouches will need to be purchased.  Please be aware that for optimum results it is recommended that the Black & Decker TimeShield laminating pouches be used, and that the cleaning sheet included be run after every use.  At the time I wrote this review, the pouches were not available through Amazon.

These 2 inch durable post-its are great for notes as well as marking pages for future reference.  I especially like their different colors so that I can use them for different purposes - yellow for signatures, green for notes & red for most important discussions.
Great bags for a great price.  No problems at all with the quality, these are, afterall, designed for a one-time use, and they do the job perfectly.

I'm a craft supply junky, and these qualify... I already own lots of specialty pens (my favorites are from Sakura, and my Copic atyouspica Glitter pens) so I wasn't sure if I'd really like these very much and I was initially concerned that the fact they are stored vertically would mean they wouldn't write well or would skip (all my other pens note they should be stored horizontally).Initially I was really impressed, the quality of both the pens and the stand are much higher then I expected for this price range. There is a very nice variety of pen types (glitter, metallic, neon, pastel)...though I do feel like it's heavier on the blues & greens and they could definitely add some more pinks/reds (and I don't even like red) so keep that in mind if you gravitate toward more pinks and reds that this set might be lacking for you.I've had them about a month now and I have no complaints. I actually find myself using these more then my more expensive pens since they are easier to see and grab (my others are in a small drawer due to the claim they need to be stored laying down, I might test that theory now though since these work perfectly kept upright). They are fun to use with cards, but our favorite use so far is with my daughters doodle books... we've sat for hours together at the table working on the doodles using these pens and I love the extra bit of pop the metallic and glitter give!You can't go wrong with these, either for yourself... for a tween or teen, or even for other adults as I've yet to me anyone who hasn't liked them... my husband even swiped a couple I had to get back (love that the stand means I know if anyone made off with one too LOL) I'm thinking of a bigger set for my older daughter for Christmas so she can keep them in her room.

This is the second Smart Weigh scale I've been asked to give an unbiased review for in exchange for a free scale, and I have to say that I'm very impressed with their products. Even though this scale is specified for weighing items for postage and shipping, it is adaptable for many uses. For example, it could come in handy in the kitchen for weighing bulk items for recipes. It has a weighing range of .1 ounce to 110 pounds, so it can be very versatile. The weighing platform is 8"x8" and 1.8" tall, so it's a good size for weighing larger items. It comes with two AAA batteries and an AC adapter. For light usage, the batteries should last a long time, but it is very handy to have the AC adapter as well for more frequent users. The display is a separate component that has a coiled cord that can reach up to about 3', so it can be mounted on a wall or placed on a shelf for easier viewing. The readout is black numbers on a lighted blue screen and the display unit can be laid flat or positioned up to a 90 degree angle (or anything in between). There is a hold function so that the weight will remain displayed. It will also display in pounds (X.X), kilograms, grams, and pounds and ounces, so there is flexibility there as well. There is also a tare function for adjusting the weight with or without packaging. On top of all of this functionality, the unit is a matte black that is attractive (well, for a scale!) and fairly compact. It is made in China, for those of you who are avoiding such products, but I feel this is a top-notch scale and recommend it.

Although I initially gave this printer 2 stars, I have decided to amend my review after getting some technical assistance. My first interaction with the machine was incredibly frustrating; this printer is not compatible with Linux, which is what I run in my home office. None of the materials that came with the machine stated that fact, so all attempts to get set up and started were useless.When my husband attempted the setup process with his Windows-based laptop, on the other hand, it was smooth sailing all the way with Wi-fi enabled printing being a definite bonus. He encouraged me to alter my review, since he liked the printer and thinks it will be a great fit for us if I switch over to Windows. I would have sincerely appreciated if it had said somewhere that the piece was not Linux-compatible so I wouldn't have wasted an afternoon fighting with it and could have had more opportunity to either switch my system over to Windows or re-evaluate whether or not this was the right printer for us.That said, it is very professional looking, it does everything you would need in a home office and I expect it will grow on me once the initial frustration wears off.
This ink works wonderfully in my printer. I don't trust refilled or rebuilt cartridges so this is a good fit for me. Just wish I could have found the higher capacity cartridge on here.

I've never had a D-ring binder before.  It works very well when filled with paper allowing the one side to remain flat but the paper to turn easily.  The thickness is exactly as described and it has plastic for cover insertion. Nice binder.

The popup dispenser works pretty well and is helpful for gift wrapping.  The tape is thicker than standard Scotch tape.  The wrist dispenser is a one-size fits all device, and the fit is not as tight on my slender wrists as I would have liked.  When removing a piece of tape, the tape tugs the dispenser away from my wrists and makes dispensing a little difficult.Other than those quibbles, it's a great idea.

I've had my share of printers and right now I have three of them on my wifi and in use:  Canon MP640 (very nice), HP Photosmart C7280(a pain), and an old R80 Inkjet (been on my desk in service for nearly 12 years - a workhorse).  The only one that compares to this new Kodak is the Canon.The Kodak is a little bulkier, there are too many openings that do not completely close up to protect it from dust and the view screen is much too small (my only real negative) making the selection of pictures harder than it has to be.  To the positive side, it only has two cartridges (black and colors) and only one paper feed for all paper types.The Kodak setup is a piece of cake and went very smoothly.  The wifi picked right up without any problems.There isn't much more to say.  The printing quality of both the Canon and Kodak are marvelous.  I was very impressed with the Kodak's sharpness in the pictures I selected to print.  I'd have to give it a 4.5 (small screen is just stupid).  But I'm rounding up due to the ink system and paper feed.****UPDATE*****09/02/2011:It is imperative that you use the software from Kodak to install the printer.  Initially, I did not and let Windows 7 find a Kodak driver for it.  It worked for a while and then Windows 7 could not find the printer.  I tried deleting the other printers and nothing worked.  So I then installed the drivers from the CD that came with the printer.  Not only did the printer install, it automatically updated the firmware of the printer from Kodak.  Once everything was completed (all automatically), the printer was the default printer and everything was good with the world.

Purchased this scanner to replace an aging Visioneer scanner that I used for the office. The Visioneer has a 1000 page daily duty cycle, so I figure that Kodak's 4000 pages is a good size upgrade. Compared to the Visioneer Strobe XP450, this one is a night and day difference... It had better be, knowing the price is about 50% more. Scanner scans papers super fast... 150dpi color pdf takes about two seconds.Of the hardware features, I found one that is slightly lacking - The feeder is advertised as 75 pages. This part is true, but the holder at the bottom that holds the scanned paper, holds maybe half  as much. When putting 50 pages in to scan at the same time, it drops the papers neatly into the tray at first, but once the scanned papers start stacking up, the scanned paper, as it comes out of the scanner, will start pushing the stack of paper all over the place, causing a huge mess... In another words, if you plan walk away after starting a 75 page scan job, you'll come back to a floor full of paper.I felt that the software interface needed improvement. Even though the scanner has pretty good default settings, I still needed to tweak a few things to optimize the scans. I have a pretty strong computer/IT background, and it still took me quite a big of time to adjust the settings before everything was perfect. The interface was not as good as Visioneer's OneTouch, there are settings hidden within multiple layers menus that you'll have to look for.There was one problem I encountered that almost caused me to return the scanner to Amazon. When I first started scanning papers, I noticed that the computer would spend quite a bit of time processing the scanned docs. For example... if it takes 30 seconds to scan 15 pages, computer requires 30 seconds more to process and safe the PDF's. I called over to tech support, clearly stated the problem, but they were unable to help me.. Just read off the script... "have you reinstalled software. have you installed all the software, etc." I was pretty pissed off... in fact, I had started to pack the scanner up before I decided to give it one more shot.I saw that the scan setting was on "PDF Searchable" so without thinking much about it, i changed it to "PDF" and scanned some paper. Luckily, this did the trick.... 30 seconds dropped down to about 2 seconds. Kodak, you are so lucky. I almost returned the scanner and bought another brand. Instead of convincing me to reinstall the software, I think your tech should be trained about different scan settings, which ones will take a lot of processing, which ones will scan fast.Overall, with my many years of IT experience, it still took me about 2 hrs to get this up and running to a point where I can scan the thousands of pages in each month. Overall, I recommend the scanner. But hope Kodak can improve upon the bottom tray in future product releases.

This pen set comes with three commonly-used ink colors--black, blue, and red. The pen design is modern, with a cap that depicts the color, as do the tip and two stripes on each pen. Each pen has a soft texture black overlay, but a more conventional grip near the pen tip would make writing a bit more comfortable and improve the overall design. The cap goes on the end when the pen is in use, and even snaps into place--unlike many pens where the cap falls off!As for writing, I'm always a bit sloppy with bold-type, smooth-rolling "rollerball" pens. I wouldn't say that the pens are completely smear-free because there are occasional "blobs," but part of that might be my own writing style (pressing pens down firmly). Helping to eliminate most smears, the ink dries almost as soon as it hits the paper. When I tried to make the ink run by putting water on a piece of paper, the red ran almost indiscernibly, and the blue and black inks stayed put.This type of pen is really useful for jotting down quick notes since it rolls so smoothly. As some people have "good scissors," I have a "good pen" that stays on my writing desk . . . and right now it's a Jetstream.
Canon's products always work.  Too bad the prices are so high for their cartridges. Would be nice if they got their prices down, but so far no problems.
These laminating pouches have worked really well for us. It's a great value and I will buy more from them in the future.

I've been using this type of calendar for years and it continues to fulfill my needs. In addition,m its sturdy and handy.

Described as part of the "Sustainable Forestry Initiative" these are letter-size pressboard office folders.  The spine, expandable to 2", is reinforced with tape billed as Tyvek. There is a slightly smaller inner cardboard folder, permanently attached to the outer folder, also reinforced along the spine.  This inner folder, which functions as a pair of dividers, also has a metal fastener attached to the top of both sides of each divider, for a total of six fasteners.  A two-hole punch is useful to make the most of the fasteners.The index tabs on the outer folders are all in roughly the center position. This is one classy little marker.  The classic Sharpie experience, it smells great and writes very well.  Permanent on most surfaces.
