The AirPrint feature works like a charm.The scanning and copying process is very good.  I liked he capacity to feed multiple documents into the machine for copying.It is as speedy as most printers.Cons:The Canon MX512 was a bit difficult to setup using the somewhat abbreviated instruction sheet.  It takes awhile too.It is a finger print and lint magnet.The front cover cannot be closed with more than six or seven sheets of paper loaded in the tray.The ink cartridges are very very expensive.There was no USB-to-printer cable included in the box.The paper catching apparatus is not the best.The machine is a bit bulky, but that is understandable considering how much it can do.I can recommend the Canon MX512, but most enthusiastically for its use in a small office. I must have moved more than anyone else I know.  Because of this experience (and dread!), I think I know a thing or two about moving boxes!These dish boxes, as they are called, are really just large double-walled moving boxes, and they can be used for a variety of things.  While I know they were originally meant to move dishes, they are best for heavy, but bulky items.In previous moves, I have loaded them up with heavy linens and they held up just fine.  This was when I had movers doing the work.  I wouldn't advise loading the boxes up with many, small, heavy items like linens or books if you are moving them yourself, as those items are probably best left to the "small"-size boxes.  However, if you have movers, why not take advantage of stuffing everything you can into as few boxes as possible.  It makes packing, unpacking and disposal/recycling much easier.  If you are moving these boxes yourself, I found they are handy for packing items like the kitchen mixer, food processor, as well as cast-iron pots and pans.  Those items really can use the double-walled thickness to prevent the box from collapsing under the weight of the hefty items.  These work perfect for those items as they require a tall, strong box.Ironically, I found that dishes and glasses are best packed in other boxes than these.  These are just too large to effectively pack dishes.  You are just left with too much room to fill around dishes, which requires excessive and a waste of packing material.  Dishes are best protected with bubble wrap or padded foam individually and placed inside of a "medium"-sized box.  I just don't place too many in the "medium"-sized box and with the bubble wrap or Styrofoam peanuts, the weight to size ratio is ideal for dishes - just enough padding and weight for a "medium" box.This set of four boxes comes in a larger 48" x 19" x 5.5" shipping box, which made it across the country by ground just fine.  (The outer shipping box was pretty beat-up though, but it you get one in better condition, it could also be re-used for packing and moving.)  They are identical in most every way to the Uhaul Dish Barrel boxes, but with the convenience of Amazon shipping directly to your home and not having to step foot in a Uhaul store.

Even though the 5510 is being replaced by the 5610, it is still a much better value.  The newer model uses the same black ink cartridge (HP 56) as the 5510 but it uses a much smaller color ink cartridge.  In fact the newer cartridge is only 5ml whereas the cartridge for the 5510 is 17 ml!!  This alone will mean that the newer printer will cost 3x more to print a color page.  Not to say that I print a lot of color copies or pictures but just the fact that it costs so much will prevent you from even considering printing pictures or greeting cards.**** Positive points for the HP OfficeJet 5510 include: ****- A very nice document feeder that supports upto 20 pages- A flatbed scanner that allows you to make copies from books or bound material- Excellent text and graphics printout and excellent copy features- Easy to use and configure with its display screen- The printer is relatively quiet for an all in one machine.  I don't understand why some user's complain that it is loud when it is actually reasonably quiet compared to a lot of other machines.**** Negative points for this printer include: ****- Installation process is not as simple as it should be.  If you fail to follow the directions EXACTLY then you may have to uninstall and start over from the beginning!- The software is nice and easy to use but it takes up too much space on your hard drive- The scanner's resolution is not as good as the newer model.  For most users it won't be a problem but if you plan to scan a lot of pictures and expect accurate colors without corrections then the newer model may be the wiser choice for you.  Personally I have scanned a few pictures and they turned out pretty good after using corrections built into the software.- The lid for the flatbed scanner does not hinge fully (like the HP PSC 2110) so it will be difficult to scan items such as large books.- The controls are not as straightforward and thorough as some of the other HP models (like the PSC 2110).  Although this model is still easy to use a lot of the essential controls are buried in menus.  Some of the other HP models have dedicated buttons for the most common features like copy quality.- I had to return a brand new unit due to a defective document feeder.  The new unit works perfectly but it is not reassuring to have a problem with a similar new unit.  An optional warranty might be a wise choice with this printer (although HP's 1 year warranty is pretty generous)Overall, despite being replaced by the newer 5610 this is still a very good purchase that will actually have lower operating costs than the newer model.

The Epson NX625 is a light weight home use all in one printer. Epson has done a very nice job including excellent every day printing, good photo printing, excellent copying, and good scanning; in a well designed package.It is important to understand that this is a light weight printer. It is not designed for an office or heavy use by many people. The construction is perfectly acceptable for home use, but does have a cheap feel to everything. The control panel buttons have a bad flexing inexpensive plastic feel to them. The menu layout is not intuitive, and the four arrow direction and OK button arrangement is too wide to navigate by feel. The paper drawer has three tabs on the back that could break off easily if mishandled. The scan cover is very lightly weight and flexible (this can be a curse or a blessing).Newer models of this printer have a full touch screen panel for selecting pictures to print and navigate the menus. If you believe in touch panel ruggedness over mechanical buttons, the newer model might be a better choice.The design choices I love on this printer - the scanner cover is a thin single piece to lift, not a huge button loaded panel like most of the newer modes. The paper all loads from the front and print output comes out the front. The paper tray, when inserted, is flush with the front of the printer (this is an excellent choice, since most printers have an ugly tray that sticks out the front). The control panel has a really nice locking tilt feature.The really great news about this printer, it works very well. Output is really nice. Normal fast copying produced a nice clean color copy that looked a lot like the original. When I loaded up a Smugmug Calibration print, some high quality photo paper, and set the copier to best quality; the copy was nearly perfect. The black contrast at full black and the first gray block were the same in the copy, which moved contrast up a tiny amount and blocked some shadow detail. Otherwise, color balance was exactly right and the light end of contrast was perfect. Totally unexpected from an inexpensive scanner.Output from a memory card (the printer accepts only small media cards, like the Sony Memory Sticks and SD cards - no CF card), was good. Using the small screen was not easy to select a picture. And navigating the menus was not intuitive, sometimes OK selected, sometimes Menu was required, and other times another button was required. The menus are pretty good; it's just fast navigating is not easy.Standard print outs were crisp and clean. I haven't seen an ink jet printer fail standard black and white text in a very long time.Scanning was another story. I did a somewhat unreasonable comparison of this scanner to a very high end flat bed Canon scanner. This Epson scanner yielded low contrast and washed out color scans compared to the Canon scanner. The key, don't expect to do high end scanning of photographs for archiving or enlarging, the Epson scanner is not up to the task. The scanner is not fast, especially at high resolution. An 8x10 took 15 minutes to scan at 1200 dpi; the Canon scanner finished this in just over one minute. The software allows a 4100 dpi setting that took 36 minutes to scan the 8x10, and had no more resolution than the 1200 setting. Highly enlarged, it was clear the scanner wasn't perfectly focused, showed some blue color fringing, and contrast was not accurate. Remember, this is a somewhat unfair test, this printer was never designed to do high resolution fast scanning. A 4x6 scans in around a minute and is the more likely size most people will use.Output speed is on par with most ink jet printers. My benchmark is an HP DeskJet 6940. The Epson printed about the same speed, but was noisier. The Epson is not loud, but it's also not quiet.Set up was a total breeze. I had this running on my wireless network and a Macintosh MacBook Pro within twenty minutes. I never connected a printer cord to the printer, there was just no need. The instruction manual is crystal clear on how to set up the printer on a wireless network.Set steps: Unpack the box - Epson did a great job with a plastic bag with handles for the printer. I've never seen a printer packaged this nicely and easy to remove from the box. Plug it in, turn it on. Select the language, and then open the scanner lid and the scanner glass. There's a box inside the scanner area where you lift the lid, shake up the supplied four ink cartridges, and snap them in their color coded locations. Close the lid and wait five minutes for the ink to prime. The paper tray is a bit delicate, there are three sliding bars to align for the paper and you aren't supposed to get the paper past the rear arrow.To connect the printer to a wireless network, enter the setup mode from the front panel, and follow the prompts for Setup Wizard. Once you've selected your network, you'll need to enter the pass code for your network. With WPA security (the printer recognizes what kind of security is enabled and generates the correct password) you'll need to pay attention to lower and upper case letters. My first try, I used all uppercase letters and the connection failed. The good news, the printer outputs a report that explains what went wrong, or right with the set up.From there, I put the CD in each of my computers and installed the appropriate driver software. The wizard there walked me straight through to the printer - amazingly simple. The software allowed me to print a test page or scan a test document. On the first try everything worked fine. I never had to get into the Windows or Mac twisted hardware wizards to add this printer. I've set up two different wireless print spoolers / routers that were major pains to make work. I can now remove my print server and just print directly to this Epson printer.The ink cartridges are not everywhere. It seems like HP has done an incredible job blanketing every store from Costco, through BestBuy, through Staples, ending in Amazon with every imaginable ink cartridge. Epson has been a lot less successful at this, the Epson ink selection at the brick and mortar stores is slim pickings. The good news, these are fairly high capacity cartridges, moderate cost, and very available right here on Amazon. The 125 series of cartridges works in a fairly large number of printers, so ink is probably a good choice with this printer. Instead of a tri-color and a black cartridge, Epson uses four independent cartridges. If you print a lot of red, then only the red cartridge has to be replaced frequently.This is a very nice printer. I was surprised at the quality of the photo copying and the photo output. Wireless was easy to set up and it just plain worked right out of the box. It appears to be a somewhat fragile printer, but that is probably OK for lighter home use.

I really liked these Avery Permanent File Folder Label Pad: each pad includes 160 write-on 1/3 cut labels, color-coded in blue, red, green & yellow.The use: I am a big fan of 1/3 cut tabbed file folders (I use them all the time), and I usually write with an ultra fine point sharpie, the name of the folder in the tab area.  This is permanent and works well, but the problem always comes when I no longer need a folder with that particular name: it looks ugly to use white-off over it (correction fluid), and since it is permanent, I can't erase it, and I don't like striking thru it and writing it below (I'm too much of a neat freak): I'm not fond of pencil for this use, so I usually would end up throwing away a perfectly good folder that would be re-usable, because I couldn't re-name it: with these new Avery file folder labels, PROBLEM SOLVED!I tested this, and I put one of these labels over the sharpie on a folder, and I couldn't even read what was behind it!  The paper is thick enough on the label to keep this from happening: now I will be able to RECYCLE and RE-use my file folders when I need to re-name them.  I a big fan of this product for that use: as far as other uses of these labels, I'll leave that to others to discover: I'm a fan of using these labels for what they are intended for, and I'm really happy to be able to be more 'green' this way...These labels are great, and highly recommended for use with 1/3 cut file folders, for the purpose of RECYCLING and highlighting folder names!

These labels do exactly what they're advertised to do, they stick easily, are removable and you can actually take them off and re-stick them several times as long as your surface is clean and not dusty. This HP Multipurpose Copy/Laser/Inkjet with 96 Brightness, I was so glad to find in a local store last week. I haven't been so excited about a product in a long time.  All those years of receipts and statements had nowhere to go.  Now, I just scan and shred.  The Fujitsu ScanSnap is so fast and easy to use.  I just put stacks of paper in and it scans, front and back.  It reorients my paper for me and saves it in PDF format.  I've put up to 42 sheets in at once.  Yes, since most everything is folded and bent in all sorts of ways, the machine will sometimes jam or scan multiple sheets at once, but it will pause and the fix is easy.  The only thing I don't like is the paper catch, which doesn't catch it all that well.  For large stacks of previously folded paper, I have to hold the paper as it's being fed, so it's not something I can leave unattended.  If the paper was something that is perfectly flat, like a fresh stack of paper, it would not need babysitting.  I don't mind, because the scanning is quick.  I went through a mound of paper in one evening.  My shredder had to be emptied twice.  Of course, I make sure to have the files automatically back up, but so far so good.Storage is easy.  The little scanner folds up into a lopsided box.  It's so cute, like it's hibernating.  The footprint is small, so I can store it away when I don't need it.The one thing I did not like was installation of Acrobat X did not go smoothly.  It simply would not install on my Windows 7 system.  The solution (I found it online) was to go to Control Panel --> Clock, Language, and Region --> Region and Language --> Administrative --> Change system locale --> English (United Kingdom).  After you change it, you have to reboot.  Then, you can install Acrobat X.  After installing Acrobat X, go back and change the language back to English (United States).  Once that's done, it's all good.Another note: this scanner does not play nice with my USB 3.0 ports.  It will only work with USB 2.0 ports.Finally, I don't feel overwhelmed by the massive amounts of paper building up in my file cabinet.  Scan it, back it up, toss it.  It's the only way to go.________________UPDATE 2/24/13: I would like to add that the ScanSnap Organizer software is wonderful.  It converts the files to searchable PDF automatically.  I can make virtual cabinets with virtual folders and searching them is a breeze.  Together with the Acrobat X software, I have total control.  There is no way a real file cabinet would be this easy.

This is just what I needed!  The blackboard is about the size of an ordinary sheet of paper and it's fairly lightweight. It would also be handy on a refrigerator or wherever people hang their shopping/to do lists (if their lives are more organized than mine). I use it as my "must do" board...showing the essential work-type things I must complete before I can answer personal email, review something for Amazon, fall asleep at my desk, etc.I formerly listed these tasks on Post-Its, but found those treacherous little bits of paper to be completely untrustworthy.  I cannot tell you how many times they'd fall down behind my desk or just light out for parts unknown.  The task would be forgotten, and I'd be all engrossed in giving my two cents worth about how much I hated the latest Bill O'Reilly book when suddenly a phone call from an irate client would ruin everthing.  Who invented deadlines anyway?  Didn't Einstein say "time is a river" so where do these people get off...anyway, back to the board.Now my "gotta" list is in bright neon, the board is stuck to the wall with industrial glue of such preternatural ability that my hands were glued together for two days despite soaking them in nail polish remover (two future reviews!) It also rendered me a bit giddy from the fumes and speaking of which, don't expect to get a buzz from the markers, they are odor free. My office is the size of a dental filling with no windows, so opening a fresh magic marker can make me black out. No such luck here.  Were it not for that, I'd have given the set a Five Star Salute.Oh, one other caveat...there is no place to put the markers.  There should be a little slot for them or a string to tie them to or something. How long can I go wearing them behind my ear? It is just a matter of time before I lose one. And you know what happens when one goes...soon a second pen will go out hunting for its brother and pretty soon all of them will be out seeking their little Neon Pen fortunes and I'll be scratching my notes on the board with a car key. In fact, Orange is already MIA, and I used up most of the Pink coloring in my fingernails while listening to a client going on and on about something.  Do those people ever get tired of the sound of their own voices?  But I digress...The Sanford Expo Neon Markers & Magnetic Dry Erase Black Board Combo Pack (and doesn't that roll off the lips like honey?)is a thing of beauty, but it's only gonna be a joy for another day or two, when I lose the last of the markers. Tested with a Mac-based system running OS 10.8, using an Airport wifi network, and compared with the Xerox Phaser 6120 (my earlier color laser) as well as an HP monochrome laser printer that's about ten years old.Setup: Straight-forward. Remove many pieces of orange tape. Try to figure out where the two pieces of plastic attach which are packed separately (didn't manage, but will keep them handy for when I do figure it out). Plug in the fax line and the AC cord and turn it on. The printed instructions are handy and allowed me to quickly set up the wifi network by entering the password on the printer. I used the CD to add the software to one computer but a laptop to which I never added the software was just as quickly able to use the new Canon. No problems at all with configuration.Operation: Unlike my Xerox 6120, the lights don't dim every time the Canon starts to run a heating cycle. While this pulls significant power in operation, it has a handy sleep mode that triggers after 20 minutes and quickly warms to operating ability thereafter. Printing speed is fast, whether printing a pdf file, Word file, or photo. I should point out that this is not a photo printer. Color accuracy is typical for a color laser printer - it's perfect for Excel files with multiple color cells, but I wouldn't use it to print photos. For that, get your self a high end inkjet photo printer. If you consider what you do to be primarily business type printing, where you want words to be absolutely crisp even in color, or you want your logo to come out perfectly, this is your printer. But if you're doing a good deal of photographed output, the ink-jet is better. Speed of printing is typical laser - very fast if you're printing in black only, and fast in full color. No comparison here to the Xerox, which I'll now use as a step-stool, and which was decidedly slow, power-hungry, and mechanically challenged (the number of paper path errors equaled the number of quality prints).Copying capability, faxing, and scanning all work quite well and can be controlled either from the Mac or from the printer's extensive  screen and keyboard entry system. As others have pointed out, this is not a two-sided printer. For that, you'll need the MF8280cdw, which also has double the memory and a 250 sheet paper cassette instead of 150.The only difficulty I've had with the printer is that I could not get iPhoto to print to it. (Though as I said -- not a photo printer). The unit is reasonably quiet (much quieter than the Xerox), fast (much faster than the old HP), and has the wireless ability that means I don't mind that it's big and weighs 65 pounds. It doesn't need to be next to my computer. Canon's website provides support information and updated software ( at this point, the disc included with the printer is up to date ). Printing from an iThing (Pad or Phone) is easy to set up using the free app from Canon. Overall high marks here.

This is a really great mousepad; perfect for polished or glass surfaces; thin, ridged, and stylish; sticky and repositionable.The outer dimensions are a standard 8.5" x 7.0", but the thinness is remarkable; like five sheets of 20lb printer paper; or about half a dime.The surface has myriad little ridges that catch light.  This effectively solves the biggest problem with modern optical mouses: they don't work on reflective surfaces.  My desk is polished granite, and my wife's is 1/4" glass.  On granite my mouse gets jumpy from time to time, but on glass it simply doesn't work without a pad.  To show you this pad's ridges I uploaded a high-magnification scan, with a dime for a sense of scale.  The ridges have a nice feel; grippy but soft, and I wish more things had this texture, like tools or steering wheels.The sticky backing is very similar to a post-it note's.  I've repositioned mine about 10 times with no noticeable deterioration in tackiness; there must be a limit, but it doesn't worry me.  There is no residue left behind after moving.  The benefit of the tackiness is that the pad can be ultra thin and not slip around.  Plus, thin is critical to prevent carpal tunnel syndrome from a continually bent wrist.  But 8.5" x 7.0" isn't large enough for me to comfortably leave the pad in the same place all the time.  To avoid cramps in my inner-elbow I resituate the mousing ballpark periodically.  And so the detriment of the tacky backing is that it takes more than a simple shove to move the pad.Not a big deal, but if I could offer a suggestion for improvement: make it bigger -- legal sized 10.5" x 14.0" would be great, so I could stretch out my arm without leaving the pad or repositioning it.  And if that were too big, the pad is thin enough to be cropped with scissors or an exacto knife.Face it, optical mouses work pretty well these days, and you usually don't need a pad.  It's not like the bad old days with those jumpy steel balls and little axles that jammed up with hair and worse things.  But if you're reading this review you probably have a special need.  I can't imagine anything better than the 3M Precise Optical Mousing Surface for glass or polished desktops.  It's cheap and it works great.

Parents: If you're going to buy your child a graphing calculator for school, DON'T insult his/her intelligence with this limited function calculator. Go with a TI-86 or TI-89 as it will serve him/her well through into college. What this means is you save money by purchasing one calculator that will be useful for SATs, GREs, AP tests, high school, algebra, calculus 1-3, college, etc...If you buy a TI-83, you will have to get a TI-86 or TI-89 in the future because a TI-83 is an OVERGLORIFIED TI-82, which is really good for pre-algebra and algebra.GRANTED you can use a TI-83 for Calculus and more advanced math, but it's a good idea to allow your child to grow intellectually by learning how to use a much more advanced calculator for Calc II and III. I had no problems using a TI-86 for Calc 2 and 3, but the TI-89 definitely helped me understand theorems that were in 3 dimensions.For those who are looking for a calculator to use at work:The TI-83 is a piece of junk. It's for kiddies in 6th grade.The TI-86 is a better engineering calc than the TI-89 due to its more intuitive menu interface for units conversions and what not.The TI-89 is better suited for theoretical math work because of its "pretty print" and units system. Plus with the right software mods, you can do differentiation/integration with the variables intact - just a time saver really.However I realize you're just trying to find info on the TI-83. My overall recommendation for the TI-83 is: don't bother. It's a solid calculator but pay a bit more and get at least a TI-86. It will serve you WELL into frosh or sophomore year of college (Calculus I-III). A TI-83 will have served its absolute purpose by the start of your senior year in high school.It's like bringing a 9mm pistol in an African Safari. It will handle meerkats and other small creatures but once you get to the larger predators - it will not work very well. The TI-86 and TI-89 is comparable to a .50AE and .50 Magnum. It can tackle small stuff but will hold its own when the big beasts come around.

UPDATE January 17th, 2014: A fellow reviewer informed me today that there are three printer models with this Envy 5530 being one of them that is part of the HP Instant Ink program. The HP Instant Ink program is a monthly pay as you go program.  Your printer must be connected to the Internet so that it can order new cartridges for when you are running low.  The cartridges, shipping and recycling are included in your monthly fee.  It starts as low as 2.99 for 50 sheets and caps out at 9.99 for 300 monthly sheets printed.  There is a roll over allowed up to the amount that you are enrolled in.  For example with the 300 sheet plan I can rollover up to 300 unprinted sheets.  If you need to print more you will but at a cost of 1 dollar for 25 sheets currently for the 9.99 plan.  You can cancel or change your plan at any time without penalty.  The printing can be black and white, colored or photos.  It doesn't matter how much ink is used, rather the amount printed.  You can keep tabs on your sheets printed from the online queue on your account once you sign up.  We supposedly do not need to worry about purchasing ink again at those last moments because it will automatically be ordered by the printer at no additional cost.  Finally, you do not begin once you sign up but rather once you install the instant ink cartridge.  From there you will begin your billing in 30 days.From what I see here this is yet another reason why this printer is a great purchase.  I am enrollin today;  if what the site claims is true I will be saving hundreds every year.I currently own an HP Photosmart network printer that is an ink hog.Right out of the box, the Envy printer set-up was simple, where the Photosmart was not as intuitive.  A CD is supplied with the printer but not necessary for operation.  The power cord supplied has finally changed and it is no longer that dreaded clunky box; just a regular power cord which plugs directly into the machine.  Compared to my older HP which had one black slot and 3 colors slots, on the ENVY there is one black cartridge and a trio color cartridge.  Overall the unit itself is thinner and has a smaller foot stamp than it's predecessor.  It also has a sleeker appearance.What really stood out to me during the set up process was the WIFI.  WIFI set-up was through the printer's touchscreen.  Once okay is clicked the printer intuitively begins to browse through available WIFI networks just like your home computer or mobile device.  After password entry you can save your configurations and your are done with that step.  You will have the obligatory congratulatory printed page that tests the functions.Printing through an older mobile device (HTC EVO 3D) was also a breeze.  There was no set-up necessary.  You just turn on your WIFI on your mobile device and you find the network that the printer is connected to.  Find something to print, click print off your menu bar and it will start to scan for available printers on your network.  Once the device finds the printer, choose it and print!  VOILA.There is automatic two-sided printing which can be rather cumbersome on other models.  I love this feature!  I did not give five stars because I tend to find further issues many months later with ALL printers.  I am concerned with how much ink will eventually cost on a monthly basis.  Currently our printer needs the ink cartridges replaced every 45 days or so at a hefty price tag of sixty-five dollars!  That is too much...  HP had claimed that model would be cheaper to operate.  I am hoping that they have fixed that with their currently printer line-up, but only time and a real world environment will truly tell.Highly recommend this model for ease of use regarding network connectivity.  Being a novice or experienced user should yield the same results; might take a bit longer for the novice though as there aren't any real detailed instructions included.  IF you need an inexpensive printer that can print borderless photos in an instant that can rival your Kinkos then this might be a good candidate for your home.  Prints fast and with ease.  I have found that the fast draft actually looks pretty amazing... almost laser like.  Worth giving it a try even if you junk it a year later.

SETUPAlthough the printer doesn't come with a printed manual, it links you to the online manual. I appreciate that Canon limits the amount of paper included with the printer. However, it needs to include two bits of information in its quick start guide: How to find the well-hidden serial number (open the scanner lid and the side doors (all of them), and look on the metal bar where the ink slides -- I've posted a photo) and how to use the keypad to set up the wireless.KEYPADThe keypad has only numbers, no letters. So it works similarly to texting on a cell phone with no keyboard. Press the * to cycle through the characters: uppercase letters, lowercase letters and numbers. When entering letters, you select the number key that has the letter and press it once, twice or three times depending on the letter you need. Other than this, printer setup is easy and fast.CONNECTING TO DEVICESThe printer comes with a CD and URL for setting up the printer on computers and devices. For iOS devices, the web page sends you to Canon's app in the App Store to download Canon's app. However, this is not a needed step for iOS devices (iPad and iPhone). Airprint connects the devices to the printer. Those on a Mac will need to set it up through the Canon website. Because the Canon is wireless and Airprint-compatible, it was painless to set up the desktop, laptop, iPad and iPhone with the printer and they all worked.PRINTINGNoise level is typical for an inkjet: noisy. Quality of printing is good. The photos print better than my previous printers did. Printer paper and photo paper (various sizes) go in the same slot. So you'll need to remove one for the other. (Some printers allow you to have both loaded at the same time.)As someone who uses both sides of paper, I appreciate the picture in the paper tray letting me know which way to put printed paper to ensure next print job goes on the blank side. When printing a multi-page job, the printer does both sides. You don't have to do odd pages and then feed them back in to do even pages.CANON PIXMA MX922I have this printer's bigger brother, theCanon PIXMA MX922 Wireless Color Photo Printer. Hands down, I recommend that one over this one. As of this writing, the price on the MX922 is lower than this one -- including the list price! (Canon's website, however, lists the MX922 for $50 more.) The MX922 has an on-screen keyboard for entering the wireless key, more on-screen features and buttons to make it effortless to navigate the settings and menus. The paper and photo paper holder is better quality and more stable.VERDICTIf this were my only printer, I wouldn't get it. It makes a good family, college student and backup printer. However, the more feature-rich MX922 is currently cheaper -- so why not go for that instead? If size matters, the MX532 is smaller, but not by much.As opportunities to test out more features come up, I will post an update. I hope this review helped you and you'll show it with a quick click of yes. If you have unanswered questions, please comment so I can update the review with answers to your questions.

At a time when some schools are considering eliminating cursive writing from their curriculum, a writing pen seems like a real connection with the past.  I think there are two reasons to have a fountain pen.  One is for collecting fine writing instruments.  This pen was not designed (or priced) as a collectible item.  It is intended to be used as an everyday writing instrument.The pen did not come with instructions, so if you are not savvy, you might need a little instructions on how to use the pen.  It comes with a reservoir that you can fill with ink from a ink supply bottle.  If you choose to use this method, unscrew the bib from the body of the pen.  Insert the bib (the writing point) into the ink jar and squeeze the metal tabs on the outside of the rubber reservoir.  The vacuum will fill the pen with ink and you can begin writing.  The pen comes with a disposable ink cartridge.  If you would prefer to use ink cartridges instead of filling the reservoir, simply pull the reservoir out – it snaps in place.  Once you have removed the reservoir you can insert the disposable ink cartridge.  Make sure the cartridge is penetrated – you can feel it when it is fully inserted – to allow the ink to flow.Once you have decided on a ink delivery method, the pen is ready to use.The pen provides a good writing experience.  The ink flows evenly so you get a good even distribution – no need for the old ink blotters.The pen has an excellent feel in your hand.  It is well balanced and the small “animal skin” around the middle provides a nice touch to the look of the pen.  The pen appears to be well designed and made with durable materials.  It should give years of satisfactory service.  Pilot makes some very high-end, collectors type pens.  Pilot is a respected manufacturer of pens. This one is designed for your everyday writing needs.

This is perhaps the fastest and easiest printer install I've ever done. The printer box has been sitting on the living floor near the front door for a couple of weeks because the box was so huge I became concerned about where I would put the printer. So I finally unboxed it today and did all the set up on the floor of the living room.Installing the cartridges was a cinch, as was setting the date and time. Then I installed the CD in the laptop and started the WiFi installation process. It has always been my experience that something goes wrong during the process of connecting the printer to the computer - you find you need another driver, or a different cable, or some piece of software that isn't on the CD, or the software interferes with something else already installed on your computer....  But not this time!  Though the software took awhile (~15 minutes) to install (while I browsed the web and worked on other stuff), everything installed flawlessly. I printed a test page immediately and, though the printer is rather noisy, it's super fast and the quality is superb. The print is much crisper than our older HP 700 series all-in-one printer, so this will no doubt become our primary printer now.Then I found a few old images, one really old black and white from the 1950's, and one color from a cheap throw-away camera, and scanned both. This probably means that I'll have to buy fully loaded cartridges right away. I deduct 1/2 a star for that peculiar decision by Brother.

My thoughts after spending some time with the Epson WorkForce WF-3640:SETUPSetting up the printer physically was problem-free. To install the software I had to download from Epson's site (my computer's CD ROM drive is broken, so I couldn't use the enclosed CD). Happily, the direct URL for downloading the software is provided in Epson's "Start Here" guide. No problems.After the physical setup, you'll want to set up your printer up for mobile printing. For that you have to go to epson(com)/iPrint. This site was a little overwhelming for me at first because you're presented with a host of things your printer can do and that you need to set up. It's not as bad as it seems, though, once you start looking into it. You just have to go through the seven tabs on the page one by one and see if you need or want to set up that function. These tabs are:Email PrintRemote PrintScan to CloudiPrint AppCreative Print AppPrint and Scan AppPartner SolutionsSome of them require that you download software or log in to epsonconnect(dot)com and set things up there, but what's required should be obvious as you're working your way through. In the event, I didn't bother with all of these options, and you probably won't either. I did not set up Remote Print or use the Creative Print App, and the Print and Scan App is just for Windows 8 tablets. (It's not a tab, but I also have not set up the computer as a fax machine, so have no experience of that.) A few comments regarding the features I have used:EMAIL PRINTAt epsonconnect(dot)com you can assign your printer a unique email address so that you can mail documents to it for printing. You can allow anyone to print on your machine using this address, or you can create a list of approved senders so that your machine will only print documents received from those addresses. This is a great safeguard, but there is a potential related problem. When I was setting up my email address, the first address I chose was taken (let's say newprinter(at)print(dot)epsonconnect(dot)com). I initially opted instead to use a very similar address, with a hyphen inserted (new-printer), but one might also choose to add a number in such a case (newprinter456). But after hyphenating, I decided to use a different email address altogether. The hyphenated version, I figured, was too close to that other person's. I, or someone on my approved sender's list, could easily leave out the hyphen somewhere down the road and send a document to the wrong printer. If we did, and if the owner of the other printer let anyone print on his computer (the "anyone can send print jobs to this printer" option at epsonconnect(dot)com), then there was a potential for our sensitive information to wind up in somebody else's home office. Maybe this is an unlikely possibility, but it worried me enough to choose a different email address, at least.SCAN TO CLOUDScan to cloud is a wonderful option with a slightly misleading name. Basically, you can scan something on the printer, then send that scan to a number of places--the cloud (e.g., your Dropbox account), your computer, or to any email address you specify. You have to set up these various accounts at epsonconnect(dot)com, but it's not hard. Once they're input, you're set. You just select the email address (say) that you want to send a scan to in a list that appears on the printer's display. You can also choose whether you want the scan to be in PDF or JPG format. It works great.IPRINT APPThe iPrint app is an Android or Apple app you can use to send stuff to your printer from your mobile device. I tried it out briefly. I successfully sent a photo to the printer, but the app crashed repeatedly when I tried to print an email using the app. I gave up pretty quickly and decided to use Apple AirPrint to print mail instead (see under the PARTNER SOLUTIONS tab). This has worked perfectly.I'm very pleased with this printer. It's easy to use. It's fast. It holds a lot of paper. It's got a very accessible, extremely convenient multi-feed envelope tray in the rear for when you need to print envelopes. The display is crisp and readable. I love that you can have preset email address for sending scans. I also love that the printer is wireless.If I were to change anything, I suppose I'd want the otherwise quite accessible "Start Here" guide to also talk us through setting up the various options to be found at epson(dot)com/iPrint, or at least to provide some kind of overview of those options. As it is, it just sends you to the page to fend for yourself.

I have used 'Avery' products for file organization in my home office and work. The file folder labels are another neat product from Avery. I got it to read QR codes that I normally read from my smartphone.  It will only read standard bar codes.

I've had a number of laminators over the years and while I don't use them a lot, when I do use them I want them to be quick and do a great job.This is no exception. I should start this review by admitting that I have a bit of a Post-It addiction.  I use them all over the place, especially in my work life.  I go through a fair number of Post-Its, and will try all sorts of new designs.  Thus, I was delighted to get the chance to review this dispenser.  This dispenser can be hung on a wall or other vertical surface, and allows one to pull out Post-Its in pop-up form.  There's also a space to store a pen.  So, this is quite a convenient little gadget, but there are some things to be aware of before purchase.  I'm not especially handy, and at first I couldn't figure out exactly how I was supposed to attach it to the wall.  I did manage to figure it out, but there aren't instructions, and the sticky velcro was not immediately obvious, at least for me.  The dispenser sticks to the wall with adhesive tabs that have velcro on one side, and are sticky on the other.  The velcro holds well, and can easily support the weight of the dispenser, and with use of a new tab, the dispenser can be moved.  That said, the package does caution that the adhesive can mar wallpaper, and I was a bit afraid of what it would do to my walls.  Thus, I ended up sticking this on the side of a file cabinet.  I can't say exactly what it will do to the walls because I'm not willing to try it.  At the end of the day, while this dispenser is certainly handy, I'm not convinced that it's so much more usefull than a desktop dispenser, which Post-It already makes.  I suspect that next to a wall phone this could be quite useful, but I don't think I'd go out of my way to upgrade if I already had another dispenser.

I worked in a shared office, and desk space is at a premium. This Fellowes Keyboard Tray has helped a lot. It has freed up a lot of space on my desk. The keyboard tray is high quality, and seems built to last. The are some cons though. First, it isn't cheap. Unless you really need the space, you may want to think twice about spending $200 for a keyboard tray. Some other things to consider are space and installation. If your desk is small, this will probably not fit. Make sure you take measurements, and make sure you have the space to install it. Installation could also be a little tricky. I briefly attempted to install it by myself, but it was a little harder than I anticipated. I decided to have a couple of my company's carpenters install it for me. Installation seemed simple to them, and it was done quickly. The Fellowes Keyboard Tray has made my life easier in my office, and I recommend it if it's a necessity.

This is an impressive printer. It really does have everything. Unpacking it is a bit of a process and getting it all set up and working can take a bit. But once you get there, you have a powerful and useful machine at your disposal.Complete all-in-one. Seriously. More than any other "all-in-one" I've seen or used. It will feed scan or bed scan, print, fax, etc. You can print from and SDMI card or USB, all of which you can easily navigate from the touchscreen panel. The most important feature (for me) is the wireless connection, allowing me to print from any device, including my phone. (Epson has an app, but you can also connect via Google.)Epson has several similar models, but this is the standard-format, so you are limited to standard 8.5" paper sizes. The paper tray is a little awkward and even a bit flimsy...the cover for it seems to fall off every time I use it. And the arms for holding papers after they print seems kind of awkward too, but you have to use it or your papers will fall on the floor.There are four separate ink cartridges. I know others have pointed out that this ink is expensive, but I'm glad that there are three separate color (plus one black) cartridges, so you can just replace the one that's actually low. For example, if you're low on red, you just replace the red, not a whole "color" cartridge. The quality is good, but I was actually surprised that photos (granted, printed on regular paper) weren't as clear as I had hoped they would be.So maybe there are a few quirky things about this printer, but it is absolutely fantastic. It's very versatile. Recommended.

Got ideas? Want to draw or maybe just write with out all those silly lines? or maybe both?  Why not?  You're a grown up! Or at least you're having grown up ideas now! So sometimes you want to sketch and sometimes you want to write and sometimes you just need a place to put all of your ideas down so you don't forget them. This notebook is for you! 70 sheets of hardcore sketch paper. It's 9 by 6 so when the world decides you should be famous you can dig out what you drew (or didn't draw) in this book and sell it to them to put in their pretty little frames and be jealous of your real talent.In all seriousness. We love this notebook. I gave it to my 8 year-old and set a limit of one picture a day and I get some pretty great dad-art for the office out of it... Occasionally my 4-year-old adds his flair as well.

I decided to try these pens after being sent a couple of them with something else I bought.  I loved them and decided to try a 10-pack of all the colors.  They work well and the colors are great!  I can use the colors on different subjects when I file things and it will make items easier to spot.  There is a free case included but be careful opening the plastic so you don't ruin the case.  Also, the .07 is the line size I like as I am not a fan of the real tiny lines on some of the pens.
This item works perfect. My office uses it all the time. Good price. I have used other brands, but this one work's best.

I ordered this because I wanted to get rid of an accordion file that I have had forever. I use it to stash my bills until it's time to pay them.Thank goodness I didn't actually buy this.  It reminds me of those corrugated boxes that you can buy to stash Chritmas ornaments in. You know, those flimsy overpriced boxes that can't protect anything.This came in a big box packed tightly with air bags to keep it safe. This consists of a flimsy corrugated box that is packed flat  and you unfold it and assemble. It is flimsy and cheap looking. I ended up buying a canvas cube to hold my incoming mail and tossed this out.If the manufacturer wants to sell these, why not at least fabricate them from a thin recyclable plastic and add some texture for strength and color for style.As it stands, this is a junky product. This is the free pen that comes with the 4.5 oz bottles of Noodler's ink. When you buy it from Noodler's it's been converted to an eyedropper pen, so that you can use the entire barrel as an ink reservoir, making it an excellent pen to take to class with you for taking notes and the rest. I'd class this as a step down in width from a Pilto Metropolitan. The line is fairly fine, but not as scratchy as a fine pen tends to be. In fact, for what it is, it's a startlingly smooth writing pen.I've tested the pen on premium paper (Rhodia, to be exact), the heavy cardstock used for time punch cards, notebook paper, as well as carbon paper from a vendor's invoice. I've also written on basic copy paper, sticky notes, and all kinds of scraps of paper you see every day. There is moderate ghosting on the other side, but because the tip is so fine, you don't see a whole lot of bleed through. Even on the thin, cruddy paper (the carbon copy), there was no feathering at all with Noodler's Heart of Darkness.Nib creep is minimal with Noodler's ink in this pen, whereas the Metro tends to have a messy looking nib every time I take it out of my bag. The cost on Amazon, however, is ATROCIOUS. Every major pen carrier will have the Platinum Preppy for $3. If you are making an order on another pen site for a more expensive pen, throw in a few Preppy pens to take advantage of the lower price everywhere else on the planet.

First, assembly: while the assembly of this chair isn't complicated, it's not entirely easy, either. The instructions are only six steps, but as usual, they read like someone used an automated internet translator to make English out of some other language. You can figure it out, but it's worded oddly. Unlike another reviewer, i had a great deal of trouble getting the casters into their slots. The screw holes all lined up nicely, but propping the chair up to connect the back to the bottom is much more easily done with two people working together. One of the armrests put up quite a fight, the other was downright easy. It probably took me about 15 minutes from start to finish to get this chair into one piece, but i got about 50% of the way through my profanity portfolio while doing it.Second, the chair once assembled: meh.No one's going to mistake this for a fancy chair. It's leather, sure, but from a few feet away you'd probably think it was fake. The sides of the chair flare out slightly where the armrests attach, giving it a bit of a Frankenstein's-neck look.The padding is very very thin. If you have a bony backside, you may not be able to sit comfortably in this chair for more than a few minutes. If you have bony elbows and tend to lean hard on the armrest, your elbows are going to hurt.And it claims to be a 'high back' chair... i guess it depends on what you mean by high back. For me, at about 5'9", the back comes to the top of my shoulders. Perhaps my expectations are unreasonable, but in the past most 'high back' chairs i've used have had backs high enough that i could lean my head on them, too. This one, well, i can tip my head back and stare at the ceiling, i suppose.The height is adjustable, and easily so, but with a fairly small range of what looks to be about 3 inches. The lowest setting is slightly too low for me, and the highest setting is slightly too high for me. This means that if you're much taller or shorter than i (to review, i'm 5'9"), you might not be able to set this chair to your liking.Lastly, the casters are pretty cheap. They can't even handle low-pile carpet, so if you plan to use this chair on a carpeted surface, plan to invest in one of those plastic mat thingies too.This is a serviceable chair, and depending on your body and your needs, it might suit you much better than it suits me. As with any chair that costs more than a few dollars, i'd strongly suggest finding a retailer with a floor model that you can sit on before you actually consider buying.
At my office we're used to Avery labels, but these from 3M are just as good. The labels are easy to print on, with strong adhesive. I wouldn't hesitate to use 3M label products again.

The Kensington wireless presenter is a simple remote slide presentation controller featuring only four buttons: three of them control the slides (next, previous, stop) and the last button triggers a red laser pointer.It is powered via two standard AAA batteries (supplied).The shape is well designed to hold comfortably in all hands large to small, and it's very easy to feel your way to the controls even in complete darkness, and you can hold a good grip thanks to its clever shape and its lush rubberized finish.The Presenter has a few features not found on competing products that justify its premium price:- USB receiver doubles as a 1GB memory stick: store your presentation and go!- low battery warning light- USB receiver fits conveniently inside the remote- auto-off: when the receiver is inserted and locked, the power to the remote is shut off, preventing unwanted laser activation.I had no trouble using the Presenter on both OSX and XP, without needing to install any driver. In my very informal tests the receiver picked up signals flawlessly from 30 feet away.This is a cleverly designed product that delivers. A little expensive, but that's the price of good design and convenience. Highly recommended.

Last year I got a Swingline Optima stapler, which is similar to this one. They are both excellent office tools and work with great ease on 60 to 70 pages. The only white-out I use anymore are these.  Good price on internet and buy several at a time so don't get frustrated when they run out.

Just follow the instructions for the website to get the software to work with Microsoft Word and your printer. Your stored mailing list will appear on the lables (test first with plain paper). The product is made well and durable and feels like it will last a long time.  The only drawback is it's smaller size.  I found that using this with a normal sized mouse was a bit uncomfortable as you have to keep having to pick up the mouse to get back on the pad.  The wrist rest is nice, but not really resting if you keep moving it.However, I have several mouses (or is that mice?) and tried them all, corded and wireless of various sizes. I don't always bring a mousepad, but the comfort level is enough that I remember to bring it along.So for the specific use with a smaller mouse and it's very durable, clean feel and wrist comfort, I highly recommend it.

Paper is paper, but the price was good and it works just fine.  I have my own business and was running a little to low on paper and received this within 2 days.  When you don't have time to go out and buy it, ordering it with Prime was terrific!

All in all, after testing out all of the features and functionality of this scanner for quite a while I have to say that as a scanner it's extremely good.  It's very fast, very efficient, and can truly process a lot of documents convert them to searchable text and so on.  It's also very easy to use.  Therefore, I give this scanner, 4/5.  There's only one reason I took off 1 star.  This scanner isn't cheap.  I have a multi-functional printer that costs about $100 less than this machine and the only difference between this Kodak and my Canon all in one is the fact that the Canon can't convert to searchable PDF.  Otherwise, in terms of speed and quality, the machines are the same.  Therefore, if you need a pure scanner because you already have a good printer, that can convert to searchable PDF and is very easy to set up and use, then get the Kodak.
I have a repeater antenna for my satelitte radio which interferred horribly with my old cordless phone.  But with these there is no interference whatsoever.  I would recommend these.
They are good and stick to pretty much whatever you put them on.I like to use them as a book mark.

HP's 3050 Deskjet printer impresses me. It prints very quickly in all the colors I could ever ask for; and setup was a breeze with that installation software and guide. It even comes with a bag that you can use to carry it with you--this printer can be used either with a USB connection to a computer or as a wireless printer. (It comes with a USB cable.) As far as scanning and copying go, these functions are also rather easy to do; the instructions make the first time you copy a snap!For printing, get HP 61 black and white cartridges and HP 61 Tri-color cartridges. If you can catch a sale on these, stock up!One reviewer notes that it doesn't have a fax feature but I agree with them when they also say that you can just scan a copy of a document into your computer and send that as an attachment to any email.Overall, I really can't think of anything negative to say about this printer. The  Wilson Jones Durable Hinge Poly Binder with Removable Ring, 1 Inch, Brown color, is a very attractive 3 Ring binder. The metal strip and rings inside are removable to enable you to recycle both the binder and the metal separately. This PVC free binder is made of an easy to clean material...just wipe and go!I found this binder perfect for keeping plastic pages I use for storing film negative strips. It sort of has a photo album look to it so it fits in with its purpose.Looks good, functional, and recyclable. What's not to love?

The Fellowes Foot Rocker with Microban Protection comes in a plain  box with drawings on the side to show how to assemble the five pieces.  In a nutshell, you snap the rockers on to the sides, slide them to lock in place, and then put the caps on the outside.  (It is sort of like putting hub caps on after putting on two tires.)  I found it very easy to put together, but could see how it might be a bit difficult for some to snap into place and slide to lock,  My wife might have had a bit of difficulty with this, it did take some pressure to do.Once assembled, you have a foot rocker that has two height options. (2  and 4 inches)  You flip it over to adjust, so you need to be happy with one of the two.  So for some people, it might not be the right height, but if you have an adjustable chair, that should solve that issue.  I sort of like that it only has the two heights, because I think more adjustments would tend to weaken the integrity of the unity and would make it more apt to break.  As it is, it is pretty sturdy.Basically, it does what it's supposed to - it sits on the floor and rocks with your feet on it.  It is solid and should hold up for a long time.  It is treated with Microban antimicrobial protection, which is supposed to help keep the unit cleaner longer.  I don't know for sure about this, but it would be simple enough to wash it to keep it clean.I don't know how much it improves circulation and reduces fatigue, but it is comfortable to have your feet on.  I also like to rock my feet a bit when at the desk typing or thinking of what I want to write.  It does creek a bit, but doesn't really bother me, and I have it in an office by myself, so I have no one to bother.  My wife, and my little girl, who are shorter, like it at the desk with the computer they use.  My little girl says she especially likes it because her feet don't reach the floor, but do reach this foot rest.  Neither of them minded the little creaking either.Overall, it is a nice little foot rest that rocks and the amazon price of 50% off the list makes it an affordable addition to a desk or work station.
I have been using these for a few months now. I like the format, the paper color and feel, the spiral binding is nice. Its a great product. Thanks!

First thing I noticed is that the material is very hard, it's slightly textured so as not to be quite so smooth.  It's a really solid, stable, spacious table. Materials have really come a long way as far as plastics are concerned, and this table top really shows that.  I considered just buying a piece of plywood and putting it on some 2x4s to make a table, but I am glad that I bought this one instead, because they really thought out all the details as to what would make a good, hard, smooth surface.  Also, this table is very strong.  It has steel girders running down the edges to make it stiff.

These ticket sets come 20 sheets to a package, with 10 tickets you can tear off on each sheet (for 200 total tickets).To print them off, load them into your printer tray just like paper (once you have the formatting set for tickets - experiment on regular paper first!).Then fold each ticket along the crease lines, which serves to also pull them apart. Leave the 'stubs' on the tickets as receipts for people and that's it.What I found is the tickets print nice and clean on the bright side, the top, which is coated with an 'eggshell' matte sheen. The bottom side uses more ink/toner, since it isn't coated at all. Since all tickets have a top and bottom, this isn't a big deal in how it looks/feels. Just save your best graphics for the 'top' side, and double-check when loading them up.In all cases, let the ink dry a little bit before tearing apart the tickets, so you don't get smears.I made up a set for raffles to go with the Cookie Lee Jewelry parties I host, and they look very nice. Also, the stubs don't come off until you pull them.NOTES: The tickets are not glossies - they are considered matte, but still have a hint of sheen to them. They are reasonably opaque (I can see my hand on the other side, but only if I hold the sheet up to the light). Both sides are printable, and they look like real tickets - not something 'crafty' you cooked up on your own. In other words, I wouldn't be afraid to use these for professional events.One last note: If you aren't a graphics expert, the company has a template set up to go with the ticket sheets. All I had to do was enter the product number at the Avery print website. Using this was super easy, and now I am looking for more excuses to make tickets for things. :)

Wheres the rest of the pencil?  I have and use and LOVe the GG 1000.  I got this as a "workshop" pencil (cause there is no way my 1000 is going into the workshop).  I figured it would be a good "work" pencil.  On that mark it is ok.  Better than a cheapy draftmatic that broke after one drop (onto concrete- so I guess I can't complain too much) but not anywhere near the level of quality of the 1000.  The tip is non retractable and the head and grip are nice.  They have good weight and the knurling on the grip is cut well and offers good grip (especially if using with gloves).  but get past the tip and grip and it's like Pentel forgot the rest of the pencil.  The body is much thinner than the grip and is made from cheap styrine plastic (think disposabel pencils).  MUCH MUCH MUCH thinner than the head.  It almost looks like they forgot the outer body of the pencil.  Yea it is not a pleasent look.  It screams CHEAP!  I got the .9mm size (grey/silver body) and there are noticable flow lines (not a huge deal- just another part of the cheap look factor).  The body is Hexagonal (oh wait what is a six side figure called???  ok I looked it up it is hexagonal) which detracts even more from the look of this pencil.  It has a cheapy pocket clip (that can be removed easily).  The push button and small ereaser are actully well made and fit nicely.  The pencil came with 3 leads (so YEA there).  It does write nicely and clicks in typical Pentel fashion.  Taking this pencil apart is worthless as all that comes apart is the head unscrews from the body and the cap and ereaser come off.  The rest of the mechanics are more or less moded into the plastic body and a serious jam is going to render this pencil useless (unlike the 1000 that can be stripped almost completly).  So overall this is an ok mechanical pencil.  THe head is nice but the body stinks. I won't be getting another one if this one comes up broken or missing.  It is in line with some of Pentels cheaper offerings- but is not even close to the same league as the 1000.

Today, I set up my new Canon Pixma MG4220 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier.The installation went smoothly, although the instructions and diagrams could have been a bit easier to read and understand.  It pays to take your time when setting up the printer, since the parts are made of flimsy plastic and you do not want to break a part inadvertently.  On the plus side, the paper loads easily in the front and you need only two ink cartridges, one black and one color. The quality of the printing is very good--crisp, clear, with bright, true-to-life colors.On the other hand, this printer is noisy both while printing and after the job is done.  I suppose I will get used to this, but it is a bit irritating.  Please be aware that this printer does not have FAX capability.  It does two-sided printing with ease, which is a useful feature.As I get to know my Canon a bit better, I will have a broader picture of its capabilities, but so far, it seems like a good basic printer that can print both wirelessly or with a USB cable (which you must buy separately.)

I received this from the Amazon Vine program.The product itself is super-helpful, especially when wrapping gifts.You wear it on your hand, so you hold the paper with one hand and grab the pre-cut tape strip with the other.Nice!However, the cost for replacement strips is much higher than a regular roll of tape.Convenience vs. cost is what it comes down to.Your choice.

The original Fisher Space pen is very nice and feels like quality. I enjoy the weight it has, it feels very sturdy and reliable. I would recommend this pen. Both help keep the lid in place.These boxes are useful for lots of household storage needs --and I've even used similar boxes to pack most of my stuff when I moved. Then, I can refeed the same sheet in the opposite direction when I need to print another label. I've always eyed wrist rests in the stores and thought they'd be a comfort, but I was never bold enough to purchase one.  Now I wish I had gotten one sooner!I use my keyboard all the time and never noticed that my wrists were in any kind of strain.  And maybe they weren't in a "strain" but they weren't as comfortable as they could be. I could immediately tell a difference after plopping down this gel wrist rest.  Something about the joint alignment must make the rest a necessary and important luxury for anyone who uses a computer often (who doesn't anymore?).I noticed there was some concern about whether or not this is a one-size-fits-all and will it work on different keyboards.  I posted a user-photo on Amazon that shows the rest sitting next to my gateway keyboard and it fits perfectly for me.  The gateway keyboard is fairly low compared to some of the others out there, though, so if you own a keyboard that isn't fairly flat this product may not work best for you.Overall, with the exception of that this size gel rest may not work for all keyboards, I cannot recommend this product enough.  It's just squishy enough to melt a little with pressure, but firm so that your wrists won't sag.  The black leather look is stylish and comfortably smooth. I've been using theFujitsu ScanSnap S1500 Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for PCin my office for years, and while I think it is an exceptional work scanner, I was glad to be given the opportunity to compare it with the Canon imageFORMULA DR-C125.  Other than the ScanSnap, I haven't come across any other scanners that excel at office-friendly, mostly pdf, letter-sized document scanning.PROS- Very small footprint. This scanner will easily fit on your desk and takes up a small amount of room.- Optional U-Turn paper path. The scanner can be set to feed paper in a "U" design so it feeds back up instead of straight ahead.  This is definitely an advantage over the ScanSnap, which allows you to fold up the front feeder, but then which requires that you leave 11" of room in front of the scanner for the paper to eject.  This is one of the best features for me.- One touch scanning.  A lot of scanners have 5 or 6 buttons on them to use for different functions, but this scanner, like the Fujitsu has a one touch that will output directly to PDF.  I don't have to spend a lot of time setting up options or opening up third party software, and it functions great using the buttons directly from the scanner.- Very fast. Only slightly slower (less than a second per page) than the ScanSnap.  This scanner processes documents  faster than any flatbed I've used and faster even than my huge Kyocera TasAlfa commercial copier/scanner.  If you have a ten page document, you can simply put it in the feeder, press the button, and it will scan and convert to PDF in around 10 seconds.- Duplex scanning. Works great.  No need to feed the paper in both directions, and the scanner doesn't have to feed the paper one way, then pull it out and feed it the other way.  It makes one pass and detects if it is a two-sided paper. Sometimes it works a little too well, as it will scan a single sheet of paper as duplex if there is really heavy ink on one side that it can see through the opposite side.  But this isn't a big issue.- TWAIN driver. The ScanSnap doesn't come with a TWAIN driver, and you must have the CD or software to install. You can't download it from Fujitsu's web site and must e-mail them for an FTP link if you lose the disc.  The Canon does have a TWAIN driver which is great for more advanced users.CONS- Poor OCR.  I had more errors with the Optical Character Recognition software than I do with the ABBYY OCR software that comes with the ScanSnap.- After 6 months of fairly heavy use, the rollers on the automatic feeder seem to be getting a little more worn, and I have noticed I occasionally will get jams due to the feeder pulling multiple sheets through at once. This usually happens with documents that are a little older and the paper might not be as crisp. But I have definitely noticed it more now than when I first got the scanner.Overall I think the DR-C125 is an excellent scanner. If I had to make a choice between the Fujitsu ScanSnap and this model, I would probably go with the DR-C125 due to my cluttered desk and the U-Turn paper feeding, but really it would be a very difficult choice to make and I don't think you can go wrong with either of them.

I found this easy and intuitive to use.  My primary use is with large pieces of colored lightweight kraft paper, to make elementary school bulletin boards. I have to say that I am as impressed by the software suite packaged with the scanner as I am with the hardware.  The included software enables you to scan documents to pdf and convert pdf documents to editable text.  You can scan to any of a number of cloud services as well as to a folder on your desk top, lap top, email or programs like drop box to transfer it to a mobile device.  It is a very flexible system!The scanner itself is well constructed, small and light.  At just under 5 lbs. it is not much heavier than many laptops and occupies about as much desk space as those little portable printers.  It is actually small and light enough to be considered portable. (While I wouldn't want to  carry it daily, it can easily be moved from room to room or home to office) though the ability to scan to the cloud eliminates the need to actually move it in most situations.At this point I have several pieces of Epson equipment, and by and large have been pretty impressed. Without my thinking about it, Epson has quietly taken over my home office.  Their wireless all in one machine took over for my Canon pixma a few years ago because of it's versatility and higher quality prints.  I got my daughter, an award winning photographer one of their flat bed scanners, and one for my office a few months later.Why am I bringing those other machines up in a review of this scanner?  The software spied them on the network, presenting me with the option of using the other scanners (to scan to the cloud...).  That's a nice bonus, as I imagine there will be times when a flat bed scanner is more appropriate.  What the scanner offers over the other 2 machines is a documents feeder which can handle 26 pages per minute and scan business cards (paper and plastic, as well as pages up to 12 x 36 "I'll be using it to organize and reduce clutter in my office, as well as keep tabs on restaurants I've discovered while traveling (having access to a file in the cloud means they will be at hand when I need them and organized in a way that I can find them!I actually have a big editing project ahead which this will make much easier, but it is useful for those other things as well ;)Where did it lose a star?  It was a long and arduous install. I had to manually update the drivers, and then it wasn't recognized.  I had to uninstall and reinstall twice to get it working properly with Windows 7. I suspect that as I use it, it will recapture that star. It really is a useful little device, and I like the small footprint.I am also a bit puzzled that it is not wireless, which seems a little odd in a device used to scan to the cloud.  The printer/ all in one machine is, which is how the software picked it up on my  home network.  It is not a huge problem as it is usb and so can be used with a variety of machines. I just like doing away with cords when possible now that I have a network set up.In sum. it is a small and very useful little machine with a nice software suite which enables you to scan and convert documents and send them to a folder, email or directly to a cloud service (it is set up for MS, google, sugar synch but can be directed elsewhere).  It is simple to use, and works as promised but takes a bit of work to set up.  It would have been n easier process if it autoupdated (as the printer did) but that is a one time issue.It connects via usb and can be installed on both windows and mac systems.  I would have preferred wireless, but usb works with most of the devices and machines I have.All in all it is a nice system which enables you to transport documents more or less anywhere, and convert them for easier editing/ manipulation.  The click to post and business card feed also make it a nice organizational system.(Note you need to have an account set up to scan to in order to be able to use cloud services/ transport).  In some ways it is surprising that was not built in, but there are quite a few services available, and it is nice that Epson gives you that choice.

Scotch Dispenser by Karim is a nice, stylish looking Scotch tape dispenser that looks nice on a desktop, kitchen counter, or other place where tape is needed and used on a frequent basis. The rounded, oval shaped container houses a roll of tape inside and the tape is easily cut by grabbing the open edge of the tape and tearing across the metal cutting bar.Tape dispensers are certainly nothing new, but the Scotch Dispenser by Karim has most of them beat for many reasons. First, I like that this dispenser is more compact in size. Other tape dispensers are long in shape and take up too much desk or counter space. Second, I like that this dispenser doesn't slide around. It is weighed down with sand and even has a gripping surface on the bottom, to keep it in place and protect the surface on which it rests. When you grab the tape, the dispenser stays put, making it easy to get the tape you need with the use of one hand.Scotch Dispenser by Karim has an interesting appearance and from a distance, it looks like it might be a paper clip holder or some other storage device. It doesn't look like other tape dispensers and that is precisely part of its appeal. Like I said, it looks stylish and can be placed in many areas of the house. It blends right in and doesn't even seem like a dispenser of any kind.I like that this product comes with a small roll of tape. However, consumers need to be ready to purchase more. The roll Scotch supplies is rather small and won't last very long. Additional rolls of tape will cost more than simply purchasing ordinary rolls of Scotch tape with a plastic dispenser, but this is only a minor complaint and when all factors are considered, the Scotch Dispenser by Karim is a very nice little tape dispenser that performs well, is easy to open and refill, and stays in place when in use. It is a product I am glad I got to know and it earns an easy recommendation.

This is a pretty good artist's sketchpad! It has many features that recommend it, although it does have one notable flaw.- PROS -* It's 11" x 14", so the pages are wide enough to do expansive, detailed work, or you can divide them in half to get twice as many smaller sheets.* The pages are thick, so you won't damage anything when you erase, yet they're (just barely) thin enough that you can trace something, provided it's backlit, such as with a light box.* It's spiral-bound, so you can flip through the pages as often as you like, without worrying about the glue loosening.* It's quite sturdy, with a heavy cardboard backing. The front is a thinner cardboard.* It has a double pocket at the front, which you can use to store notes, reference photos, or other sketches. (It will NOT hold pencils, erasers, or other drawing tools.)* You get 70 sheets, which means it'll last a decent amount of time.* According to the description, you can use this sketchpad with pencil, pen, marker, pastel, and charcoal. I'm guessing it's not quite heavy enough for use with watercolor pencil or watercolors, at least, not without bleed-through. It also claims to be acid-free.* Best of all, the pages are perforated along one side, so if you want to remove a sketch for scanning, it will tear out cleanly. Just make sure you fold the paper along the perforated edge first, to make it easier to tear the page out.- CONS -* For some reason, the paper doesn't seem to erase very well. I use a kneaded eraser, which normally does a good job of picking up graphite. When I tested this paper, however, the erased marks were faintly visible. I even tried a fresh eraser, in case the issue was with my kneaded eraser, but I got the same results. This isn't as much of an problem for me, since I always scan my drawings and clean them up in Photoshop. But if you expect a clean, perfect sketch, you're not going to get it unless you trace your finished drawing onto a clean sheet of paper.I'll give this sketchpad 4 stars, because it has a lot of great features. Just beware of the erasing issue! Recommended for preliminary sketches or studies, rather than finished pieces of art.
